opportunities.title: Ajou University International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarships (Spring 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with TOPIK level 3 or equivalent can apply by 20 November 2026 for Spring 2027 entry to Ajou University, Korea, with scholarships of up to 100% tuition.
opportunities.description:
Ajou University in Suwon, South Korea, offers a range of tuition scholarships to international students entering its undergraduate programmes. The current admission round is for the Spring 2027 semester, with online applications and documents due by 5 pm Korean time on 20 November 2026.

New students can receive Ajou Frontier Scholarships of up to 100% tuition for as long as four years, chosen internally for outstanding grades, including a Frontier U award for students from OECD aid-recipient countries with no current Ajou students or those facing war or disaster. Ajou Global Scholarships of 30% to 100% for the first semester are tied to Korean (TOPIK) or English test scores.

Since applicants need TOPIK level 3 or an Ajou Korean language pass, this suits African students who have already studied Korean or completed a Korean language course.
opportunities.benefits: Ajou Frontier Scholarships: 100% tuition for 4 years (S), 2 years (A), 1 year (J) or 1 semester (O); Frontier U: 100% for 1 semester to 4 years. Ajou Global Scholarships for the first semester: 100% (TOPIK 6, IELTS 8.0 or TOEFL iBT 100), 70% (TOPIK 5, IELTS 7.0, iBT 90), 50% (TOPIK 4, IELTS 6.5, iBT 80) or 30% (TOPIK 3, IELTS 5.5, iBT 75). Challenger Scholarships of 20-30% for Ajou Korean language levels 5-6.
requirements: Applicant and both parents are non-Korean citizens
High school graduate (or expected) with a qualification recognised by the home country
TOPIK level 3 or higher, or a level 3+ pass at an affiliated Korean language centre, or a pass in Ajou's Korean exam
For Global Scholarships: the TOPIK, IELTS or TOEFL score for the chosen tier
documents: Admission documents as listed in Ajou's admission guide (school certificates, transcripts, language scores, passport copies)
opportunities.selection_process: Frontier Scholarships are chosen internally based on outstanding grades; Global Scholarships depend on language test scores at entry.
important_dates: Application and documents: 28 September to 20 November 2026, 17:00 KST
opportunities.about_provider: Ajou University is a private research university in Suwon, near Seoul, with strengths in engineering, IT and business. Its international admissions office handles applications from foreign students and also runs a Korean language programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through Ajou's international undergraduate admissions site and submit the documents in the admission guide by 5 pm KST on 20 November 2026. Scholarships are considered as part of admission. Contact admission@ajou.ac.kr with questions.
opportunities.notes: Global Scholarships only apply to the first semester; later semesters depend on grades. Ajou also handles GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) undergraduate applications.

opportunities.title: BiO Global South Conference Travel Grants (20 November 2026 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers based in most African countries can apply by 20 November 2026 for up to GBP 3,000 to attend an international conference abroad.
opportunities.description:
The Company of Biologists offers Global South Conference Travel Grants through its journal Biology Open to help early-career researchers based in the Global South attend an international scientific meeting held in a country other than their own. The current round closes on 20 November 2026 and covers travel after 21 December 2026.

Each grant is worth up to GBP 3,000 and can pay for registration, travel, accommodation, subsistence and visa fees. Because demand is high, eligible applications are chosen by random lottery, and further rounds close on 18 June 2027 and 19 November 2027.

Most African countries are on the eligible Global South list (including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Ethiopia and Tanzania), making this one of the most accessible conference travel grants for African PhD students and postdocs.
opportunities.benefits: Up to GBP 3,000 per applicant towards conference registration, travel, accommodation, subsistence and visa fees. Awards may be partial. Travel insurance is not covered and costs already incurred are not funded retrospectively.
requirements: Based in a country on the Global South list in the applicant handbook (most African countries; Sudan, South Sudan and Zimbabwe are not listed)
Usually a PhD student or postdoc early in their career; independent group leaders without travel funding may also apply
Attending an international scientific meeting in a different country from where you are based (not a Company of Biologists Journal Meeting or Workshop)
No other Company of Biologists funding in the past 12 months
Unsuccessful applicants must wait 12 months to reapply
documents: Signed supervisor letter on headed paper (or head-of-department letter for PIs confirming no independent travel funds)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are checked for eligibility and scope, then grantees are chosen by random lottery among the eligible applications.
opportunities.about_provider: The Company of Biologists is a not-for-profit publisher and UK registered charity (no. 277992) that runs five journals: Development, Journal of Cell Science, Journal of Experimental Biology, Disease Models & Mechanisms and Biology Open. Its surplus funds grants and events for the research community.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Click Apply on the grant page to reach the Company of Biologists grants portal, complete the form in English and upload the supervisor letter, abstract and CV before 20 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: After the meeting you must send receipts, return unspent money within a month, submit a 250-word report with two photos within three months, and acknowledge Biology Open in your talk or poster. Travel must take place within six months of the award.

opportunities.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship via Bordeaux INP (Master's, 2027-2028)
opportunities.provider: Bordeaux INP / French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International master's or engineering applicants aged 29 or under (born after 31 March 1997), without French nationality, with an average of at least 15/20, applying to a Bordeaux INP school.
opportunities.description:
Bordeaux INP, a group of six public engineering schools in Bordeaux, is accepting applications from international students who want the school to nominate them for the French government's Eiffel Excellence Scholarship for 2027-2028. Bordeaux INP only handles master's-level (engineering degree) applications for this programme, not PhDs.

Candidates choose a course at one of the six schools: ENSC (cognitive engineering), ENSEGID (environment and georesources), ENSEIRB-MATMECA (electronics, computer science, mathematics and telecoms), ENSMAC (materials, food and chemistry), ENSPIMA (aeronautical maintenance) or ENSTBB (biotechnology). A committee picks the strongest files at the end of November and in early December 2026, and only files averaging 15/20 or more are passed on to Campus France for the national jury.

The Eiffel scholarship is among the most prestigious French government awards and is a strong route for African engineering and science students into a French grande école. The internal call closes on 20 November 2026 at midnight French time.
opportunities.benefits: The Bordeaux INP page does not list the amounts; the allowance and other benefits are those of the national Eiffel programme published by Campus France.
requirements: Aged 29 or under (born after 31 March 1997)
Not a dual national holding French citizenship
Not holding another French government, Erasmus+ or AUF grant
Only one Eiffel application; not previously rejected or funded by Eiffel
Not on an apprenticeship contract or off-site training course
Academic average of at least 15/20 to be forwarded to Campus France
Non-French speakers must provide a French language diploma (DELF, DALF or TCF)
documents: Certificate of degree dates and grading system issued by the university
Transcripts for the last three years
Copy of the last degree obtained
DELF, DALF or TCF certificate for non-French speakers
opportunities.selection_process: A Bordeaux INP committee reviews complete files at the end of November and early December 2026. Only candidates with an average of at least 15/20 are sent on to Campus France, whose national jury makes the final choice in mid-April 2027.
important_dates: Bordeaux INP deadline: 20 November 2026, midnight French time
Internal committee: late November to early December 2026
Candidates told of the internal result: mid-December 2026 to early January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Bordeaux INP (Institut polytechnique de Bordeaux) brings together six engineering schools in Bordeaux. The Eiffel programme was developed by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its national selection is run by Campus France.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Upload every document as a separate PDF on the Bordeaux INP MoveOn form (https://inpb.moveonfr.com/locallogin/68dbf6dd1edb117d08043401/eng) before the deadline. Late or incomplete files are rejected. Questions can be sent to bourse.eiffel@bordeaux-inp.fr.
opportunities.notes: All documents are mandatory and incomplete files are rejected outright. One calendar line on the page still says "2026 campaign", but the call is for the 2027-2028 academic year.

opportunities.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship via ENS de Lyon (2027-2028)
opportunities.provider: ENS de Lyon / French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-French nationals applying for a master's (up to 29, born after 31 March 1996) or PhD (up to 35, born after 31 March 1990) at ENS de Lyon for 2027-2028.
opportunities.description:
The France Excellence Eiffel programme is the French government's flagship scholarship for international students coming to France for a master's or a doctorate. Candidates cannot apply to the national programme on their own: a French higher-education institution must select them and put their file forward to Campus France, which runs the national jury.

ENS de Lyon, one of France's grandes écoles for research and teaching in the sciences and humanities, has opened its internal call for the 2027-2028 Eiffel round. Students who want to be nominated by ENS de Lyon must send their file through the school's online form by 20 November 2026; an internal ENS committee then picks the candidates it will submit in December 2026, and Campus France announces the final laureates in April 2027.

For African students this is one of the few routes into a fully funded French master's or PhD that does not depend on a bilateral agreement with their home country. Because the ENS call closes on the same day this listing was checked, anyone interested should act immediately.
opportunities.benefits: The page does not state the amounts; it refers applicants to the Campus France Eiffel website for the allowance and benefits paid by the national programme.
requirements: Not a French citizen
Master's track: no previous studies in France and aged 29 or under (born after 31 March 1996)
PhD track: aged 35 or under (born after 31 March 1990)
For a joint PhD, the co-supervision agreement must already be approved
Master's candidates must also apply separately to the chosen ENS de Lyon master's programme
documents: Online application form on the ENS de Lyon MoveOn portal
Supporting documents set out in the programme regulations (PDF linked on the page)
opportunities.selection_process: An ENS de Lyon committee reviews all internal applications in December 2026 and chooses which candidates to nominate. Campus France's national jury then makes the final decision and publishes results in April 2027.
important_dates: ENS de Lyon internal deadline: 20 November 2026
opportunities.about_provider: ENS de Lyon is a French grande école that trains researchers and teachers in the sciences and humanities. The Eiffel programme itself was created by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and is administered by Campus France.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the ENS de Lyon online Eiffel form (https://enslyon.moveonfr.com/form/6ac5ef62ae371f890e043b84/eng) before the deadline. Master's candidates must also submit a normal application to their ENS de Lyon master's programme. Questions go to the scientist mobility office (scientist.mobility at ens-lyon.fr).
opportunities.notes: The page stresses that this procedure is only for the Eiffel grant, not for admission. Age limits on the ENS page differ slightly from other French universities' pages, so check the official regulations.

opportunities.title: Gerda Henkel Foundation Research Scholarships (historical humanities)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral historians, archaeologists and other historical humanities researchers of any nationality with a published PhD from the last ten years can apply by 20 November 2026 for 1-24 month research scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Gerda Henkel Foundation awards research scholarships to postdoctoral researchers in the historical humanities, including archaeology, history, historical Islamic studies, art history, history of law, prehistory and history of science. Neighbouring disciplines qualify if the central research question is historical.

Scholarships run for one to 24 months and pay a monthly stipend plus travel and material costs as needed. The current deadline of 20 November 2026 feeds into the Foundation committee's spring 2027 meeting, with decisions in April 2027 and funding starting from May 2027 at the earliest.

The Foundation funds researchers regardless of nationality or place of work and does not require an institutional affiliation, which makes it a valuable option for African historians and archaeologists who have published their doctoral thesis.
opportunities.benefits: Postdocs receive EUR 2,760 per month; researchers with a habilitation or equivalent receive EUR 3,720 per month. A family allowance of EUR 480 for the first child and EUR 120 for each further child under 18 is added, plus travel and material costs as required. Short-term scholarships are capped at EUR 30,000. No overheads or tuition fees are paid.
requirements: PhD (or habilitation) in a historical humanities field; PhD awarded within the last ten years (does not apply to habilitation holders)
Doctoral thesis published as a full monograph with an ISBN
Research project different from the thesis topic
No previous Gerda Henkel scholarship in the last five years and no rejected application in the last three years
No salary or pension during the scholarship
Any nationality and place of work; no institutional affiliation needed
Doctoral candidates are not eligible
documents: Project description of up to 8 pages (11 pt, 1.5 spacing) plus bibliography
Copies of master's and PhD certificates
One (maximum two) recommendation letters uploaded by the referee through the Foundation's online form
opportunities.selection_process: The Foundation's committees meet twice a year to decide on applications. Incomplete applications are not considered and reasons for rejection are not given.
important_dates: Deadline: 20 November 2026 (for the spring 2027 committee meeting)
opportunities.about_provider: The Gerda Henkel Foundation, established in 1976 in Düsseldorf, Germany, supports research in the historical humanities and cultural heritage. It has funded more than 9,000 projects.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online application form on the Gerda Henkel Foundation website in German or English, with PDFs of up to 6 MB each, and ask your referee to upload their letter through the online recommendation form. Applications by email are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Any use of generative AI must be declared. You may only apply to one Gerda Henkel programme per year, and conference-only funding is not available.

opportunities.title: Harvard Mahindra Humanities Center Postdoctoral Fellowships in Environmental Humanities 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent humanities PhDs of any nationality (degree from May 2024 onward) with an environmental humanities project.
opportunities.description:
The Mahindra Humanities Center at Harvard University is offering four one-year postdoctoral fellowships for 2027-28 on the theme of environmental humanities. Scholars from any humanistic discipline can apply, as long as their research speaks to the environment, and fellows spend the year in residence in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Fellows take part in a seminar that meets every two weeks across both semesters, alongside the Center's wider programme of lectures and events. International fellows hold the post from 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028 on a J-1 research scholar visa or F-1 OPT. There is no nationality restriction, so recent African PhDs working on climate, land, water, extraction or ecological history are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $70,000 for the year, medical insurance, $2,500 in research funds, and up to $1,500 for moving costs (only for fellows not already living in Greater Boston).
requirements: PhD awarded on or after May 2024, or all degree requirements including the defence completed by 1 August 2027
Research in a humanities discipline connected to environmental humanities
Able to be in residence at Harvard from September 2027 to August 2028
No nationality restriction
documents: One writing sample of up to 40 pages
Three referees, who are asked for letters automatically after you submit
opportunities.about_provider: The Mahindra Humanities Center is Harvard's main hub for interdisciplinary work in the humanities. It runs seminars, lectures and fellowships that bring scholars from around the world to Harvard.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Harvard's ARIES academic positions portal (posting 16602), uploading the CV, research statement and writing sample and entering three referees. Referees are emailed automatically and must upload their letters by 4 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Four fellowships are offered. Questions go to the Center's fellowship coordinator, Lisa Brown. The Center also runs Interdisciplinary Dissertation Completion Fellowships.

opportunities.title: ICTP School and Workshop on Birational and Enumerative Geometry of Moduli Spaces (Feb 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: School and workshop in Trieste, 15 to 26 February 2027, with no registration fee and a limited number of grants that give priority to participants from developing countries.

opportunities.title: INET-YSI Ageing and Sustainable Futures Conference 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and researchers within five years of their PhD, from any country, can submit an extended abstract by 20 November 2026 to the YSI ageing conference in Guwahati, India (8-10 February 2027), with travel support for a few.
opportunities.description:
The INET Young Scholars Initiative (YSI) is holding the Ageing and Sustainable Futures Conference, its "Conference 2.0", at the Omeo Kumar Das Institute of Social Change and Development (OKDISCD) in Guwahati, India, from 8 to 10 February 2027, together with Utrecht University. It looks at ageing and development, with a focus on South Asia and Northeast India.

The two-and-a-half-day event includes a pre-conference workshop, keynotes, young scholars' paper sessions and a stakeholder session. PhD students and early-career researchers submit an extended abstract first, and selected authors then send a full paper.

A few selected participants receive a travel stipend and accommodation. There is no nationality restriction, so African early-career researchers working on ageing, care, demography or social policy can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A few selected participants receive a travel stipend and accommodation (amounts not stated). Visa arrangements are the participant's responsibility. No conference fee is mentioned.
requirements: PhD student or early-career researcher (within 5 years of PhD)
Research relevant to ageing and sustainable development
Papers from East India especially encouraged
Selected authors must submit a full paper before the conference
documents: Extended abstract of 2,500-3,000 words in PDF (Times New Roman 12, 1.15 spacing, title and 3-5 keywords, no author names; title as file name)
Full paper by 15 January 2027 if selected
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on the quality of the extended abstract and on regional representation.
opportunities.about_provider: The Young Scholars Initiative began in 2012 as part of the Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET) in New York. It is a global network of more than 20,000 young economists and social scientists, with no age or academic membership requirements.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register or log in as a YSI member on the YSI website and submit your anonymised extended abstract through the event page by 20 November 2026. Questions can go to ysi@ineteconomics.org.
opportunities.notes: YSI membership is free. Travel support is limited to a few participants, so mention need where the form allows.

opportunities.title: Journalism Special Issue: Locally Informed? Information Inequalities and Local Journalism
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can send an 800-1,000 word extended abstract by 20 November 2026 for a special issue on local journalism and information inequalities; full manuscripts are due 30 June 2027.

opportunities.title: Korea Youth Summit 2027 (Seoul)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Youth summit in Seoul (5-8 April 2027) for ages 15-40 of any nationality; limited scholarships cover hotel, meals and local costs but not airfare, and an application fee applies.

opportunities.title: Mo Ibrahim Foundation Leadership Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African nationals under 40 (under 45 for mothers) with a master's and 7+ years' experience can apply by 20 November 2026 for 12-month leadership fellowships at AfDB, UNECA or ITC with a USD 100,000 stipend.
opportunities.description:
The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships, created by the Mo Ibrahim Foundation in 2011, identify and mentor the next generation of outstanding African leaders. Each year a small group of Fellows spends 12 months working in the executive office of a major institution, with direct mentoring from its head.

For the 2027 round, Fellows are placed at the African Development Bank in Abidjan, the UN Economic Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa, or the International Trade Centre in Geneva. Fellows receive a stipend of USD 100,000 and join the Foundation's Now Generation Network of young African leaders.

The programme is only open to African nationals, and applicants apply through the host organisation of their choice, so each host's own vacancy page sets the final details.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 100,000 for the 12-month fellowship, executive-level work experience at AfDB, UNECA or ITC, direct mentoring by the head of the host organisation, and membership of the Now Generation Network.
requirements: National of an African country
Master's degree
At least 7 years of relevant work experience
Under 40 years old (under 45 for women with children)
Any additional criteria set by the host organisation
documents: Application through the chosen host organisation's vacancy portal (AfDB, UNECA or ITC), with the documents that host requests
opportunities.selection_process: Each host organisation runs its own recruitment and selection for its Fellow; the Foundation's page does not describe the stages.
opportunities.about_provider: The Mo Ibrahim Foundation was founded in 2006 by Sudanese-British entrepreneur Mo Ibrahim to promote good governance and leadership in Africa. It is known for the Ibrahim Index of African Governance and its leadership prize and fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a host and apply through its vacancy page linked from the Foundation's fellowship page: the AfDB 2027 fellowship vacancy, the ITC posting on the UN careers portal, or the UNECA programme notice. Read the host's criteria carefully before 20 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Only three or so Fellows are selected each year, so tailor your application to the host's mandate. Women with children have a higher age limit of 45.

opportunities.title: Newberry Library Long-Term Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders of any nationality can apply by 20 November 2026 for 4-9 month residential fellowships at Chicago's Newberry Library paying USD 5,000 a month.
opportunities.description:
The Newberry Library in Chicago offers Long-Term Fellowships for 2027-28 to scholars who want to spend four to nine months in residence working on a major project, such as a book, that draws on the library's collections. The programme is humanities-centred but open to any field.

Fellows receive USD 5,000 per month and join the library's weekly colloquium and fellows' seminar. Nine-month fellowships start in September; four- or five-month fellowships start in September or January. About ten fellows are chosen each year.

Non-US citizens can apply and the library issues the paperwork for J-1 visas, so African scholars with a completed PhD and a project linked to Newberry holdings, for example on the Americas, maps or Indigenous history, can compete.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 5,000 per month for 4 to 9 months of residence. Housing is not provided and visa fees are not paid; the library issues the DS-2019 form for a J-1 visa.
requirements: PhD completed by the application deadline (including defence)
Open to scholars at any career stage; institutional affiliation not required
Non-US citizens eligible
Project must make substantial use of Newberry collections
Continuous residence in Chicago for 4 to 9 months; no other fellowship held at the same time
Former Long-Term fellows must wait five years
documents: Project title and abstract (up to 300 words)
List of Newberry materials to be used (up to 300 words)
Two recommendation letters in English submitted via SlideRoom
opportunities.selection_process: Two rounds: Newberry staff first rate how relevant and unique the collection items are to the project, then an independent interdisciplinary panel of senior scholars selects fellows on research contribution, collections usage and viability. Notifications are sent in early March.
opportunities.about_provider: The Newberry Library is an independent research library in Chicago, open to the public since 1887, with major collections in history, literature, maps and the humanities. It runs a wide fellowship programme for researchers and artists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Newberry's SlideRoom portal by 11:59 pm Central Time on 20 November 2026 and have your two recommenders submit their letters there by 30 November. Applications cannot be edited after submission.
opportunities.notes: Generally only one Long-Term fellowship a year goes to a Chicago-area resident. The Newberry also offers one-month Short-Term Fellowships (deadline 4 December 2026).

opportunities.title: Youth Global Forum 2027 (Paris)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people aged 16-46 from any country can apply by 20 November 2026 for 30 fully funded or 40 partially funded seats at the Youth Global Forum in Paris (20-23 January 2027), after paying a USD 19.99 application fee.
opportunities.description:
The Youth Global Forum 2027 is a four-day leadership event in Paris, France, from 20 to 23 January 2027, organised by CGDL, a Canadian public policy institute based in Toronto. It brings together about 250 young people for keynotes, panels, workshops, policy masterclasses and guided visits to UNESCO headquarters and other institutions.

There are several participation categories. Thirty Fully Funded seats cover round-trip airfare support, a shared four-star hotel room, meals, workshops, visits and a visa invitation letter, and 40 Partially Funded seats cover everything except airfare. These are competitive, with a deadline of 20 November 2026; paid self-funded and admission-only seats are also sold.

The forum is open to young people from all countries and backgrounds aged 16 to 46. African applicants should note that even the funded categories require a non-refundable-looking application fee of about USD 19.99.
opportunities.benefits: Fully Funded: round-trip airfare support, twin-share 4-star hotel, meals, workshops, institutional visits, certificate and visa invitation letter. Partially Funded: the same without airfare. Paid categories: Forum Admission USD 399 (meals and programme) and Self-Funded USD 699 (adds accommodation).
requirements: Aged 16 to 46
Open to all nationalities and academic backgrounds
No prior experience required
Able to travel to Paris for 20-23 January 2027 (visa needs do not affect selection)
documents: Online application form with passport name, nationality, contact details and motivation answers
Application fee payment (USD 16.99 plus USD 3 processing, total USD 19.99)
opportunities.selection_process: Funded categories are scored on motivation and clarity of purpose, leadership potential and community engagement, relevance to the forum's themes, and global awareness. Paid categories are not competitive.
opportunities.about_provider: CGDL describes itself as a Canadian public policy institute that drives global change through dialogue, innovation and leadership. It runs annual youth forums in different cities, including Madrid in 2026.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the combined funded-category form on thecgdl.org and pay the application fee by card before 20 November 2026. Contact info@thecgdl.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: This is an event run by a private organiser and funded seats require a paid application fee; read the refund policy before paying.

opportunities.title: 10th Annual South Asia Conference 2027 (Dublin City University)
opportunities.provider: Ireland India Institute, Dublin City University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from any country, especially doctoral and early-career scholars, can submit abstracts by 21 November 2026 for DCU's South Asia Conference in Dublin (14-16 April 2027), with limited bursaries.
opportunities.description:
The Ireland India Institute at Dublin City University is calling for papers for its 10th Annual South Asia Conference, to be held in person at DCU's All Hallows Campus in Dublin from 14 to 16 April 2027. The theme is upheaval and resilience in South Asia, with ten sub-themes ranging from inequality, politics and economics to digital life, migration, ecology, law and history.

Abstracts are due by 21 November 2026, and successful applicants hear by 15 January 2027. Registration fees are modest, from EUR 30 to EUR 70, and a limited number of needs-based bursaries are available to accepted presenters.

Doctoral and early-career researchers are especially encouraged, and the call welcomes under-represented voices, so African scholars working on South Asia or on South-South links can take part.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present at an international conference in Dublin. A limited number of needs-based bursaries are offered to accepted presenters. Registration fees: EUR 30 (students in South Asia), EUR 50 (staff in South Asia or students elsewhere), EUR 70 (staff and independent researchers outside South Asia).
requirements: Research on South Asia related to one or two of the conference sub-themes
Doctoral and early-career researchers especially encouraged
Able to attend in person in Dublin, 14-16 April 2027
documents: Abstract submitted through the conference's online survey form
important_dates: Conference: 14-16 April 2027, DCU All Hallows Campus, Dublin
opportunities.about_provider: The Ireland India Institute at Dublin City University builds academic knowledge on India and South Asia, with a focus on the Sustainable Development Goals, and fosters collaboration between Irish, European and South Asian partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the online form linked from the conference page by 21 November 2026, choosing one or two sub-themes. Ask about bursaries once accepted; contact southasiaconference@dcu.ie.
opportunities.notes: This is a conference with a registration fee rather than a funded award; bursaries are limited and needs-based.

opportunities.title: A.S. Hornby Educational Trust Scholarships 2027-28 (MEd TESOL, University of Exeter)
opportunities.provider: University of Exeter / A.S. Hornby Educational Trust
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Experienced English teachers (3+ years) living and working in low- and middle-income countries, excluding countries without UK student visas such as Cameroon and Sudan.
opportunities.description:
The A.S. Hornby Educational Trust, together with the University of Exeter's School of Education, funds up to ten experienced English language teachers from low- and middle-income countries to take the one-year MEd in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL), starting in September 2027.

The scholarship is fully funded and is aimed at teachers who will return to strengthen English language teaching in their own countries. Most African countries are eligible as OECD DAC recipients, but Exeter cannot accept applicants from countries where the UK does not issue student visas, which currently includes Cameroon and Sudan. Applicants should be working teachers with at least three years of full-time experience.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees, a monthly living stipend and return international travel for the one-year MEd TESOL.
requirements: Resident in and working in an OECD DAC least developed, low, lower-middle or upper-middle income country
Not from a country where the UK issues no student visas (Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar, Sudan are excluded)
At least 3 years of full-time TESOL or related teaching experience after the first degree
Undergraduate degree equivalent to a UK upper second class or better
Not already holding a doctorate or a UK master's in TESOL, applied linguistics, English or a related field
No language test needed to apply, but English proficiency must be stated
documents: Online application form (31 questions) covering employment history, a supporting statement on an English teaching initiative you led, and your fit with the MEd
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted on the online form, shortlisted candidates are interviewed between 15 and 24 February 2027, and final decisions follow by early March.
opportunities.about_provider: The A.S. Hornby Educational Trust supports English language teaching around the world, building on the legacy of the lexicographer A.S. Hornby. The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university whose School of Education is well known for TESOL.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the Exeter award page before 22 November 2026. Shortlisted applicants are then asked for documents and invited to an interview.
opportunities.notes: Up to 10 awards. The guidance strongly discourages AI-written answers. Questions go to hassenquiries@exeter.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: CRG International PhD Programme 2027 (Barcelona)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to candidates of any nationality who hold (or will hold by September 2027) a bachelor's plus master's in biomedical or related sciences totalling at least 300 ECTS, or an equivalent degree giving access to a PhD in Spain.
opportunities.description:
The Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) in Barcelona has opened its International PhD Programme call for 2027. The call offers PhD fellowships in about 18 research groups, and each applicant may choose up to two labs. Successful candidates are hired on a four-year employment contract and must start no later than October 2027.

The selection runs in stages over the winter. Applications close at midnight (CET) on Sunday 22 November 2026, pre-selection results are expected by late December, an online panel interview follows on 13 January 2027, and shortlisted candidates are invited to in-person interviews in Barcelona from 23 to 26 February 2027, with travel and accommodation paid by CRG.

The call states clearly that it is open to candidates of any nationality, and applicants do not need to contact supervisors in advance. For African life-science graduates with a strong master's, it is a well-paid, structured route into genomics and biomedical research at a leading European institute.
opportunities.benefits: A four-year employment contract with a competitive salary set under Spanish rules (no figure published), health and occupational insurance and Social Security coverage. Travel and accommodation for the in-person interviews in Barcelona are covered. Up to 5 fellowships are funded by the Spanish research agency (MICIU/AEI) and FSE+; the others are funded by the labs.
requirements: Any nationality

Bachelor's plus master's in biomedical or related sciences in the European Higher Education Area totalling at least 300 ECTS, or an equivalent degree allowing PhD access in Spain (degree may be completed by September/October 2027)
Excellent academic record and research experience
High working level of English
Not eligible if previously invited to a CRG PhD interview, if your master's was done at CRG, or if you worked at CRG for more than 3 months before the deadline
documents: Online application form (education, transcripts, awards, research experience and interests)
Academic transcripts (translated if not in Catalan, Spanish or English)
Proof of master's enrolment if the master's transcript is not yet available
Two reference letters, which must be submitted in the system before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are pre-selected on the record, the references and fit with the chosen labs. Pre-selected candidates have an online panel interview, and the strongest are invited to in-person interviews with the groups in Barcelona.
important_dates: In-person interviews in Barcelona: 23 to 26 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The CRG is a biomedical research centre of excellence in Barcelona, with international research teams working on genomics, systems biology and related fields, supported by shared core technology facilities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply once through the CRG recruitment portal for the 2027 PhD call, choosing up to two labs and uploading your documents. Make sure both referees have submitted their letters before the deadline, as incomplete applications are not considered. The application cannot be edited after submission, so check it carefully first; questions go to training@crg.eu.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per person is allowed. The FAQ PDF on the call page answers common questions about degrees and documents. CRG also hosts other PhD funding schemes such as INPhINIT 'la Caixa' fellowships.

opportunities.title: Medical University of Vienna PhD Programme: Autumn Call 2026/27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a completed master's-level university degree in a relevant field and two academic referees can apply for funded PhD positions at MedUni Wien.
opportunities.description:
The Medical University of Vienna recruits doctoral researchers for its PhD programme (UN094) through an annual autumn call. In the 2026/27 call, applicants can rank up to three advertised PhD positions; the application period ran from 5 October and closes at 23:55 Austrian time on 22 November 2026.

Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online on 9 to 11 December 2026 and then invited for a campus visit in Vienna on 26 to 28 January 2027. Start dates are flexible. Successful candidates are employed as scientific staff under the Austrian universities' collective agreement. If this round is missed, a Spring Call 2027 runs from 16 March to 23 April 2027.

The call is run in English and the pages read state no nationality restriction, so it is a realistic option for African graduates in medicine, biomedical sciences and medical technology who want a salaried PhD in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Employment as a scientific employee under the collective agreement (salary level B1, 30 hours a week), paid as twelve monthly salaries plus special payments in March, June, September and November, with 25 days of paid leave. The exact amount is not published on the page, and the page notes that admission alone does not guarantee full funding: funding depends on the project.
requirements: Completed university degree(s) with official final certificates
Official transcripts with grades
Application written in English
Two academic referees at principal scientist, group leader or lecturer level or above
documents: Degree certificates (translated if not in English or German)
Transcripts (translated if not in English, German or French)
Contact details of two academic referees
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through a three-step evaluation weighted about 70% on academic performance and 30% on non-academic qualities. Shortlisted candidates have an online interview and then an on-campus interview during the visit week.
important_dates: Application period: 5 October to 22 November 2026 (23:55 CET)
opportunities.about_provider: MedUni Wien is one of Europe's largest medical universities and research institutions, located in Vienna's 9th district. Its PhD programme offers doctoral training across clinical, biomedical and medical-technology research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose up to three open PhD positions on MedUni Wien's open-positions list and apply through the online portal before the deadline, uploading each document as a PDF of up to 20 MB. Questions about the call go to phdrecruitment@meduniwien.ac.at.
opportunities.notes: Unsolicited applications directly to supervisors outside the call are also accepted. The next autumn call (2027/28) is planned for 15 October to 19 November 2027.

opportunities.title: Science Tokyo IGP(A) Fall 2027 with MEXT University-Recommended Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Japanese applicants with a confirmed Science Tokyo supervisor can apply by 22 November 2026 for Fall 2027 integrated doctoral study with possible university-recommended MEXT funding.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Science Tokyo runs the International Graduate Program (IGP) A, an English-taught route into its master's and integrated doctoral programmes starting in Fall 2027. A limited number of outstanding applicants to the Integrated Doctoral Programme can be recommended by the university for a Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship.

The institute was formed on 1 October 2024 by merging Tokyo Institute of Technology and Tokyo Medical and Dental University, and IGP(A) covers 14 departments across five programmes. Integrated doctoral study (master's plus doctorate) takes three to five years in Tokyo. Several students per department may be nominated for MEXT; overseas applicants can also apply for a six-month JASSO grant.

The application deadline is 22 November 2026, but applicants must first obtain a consent letter from a Science Tokyo faculty member who agrees to supervise them, and the consent-letter deadline (15 November 2026) has passed, so only applicants who already secured one can still apply this round.
opportunities.benefits: MEXT scholars receive the Japanese Government scholarship (amount set by MEXT) and do not pay the JPY 30,000 application fee. Other overseas applicants may receive a JASSO grant of JPY 48,000 per month for six months (October 2027 to March 2028). Regular fees are JPY 282,000 enrolment and JPY 635,400 tuition per year.
requirements: Not a Japanese citizen (for MEXT)
16 years of schooling outside Japan, or an equivalent route (a bachelor's after 3+ years at a non-Japanese university or 15 years plus individual assessment, by prior arrangement)
Applying to the Integrated Doctoral Programme for the MEXT route
Outstanding academic record
Consent letter from a Science Tokyo faculty member who will be your supervisor
English proficiency evidence for the MEXT application
documents: Evaluation sheet and recommendation from your current supervisor
Consent letter from your intended Science Tokyo supervisor
MEXT scholarship form, dean's recommendation letter and English proficiency proof
opportunities.selection_process: Each department screens applications and selects successful candidates and MEXT nominees. Results are released on 3 March 2027; MEXT nominees learn of their nomination in mid-March and of the final MEXT decision by early August 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of Science Tokyo is a national university in Tokyo created in 2024 from Tokyo Tech and Tokyo Medical and Dental University. It is one of Japan's leading institutions for science, engineering and medicine.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email a prospective supervisor and obtain their consent letter, send it to the Admissions Division, then use the URL and password you receive to apply online and submit documents by 22 November 2026. Apply for MEXT through the separate scholarship form in the same window.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are rejected. If you missed the consent-letter deadline, contact inquiries.int.grad.se@adm.isct.ac.jp and plan for the next intake.

opportunities.title: Tarbell Fellowship in AI Journalism 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and subject experts aged 18 or over by 7 June 2027 can apply by 22 November 2026, but the programme mainly suits people already allowed to work in the US, UK or Hong Kong.
opportunities.description:
The Tarbell Fellowship is a one-year, paid programme that turns journalists and people with deep subject knowledge into reporters who cover artificial intelligence. Fellows first follow a three-month remote training course, then meet in person for a week-long summit, and finally spend nine months working as a reporter inside one of the programme's partner newsrooms.

The 2027-28 cohort trains remotely from 7 June to 6 August 2027, attends the summit planned for 16 to 20 August 2027 (dates still marked as to be confirmed), and works in a newsroom placement from September 2027 to May 2028. Partner outlets are based in the United States, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong.

No university degree is required, which makes the fellowship open to self-taught reporters and specialists moving into journalism. African applicants should note one important limit: the programme is aimed mainly at people who already have the right to work in the US, UK or Hong Kong, and visa sponsorship is rare and depends on the partner newsroom agreeing to it.
opportunities.benefits: A salary of USD 75,000 to 120,000 for the year, depending on experience and city; senior fellows with seven or more years of experience receive USD 115,000 to 135,000. Travel and accommodation for the in-person summit are fully paid.
requirements: Aged 18 or over by 7 June 2027
No degree required
Mainly for applicants with the right to work in the US, UK or Hong Kong; visa sponsorship is uncommon and needs a partner newsroom's approval
Able to complete remote training, attend the in-person summit and work a nine-month newsroom placement
Application must be written without AI assistance
documents: One to three writing samples (4,500 words in total at most, at least one in prose)
Short written answers on the application form
opportunities.selection_process: Selection runs in stages: the written application, a work test in December 2026 and January 2027, and then interviews with Tarbell and with partner newsrooms in January and February 2027. Applicants are told by the end of December whether they move to stage two, and fellows are chosen in late March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Tarbell Center for AI Journalism is a US-based nonprofit that supports reporting on artificial intelligence. It trains fellows and places them with partner news organisations in the US, UK and Hong Kong.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked from the fellowship page, attaching your CV and writing samples and answering the short questions. Do not use AI tools to draft any part of the application. Shortlisted applicants then complete a work test and interviews.
opportunities.notes: Only two days remain before the deadline. Applicants without existing work rights in the US, UK or Hong Kong should read the visa note carefully before applying.

opportunities.title: Birkbeck International Excellence Scholarship (January 2027 intake)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international students resident in eligible countries, including many in Africa, with an unconditional offer for a full-time January 2027 postgraduate programme.
opportunities.description:
Birkbeck, University of London offers the International Excellence Scholarship to self-funding international students starting a full-time postgraduate programme in January 2027. It is a fee discount of £3,000 rather than a full scholarship, so winners still pay the rest of their tuition and cover their own living, travel and visa costs.

The award is open to students who are ordinarily resident in a long list of countries and territories, which includes many African countries such as Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Selection is based on a personal statement, which makes it a realistic option for applicants who already hold an unconditional offer and can fund most of their studies in London.
opportunities.benefits: £3,000 taken off the tuition fee. It does not cover the remaining fees, living costs, travel or visa costs.

Evidence of funding for the remaining tuition

opportunities.how_to_apply: First obtain an unconditional offer for a January 2027 full-time postgraduate programme. Then complete Birkbeck's online scholarship form for your region (linked from the official page) with your personal statement before the round 2 deadline.
opportunities.notes: Birkbeck runs separate scholarships for other regions (for example the Global Future and Vice-Chancellor's International awards), which are not open to African residents.

opportunities.title: CFA Institute Access Scholarship (August 2027 exam window)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Candidates worldwide with financial need who meet CFA Program registration rules may apply by 23 November 2026 for a reduced exam fee in the August 2027 window.
opportunities.description:
The CFA Institute Access Scholarship lowers the cost of sitting the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) exams for candidates who could not otherwise afford the full programme fees. This round is for the August 2027 exam window and is open to candidates at Level I, Level II or Level III.

The CFA charter is one of the most widely recognised qualifications in investment management, financial analysis and banking. The exams are taken at testing centres during set windows, and the scholarship replaces the normal registration fee with a much lower one.

For African graduates and young professionals in finance, where exam fees can be a real barrier, this is a practical way to start or continue the CFA Program. The application window is short, so applicants should act quickly.
opportunities.benefits: The registration fee for the chosen exam is reduced to 400 USD (plus any applicable tax). Awards made from 4 March 2026 come under the Premium package, which includes the Practice Pack. The award does not cover the one-time enrolment fee unless the page says so, and it is valid for one exam cycle only.
requirements: Must meet the standard CFA Program registration requirements

Applying for the August 2027 exam window (Level I, II or III)
Cannot be combined with any other CFA Institute scholarship
documents: Online application form on the CFA Institute scholarship portal (SmApply)
opportunities.selection_process: CFA Institute reviews applications and makes the awards. Financial need weighs heavily. Decisions are final.
important_dates: Next window (November 2027 exam): 9 February to 2 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: CFA Institute is the global, not-for-profit association of investment professionals that awards the Chartered Financial Analyst designation. It sets the CFA curriculum and exams and runs several scholarship schemes to widen access to the programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the CFA Institute Access Scholarship portal (SmApply), using a computer rather than a phone. A confirmation email follows submission; contact CFA Institute support if none arrives. Results are emailed about four weeks after the window closes.
opportunities.notes: If you win the award and then fail to register, schedule or sit the exam, you lose eligibility for future CFA scholarships. Paid deferral is not allowed, only emergency deferral. The number of awards is not stated.

opportunities.title: ICTP School on Synchrotron Light Sources and Their Applications (online, Jan 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scientists and students worldwide, especially from Africa, may apply by 23 November 2026 to a free online ICTP school on synchrotron light sources in January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The School on Synchrotron Light Sources and Their Applications is an online training school run by the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP). It is co-sponsored by the African Light Source initiative (AfLS2020), the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF), the LAAAMP project and SESAME, and several lecturers come from African institutions.

The school runs online from 11 to 22 January 2027 on Central European Time. It has three modules: the physics of accelerators and beamlines; how light sources are funded and justified in social and economic terms; and the most common beamline techniques used in research.

Because Africa is working towards its own synchrotron facility, the school is especially relevant to African physicists, chemists, materials scientists and science-policy staff who want to understand and use light-source science.
opportunities.benefits: There is no registration fee. The school is fully online, so no travel is needed. The page lists no stipend or travel support.
requirements: Interest or background in accelerator physics, beamline science or applications of synchrotron light

Application submitted through the ICTP e-applications portal by 23 November 2026

opportunities.selection_process: ICTP selects participants from the online applications. The event page does not publish detailed criteria.
opportunities.about_provider: ICTP, based in Trieste, Italy, is a UNESCO Category 1 institute that has supported scientists from developing countries for six decades through schools, workshops and research visits.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply for activity smr 4334 on the ICTP e-applications portal, linked from the event page. Questions go to the school secretariat at smr4334@ictp.it.

opportunities.title: International Blue Carbon Institute Fellowship (2026 call)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Blue carbon experts from any region, with applicants from Africa particularly encouraged, can apply by 23 November 2026 for a two-year USD 60,000 IBCI fellowship.
opportunities.description:
The International Blue Carbon Institute (IBCI), hosted by Conservation International, runs a fellowship programme that funds one expert each cycle to carry out a multidisciplinary project on blue carbon ecosystems: mangroves, salt marshes, seagrasses and kelp. The current call, labelled the 2026 cycle, selects one fellow for a two-year programme.

The fellow receives a USD 60,000 grant spread over two years for research, travel, equipment and publication costs, and may also be funded to attend the annual meetings of the International Blue Carbon Scientific Working Group.

Applications are welcome from all regions, and for this cycle the institute particularly encourages applicants from Africa, making it a strong opportunity for African coastal scientists and practitioners.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of USD 60,000 over two years for project work, research, travel, equipment and publication fees, plus possible funding to attend the annual International Blue Carbon Scientific Working Group meetings.
requirements: Open to all regions; applicants from the Global South and especially Africa are encouraged this cycle
Blue carbon expert or professional (typically an advanced master's or PhD and about 5 years of expertise)
A multidisciplinary blue carbon project proposal
Proof of employment or support from your institution
documents: Proof of employment or institutional letter of support
opportunities.selection_process: A committee of global and regional blue carbon experts assesses technical content, alignment with IBCI priorities, local and regional impact, and geographic representation. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed. One fellow is selected.
opportunities.about_provider: Conservation International is a global environmental non-profit. Its International Blue Carbon Institute acts as a hub for sharing expertise on blue carbon research and putting it into practice.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the application form and budget templates from the IBCI fellowship page, complete them and upload them with your CV and institutional letter through the upload link on the page by 23 November 2026. Uploads cannot be edited afterwards; email IBCI@conservation.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: Only one fellow is chosen, so a well-costed project with clear local impact is essential.

opportunities.title: Long Read Sequencing: Platforms, Approaches and Applications (course with bursaries, March 2027)

opportunities.description:
Wellcome Connecting Science runs a six-day residential course, "Long read sequencing: platforms, approaches and applications", at the Wellcome Genome Campus near Cambridge, UK, from 14 to 19 March 2027. It is organised by Mike Quail and Kim Judge of the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

The hands-on course is for clinical, industry and academic researchers and university students already using long-read sequencing or planning to, and no extensive sequencing experience is needed. The subsidised fee of GBP 982 includes accommodation and all meals.

Bursaries of up to 50% of the course fee are available on merit and are requested in the same application, which helps African researchers attend. Places are limited and chosen on merit.

No extensive prior sequencing experience required
Sponsor statement from a supervisor, line manager or head of department
Able to attend in person in the UK (visitor visa if needed)
documents: Online application form (including bursary request and justification)
Sponsor statement as a PDF from your supervisor or manager

Course: 14-19 March 2027, Wellcome Genome Campus, UK
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome Connecting Science is the training and events arm of the Wellcome Sanger Institute on the Wellcome Genome Campus, funded by Wellcome. It runs courses and conferences in genomics and biomedical science for scientists worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the course's online applicant portal by 23:59 GMT on 23 November 2026, tick the bursary option and explain your need, and upload your sponsor's statement as a PDF. Applications without it are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Visa letters are available on request. Contact events@sanger.ac.uk with questions.

opportunities.title: PhD Scholarship: Generative AI and Workers' Freedom of Association in Southeast Asia

Foundations in machine learning and AI
Strong linear algebra, probability, statistics and optimisation
Research experience in ML/AI and skills in Python and PyTorch
documents: CV showing the required technical skills

opportunities.about_provider: The University of Sydney is Australia's oldest university and a leading research institution. Its Business School hosts the ARC project behind this scholarship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact the project supervisors, apply for PhD admission at the Business School, and submit the scholarship application form SC5995 linked from the official page before 23 November 2026.

opportunities.title: TWAS Research Professors in Least Developed Countries 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Institutions in least developed countries can apply by 23 November 2026 to have a TWAS Fellow, Young Affiliate or alumnus appointed as a visiting research professor for one year, with short visits paid by TWAS.
opportunities.description:
Through this scheme, TWAS appoints distinguished scientists as TWAS Research Professors at institutions in least developed countries (LDCs) for one year. During the appointment the professor visits the host institution for two to four weeks to give lectures, advise on research and work with local scientists.

The request comes from the institution or research group in the LDC, which names the scientist it wants to invite. Only TWAS Fellows (members) and TWAS Young Affiliates or alumni can be appointed, and the scheme covers the natural sciences.

Many African countries are classed as LDCs, so their universities can use this programme to bring an internationally known scientist to strengthen teaching and research at no travel cost to them.
opportunities.benefits: TWAS pays the professor's economy-class round-trip travel and related travel costs, plus an honorarium (amount not stated). The host institution covers local and living costs during the visit.
requirements: Host must be an institution or research group in a least developed country
The appointee must be a TWAS Fellow or a TWAS Young Affiliate or alumnus
Appointee must hold a PhD
Natural sciences
No age limit
Only one TWAS or OWSD programme application per calendar year
documents: Online application form completed by the host institution (further documents as requested in the form)
opportunities.selection_process: TWAS reviews the requests submitted through its online form; the page does not describe the selection steps in detail.
important_dates: Visit length: two to four weeks
opportunities.about_provider: The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS), based on the ICTP campus in Trieste, Italy, works to advance science in developing countries through fellowships, exchanges, grants and prizes. It operates under UNESCO's administration.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The LDC host institution completes the online TWAS form naming the scientist it wishes to appoint and submits it before 23 November 2026. Questions go to exchanges@twas.org.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is only three days away. Applicants may apply to only one TWAS or OWSD programme per calendar year.

opportunities.title: TWAS Visiting Expert Programme 2027

For African universities and research groups, this is a low-cost way to get expert input on a research programme, set up new collaborations and train young researchers locally. TWAS particularly welcomes nominations of women scientists.
opportunities.benefits: TWAS pays the most direct economy-class round-trip travel for the visiting expert. The host institution covers local costs during the visit.

Natural sciences other than physics and mathematics
Visit of two to four weeks

Supporting statement from the head of the host institution (template in the form)

opportunities.title: WHO Europe Summer School 2027: Systems Thinking for NCD Prevention and Healthy Ageing (Nice)
opportunities.provider: WHO Regional Office for Europe / Université Côte d'Azur
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and early to mid-career health professionals can apply by 23 November 2026 for a free WHO Europe summer school on NCD prevention and healthy ageing in Nice (20-23 July 2027); travel is self-funded.
opportunities.description:
The WHO Regional Office for Europe, together with its Collaborating Centre at Université Côte d'Azur and the Ulysseus European University, is running a 2027 summer school on systems thinking and innovation for preventing noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and supporting healthy ageing. It takes place in person in Nice, France, from 20 to 23 July 2027.

The interactive, project-based programme is taught in English to 30 participants and ends with a certificate of participation. It is designed for PhD students and early and mid-career professionals such as researchers, postgraduates, health practitioners and policy-makers.

There is no tuition fee and lunches, coffee breaks and a welcome dinner are provided, but travel and accommodation are not, so African applicants would need their own funding to attend.
opportunities.benefits: Free tuition, daily lunch and coffee breaks, a welcome dinner on 21 July 2027 and a certificate of participation. Travel, accommodation and other costs are paid by participants.
requirements: PhD student, postgraduate, researcher, health practitioner or policy-maker in early or mid career
Relevant experience in public health, innovation, healthy ageing, NCD prevention or NCD risk factors
Good English
Able to attend in person in Nice, 20-23 July 2027
documents: Online application form including education, experience and a personal statement
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are selected on relevant professional experience, education, their personal statement and their potential for future collaboration. Thirty places are available, with results by 18 December 2026.
opportunities.about_provider: The WHO Regional Office for Europe is one of the World Health Organization's six regional offices, working with 53 countries. Its Division of Prevention and Health Promotion leads this summer school with Université Côte d'Azur.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the WHO online application form linked from the call announcement by 23 November 2026, including a clear personal statement on your work in NCD prevention or healthy ageing.
opportunities.notes: Only 30 places; self-funded travel and accommodation.

opportunities.title: EMBL Conference: From Molecules to the Future of Predictive Biology (Peer Bork Memorial Symposium) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit an abstract by 24 November 2026 for EMBL's predictive biology symposium in Heidelberg (16-19 February 2027), with travel grants up to EUR 1,000 for those from outside Europe.
opportunities.description:
EMBL is hosting "From Molecules to the Future of Predictive Biology", a four-day symposium in memory of the bioinformatician Peer Bork, at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, from 16 to 19 February 2027. It is open to all and can be attended on site or virtually.

Researchers can submit an abstract by 24 November 2026 to present on site. Registration costs EUR 100 on site or EUR 50 virtually, and EMBL offers fee waivers, travel grants and childcare grants to those who apply by the abstract deadline.

Travel grants of up to EUR 1,000 for participants coming from outside Europe make this a realistic option for African computational biologists who want to present their work at a leading European lab.
opportunities.benefits: Financial assistance includes registration fee waivers, travel grants (up to EUR 400 within Europe and up to EUR 1,000 from outside Europe, possibly reduced) and childcare grants. Registration: EUR 100 on site, EUR 50 virtual; accommodation is not included.
requirements: Open to all researchers (academia, PhD students, industry, editors)
Abstracts accepted for on-site participants only (max 2,000 characters)
Financial assistance must be requested by the abstract deadline
documents: Registration and financial assistance request through the EMBL portal
opportunities.selection_process: Abstract results come about 21 days after the deadline. Financial support is judged on scientific merit, location, need and impact on the applicant's career.
important_dates: Abstract and financial assistance deadline: 24 November 2026
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL is Europe's life sciences laboratory, an intergovernmental organisation with more than 80 independent research groups. Its Course and Conference Office runs scientific meetings at the Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and submit your abstract through the EMBL event page by 24 November 2026, requesting a fee waiver or travel grant in the same portal. Contact events@embl.org with questions.

opportunities.title: IREX Community Solutions Program 2027 (USA)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Community leaders aged 27-39 with 5+ years' experience from 11 African countries (including Ghana, Kenya and Cameroon) can apply by 24 November 2026 for a fully funded 2027 U.S. professional exchange.
opportunities.description:
The Community Solutions Program (CSP) is a professional exchange of the U.S. Department of State, run by IREX, for experienced community leaders working on regional economic development. The 2027 application opened on 27 October 2026.

Selected fellows spend about three to four months in the United States, including a 12-week practicum with a U.S. host organisation from 9 August to 29 October 2027, framed by an orientation (2-5 August) and closing workshop (1-4 November). They then lead a nine-month SCALE-Up project back home.

The programme is fully funded, and eleven African countries are eligible this year, including Ghana, Kenya, Cameroon, Ethiopia and Rwanda.
opportunities.benefits: J-1 visa support, round-trip travel to the United States, a monthly living allowance, health coverage and accessibility accommodations during the U.S. programme.
requirements: Citizen of a listed country (in Africa: Botswana, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda or Uganda), living and working there
Aged 27 to 39 at the time of applying
At least 5 years of experience on community issues
High English proficiency (semi-finalists without TOEFL 520 take an institutional test)
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and no U.S. permanent residency application in the last 3 years
Eligible for a J-1 visa and committed to return home for 2 years
documents: Online application in English (with sector and training-track choices)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened for eligibility and scored by a selection committee; about three semi-finalists per placement are interviewed in English, and U.S. embassies give input.
opportunities.about_provider: IREX is a global development and education organisation that runs the CSP on behalf of the U.S. Department of State, which sets eligibility. U.S. embassies take part in selecting fellows.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the CSP application instructions and submit the online application at csp.irex.org in English before 11:59 PM EST on 24 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Prior U.S.-government exchange participants may be subject to a two-year home residency rule.

opportunities.title: University of Erfurt Thuringian State Graduate Doctoral Scholarships (start April 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with above-average results accepted as doctoral candidates at the University of Erfurt can apply by 24 November 2026 for a EUR 1,400-a-month state doctoral scholarship starting April 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Erfurt in Germany is offering up to four doctoral scholarships funded by Thuringian State Graduate Support for researchers joining its Erfurt Doctoral and Postdoctoral Programme (EPPP). Scholarships begin on 1 April 2027 (and no later than 1 July 2027).

The scholarship runs for three years and can be extended by one year, paying a monthly basic amount of EUR 1,400 plus family allowances and up to EUR 600 a year for research and travel. Applicants must be accepted as doctoral candidates by an Erfurt faculty or the Max-Weber-Kolleg.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African graduates with strong results and a doctoral project in Erfurt's fields, such as humanities, social sciences, education or theology, can apply.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 1,400 per month for three years (extendable by one year), plus a family allowance of EUR 300 a month for the first child and EUR 150 for each further child, and up to EUR 600 a year for research and travel costs on request.
requirements: Above-average academic results
Accepted as a doctoral candidate at an Erfurt faculty or the Max-Weber-Kolleg
Enrolled and a member of the Graduate Centre by the start date
Health insurance; no other funding for the same purpose
Outside work limited to 12 hours a week (research/teaching) or 5 hours (other)
documents: Project exposé of 6-8 pages with a three-year schedule
Recommendation letter from a professor, emailed separately
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are judged on research aptitude, project quality, grades, previous work, research potential, methodology and plausibility of the plan. Results are expected by the end of February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Erfurt is a public university in Thuringia, Germany, known for the humanities, social sciences and the Max-Weber-Kolleg for cultural and social studies. Its Research and Graduate Services office manages the state graduate scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email all documents as one PDF (max 5 MB) to graduiertenfoerderung@uni-erfurt.de with the subject 'Application for the State Graduate Scholarship 2026 - surname, first name' before the deadline, and have your professor email their recommendation separately.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not considered. Contact Ms Xiaolei Dong (+49 361 737-5042) with questions.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Sanger Institute Four-Year PhD Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a first or good 2:1 (or equivalent) from any country can apply by 24 November 2026 for fully funded four-year PhDs at the Wellcome Sanger Institute starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Wellcome Sanger Institute's Four-Year PhD Programme trains students in genomics and related biology at its campus in Hinxton, near Cambridge, UK, with degrees awarded by the University of Cambridge. Applications for the October 2027 intake are now open.

Students apply to the programme rather than to one supervisor, and spend their first eight months on three rotation projects before choosing a thesis lab. At least 12 funded studentships are offered, with a tax-free stipend rising from GBP 25,649 to GBP 27,385 a year and full tuition fees paid whatever the student's nationality.

International students also have visa and immigration health surcharge costs reimbursed, which makes this one of the most generous fully funded PhD routes open to African biology graduates.
opportunities.benefits: Tax-free stipend (from October 2026 rates): GBP 25,649 in year 1, GBP 26,228 in year 2, GBP 26,806 in year 3 and GBP 27,385 in year 4. Full tuition fees for funded students regardless of nationality, plus reimbursement of visa and immigration health surcharge costs for international students. No application fee (Cambridge charges GBP 20 at admission).
requirements: First-class or good upper second-class (2:1) degree, or an equivalent overseas qualification
Open to all nationalities for funding
If English is not your first language, meet University of Cambridge English requirements before admission
Two academic referees
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed on 25 January 2027 by two faculty members and a panel, in person with a video fallback. Studentships are awarded competitively after interviews.
opportunities.about_provider: The Wellcome Sanger Institute is a world-leading genomics research centre on the Wellcome Genome Campus, operated by the charity Genome Research Limited and funded by Wellcome. Its PhD students are members of the University of Cambridge.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the Sanger PhD online application with your transcripts and referee details before 09:00 GMT on 24 November 2026, and make sure both referees submit by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: You apply to the programme, not a specific lab, so show broad interest in genomics research. Contact the Postgraduate Programme Office on +44 (0)1223 834244.
