opportunities.title: HKU Entrance Scholarships for International Applicants (September 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to HKU for September 2027 entry are considered automatically for entrance scholarships of up to full tuition plus housing and living support, with priority evaluation for applications by 25 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The University of Hong Kong considers every applicant on its international admission route (IAS/NJ/DAS) for September 2027 entry for its entrance scholarships. There is no separate form; awards are decided alongside admission.

Top-ranking applicants can receive up to a full tuition waiver plus an accommodation scholarship and a living allowance each year. The scholarships are funded by donors, external bodies and government sources in Hong Kong and overseas, and are awarded on academic merit together with non-academic achievement.

HKU evaluates applications received by 12:00 noon Hong Kong time on 25 November 2026 in its first round, and continues to accept applications on a rolling basis until 25 August 2027. Applying early gives African applicants the best chance at the limited scholarship funds.
opportunities.benefits: Up to a full tuition waiver plus an accommodation scholarship and a living allowance per year for top applicants; other awards vary. For reference, non-local tuition is about HKD 250,000 (non-STEM) or HKD 280,000 (STEM) a year.
requirements: Applying for undergraduate entry in September 2027 with international or overseas qualifications
Strong academic results plus non-academic achievements
Meet the entry requirements of the chosen programme
An interview or test may be required for some programmes
documents: School results; final results are needed to confirm an offer
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic merit and non-academic achievements; some programmes interview or test candidates. Scholarships are considered automatically with the admission decision.
important_dates: First evaluation of applications received by 25 November 2026 (12:00 noon HKT)
Final application deadline: 25 August 2027 (12:00 noon HKT)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Hong Kong is Hong Kong's oldest university and a leading research institution in Asia. It also offers merit-based scholarships to enrolled students through its scholarships office.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through HKU's undergraduate admissions system for the international route and pay the HKD 780 fee. Submit by noon on 25 November 2026 to be in the first evaluation, which gives the best access to scholarships.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per admissions year is allowed and fees are not refundable. Accept offers within three to four weeks.

opportunities.title: HKUST University Admissions Scholarship for Other Qualifications Holders 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduate applicants to HKUST for 2027/28 who apply by the 25 November 2026 Priority Round are considered automatically for awards up to full tuition plus HKD 65,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
HKUST's University Admissions Scholarship for Other Qualifications Holders rewards top undergraduate applicants who apply with international or non-standard school qualifications such as IB, GCE A-Level, SAT/AP or national school-leaving certificates. It is part of admission to the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology for 2027/28 entry.

Awards are merit-based and assessed holistically. They can be one-off or renewable, and range from partial tuition waivers up to full tuition plus an allowance of HKD 65,000 per academic year, renewable for the normal study period if performance stays satisfactory. Schools or programmes may add top-ups within that maximum.

There is no separate scholarship form: applicants are considered when they apply for admission. Applying by 25 November 2026 puts you in HKUST's Priority Round, which matters for scholarship chances, and African applicants are eligible to apply.
opportunities.benefits: Up to full tuition plus an allowance of HKD 65,000 per academic year, renewable for the normal study duration subject to satisfactory performance. Smaller awards may be one-off or partial tuition waivers.
requirements: Applying for undergraduate admission to HKUST for 2027/28 with a non-local / 'other' qualification (e.g. IB, GCE A-Level, SAT/AP, national school-leaving exams)
Outstanding academic results
Meet HKUST's general admission requirements for your qualification
documents: School transcripts and qualification results as required for admission
opportunities.selection_process: Holistic assessment of the applicant's full profile; decisions are normally sent together with the admission offer.
important_dates: Applications continue to be accepted after the Priority Round
opportunities.about_provider: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology is a leading research university in Hong Kong focused on science, engineering, business and the humanities. Its undergraduate admissions office runs the entrance scholarships, with further support from the Scholarship and Financial Aid Office.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the HKUST undergraduate application through join.hkust.edu.hk/apply by 25 November 2026 for Priority Round consideration. No separate scholarship application is needed.
opportunities.notes: The 25 November date is the Priority Round deadline for admission; later applicants may still be considered but early applicants have the best chances. Ask the Scholarship and Financial Aid Office about need-based aid.

opportunities.title: International 2027 Early Acceptance Award (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with a January 2027 Westminster master's offer who pay a GBP 5,500 deposit by 25 November 2026 automatically get GBP 3,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The University of Westminster in London gives a GBP 3,000 International 2027 Early Acceptance Award to international postgraduate students who start a full-time master's in January 2027 and commit early by paying their deposit. The award is taken off the first year's tuition fee.

There is no application: eligible offer holders receive it automatically once they pay a minimum tuition deposit of GBP 5,500 by midnight (UK time) on 25 November 2026. It is a one-off award for new students on the UK campus and does not continue into later years.

For African students already holding a January 2027 Westminster offer, it is a simple way to cut costs by GBP 3,000, provided they fund their studies privately.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off GBP 3,000 reduction in tuition fees for the January 2027 start.
requirements: Holding and accepting an offer for a full-time master's starting January 2027 on Westminster's UK campus
Assessed as paying overseas (international) fees
Pay a minimum GBP 5,500 tuition deposit by 25 November 2026
Self-funded or funded by a loan you repay personally (not fully sponsored by an organisation that is invoiced)
Not eligible: PG Diplomas/Certificates, distance learning, research degrees, short courses, study abroad or partner programmes outside the UK
documents: Tuition deposit payment of at least GBP 5,500, or evidence of a loan application if exempt from the deposit
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: every eligible student who pays the deposit by the deadline receives the award.
important_dates: Deposit deadline: 25 November 2026, midnight UK time
Programme start: January 2027 (semester runs 18 January to 9 April 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Westminster is a public university and charity based on Regent Street in central London. Its second semester of the 2026/27 year runs from 18 January to 9 April 2027.
opportunities.how_to_apply: There is no application. Accept your January 2027 offer and pay the GBP 5,500 deposit before midnight UK time on 25 November 2026, and the award is added automatically.
opportunities.notes: It cannot be combined with other Westminster awards. Applicants for the competitive January International Excellence Award who pay the deposit in time receive this award instead.

opportunities.title: Milliman Opportunity Scholarship, Non-US Programme 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time undergraduates in actuarial, data, computing, finance, economics, maths or statistics majors who live and study in Canada, Ireland, the UK, South Africa or Australia and have a birth parent from a listed under-represented group can apply by 25 November 2026 for up to USD 5,000.
opportunities.description:
The Milliman Opportunity Scholarship Non-U.S. Program is funded by Milliman, a global actuarial and consulting firm, and administered by Scholarship America. It supports high-achieving undergraduates from under-represented groups who are studying quantitative fields outside the United States.

Awards are up to USD 5,000 and are not renewable, though students can reapply each year they remain eligible. Eligibility depends on the country where the student lives and studies and on the ethnic background of at least one birth parent: for example, students of African descent in Canada, Black African or Black Caribbean students in the UK and Ireland, and Black or Coloured students in South Africa.

For African students this is relevant to those already living and studying in one of the five countries, including South Africa and the African diaspora in Canada, the UK and Ireland. Financial need is not required; selection rests on academic performance and an essay.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 (non-renewable; students may reapply in later years). Paid in February, by wire transfer outside Canada.
requirements: Live and attend university in Canada, Ireland, the UK, South Africa or Australia

At least one birth parent from a listed group: Canada - African descent, Latino/Hispanic, Native North American or Pacific Islander; UK/Ireland - Black African, Black Caribbean, Irish Traveller or Romani; South Africa - Black or Coloured; Australia - Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander
Full-time undergraduate at an accredited institution
Major in actuarial science, computer science, data analytics, data science, economics, finance, mathematics, programming or statistics
High academic achievement
Enrolled for Spring 2027 (Canada, Ireland, UK) or the first semester of 2027 (South Africa, Australia)
documents: Current, complete official transcript showing name, school, grades and credit hours per course and term (grade reports not accepted)
Required essay on how the award would affect your academic career and goals
Optional essays on personal identity and heritage and on passion for your field
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarship America selects about 20 to 30 finalists based on academic performance and the essay; Milliman then chooses the recipients and award amounts, and may also consider leadership and disadvantage such as first-generation status. Financial need is not required.
important_dates: Deadline: 25 November 2026, 3:00 pm US Central Time
opportunities.about_provider: Milliman is a global actuarial, risk management and technology consulting firm. Scholarship America is a US nonprofit, based in Minneapolis, that designs and runs scholarship programmes for companies and foundations.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Click Apply on the Scholarship America page, create an account on its application portal using a personal email address, and upload your transcript and essays before the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Contact millimanopportunitynonus@scholarshipamerica.org or +1 507-931-1682.

opportunities.title: PVRI Early Career Travel Awards (supported by Bayer AG), PVRI 2027 Bangkok
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career pulmonary hypertension researchers and clinicians from any country can apply by 25 November 2026 for up to GBP 1,750 to attend PVRI 2027 in Bangkok.
opportunities.description:
The Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute (PVRI) offers Early Career Travel Awards, supported by Bayer AG, to help young professionals attend the PVRI 2027 Congress in Bangkok, Thailand. The congress is a major international meeting on pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary vascular disease.

The awards reimburse real travel and accommodation costs from a total pool of GBP 10,000, capped at GBP 1,750 per recipient under the terms and conditions. Non-members who win also receive a free year of PVRI membership.

There is no nationality limit, and priority goes to people who could not attend without support, which makes this a good fit for African clinicians and researchers working on pulmonary hypertension.
opportunities.benefits: Reimbursement of documented travel and accommodation costs up to GBP 1,750 per recipient (total pool GBP 10,000), paid by bank transfer after receipts. Delegate fees are not covered unless approved in advance. Non-members get one year of free PVRI membership.
requirements: Early career: within 10 years of completing a PhD or MD (excluding leave periods)
No tenured or senior academic post and no major independent research funding (e.g. grants above USD 100,000)
Actively working or studying in pulmonary hypertension
Demonstrable need for financial support
Agree to publicity, post-congress knowledge sharing and follow-up evaluation
One application per person; register for the congress within one month of notification
documents: Online application form (career level, years in the field, estimated travel and accommodation costs)
Receipts after the congress for reimbursement
opportunities.selection_process: Priority goes to applicants who could not attend without support, show commitment to pulmonary hypertension, show initiative and leadership potential, and will engage with PVRI beyond the congress. PVRI aims for fair representation across countries, disciplines, backgrounds and gender. Bayer has no role in selection and decisions are final.
opportunities.about_provider: PVRI is a registered charity in England and Wales (no. 1127115) dedicated to pulmonary hypertension research and care. It runs task forces and regional networks across the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the PVRI 2027 travel awards page before 09:00 GMT on 25 November 2026. If successful, register for the Bangkok congress within a month and keep all receipts.
opportunities.notes: Funds are paid as reimbursement only, so you must pay upfront. No individual feedback is given.

opportunities.title: Barts Charity Doctoral Training Programme 2027
opportunities.provider: Queen Mary University of London / Barts Charity
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least a UK 2:1 BSc (or equivalent) in a relevant subject can apply by 26 November 2026 for a four-year funded biomedical PhD at Queen Mary University of London starting autumn 2027; overseas candidates must cover the Home/Overseas fee difference.
opportunities.description:
The Barts Charity Doctoral Training Programme is a four-year PhD programme run by the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry at Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) with funding from Barts Charity. It trains future biomedical researchers whose work addresses health inequalities affecting the diverse communities of East London, and it recruits five PhD students a year over five years.

Students apply to the programme as a whole rather than to one project. After recruitment they choose a project from the programme's list, and they spend four years based in London with a tax-free stipend, research budget, conference travel funds and a laptop. The 2027 cohort is expected to start in late September or early October 2027.

The programme welcomes both home and overseas candidates, so applicants from African countries can compete. The key financial point is that the studentship pays tuition only at the Home rate: overseas students must show at interview how they will pay the difference to the Overseas fee for the whole PhD, as well as visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge.
opportunities.benefits: Tax-free stipend starting at GBP 28,700 a year with annual increases; tuition fees at the QMUL Home rate; research consumables of up to GBP 30,000 over the PhD; up to GBP 1,000 for conference travel; an additional research training and student experience fund; a laptop; eligibility to apply to the QMUL Postgraduate Research Fund. Not covered: the Home/Overseas fee difference, visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge.
requirements: At least a UK upper second-class (2:1) BSc or equivalent in a relevant discipline
A master's degree and research experience are advantages but not required
QMUL minimum English language requirement for the programme
Home and overseas candidates accepted; overseas candidates must fund the Home/Overseas fee difference for the full PhD
Only one Stage Two application per person (duplicates are disqualified)
documents: Stage One QMUL MySIS online application (course code RFQM-W6XF-09) with a personal statement typed into the form
Stage Two anonymised Barts DTP application form (Word template) quoting the 9-digit Stage One reference
Evidence of how overseas costs will be covered (if invited to interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through two stages. The anonymised Stage Two form is scored by a shortlisting panel, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in early February 2027. Candidates are judged on their potential to carry out or support world-leading biomedical research, as shown in the application and interview.
important_dates: Start: late September or early October 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Queen Mary University of London is a research-intensive university in East London whose Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry includes Barts and The London School of Medicine and Dentistry. Barts Charity is a health charity that funds research and care linked to the hospitals and communities of East London.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First submit the Stage One application on QMUL's MySIS portal for course RFQM-W6XF-09 and note the 9-digit reference you receive. Then complete the anonymised Stage Two form on the programme's online form, leaving identifying details out of sections 4 and 5. Questions go to bartsdtp@qmul.ac.uk; fee-status and visa questions go to QMUL Admissions.
opportunities.notes: Browse the published project list before applying, since projects are chosen after recruitment. Budget carefully: overseas students pay the fee difference, visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge themselves.

opportunities.title: Exeter Excellence Scholarships 2026/27: Postgraduate Taught, Round 4 (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International fee-paying students with a 2:1-equivalent degree and an offer for an eligible January 2027 business, computing or engineering master's at Exeter can apply for £3,000 to £10,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
Round 4 of the 2026/27 Exeter Excellence Scholarships is for international students starting a taught master's degree at the University of Exeter in January 2027. It offers first-year tuition discounts of £3,000, £5,000 or £10,000.

Only programmes in the Faculty of Environment, Science and Economy that start in January are covered: MSc Business Analytics, Business and Management, Finance and Management, International Business and Strategy, Marketing Management, Advanced Data Science, Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering Business Management and International Supply Chain Management.

The round closes on 26 November 2026, so African applicants who already hold an offer for one of these January courses should act quickly.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off first-year tuition discount of £3,000, £5,000 or £10,000. It can be combined with Exeter's country-specific postgraduate scholarships for certain Asian countries, up to £10,000 in total.
requirements: International fee status
UK 2:1 degree or equivalent (typically expected)
Conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible January 2027 programme
Must not have applied in Rounds 1 or 2 of the 2026/27 scheme for the same programme
documents: Personal statement of up to 300 words answering three questions on your ambitions, your contribution on campus and acting as an ambassador
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are based on academic merit plus ambitions, a clear plan, social responsibility and willingness to engage with the community. Applicants hear no later than 10 December 2026.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university and member of the Russell Group, with campuses in Exeter and Cornwall.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Make sure you hold an offer for an eligible January 2027 master's, then complete the Round 4 webform linked from the award page. Questions go to admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Postgraduate certificates and diplomas, apprenticeships and online programmes are not eligible.

opportunities.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship via Université Paris-Saclay (Master's, 2027-2028)
opportunities.provider: Université Paris-Saclay / French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students born after 31 March 1997 who are not already studying in France, applying to a Paris-Saclay master's programme for 2027-2028.
opportunities.description:
Université Paris-Saclay selects international master's candidates and submits their files to Campus France for the France Excellence Eiffel scholarship, the French government's top award for foreign students. For the 2027-2028 round, students must contact the coordinator of the Paris-Saclay master's programme they want to join before 26 November 2026, which is the university's internal deadline.

The university supports candidates across seven fields: biology and health, ecological transition, mathematics and digital sciences, science and engineering, law and political science, economics and management, and French history, language and civilisation. Successful master's laureates receive a monthly allowance for 12 months (second year of a master's) or 24 months (both years).

Paris-Saclay is one of Europe's largest research universities, so an Eiffel award here gives African students a fully funded place in a top-ranked programme. The PhD strand of the same call closed on 6 November 2026; this listing covers the master's strand only.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of EUR 1,200 for master's laureates, plus certain direct services provided by the Eiffel programme, for 12 months (M2) or 24 months (M1 and M2).
requirements: International student born after 31 March 1997
First Eiffel application, through one institution only
Not already studying in France
Not holding another French government scholarship
Polytech Paris-Saclay engineering degrees are not eligible
Dual nationals with French citizenship are not eligible
French language certificate if the programme is taught in French
documents: Transcripts since the first year of higher education
French language certificate for French-taught courses
Professional project (1-2 pages), optionally with an external reference letter
opportunities.selection_process: Programme coordinators and the university review the files and decide which candidates to support; only one application per student can go to the national jury. Candidates hear the university's decision by 7 December 2026, and Campus France announces laureates in April 2027.
important_dates: Contact the master's coordinator: before 26 November 2026
Campus France application step: from February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Université Paris-Saclay is a major French research university south of Paris that brings together faculties, grandes écoles and national research organisations. It receives, supports and forwards Eiffel applications to Campus France, which runs the national programme for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find your master's programme in the Paris-Saclay course catalogue (https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/en/education/deuxieme-cycle) and contact its coordinator with your file before 26 November 2026. If the university supports you, you complete the Campus France step from February 2027. Questions go to international.scholarship@universite-paris-saclay.fr.
opportunities.notes: The page lists the laureate announcement as "week of April 12th, 2026", which appears to be a typo for 2027. The PhD strand (deadline 6 November 2026) is closed.

opportunities.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship via University Recommendation: Ritsumeikan Graduate School of Life Sciences (September 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of any country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (including many African countries), born on or after 2 April 1992, with a CGPA of at least 2.30 on MEXT's 3.00 scale and English at CEFR B2, applying for the master's or doctoral programme in Advanced Life Sciences starting September 2027.
opportunities.description:
Ritsumeikan University is running an internal selection to nominate candidates to Japan's Ministry of Education (MEXT) for the Japanese Government Scholarship through the University Recommendation track. The round published so far is for the Graduate School of Life Sciences, covering the master's and doctoral programmes in Advanced Life Sciences, with entry in September 2027. The university describes the award as a full-ride scholarship, and the university's recommendation is the only way to be put forward for this scholarship by Ritsumeikan.

The window is short: applications are taken from 17 to 26 November 2026, and the first screening results are released on 24 December 2026. Candidates who pass are recommended to MEXT, which makes the final choice, with admission and scholarship results expected in late June 2027. Successful scholars arrive in Japan in mid-September 2027, and the fall semester begins on 26 September 2027.

For African graduates in biology, biotechnology and related life-science fields, this is one of the few MEXT routes still open for 2027. The selection guidelines say preference is given to applicants from MEXT's designated priority countries, and that list includes many African countries. Guidelines for the Graduate School of Science and Engineering may be released later, so applicants in other fields should keep checking the page.
opportunities.benefits: A full Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship, which the university calls full-ride; the exact monthly stipend, tuition and travel terms are set out in the MEXT outline document linked from the official page. There is no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan
Born on or after 2 April 1992
Good physical and mental health
Cumulative GPA of at least 2.30 out of 3.00 on MEXT's grading scale
English at CEFR B2 or higher, or most recent degree studied in English
Master's track: 16 years of education or a qualifying bachelor's degree; doctoral track: a master's degree or equivalent
Willing to newly enter Japan to study (enrolment as a non-degree research student is not possible)
documents: Field of study and research plan, written by the applicant (not AI-generated)
Recommendation letter from a dean or higher, addressed to the President of Ritsumeikan University (mandatory)
Official transcripts with an explanation of the grading scale
English test score taken within two years before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Ritsumeikan first screens the documents and may hold interviews. Candidates who pass this primary screening are recommended to MEXT, which selects the final scholarship recipients. Preference is given to nationals of MEXT's designated countries.
important_dates: Applications: 17 to 26 November 2026 (11:59 pm Japan time)
Final admission and scholarship results: late June 2027 (scheduled)
opportunities.about_provider: Ritsumeikan University is a private university in Japan with campuses in the Kyoto, Shiga and Osaka areas. It recruits international graduate students through several scholarship schemes, including MEXT embassy and university recommendation, the ABE Initiative and JICA programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the university's online application form, then email all the required files to the Ritsumeikan graduate admissions office (cger-bkc@st.ritsumei.ac.jp) by 11:59 pm Japan Standard Time on 26 November 2026. Read the Graduate School of Life Sciences application guidelines PDF on the official page first, and arrange the dean-level recommendation letter early, as it is compulsory.
opportunities.notes: Only the Graduate School of Life Sciences guidelines have been published for this round; Science and Engineering guidelines may follow. MEXT's own guidelines were expected to be finalised in November 2026. Previous MEXT scholars and people already receiving another foreign-government scholarship are usually excluded, so check the guidelines.

opportunities.title: EE HPC SOP 2027 workshop at HPC Asia 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and practitioners anywhere can submit papers on energy-efficient HPC practice by 27 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Energy Efficient HPC State of the Practice workshop (EE HPC SOP) is a half-day, peer-reviewed workshop, now in its seventh edition, held alongside the HPC Asia 2027 conference. It collects papers on how supercomputing centres and data centres actually manage energy use, cooling, power and sustainability in practice.

HPC Asia 2027 takes place at Yonsei University in Seoul, South Korea, from 17 to 19 February 2027; the exact workshop date is still to be announced. Topics include HPC energy management, cooling, digital twins of facilities and the infrastructure behind AI workloads.

The call is open to researchers and practitioners from any country. African engineers and researchers working on data-centre efficiency, energy systems or HPC operations can use it to publish practical work in an ACM-format venue and connect with the international HPC community.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of peer-reviewed full or short papers and a chance to present at HPC Asia 2027 in Seoul. No funding is offered; authors of accepted papers must register for HPC Asia 2027.
requirements: Full papers: up to 8 pages plus 2 pages for references and appendix
Short papers: up to 4 pages plus 1 page for references
ACM sigconf format, submitted as PDF
Open to authors from any country
At least one author must register for HPC Asia 2027
documents: Paper manuscript in ACM sigconf PDF format
opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind peer review, with at least three reviews for each paper.
important_dates: Abstract registration and paper deadline: 27 November 2026 (AoE)
opportunities.about_provider: The workshop is run by the Energy Efficient HPC Working Group (EE HPC WG), an international group of supercomputing sites and experts focused on energy efficiency, with Natalie Bates of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory as contact.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper in ACM sigconf format and submit it through the workshop's EasyChair submission site by 27 November 2026 (Anywhere on Earth).

opportunities.title: IXPUG Workshop at HPC Asia 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit HPC, AI and data analytics papers to the IXPUG workshop at HPC Asia 2027 in Seoul; travel is self-funded.
opportunities.description:
The Intel eXtreme Performance Users Group (IXPUG) is holding a half-day workshop at HPC Asia 2027, which takes place at Yonsei University in Seoul, Korea, from 17 to 19 February 2027. The workshop combines invited talks and contributed papers on high-performance computing, machine learning and data analytics on Intel platforms.

Researchers can submit regular papers of up to 18 pages or short papers of up to 10 pages in single-column format. Topics include application performance, accelerators, AI workloads and data analytics.

This is a publication and presentation opportunity rather than a funded award: no fees waivers or travel support are mentioned, so African researchers would need their own funding to attend.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are presented at the IXPUG workshop during HPC Asia 2027. No travel support, stipend or fee waiver is mentioned.
requirements: Original work not submitted elsewhere at the same time
Topics in HPC, machine learning, data analytics or accelerators on Intel technologies
Regular papers up to 18 pages or short papers up to 10 pages, single-column PDF including references
documents: Paper in single-column PDF following the HPC Asia 2027 format
important_dates: Paper deadline: 27 November (year shown inconsistently on the official page)
opportunities.about_provider: IXPUG is an open community forum of users and developers who share know-how on getting the best performance from Intel computing platforms. The 2027 workshop is chaired by Toshihiro Hanawa of the University of Tokyo.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the workshop's EasyChair submission page linked from ixpug.org, and register for HPC Asia 2027 if accepted. Confirm the exact deadline with info@ixpug.org.

opportunities.title: MPIIB-ISI International Summer Internship 2027
opportunities.provider: Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Enrolled bachelor's (after 4 semesters) or master's students in life sciences, from any country, can apply by 27 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The MPIIB International Summer Internship (MPIIB-ISI) is a three-month, voluntary research internship at the Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology in Berlin. Bachelor's and master's students from around the world join a research group, work on a real project in infection biology, and take part in a soft-skills programme designed to prepare them for future PhD applications.

The 2027 internship runs from 1 September to 30 November 2027. Interns receive a stipend for living costs in Berlin, help with travel costs and accommodation near the institute, so the programme is effectively funded for those selected.

The institute openly encourages students from low- and middle-income countries to apply, which makes this a strong opportunity for African life-science, medical, biochemistry and epidemiology students who want hands-on experience at a top European research institute and a stepping stone towards a PhD.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of EUR 1,400 to cover living costs in Berlin, compensation for travel costs, and accommodation close to the institute.
requirements: Enrolled at a university (needed for the visa)
Students without a bachelor's degree must have completed at least 4 semesters when applying
Strong academic record in a relevant field such as biology, medicine, biochemistry or epidemiology
Good English
Available for the whole internship, 1 September to 30 November 2027
No nationality restriction; applicants from low- and middle-income countries are encouraged
documents: Motivation letter on the institute's template (sections of 150, 150, 150 and 300 words)
Reference letter from a professor or postdoc
Transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate studies
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are pre-selected, shortlisted candidates have an online interview, and successful candidates receive an offer letter. No individual feedback is given.
important_dates: Final selection: February 2027 (if not contacted by 1 March 2027, assume you were not selected)
opportunities.about_provider: The Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology (MPIIB) in Berlin is part of the Max Planck Society, Germany's leading organisation for basic research. It studies how pathogens cause disease and how the immune system responds.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the application guide and project list on the MPIIB-ISI pages, then submit your documents through the institute's online job portal before 27 November 2026. Applications sent by email are not reviewed.
opportunities.notes: Credit points from your home university are not required. Check the project list and FAQ on the institute's website before writing the motivation letter.

opportunities.title: MRC North West Doctoral Programme in Medical Sciences (NW-DMS) Studentships 2027
opportunities.provider: University of Manchester and University of Liverpool
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international graduates with a first or 2.1-equivalent degree may apply by 27 November 2026 for funded medical-science PhDs at Manchester and Liverpool starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The MRC North West Doctoral Programme in Medical Sciences (NW-DMS) offers funded PhD studentships run jointly by the University of Manchester and the University of Liverpool, with funding from the Medical Research Council and partners such as NHS trusts, Bionow, UK Biobank and Evotec.

Students carry out a research project in medical science alongside structured doctoral training, based in Manchester or Liverpool. The 2027 cohort starts in October 2027, and applicants may apply for up to two advertised projects.

The programme is open to UK and international applicants, so African graduates in biomedical and health sciences can compete for a funded PhD at two major UK research universities. Competition is very strong.
opportunities.benefits: Funded PhD studentship with research training (the programme page does not give the stipend and fee amounts; check the individual project adverts).
requirements: First or Upper Second-class UK honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant discipline, or about to obtain one
Open to UK and international applicants
A master's and research experience are common among successful applicants but not required
Up to two project applications
documents: Online application for the chosen project(s)
Supporting documents as described in the programme's application guide
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed in the week of 8 February 2027, and awards are made in the week of 22 February 2027.
important_dates: Projects advertised and applications opened: 30 October 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Manchester's Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health and the University of Liverpool are leading UK research universities. NW-DMS is their joint MRC-funded doctoral training partnership.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check your eligibility, choose up to two projects from the programme list, contact the supervisors, prepare your documents and submit the online application by 27 November 2026, following the step-by-step guide on the programme page. Questions go to fbmh.doctoralacademy.admissions@manchester.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is close. Manchester also lists International Partnership PhD studentships and a Diversity scholarship on the same funding pages.

opportunities.title: Sabanci University Graduate Scholarships (Spring 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Merit-based full scholarships for applicants to Sabanci's spring 2027 thesis master's and PhD programmes in engineering, science and management.
opportunities.description:
Sabanci University in Istanbul offers merit-based graduate scholarships to students admitted to its graduate programmes, and its spring 2027 (2026-2027 spring term) admission round is now open. The spring round covers thesis-based master's and doctoral programmes in the Faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences, and the PhD in Management at the Business School.

Full scholarships waive tuition completely and add a monthly stipend, free dormitory housing, a transport allowance, health insurance and a laptop. A higher Distinguished Science and Technology PhD scholarship is also available.

The awards are based on academic merit and the pages do not limit nationality, so African students aiming for a research master's or PhD in engineering, science or management in Türkiye can compete for them.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarships (2026-27 figures): 100% tuition waiver; monthly stipend of 43,500 TL for master's students (10 months) and 67,500 TL for PhD students (12 months), rising to 75,000 TL after the PhD qualifying exam; free dormitory; 10,000 TL transport support; health insurance; a laptop. Distinguished Science and Technology PhD scholarship: 115,000 TL stipend and a USD 3,000 research fund after the qualifying exam. International tuition without scholarship is listed as USD 24,500 per year.
requirements: Admission to a thesis-based master's or PhD in Engineering and Natural Sciences, or the PhD in Management, for spring 2027
Awards based on academic merit
No nationality restriction stated on the scholarship pages
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on academic merit as part of the graduate admission review.
important_dates: Engineering and Natural Sciences (thesis master's and PhD) deadline: 27 November 2026
opportunities.about_provider: Sabanci University is a private research university in Tuzla, Istanbul, Türkiye. It offers graduate programmes in engineering, natural sciences, management and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for a graduate programme on Sabanci University's admissions system before the deadline for your programme; you are considered for scholarships as part of the admission. Check the graduate programmes and registration pages for the documents required.
opportunities.notes: Project-based scholarships (TÜBİTAK and industry projects) and TÜBİTAK BİDEB 2210/2211 support are also mentioned on the scholarships page.

opportunities.title: Swansea International Excellence Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Overseas students holding an offer for a Swansea University undergraduate or taught postgraduate course starting in January or March 2027 can apply by 27 November 2026 for a tuition discount of up to GBP 5,000.
opportunities.description:
Swansea University's International Excellence Scholarships give overseas students a discount on their first-year tuition fees when they start an undergraduate or taught postgraduate course in Wales. This round is for students beginning in January or March 2027, and it rewards applicants who have shown academic excellence or strong potential.

The award is worth up to GBP 5,000 off the first year's fees. Undergraduates who receive the full GBP 5,000 can get a further GBP 2,000 off their second year if they average at least 70% in their first year. The scholarship does not cover living or travel costs.

African applicants are eligible as overseas students; they apply using the 'Rest of the World' form, based on the country they have normally lived in for the past five years. Each student may submit only one application, and the full terms and conditions linked from the page set the detailed rules.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fee discount of up to GBP 5,000 for the first year of study; undergraduates awarded the full GBP 5,000 receive an extra GBP 2,000 discount in year two if they achieve an average of at least 70% in year one. Living and travel costs are not covered.
requirements: Overseas (international fee-paying) student
Holding an offer for an undergraduate or taught postgraduate course at Swansea starting January or March 2027
Evidence of academic excellence or potential
Apply using the form for your country of ordinary residence (last 5 years, not counting residence only for study)
Only one application per student
Meet the full scholarship terms and conditions
documents: Scholarship application form (Rest of the World or China version)
Proof of average score or GPA from your institution if it is not on the transcript
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic excellence or potential shown in the transcripts. The page does not state the number of awards or further stages.
opportunities.about_provider: Swansea University is a public research university in Swansea, Wales, and a registered charity (No. 1138342). It offers a range of scholarships and bursaries for international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First obtain an offer for a January or March 2027 course at Swansea. Then complete the International Excellence Scholarship form for your region (African applicants use the Rest of the World form) and upload your transcripts before 12:00 GMT on 27 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Read the full terms and conditions linked from the page before applying. Swansea's international scholarship advice page explains other awards for later intakes.

opportunities.title: Griffith Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship (Trimester 1, 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Australian, non-New Zealand students with an offer for a full-time Griffith undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree starting Trimester 1 2027 and a GPA of at least 6.0/7 can apply by 28 November 2026 for a 50% tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Griffith University's Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship rewards a limited number of outstanding international students starting undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees at its campuses in Queensland, Australia. This entry covers students beginning in Trimester 1 of 2027.

The scholarship pays half of the tuition fees for the full length of the degree, provided the student keeps meeting the conditions: passing every course each trimester and keeping a cumulative GPA of at least 5.5 on Griffith's 7-point scale. It applies to tuition only and cannot be deferred.

African students are eligible as citizens of a country other than Australia or New Zealand. Places are limited and the scholarship is withdrawn once the quota is filled, so applicants should secure their letter of offer early and apply well before the closing date.
opportunities.benefits: 50% of tuition fees for the standard length of the undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, applied each trimester by census date. Covers tuition only; other fees, living costs and travel are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand
New international fee-paying student with an offer by the closing date
GPA of 6.0 or above on a 7-point scale (or equivalent)
Meets all academic and English language entry requirements for the program
Full-time study starting Trimester 1 2027
Not eligible: research degrees, online, diploma, Masters Qualifying, MBA (5158), English language, Study Abroad, part-time-only or offshore/partner programs
To keep it: pass all courses and maintain a cumulative GPA of 5.5/7 each year
opportunities.selection_process: Applications that meet all eligibility requirements are reviewed by a university panel. Numbers are limited and the scholarship is closed once the quota is reached.
important_dates: Year 12-only applicants: apply by 21 December 2026, outcome by 24 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: Griffith University is a public university in Queensland, Australia, with campuses including the Gold Coast and Brisbane. It runs a range of scholarships for international students commencing coursework degrees.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your Griffith undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program first. Once you receive the Letter of Offer, submit the scholarship application with your academic records and a personal statement before the Trimester 1 2027 closing date. Accept both the program and scholarship offers by the date given in your Scholarship Letter.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship is non-refundable if you withdraw and cannot be deferred. Recipients may be featured in Griffith marketing.

opportunities.title: Biological Physics Summer Internship 2027
opportunities.provider: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's and senior bachelor's physics students worldwide can apply by 29 November 2026 for a funded biophysics internship in Dresden.
opportunities.description:
The Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems (MPI-PKS) in Dresden invites master's and advanced bachelor's students to spend a summer doing research in its Biological Physics department. Interns join one of the research groups led by Frank Jülicher, Fridtjof Brauns, Pierre Haas, Christina Kurzthaler or Marko Popović.

The internship lasts up to 90 days and the dates are agreed with the group leader. Interns receive financial support from the institute during their stay.

The call has no nationality limits, so African physics students interested in biophysics, active matter or the physics of living systems can apply for research experience at one of Germany's leading theoretical physics institutes.
opportunities.benefits: Financial support during the internship (the amount is not stated on the page).
requirements: Master's student or senior bachelor's student in physics or a related subject
Interest in biological physics
Enrolled at the home university during the internship
No nationality restriction stated
important_dates: Internship: up to 90 days in 2027, dates agreed with the group leader
opportunities.about_provider: MPI-PKS in Dresden is a Max Planck Society institute for theoretical research on complex systems, with a large Biological Physics department.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked from the institute's Biological Physics internship page before 29 November 2026.

opportunities.title: IEEE E-TEMS 2027 European Technology and Engineering Management Summit: Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit an extended abstract or a full paper by 29 November 2026 for the June 2027 summit in Trondheim.
opportunities.description:
The 2027 IEEE European Technology and Engineering Management Summit (E-TEMS 2027) is the sixth event in this series. It is hosted by the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering at NTNU and takes place from 17 to 19 June 2027 in Trondheim, Norway, with support from IEEE TEMS, IEEE Smart Cities and EuroPIM.

The summit invites research on technology and engineering management, innovation and related topics. Authors can send either a short extended abstract of one to two pages or a full paper of four to six pages, and accepted extended abstracts are later developed into full papers. Proposals for a doctoral workshop are also welcome early on.

For African engineers and management researchers, E-TEMS is a chance to present work at an IEEE-backed venue in Europe. The pages read show no travel funding, so applicants should plan their own funding.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation of peer-reviewed work at an IEEE summit. No funding or fee waivers were stated on the pages read.
requirements: Extended abstract of 1 to 2 pages, or a full paper of 4 to 6 pages
Submission should combine a synopsis, research design, related theory, main findings, validation and keywords
Submission through EasyChair by 29 November 2026, 23:59 CET
documents: Extended abstract (1-2 pages) or full paper (4-6 pages)
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are reviewed by the programme committee. Extended abstract authors hear back by 15 January 2027 and then submit a full paper, which is reviewed again before acceptance.
important_dates: Abstract registration and submission deadline: 29 November 2026 (23:59 CET)
opportunities.about_provider: IEEE E-TEMS is a European summit backed by the IEEE Technology and Engineering Management Society. The 2027 edition is hosted by the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) in Trondheim.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and upload your extended abstract or full paper on the EasyChair site for IEEE E-TEMS 2027 before the deadline. Those interested in the doctoral workshop should contact the organisers early.
opportunities.notes: The conference website still shows some old 2023 and 2025 text, including outdated "registration closed" notices; rely on the 2027 dates. Fees were not shown on the pages read.

opportunities.title: Summer@EPFL Research Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: EPFL School of Computer and Communication Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's (second year or later) and master's students in computing and electrical fields worldwide can apply by 29 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
Summer@EPFL is a research fellowship run by the School of Computer and Communication Sciences at EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland. Selected bachelor's and master's students spend two to three months working in one of the School's research labs, usually between May and September, with the exact dates agreed with the host lab.

Fellows receive a monthly living allowance and a refund of their travel costs, making this a funded way to gain serious research experience at one of Europe's top technical universities. The programme has been running for well over a decade.

No nationality limit is stated, so strong African students in computer science, computer engineering, telecommunications or electrical engineering can apply and use the fellowship to build towards graduate study abroad.
opportunities.benefits: A living allowance of CHF 1,800 per month (pro rata) and reimbursement of travel (second-class train or economy flight). Accommodation must be arranged and paid by the fellow.
requirements: Enrolled in a BSc, BTech, MSc, MTech or equivalent in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Telecommunications or Electrical Engineering
At least in the second year of the bachelor's when applying
Still enrolled during the fellowship
PhD students are not eligible
Excellent academic results
opportunities.selection_process: Competitive selection by EPFL faculty. Applicants choose up to three research domains and up to three professors; no recommendation letters are needed.
important_dates: Fellowship: 2 to 3 months, usually May to September 2027
opportunities.about_provider: EPFL (École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne) is one of Switzerland's two federal institutes of technology. Its School of Computer and Communication Sciences (IC) hosts the Summer@EPFL programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Summer@EPFL application website, upload your CV, transcripts and motivation letter, and choose your domains and professors before 29 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: Offers usually come 4 to 6 weeks after the deadline. The site may stay open a day or two past the deadline, but this is not guaranteed.

opportunities.title: Weizmann Outstanding Postdoctoral Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International researchers within 4 years of their PhD who have a Weizmann host can apply by 29 November 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Weizmann Outstanding Postdoctoral Program brings excellent international early-career scientists to the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel. It works in two steps: selected candidates first make a fully paid visit of five to seven days to meet potential host laboratories, and then go through the admission review.

Those admitted receive a tax-free Excellence Fellowship of USD 55,000 a year for three years. Candidates must start within four years of completing their PhD or MD, and must not already be a doctoral student or postdoc at Weizmann.

The programme is open to international candidates in all the Institute's fields, so African researchers with a strong PhD record can use it to secure a well-funded postdoc at one of the world's top basic-science institutes.
opportunities.benefits: A tax-free Excellence Fellowship of USD 55,000 per year for three years (paid in NIS). The pre-application visit includes round-trip economy airfare and accommodation on campus or in a nearby hotel.
requirements: International candidate not currently a doctoral student or postdoc at Weizmann
Starting within 4 years of the PhD or MD
Start date depends on submission of the PhD thesis
A Weizmann host PI willing to support the visit
documents: PhD certificate or letter stating the thesis submission date
At least two reference letters, including one from the PhD advisor
Letter of support from the Weizmann host

Application in English

opportunities.title: Berea College 100% Funding for Admitted International Undergraduates (Fall 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school leavers from any country with outstanding exam results can apply by 30 November 2026 for fall 2027 entry; every admitted international student receives aid covering tuition, housing, food and fees.
opportunities.description:
Berea College, a small liberal arts college in Kentucky, USA, gives every international student it admits a combination of financial aid and scholarships covering 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees. There is no separate scholarship competition: being admitted is what triggers the funding.

In return, all students take part in the college's Work Program, working at least ten hours a week on campus. Students pay their own personal expenses, and a deposit of US$2,200 is required before the college issues the I-20 form needed for a student visa; this deposit can later go towards some expenses, and the college can adjust it for students who genuinely cannot afford it.

Berea is unusually generous for a US college, which makes it one of the few realistic routes to a fully funded American bachelor's degree for African school leavers. Competition is intense, because the college admits about 40 or fewer new international students each year, and entry is only for the fall term.

Transfer places are very limited
