opportunities.description:
The Echidna Global Scholars Program is a six-month visiting fellowship at the Brookings Institution's Center for Universal Education (CUE) in Washington, DC. Each cohort brings together mid-career leaders from the Global South who carry out research on gender-transformative education, meaning education policy and practice that tackles the gender norms holding girls and women back.

The programme has run since 2012 and is funded by Echidna Giving. It has completed 14 cohorts and has 48 alumni from 25 countries. Applications for the 2027 visiting fellowship are open now and close on 1 December 2026.

Fellows spend their time producing policy research with the support of Brookings experts, then take it back to their own country. That makes the programme especially relevant to African education researchers, NGO leaders, academics and civil servants who already work on girls' education and want a global platform for their work.
opportunities.benefits: A six-month visiting fellowship at Brookings with research support and mentoring from the Center for Universal Education. The pages read do not state the stipend or other amounts.

At least 10 years of professional experience in research or academia, NGOs, community or civil-society organisations, or government
Background in education, development, public policy, economics or a related social science or humanities field
Substantial experience in and ties to a Global South country, with a clear plan to return there
Good command of English
documents: Research proposal of 3 to 5 pages on gender-transformative education
opportunities.selection_process: Brookings reviews the cover letter, CV, questionnaire and research proposal against the programme's eligibility criteria and its focus on gender-transformative education. The pages read do not describe interview stages.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Clinical Linguistics (EMCL) 2027

opportunities.description:
The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Clinical Linguistics (EMCL) is a two-year research master taught in English by a consortium of the University of Groningen, Ghent University and the University of Eastern Finland. It trains students in the linguistic, cognitive and neurological study of speech and language disorders, for the 2027-2029 intake.

Students move between the partner universities and attend an edition of the Science of Aphasia conference. A limited number of EU-funded Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover full tuition and a monthly allowance, and some scholarships are reserved for particular countries.

Graduates in speech and language therapy, linguistics, psychology, biomedical sciences or special education from African countries can apply for a fully funded European research master by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (limited number, up to two years): full tuition waiver and €1,400 per month for travel, visa, insurance and living costs. Self-funded students pay a consortium fee of €18,000 (non-EU) or €9,000 (EU/EEA) for the whole programme, which covers registration, administration, insurance, excursions, lab costs and one Science of Aphasia conference, but not books, housing or travel.
requirements: At least three years of higher education (BA, BSc or equivalent) in speech and language pathology, linguistics (at least 60 ECTS of general linguistics), biomedical sciences, psychology or special education

English: IELTS Academic 7.0 (6.0 per part), TOEFL iBT 100 (21 per part) or the new TOEFL scale 5/6 (4 per part), PTE Academic 71, LanguageCert 75, Cambridge C1/C2 or Linguaskill 185; tests no older than two years
Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted as proof of English
Previous Erasmus+ or Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders cannot get the scholarship
documents: Official transcripts and degree certificate (with translations if needed)
For linguistics backgrounds: transcript showing at least 60 ECTS in linguistics
opportunities.selection_process: A selection board ranks all eligible applicants, and offers with or without a scholarship are made from mid-February 2027.
important_dates: Application portal open: 1 October to 1 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: EMCL is run by three European universities with strong linguistics and clinical research groups: Groningen (Netherlands), Ghent (Belgium) and Eastern Finland. It is co-funded by the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the application form from the EMCL website and submit it with all documents through the EMCL portal on Formdesk between 1 October and 1 December 2026. Upload everything at once, because missing documents cannot be added later and English proof cannot follow after the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Finnish residence permits may require biometrics in a third country for some nationalities, so plan visa steps early.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Public Policy (Mundus MAPP) 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: Mundus MAPP consortium (CEU, IBEI, ISS Rotterdam, University of York)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of three-year social science bachelor's degrees with a GPA of at least 3.17/4.0 can apply; scholarship applicants must apply by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Mundus MAPP is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in Public Policy, co-funded by the European Union and run by a consortium of Central European University (CEU), the Institut Barcelona d'Estudis Internacionals (IBEI), the International Institute of Social Studies (ISS) in The Hague and the University of York. The 2027-2029 cohort is now recruiting.

Students study in two different countries, with at least 30 ECTS in each, following tracks such as CEU-IBEI, ISS-IBEI or ISS-York. The programme focuses on policy analysis and global and regional governance.

Top-ranked applicants receive full EU scholarships covering tuition and a monthly allowance. Applicants from many English-speaking African countries with an English-taught degree do not need an English test, which lowers the cost of applying.
opportunities.benefits: EMJM scholarship (limited number, for 24 months): €1,400 per month (up to €33,600) for travel, visa, installation and living costs, plus a full tuition waiver. Institutional scholarship: one per track, a 50% tuition waiver in both years, with no stipend. Health insurance is arranged by the consortium. Not covered: the study visit and winter school (about €600 to €1,000 each) and travel between home and the consortium countries.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least three years from a recognised university, preferably in the social sciences (natural science and engineering degrees are not eligible)
Upper second class (2.1) where applicable and a GPA of at least 3.17 out of 4.0, given on a 4.0 scale
Residence in a country other than those of your chosen track
Not already an EMJM scholarship holder

English: TOEFL iBT 95, IELTS Academic 7.0, Duolingo 130, PTE Academic 76 or Cambridge C1/C2, unless you are a citizen of a listed English-speaking country (including Botswana, Gambia, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Namibia, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia) with an English-taught degree
Work experience is preferred but not required
documents: Transcripts with GPA converted to a 4.0 scale
opportunities.selection_process: Each application is assessed by at least two evaluators. EMJM scholarships go to the top-ranked candidates on academic merit. Appeals are allowed only on procedural grounds, by 20 April 2027.
important_dates: Deadline for scholarship applicants and early self-funded applicants: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: Mundus MAPP is delivered by four European institutions with strong public policy and international studies programmes: CEU, IBEI, ISS (Erasmus University Rotterdam) and the University of York. The programme is co-funded by the Erasmus+ programme of the European Union.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Mundus MAPP online portal by 1 December 2026 if you want a scholarship, choosing your study track and including your GPA, English scores and motivation statement. Check the admissions checklist on the programme site before submitting.
opportunities.notes: Your country of residence must differ from the countries on your chosen track. Budget for the study visit, winter school and your own travel, which the scholarship does not cover.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Transfers-Fluids-Materials for Aeronautics Sustainable Applications (TFMASA) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mechanics or physics graduates worldwide with IELTS 6.5 may apply by 1 December 2026 for a fully funded Erasmus Mundus master in aeronautics.
opportunities.description:
TFMASA (Transfers, Fluids and Materials for Aeronautics Sustainable Applications) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in aeronautical engineering. It is run by a consortium of the University of Bordeaux in France, UCLouvain in Belgium and BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg in Germany.

Students start in Bordeaux, spend the second semester at UCLouvain and the third at BTU Cottbus, and finish with a fourth-semester internship. This call is for the 2027-2029 cohort.

African applicants fall in the partner-country scholarship category, which pays a monthly allowance and covers tuition and insurance, making TFMASA a fully funded route into aerospace, fluid mechanics and materials engineering in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship for partner-country students: 1,400 EUR per month plus 4,500 EUR per year towards tuition and insurance. No more than 10% of scholarships go to one nationality.
requirements: Bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) in mechanics, physics or a closely related field before the programme starts
English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 6), TOEFL iBT 93, CAE or CPE grade B/C, or a university letter confirming English-medium instruction; tests less than 3 years old at the start
Not a current or former Erasmus Mundus scholarship holder
documents: Europass CV showing your university's ranking
Transcripts and diplomas with certified English translations
opportunities.selection_process: Competitive review of academic record, motivation and potential, followed by interviews for shortlisted candidates in mid-February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The TFMASA consortium brings together the University of Bordeaux, UCLouvain and BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg, with EU Erasmus Mundus funding.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply only through the TFMASA online application portal linked from the programme's application page before 10:00 CET on 1 December 2026; email and paper applications are not accepted and late ones are rejected automatically.
opportunities.notes: The portal address still contains '2026'; check it is the 2027-2029 call before submitting.

opportunities.title: Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide 2027
opportunities.provider: OeAD (Austrian Agency for Education and Internationalisation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students, postgraduates, postdocs and researchers from universities outside Austria can apply for a 1 to 9 month research stay in Austria.
opportunities.description:
The Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide is a scholarship from Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation (OeAD), funded by the Austrian science ministry, that brings international doctoral students, postgraduates, postdocs and researchers to Austria for a research stay at an Austrian university or research institution.

Grants last between one and nine months and cannot be extended. All fields of study are eligible, and the aim is to strengthen exchange between Austrian institutions and researchers from abroad. For stays in 2027/28 the application deadline has been moved to 1 December 2026.

African doctoral candidates and early-career researchers who have a host contact in Austria can use this grant to fund a focused research visit.
requirements: Doctoral student, postgraduate, postdoc or researcher at a university outside Austria
Research stay at an Austrian university or research institution
Any field of study
Stay of 1 to 9 months (no extensions)
opportunities.about_provider: OeAD is Austria's national agency for international cooperation in education and research. It manages Austrian government scholarships, including the Ernst Mach programmes, and publishes them in its grants.at database.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the full conditions for the Ernst Mach Grant Worldwide in the OeAD grants.at database, then submit your application online there by 1 December 2026. Contact OeAD through its online contact form with questions.
opportunities.notes: The deadline for 2027/28 stays was brought forward to 1 December 2026, so do not wait for the old spring date. OeAD also runs an Ernst Mach grant for bachelor's and master's students from non-European countries at Austrian universities of applied sciences (research visits of 4 to 10 months, deadline 1 February 2027) and an Ernst Mach follow-up grant for former OeAD scholars from non-European developing countries (at least three years after the last OeAD-funded stay, deadline 1 February 2027). Full conditions for every OeAD programme are listed in the grants.at database.

opportunities.title: FINEC 2027 Financial Econometrics Conference (SoFiE sponsored)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit financial econometrics papers by 1 December 2026 (GBP 30 fee) for the 21-23 April 2027 conference at Lancaster.
opportunities.description:
FINEC 2027 is a joint financial econometrics conference sponsored by the Society for Financial Econometrics (SoFiE) and hosted by Lancaster University Management School in the UK. It runs fully in person at Lancaster University on 21-23 April 2027, with no online sessions.

The organisers invite papers on high-frequency econometrics, market microstructure, forecasting, asset pricing, volatility, fintech and blockchain, climate econometrics, machine learning and factor models. Keynote speakers include Torben Andersen, Oliver Linton, Roberto Renò and Viktor Todorov.

For African doctoral students and researchers in finance and econometrics, it is a chance to present to leading figures in the field and compete for a best-paper prize.
opportunities.benefits: The Lancaster Financial Econometrics Prize of £1,000 for the best paper. No travel grants are stated.
requirements: Research paper in financial econometrics or a related listed topic
Paper submitted as a PDF
Payment of the £30 submission fee
In-person presentation at Lancaster if accepted
documents: Flywire payment reference for the £30 submission fee
opportunities.about_provider: The conference is organised by Lancaster University Management School's Centre for Financial Econometrics, Asset Markets and Macroeconomic Policy (EMP) with its departments of Accounting and Finance and of Economics. It is sponsored by SoFiE, the international society for financial econometrics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pay the £30 submission fee through the Flywire link on the call page, then upload your paper and enter the payment reference in the conference's Qualtrics submission form by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The payment link's address refers to a different 2026 conference, so you may want to confirm it with the organisers before paying.

opportunities.title: Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme at Oxford 2027 (DPhil)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Candidates from any country who meet University of Oxford DPhil entry requirements and fit an EIT research project can apply by 1 December 2026 for fully funded doctoral study starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme funds full-time doctoral (DPhil) study at the University of Oxford for students who will work on research projects linked to the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT) in Oxford. EIT, founded and funded by Larry Ellison, works on science and technology for global challenges such as health, food security, climate and AI.

Applications for October 2027 entry opened in mid-September and close on 1 December 2026. Depending on the project, candidates either apply through the EIT portal (pathogen, MDLS, plant biology and economics projects) or through Oxford's own route (the AI and robotics centre for doctoral training, the generative biology doctoral training programme and correlates of immunity). Conditional offers and Oxford applications follow from January to March 2027, with announcements in April 2027.

The programme recruits from around the world and pays tuition and living costs, which makes it a strong option for African graduates with excellent records in the life sciences, AI, economics and related fields. The separate undergraduate Ellison round for 2027 entry has already closed.
opportunities.benefits: University of Oxford tuition fees, a living stipend (amount not stated), travel and conference costs, a technology set-up allowance and arrival costs such as flights, visa and healthcare. Packages differ for the doctoral training routes.
requirements: Meet University of Oxford DPhil entry requirements
Full-time doctoral study starting October 2027
Research interests aligned with an EIT project
Excellent academic record (EIT gives a GPA of 3.7/4 as an example of the standard expected)
Final-year students may apply
documents: EIT online application or Oxford application, depending on the project route
opportunities.selection_process: EIT looks for alignment with one of its projects, academic excellence, innovation, collaboration, tenacity and integrity. Shortlisted candidates receive conditional offers and complete an Oxford application between January and March 2027; final announcements come in April 2027.
important_dates: Conditional offers and Oxford applications: January to March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Ellison Institute of Technology is a research institute in Oxford founded by Larry Ellison to develop solutions to global problems in health, food, climate and AI. Its scholars programme funds students at the University of Oxford.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the EIT graduate research areas and pick a project. For pathogen, MDLS, plant biology and economics projects apply on the EIT Ellison Scholars portal; for the AI and robotics, generative biology and correlates of immunity routes apply through the University of Oxford. Submit before 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The undergraduate Ellison Scholars round for October 2027 entry closed on 31 July 2026.

opportunities.title: HKU Presidential PhD Scholar Programme 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The University of Hong Kong Graduate School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All applicants to full-time PhD study at HKU who apply in the main round (1 September to 1 December 2026) are considered for the HKU Presidential PhD Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The HKU Presidential PhD Scholar Programme (HKU-PS) is the University of Hong Kong's most prestigious funding package for new doctoral students. It is offered to selected full-time PhD students admitted for 2027-28 and combines a tuition fee waiver, a monthly scholarship, a cash award, a travel allowance and a guaranteed hall place in the first year.

Applicants are considered automatically if they apply for a full-time PhD during the main round, which runs from 1 September to 1 December 2026. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed. HKU also encourages applicants to apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme at the same time.

The package is worth up to about US$57,000 in the first year, which makes it one of the most valuable PhD awards in Asia for African researchers in any field.
opportunities.benefits: For 2027-28 admission the package is worth up to about HK$445,800 (US$57,150) in year one and up to about HK$428,300 (US$54,920) in later years. It includes a cash award of HK$40,000 in year one and HK$20,000 in later years, a tuition fee waiver of HK$49,500 a year, a postgraduate scholarship of HK$28,700 a month, a travel allowance of HK$14,400 a year and a guaranteed hall place in year one.
requirements: Applicant for full-time PhD study at HKU for 2027-28
Application submitted in the main round (1 September to 1 December 2026)
Meet HKU and programme admission and English requirements
Outstanding academic and research potential
documents: HKU research postgraduate online application with the documents required by the chosen programme (transcripts, degree certificates, research proposal, references, English test results if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: All full-time PhD applicants in the main round are considered. Shortlisted candidates may be invited to an interview.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Hong Kong is Hong Kong's oldest university and a leading research institution in Asia. Its Graduate School oversees research postgraduate admissions and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a supervisor and programme, then submit the HKU research postgraduate online application (linked from the HKU-PS page) by 1 December 2026. No separate scholarship form is needed; also consider applying for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme.
opportunities.notes: The number of awards is not stated.

opportunities.title: HKU School of Computing and Data Science Master Programmes Entrance Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The University of Hong Kong, School of Computing and Data Science
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to HKU's taught master's programmes in computing and data science for 2027-28 who apply by the main-round deadline (1 December 2026, noon HKT) are considered for entrance awards of HK$10,000 to HK$50,000.
opportunities.description:
The University of Hong Kong's School of Computing and Data Science (CDS) awards entrance scholarships to strong applicants for its taught master's programmes, such as the MSc in Computer Science, for the 2027-28 intake. Awards range from HK$10,000 to HK$50,000 and are given on academic performance, with an interview where applicable.

The main application round closes at noon Hong Kong time on 1 December 2026 and a clearing round on 30 April 2027. Applying in the main round gives the widest choice of places and awards. The school also lists other awards, including an International Postgraduate Scholarship for Computer Science for non-local students with an overseas bachelor's degree, and several HK$100,000 prizes for top students.

For African computer science and engineering graduates these awards reduce the cost of a one-year master's at a top-ranked Asian university, though applicants should plan funding for most of the tuition and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: CDS Master Programmes Entrance Scholarship: HK$10,000 to HK$50,000. Other school awards include the International Postgraduate Scholarship for Computer Science (full or partial, for non-local students with an overseas bachelor's), the Tongcheng Travel Scholarship (HK$100,000, up to three, CGPA 3.8 or above) and the QRT-HKU Excellence Prize (HK$100,000, up to four, CGPA 3.5 or above, full-time students).
requirements: Applicant to a CDS taught master's programme for the 2027-28 intake
Strong academic performance
Interview if requested
Meet HKU's admission and English language requirements
documents: English language test score if required
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are decided on academic performance, with an interview where applicable, as part of the admission review.
important_dates: Main round deadline: 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon HKT
Clearing round deadline: 30 April 2027, 12:00 noon HKT
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Hong Kong, founded in 1911, is Hong Kong's oldest university. Its School of Computing and Data Science runs taught master's programmes in computer science, data science and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a CDS taught master's programme on the HKU taught postgraduate admissions portal, pay the HK$780 application fee and upload your documents in the online admission system before the main-round deadline. Applicants are considered for the entrance scholarship as part of admission.
opportunities.notes: The application fee is HK$780 per programme for 2027-28.

opportunities.title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding graduates of any nationality seeking full-time PhD admission at one of eight Hong Kong universities.
opportunities.description:
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) was set up by the Research Grants Council (RGC) in 2009 to attract the best students from around the world to do a PhD in Hong Kong. For the 2027/28 intake, 400 fellowships will be awarded.

Fellows study full time at one of eight Hong Kong universities: City University, Hong Kong Baptist University, Lingnan, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Education University, Polytechnic University, HKUST and the University of Hong Kong. Each applicant may choose up to two programmes or departments.

The scheme is open regardless of country of origin, work experience or ethnic background, and it pays one of the most generous PhD stipends in Asia, which makes it a strong option for high-achieving African graduates.
opportunities.benefits: For 2026/27 the stipend was HK$344,400 a year (about US$44,150) plus a conference and research travel allowance of HK$14,400 a year (about US$1,840), for up to three years. The 2027/28 rates are not yet stated.
requirements: Open to applicants of any nationality, work background or ethnicity
Must seek admission as a new full-time PhD student at one of the eight universities
Outstanding academic record and research potential
Must meet the chosen university's own admission requirements
documents: HKPFS initial application (online) to obtain an HKPFS reference number
Full PhD application to the chosen university with the documents it requires
opportunities.selection_process: Two RGC selection panels (one for sciences, medicine, engineering and technology; one for humanities, social sciences and business) assess shortlisted candidates. The main criterion is academic excellence, followed by research ability and potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership.
important_dates: Initial application deadline: 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon Hong Kong time
University full application deadline: 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm Hong Kong time
opportunities.about_provider: The Research Grants Council operates under Hong Kong's University Grants Committee and funds research at Hong Kong's universities. It runs the HKPFS together with the eight participating universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First submit an initial application in the HKPFS electronic system to get your reference number, then submit a full PhD application to your chosen university (up to two programmes) quoting that number, both by 1 December 2026. Submit the initial application early because it closes at noon.
opportunities.notes: Note the two different closing times on 1 December: noon for the RGC initial application and 11:59 pm for most university applications.

opportunities.title: IAS School of Mathematics Memberships and Postdoctoral Positions 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at any career stage (postdoc categories within 5 years of PhD) apply through MathJobs for stipendiary memberships of one or two years.
opportunities.description:
The School of Mathematics at the Institute for Advanced Study (IAS) offers research memberships in mathematics and theoretical computer science for periods of 2 to 11 months, hosting about 85 members a year with support from the US National Science Foundation.

Categories include postdoctoral memberships for those up to five years from the PhD (one or two years), joint postdoctoral positions with DIMACS at Rutgers, Princeton (Veblen Instructorship) and the Bourgain Fellowship, Von Neumann Fellowships for those 5 to 15 years from the PhD, other mid-career and senior memberships, and a special-year programme open to all career stages.

The School encourages applications from women, minorities and mid-career scientists, and there is no stated nationality restriction, so African mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists can apply.
opportunities.benefits: The School offers competitive salaries, on-campus housing and other resources; Von Neumann Fellows receive a grant equivalent to a competitive salary, while some senior members receive limited support. Amounts are not stated.
requirements: Mathematician or theoretical computer scientist at any career stage
Postdoctoral membership: no more than five years from the PhD
Von Neumann Fellowship: 5 to 15 years from the PhD
Joint positions require applying to both institutions
documents: Application and supporting materials submitted through MathJobs
Reference letters (due by the same deadline)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute for Advanced Study is an independent research institute in Princeton, New Jersey. Its School of Mathematics hosts mathematicians and theoretical computer scientists at all career stages.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to the IAS School of Mathematics through MathJobs; all materials, including reference letters, are due by 1 December.

opportunities.title: IEEE CCGrid 2027: Call for Papers
opportunities.provider: IEEE / HPCC Lab, University of North Texas
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers in cluster, cloud, internet and AI systems computing can submit full papers (abstract by 24 November 2026, paper by 1 December 2026) to the May 2027 symposium in Dallas-Fort Worth.
opportunities.description:
The 27th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Cluster, Cloud and Internet Computing (CCGrid 2027) will be held from 24 to 27 May 2027 in the Dallas-Fort Worth area of Texas, hosted by the HPCC Lab at the University of North Texas and held together with ICFEC 2027 and QSys 2027. The call for papers is open now.

Papers are invited across seven tracks: hardware and networking; software systems; AI and machine learning systems; large language model and agentic AI systems; performance modelling; security and resilience; and sustainable computing. Accepted papers appear in IEEE Xplore.

CCGrid is one of the established venues in distributed and cloud computing, so an accepted paper carries weight for African computer scientists and PhD students building a research record. The organisers say student travel grants will be announced later.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted papers in IEEE Xplore and a presentation slot at the symposium. Travel grants are listed as 'to be announced'; no amounts are published yet.
requirements: Original, unpublished research in one of the seven tracks
Paper of up to 10 letter-size pages including references, in the IEEE conference template
Double-blind submission
At least one author must register and present in person, or the paper is dropped from the proceedings
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review by the programme committee, with decisions on 1 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: CCGrid is a long-running IEEE symposium on distributed, cluster and cloud computing. The 2027 edition is organised by the High Performance Cloud Computing (HPCC) Lab at the University of North Texas with general chairs from UNT, the University of Messina and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract on the CCGrid 2027 EasyChair site by 24 November 2026, then upload the full anonymised paper by 1 December 2026. Watch the conference website for the travel grant call, doctoral symposium and mentorship session.
opportunities.notes: Up to two extra pages can be bought at the camera-ready stage. The conference also runs a doctoral symposium and a mentorship session (see hpcclab.org/ccgrid27).

opportunities.title: IIAS - National Library of Israel Individual Fellowship 2028-2029
opportunities.provider: National Library of Israel and Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tenured humanities scholars at institutions outside Israel may apply by 1 December 2026 for a 2028-2029 residential fellowship in Jerusalem.
opportunities.description:
The IIAS - National Library of Israel Individual Fellowship is a joint residential fellowship in Jerusalem for the 2028-2029 academic year. Fellows divide their time between the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies at the Hebrew University and the National Library of Israel.

It is open to research in Jewish studies, Israel studies, Islam and Middle Eastern studies, music and the general humanities, with preference for projects that use the library's special collections. Fellows stay for ten months from 1 September, or five months from 1 September or 1 February.

The fellowship is for established, tenured scholars at institutions outside Israel, including senior African academics in the humanities and Islamic or Middle Eastern studies.
opportunities.benefits: A generous fellowship and subsidised accommodation (amounts not stated).
requirements: Established scholar holding a tenured position at an academic or research institution outside Israel
Not open to postdoctoral researchers
Research in Jewish studies, Israel studies, Islam and Middle Eastern studies, music or the general humanities
Able to reside in Jerusalem for 10 months (from 1 September) or 5 months (from 1 September or 1 February)
documents: Complete application materials (incomplete applications are not considered)
opportunities.selection_process: IIAS and the National Library review applications, giving preference to projects using the library's special collections. Decisions come within seven months of the deadline.
important_dates: Decisions: within seven months of the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies, founded in 1975 at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, hosts research groups and individual fellows. The National Library of Israel holds major collections in Judaica, Islam and the Middle East.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the call page to submit the online form by 1 December 2026. Questions go to iiassecret@savion.huji.ac.il.
opportunities.notes: IIAS also runs general Individual Fellowships and Research Groups for 2028-2029 with the same 1 December 2026 deadline.

opportunities.title: IIAS Open Call for Individual Fellowships 2028-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tenured academics in any discipline, from Israel or abroad, can apply for a 5 or 10 month residency in Jerusalem in 2028-2029.
opportunities.description:
The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem invites tenured scholars from Israel and abroad to apply for individual fellowships for the 2028-2029 academic year. Fellows spend time in residence at the Institute on the Givat Ram campus in Jerusalem working on an innovative research project in any discipline.

Residencies last either 10 months from 1 September or 5 months starting on 1 September or 1 February, within an academic year that runs from 1 September to 30 June. Two or three scholars working on the same project must each apply individually.

The call is aimed at established, tenured academics, so it suits senior African researchers who want an extended research stay at an international institute for advanced study.
opportunities.benefits: Fellows from abroad receive what the Institute describes as a generous fellowship, plus subsidised accommodation. Amounts are not stated.
requirements: Tenured position at an academic research institution (in Israel or abroad)
Not open to postdoctoral researchers
Former IIAS fellows may apply only 10 years after their previous term ended
An innovative research project in any field
documents: Online application form with personal details
Names and contact details of four international experts
Letter of intent of up to 1,000 words describing and justifying the project
Professional CV and full list of publications
opportunities.selection_process: The IIAS Academic Committee reviews applications and announces decisions within seven months of the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered.
important_dates: Decisions: within seven months of the deadline
Residency: from 1 September 2028 (10 or 5 months) or from 1 February 2029 (5 months)
opportunities.about_provider: The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies was founded in 1975 and is based at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It hosts individual fellows and research groups from all disciplines each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the "Apply Here" link on the IIAS homepage to fill in the online form, upload your letter of intent, CV and publication list, and name four international experts, all before midnight on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The Institute also runs an open call for research groups (5 to 8 core fellows) with the same 1 December 2026 deadline. Contact: iiassecret@savion.huji.ac.il.

opportunities.title: IIAS Open Call for Research Groups 2028-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars from any institution worldwide may propose a 5-8 person research group in residence in Jerusalem in 2028-2029 by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem invites scholars to propose Research Groups for the 2028-2029 academic year. A Research Group brings together five to eight core fellows, plus one postdoctoral fellow, to work on a shared question while in residence at the Institute.

Residencies last 10, 5 or 3 months, and the group works on the Edmond J. Safra Campus at Givat Ram in Jerusalem. Fellows coming from abroad receive what the Institute calls a generous fellowship, together with family accommodation.

Scholars from any institution in Israel or abroad may lead or join a proposal, so African researchers can take part as group leaders or members in a collaborative, internationally reviewed research project in any discipline.
opportunities.benefits: A residential fellowship in Jerusalem for each group member; fellows from abroad receive a fellowship stipend and family accommodation. Amounts are not stated on the call page.
requirements: Scholars affiliated with any institution in Israel or abroad may apply
Groups have 5 to 8 core fellows plus one postdoctoral fellow
Residency of 10, 5 or 3 months during the 2028-2029 academic year
Former IIAS fellows may apply only after 10 years since their last fellowship
documents: Pre-proposal with an extended abstract, a list of potential members and key scholars
Full proposal written to the IIAS guidelines and template (short-listed groups)
opportunities.selection_process: The Institute's Academic Committees draw up a short list. Each short-listed proposal is reviewed by at least three external referees. In recent years 40 to 50% of short-listed proposals were accepted.
opportunities.about_provider: The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies is an institute for advanced research hosted by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It runs Research Groups alongside individual fellowships and joint programmes such as the NLI-IIAS fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the online application link on the IIAS Research Groups call page to submit the Initial Form and pre-proposal by midnight on 1 December 2026. Short-listed groups then prepare a full proposal using the Institute's guidelines and template. Questions can go to iiassecret@savion.huji.ac.il.
opportunities.notes: The call and application pages give slightly different decision times (six or seven months), but both point to decisions by the end of July.

opportunities.title: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International high school graduates entering a direct-entry programme with a 90% average and demonstrated leadership can apply for a $25,000 entrance award.
opportunities.description:
The International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is the University of Manitoba's flagship entrance award for international high school students who combine outstanding grades with leadership. It is given to students starting their first year of an undergraduate programme in 2027/28.

Each year the university gives three awards: one worth $25,000 and two worth $10,000. The top award goes to a student entering a direct-entry programme (including University 1) with a very high admission average, while the two smaller awards are open to international applicants who meet the normal admission requirements and show strong leadership.

The University of Manitoba is in Winnipeg, Canada. African secondary school students applying for undergraduate study in Canada can compete for these awards by sending a complete admission and award application before the 1 December deadline.
opportunities.benefits: One award of $25,000 and two awards of $10,000 each, paid towards first-year study.
requirements: International student currently in high school
Applying to a direct-entry programme or University 1 and studying full time (at least 80% course load) in first year

$25,000 award: admission average of at least 90% over five of the listed senior courses (for example Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, English, History, Geography, Music or Visual Arts)
$10,000 awards: meet the minimum admission requirements for University 1 or a direct-entry faculty
Strong leadership and community involvement
documents: University of Manitoba admission application and application fee
One reference letter from a current teacher or principal (translated into English if needed)
Predicted or interim grades and transcripts (grades due by 1 March)
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisted applicants are ranked first, second and third using both the award application and the admission application.
important_dates: Complete application and documents: by 1 December 2026
Predicted or interim grades: by 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Manitoba is a research university in Winnipeg, Canada. Its Financial Aid and Awards office runs entrance scholarships for new domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission through the University of Manitoba's admissions portal and pay the fee, then complete the award application and arrange the teacher or principal reference letter. All parts must arrive by 1 December.
opportunities.notes: Contact: awards@umanitoba.ca, +1 204 474 9531. The university also lists other entrance awards and international student awards on its financial aid pages.

opportunities.title: International Nieman Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US journalists with five or more years of full-time experience can apply by 1 December 2026 for a paid year at Harvard.
opportunities.description:
The International Nieman Fellowship gives experienced journalists from outside the United States an academic year at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Fellows audit Harvard classes, take part in Nieman seminars and pursue a study plan of their choice, starting in mid-August 2027.

Fellows receive a stipend of USD 90,000 over nine months, with extra allowances for health insurance and child care. About two dozen journalists are chosen each year across all Nieman fellowships.

The international category is for non-US citizens, so African journalists with at least five years of full-time experience are strongly encouraged to consider it; no degree is required.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 90,000 over nine months, a health insurance supplement of up to USD 6,250 each for the fellow and a spouse and USD 3,750 per child under 18, and a child-care allowance of USD 10,500 (one child aged 12 or under) up to USD 16,750 (four or more).
requirements: Non-US citizen (including those working in the US)
Working journalist with at least five years of full-time media experience (public relations excluded)
Fluent English
No residential fellowship of four months or more in the past five years
No age limit and no degree required
documents: Profile (up to 100 words) and study summary (up to 50 words)
Four samples of published work (print or digital)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are judged on their essays, work samples and recommendation letters, and finalists have Zoom interviews.
opportunities.about_provider: The Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard, founded in 1938, runs the oldest mid-career fellowship programme for journalists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Nieman Foundation's SlideRoom portal by 1 December 2026 and ask your three recommenders to submit by 15 December.
opportunities.notes: Nationals of countries for which the US has suspended J visas are advised to wait unless they hold another passport.

opportunities.title: Ishibashi Foundation / Japan Foundation Fellowship for Research on Japanese Art FY2027
opportunities.provider: The Japan Foundation with the Ishibashi Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Curators, art researchers, educators and conservators living outside Japan, from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan, researching Japanese art.
opportunities.description:
This fellowship, run by the Japan Foundation together with the Ishibashi Foundation, brings art professionals from outside Japan for a short research stay in Japan. It is aimed at museum curators, researchers, educators and conservators whose work deals with Japanese art, with a main focus on contemporary Japanese art.

Fellows spend between 21 and 59 days in Japan and must arrive between 20 June 2027 and 31 March 2028. The stay is meant for research, such as studying collections, meeting artists and specialists, and visiting institutions.

The call is open to people living outside Japan who hold the nationality or permanent residence of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan, so African curators and art researchers can apply. It is selective: 14 of 75 applications were funded in FY2026. Applications close on 1 December 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Japan time.
opportunities.benefits: Round-trip discount economy airfare to Japan plus a stipend and allowances for the research stay (amounts are given in the separate application instructions).
requirements: Living outside Japan
Nationality or permanent residence of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan
Work as a curator, researcher, educator or conservator with a project on Japanese art
Good health and Japanese or English proficiency
Must stay continuously in Japan during the fellowship
Not applying for another Japan Foundation grant in the same year; project not for religious or political purposes
Past Japan Foundation fellows must wait three years
documents: Online application through the Japan Foundation portal (see the programme's application instructions for the full list)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed competitively by the Japan Foundation; 14 of 75 were selected in FY2026. Applicants are notified in April 2027.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 December 2026, 1:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time
Arrival in Japan: between 20 June 2027 and 31 March 2028
opportunities.about_provider: The Japan Foundation is Japan's public organisation for international cultural exchange, supporting arts, Japanese-language education and Japanese studies around the world. The Ishibashi Foundation is a Japanese foundation that supports art and culture and co-funds this fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the FY2027 application instructions for this fellowship and submit the application through the Japan Foundation online portal (apply.jpf.go.jp) before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Short stays only (21-59 days). Plan contacts with Japanese museums or researchers in advance so the research plan is concrete.

opportunities.title: Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Fellowship FY2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates and researchers in the humanities or social sciences from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who need to do research in Japan.
opportunities.description:
The Japan Foundation's Japanese Studies Fellowship pays for scholars from outside Japan to spend a period carrying out research in Japan on a topic in the humanities or social sciences. Researchers in the natural sciences, medicine and engineering cannot apply. Fellows must arrive in Japan between 20 June 2027 and 20 March 2028 and remain there for the whole fellowship.

There are two tracks. Doctoral candidates who have finished (or will have finished) their coursework can stay for 4 to 12 months to work on their dissertation, while researchers with a PhD or equivalent experience can come either for a short visit of 21 to 89 days or for 4 to 12 months. Every applicant needs an advisor or host in Japan who agrees to support the project before the deadline.

The scheme is open to citizens or permanent residents of any country that has diplomatic relations with Japan who live in that country, which includes African nations. It is competitive: in FY2026, 96 of 286 applicants were selected. Applications close on 1 December 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Japan time.
opportunities.benefits: Doctoral candidates: stipend of JPY 310,000 per month. Long-term researchers: JPY 400,000 per month. Long-term fellows also receive a settling-in allowance (JPY 250,000), departure allowance (JPY 50,000), up to JPY 50,000 for a health certificate, a dependant allowance of JPY 10,000 per person and up to JPY 25,000 in enrolment fees. Short-term researchers receive JPY 17,000 per day. All fellows receive a round-trip economy air ticket and overseas travel insurance.
requirements: Citizenship or permanent residence of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan, and residence in that country
Research in the humanities or social sciences (not natural sciences, medicine or engineering)
Doctoral track: enrolled PhD candidate who has completed coursework by the fellowship start
Researcher track: PhD or equivalent professional experience at the time of application
Good health and enough Japanese or English to carry out the research
A Japan-based advisor or affiliate arranged by the deadline
Must stay continuously in Japan during the fellowship
Past Japan Foundation fellows must wait three years; doctoral candidates under 35 get priority
documents: Applicant and project information (project summary up to 2 pages)
Two reference forms from two referees
Letter of Affiliation form signed by the Japan-based advisor
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the quality of the research project, the need to carry it out in Japan, its feasibility and the applicant's achievements. In FY2026, 96 of 286 applications were successful. Results are announced by the end of April 2027.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 December 2026, 1:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time
Arrival in Japan: between 20 June 2027 and 20 March 2028
opportunities.about_provider: The Japan Foundation is Japan's public body for international cultural exchange, set up to promote understanding of Japan through arts and culture, Japanese-language education and Japanese studies. It runs grant and fellowship programmes worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the FY2027 forms from the Japan Foundation's Japanese studies page, complete them and upload everything through the online application portal (apply.jpf.go.jp) before the deadline. Referees upload their reference forms through a dedicated link in the portal. US citizens and residents apply through the Japan Foundation New York portal instead.
opportunities.notes: Secure your Japan-based affiliation early, as it must be in place by the deadline. Contact: RJS-FW@jpf.go.jp, +81-3-5369-6069.

opportunities.title: Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship 2027
opportunities.provider: Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre, Queen's University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and recent graduates of any post-secondary institution in Africa, in any discipline, who can give at least 10 hours a week can apply by 1 December 2026 for the free, fully online eight-month programme.
opportunities.description:
The Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship is a free, fully virtual eight-month programme run by the Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre (DDQIC) at Queen's University in Kingston, Canada, with support from the Mastercard Foundation. It helps African students and recent graduates turn business ideas into ventures through online courses, coaching and a pitch competition.

The 2027 cohort runs from January to August 2027 in phases: Explore (January to February), Ignite (March to April) and Launch and Fellowship (May to August), ending with graduation in August. More than 1,000 candidates start the first phase, about 180 finalists progress, and up to 60 are named Fellows. Applications close on 1 December 2026 and results are announced in late December.

Because it is online and open to any discipline at any African post-secondary institution, the programme is an accessible way for young African founders to gain business training, mentors and a chance at seed funding without leaving home.
opportunities.benefits: Free courses, coaching and micro-credentials; a stipend for up to 60 Fellows (stated as CAD 500 on the page and FAQ, and as USD 350 in the timeline); pitch competition prizes of up to CAD 15,000; and seed funding for Fellows who reach the Launch phase.
requirements: Student or recent graduate of a post-secondary institution in Africa
Any field of study
Able to commit at least 10 hours a week for eight months
Able to work in English (mentoring may also be in French)
documents: Online application form (Qualtrics); the page does not list other documents
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates progress through phases based on completing milestones and the quality of their venture pitches: over 1,000 take part in phase one, around 180 finalists go on, and up to 60 are selected as Fellows.
important_dates: Launch and Fellowship: May to August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre is the entrepreneurship hub of Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario. It runs venture programmes for students and, with the Mastercard Foundation, this fellowship for African students and graduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the programme page before 1 December 2026. Successful applicants join the Explore phase in January 2027 and advance by completing assignments and pitching their ventures.
opportunities.notes: All content is online and self-paced within each phase. Check the page for the confirmed stipend amount, since it states two figures.

opportunities.title: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships 2027-2029 (TU Delft MSc)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Excellent non-EU applicants aged 35 or under who have applied to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme by 1 December 2026 can be considered for one of 16 full scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are TU Delft's main full scholarships for international master's students. For the 2027 intake the university offers 16 awards, two per faculty, to outstanding applicants admitted (or conditionally admitted) to one of its two-year regular MSc programmes in Delft, the Netherlands. Each award runs for the full 24 months of the programme.

The scholarships are paid from a fund left by Justus van Effen, a TU Delft graduate from the 1940s, and his wife Louise. They are intended for applicants who rank roughly in the top 10% of their bachelor's class, although applicants do not need to prove a ranking. The deadline for both the MSc application and the scholarship form is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET, and applicants hear the outcome by email by the end of March 2027.

For African engineers, scientists and designers this is one of the few awards in the Netherlands that covers both full non-EU tuition and a living allowance, so it is worth applying early: the English test result and all admission documents must already be in the MSc application when the scholarship deadline passes.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees for the two years of the MSc (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student's nationality) plus a monthly contribution towards living costs for 24 months; the exact monthly amount is set in the scholarship contract. The second year continues only if the student earns at least 48 of the 60 ECTS credits of year one.
requirements: International applicant without EU citizenship (dual EU/non-EU nationals are not eligible)
Aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027
Admitted or conditionally admitted to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme (not a joint programme)
Excellent academic record, as an indication in the top 10% of the bachelor's cohort
Not a TU Delft bachelor's student and no Dutch bachelor's degree
English language certificate uploaded before the deadline unless exempt
Not available for Metropolitan Analysis Design and Engineering, Applied Geophysics, Berlage Post-master, Industrial Ecology or GIMA
documents: Complete MSc application (bachelor's diploma or proof of enrolment, transcript, English test certificate, motivation letter, CV, passport/ID)
Form and reference letter combined into a single PDF
opportunities.selection_process: The Admissions Office first assesses the MSc application. Applicants with a positive assessment are then reviewed by the selection committee of the faculty that runs their programme, which chooses its two scholarship holders on academic excellence and motivation. Results are sent by email by the end of March 2027.
important_dates: Deadline for MSc application and scholarship form: 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: TU Delft is the oldest and largest technical university in the Netherlands, with eight faculties covering engineering, applied sciences, architecture and design. Its scholarship programmes are run with the faculties, which select their own candidates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your chosen two-year MSc through TU Delft's online application system and upload every required document, including the English test result, before 1 December 2026. Download the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029 from the scholarships page, combine it with one reference letter in a single PDF and upload it in the same application before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Holders may not combine the award with any other scholarship, and part-time work is discouraged. Programmes that are joint degrees with other universities are excluded.

opportunities.title: Kansas State University International Scholarships (Wildcat Nonresident) for Spring 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international undergraduates with a GPA of 3.25 or more can receive automatic tuition awards; apply for spring 2027 by the 1 December 2026 priority date.
opportunities.description:
Kansas State University in Manhattan, Kansas, gives automatic scholarships to new international undergraduates based on their secondary-school grade point average. The main award, the Wildcat Nonresident Award, reduces the higher out-of-state part of tuition.

The awards apply to the 2027 entry terms. For a spring start, international applicants should apply by the priority date of 1 December; the fall priority date is 1 May. The university also runs a scholarship network and competitive awards that need extra materials.

For African students with strong school results, these awards can cut tuition at a large US public university by up to about 19,000 USD a year.
opportunities.benefits: Wildcat Nonresident Award (estimated, based on 30 credit hours a year): GPA 3.90+ covers 100% of the nonresident tuition portion (about 19,101 USD a year); 3.75 to 3.89 covers 80% (about 15,281 USD); 3.50 to 3.74 covers 60% (about 11,461 USD); 3.25 to 3.49 covers 50% (about 9,551 USD). Graduates of GEMS Education schools have a similar partnership scale.
requirements: Admitted as a new international undergraduate at the Manhattan campus
Secondary-school GPA of at least 3.25 (weighted or unweighted)
Apply by the priority date: 1 December for spring, 1 May for fall
documents: K-State Scholarship Network application for additional awards
Supplemental materials or interview for competitive awards
opportunities.selection_process: Wildcat Nonresident Awards are given automatically by GPA band. Competitive scholarships are judged on extra materials and sometimes an interview.
important_dates: International priority date for spring start: 1 December 2026
International priority date for fall start: 1 May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Kansas State University is a public land-grant research university in Manhattan, Kansas. Its Office of Student Financial Assistance manages undergraduate scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to K-State by the priority date, then complete the K-State Scholarship Network application for additional awards. Contact finaid@k-state.edu with questions.
opportunities.notes: 1 December is a priority date, not a hard closing date. Amounts are estimates, and the Olathe and online campuses have different deadlines.

opportunities.title: Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellowship 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded fellowship for accomplished mid-career journalists.

opportunities.title: LIDo Doctoral Training Partnership PhD Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a strong bioscience, physical science, computing, engineering or maths degree can apply for four-year BBSRC PhDs in London; up to seven places cover overseas fees.
opportunities.description:
The London Interdisciplinary Doctoral Programme (LIDo) is a BBSRC-funded doctoral training partnership that trains bioscience PhD students across a group of London research institutions. It recruits a new cohort each year for four-year PhDs starting in 2027.

There are two routes. In the standard DTP route, students spend their first year doing two four-month research rotations at two partner institutions before choosing a PhD project. In the iCASE route, students apply directly to a named project with an industry partner and spend between 3 and 18 months working with that company.

Projects must fall within the BBSRC's remit, so clinical work, human cancer and non-infectious human disease research are excluded. The programme welcomes students from biological, biomedical, veterinary, physical, computational, engineering and mathematical backgrounds, and some studentships cover full overseas fees, which makes it open to strong African applicants.
opportunities.benefits: Each studentship pays home tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI London rate of £23,805 per year for four years. Up to seven studentships a year also cover full overseas fees. Visa and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: First-class or high upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), or a relevant master's
Degree in a biological, biomedical, veterinary, physical, computational, engineering or mathematical subject
Comfortable with computers and some numeracy (at least GCSE maths or statistics, or equivalent)
If English is not your first language: proof of English, preferably IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in each part
documents: Online LIDo application (sections set out in the application overview PDF)
Evidence of English proficiency where needed
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted using LIDo's published guidelines and shortlisted candidates are interviewed on Zoom. iCASE applicants have two interviews, one with a LIDo panel and one with the project supervisors. In the 2025/26 round about 900 people applied and over 300 were interviewed.
opportunities.about_provider: LIDo is a doctoral training partnership of UK universities and research institutes in London, funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). It offers about 26 studentships a year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the LIDo website and complete the online application before the deadline. You can choose the rotation-based DTP route or apply directly to named iCASE projects. Read the FAQ and shortlisting guidelines first.
opportunities.notes: Only up to seven of the 26 studentships cover overseas fees, so competition for international places is strong. Visa and relocation costs are your own.

opportunities.title: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LEXS) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top-10% non-EEA graduates applying to a September-start Leiden master's can apply for a partial tuition scholarship by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS) is a partial tuition-fee scholarship for outstanding non-EEA students admitted to a full-time master's programme at Leiden University in the Netherlands, starting in September. It is awarded for the length of the programme.

About 25 scholarships are given each year and more than a thousand students apply. The award level is set by the university at one of five amounts and cannot be negotiated. The LLM (non-advanced) and the MSc programmes of Leiden Law School are excluded, and February-start programmes do not qualify.

African graduates in the top 10% of their class can apply simply by adding a short motivation letter to their Leiden master's application before the 1 December deadline.
opportunities.benefits: A tuition-fee contribution of €10,000, €15,000, €17,500, €18,500 or €19,000 a year, for the duration of the programme. It is not a full scholarship: recipients from outside the EEA must still prove sufficient funds for their visa.
requirements: Non-EEA/EFTA passport and not eligible for Dutch government student finance (LLM Advanced Studies and MSc International Relations and Diplomacy are open to all nationalities)
Among roughly the top 10% of graduates in your previous relevant degree
Applying for a full-time September-start master's (not the LLM non-advanced or Law School MSc programmes)
Not already holding a Leiden master's, except where a previous master's is required
documents: Leiden master's application with application fee paid
Signed agreement to the LExS terms and conditions (if awarded)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculty selection committees nominate recipients within 10 weeks of the deadline, and all applicants are told the outcome before the end of March.
important_dates: Nominations: within 10 weeks of the deadline
All applicants informed: before end of March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands. Its Student and Educational Affairs scholarships team manages the LExS.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your online application for a Leiden master's programme and pay any fee, then open the Scholarships section of the application screen, select LExS and upload your motivation letter before 1 December 2026. Allow up to three working days to create your application, and apply separately for each programme.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. The LExS cannot be combined with another full external scholarship. Contact: scholarships@sea.leidenuniv.nl.

opportunities.title: Managing the Atom Fellowship 2027-2028 (Harvard Belfer Center)
opportunities.provider: Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students at dissertation stage, recent PhDs, faculty and mid-career professionals from any country with a nuclear policy research project can apply by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Project on Managing the Atom at Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center offers ten-month research fellowships in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from 1 September 2027 to 30 June 2028. Fellows work on nuclear policy, with priority given to research on rethinking nuclear deterrence and reducing its dangers, and on resolving regional nuclear proliferation crises.

The fellowship is open to pre-doctoral researchers in the dissertation stage, postdoctoral researchers, university faculty and mid-career professionals from academia, national laboratories, government and industry. Applications opened on 1 October 2026 and close on Tuesday 1 December 2026, with recommendation letters due by 15 December 2026.

The Belfer Center welcomes applicants from all over the world and runs an application mentorship programme for applicants from developing countries and other under-represented groups, which makes this a realistic opportunity for African scholars of nuclear energy, security and diplomacy.
opportunities.benefits: A 10-month stipend of USD 50,000 for pre-doctoral fellows or USD 60,000 for postdoctoral fellows, health insurance, discounted public transport passes, shared office space and modest administrative support. Self-funded scholars can be offered non-stipendiary appointments; applicants must say whether they need full or partial funding.
requirements: Doctoral student in the dissertation stage who has passed general exams, or a recent PhD (or equivalent), or a university faculty member or mid-career professional
A research project with a clear nuclear policy focus
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: Research statement of 3 to 5 double-spaced pages, including a statement of policy relevance
Writing sample of under 50 double-spaced pages
opportunities.selection_process: The project reviews the research statement, writing sample, CV and references, looking for strong research with policy relevance to its priority areas. Applicants are notified by 15 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs is Harvard Kennedy School's hub for research and teaching on international security, science, technology and diplomacy. Its Project on Managing the Atom studies nuclear weapons, nuclear energy and non-proliferation policy.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the Belfer Center fellowship portal linked from the fellowship page and submit the research statement, CV, writing sample and (for pre-docs) transcript by 1 December 2026. Enter three recommenders, who must upload their letters by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Applicants from developing countries can ask for help through the Belfer Center's application mentorship programme (contact details on the fellowship page).

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Arizona State University 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholarship at Arizona State University for academically talented young Africans with financial need and a commitment to giving back to their communities.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at UC Berkeley (master's)
opportunities.provider: UC Berkeley Center for African Studies with the Mastercard Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of African countries who apply to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less in its first application round can be considered for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of California, Berkeley supports talented young Africans who are admitted to Berkeley master's degrees of two years or less. It is run by Berkeley's Center for African Studies in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, and the university is recruiting scholars through autumn 2028. The programme is not open to undergraduates or doctoral students.

There is no single scholarship deadline. Applicants apply to one of the eligible Berkeley master's programmes (including the MBA, Master of Journalism, MPH, MPP and several Master of Engineering degrees) by that programme's first-round deadline, which falls between September and early January, mostly in December. Programmes then nominate candidates, who are invited to a supplemental application in February, interviewed online in March and told the final decision in late March or early April.

The programme looks for academic excellence, leadership potential, a commitment to community and an intention to return to Africa, and gives priority to applicants with an African first degree, no earlier postgraduate degree and no previous Mastercard Foundation support.
opportunities.benefits: The scholarship supports the full cost of a Berkeley master's degree for selected scholars; the pages read do not list amounts. African applicants can also request a waiver of the Berkeley graduate application fee.
requirements: Citizen of an African country (Africans displaced or with refugee status within Africa included)
Not a dual citizen, asylee, refugee or permanent resident of the US, Canada, the UK or the EU
Applying to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less, in its first application round (before January)
Academic excellence and leadership potential
Commitment to community and intention to return to Africa
Priority for applicants with an African undergraduate degree and no previous postgraduate degree
documents: UC Berkeley graduate application with the documents required by the chosen programme
Supplemental Mastercard Foundation Scholars application (by invitation, in February)
opportunities.selection_process: Graduate programmes nominate admitted candidates; nominees complete a supplemental application in February and an online interview in March, and final decisions are made in late March or early April. There are always more qualified candidates than places.
important_dates: Programme deadlines: September to early January, most in December (first round only)
Fee-waiver application: by 15 November (passed for this cycle)
Final decisions: late March or early April
opportunities.about_provider: The University of California, Berkeley is a leading public research university in California. Its Center for African Studies runs the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, part of the Mastercard Foundation's network of partner universities that fund African students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose an eligible master's programme and submit the UC Berkeley graduate application by that programme's first-round deadline. If nominated, you will be invited to complete the Scholars Program supplemental application and an online interview. Questions go to mcfs.programinfo@berkeley.edu.
opportunities.notes: Only master's programmes of two years or less qualify; bachelor's, doctoral, concurrent and dual degrees do not. You must apply in your programme's first round. The pages say there are always more strong candidates than places, and the programme recruits through fall 2028. Eligibility questions: mcfs.programinfo@berkeley.edu.

opportunities.title: Max Planck School of Biomedical AI: Fully Funded PhD Positions (First Cohort, 2027)
opportunities.provider: Max Planck School of Biomedical Artificial Intelligence (BMAI)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's graduates (or students finishing by September 2027) in computer science, maths, statistics, engineering, physics or a computational life-science field, from any country.
opportunities.description:
The Max Planck School of Biomedical Artificial Intelligence is recruiting its very first cohort of doctoral researchers. It offers 25 fully funded positions for a three-year PhD that combines artificial intelligence with the life sciences, starting on 1 September 2027. The school is coordinated from the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry near Munich and links research groups at leading German universities and research institutions.

Each doctoral researcher is co-supervised by two of the school's fellows and joins recurring week-long schools that bring the cohort together. Researchers get access to the partner institutions' labs and computing environments, support to present at an international conference each year, and mentoring. The working language is English.

The call sets no nationality limit, so African graduates with a strong quantitative background, whether in computing, mathematics, engineering or physics, or in biology with solid programming skills, can compete for a salaried PhD at the meeting point of AI and biomedicine. Applications for this first round close on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded three-year PhD with a competitive employment contract at a participating university or research institution (salary amount not stated). Co-supervision by two BMAI fellows, recurring one-week schools, access to research environments, support for attending an international conference each year, and mentoring.
requirements: A master's degree (MSc or equivalent), or completion of one by September 2027
Background typically in computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, physics or a related field
Life-science graduates are welcome if they have a strong computational background
Good English (the working language)
No nationality restriction is stated
opportunities.selection_process: The posting does not describe the selection stages. Candidates apply online with their documents and are assessed by the school for the 25 places in the first cohort.
opportunities.about_provider: The Max Planck Schools are joint graduate programmes of the Max Planck Society and German universities that bring together leading researchers in one field across many sites. The new School of Biomedical AI focuses on applying and developing artificial intelligence for the life sciences and medicine.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and apply online through the school's application portal linked from the official DAAD posting (mps.cloud.opencampus.net), uploading a motivation letter, CV, certificates and transcripts. Further details of the process are on the school's site, biomedicalai.maxplanckschools.org. Questions go to the coordination team at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry.
opportunities.notes: 25 positions in this first cohort. Contact: Valerie Griesche, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, +49 89 8578 2053.

opportunities.title: Miami University Presidential Fellows Program (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High-achieving first-year applicants for fall 2027 with SAT or ACT scores can apply by 1 December for one of 15 full rides.
opportunities.description:
The Presidential Fellows Program is Miami University's top scholarship for first-year students entering in fall 2027. Each year 15 Fellows are chosen and receive a full-ride award for four years at the university in Oxford, Ohio, together with an academic enrichment fund.

Applicants show their interest on the admission application and submit everything by the firm 1 December deadline. Semi-finalists then submit extra materials, and finalists are invited to interviews on campus in February.

The page does not limit nationality, so high-achieving African secondary school students applying to Miami can be considered, but they must self-report ACT or SAT scores, which are required for fall 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition and fees for eight semesters (while keeping a 3.50 GPA), housing up to the cost of a standard double room, the Diplomat Standard meal plan with USD 500 Dining Dollars, and an academic enrichment fund of up to USD 5,000.
