Books, computers, health insurance, study-abroad fees and deposits are not covered.
requirements: Indicate interest in the programme on the admission application
Self-reported ACT or SAT scores (required for fall 2027)
Keep a cumulative GPA of 3.50 to renew the award
All materials submitted by 1 December
documents: Admission application and materials through the application status page
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on the full admission application, test scores, semi-finalist supplemental materials and an on-campus finalist interview in February. Choices are finalised within two weeks after the interviews.
opportunities.about_provider: Miami University is a public research university founded in 1809 in Oxford, Ohio, known for its strong undergraduate teaching.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Miami for fall 2027, mark your interest in the Presidential Fellows Program and complete all materials through the application status page by 1 December. Contact PresidentialFellows@MiamiOH.edu with questions.

opportunities.title: Montana State University Presidential Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Incoming first-year students with an unweighted high-school GPA of at least 3.7 who are fully admitted to Montana State University can apply by 1 December 2026 for a four-year tuition waiver and stipend.
opportunities.description:
The Presidential Scholarship is Montana State University's most prestigious academic award for new undergraduates. Run through the Honors College in Bozeman, Montana, it supports first-year students who start in 2027 for up to eight semesters of study, and both Montana residents and non-residents can apply.

The 2027 Presidential Scholarship is open now and closes at midnight Mountain Standard Time on 1 December 2026. Applicants must already be accepted to MSU with full (not conditional) admission and must submit the general scholarships application and a separate Presidential application with recommendations.

Recipients usually have an unweighted GPA of 3.9 or higher and rank in the top 3% of their class, and they act as ambassadors for the university through leadership and service. International students who are not selected are still considered automatically for MSU's international merit scholarship of USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 a year.
opportunities.benefits: A yearly tuition waiver, a stipend (amount not stated on the page) and priority course registration for up to eight semesters. Renewal requires a 3.5 MSU GPA and an average of 16 MSU credits per semester. Separately, international undergraduates with a GPA of 2.5 or higher and full admission are considered automatically for an international merit scholarship of USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 a year.
requirements: Incoming first-time first-year student (fewer than 12 university credits)
Unweighted high-school GPA of 3.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale
Full (not conditional) admission to Montana State University
Evidence of leadership and service
documents: General Scholarships Application in the Cat$cholarships portal
Recommendations from one high-school counselor and two other recommenders, uploaded through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: The Honors College reviews applications for academic excellence, leadership and service, and fit with the Honors College. Recommendations are submitted through the portal only; mail and email are not accepted.
opportunities.about_provider: Montana State University is a public land-grant research university in Bozeman, Montana. Its Honors College offers smaller classes and enrichment for high-achieving undergraduates and manages the Presidential Scholarship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply and be accepted to MSU, then claim your NetID. Sign in to the Cat$cholarships portal, submit the General Scholarships Application, then complete the Presidential Scholarship application and invite your counselor and two recommenders before midnight MST on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Applicants with 12 or more university credits are not eligible. The international merit scholarship is not given to conditionally admitted students.

opportunities.title: National Geographic Society Grants: The Human Thread (Storytelling) RFP
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Storytellers aged 18 or over anywhere may apply online for funding for a human-experience storytelling project by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The National Geographic Society is accepting proposals under a request for proposals called "The Human Thread", which funds storytelling projects that shed light on the wide range of human experience. The opportunity is supported by Lilly Endowment Inc. and is listed among the Society's current funding calls with a closing date of 1 December 2026.

National Geographic grants back explorers, storytellers, educators and scientists, and each request for proposals sets its own focus and budget. Projects funded under this call must start at least six months after the deadline, so successful work would begin from mid-2027 onwards.

For African photographers, filmmakers, writers and other storytellers, this is a chance to obtain funding and recognition from one of the world's best-known organisations for exploration and storytelling. Applications are made online only, through the Society's funding portal.
opportunities.benefits: Grant funding for a storytelling project. The budget is set per request for proposals; the amount for this call is given on the RFP page in the funding portal, not on the main grants page.
requirements: Applicants must be at least 18 years old
The project must start at least six months after the 1 December 2026 deadline
An applicant may lead only one National Geographic project at a time
Final reports on any earlier National Geographic Society grants must have been submitted
The project must match the focus of The Human Thread request for proposals
documents: Online application in the National Geographic Society Funding Portal
Project budget following the Society's budget guidelines
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are reviewed by the Society against the focus of the request for proposals; the grants page does not describe the stages in more detail.
important_dates: Earliest project start: six months after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The National Geographic Society is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) organisation founded in 1888. According to its grants page it has awarded more than 16,000 grants to explorers, scientists, educators and storytellers worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the National Geographic Society Funding Portal (funding.nationalgeographic.org), open The Human Thread request for proposals and submit your application there before 1 December 2026. Applications sent by email or post are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: The detailed RFP page sits behind the portal login, so read it there for the exact focus, budget limit and any geographic rules before you apply.

opportunities.title: Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Two-year funded postdoctoral fellowship at Dartmouth for recent PhDs doing computational research in any discipline.

opportunities.title: Next Asia Policy Lab Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs working on contemporary Asia in one of SNAPL's four tracks can apply for a two-year Stanford postdoc.
opportunities.description:
The Stanford Next Asia Policy Lab (SNAPL), directed by Professor Gi-Wook Shin and housed at APARC, is recruiting two postdoctoral fellows for 2027-2029. Each fellow spends two years in residence at Stanford from fall quarter 2027, leads a thematic research group and helps with student programmes.

The fellowships are organised around four tracks: talent flows and development; nationalism and racism; US-Asia relations; and democratic crisis and reform, all with a focus on contemporary Asia.

No nationality rule is stated, so African scholars whose work on migration, race, democracy or great-power relations connects with Asia can apply for two years of salaried research at Stanford.
opportunities.benefits: Annual salary of $83,000 plus benefits for two years, with a possible extension.
requirements: PhD received within three years of the fellowship start date
Dissertation approved for conferral by 30 June 2027 and certified by 31 August 2027
Research fitting one of the four SNAPL tracks on contemporary Asia
Residence at APARC for the fellowship
documents: Formal letter of request setting out research plans and solo and co-authored publications
Academic CV of up to two pages with a publication list
Three recommendation letters emailed to SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu
opportunities.about_provider: SNAPL is a research lab at Stanford's Walter H. Shorenstein Asia-Pacific Research Center (APARC), part of the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies. It studies policy challenges facing Asia and the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online Qualtrics application linked from the SNAPL fellowships page with your letter of request and CV, and have three referees email letters to SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: SNAPL also offers a one-year STINT-SNAPL postdoc (same deadline) and visiting fellowships with a 1 March 2027 deadline. Contact: Natalia Slavney, SNAPLcontact@stanford.edu.

opportunities.title: Notre Dame College of Arts and Letters Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Humanities PhDs worldwide who earned their doctorate within three years may apply by 1 December 2026 for a two-year, 75,000 USD-a-year Notre Dame postdoc.
opportunities.description:
The Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program in the College of Arts and Letters at the University of Notre Dame offers two-year postdoctoral posts to early-career scholars. The programme was set up in 2025 to support new researchers through interdisciplinary work and close mentorship.

The 2027-2029 cohort is hosted by Art, Art History and Design; English; German, Slavic and Eurasian Studies; History and Philosophy of Science; the Initiative on Race and Resilience; Philosophy; Romance Languages and Literatures; and Theology. Fellows are based on the campus in Notre Dame, Indiana, USA.

The salary is generous and Notre Dame plans to sponsor visas, so the fellowship is open in practice to recent African PhDs in the humanities. Romance Languages lists Africa among its new areas of interest.
opportunities.benefits: Salary of 75,000 USD a year for two years, plus a one-time 15,000 USD fund for research and training, and office space. The university plans to support visas for fellows.
requirements: Doctorate from an accredited institution received within three years of the cohort start date (longer if parental or FMLA leave was taken in the past two years)
ABD applicants may apply if they will defend by June before the start
Master's-only applicants are not eligible
Current Notre Dame students, graduates and fellows are not eligible
Research fitting one of the participating departments
documents: Cover letter, up to 4 pages (double-spaced, 12-point, 1-inch margins)
Research statement, up to 5 pages, same format
Writing sample of up to 10,000 words
At least three recommendation letters submitted through Interfolio by the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed and finalists are interviewed. Applications missing any letters are not reviewed. Do not contact faculty to arrange a mentor in advance, though you may name faculty you would like to work with.
important_dates: Application deadline: 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm US Eastern time
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Notre Dame is a private Catholic research university in Indiana, USA. Its College of Arts and Letters is its largest college, covering the humanities, arts and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Interfolio (free Dossier account), uploading the cover letter, research statement and writing sample, and arranging three letters there by 1 December 2026. Questions go to alprovostpostdocs@nd.edu.
opportunities.notes: Holding a permanent position does not disqualify you. The FAQ page sets the formatting limits strictly, so follow them.

opportunities.title: Public Humanities special issue: African American Roots and Routes (call for articles)
opportunities.provider: Public Humanities journal (Cambridge University Press), guest editor Neal A. Lester
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars can propose chapters for an edited Cambridge volume on African American roots and routes.
opportunities.description:
The open-access journal Public Humanities, published by Cambridge University Press, plans a special issue on "African American Roots and Routes", guest edited by Neal A. Lester of Arizona State University. The issue invites articles on African American beginnings and their routes, written in accessible language for a wide readership.

Authors first send a 300-word abstract with a proposed title to the guest editor. Full articles of no more than 6,500 words (excluding abstract, notes and bibliography) then go through the journal's peer-review system and appear digitally in open access.

Scholars of the African diaspora, including African researchers working on transatlantic histories and cultures, can contribute.
requirements: Article on African American beginnings, roots or routes
Accessible writing for a broad public readership
Maximum 6,500 words excluding abstract, footnotes and bibliography
documents: 300-word abstract with proposed title (to the guest editor)
Full article submitted through the Public Humanities ScholarOne site (mc.manuscriptcentral.com/pubhum)
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email a 300-word abstract and proposed title to guest editor Neal A. Lester (neal.lester@asu.edu) by 1 December 2026, then submit the full article through the Public Humanities online peer-review system.

opportunities.title: RAND Graduate Student Summer Associate Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time doctoral or professional-degree students with at least two years of graduate study (and some engineering, computing and operations research master's students) who will live in the US during summer 2027 can apply by 1 December 2026 for a paid 12-week research placement at RAND.
opportunities.description:
RAND's Graduate Student Summer Associate Program places advanced graduate students on real, funded RAND research projects for 12 weeks (60 working days) in summer 2027. Each summer associate is matched with a project and a mentor and produces research that feeds into RAND's policy work.

Associates can work in person at RAND's offices in Santa Monica, Washington DC, Pittsburgh or Boston, or remotely from home, but they must live in the United States for the whole assignment. Tentative start dates are 24 May and 14 June 2027, and the placement must be completed between May and October.

US citizenship is not required except for particular projects, so international students, including Africans studying at US universities or able to be in the US for the summer, can apply. The programme is highly selective: RAND receives more than 600 applications a year and expects about 15 to 20 placements for 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Approximately USD 15,000 (before taxes) for the 12-week placement, paid every two weeks. Relocation costs are not provided. RAND supplies documentation to a student's international office where work authorisation is needed.
requirements: Full-time graduate student with at least two years of doctoral or professional-degree study (PhD, EdD, DrPH, JD, MD, etc.)
Enrolled full-time in spring and fall 2027 and not graduating before December 2027
Master's students considered only in engineering, computer or information science and operations research
Undergraduates and postdocs are not eligible
Must live in the United States for the entire assignment; international students planning to be in the US in summer 2027 may apply
Work authorisation for the position (RAND provides supporting documents)
Only one application per person
documents: Online application with university, department and degree details
Answers to three short questions (up to 250 words each)
Contact details for two recommenders (letters requested only after interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications receive a holistic review. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed between early February and March 2027, and offers are usually made in mid-to-late March. Fewer than 10% of applicants receive offers.
important_dates: Tentative start dates: 24 May and 14 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: RAND is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research organisation that works on public policy challenges. It has offices across the United States as well as in Europe and Australia.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Apply Now' link on RAND's Summer Associate page, which leads to RAND's Workday careers site. Submit your CV, cover letter and short answers and name two recommenders. Students in disciplines not listed among RAND's priorities can email Summer_Director@rand.org first.
opportunities.notes: Extra applications from the same person are withdrawn at random, so submit only one. Check the priority disciplines listed for 2027 before applying.

opportunities.title: Salzburg Global Seminar Internship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Internship at Schloss Leopoldskron in Salzburg for senior undergraduates, graduate students and young professionals aged 18+, with room, board, travel and insurance covered in kind.
opportunities.description:
Salzburg Global Seminar has opened its call for 2027 internships. Interns join its teams either at Schloss Leopoldskron in Salzburg, Austria, or in its Washington, D.C. office, and support its international programmes and operations.

In Salzburg the roles include Communications, Development, Library and Program internships; in Washington there are Donor Communications, Advancement and Program internships. Salzburg internships can last at most 90 days because of Austrian labour and visa rules, while D.C. internships usually last three to four months. The working language is English, and German is not required.

Salzburg internships are unpaid but include free room and board at the Schloss, travel and insurance, so they are a realistic way for African students and graduates to gain experience in an international non-profit in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Salzburg: unpaid, but interns receive room and board at Schloss Leopoldskron, travel to and from Salzburg, accident and health insurance (excluding pre-existing conditions, dental and glasses) and help with visa processing; a €100 security deposit is refunded if there is no damage, and visa fees are paid by the intern. Washington, D.C.: a stipend (amount not stated).
requirements: At least 18 years old
Program and Development internships in Salzburg are open to bachelor's students; Communications and Library need a completed relevant degree
Non-EU citizens need a visa for Salzburg (support is given)
D.C. roles require US work authorisation
English is the working language; German not needed
documents: Assignments where a role requires them
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed only during an open call, and the organisation describes the process as highly competitive. Spontaneous applications are not reviewed and individual questions about applications are not answered.
opportunities.about_provider: Salzburg Global Seminar is an independent non-profit founded in 1947, with offices in Salzburg and Washington, D.C. It has run programmes involving participants from more than 170 countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on Salzburg Global's online application platform through the current openings linked from the internships page, and apply to the role(s) you want with your CV, cover letter and any required assignment. You may apply for more than one role, but the organisation advises focusing.
opportunities.notes: Academic credit can be arranged. Rejected applicants may reapply in a later call. Contact: info@SalzburgGlobal.org.

opportunities.title: Shorenstein Postdoctoral Fellowship on Contemporary Asia 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs (within three years) researching contemporary Asia can apply for a 10-month Stanford postdoc.
opportunities.description:
Stanford's Walter H. Shorenstein Asia-Pacific Research Center (APARC) offers postdoctoral fellowships for junior scholars researching contemporary Asia. Fellows spend a 10-month appointment in residence at Stanford, starting in the fall quarter of 2027, turning their research into a publishable product such as a book or articles.

Projects may focus on political, economic or social change in Northeast, Southeast or South Asia, or on international relations and political economy in the Asia-Pacific. APARC normally appoints two such fellows each year.

There is no stated nationality restriction, so African scholars with a recent PhD on Asia, or on Africa-Asia relations within the region's political economy, can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Pay based on an annual rate of $83,000, prorated for the 10-month appointment, plus up to $3,000 for research expenses.
requirements: PhD awarded no more than three years before the fellowship starts
Degree conferred and certified by 30 June 2027 (proof due by 31 August 2027)
Research on contemporary Asia-Pacific politics, economy, society or international relations
Residence at Stanford for the full appointment
documents: Research statement of up to five double-spaced pages describing the project and its publishable output
Three recommendation letters emailed as PDFs to shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu
important_dates: Deadline for all materials including letters: 1 December 2026 (Pacific Time)
opportunities.about_provider: APARC is part of Stanford's Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies and is based in Encina Hall. It runs research programmes and fellowships on the politics, economics and societies of the Asia-Pacific.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in APARC's online Qualtrics form, upload your CV and research statement as PDFs and submit, then have three referees email their letters to shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu before the deadline. You receive a confirmation email once every part, including all three letters, has arrived.
opportunities.notes: Stanford is closed from 21 December 2026 to 1 January 2027, so replies may be slow then. Contact: Kristen Lee, shorensteinfellowships@stanford.edu.

opportunities.title: TU Delft Faculty Scholarship: MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics) 2027
opportunities.provider: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), Faculty of EEMCS
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants with a bachelor's grade average of at least 80% of the maximum who apply to the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) by 1 December 2026 can win one of up to two partial tuition scholarships.
opportunities.description:
TU Delft's Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) offers up to two partial scholarships to excellent international students who start the two-year MSc in Electrical Engineering, track Microelectronics, in September 2027. The award is given through the faculty's Microelectronics department, where the scholarship holder also carries out the master's thesis.

The scholarship reduces the tuition fee (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student) and can be renewed for the second year if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 out of 10 in year one. An outstanding thesis project (grade 9 or higher) can lead to the offer of a PhD position in the department.

The award suits African electrical and electronic engineering graduates with very strong grades who want to specialise in chip design, circuits and microsystems. Because it is partial, applicants should plan other funding for living costs or apply for the Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship at the same time.
opportunities.benefits: A partial waiver of the tuition fee for year one (at the statutory or institutional rate), renewable for year two if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 (80%). No monthly allowance is stated.
requirements: International applicant
Admitted or conditionally admitted to the two-year MSc Electrical Engineering, track Microelectronics
Bachelor's degree from a well-regarded university outside the Netherlands
Grade average of at least 80% of the maximum of the grading scale
English language certificate uploaded before the deadline unless exempt
documents: Complete MSc application (diploma or proof of enrolment, transcript, English test certificate, motivation letter, CV, ID)
opportunities.selection_process: After the Admissions Office gives a positive assessment of the MSc application, the Microelectronics department selects up to two scholarship holders on academic excellence. Results are sent by email by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: TU Delft is the largest technical university in the Netherlands. Its Faculty of EEMCS hosts the Microelectronics department, which works on integrated circuits, sensors and microsystems.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) through TU Delft's online application system with all documents, including your English test result, before 1 December 2026. Add the scholarship application form and one reference letter to the same application before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: The master's thesis must be done in the Microelectronics department; a thesis grade of 9 or higher can lead to a PhD offer.

opportunities.title: The Black Scholar Special Issue: Adjacency: Black Alternatives
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars and writers anywhere may submit articles or shorter pieces on alternative cultural expressions of Blackness by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Black Scholar, a long-running journal of Black studies and research, has opened a call for contributions to a themed special issue titled "Adjacency: Black Alternatives". The issue looks at less familiar, alternative ways in which Blackness is expressed in culture, with suggested themes that include neurodivergence, speculative fiction, artificial intelligence and sustainability.

The special issue is guided by three guest editors, Joshua K Reason, Alexandria C. Cunningham and Suzanne Nimoh, and is planned to appear as issue 57.4 in Winter 2027. It accepts both full peer-reviewed research articles and shorter pieces such as essays, roundtables and interviews.

For African scholars, writers and researchers working on Black culture, the diaspora, technology or futures thinking, this is a chance to publish in an established international journal of Black studies. Submission is online and open to authors anywhere; there is no fee or travel involved.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in a themed special issue (issue 57.4, Winter 2027) of The Black Scholar after peer review. The call does not mention any payment or fee.
requirements: Peer-reviewed research articles of 5,000 to 7,500 words
Essays, roundtables and interviews of 4,000 to 5,000 words, endnotes included
Work must fit the special issue theme of alternative cultural expressions of Blackness
Authors must follow the journal's submission guidelines
Authors must obtain permission for any third-party material they reproduce
documents: Manuscript prepared under The Black Scholar's submission guidelines
Permissions for any third-party material used
opportunities.selection_process: Full articles go through the journal's peer review; the guest editors shape the issue around the stated theme.
opportunities.about_provider: The Black Scholar describes itself as a journal of Black studies and research. It is published by Taylor & Francis and run by an editorial team that includes a managing editor named on its website.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your manuscript according to the journal's guidelines on theblackscholar.org, then submit it through the journal's Taylor & Francis submission page (tandfonline.com/journals/rtbs20) by 1 December 2026, indicating that it is for the "Adjacency: Black Alternatives" special issue.
opportunities.notes: Word limits include endnotes for the shorter formats. The call was posted on 17 July 2026.

opportunities.title: Tropical Medicine and Clinical Decision Making short course 2027, Antwerp
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Medical doctors with a university (master's) degree in medicine, including physicians from low- and middle-income countries, who want training in tropical medicine for resource-limited settings.
opportunities.description:
Tropical Medicine and Clinical Decision Making is a ten-week, face-to-face short course at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, running from 4 January to 12 March 2027. It is taught in English and is worth 10 ECTS credits, with classes on weekdays from about 9:00 to 16:00.

The course covers the pathology of tropical diseases, laboratory practice and, above all, how to make sound clinical decisions with limited diagnostic tools. It is designed for doctors with little or no experience in tropical settings and for physicians from low- and middle-income countries who want to sharpen their clinical skills.

It can be taken on its own, combined with ITM's 'Challenges in International Health' course to earn a postgraduate certificate (renamed the Postgraduate in Clinical Tropical Medicine and International Health from 2027), or counted towards the MSc in Tropical Medicine.
opportunities.benefits: A fee-paying course: EUR 1,225 for EEA participants and EUR 3,360 for non-EEA participants. ITM states that no scholarships are available for this course; travel and living costs are not covered.
requirements: University (master's) degree in medicine
Course taught in English
Able to attend in person in Antwerp from 4 January to 12 March 2027
documents: Online application through the ITM student portal
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp is a Belgian research and training institute for tropical medicine, international public health and global one health, with a long tradition of training health workers from Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through ITM's student portal (enrolment page for the 2026-2027 course) before 1 December 2026. Questions go to tmih@itg.be.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is very close, and a Belgian visa takes time, so non-EEA doctors should apply immediately. Credits count towards ITM's MSc in Tropical Medicine.

opportunities.title: UBC Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Black Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons with financial need entering a UBC degree can apply by 1 December.
opportunities.description:
The Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award is a University of British Columbia entrance award for students who self-identify as Black, including African, African-American, African-Canadian and Afro-Caribbean students, and who show strong academics and financial need. It applies to direct-entry undergraduate programmes at UBC Vancouver and UBC Okanagan.

Applicants must apply to UBC and submit the separate entrance award application by 1 December. UBC contacts recipients by 15 May, and awards apply only to the student's first-choice campus and degree.

opportunities.title: Vanderbilt Ingram Scholars Program 2027

opportunities.description:

It was created in 1993 by E. Bronson Ingram and is run by Vanderbilt's Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships.

Ingram Scholars do about 20 hours of community service a month and design a summer service project after their second year, for which they receive extra funding. The scholarship is renewed each year to graduation as long as scholars keep a 3.0 GPA and meet the service requirements. First-year applicants for fall 2027 must submit the Ingram application electronically through their MyAppVU account by 1 December 2026.

Vanderbilt's scholarship FAQ confirms that international applicants can receive any of its merit scholarships, so this is a realistic route for African students with strong service records to study at a leading US university with tuition, fees and housing paid.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition, all required fees and the value of on-campus housing each year, renewable to graduation; a stipend for a summer service project; and additional need-based aid if a student's need exceeds full tuition.

Strong record of civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, character and leadership
Ingram application submitted via MyAppVU by 1 December 2026
To renew: 3.0 GPA and about 20 hours of service a month

For African students aiming at a top US university, these awards add to Vanderbilt's other aid and can make the cost of study much lower.

opportunities.title: Wageningen Africa Scholarship Programme (ASP) MSc 2027

opportunities.description:
The Africa Scholarship Programme (ASP) at Wageningen University & Research supports talented African students to complete a two-year MSc at Wageningen in the Netherlands, starting in September 2027, as part of the university's commitment to capacity building in Africa.

There is no separate scholarship form: applicants are assessed if they submit a complete MSc application before 1 December 2026, already hold their bachelor's degree and have their English test results by that date. The WU Scholarship Selection Committee then selects finalists, and the final awards are decided by lottery.

The scholarship covers tuition, living costs and travel for the full 24 months, making it one of the most complete master's awards in the Netherlands for African citizens in life sciences, agriculture, food and environment.

English test results meeting WUR's requirements available before 1 December 2026
Preference for applicants without a master's degree

Wageningen is among the world's leading universities in agriculture, food, nutrition and environmental sciences, so the scholarship is especially relevant for African students who want to build careers in food security, rural development, climate and natural resources. Many African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe, are on the eligible list.

opportunities.title: International Scholars Program (UBC)

UBC's International Scholars Program (ISP) is the University of British Columbia's flagship package of need- and merit-based awards for outstanding international students entering a first undergraduate degree in September 2027, at UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan. opportunities.title: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and journalism professionals of any nationality with at least five years of experience at editorially independent organisations.
opportunities.description:
The John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships give working journalists, and people whose jobs support journalism, nine months at Stanford University to step back from daily work, learn and think about the problems facing news. The fellowship runs full time and in residence from September to May. Fellows are not asked to deliver a set project, and no university degree is needed to be selected.

Applications for the 2027-28 cohort are open now, and there are separate tracks for US-based and international applicants. The programme is a good fit for African reporters, editors and newsroom managers with solid experience, because it pays a large stipend and covers Stanford tuition and health insurance, so a fellow can take a full academic year away from work.

The fellowship is aimed at people already established in the field. Students, interns, PR staff, government employees and full-time academics are not the intended audience, and applicants must work for media that is editorially independent.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$135,000 for the nine months; Stanford tuition and health insurance; a health supplement for dependants who enrol in Stanford coverage; help with finding housing; coaching and workshops during the year.

opportunities.description:
AI4SC 2027 is the third AAAI Bridge on Artificial Intelligence for Scholarly Communication, a two-day programme on 16-17 February 2027 in Montréal, Canada, co-located with the 41st AAAI Conference. It is chaired by Anna Jacyszyn of FIZ Karlsruhe.

The bridge brings together AI researchers and the scholarly publishing community to discuss how AI can support research discovery, peer review and publishing. It accepts long, short and poster or demo papers for proceedings, as well as non-archival talk proposals, lightning-talk abstracts and tutorial proposals.

It is open to researchers anywhere and is a good venue for African researchers in AI, digital libraries or research information systems, though attendees must register for AAAI-27.

opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind review by at least three programme committee members per submission.
important_dates: Submission deadline: 3 December 2026 (end of day AoE)
opportunities.about_provider: AAAI, the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence, runs the annual AAAI Conference, which includes bridge programmes linking AI with other fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through EasyChair (conference ai4sc2027) by 3 December 2026. Lightning-talk abstracts can be sent until 14 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Contact: ai4sc2027@easychair.org.

opportunities.title: Cambridge Trust Scholarships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to University of Cambridge courses starting in 2027/28, subject to each award's criteria.
opportunities.description:
The Cambridge Trust is the largest provider of scholarships for international students at the University of Cambridge, offering full-cost and part-cost awards for PhD, master's and some undergraduate study. Its scholarship search covers courses starting in the 2027/28 academic year.

For postgraduate study, most awards require significant academic achievement and potential and are based partly on financial need. Some awards are limited to particular nationalities, and courses such as the MBA, MFin, MEd and postgraduate certificates and diplomas are not funded.

African applicants are considered automatically for many awards by completing the funding section of the University's graduate application before their course's funding deadline.
requirements: Applying for a Cambridge master's (MPhil, MASt, LLM with restrictions) or PhD
Significant academic achievement and potential, and for most awards financial need
Not funded: MBA, MFin, EMBA, MEd, PGCert, PGDip and similar courses
Not for a degree at the same or lower level than one already held
documents: University of Cambridge graduate application with the funding section completed
important_dates: Awards made: mid-February to end of July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Cambridge Trust funds international and UK students at the University of Cambridge, often in partnership with colleges and other donors.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose your course, check the scholarships you may qualify for, optionally pick up to two colleges, and submit your University application through the Applicant Portal by your course's funding deadline with the funding section completed. Some partner awards need a separate application.

opportunities.title: Concordia Carlini-DeLuca RISE Award 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time Concordia science or engineering undergraduates in second year or above with a GPA of at least 3.30, including international students.
opportunities.description:
The Carlini-DeLuca Undergraduate RISE Award (Resilience In Science and Engineering Pathways to Success) is one of Concordia University's application-based awards for 2026-27. It recognises science and engineering undergraduates who have kept up strong studies while dealing with serious personal strain or exceptional challenges.

The award is worth CA$1,500 and is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students. That means African students already studying science or engineering at Concordia in Montreal can apply on the same terms as Canadians.

It is a one-off award for current students rather than an entrance scholarship, so it suits African students in their second year or later who want to have their resilience and results recognised.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time award of CA$1,500.
requirements: Undergraduate in science or engineering at Concordia
Second year of study or higher
Minimum GPA 3.30
Full-time in fall 2026 and winter 2027
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or international student
Has faced significant personal strain or exceptional challenges
documents: Online application form (Microsoft Form linked from the awards page)
opportunities.about_provider: Concordia University is a large public university in Montreal, Canada. Each autumn it opens a round of application-based awards for its undergraduates across all faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Open Concordia's application-based awards page, find the Carlini-DeLuca RISE Award in the Faculty of Arts and Science section, and complete its online form before midnight on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: The same page lists other Concordia awards open to international students with the same 3 December deadline, such as the Colors of Concordia Award and the Back on Track Award.

opportunities.title: Concordia Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Concordia undergraduates in eligible tech, engineering or finance programmes with a GPA of 3.30+ who identify as Black or Asian, including international students.
opportunities.description:
The Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship is a Concordia University award funded by Morgan Stanley. It supports undergraduates from under-represented racial and ethnic groups in business technology, computing, engineering and quantitative finance programmes at Concordia's John Molson School of Business and Gina Cody School of Engineering and Computer Science.

The scholarship is worth CA$2,500 and is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students who self-identify as Black, Southeast Asian, South Asian or East Asian. African students enrolled in the eligible programmes can therefore apply.

It is part of Concordia's 2026-27 round of application-based awards, which all close on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time award of CA$2,500.
requirements: Undergraduate, full-time or part-time, in an eligible programme (Business Technology Management, Computer Engineering, Computer Science including Computational Arts, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Mathematical and Computational Finance)
GPA of 3.30 or higher
Self-identifies as Black, Southeast Asian, South Asian or East Asian
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or international student
documents: Online application form (Microsoft Form linked from the awards page)
opportunities.about_provider: Concordia University is a large public university in Montreal, Canada. Morgan Stanley, the global financial services firm, funds this award to widen diversity in technology and finance.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Go to Concordia's application-based awards page, find the Morgan Stanley Race and Ethnic Diversity Scholarship under the business or engineering section, and submit the online form before midnight on 3 December 2026.

opportunities.title: ITCILO Global Youth Forum 2027: Sustainable Development at the Frontiers of New Tech
opportunities.provider: International Training Centre of the ILO (ITCILO)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and young professionals aged 18 to 30 interested in international civil service; EUR 600 partial scholarships for nationals of ODA-eligible (DAC list) countries.
opportunities.description:
The Global Youth Forum is a two-week, in-person training course run by the International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization on its campus in Turin, Italy. The 2027 edition, titled "Sustainable Development at the Frontiers of New Tech", takes place from 18 to 29 January 2027 and is taught in English.

The forum is designed for undergraduate and graduate students and young professionals who want a career in international organisations. Participants learn how the UN system and development agencies work, with this edition focused on how new technologies are reshaping sustainable development.

African applicants are eligible for a partial scholarship because the centre reserves its EUR 600 awards for nationals of countries on the OECD DAC list of aid recipients, which includes every African country. Shortlisted applicants go through a short motivation interview.
opportunities.benefits: Partial scholarship of EUR 600 towards the course cost for nationals of DAC-list countries, awarded after a motivation interview. The full cost is EUR 3,950 (tuition EUR 2,330 plus subsistence EUR 1,620); travel is not mentioned.
requirements: Aged 18 to 30
Undergraduate or graduate student, or young professional
Interest in a career in international civil service
Good English
Scholarship only for nationals of OECD DAC-list countries
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants who are shortlisted for a partial scholarship take part in a motivation interview; scholarships are awarded after this interview.
important_dates: Applicants needing a Schengen visa must secure their place by 3 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The International Training Centre of the ILO (ITCILO), based in Turin, is the training arm of the International Labour Organization and runs courses for governments, workers, employers and young professionals worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the ITCILO course page (apply link https://oarf2.itcilo.org/STF/A9020032/en, course code A9020032). Complete the scholarship part of the form as early as possible. Questions go to itcilo_youthforum@itcilo.org.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship covers only EUR 600 of the EUR 3,950 cost, so participants must fund the rest. The scholarship form deadline (20 November 2026) is much earlier than the course deadline.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-MSA-COMSTECH-SESAME School on AI-Driven Biomaterials Design (Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: School at SESAME in Allan, Jordan, 14 to 25 March 2027, for early-career researchers who submit a poster abstract, with no fee and limited grants prioritising developing-country participants.
opportunities.description:
The Joint ICTP-MSA-COMSTECH-SESAME School on AI-Driven Biomaterials Design runs from 14 to 25 March 2027 in Jordan (the event page lists "Allan - Jordan", home of the SESAME synchrotron). It takes early-career researchers from characterisation to additive manufacturing and from lab to market.

Topics include synchrotron micro-CT and FTIR, atomic force microscopy, AI-driven design and 3D printing of biomaterials. Participants present a short research poster.

There is no registration fee and a limited number of grants give priority to participants from developing countries, so African researchers in materials science, biomedical engineering or physics are a key target group.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants are available, with priority for participants from developing countries; amounts are not stated.
requirements: Early-career researcher in a relevant field
Online application through the ICTP e-portal
Short research abstract for a poster using the ICTP template
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste is a UNESCO Category 1 institute that runs schools and workshops for scientists from developing countries. This school is co-organised with MSA University, COMSTECH and SESAME.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the "Apply here" link on the ICTP event page (smr 4343), which leads to the ICTP e-portal, and upload your poster abstract by 3 December 2026. Request a grant in the application if you need travel support.
opportunities.notes: Contact: smr4343@ictp.it.

opportunities.title: Kyoto University International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary school graduates with strong grades and English can apply; no Japanese is needed.
opportunities.description:
The Kyoto University International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP) is a four-and-a-half-year bachelor's route for international students. It starts with a six-month preparatory course in Japanese and foundation subjects, followed by a four-year degree in the student's chosen faculty at Kyoto University in Japan, for the October 2027 intake.

No Japanese is needed at the time of application. The programme looks for applicants with strong academic records, good English, motivation and a broad world view, and all students receive scholarships.

Kyoto iUP gives African secondary school leavers a funded path into one of Asia's top universities, with a monthly allowance in the preparatory phase and dormitory housing at the start.
opportunities.benefits: All Kyoto iUP students receive scholarships that waive the admission fee in full and tuition in full or in part for four and a half years. During the preparatory course, students can receive an allowance of up to JPY 120,000 per month, and further merit-based allowances from supporters may follow. Dormitory housing is provided for the first one and a half years.
requirements: Strong academic record
English proficiency (Form C English Proficiency Evaluation)
Motivation and a global outlook
Japanese not required at application
Must pass the eligibility screening set out in the application guidelines
documents: Form B: Evaluation (some forms uploaded by the school)
Form C: English Proficiency Evaluation Form
All documents in English or with English translations
important_dates: Online application system open: 2 November to 3 December 2026 (5 pm Japan time)
opportunities.about_provider: Kyoto University is one of Japan's leading national research universities. Kyoto iUP is its programme for recruiting international undergraduates into its regular faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the Application Guidelines for October 2027 Enrolment, then apply through the Kyoto iUP online application system while it is open, pay the application fee and click "Complete" before 5 pm Japan time on 3 December 2026. Late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Check the eligibility screening and FAQ on the Kyoto iUP site before applying, and make sure your school uploads its forms on time.

opportunities.title: MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people aged 18-26 from any country with fluent English who commit to a year-long community leadership programme.
opportunities.description:
The MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship is a year-long leadership programme for people aged 18 to 26 who want to tackle problems in their own communities. It runs in three phases: a one-month community needs assessment in June 2027, a 10-day in-person training in New York City and Burlington, Vermont from 20 to 29 July 2027, and then ten months of carrying out a community project with an alumni mentor, ending in July 2028.

Projects focus on education, health or economic security. The programme has no geographic restrictions, so young Africans can apply and then run their projects at home with support from MCW's alumni network.

The first-round deadline is 3 December 2026; a second round closes on 8 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Economy return international flights; housing from 19 to 29 July 2027; three meals a day from 20 to 29 July; round-trip travel between New York City and Burlington; mentoring by alumni during the project year. Passport, visa and in-country costs are not covered, and no stipend is mentioned.
requirements: Aged 18 to 26 on 1 June 2027 (no exceptions)
Open to all countries
Fluent written and spoken English
Able to obtain a visa and travel documents
Commitment to all three phases
Reliable email and internet access
documents: Online application in English with two essays (a community issue and a leadership challenge)
Resume of no more than one page
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed in two rounds, followed by interviews with alumni. MCW warns that answers written with AI tools will hurt an applicant's chances.
important_dates: First-round deadline: 3 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. New York time
opportunities.about_provider: MCW Global is a non-profit based in New York that trains young leaders and supports community projects around the world, with a strong presence in Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through MCW's applicant portal (applicant.mcwglobal.org) with your essays, one-page resume and two recommendation letters. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by alumni in February 2027, and successful fellows confirm by paying a refundable US$100 deposit.
opportunities.notes: The US$100 deposit is returned when the fellowship is completed. Write your own essays; MCW says AI-generated answers count against you.

opportunities.title: Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhD holders of any nationality with a sponsor at a US non-profit institution, doing basic plant biology research.
opportunities.description:
The Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology fund three years of basic research on fundamental questions in plant biology at a US non-profit university or research institute. The 2027 call supports two kinds of fellow: plant biologists who want to learn new skills from a mentor outside their field, and researchers from other fields who want to bring their expertise to plant biology. Up to two mentors are allowed.

The awards are generous: an US$85,000 annual stipend plus up to US$35,000 a year for research and related costs. Both US citizens and foreign applicants may apply, so African PhD holders who find a US host can compete.

Fellows start between July and October 2027 after decisions in May 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Up to US$360,000 in total over three years: a stipend of US$85,000 per year, an annual allowance of up to US$35,000 (for health insurance, supplies, travel and similar costs) and up to US$2,000 for relocation. No indirect costs are paid.
requirements: PhD (or equivalent) awarded no earlier than three years before the deadline, or expected by the start date
US citizens and foreign nationals may apply
Must be hosted by a US non-profit research university or institution
The sponsor cannot be the applicant's thesis adviser
Only one application per sponsor per year
Cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at the same time
documents: Proposal narrative on the Simons template
Sponsor biosketch (max 5 pages) and other-support document
Four confidential letters: thesis adviser, two research scientists and the sponsor
Institutional assurances (IRB, IACUC or biosafety) where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by Simons Foundation scientific staff and an external expert committee.
important_dates: Start: the first of a month between 1 July and 1 October 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Simons Foundation is a private foundation in New York that funds research in mathematics and the basic sciences. Its Life Sciences division runs this plant biology fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The applicant creates the application in their own Simons Award Manager (SAM) account at sam.simonsfoundation.org, uploads the documents and arranges the four letters. The host institution's signing official must approve it before final submission by noon Eastern time on 3 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Simons offices are closed 25-27 November 2026, so ask questions early.

opportunities.title: AAAI-27 Student Scholar and Volunteer Program (Montreal, Feb 2027)
opportunities.provider: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time student AAAI members who submitted a paper to AAAI-27 and have a faculty recommendation can apply between 30 November and 4 December 2026 for partial travel support or complimentary volunteer registration.
opportunities.description:
The AAAI-27 Student Scholar and Volunteer Program helps students attend the 41st AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, held in Montréal, Canada, from 16 to 23 February 2027. It offers partial travel support to student scholars and free technical programme registration to a limited number of volunteers.

Applications open on 30 November 2026 and close on 4 December 2026. Applicants must be full-time students, AAAI members, and have submitted a paper to the conference with a recommendation from their faculty adviser.

African students with papers at AAAI-27 can use the programme to reduce the cost of attending one of the world's largest AI conferences.
opportunities.benefits: Partial travel support for selected student scholars (amount not stated) and complimentary technical programme registration for a limited number of volunteers. Volunteers are not paid.
requirements: Full-time undergraduate or graduate student
AAAI member
Submitted paper(s) to AAAI-27
Recommendation letter(s) from a faculty adviser
Repeat applicants must have met earlier volunteer and reporting duties
opportunities.selection_process: If requests exceed funds, preference goes first to students with an accepted technical paper and then to students actively taking part in the conference. Volunteer places also favour participating students.
opportunities.about_provider: The Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) is a scientific society that promotes AI research and runs the annual AAAI Conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply during the 30 November to 4 December 2026 window using the form announced on the AAAI-27 Student Scholar Volunteer Program page. Do not register for the conference until you hear back, or you lose the free registration.
opportunities.notes: Early registrants are not refunded. Contact: scholars@aaai.org.

opportunities.title: ACM MobiSys 2027 Call for Papers (Ho Chi Minh City, Jun 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Papers for ACM MobiSys 2027 in Ho Chi Minh City (21-25 June 2027) are due 4 December 2026 with abstracts by 27 November; travel support has not been announced yet.
opportunities.description:
ACM MobiSys 2027, the 25th International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services, takes place in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, from 21 to 25 June 2027. It is sponsored by ACM SIGMOBILE and is one of the top venues for research on mobile and wireless systems.

The call seeks original papers on mobile systems, applications and services. Since 2026 review is single-blind, so author names appear on submissions, and there is an Emerging Ideas track for early-stage work. Reviews include an early rejection round and a rebuttal.

For African researchers in mobile computing, IoT and networking, MobiSys offers a high-impact publication and a conference in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are published by ACM. Authors whose institutions are not in ACM Open pay a 2027 article processing charge of $500 (ACM/SIG members) or $750 (non-members). No travel grants are stated.
requirements: Original work not under review elsewhere
At most 12 pages of main content (double column, 10 pt, US Letter, ACM sigconf template); references and appendix unlimited
Author names and affiliations included (single-blind review)
Human-subjects work needs ethics (IRB or similar) approval
At least one author registers at a non-student rate and presents in person
opportunities.selection_process: Papers go through an early rejection round, a rebuttal of up to 500 words, then conditional acceptance with shepherding. Accepted papers receive a one-page public review.
opportunities.about_provider: ACM SIGMOBILE is the Association for Computing Machinery's special interest group on mobility of systems, users, data and computing. It runs MobiSys, MobiCom and other leading conferences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract by 27 November and upload the full paper by 4 December 2026 on HotCRP (mobisys27.hotcrp.com). For the Emerging Ideas track, start the title with "[Emerging Ideas]" and tick the box.
opportunities.notes: Deadlines will not be extended, placeholder abstracts are desk-rejected, and authors cannot be changed after submission.

opportunities.title: ASLE 2027 roundtable: Transboundary Waters and Critical Border Zones
opportunities.provider: Association for the Study of Literature and Environment (ASLE)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars can send abstracts for an in-person roundtable at the ASLE 2027 conference at the University of Maryland, 22-24 June 2027.
opportunities.description:
This call invites contributors to a proposed roundtable, "Riparian Terrors, Borderline Terroirs: Transboundary Waters and Critical Border Zones", for the 2027 biennial conference of the Association for the Study of Literature and Environment (ASLE). The conference runs on 22-24 June 2027 at the University of Maryland, College Park, under the theme "Territory: Terra, Terroir, Terror".

The organisers, Priyanka Sharma (George Washington University) and Minket Lepcha (University of Manitoba), will include selected abstracts in a roundtable proposal to ASLE, which makes the final decision. ASLE roundtables have a chair and five to seven panellists who each speak for 8 to 10 minutes, and most sessions are in person only.

Scholars writing on rivers, borders and environmental conflict, including on African transboundary waters such as the Nile, Niger or Zambezi basins, can respond.
opportunities.benefits: ASLE offers a small number of $500 travel awards for members in precarious circumstances without institutional funding; applications open in late February 2027.
requirements: Abstract of up to 300 words on transboundary waters or border zones
Short bio of under 100 words
Able to attend in person in College Park, Maryland
Only one individual abstract per person may be submitted to ASLE
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers select abstracts for their roundtable proposal, which ASLE then reviews; ASLE decisions are due by 26 February 2027.
important_dates: Abstracts to the roundtable organisers: 4 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: ASLE, the Association for the Study of Literature and Environment, is an international scholarly association for environmental humanities. It holds a biennial conference in the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract and bio to the roundtable organisers at the address given in the call by 4 December 2026. If selected, you will be included in the roundtable proposal they submit to ASLE through its Pheedloop portal.
opportunities.notes: Questions about the conference: 2027asleconf@gmail.com.

opportunities.title: Andlinger Center Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellows 2027
opportunities.provider: Princeton University Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhDs (within three years) in energy or environment fields with two Princeton mentors.
opportunities.description:
Princeton University's Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment is recruiting Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellows for 2027. Fellows design an interdisciplinary research plan on energy and the environment with at least two Princeton faculty members or senior researchers as mentors.

Appointments are expected to last two years, renewed after the first year on good performance, starting as early as June 2027 in Princeton, New Jersey. Teaching is not required, but fellows may give guest lectures.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African scientists and engineers with a recent PhD in energy, climate or environmental fields can apply for a well-paid, prestigious postdoc.
opportunities.benefits: Salary of $75,000 per year plus $3,500 per year for conference travel and career development, and Princeton's benefits package for eligible employees.
requirements: Doctorate in a related field awarded no more than three years before the start date
Research plan co-developed with two or more Princeton faculty or senior researchers
Preference for candidates not currently at Princeton
The primary mentor cannot be hosting a current Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellow
Background check required
documents: Contact details of the Princeton primary mentor(s), plus a mentor letter committing part of the funding
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the strength of the research, its interdisciplinary framing, its fit with the Center's mission and whether it builds new collaborations.
opportunities.about_provider: The Andlinger Center for Energy and the Environment at Princeton University supports research and education on sustainable energy and environmental technologies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with your proposed Princeton mentors, then submit your application on Interfolio (apply.interfolio.com/189606) by 4 December 2026. Your mentors must send a supporting letter and commit part of the financial support.
opportunities.notes: Contact: Charles Sharpless, csharpless@princeton.edu.

opportunities.title: Cannes Lions 2027 Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded trip to Cannes Lions for under-30 creative professionals from under-represented groups.
opportunities.description:
The LIONS Scholarship gives ten under-represented young creative and marketing professionals a fully funded place at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity in 2027. Five places are on the Creative Academy, for creatives such as art directors, copywriters, designers and journalists, and five on the Brand Marketing Academy, for client-side marketers.

Scholars attend their academy and receive a Young Lions festival pass, joining the world's biggest gathering of the advertising and creative industry in Cannes, France. The programmes are in English.

The scholarship is meant for talent under-represented in the industry, so young African creatives and marketers with at least two years of work experience are a natural fit.
opportunities.benefits: A fully funded trip to Cannes Lions 2027, including travel, accommodation and a food allowance during festival week, plus a Young Lions festival pass. There is no application fee. Guests and family are not funded.
requirements: Born on or after 25 June 1996 and at least 18 years old (proof of age required)
At least two years of work experience in a relevant role
Creative Academy: working creative; Brand Marketing Academy: brand or client-side marketer
Able to take part in English
documents: Online application (see the official Entry Kit for details)
opportunities.selection_process: A two-stage process: a jury of more than 40 creatives builds a shortlist from the first applications, then a final stage selects the ten scholars.
opportunities.about_provider: Cannes Lions is the annual international festival of creativity for the advertising, marketing and communications industry, operated by Informa Events (Europe) Limited.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the LIONS Scholarship Entry Kit and apply through the Cannes Lions competitions portal (competitions.canneslions.com) before 00:01 GMT on 4 December 2026. You may apply to both academies but can be accepted onto only one.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is one minute past midnight GMT, so submit on 3 December. You can reapply in later years. Contact: talentprogrammes@canneslions.com.

opportunities.title: DTU PhD scholarship: Data-driven Design of Architected Materials
opportunities.provider: Technical University of Denmark (DTU Engineering Technology)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried three-year DTU PhD position open to international applicants with a relevant two-year master's (120 ECTS) and good English.

opportunities.title: IEEE I2MTC 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide may submit full papers by 4 December 2026 for IEEE I2MTC 2027 in Chongqing; student first authors can request a travel grant.
opportunities.description:
IEEE I2MTC is the flagship annual conference of the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society. The 2027 edition, themed "Smart Instrumentation for a Connected World", invites full papers on all aspects of instrumentation and measurement, from sensors and metrology to measurement for agriculture, food production and food safety.

The conference takes place in Chongqing, China, from 17 to 20 May 2027. Accepted papers are presented at the conference and published in IEEE Xplore.

For African engineers and researchers in electrical engineering, sensing and measurement, it is a recognised venue to publish and meet peers. Student first authors can also ask for a student travel grant.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the proceedings and IEEE Xplore for accepted papers. Students who are first authors of a student paper can be considered for an IMS Student Travel Grant (amount not stated on the page).
requirements: Original full paper on instrumentation or measurement
Submitted through EDAS by 4 December 2026
For a travel grant: student first author, paper flagged as a student paper, favourable reviews
Travel grant winners must register and pay in full by 5 March 2027 and attend the conference
documents: Full paper (PDF) in the conference format
Tick box for the student travel grant at first submission (if applying)
opportunities.selection_process: Papers go through peer review with a first-round decision and a revised-paper stage. Travel grants favour IMS student members and papers with good reviews.
important_dates: Student travel grant: full registration by 5 March 2027; recipients told 3 April 2027
Early registration and final manuscript: 19 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society (IMS) is the IEEE society for measurement science and instrumentation. I2MTC is its main international conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the full paper through EDAS (edas.info, conference N35663). To be considered for the student travel grant, tick the travel grant option when you first submit. Joining IEEE IMS as a student member gives priority for grants.
opportunities.notes: Travel grant winners who do not attend the conference and awards ceremony lose the grant. The IMS Conference Equity Travel Grant is a separate scheme on the conference site.

opportunities.title: Italian Academy Fellowship Program 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Italian Academy for Advanced Studies, Columbia University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality holding a PhD (or completing one by June 2027) can apply for a salaried residential research fellowship in New York.
opportunities.description:
The Italian Academy for Advanced Studies at Columbia University in New York offers residential research fellowships to advanced scholars, from postdoctoral researchers to full professors. Its homepage announces a call for 2027-28 fellowships.

Fellows spend one or two semesters in residence (fall: September to December; spring: January to April). Projects are proposed in English, and scientists must arrange a collaboration with a Columbia lab director before applying.

There is no stated nationality restriction, so African scholars across the humanities, social sciences and sciences can consider it once the official call details are published.
opportunities.benefits: According to the fellowship page, a taxable salary of $5,000 to $8,000 per month, a travel allowance for airfare to and from New York, and part of health insurance costs. Housing is not provided, though the Academy helps with Columbia housing applications.
requirements: Advanced scholar, from postdoctoral to full professor level
Doctorate in hand by the summer after applying
Residence for one or two semesters
Scientists must secure a pledged collaboration with a Columbia lab
No concurrent fellowships; former fellows wait four years
opportunities.about_provider: The Italian Academy for Advanced Studies is a research institute at Columbia University, 1161 Amsterdam Avenue, New York.

opportunities.title: National Council for Black Studies 51st Annual Conference 2027: Call for Abstracts
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars, students, educators, artists and community practitioners working in Black and Africana Studies can propose papers, panels, roundtables, workshops or media presentations by 4 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The National Council for Black Studies is holding its 51st Annual Conference from 17 to 20 March 2027 at the Courtland Grand Hotel in Atlanta, Georgia, and has opened its call for abstracts. The theme is 'A Resilient Life-Affirming Pedagogy: Black Studies as Truth-Telling and Transformative Practice', inviting reflection on how the teaching and study of African and African-descended peoples can tell hard truths and drive change.

The call welcomes individual presentations as well as organised panels, roundtables, workshops and media presentations from across Black and Africana Studies. Proposals may come from established scholars, graduate and undergraduate students, educators, artists, activists and community practitioners.

For African researchers and students working on the continent, its diasporas, pan-Africanism or Black intellectual traditions, the NCBS conference is one of the main North American meetings in the field and a good place to build networks with Africana Studies departments in the United States. Note that the call itself does not mention travel funding.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted presenters get a slot on the programme of the field's main US conference. The call does not mention travel grants, fee waivers or stipends.
requirements: Work related to Black or Africana Studies, ideally engaging the 2027 theme
Open to professionals, graduate students and undergraduates (state your status)
Panel, roundtable and workshop proposals compete for a combined maximum of 24 accepted sessions
Presenters attend the conference in Atlanta, 17-20 March 2027
documents: Names and titles of all presenters
opportunities.selection_process: Individual abstracts are reviewed on a rolling basis, so early submission is encouraged. Panels that engage directly with the conference theme are preferred, and NCBS members receive priority for panel, roundtable and workshop slots.
opportunities.about_provider: The National Council for Black Studies is a US-based professional organisation for scholars and practitioners of Black, African American and Africana Studies. It promotes the discipline through its annual conference, publications and support for academic programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your title, abstract and presenter details and submit them through the NCBS conference submission system (All Academic) linked from the call. Because abstracts are reviewed as they arrive, submit well before 4 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Media presentations are accepted. Membership in NCBS improves the chances of a panel proposal being accepted.

opportunities.title: Newberry Library Short-Term Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders and ABD candidates of any nationality receive $3,000 a month, usually for one month, to research the Newberry's collections in Chicago.
opportunities.description:
The Newberry Library in Chicago offers Short-Term Fellowships for 2027-28 to scholars who need to consult specific items in its collections. Fellows spend one or two months in residence at any point between June 2027 and August 2028.

The fellowships are open to PhD holders at any career stage, including curators, librarians and independent scholars, and to doctoral candidates who are ABD. No institutional affiliation is needed, but the project must show why particular Newberry materials are essential.

African historians and humanities scholars working on topics such as the Atlantic world, maps, travel and exploration, or early modern history can use the fellowship to fund archival research in Chicago.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of $3,000 per month for one or two months. Housing is not provided, so the stipend must cover accommodation, travel and living costs.
requirements: PhD holder at any career stage, or ABD doctoral candidate
Project that needs specific items in the Newberry's collections
Residence in Chicago for one or two months between June 2027 and August 2028
Some fellowships carry extra residency or membership rules (see FAQ)
documents: List of Newberry materials to consult (maximum 300 words)
One recommendation letter in English, sent by the referee (up to 14 December 2026)
opportunities.about_provider: The Newberry Library is an independent research library in Chicago with major collections in the humanities. It runs short- and long-term fellowship programmes for researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your application through the Newberry's SlideRoom portal by 4 December 2026, then have your referee upload their letter within ten days. The library matches applicants to its named fellowships automatically, except those with special requirements.
opportunities.notes: Long-term Newberry fellowships close on 20 November 2026. Contact: research@newberry.org.

opportunities.title: Obama Foundation Leaders Africa 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Changemakers aged 24-45 living in Africa with 3+ years of Africa-focused leadership experience can apply by 4 December 2026 (priority 23 November) for the free 2027-2028 Obama Foundation Leaders Africa programme.
opportunities.description:
Obama Foundation Leaders Africa is an eight-month leadership development programme for 35 emerging leaders who are driving change across the African continent. Applications for the 2027-2028 cohort opened on 9 November 2026.

The programme runs from the week of 1 September 2027 to no later than 1 May 2028 and takes about 8 to 12 hours a month, with weekly sessions, coaching and small community groups. The main page describes it as hybrid and the FAQ as virtual, so applicants should expect mostly online participation. Participants join a global network of more than 1,800 Obama Leaders alumni.

It is designed for people already leading changemaking work focused on Africa, whatever their job title or formal education, and there is no cost to take part.
opportunities.benefits: Free leadership training, coaching, peer community groups and lifelong membership of the Obama Leaders network. There is no stipend and no grant for participants' own projects.
requirements: Live in an eligible African country for the whole programme and be a citizen, permanent resident, refugee or asylum seeker there, or have lived there for 5+ years
Work focused on Africa, with at least 3 years of relevant experience
Hold a leadership role in changemaking work (no title needed)
Aged 24 to 45 on 1 September 2027
Professional-level English
Not a previous Obama Leaders participant
Not standing for elected office from acceptance until 1 May 2028
