Minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 out of 4.0 depending on the programme
English proficiency meeting MBZUAI's criteria
Final-year students can apply with current transcripts
Only one application per cycle
documents: Bachelor's transcript and certificate (or expected-graduation letter)
Master's transcript (PhD applicants with a master's)
Referees: three for PhD, two for MSc
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants sit a screening exam in advanced maths and programming (PhD candidates also machine learning and core computer science); some are invited to a technical interview. Merit funding is considered during review.

opportunities.title: MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship for Early-Career Researchers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-French researchers with a PhD from the last five years can apply for a 12-month funded climate research stay in a French lab.
opportunities.description:
The Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) 2027 Visiting Fellowship brings early-career foreign researchers to France for a 12-month research stay in a French laboratory. It is funded by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs with the Ministry of Higher Education and Research, and run by Campus France.

Projects must address climate and environmental topics, such as Earth system science, climate and sustainability, the energy transition, environmental social challenges or One Health; purely medical projects are not eligible. Stays start between September and December 2027.

Any nationality except French is eligible, so African researchers who earned their PhD in the last five years can apply with a French host laboratory.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of 2,500 euros for 12 months plus a 500 euro settling-in payment, with health, civil liability and repatriation insurance. International travel is not covered. It cannot be combined with a French employment contract or other French government funding.
requirements: Doctorate awarded less than five years before the deadline (defended December 2021 to December 2026)
Any nationality except French
Not living and working in France when applying
No previous MOPGA fellowship
A host laboratory in France and a climate or environment project
documents: Support letter from the host supervisor co-signed by the lab director
Project description in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Experts appointed by the ministry review applications, then a scientific committee makes the final choice; results are expected in May-June 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Campus France is the French national agency for promoting higher education and managing government scholarships. MOPGA was launched by the French government to attract climate researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a host laboratory in France and build the project with them, then apply online on Campus France's SMApply portal (MOPGA 2027) in English or French before 15 December 2026. Emailed applications are not accepted. Contact: mopga@campusfrance.org.
opportunities.notes: Contact host labs early, since the supervisor letter must be co-signed by the lab director.

opportunities.title: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women from outside the US and Canada doing graduate study there, with a year of coursework left, may apply by 15 December 2026 for up to 12,500 USD.
opportunities.description:
The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS) supports women from outside the United States and Canada who are doing graduate study in those countries. The fund was created in 1949 and is run by P.E.O. International, a women's educational organisation.

Applications are accepted each year from 15 September to 15 December, and awards are announced in May. The scholarship helps with study costs but is not meant to pay all expenses.

For African women admitted to master's or doctoral programmes in the US or Canada who plan to return home and use their education to promote peace and development, it is a valuable top-up award.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 12,500 USD (smaller amounts are possible). The award is not meant to cover all academic or personal costs.
requirements: A woman who is not a US or Canadian citizen or permanent resident
Pursuing a graduate degree at an accredited college or university in the US or Canada
At least one full academic year of formal coursework remaining, enrolled and in residence for the whole year
Intends to return to her home country to use her education to foster world peace
Not eligible as a first-time applicant if only the dissertation remains; online-only study, research or internships without coursework do not qualify
documents: Statement of other financial resources (family support, waivers, work, assistantships, other scholarships)
opportunities.selection_process: Need-based; the IPS Board of Trustees selects recipients and awards are announced in May.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the IPS form on the P.E.O. online application portal (CommunityForce) between 15 September and 15 December. Read the IPS policies and procedures document first.

opportunities.title: Politecnico di Milano Merit-Based Scholarships for International MSc Students 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc at Politecnico di Milano for 2027-28, who paid the application fee by 1 December 2026, can apply for one of 64 merit awards by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Politecnico di Milano, Italy's largest technical university, offers 64 merit-based scholarships to international students entering the first year of its English-taught Laurea Magistrale (MSc) programmes in the 2027-2028 academic year. The awards cover programmes on the Milan campus and on the regional campuses of Piacenza, Cremona, Lecco and Mantova.

Every award includes a waiver of the tuition fee, and most also pay a cash grant of EUR 2,500 to EUR 10,000 for the year. The application window ran from 1 October 2026 and closes at 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026; to qualify, students must have applied for admission and paid the application fee between 1 October and 1 December 2026.

The scholarships are a good fit for African engineering, architecture and design graduates who want a well-ranked European technical degree at moderate cost. Priority is given to students from countries affected by war or civil conflict, and the commission also considers geographic balance and gender balance.
opportunities.benefits: All awards waive the tuition fee for the year (students still pay an administrative fee of about EUR 170-190 and insurance). Platinum (10 awards, Milan): EUR 10,000 gross paid in two instalments of EUR 5,000. Gold (18, Milan): EUR 8,000 gross in two instalments. Gold Piacenza (16; SAL, LLH and RES programmes): EUR 5,000 gross in two instalments. Bronze (10, Piacenza; Mechanical Engineering and Mechatronics for Manufacturing): EUR 2,500 in one payment. Silver (10; Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza): tuition waiver only. Awards can be renewed for year two if the student earns 1,000 points (Platinum) or 700 points (other awards) by 10 August 2028.
requirements: International student
Admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc (Laurea Magistrale) for 2027-2028
MSc application fee paid between 1 October and 1 December 2026
Strong grade average and academic record
Valid English language certificate, verified by the International Students Office (by 4 March 2027 according to the page)
documents: Scholarship application form in Politecnico Online Services

opportunities.selection_process: A university commission ranks candidates on academic merit (grade average and achievements), how well their previous studies match the chosen MSc, their documents and the form. Priority goes to students from countries affected by military aggression or civil war, and geographic origin, gender balance and age are also considered. Results come three to four months after the deadline.

Then fill in the merit-based scholarship form in the same portal before 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026. Questions go to international-scholarships@polimi.it.
opportunities.notes: The page and the official call give slightly different administrative fees (about EUR 170 versus about EUR 190). Egyptian, Ethiopian, Ghanaian and Tunisian students can also look at the Italian government's Invest Your Talent in Italy scheme.

Two sessions run each year, with one intern selected per session, and a successful internship counts in the candidate's favour in later PhD admission.

For African students interested in language technology, this is a supported way to test a research career in a leading European NLP group.

documents: CV naming your programme and university
Transcript with grades and the grading scale
Proposed topics or project proposal and preferred supervisors

important_dates: Internship period: roughly March to May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ÚFAL is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at Charles University in Prague and is one of Europe's major centres for computational linguistics and natural language processing.

opportunities.title: Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowship in Engineering 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who completed, or will complete, a doctorate between June 2025 and September 2027 can apply for a two-year engineering postdoc at Notre Dame.

The fellowship pays a $75,000 annual stipend and a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development. Scholars of all nationalities can apply, which makes it open to African engineers who have recently finished, or are about to finish, a PhD.

The programme aims to develop future leaders in engineering research, so applicants need a clear research plan at the forefront of their field.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of $75,000 a year for 24 months plus a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development.

Open to scholars of all nationalities
Primary mentor from the College of Engineering
Current Notre Dame postdocs are not eligible

opportunities.title: SFU Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarships (international) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High school students worldwide with at least a 90% average (or 31 IB points) who apply for fall entry to SFU can apply for an entrance scholarship worth up to $140,000.

Academic and extracurricular excellence
Must submit a separate scholarship application

opportunities.title: Cumbria International Undergraduate Scholarship 2027

opportunities.title: French-African Foundation Young Leaders Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African (or French) nationals aged 28 to 40 with at least five years of professional experience, demonstrated leadership and fluent English.
opportunities.description:
The Young Leaders Program is the flagship initiative of the French-African Foundation. Each edition brings together a class of rising leaders from African countries and France for two intensive weeks, one spent in France and one in an African host country, built around meetings with influential figures, expert-led training, exchanges with decision-makers and mentoring.

The programme runs under the high patronage of the President of France and the President of the African host country. Previous editions were held in Senegal (2021), Rwanda (2023) and Madagascar (2025); the 2025 class of 30 laureates was chosen from more than 8,000 applications from over 40 African countries and France. The 2027 host country and exact dates have not yet been announced on the page.

The programme is aimed at mid-career professionals in any sector (business, public service, civil society, culture, science) who already have a record of impact and want to build lasting bridges between Africa and France. Being selected gives access to a high-level Africa-France network.
opportunities.benefits: Two weeks of leadership training, mentoring, networking and meetings with senior decision-makers in France and an African country, plus membership of the Young Leaders network. The page does not state whether travel or accommodation costs are covered.

Fluent English

opportunities.selection_process: An independent, high-level jury that is renewed each year assesses applicants on excellence, commitment and potential, and selects the class of laureates.
important_dates: Programme: two weeks in 2027 (dates and African host country to be announced)
opportunities.about_provider: The French-African Foundation is a foundation that works to strengthen ties between African countries and France by connecting leaders from both. The Young Leaders Program is its flagship initiative.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the programme page (https://form.typeform.com/to/IG4sh2v4) before 16 December 2026 at 3:00 PM GMT. Questions can be sent to communication@french-african.org.
opportunities.notes: Competition is very strong (over 8,000 applicants for 30 places in 2025), so show concrete impact and a clear Africa-France angle. The page does not mention a stipend or travel cover, so confirm costs with the foundation.
