opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) that organises scientific conferences across the life sciences. Alongside its meetings it runs financial-aid schemes, including student and postdoc scholarships and Global Health Awards, the latter supported in part by the Gates Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the meeting page and pay the refundable abstract fee, then complete the scholarship (or Global Health Award) application on Keystone's SurveyMonkey Apply portal (keystonesymposia.smapply.us) and arrange for your mentor's letter. All deadlines close at 11:59 pm US Mountain Standard Time. Questions on scholarships go to scholarships@keystonesymposia.org.
opportunities.notes: One scholarship per meeting year and one per lab. Scholarships are reimbursed after the meeting, so keep all receipts. Keystone also lists Early-Career Travel Awards and student discounts on its financial-aid pages.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Epigenetics in Health and Disease (D4) Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs (within 8 years of their doctorate) who will present a poster in person; apply by 17 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Keystone Symposia offers scholarships to help graduate students and postdoctoral fellows attend its scientific meetings in person. This award is for the 2027 meeting "Epigenetics in Health and Disease" (D4), organised by Liling Wan of the University of Pennsylvania and Bradley Bernstein of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

The meeting runs from 12 to 15 April 2027 at the Rimrock Resort in Banff, Alberta, Canada, and can also be followed by livestream or on demand. It brings together researchers working on chromatin, gene regulation and the epigenetic basis of disease.

Scholarship holders must attend in person and present a poster, so the award is a practical way for early-career African researchers in molecular biology, genetics or biomedical science to present their work at a high-level international meeting and meet leaders in the field.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 1,500 USD towards in-person attendance, covering airfare (some restrictions apply), ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee. It is paid as a reimbursement against receipts. A refundable 50 USD abstract fee applies for in-person meetings.
requirements: Graduate student working towards a higher degree, or postdoctoral fellow within 8 years of a PhD, MD or DVM (counted at the meeting start date)
Enrolled or employed in that role at the start of the meeting
Must attend in person and present a poster abstract
One scholarship per person per meeting year (1 July to 30 June)
One application per abstract and one award per lab
documents: Abstract of up to 1,000 words with authors and affiliations
Letter from your mentor, submitted on your behalf
opportunities.selection_process: The meeting organisers review applications and score the abstract on its relevance to the meeting topic, the significance of the question and results, and the style and clarity of presentation.
important_dates: Scholarship and short-talk abstract deadline: 17 December 2026 (11:59 pm US Mountain time)
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia is a non-profit organisation based in the United States that runs scientific conferences in the life sciences around the world. It funds scholarships and travel awards to widen participation by early-career scientists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract and scholarship application through the Keystone Symposia financial aid portal (keystonesymposia.smapply.us) before 17 December 2026, and ask your mentor to upload their letter. The organisation's scholarship user guide explains each step; contact scholarships@keystonesymposia.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: Start early, as the portal has several steps. NIH employees receive registration only.

opportunities.title: GAAAH 2027 Conference Call for Papers: Under Siege but Undefeated
opportunities.provider: Graduate Association for African American History, University of Memphis
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate and undergraduate students working on any topic in Black Studies can submit a paper or panel proposal by 18 December 2026 for the GAAAH conference in Memphis, 24-26 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Graduate Association for African American History (GAAAH) at the University of Memphis is inviting proposals for its 2027 annual conference, themed "Under Siege but Undefeated: Countering the Erasure of Black History". The conference takes place from 24 to 26 February 2027 at the Maxine A. Smith University Center on the Memphis campus in Tennessee, with historian and writer Dr Clint Smith as keynote speaker.

The organisers welcome papers on any subject within Black Studies, from any discipline and using any method, which makes the call relevant to students researching Africa, the African diaspora and transatlantic Black history. Both individual papers and complete panels can be proposed.

The meeting is run by graduate students for graduate and undergraduate presenters, so it is a supportive first conference for early researchers. Limited travel funding is available from the university's African and African American Studies programme on a first-come, first-served basis.
opportunities.benefits: Limited travel funding from the University of Memphis African and African American Studies (AAAS) Program, given first-come, first-served; no amounts are published. No registration fee is mentioned in the call.
requirements: Graduate or undergraduate student
Paper on any topic within Black Studies
Individual paper or full panel proposal
Able to present in person in Memphis, 24-26 February 2027
documents: Individual paper: abstract of up to 300 words, paper title, CV or resume and email address
Panel: one email with a 200-word panel description plus each panellist's CV and email
Full paper by 31 January 2027 if accepted
opportunities.selection_process: The GAAAH organising committee reviews proposals and notifies applicants by 8 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: GAAAH is a graduate student association in the Department of History at the University of Memphis that organises an annual conference on African American and Black history.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract, title and CV (or the panel package) to the GAAAH president, Neil Sharma, at the address in the call PDF by 18 December 2026. For travel funding, contact Dr Brian Kwoba of the AAAS Program early, since support is first-come, first-served.
opportunities.notes: The call says students 'from around the country' are welcome; it does not exclude international presenters, but international participants need their own US visa and should ask about travel funding as early as possible.

opportunities.title: H2O'Lyon Water Science/Collegium Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: H2O'Lyon Graduate School and Collegium de Lyon
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Professors or equivalent researchers based outside France with a freshwater research project; apply by 18 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The H2O'Lyon Water Science/Collegium Fellowship brings an established researcher from outside France to Lyon for a residential stay devoted to freshwater research. It is offered jointly by the Collegium de Lyon, the Université de Lyon's institute for advanced study, and the H2O'Lyon graduate school, and each fellow is matched with one of H2O'Lyon's partner laboratories.

The fellowship lasts between 5 and 10 months during the academic year, from September 2027 to June 2028. Fellows live at the Collegium's residence and work on a project on freshwater issues such as hydrology, water quality, aquatic ecosystems or water and society.

For senior African researchers working on water resources, this offers time away from teaching, a furnished apartment and contact with a large interdisciplinary water science community in France.
opportunities.benefits: Furnished, all-inclusive accommodation in a Collegium apartment (household insurance not included), administrative support, a monthly stipend of 1,100 EUR and payment of travel costs.
requirements: Holds a professorship or an equivalent research position at an academic institution outside France
A research project on freshwater issues that fits an H2O'Lyon partner laboratory
Available for a 5 to 10 month residence between September 2027 and June 2028
documents: Completed application form (downloadable from the official page)
Research project description as requested in the form
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed on 13 January 2027 and results are announced at the end of January 2027. The page does not list detailed criteria.
important_dates: Fellowship period: September 2027 to June 2028 (5 to 10 months)
opportunities.about_provider: The Collegium de Lyon is the institute for advanced study of the Université de Lyon and a member of the French network of institutes for advanced study. H2O'Lyon is a graduate school that brings together Lyon's laboratories working on water science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the application form from the Collegium de Lyon call page, complete it with your project, and email it with your CV to h2olyon@univ-lyon1.fr by 18 December 2026. Be ready for an interview on 13 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The Collegium runs other 2027-2028 fellowships with Inria, INSERM and SHAPE-Med@Lyon (One Health).

opportunities.title: Internet Society Fellowship Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Emerging internet leaders worldwide.

opportunities.title: Call for Chapters: Indigenous Worlds in Transition (Society, Ecology and Justice among Tribal and Marginalised Communities)
opportunities.provider: Jananayak Chandrashekhar University, Ballia and Banaras Hindu University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can send chapter proposals for an edited volume on tribal and marginalised communities, ecology and justice.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EMMIR Migration and Intercultural Relations scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in social sciences and related fields with at least a C+ average and English proficiency; apply by 20 December 2026 for scholarships.
opportunities.description:
EMMIR, the European Master in Migration and Intercultural Relations, is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's programme coordinated by the University of Oldenburg in Germany. Edition 14 runs from 2027 to 2029 and offers full scholarships as well as tuition-free and fee-paying places.

The two-year programme is taught by a consortium of eight universities in Europe, Africa and Asia, with study periods in cities such as Oldenburg, Stavanger, Nova Gorica, Prague, Accra, Mbarara and Kolkata. Students learn migration theory, intercultural relations and empirical research methods, and spend time at several partner institutions.

Because the consortium includes African partners and the programme focuses on migration in the Global South as well as Europe, it is especially relevant for African graduates in social sciences, law, development studies or journalism who want an international, fully funded master's degree.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus+ scholarship (limited, merit-based): 1,400 EUR per month for 24 months, plus health insurance and university registration and service fees; travel between study sites is paid from the stipend. Non-fee-paying self-funded places: no participation fee, insurance and fees covered, but living and travel costs are your own. Fee-paying self-funded places: 4,500 EUR per semester plus living costs.
requirements: First degree (bachelor's or equivalent) in a related field such as social sciences, history, cultural studies, education, law, economics, development studies or journalism
Final grade of at least C+ or equivalent, shown on the certificate
Documented knowledge of migration studies, intercultural relations and empirical methods
Proof of English proficiency unless a waiver applies (certificates valid for 2 years; TOEFL code 3556)
Last degree normally not older than 5 years (otherwise explain in your statement)
Not a previous holder of an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship
documents: Final degree certificate or transcript showing the final grade
opportunities.selection_process: A Consortium Selection Board assesses the level and relevance of academic qualifications, research or professional experience, motivation and knowledge of second or third languages. Hard copies are verified after the admission notice. EMMIR does not pre-check eligibility.
important_dates: Deadline for scholarship and non-fee-paying places: 20 December 2026
Fee-paying places: open until filled, at the latest 15 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Oldenburg is a public university in north-west Germany and coordinates the EMMIR consortium. EMMIR has been running as an Erasmus Mundus programme for over a decade with partners on three continents.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the requirements and application procedures on emmir.org, then submit the online application through the EMMIR application platform by 20 December 2026 with your degree documents, language proof and statement of purpose. Questions should be sent through the official contact page only; EMMIR has no official social media groups.
opportunities.notes: Preference goes to applicants with relevant professional experience. The FAQ and application procedures pages answer most questions.

opportunities.title: European Youth Assembly 2027 (Amsterdam, Mar 2027)
opportunities.provider: Center for International Policy and Sustainability (CIPS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people of any nationality, generally aged 17 to 47, can apply for funded seats by 20 December 2026 (application fee applies).
opportunities.description:
The European Youth Assembly 2027 is a four-day youth leadership and policy event in Amsterdam, organised by the Center for International Policy and Sustainability (CIPS), a Canada-based organisation. Despite the name, the organisers state that it has no link to the European Union or its institutions.

The assembly takes place from 17 to 20 March 2027 and offers sessions, networking, a certificate and speaking opportunities. CIPS offers a limited number of fully funded and partially funded seats through a competitive application, alongside paid passes sold first come, first served.

Applicants from any country and discipline can apply, generally aged 17 to 47. African applicants should read the package details carefully: the funded seats require a non-refundable application fee, and the official page describes the partially funded and free pass packages inconsistently.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded seats (30): round-trip airfare support, hotel in Amsterdam, breakfast, visa invitation and support, meals and coffee breaks during sessions, certificate, merchandise and a speaking opportunity. Partially funded seats (20) and free assembly passes (50) are also listed, but the page's descriptions of what they include are inconsistent. Paid direct-access passes cost 499 USD without accommodation or 799 USD with accommodation; a visa invitation letter alone costs 99 USD.
requirements: Generally aged 17 to 47
Open to all nationalities and disciplines
Non-refundable application fee of 17.99 USD for funded-seat consideration (it does not guarantee selection)
Ability to travel to Amsterdam for 17 to 20 March 2027
opportunities.selection_process: Funded seats are awarded through a rubric-based merit review looking at application quality, motivation and potential, leadership and impact, relevance and contribution, diversity and representation, and overall profile.
opportunities.about_provider: The Center for International Policy and Sustainability (CIPS) is an organisation based in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada, that runs international youth assemblies and leadership events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the funded application form on the CIPS website and pay the 17.99 USD application fee by 20 December 2026. Alternatively, buy a direct-access pass on the CIPS site while seats last. Questions go to contact@thecips.org.
opportunities.notes: This is a private, fee-charging event, not an EU programme. Check the CIPS refund policy and confirm exactly what your seat includes before paying.

opportunities.title: Killam Postdoctoral Fellowships at Dalhousie University 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhD graduates (Sept 2023 to Sept 2027) from institutions other than Dalhousie, in any discipline; apply by 20 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Killam Postdoctoral Fellowships at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Canada, are prestigious two-year awards funded by the Killam Trusts. They are open to recent PhD graduates in all disciplines who want to carry out an independent research programme at Dalhousie.

Fellows receive a substantial salary with benefits, relocation support and research and travel allowances. Applicants must have earned their PhD elsewhere, and must never have held an academic or other job at Dalhousie.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African researchers who completed or will complete a PhD between September 2023 and September 2027 can apply. Contacting the intended department early is essential, because faculty support for the proposed project is part of the process.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 60,000 CAD per year for up to two years, made up of a 50,000 CAD taxable stipend with full benefits, a relocation allowance, a one-time 3,000 CAD research allowance and a 1,000 CAD conference travel grant. Up to 12 months of parental leave is available, with four months supported by Killam.
requirements: PhD completed, or to be completed, at an institution other than Dalhousie between 15 September 2023 and 30 September 2027
Never held any academic or employment position at Dalhousie
Support from the intended Dalhousie department and faculty host
Open to all disciplines
documents: Application through the Faculty of Graduate Studies online scholarship portal
Full application package as set out in the 2027 competition guidelines (research proposal, CV and supporting letters)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged 50% on research excellence and leadership and 50% on the quality of the proposed research programme, using criteria comparable to Canada's tri-agency postdoctoral awards. Results are sent in March 2027.
important_dates: Application deadline: 20 December 2026, 11:59 pm Atlantic time
opportunities.about_provider: Dalhousie University is a major research university in Halifax, Nova Scotia. The Killam Trusts, established by the Killam family, fund Killam scholarships and fellowships at a small group of Canadian universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First contact your intended Dalhousie department to confirm the project is feasible and that a supervisor will support it. Then complete the application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies online scholarship portal by 20 December 2026, following the competition guidelines. Questions go to the Scholarships Liaison Officer at fgs.slo@dal.ca.
opportunities.notes: Dalhousie also offers Donald Hill Family Postdoctoral Fellowships and hosts Canada Postdoctoral Research Awards.

opportunities.title: World Physiotherapy Congress 2027 Bursary (Guadalajara)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Qualified physiotherapists who are nationals and residents of a low or lower-middle income country whose national association pays World Physiotherapy's reduced membership fee can apply by 21 December 2026 for a bursary to attend the 2027 congress in Mexico.
opportunities.description:
World Physiotherapy offers a limited number of bursaries so that physiotherapists from low and lower-middle income countries can attend the World Physiotherapy Congress 2027, held in Guadalajara, Mexico, from 14 to 16 May 2027. The congress, hosted with the Mexican physiotherapy association AMEFI, is the main global meeting of the profession, with three days of scientific sessions, networking and professional development.

A bursary can be full or partial and pays the main costs of attending, from travel and hotel to registration and visa. Applicants do not need an accepted abstract. The application form closes at 23:59 UTC on 21 December 2026, and applicants are told the outcome in February 2027.

The award is designed for physiotherapists who will bring what they learn back to their workplace and country, so it suits African clinicians, educators and postgraduate physiotherapy students whose national association is a World Physiotherapy member paying the reduced fee.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial support covering an economy return flight or ground transport, four nights' hotel with breakfast, full three-day congress registration, an allowance of USD 60 for local transport and meals, travel insurance, the visa fee and a social event ticket where applicable. Extra events, personal expenses and travel to embassies are not covered.
requirements: Qualified physiotherapist who is employed or enrolled in a relevant postgraduate programme (entry-level students are not eligible)
Member in good standing of a World Physiotherapy member organisation
National and resident of a low or lower-middle income country whose member organisation pays the reduced membership fee
Commitment to return to your home country after the congress
Not a previous bursary recipient
Evidence of efforts to find other funding
opportunities.selection_process: A World Physiotherapy panel reviews applications against five outcome-based criteria: the benefit to the applicant's professional development, how learning will be shared with the employer, the local impact, the contribution to developing the profession, and the applicant's efforts to secure other funding.
opportunities.about_provider: World Physiotherapy (formerly the World Confederation for Physical Therapy, WCPT) is the global body representing physiotherapists through its national member organisations. It organises the World Physiotherapy Congress every two years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online bursary application on the congress's Oxford Abstracts portal, linked from the bursary page, before 21 December 2026. Explain how attending will benefit you, your employer and physiotherapy in your country, and what other funding you have sought.
opportunities.notes: Recipients must send a report within one month of the congress. The abstract call for the congress closed on 29 September 2026.

opportunities.title: University of Pisa Winter School 2027: EU Fundamental Values and a Fair, Rules-based Global Order
opportunities.provider: Università di Pisa / Jean Monnet Centre EU4GlobalOrder
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to students at any level, researchers and professionals with a secondary school diploma and an interest in EU and international law; apply by 22 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
This short school at the University of Pisa looks at how the European Union's founding values can support a fair, rules-based international order and a more inclusive, effective multilateral system. It is run with the Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence EU4GlobalOrder and combines lectures, small-group work and a moot court exercise over four days.

The school takes place from 1 to 4 February 2027 at Palazzo della Sapienza in Pisa, with the option of following online through Microsoft Teams. It amounts to 32 hours of teaching in English and carries 3 ECTS credits for participants who attend at least 90% of the sessions. Up to 100 people can take part, and the course only runs if at least 10 enrol.

The audience is unusually broad: undergraduates, master's and PhD students, postdocs, lecturers, school teachers, lawyers, civil servants, politicians and staff of international organisations can all apply. For African applicants interested in EU law, international law and multilateral diplomacy, the online option and the tuition-only scholarships make it a low-cost way to earn European credits and build a network.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition is 250 EUR. The EU4GlobalOrder Jean Monnet Centre awards scholarships case by case that cover the tuition fee (250 EUR) only. Travel, meals and accommodation are not covered. Participants who attend at least 90% of the course receive 3 ECTS credits.
requirements: A secondary school (high school) diploma
A demonstrated interest in European Union law and international law
Working command of English (no specific test or score is required)
Open to students at any level, PhD candidates, postdocs, academics, teachers, lawyers, civil servants and international-organisation staff
Availability to attend at least 90% of the 32 hours to earn the 3 ECTS credits
documents: Passport (for foreign applicants) or other identity document
Completed enrolment form, signed in both places
Any further document requested on the school's page
opportunities.selection_process: The official page does not describe a ranking or interview. Applicants upload their documents through the university portal and receive an admission letter; tuition scholarships are decided case by case by the Jean Monnet Centre. The course is activated only if at least 10 students enrol.
important_dates: School dates: 1 to 4 February 2027 (in Pisa and online)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Pisa is one of Italy's oldest public universities and runs an international programme of short summer and winter schools. The EU4GlobalOrder Jean Monnet Centre of Excellence, based in its law department, works on the EU's role in the global legal order and funds the school's scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the University of Pisa's Alice student portal (studenti.unipi.it), following the university's step-by-step summer and winter school guide, upload the identity document, signed enrolment form and CV, and enrol in this school before 22 December 2026. Pay the 250 EUR fee through the Pago Atenei system only after you receive the admission letter. Questions go to support.summerschool@unipi.it.
opportunities.notes: An Italian tax code or residence permit is not needed to apply. The fee is non-refundable unless the course is cancelled. The page sometimes calls it a summer school, but the dates are 1 to 4 February 2027. Coordinator: Prof. Leonardo Pasquali.

opportunities.title: Peking University Scholarships for New International Graduate Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese citizens applying to full-time master's or PhD programmes at Peking University for September 2027 can be considered for its scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Peking University (PKU) is accepting applications from international students for full-time master's and doctoral programmes starting in September 2027, and applicants can be considered for several scholarships at the same time. These include the PKU Scholarship for New International Students, the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B, university programme) and the Beijing Government Scholarship.

Admission follows an 'application plus examination' model: the International Student Division checks the file, then each school's expert panel reviews it and runs a second-round assessment between January and March 2027. Programmes are offered in Chinese and in English across PKU's campuses in Beijing and its Shenzhen Graduate School.

For African graduates, this is a route to one of China's top two universities with funding that can cover tuition, housing, living costs and insurance. The first-round window runs until 25 December 2026, so documents such as authenticated degree certificates should be prepared early.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) offers full or partial cover of tuition, accommodation, living allowance and medical insurance; the PKU Scholarship for New International Students covers full or partial tuition, living expenses and medical insurance; the Beijing Government Scholarship (Types A, B, C) ranges from tuition and insurance up to tuition, housing, a living stipend and insurance. The page does not give amounts.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen with a valid passport, in good health and with no criminal record
Master's: bachelor's degree recognised by China's Ministry of Education
PhD: master's degree (bachelor's holders may apply to some science and engineering PhDs)
Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 6 with at least 200 (sciences) or 210 (humanities) and writing 65 or more
English-taught programmes: TOEFL, GRE (above 315) or other proof as each programme sets
Beijing Government Scholarship age limits: master's 35 or under, PhD 40 or under
documents: Personal statement and research plan (about 1,500 words for master's, 3,000 for PhD)
Any extra materials required by the school
opportunities.selection_process: The International Student Division first checks eligibility, then school expert panels review the files and hold a second-round assessment (January to March 2027) of research ability, language and potential. A preliminary admission list is released by the end of May 2027.
important_dates: Preliminary admission list: by end of May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Peking University, founded in 1898, is one of China's leading comprehensive research universities. Its International Student Division handles admission and scholarships for degree-seeking international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through PKU's International Student Service System (studyatpku.com), choosing up to two programmes and paying the non-refundable RMB 800 fee per programme. Indicate the scholarships you wish to be considered for, upload all documents and submit before 25 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Master's programmes last 2 to 3 years and PhDs 4 to 5 years. Beijing Government Scholarship holders cannot hold another Chinese government or PKU scholarship. Check each school's catalogue for language scores, as the general guide's TOEFL figure is unclear.

opportunities.title: Sahmyook University International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarships 2027 (second round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International freshmen applying in the 8 to 29 December 2026 round receive tuition waivers tiered by TOPIK level.

opportunities.title: Field Museum African Visiting Scholars 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African researchers, academics, postdocs and master's or PhD students based at an African institution, with a Field Museum sponsor; apply by 30 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Field Museum in Chicago runs the African Visiting Scholars programme to bring African researchers to work with its collections from Africa. This is the eighth call, and it funds a research visit to Chicago in 2027 for scientists who live and work on the African continent.

Scholars use the museum's collections and facilities to study African biodiversity, cultures, geology or conservation, ideally building on historic African material held in Chicago and strengthening links between the museum and African institutions. Funding begins in late January 2027 and visits should take place during 2027 unless the museum approves otherwise.

Only two awards are made in this round, and priority goes to people who have not received the scholarship before. Because every applicant needs a Field Museum scientist as sponsor, the key first step is to contact a curator or researcher whose work matches your project well before the deadline.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 9,000 USD per award, covering travel, lodging, living costs in Chicago and visa fees. Two awards are available. Under US rules the scholarship counts as taxable income.
requirements: African scientist living and working in Africa
Research scholar, professor or postdoc affiliated with an academic institution; master's and PhD students are also eligible (undergraduates are not)
A sponsor among the Field Museum's full-time regular scientific staff (PhD preferred, at least an MSc); postdocs cannot sponsor
Each sponsor can endorse at most two applicants
A project that uses Field Museum collections, with emphasis on African biodiversity, culture, geology or conservation
Priority to applicants who have not received this scholarship before
documents: A single PDF with: a research proposal of no more than 2 pages on the museum's template
The 'CAT Communication' email from your sponsor, copying the relevant collections team
A Museum Facilities Approval Letter if you will use laboratories
An endorsement letter from your Field Museum sponsor, submitted through the official online form
One external recommendation letter, submitted through the official online form
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are judged on how well they use the museum's collections, especially historic African material, how they advance research on African biodiversity, culture, geology or conservation, and how they strengthen links with African institutions. Only two scholars are funded, with priority for first-time recipients.
opportunities.about_provider: The Field Museum is a natural history museum in Chicago with large scientific collections and research staff in biology, anthropology and geology. Its African Visiting Scholars programme is aimed at deepening research ties with institutions in Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact a Field Museum scientist to agree on a project and secure their sponsorship, then prepare the 2-page proposal on the template. Submit the single PDF through the application form linked on the official page, and ask your sponsor and external referee to send their letters through the separate online letter form by 30 December 2026; emailed or paper letters are not accepted. Questions go to scholarship@fieldmuseum.org.
opportunities.notes: Only the four listed items may go in the PDF. Letters sent by email or post are not accepted.

opportunities.title: IEEE ICME 2027 Call for Papers (Xiamen, Jul 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to researchers worldwide working on multimedia; regular papers are due 30 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
IEEE ICME, the International Conference on Multimedia and Expo, is the flagship multimedia research meeting of the IEEE and is sponsored by four IEEE societies. The 2027 edition invites regular papers, special-session papers and proposals across multimedia signal processing, systems, communications, analysis and applications.

The conference will be held in Xiamen, China, from 13 to 17 July 2027, with oral and poster sessions, tutorials, workshops, special sessions and grand challenges. Accepted papers are reviewed by peers through Microsoft CMT, with an author rebuttal period in early 2027.

The call is open to the whole multimedia research community, so African master's and PhD students, postdocs and faculty working on audio, video, image, vision or multimedia AI can submit. The conference pages do not mention travel grants, so authors should plan their own funding and request a visa invitation letter early.
opportunities.benefits: This is a call for papers with no award or stipend. Accepted authors present at IEEE ICME 2027 and their papers enter the conference proceedings. The organisers can provide an invitation letter for visa applications. Registration fees are not given on the pages reviewed.
requirements: Original research paper in multimedia or a related field
Submission through Microsoft CMT by the paper deadline
At least one author must register by the camera-ready deadline (10 May 2027)
No nationality, degree or age restrictions are stated
documents: Full paper prepared to the ICME 2027 author guidelines
Rebuttal response during the rebuttal window, if needed
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed through Microsoft CMT, with an author rebuttal period from 26 February to 4 March 2027. Acceptance is announced on 24 March 2027.
important_dates: Regular paper deadline (including special sessions): 30 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: IEEE is the world's largest technical professional organisation. ICME is jointly sponsored by the IEEE Signal Processing, Circuits and Systems, Communications and Computer societies and is one of the main venues for multimedia research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the call for papers on the ICME 2027 website, prepare your paper to the author guidelines and submit it through the Microsoft CMT system by 30 December 2026. Respond during the rebuttal window if invited, and if accepted, upload the camera-ready version and register an author by 10 May 2027.
opportunities.notes: Submission opened in early November 2026. The pages reviewed list no travel grants or student support. Proposals for workshops, tutorials and grand challenges have earlier deadlines.

opportunities.title: 3rd GHI World Congress 2027 (Konya): call for abstracts
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Food-science researchers worldwide may submit abstracts by 31 December 2026 to the GHI World Congress in Konya, Türkiye (no travel funding).
opportunities.description:
The 3rd World Congress of the Global Harmonization Initiative (GHI2027) is an international scientific meeting on food safety, food regulation and food systems. It invites abstracts for oral and poster presentations on nine themes, including regulatory alignment, climate and risk, trade, AI and data, novel foods, food processing, ethics, laboratory methods and future scenarios.

The congress takes place in Konya, Türkiye, from 5 to 9 July 2027. Accepted abstracts appear in a Book of Abstracts with an ISBN, and authors can later submit full papers to an invited journal issue.

It suits African food scientists, nutritionists and regulators who want to present work on harmonising food-safety rules. Young-scientist and poster awards are offered, but the organisers do not pay travel costs.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at the congress and publication in the Book of Abstracts; three young-scientist awards and three poster awards. Submission, travel and accommodation are not paid by the organisers. Up to two abstracts per person are included in the registration fee.
requirements: Abstract in English, one paragraph of at most 300 words (about 2,000 characters), no references
Title of at most 20 words without abbreviations
Research abstracts structured as introduction, purpose, methods, results and conclusions
Up to 10 authors and one presenting author marked with an asterisk; the presenter must register
documents: Abstract submitted through the online form (one figure, table or photo allowed)
opportunities.selection_process: The scientific committee reviews abstracts and notifies authors by 30 January 2027.
important_dates: Presenting author registration for the Book of Abstracts: by 30 April 2027
Full papers for the invited journal: 31 December 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Global Harmonization Initiative is an international network of scientists and organisations that works to harmonise food-safety regulations and legislation worldwide based on science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the abstract following the guidelines and submit it through the Submit Your Abstract form on the congress website by 31 December 2026. Questions go to 2027@ghiworldcongress.org.
opportunities.notes: The guidelines page also mentions withdrawal of abstracts if the author is not registered by 30 January 2027, which conflicts with the 30 April date; confirm with the organisers. Hotels are expected to sell out early.

opportunities.title: AUTOMATION 2027: 31st Conference on Automation, Innovations and Future Perspectives (Call for Papers)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from any country working on automation and robotics; full papers due 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
AUTOMATION 2027 is the 31st edition of a long-running conference on automation, control, robotics and measurement, organised by the Łukasiewicz Research Network's Industrial Research Institute for Automation and Measurements (PIAP) in Warsaw. It is scientifically sponsored by the Automatic Control and Robotics Committee of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

The conference takes place at PIAP in Warsaw from 5 to 7 May 2027. Papers of 6 to 10 pages are presented orally in English or Polish, and full texts in English are published by Springer in its Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems series, which is indexed in Scopus.

The organisers welcome contributions from domestic and foreign research centres, so African engineers and graduate students in control, robotics, mechatronics or industrial automation can submit. A reduced student fee makes it a relatively affordable venue for a Springer publication.
opportunities.benefits: This is a call for papers with no funding. Accepted papers are published in Springer's Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems (Scopus-indexed). Conference fee: 400 EUR for the first paper, 160 EUR per additional paper, and 200 EUR for bachelor's, master's or doctoral students.
requirements: Original paper on automation, control, robotics or measurement, not submitted elsewhere
Length of 6 to 10 pages following Springer's author instructions
Full text in English
Payment of the conference fee by 15 April 2027
documents: Invoice details (tax number) for the conference fee
opportunities.selection_process: Submitted papers are peer reviewed and authors are notified on 22 February 2027. Detailed criteria are not stated.
important_dates: Author registration and full paper deadline (extended): 31 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: PIAP is part of the Łukasiewicz Research Network, Poland's largest applied research network. It develops robots, automation and measurement systems and has run the AUTOMATION conference for three decades.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an EasyChair account and submit your full paper to the automation2027 conference by 31 December 2026. If accepted, pay the conference fee by bank transfer by 15 April 2027. Contact konferencja@piap.lukasiewicz.gov.pl with questions.
opportunities.notes: Web of Science indexing of the proceedings is not guaranteed.

opportunities.title: CEPE 2027 (Computer Ethics: Philosophical Enquiry) call for papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open call for research on computer and information ethics; submissions due 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
CEPE (Computer Ethics: Philosophical Enquiry) is a long-running international conference on the ethics of computing and information technology. The 2027 edition, hosted through the University of Turku with the International Society for Ethics and Information Technology (INSEIT), invites abstracts, full papers, panels and roundtables.

The conference takes place from 26 to 28 May 2027. Submissions go through double-blind peer review, accepted abstracts appear in the book of abstracts, and selected full papers can go on to journals connected with the conference.

The call has no stated eligibility limits, so African philosophers, computer scientists, law and policy researchers and graduate students working on AI ethics, data justice, privacy or digital rights can submit. It is a good venue for building ties with the European computer ethics community.
opportunities.benefits: This is a call for papers with no stated funding or fee waivers. Accepted abstracts are published in the book of abstracts, and selected full papers are considered for associated journals.
requirements: Work on the ethics of computing or information technology
Papers of up to 5,000 words excluding the bibliography, or an abstract, panel or roundtable proposal
Submissions prepared for double-blind review
No nationality or degree restrictions are stated
documents: Abstract, full paper (up to 5,000 words excluding bibliography), panel or roundtable proposal
Full manuscript by 15 March 2027 if you want journal consideration
opportunities.selection_process: All submissions are double-blind peer reviewed. Acceptance of abstracts is announced on 31 January 2027.
important_dates: Submission deadline (abstracts, full papers, panels, roundtables): 31 December 2026
Full manuscript (required for journal submission): 15 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: CEPE is the conference series of INSEIT, the International Society for Ethics and Information Technology. The 2027 conference is chaired by Kai Kimppa of the University of Turku in Finland.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your abstract, paper or proposal in anonymised form and email it to INSEIT at director@inseit.eu by 31 December 2026. If accepted and you want journal consideration, send the full manuscript by 15 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: The call page does not state fees, travel grants or the exact venue; check the conference site's travel pages before planning.

opportunities.title: Call for Book Chapters: Social Change and Shared Futures
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open call for social science chapters for an open-access book; full chapters due 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
CalbisPress, an independent academic publisher, is collecting chapters for an edited open-access book titled "Social Change and Shared Futures". The volume is edited by Fatma Halide Kıvrak of Ibn Haldun University in Türkiye and Martin Mulyadi of Shenandoah University in the United States.

Chapters should focus on social processes, institutions, inequality or human development. The provisional table of contents has 40 chapters in five parts, with open slots in each part for new contributions, and publication is expected in April 2027 after review and production.

The call is open with no stated restrictions and welcomes comparative perspectives from under-represented regions. Because there is no chapter fee and the book is gold open access, it is an accessible publishing option for African social scientists and graduate students.
opportunities.benefits: Gold open-access publication with no chapter publication fee. Royalties or honoraria are not stated.
requirements: Chapter on social change, institutions, inequality or human development
Suggested length of 6,000 to 8,000 words
Submission prepared for anonymous peer review
No nationality or career-stage restrictions stated
documents: Title page with author details and author contributions
opportunities.selection_process: Chapters go through editorial assessment and peer review. The table of contents is not final until review is complete, and choosing a slot does not reserve it.
important_dates: Full chapter deadline: 31 December 2026, 23:59 Türkiye time
opportunities.about_provider: CalbisPress is an independent academic publisher based in Istanbul and London, operated by Bussecon International Ltd, that publishes open-access books and journals.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the chapter author guidelines on the CalbisPress site, optionally send an outline to an editor first, and submit the title page and anonymised manuscript through the book's online submission page by 31 December 2026, listing all authors in the metadata.
opportunities.notes: Indexing in services such as Scopus or Web of Science is marked as 'in preparation', not guaranteed. CalbisPress has other open chapter calls listed on its site.

opportunities.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) University Program at Northwestern Polytechnical University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International graduates under 30 (master's) with strong grades and English or Chinese proficiency; first round closes 31 December 2026, second 28 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU) in Xi'an, China, recruits international master's and PhD students for the Chinese Government Scholarship University Program (Type B), in which the university itself nominates candidates to the China Scholarship Council (CSC). NPU is a leading Chinese university for aeronautics, astronautics and marine engineering.

The scholarship covers the full study period of the degree (the master's programme lasts 2.5 years and starts in the autumn). There are two application rounds: the first closes on 31 December 2026 and the second on 28 February 2027.

The programme is open to non-Chinese citizens with good grades and English or Chinese proficiency, so African graduates in engineering and science can apply. Some schools require a supervisor's acceptance letter, so contacting an NPU professor early improves your chances.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition, campus dormitory, monthly stipend (3,000 CNY for master's students, 3,500 CNY for doctoral students) and comprehensive medical insurance (800 CNY per year). Partial scholarships cover one or more of these items. Airfare and visa costs are not mentioned.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen with a valid passport
Under 30 on 1 September 2027 (master's)
Bachelor's degree by 1 September 2027 (master's); master's degree for PhD
Average grade of at least 80% for CSC applicants
English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 5.5), TOEFL 85, Duolingo 120 or PTE 58; or HSK 5 (200+) for Chinese-taught majors
Good physical and mental health
Supervisor acceptance letter for some schools (e.g. aeronautics, astronautics, materials, mechanical, electronics, automation, physics, chemistry, life sciences)
documents: Passport information page (valid to at least 31 December 2027)
Highest degree diploma or pre-graduation certificate
Two recommendation letters from associate or full professors
Study plan on the NPU template
Foreigner physical examination form (within six months)
Bank statement showing at least 5,000 USD
opportunities.selection_process: NPU reviews applications in two rounds and then interviews or tests candidates, usually 7 to 10 working days after each deadline. It then recommends successful candidates to the CSC, whose experts check and confirm the awards.
important_dates: First batch: 1 November to 31 December 2026, 17:00 Beijing time
Second batch: 1 January to 28 February 2027, 17:00 Beijing time
Interviews: 7 to 10 working days after each deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Northwestern Polytechnical University is a public research university in Xi'an, Shaanxi, known for aerospace and engineering. It acts as a host institution for the China Scholarship Council's university programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the NPU online admission portal (admission.nwpu.edu.cn) and pay the non-refundable 600 CNY application fee, then also complete the CSC application form on the Campus China site as instructed. Applications not made through the NPU portal are not accepted. Contact admission-pg@nwpu.edu.cn or internationalcollege@nwpu.edu.cn with questions.
opportunities.notes: You may hold only one scholarship (CSC or NPU). Your chosen programme cannot be changed after admission. A 3,000 CNY deposit is refunded at registration. NPU also offers a President Scholarship and a Xi'an Belt and Road Scholarship.

opportunities.title: CityUHK (Dongguan) International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International (non-Chinese) school leavers aged 18+ with strong A-Level/IB or equivalent results and English scores such as IELTS 6.5.
opportunities.description:
City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) is admitting international students to its four-year bachelor's programmes for 2027 entry, and every admitted applicant is considered for its International Undergraduate Entrance Scholarship. This is the mainland China campus in Dongguan, Guangdong, not the Hong Kong campus.

There are two awards. The Full Scholarship pays full tuition for four years, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living allowance and medical insurance; the International Talent Scholarship pays RMB 50,000 a year towards the four-year programme plus medical insurance. Awards go to applicants with outstanding academic results and achievements, and competition is strong.

Applications are taken in three rounds, and the first round closes on 31 December 2026 (Beijing time). For African school leavers with good A-Level, IB or national results and strong English, it is a way to study in China with most or all costs covered.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship: full tuition for the four-year programme, on-campus accommodation each year, a living allowance of RMB 2,500 per month for 12 months a year, and general medical insurance. International Talent Scholarship: RMB 50,000 per year for the four-year programme plus general medical insurance. (For reference, 2026-entry tuition was RMB 115,000 per year.)
requirements: Foreign citizen without Chinese nationality (Chinese-heritage applicants are screened out by the eligibility survey)
Applicants under the Ministry of Education rule need 4 years of foreign nationality and 2 years living abroad in the last 4 years, as of 30 April of the admission year
At least 18 years old (applicants under 18 need a guardian living in mainland China)
Completed high school with a strong record, e.g. GCE A Level grade E or better in three subjects or IB Diploma 30+; other qualifications assessed case by case
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, PTE 62, TOEFL iBT 79 (older format), SAT EBRW 590, ACT 24 English and 24 Reading, or Cambridge CAE/CPE grade C, taken within 2 years; home-edition tests not accepted
documents: Passport copy and proof of nationality
Qualification or high-school certificate (or enrolment letter)
English test result (waived for native speakers)
Optional: reference letter, talent or competition evidence
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic performance, achievements and overall excellence. Shortlisted applicants are invited to an online interview, then receive a conditional or unconditional offer; scholarships are decided at the same time.
opportunities.about_provider: City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan) is a campus of City University of Hong Kong in Dongguan, in mainland China's Greater Bay Area. It admits international students to English-taught undergraduate programmes through its own international admissions office.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the international admissions system (intladmissions.cityu-dg.edu.cn), complete the eligibility survey and upload the documents. Admitted applicants are considered for the entrance scholarship automatically; apply in round 1 for the best chance. Questions go to intladmissions@cityu-dg.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: The guide prints the new TOEFL score as '4.5 out of 6'; check the exact TOEFL requirement with the university. Fees and residence permit costs (RMB 400-1,000) are extra if not covered.

opportunities.title: DTU PhD scholarship: MRI Radiofrequency Detector Development
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried three-year DTU PhD position open to international applicants with a relevant two-year master's (120 ECTS) and good English.

opportunities.title: Diploma Course in Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (DTM&H) 2027, Hamburg
opportunities.provider: Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine (BNITM)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Qualified medical doctors from any country who are licensed to practise medicine in the country where they graduated; doctors from low- and middle-income countries pay a reduced fee.
opportunities.description:
The Diploma Course in Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (DTM&H) is a full-time, in-person training programme for physicians, run in Hamburg by the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine. The 2027 course runs from 5 April to 25 June 2027 and cannot be followed online.

The course prepares doctors to diagnose, treat and prevent tropical and travel-related diseases, combining lectures with laboratory and microscopy training. It ends with a multiple-choice examination and a practical microscopy exam; participants must attend at least 80% of the course and score at least 60% overall to receive the diploma.

For African doctors the course is relevant because the institute applies a reduced fee to participants from low- and middle-income countries, which covers most of the continent. The separate BNITM scholarship round for the 2027 course has already closed, so applicants now need to fund the reduced fee and living costs themselves or through an employer.
opportunities.benefits: This is a fee-paying course with a reduced rate for applicants from low- and middle-income countries: the regular fee is EUR 4,900 (EUR 500 registration plus EUR 4,400), and the reduced fee is EUR 3,900, based on the World Bank country classification. The fee covers teaching and the examination only; travel, accommodation and living costs (estimated at about EUR 1,500 a month in Hamburg) are not included. The BNITM scholarships for the 2027 course are closed.
requirements: Qualified medical doctor (MD, MBBS or equivalent) from any country
Licence to practise medicine in the country of graduation
Good command of English (no specific test named)
Ability to attend in person in Hamburg for the full course
documents: Proof of medical qualification and licence to practise
opportunities.selection_process: Places are taken through registration; the registration fee is due immediately and the balance by 15 January of the course year. To pass, participants need at least 80% attendance and a combined score of at least 60% in the written and practical microscopy exams.
important_dates: Scholarship information for the 2028 course: August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine, founded in Hamburg in 1900, is Germany's largest institution for research, care and teaching in tropical and infectious diseases. It has offered its diploma course in tropical medicine since 1905.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register online through the BNITM DTM&H registration page and pay the EUR 500 registration fee straight away, then pay the remaining fee by 15 January 2027. Visas and insurance are the participant's own responsibility, so start the German visa process as soon as your place is confirmed.
opportunities.notes: Health insurance is strongly recommended. Doctors who need a scholarship should watch for the 2028 scholarship call, due in August 2027. Contact: tropmed@bnitm.de.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus European Master in Law and Economics (EMLE) 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least 240 ECTS, ideally in law or economics; non-Europeans apply by 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The European Master in Law and Economics (EMLE) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's programme run by a consortium of European universities, with its directorship at the University of Hamburg's Institute of Law and Economics. It trains lawyers and economists to analyse legal rules with economic tools.

The programme lasts one academic year (2027/2028) and is split into three terms, with students moving between two or three partner universities and meeting for a mid-term event. Teaching is in English.

Non-European applicants, including Africans, have an earlier deadline of 31 December 2026. Erasmus+ scholarships go to the highest-ranked students, and a separate outreach scholarship waives tuition for up to two applicants who will go on to teach law and economics at home, which suits African junior lecturers.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus+ scholarship for top-ranked students: a monthly contribution of up to 1,400 EUR towards travel, visa, installation and living costs, plus insurance for the academic year (about 10 merit scholarships per year plus 5 for Erasmus+ target regions). EMLE Outreach Scholarship: full tuition waiver for up to two applicants who will teach law and economics. Tuition without a scholarship is 12,000 EUR for non-European students (7,500 EUR for European students).
requirements: At least 240 ECTS or equivalent prior higher education (normally four years of full-time study)
Degree in law or economics preferred; other degrees accepted with a strong interest in economic analysis of law
Final-year students may apply if they graduate before July 2027

English proof for admitted students: TOEFL iBT 95 (reading 13, listening 12, speaking 18, writing 21) or IELTS Academic 7.0 with no section below 6.0, or Cambridge CPE A-C / CAE A-B; tests not older than two years
Non-European passport holders follow the 31 December deadline
documents: Degree certificate and transcript or degree supplement for each degree (or transcript to date)
One or two recommendation letters on the EMLE form, sent by the referees from professional emails
Proof of residence issued within 12 months before the deadline (passports not accepted)
For the Outreach Scholarship: project plan and institutional endorsement letter sent to application@emle.org
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are ranked: 40% university career (duration, degrees, grades), 25% motivation letter, 25% affinity with law and economics, and 10% recommendation letters. Appeals can be filed within four weeks of the decision.
important_dates: Deadline for non-European applicants: 31 December 2026, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: EMLE is one of the longest-running Erasmus Mundus programmes and is led from the University of Hamburg. It brings together universities across Europe and beyond that specialise in law and economics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online at apply.emle.org before 31 December 2026, uploading transcripts, the motivation letter and proof of residence and arranging for your referees to submit letters on the EMLE form. Outreach Scholarship candidates must also email their project plan and endorsement to application@emle.org before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not reviewed. Holders of Chinese, Indian or Vietnamese degrees need an APS certificate for Hamburg. English test results are only needed after admission.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Plant Health in Sustainable Cropping Systems (PlantHealth), first call
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a 180-ECTS bachelor's in agronomy, agriculture or a related field with some plant-health coursework and B2 English, from any country.
opportunities.description:
PlantHealth is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (120 ECTS) on protecting crops in sustainable farming systems. It is run by a European consortium coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), and students move between partner campuses: UPV in Valencia, AgroParisTech, the University of Göttingen, Institut Agro and the University of Padova. Teaching is in English and French and the programme is delivered in person.

The first application call is open from 1 October to 31 December 2026; online applications must be in before midnight (CET) at the start of 1 January 2027, and results are expected at the end of February 2027. The dates point to a cohort starting in autumn 2027. Only applicants in this first call can be considered for the EU-funded Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarships or consortium grants. A second call (20 May to 15 June 2027) is only for self-funded or externally funded candidates.

For African graduates in agronomy or agriculture, the programme is a fully funded route to training in plant pathology, pest management and crop protection across several European countries, and the scholarship is open to non-EU students.
opportunities.benefits: The Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarship covers 100% of the participation (tuition) costs, health insurance and mandatory academic costs, and pays €1,400 per month for up to 24 months. Without a scholarship, total participation costs are €10,000 for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland (€9,000 for EU/EEA/Swiss students), paid in two instalments; self-funded students may receive an Erasmus+ grant of about €300 per month in the second year.
requirements: An official bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS in agronomy, agriculture or a related field
At least 4 ECTS of coursework in plant health or crop protection
Final-year students may apply if they will graduate before the end of August
English at B2 level shown by IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge (FCE/CAE/CPE), Trinity ISE, ESOL, OTE or PTE (Duolingo, TOEIC and university certificates are not accepted)
Native speakers or graduates taught entirely in English are exempt with proof
Applicants who already received an EMJM scholarship, or who hold another EU grant at the same time, cannot get the scholarship
documents: Two signed and stamped recommendation letters with referee contact details
Motivation statement of up to 1,000 characters in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on academic record (GPA and merits) for 60%, the recommendation letters for 20% and the applicant's motivation for 20%. Scholarships are awarded only to applicants of the first call.
important_dates: First call closes: 31 December 2026 (before 1 January 2027, 00:00 CET)
Second call (self-funded only): 20 May to 15 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The PlantHealth consortium is a group of European universities offering an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the European Union. It is coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València in Spain, with AgroParisTech, Institut Agro, the University of Göttingen and the University of Padova as partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an applicant account and submit the single online form on the PlantHealth portal (planthealth.upv.es/user/create_applicant); the same form is used for scholarship and self-funded applications. Upload your diplomas, transcripts, CV, English certificate and two recommendation letters, and write the short motivation statement in the form before the first-call deadline.
opportunities.notes: Apply in the first call if you need funding: second-call applicants cannot receive scholarships. Check the consortium's financial support page and the University of Padova's scholarships for second-year students at Padova.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Public Health in Disasters (PHID) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in health, management, law or social sciences with C1 English may apply by 31 December 2026 for a fully funded Erasmus Mundus master in public health in disasters.
opportunities.description:
The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Public Health in Disasters (PHID) is a two-year master's on public health in emergencies and disaster settings. It is run by the University of Oviedo in Spain (coordinator) with Karolinska Institutet in Sweden and the University of Nicosia in Cyprus, with EU funding; the Amhara Public Health Institute in Ethiopia is among its associated partners.

Applications are open from 1 October to 31 December 2026. Up to 25 students are admitted, and the programme lasts up to 24 months with study periods at the consortium universities.

African applicants count as partner-country students and can receive full scholarships, making PHID a strong option for health, humanitarian and emergency-management professionals from the continent.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship with a monthly allowance of 1,400 EUR for up to 24 months, a travel and installation contribution, and a fee waiver covering tuition, insurance and mandatory costs. Without a scholarship, fees are 18,000 EUR for partner-country students for the whole programme (9,000 EUR for programme-country students).
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years and 180 ECTS (or equivalent) in health, management, law, social or technical fields

English at C1: IELTS 6.5 overall (6.5 writing, at least 6.0 in other parts), TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 20) or TOEFL paper 550; native speakers from the UK, Ireland, USA, Australia, New Zealand and Canada exempt
Professional and research experience counts in scoring
All documents in English or officially translated
documents: Certified scans of diploma and transcripts
Average mark calculated on a 0 to 100 scale
Course descriptions in health, logistics or sociology
At least two reference letters (one academic, one employer), signed and stamped
opportunities.selection_process: Academic record 30%, professional and research experience 30%, and an interview for top-ranked applicants 40%. Scholarships follow the ranking.
important_dates: Official decision: mid to late May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The PHID consortium is led by the University of Oviedo with Karolinska Institutet and the University of Nicosia and is funded by the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the PHID website and the University of Oviedo application system by 31 December 2026, uploading all documents. Certified hard copies are needed after admission.
opportunities.notes: Dates after the deadline are approximate. Self-funded places are also available.

opportunities.title: Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at NTU 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality with a non-computer-science PhD from the last 3 years who propose an AI-in-science project with an NTU mentor.
opportunities.description:
The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore supports early-career researchers who want to apply artificial intelligence to problems in engineering, the natural sciences or the mathematical sciences. It is part of a global programme funded by Schmidt Sciences to speed up the use of AI across STEM research.

Fellows work at NTU for up to two years with a faculty mentor, receive a competitive salary package and travel allowances, and take at least one AI course module each year to build their skills. The current call closes on 31 December 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time.

The fellowship targets scientists whose PhD is not in computer science, which makes it a good fit for African researchers in fields such as chemistry, physics, biology, materials or civil engineering who want to add AI methods to their work. The page sets no nationality limit.
opportunities.benefits: Up to two years of postdoctoral employment at NTU with an attractive remuneration package (amount not published), travel allowances, and AI training through at least one AI module per year.
requirements: PhD (or equivalent) obtained within the last 3 years, in a field other than computer science
Excellent academic record and research potential
Research project applying AI to engineering, natural sciences or mathematical sciences
An NTU faculty member who agrees to mentor the project and writes a support letter
documents: CV with Scopus Author ID and full publication list
Official transcript or degree certificate in English
Research proposal of up to 2 pages (using the template on the page)
Support letter from the NTU mentor, attached to the proposal
Names of two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor (NTU contacts them)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic record, research potential and the quality of the AI-in-science proposal with its NTU mentor. The page does not describe interview stages.
opportunities.about_provider: Nanyang Technological University is a leading research university in Singapore. Schmidt Sciences, founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt, funds this AI in Science postdoctoral programme at a group of universities worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First find an NTU faculty mentor and agree a project, then submit the application on NTU's TRACS portal (apps.ntu.edu.sg/TRACS_ui/welcomepage?pgm=EWSA) with the proposal, CV, transcripts and publications. Your two referees will be contacted by NTU after you submit. Questions go to FA-RSO@ntu.edu.sg.
opportunities.notes: Computer science PhDs are not eligible. NTU also lists other postdoctoral schemes on its research careers pages, such as the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship and the Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship.

opportunities.title: FAO Headquarters Internship Programme 2027

GAMIC 2027 is the second Global Agriculture Multidisciplinary International Conference, hosted by the College of Agriculture, Forestry and Natural Resource Management at the University of Hawaii at Hilo together with Mindanao State University at Naawan in the Philippines. It invites abstracts on 17 themes including sustainable agriculture, agroecology and food security.

The conference runs on 5 and 6 February 2027 on the UH Hilo campus in Hawaii, and presenters may take part in person or online. Keynote speakers include the soil scientist Rattan Lal.

It suits African agricultural scientists and students who want to present work to an international audience; the online option makes it reachable without travel. Note that the conference does not fund travel.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present (in person or virtually) at an international agriculture conference; selected work may be published in the Pacific Agriculture and Natural Resources journal. No travel funding is offered. Registration costs 300 USD early (to 30 November 2026), 400 USD regular (1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027), 300 USD online only, or 200 USD for students and Hawaii residents.
requirements: Abstract on one of the conference themes
One paragraph of at most 250 words, title up to 80 characters, up to 5 keywords

State whether you will present in person or virtually
documents: Abstract submitted through the conference Google Form
Registration and fee payment through the UH Hilo payment page

opportunities.title: ICTP Workshop on Scientific Computing and AI, Kuwait City (Apr 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and early-career researchers based in the Arab region, including North Africa; apply by 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
This three-day workshop, run by the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) together with Kuwait University, trains students and early-career researchers in high-performance computing, scientific data analysis and artificial intelligence for science. Topics include deep learning for science, data analysis pipelines, HPC for science and AI, foundation models for science and edge AI.

It takes place in Kuwait City from 3 to 5 April 2027 and is followed by the first joint Kuwait University-ICTP Science Symposium, which all workshop participants must also register for. Selected participants present posters of their own research.

The call is aimed at students and early-career researchers based in the Arab region, which includes North African countries such as Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, Sudan and Mauritania. There is no registration fee and ICTP offers a limited number of attendance grants, with priority for participants from developing countries.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants are available to support attendance, with priority for participants from developing countries; amounts are not stated.
requirements: Student or early-career researcher based in the Arab region
Interest in scientific computing, HPC, data analysis or AI for science
Must also register for the Kuwait University-ICTP Science Symposium that follows the workshop
documents: Online application form in the ICTP e-applications portal
Optional research abstract on the ICTP template, for poster presentation
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers select participants from the online applications and choose some of them to present posters. Detailed criteria are not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: ICTP, based in Trieste, Italy, is a UNESCO category 1 institute that has supported scientists from developing countries for six decades. It runs schools and workshops worldwide with partner institutions such as Kuwait University.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Apply here' link on the ICTP Indico event page (smr 4433), which leads to the ICTP e-applications portal, and attach an abstract on the provided template if you want to present a poster. Register for the follow-on symposium too. Questions go to smr4433@ictp.it.
opportunities.notes: Grants are limited, so mention clearly in your application if you need financial support.
