opportunities.title: ITLOS Internship Programme July-September 2027
opportunities.provider: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with at least three years of university study or recent graduates, usually aged 32 or under, with good English or French and an interest in international law.
opportunities.description:
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) in Hamburg runs a three-month, full-time internship programme for students and recent graduates interested in international law. The call now open is for the July to September 2027 period, with applications due by 31 December 2026; applications for later periods can also be submitted.

Interns support the Registry in areas such as law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science and translation. About 20 internships are offered each year, and since 1997 the Tribunal has hosted 420 interns from 106 States.

The internship itself is unpaid, but a trust fund gives a limited number of allowances for travel and living costs to nationals of developing countries in financial need, which includes many African countries. This makes it a realistic way for African law and international relations students to gain experience at an international court.
opportunities.benefits: Internships are unpaid. The Trust Fund for the Law of the Sea gives a limited amount of funding to cover travel and living costs, paid as a monthly allowance, for selected interns who are nationals of and normally live in an OECD DAC developing country and are in financial need. Funding must be requested in the online application form; late requests are not considered.
requirements: At least three years of university study completed
Enrolled in a degree or postgraduate course during the internship, or graduated within 12 months before applying
Normally aged 32 or under
Good English and/or French
Interest in international law; background in law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science or translation
Not currently in employment
documents: Cover letter of up to one page
Optional: research or writing sample up to 10 pages
Optional: proof of enrolment, degrees and transcripts
Translations of documents not in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: An Internship Selection Committee reviews complete applications, and the Registrar decides with the approval of the President. Geographic diversity and gender balance are taken into account, and applicants hear the result about one month after the deadline.
important_dates: Results: about one month after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: ITLOS is an independent international court set up under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. It sits in Hamburg, Germany, and settles disputes about the interpretation and application of the Convention.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online internship application form on the ITLOS website and upload your cover letter and CV, plus any optional documents. If you need financial support, request it in the same form when you apply. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: No time of day is given for the deadline, so apply early. Questions go to press@itlos.org.

opportunities.title: Journal of African Social Inquiry: Call for Papers 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide may submit English papers on African societies by 31 December 2026 (and later quarterly deadlines) at no cost.
opportunities.description:
The Journal of African Social Inquiry, published by CalbisPress, has opened its call for papers for its four 2027 quarterly issues. It welcomes research on African societies, governance, development and inequality.

Submissions go through an online journal system and are reviewed double-anonymously. There are four submission deadlines in 2027, one for each issue, starting with 31 December 2026 for the January 2027 issue.

There are no submission or publication fees for the 2027 calls, which makes it a low-cost outlet for African researchers and graduate students in the social sciences. Note that it is a new journal: indexing is not guaranteed and would only start after the first issue.
opportunities.benefits: Free submission and free publication for all 2027 calls, even if publication happens after 2027.
requirements: Original article on African social, political, economic or development questions
Written in English
Two files: a title page with author details and contributions, and a fully anonymised manuscript
All co-authors entered in the submission system
documents: Identified title page with author contributions
opportunities.selection_process: Double-anonymous peer review.
opportunities.about_provider: CalbisPress is an independent academic publisher operated by Bussecon International Ltd. It runs several open journals, including the Journal of African Social Inquiry.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the journal's online submission system (OJS) and upload the title page and anonymised manuscript, following the submission guidelines on the journal site.
opportunities.notes: The publisher says indexing is not guaranteed and would begin after the first issue, so weigh this when choosing where to publish.

opportunities.description:
The Microsoft AI Economy Institute has opened its fourth research call, focused on AI and jobs. Selected principal investigators join a 12-month Senior Fellows programme with bi-weekly virtual workshops and an in-person workshop, and contribute a book chapter and a journal manuscript.

Each selected proposal receives a research gift of USD 75,000 and a travel allowance. Research starts in May 2027. The institute states that the research is independent and does not represent Microsoft's views.

The call is open to researchers at accredited universities and research institutions worldwide, so African economists, social scientists and computer scientists with a PhD can apply to study how AI is changing work.
opportunities.benefits: A research gift of USD 75,000 per proposal, plus a travel allowance of USD 7,500 for awardees based in the US, Canada or Mexico, or USD 20,000 for those based elsewhere.

opportunities.about_provider: The Microsoft AI Economy Institute, launched in 2025, funds and convenes independent research on the economic effects of artificial intelligence.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the biosketch and Project Overview Form through the Open Call 4 application portal linked from the Microsoft Research page by 31 December 2026.

opportunities.title: Northern College International Entrance Scholarship (Winter 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students admitted full time to an eligible Northern College programme for Winter 2027.
opportunities.description:
Northern College in northern Ontario, Canada, gives an International Entrance Scholarship worth CAD 2,000 to new international students starting an eligible programme. The award is open for the Winter 2027 intake, and the application deadline is 31 December 2026.

The money is paid in two parts: CAD 1,000 in the first semester and another CAD 1,000 in the second semester if the student has failed no courses. For Winter 2027 the eligible programmes are Cybersecurity (Timmins), Animal Grooming, Companion Animal Physical Rehabilitation and Veterinary Technician (Haileybury), and the Pre-Health Sciences Pathway (Timmins).

The scholarship is modest, but it reduces first-year costs for African students who have been admitted to one of these college programmes.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 2,000 in total: CAD 1,000 in the first semester and CAD 1,000 in the second semester, provided no courses are failed in the first semester.

Registered full time in the eligible programme and campus
Not exempt from international tuition fees
Has not studied at Northern College before
documents: Offer of admission to an eligible Winter 2027 programme

opportunities.title: Nusa Putra International Undergraduate Scholarships 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International high-school graduates aged up to 22 (26 for the Berlian scheme) with English proof.
opportunities.description:
Nusa Putra University in Sukabumi, West Java, Indonesia, offers international undergraduate scholarships for its English-taught bachelor's degrees starting in the 2027/2028 academic year. The awards last for the full eight semesters of a degree.

There are three schemes. The Genusian Scholarship is the most complete, covering tuition, a monthly living allowance, housing help, visa sponsorship and health insurance. The International Islamic Boarding Scholarship offers the same support with full residence in the university's pesantren (Islamic boarding school). The Berlian Scholarship covers tuition and language and academic support only.

Registration runs from 1 November to 31 December 2026, and every stage of selection, including a computer-based test and interviews, takes place online, so African school leavers can apply without travelling. Results are announced on 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Genusian Scholarship: 100% tuition for 8 semesters, a monthly living allowance, housing assistance, KITAS C316 student visa sponsorship, Indonesian language classes (BIPA), health insurance in Indonesia and airport pick-up. International Islamic Boarding Scholarship: the same, plus a full pesantren dormitory place. Berlian Scholarship: 100% tuition for 8 semesters, BIPA classes, airport pick-up and academic mentoring (no living allowance, visa fees, housing or insurance). None of the schemes pays for the passport, international flights or medical checks.
requirements: High-school graduate with a strong academic and disciplinary record
Maximum age 22 for the Genusian and Islamic Boarding schemes; 26 for the Berlian scheme
Islamic Boarding scheme: practising Muslim willing to live full time in the pesantren
English proof: valid TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo result, or an official certificate of English-medium schooling
Passport valid for at least 18 months from the planned entry date
documents: Confidential recommendation letter from a principal, senior teacher, counsellor or community leader
High-school diploma and transcripts for grades 10-12
Certified English translations of documents not in English
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is fully online: document screening, a computer-based test (CBT) and an interview; Islamic Boarding applicants also take a Quran recitation test.
opportunities.about_provider: Nusa Putra University is a private university in Sukabumi, West Java, Indonesia, offering English-taught bachelor's programmes to international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a scheme and register on the university's application portal (apply.nusaputra.ac.id, with a separate link for each scheme) before 31 December 2026. Upload the documents, then take part in the online test and interview on the dates given.
opportunities.notes: Indonesian national schemes listed on the same site (such as KIP-Kuliah) are not for international students.

opportunities.title: SPICE 2027: Seventh International Conference on the SMILE Project and Intercultural Communication Education (Call for Abstracts)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and teachers in intercultural communication and language education may submit abstracts by 31 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
SPICE 2027 is the seventh international conference linked to the SMILE project, an international exchange and teaching initiative on intercultural communication and foreign language education. The conference invites abstracts on intercultural communication education, foreign language teaching, the use of ICT in learning and new educational programmes.

The main event is a one-day conference on Saturday 20 March 2027 at Tunghai University in Taichung, Taiwan, centred on practical reports from SMILE activities that run from March 2026 to January 2027. A companion event, I-WIT 2027, takes place in Kaohsiung and Taichung from 18 to 20 March 2027.

The call is open to researchers and teachers in related fields, which makes it a modest, friendly venue for African language educators, applied linguists and graduate students who want to present classroom-based or intercultural research in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: This is a call for abstracts with no stated funding. Accepted presenters take part in the conference; registration and payment are required (amounts are not stated on the call page).

Abstract of fewer than 500 words
All presenters must register and pay by 20 January 2027
No nationality or degree restrictions are stated
documents: Abstract in PDF format, under 500 words

opportunities.title: Takemi Program in International Health Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career health professionals and researchers with a graduate degree, publications and already-collected data, from any country.
opportunities.description:
The Takemi Program in International Health at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston is a one-year, in-person research fellowship for mid-career health professionals and researchers, mainly from low- and middle-income countries. It describes itself as the oldest continuing mid-career research and training programme in global health, and since 1983 it has hosted 330 fellows from 62 countries, about 70 of them from Africa.

Fellows spend an academic year (1 August to 30 June) analysing data they have already collected, writing papers, attending seminars and building networks. Applications for the 2027-2028 year are open until 31 December 2026 at midnight US Eastern time, with decisions in February and applicants informed by March.

Applicants should note that the programme itself does not fund fellows: most must bring their own funding, and only very limited internal support exists for two fellows from low-income countries. It suits African health researchers who already have funding or an employer's support and want a year at Harvard to turn their data into publications and policy.
opportunities.benefits: The programme gives a year of in-person research time at Harvard, seminars, mentoring and a certificate, but it does not provide funding. Limited internal support (from a Japan Pharmaceutical Medical Association donation) may cover two fellows from low-income countries, decided at acceptance. Fellows must show at least US$36,410 a year for the J-1 visa; the page estimates real costs at US$60,000-77,000 a year (2024-25 figures).
requirements: A completed graduate (advanced) degree in any discipline
Significant work and research experience, including publications in internationally recognised journals
Leadership potential in your home country
Good English (TOEFL, IELTS, or a transcript from an English-medium university)
Commitment to a career in health
Data already collected before the fellowship (active data collection is not supported)
Able to attend in person for the full year
documents: Research proposal of up to 5 pages (single-spaced, 12-pt Times New Roman, with aims, background, data sources and methods)
Statement of interest answering five set questions
Publications list and one sample English-language publication
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews applications and meets in mid-February to choose fellows; applicants are told by March. Reapplying in later years is allowed.
important_dates: Deadline: 31 December 2026, midnight US Eastern time
Fellowship year: 1 August 2027 - 30 June 2028 (orientation late August)
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is Harvard University's school of public health in Boston. The Takemi Program, named after Dr Taro Takemi of the Japan Medical Association, has trained mid-career global health leaders there since 1983.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form (Harvard Qualtrics link on the apply page), uploading your CV, proposal, statement and publications, and ask three referees to email their letters. Start looking for funding early, using the programme's list of possible funding sources. Questions go to takemi@hsph.harvard.edu.
opportunities.notes: There is no programming in January and no remote option. Plan funding in advance: most fellows are supported by their employer, government or an external funder.

opportunities.title: Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: Nanyang Technological University and Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality within 5 years of their PhD proposing AI, data, software, security or autonomy research.

The Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship is a two-year independent research fellowship split between Singapore and Sweden. Fellows spend the first year at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and the second year with a research group in the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) in Sweden. opportunities.benefits: In the Singapore year: an annual salary of up to SGD 80,000, a research grant of up to SGD 100,000, and a relocation allowance and housing grant for the fellowship. In the Sweden year: an annual support package covering salary, supervision and travel at WASP's standard postdoctoral level.

Top 3 publications in PDF and other supporting documents
Two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor

opportunities.title: Harvard College need-based financial aid for first-year students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school students worldwide applying to Harvard College for autumn 2027 by 1 January can receive need-based aid meeting full need.
opportunities.description:
Harvard College admits first-year students and gives need-based financial aid to all admitted students who qualify, including international students on the same terms as US students. Harvard meets full demonstrated need, and about a quarter of families pay nothing.

For entry in autumn 2027, Regular Decision applicants submit their part of the application by 1 January 2027, and financial aid forms (CSS Profile and IDOC documents) by 1 February 2027. Decisions are released at the end of March.

For outstanding African secondary-school students, Harvard's aid can cover the full cost of a degree, so family income need not decide whether you apply.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based aid that meets full demonstrated need for admitted students, including international students; amounts depend on family finances.
requirements: Completed (or completing) secondary school and seeking a first bachelor's degree
Not already holding a bachelor's degree or previously enrolled at university as a degree student
SAT or ACT scores, or in exceptional cases strong results from AP, IB, A Levels or national exams
CSS Profile (Harvard code 3434) for aid
documents: Common Application with the Harvard supplement (five short questions)
School report with counsellor letter and transcript
Two teacher recommendations and the midyear report
CSS Profile and IDOC documents: parents' and student's full 2025 tax returns as filed, or non-filer statements, with translations
opportunities.selection_process: Holistic admissions review; aid is calculated separately and does not affect the admission decision.
important_dates: Regular Decision application: 1 January 2027, 11:59 pm local time
Financial aid (CSS Profile and IDOC): 1 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is the oldest university in the United States. Harvard College is its undergraduate school.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application with the Harvard supplement by 1 January, then complete the CSS Profile and upload IDOC documents by 1 February. International students who cannot pay the CSS Profile fee can use Harvard's alternate aid application.
opportunities.notes: Harvard accepts late aid applications but does not track aid files before admission decisions. Counsellor materials may arrive up to a week after 1 January.

opportunities.title: IGVI Travel Grant Program (January 2027 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Humanities and social-science scholars based in a World Bank low- or lower-middle-income country can apply by 1 January 2027 (and each 1 May and 1 September) for help with conference or research travel.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Global Value Inquiry (IGVI) runs a travel grant programme for scholars in the humanities and social sciences whose work deals with questions of value, preferably with a philosophical focus. Grants help pay for attending conferences and workshops or for research trips.

There are three application rounds every year, closing on 1 January, 1 May and 1 September, and applications are usually processed within about two weeks. The next round closes on 1 January 2027.

The programme is aimed specifically at scholars based in World Bank low- and lower-middle-income countries, which covers most of Africa, and there is no career-stage limit, membership requirement or abstract requirement.
opportunities.benefits: Contribution to travel costs for conferences, workshops or research trips, assessed against IGVI's flat-rate cost tables.
requirements: Based in a World Bank low- or lower-middle-income country
Working in the humanities or social sciences on value inquiry (philosophical focus preferred)
Proof that you have applied to the event or research activity
Any career stage
documents: Proof of application to the event or activity
Cost evidence (for example a travel agent quote or screenshot)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the relevance of the research project and of the trip, and on available funds in that round.
important_dates: Later rounds: 1 May and 1 September each year
Decision: about two weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: IGVI is a research institute that supports inquiry into values across the humanities and social sciences, with a focus on including scholars from the Global South. It funds travel, research grants and research positions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the application form from the IGVI website and email it with your CV, project description, proof of event application and cost evidence to info@igvi.org on or before the round deadline.
opportunities.notes: IGVI also advertises an Impact Research Supplementary Grant and research positions on its opportunities page.

opportunities.title: Northeastern State University International 50% Tuition Waiver (Spring 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully admitted international bachelor's or master's students who live on campus and meet GPA minimums (3.0 freshmen, 2.75 transfers).
opportunities.description:
Northeastern State University (NSU) in Oklahoma, USA, offers a Non-Resident 50% Tuition Waiver to international students working towards their first bachelor's or master's degree. For the Spring 2027 term the application deadline is 1 January.

The waiver halves the non-resident part of tuition, bringing costs closer to in-state rates. Students must be fully admitted (not on conditional or probationary admission) and must live on campus, unless they are legacy students whose parent, grandparent or sibling holds an NSU degree.

NSU also lists a General International Student Scholarship and merit awards of USD 500 to 5,000 for new international students, so African students can combine support to make study in the US more affordable.
opportunities.benefits: Waives 50% of the non-resident portion of tuition for first bachelor's and master's degrees. Published rates: non-resident USD 334.25 per credit hour (undergraduate) and USD 365.25 (graduate), against in-state rates of USD 245.25 and USD 309.75. Separate merit awards for new international students range from USD 500 to 5,000 for one year.
requirements: International student pursuing a first bachelor's or master's degree
Full regular admission (not conditional, alternative or probationary)
Live in on-campus housing (legacy students exempt)
Incoming freshmen: GPA of at least 3.0
Transfer students: GPA of at least 2.75
Graduate students: must live on campus
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants who meet the admission, GPA and housing conditions and apply by the deadline are considered for the waiver.
opportunities.about_provider: Northeastern State University is a public regional university in Tahlequah, Oklahoma, with campuses in Tahlequah, Muskogee and Broken Arrow. It is the oldest institution of higher learning in Oklahoma.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Gain regular admission to NSU, then complete the Apply Now waiver form linked from the international scholarships page before 1 January for Spring 2027. For the other international scholarships, email international@nsuok.edu.
opportunities.notes: The waiver covers only part of non-resident tuition. Fall 2027 applicants have later deadlines (1 August), and the NSU Foundation scholarship for new international students has a priority deadline of 1 March 2027.

opportunities.title: Princeton Financial Aid for International Undergraduates
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Need-based aid meeting full demonstrated need for admitted international undergraduates.

opportunities.title: TU/e Scholarship for Excellence: Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to an eligible TU/e master's for September 2027 with a GPA of at least 7.5/10 and no prior Dutch degree study.
opportunities.description:
Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) in the Netherlands offers the TU/e Scholarship for Excellence to top students starting a full-time master's on 1 September 2027. The 2027-2028 edition, titled 'Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation', is funded by the Dutch national Beethoven Program and supports master's programmes linked to the semiconductor and high-tech industry.

Eligible programmes include Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Data Science and AI, Embedded Systems, Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Systems and Control, Sustainable Energy Technology, Automotive Technology, Nuclear Fusion, and Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Systems. About 35 awards are made, 15 of them for students from outside the EEA, and only about 2% of applicants succeed.

The award is €7,500 a year for two years, so it is a partial scholarship rather than full funding. Non-EEA winners also receive part of the NL Scholarship in their first year. Strong African engineering and science graduates with a GPA of 7.5/10 or better can apply as part of their master's application by 1 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €7,500 per academic year for two years (€15,000 in total). Non-EEA recipients also receive a share of the NL Scholarship in year one (not applied for separately). It is not a full scholarship; keeping the year-two award needs at least 45 ECTS in year one.
requirements: Applied for a full-time TU/e master's starting 1 September 2027 in an eligible programme
High-school diploma or bachelor's obtained outside the Netherlands
No previous Dutch higher education (exchange periods allowed)
GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 (or equivalent) on the latest transcript
Able to meet Dutch visa and residence-permit rules
Not a JADS joint master's or European double degree, and not admitted on an earlier intake's decision
documents: Confirmation in the application that you want to be considered
opportunities.selection_process: The International Office checks eligibility, then a Scholarship Selection Committee ranks candidates. Results are confirmed by the end of March 2027 and cannot be appealed.
opportunities.about_provider: Eindhoven University of Technology is a Dutch research university focused on engineering, science and technology. It sits in the Brainport Eindhoven region, home to ASML and other high-tech and chip companies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible TU/e master's and, in that application, indicate that you want to be considered for the scholarship and add a brief motivation. Submit the complete application by 1 January 2027 at 23:59 CET. Questions go to io@tue.nl with 'TU/e Scholarship' in the subject line.
opportunities.notes: About 2% of applicants are selected. TU/e also lists the Changemaker Scholarship (housing for 10 months, same deadline) and external schemes such as the ASML Technology Scholarship.

opportunities.title: University of Notre Dame Need-Blind Admission and Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying to Notre Dame for fall 2027 are reviewed need-blind; apply by 1 January 2027 and file the CSS Profile by 15 January 2027 for need-based aid.
opportunities.description:
The University of Notre Dame in Indiana reviews international first-year applicants on a need-blind basis, meaning that a student's ability to pay does not affect the admission decision. Admitted international students who apply for aid are considered for need-based support from the university.

For entry in fall 2027, Regular Decision applicants must submit the admission application by 1 January 2027 and the 2027-28 CSS Profile by 15 January 2027. Aid is awarded on the basis of academic qualifications, financial need and the funds available, and can include university scholarships and student employment.

Need-blind review for international students is rare among US universities, which makes Notre Dame worth considering for strong African applicants who need financial help.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based aid that may include university scholarship assistance and student employment (amounts depend on need). Merit scholarships are limited and separate.
requirements: International first-year applicant for fall 2027
Admission application by 1 January 2027 (Regular Decision)
2027-28 CSS Profile by 15 January 2027 (school code 1841)
documents: Documents requested through College Board IDOC, such as parents' tax returns or a non-filer statement and 2025 earnings statements
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is need-blind; after admission, aid is awarded based on academic qualifications, demonstrated need and available funds.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Notre Dame is a private Catholic research university in Indiana, USA. Its Office of Financial Aid handles need-based aid for domestic and international undergraduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the admission application first, then complete the CSS Profile for international applicants and upload any IDOC documents requested. Questions go to finaid@nd.edu or 574-631-6436.

opportunities.title: Cornell University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying to Cornell for autumn 2027 must file the CSS Profile by 2 January 2027 (Regular Decision) to receive aid meeting full need.
opportunities.description:
Cornell University offers need-based financial aid to international first-year and transfer undergraduates. Admission is need-aware for international applicants, which means asking for aid can be considered in the decision, but Cornell meets 100% of the demonstrated need of every international student it admits.

For entry in autumn 2027, Regular Decision applicants submit the 2027-28 CSS Profile by 2 January 2027, and aid offers are expected in early April 2027.

For African students admitted to Cornell, the aid can make an Ivy League education affordable, combining grants, a work-study job and, depending on family income, reasonable loans.
opportunities.benefits: Cornell meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international undergraduates through Cornell grants, an annual work-study award and, depending on income, reasonable loans. Grant aid above tuition and mandatory fees is subject to 14% US tax withholding unless a tax treaty applies.
requirements: Applying as an international first-year or transfer student
CSS Profile completed when applying for admission
Need-based: aid depends on family finances, not grades
US citizens with dual nationality, eligible non-citizens and undocumented US high-school graduates follow the US instructions instead
documents: Documents requested later through College Board IDOC (signed copies only)
opportunities.selection_process: Cornell reviews the CSS Profile and documents and sends admitted students a preliminary aid estimate.
opportunities.about_provider: Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, is a private Ivy League research university. Its Office of Financial Aid manages need-based aid for undergraduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the CSS Profile online as soon as possible after 1 October 2026, choosing Cornell University (code 2098), and submit any documents Cornell later requests through IDOC. Contact finaid@cornell.edu with your name and admissions ID.
opportunities.notes: International students generally cannot get a CSS Profile fee waiver. Because admission is need-aware, apply for aid at the time you apply for admission; you cannot usually apply later.

opportunities.title: Duke Karsh International Scholars Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full scholarship for international first-year undergraduates at Duke.

opportunities.title: Gordon Research Seminar: Tropical Infectious Diseases 2027 (Carl Storm Fellowships)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs with a science or engineering degree can apply (with an abstract) to the 30-31 January 2027 seminar in Oxnard, California; Carl Storm Opportunity Fellowships offer financial assistance.

opportunities.title: University of Chicago International Undergraduate Scholarships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Need-based aid for admitted international undergraduates.

opportunities.title: Yale College Financial Aid, Regular Decision (Fall 2027 Entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school students worldwide applying to Yale College for autumn 2027 by 2 January can receive aid meeting 100% of need with no loans.
opportunities.description:
Yale College admits first-year students without regard to their ability to pay and meets 100% of every admitted student's demonstrated financial need, whatever their citizenship, without loans. This item covers the Regular Decision round for entry in autumn 2027.

Applicants apply for admission by 2 January and submit financial aid forms by 15 February. Decisions are released in late March, and admitted students reply by 1 May.

For talented African secondary-school students, Yale's need-based aid can cover the full cost of study, including travel, which makes it one of the most generous routes to a US undergraduate degree.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based scholarships covering 100% of demonstrated need with no loans. Families earning under 100,000 USD with typical assets are expected to pay nothing, which covers tuition, fees, housing, food and travel, plus a 2,000 USD start-up grant in the first year. Families under 200,000 USD receive at least full tuition. The average need-based scholarship is about 75,220 USD a year.
requirements: Applying as a first-year student for autumn 2027 through Regular Decision
School report with transcript and recommendation letters
ACT or SAT scores (Yale's testing policy applies)
CSS Profile for all aid applicants (Yale code 3987)
documents: Parents' tax or income documents via IDOC (or a non-filer statement)
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is decided on the same criteria for all rounds; aid is calculated separately from need.
opportunities.about_provider: Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, is a private Ivy League research university. Yale College is its undergraduate school, and its financial aid is need-based only.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the first-year application by 2 January, then complete the CSS Profile and upload family financial documents through IDOC by 15 February. Track everything on the Yale applicant status portal.
opportunities.notes: The 2 January date is for admission only; aid paperwork is due later. International applicants should read Yale's international students page for country-specific guidance.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Flood Risk Management 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Erasmus Mundus scholarships for the Flood Risk Management joint master's; scholarship applications due 3 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Groundwater and Global Change 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Erasmus Mundus scholarships for the Groundwater and Global Change joint master's; scholarship applications due 3 January 2027.

opportunities.title: FASPE Journalism Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: FASPE (Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career journalists and journalism graduate students worldwide (generally under 10 years' experience) may apply by 3 January 2027 for a fully funded ethics fellowship in Berlin and Poland.
opportunities.description:
The FASPE Journalism Fellowship is a fully funded two-week seminar on ethics in journalism. Fellows study how journalists and the press behaved in Nazi Germany and occupied Europe and use that history to think about the ethical choices journalists face today.

The 2027 programme runs from 18 June to 2 July 2027 in Berlin and Poland, including a visit to Auschwitz. It brings together a small group of 13 to 16 early-career journalists and journalism students.

It is a strong opportunity for African journalists early in their careers who want an intensive, international experience focused on media ethics, alongside peers from other countries.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded: FASPE covers programme costs so that money does not decide who takes part (exact items are not listed on the page).
requirements: One of: (a) some journalism experience and enrolled in a graduate programme with plans to work as a journalist; (b) a completed undergraduate degree and working as a journalist; or (c) a completed graduate degree and working as a journalist
Generally no more than 10 years of professional experience
Published work preferred
Able to attend the full programme from 18 June to 2 July 2027
opportunities.selection_process: FASPE reviews written applications and selects 13 to 16 fellows each year.
important_dates: Application deadline: 3 January 2027, 11:59 pm US Eastern time
Programme: 18 June to 2 July 2027, Berlin and Poland
opportunities.about_provider: FASPE (Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics) is a New York-based non-profit that runs ethics fellowships for journalism, law, business, medicine, design and technology, and clergy, using the history of the Holocaust.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through FASPE's Submittable portal, uploading the CV, transcripts and essays. Ask your two referees to send letters by 10 January 2027. Questions go to applications@faspe-ethics.org.
opportunities.notes: FASPE also runs 2027 fellowships for law, business, design and technology, medicine and clergy with similar timelines.

opportunities.title: KAUST Graduate Fellowship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates worldwide with a GPA of 3.0 or above and strong English may apply by 3 January 2027 for fully funded MS or PhD study at KAUST starting fall 2027.
opportunities.description:
The KAUST Fellowship is the funding package that King Abdullah University of Science and Technology gives to students it admits to its MS, MS/PhD and PhD programmes. There is no separate fellowship application: applying for admission is applying for the fellowship.

KAUST is a graduate-only research university on the Red Sea coast at Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, teaching science and engineering in English. The fall 2027 semester starts on 29 August 2027, and Round 2 of admissions is open now.

The package is among the most generous for graduate study anywhere, worth roughly 70,000 to 80,000 USD a year, which makes it very attractive to strong African graduates in science, engineering and computing.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition and bench fee (up to 35,000 USD a year); a stipend of 20,000 USD a year for MS students and 25,000 to 30,000 USD a year for PhD students; free base housing on campus; health insurance for the student and eligible dependents on campus; and relocation support (visa, travel and moving).
requirements: Bachelor's degree for the MS, or master's degree for the PhD, in a relevant subject from a recognised institution
At least 18 years old
Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent (about 90% of admitted students have above 3.3)

English: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in each part, or PTE Academic 71 (67 each), or Cambridge C1/C2 185 (176 each); waived for in-person degrees from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand
GRE optional; no work experience needed
documents: Official transcripts from every institution, with grading scale (plus certified English translation if needed)
Statement of purpose of about 750 words
Three referees with academic email addresses
opportunities.selection_process: Admissions staff check eligibility, then a faculty committee ranks and shortlists candidates. Shortlisted applicants have an online academic interview and/or test. Decisions are sent by email and are final, without individual feedback.
important_dates: Reference letters: within 7 days after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is a graduate research university in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, founded in 2009. It focuses on science, technology and engineering and recruits students from around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the KAUST admissions portal for an MS, MS/PhD or PhD programme by 3 January 2027. Your referees are contacted by the system and must submit within seven days of the deadline. Shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview.
opportunities.notes: KAUST says the dates are tentative. Some students who already hold external funding may not be eligible for the fellowship. The number of awards is not stated.

opportunities.title: ACL 2027 Call for Main Conference Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: NLP researchers worldwide may submit to ACL Rolling Review by 4 January 2027 for ACL 2027 in Kyoto.
opportunities.description:
ACL 2027, the 65th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, invites long and short papers on natural language processing and computational linguistics. This year's special theme is homogenisation and knowledge collapse in large language models.

The meeting is in Kyoto, Japan: tutorials on 17 August, workshops on 18 and 19 August and the main conference from 20 to 22 August 2027. Papers are first submitted to ACL Rolling Review (ARR) and then committed to ACL 2027 after review.

The programme chairs include David Adelani and Jan Buys of the University of Cape Town, and the call is a key venue for African NLP researchers working on African languages and multilingual models.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the ACL 2027 proceedings and presentation in Kyoto; accepted papers get one extra page (9 for long, 5 for short).
requirements: Original NLP or computational linguistics research
Long papers up to 8 pages, short papers up to 4 pages, under ARR rules
Double-blind and no dual submission
A registered presenting author by the early registration deadline
documents: Paper submitted to ACL Rolling Review via OpenReview
opportunities.selection_process: Two stages: review in ACL Rolling Review, then commitment of reviewed papers to ACL 2027, where the programme committee decides acceptance. Papers reviewed in earlier ARR cycles may also be committed.
important_dates: ARR submission deadline: 4 January 2027, 11:59 pm AoE
Commitment, notification and camera-ready dates: to be announced
opportunities.about_provider: The Association for Computational Linguistics is the main international scientific society for people working on computational problems involving human language.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the paper to the January 2027 ARR cycle on OpenReview by 4 January, then commit it to ACL 2027 when the commitment link opens. The author list cannot change at commitment.
opportunities.notes: Questions on submission go to editors@aclrollingreview.org and on commitment to acl27-pcs@googlegroups.com.

opportunities.title: ECAS 2027 call for papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide may propose papers by 4 January 2027 to ECAS 2027, the European Conference on African Studies.
opportunities.description:
ECAS 2027 is the European Conference on African Studies, the main conference of AEGIS, the European network of African studies centres, organised with NomadIT. The call for papers invites proposals to the conference's accepted panels across the humanities and social sciences.

The conference runs fully in person from 30 June to 3 July 2027. Panels have four or five papers in 105-minute sessions, and the working language is English.

It is one of the largest gatherings of Africanist scholars worldwide and a strong place for African researchers to present work, build networks and find collaborators. A fee-waiver call for successful presenters opens in early 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at ECAS 2027. A fee-waiver scheme opens in early 2027 for successful paper presenters (amounts not stated).
requirements: Paper proposal to one of the open ECAS 2027 panels
Short abstract under 300 characters and long abstract under 250 words
At most four roles and one paper per person
Presentations are in person and in English
documents: Online paper proposal form (title, authors and emails, short and long abstracts)
opportunities.selection_process: Panel convenors select the papers for their panels in January 2027.
important_dates: Call for papers: 26 October 2026 to 4 January 2027
Papers marked up by convenors: January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: AEGIS (Africa-Europe Group for Interdisciplinary Studies) is a network of European centres of African studies. It holds ECAS every two years, with NomadIT handling conference organisation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Browse the ECAS 2027 panels and use the Propose paper button on the panel you choose to submit by 4 January 2027. Questions go to admin@ecasconference.org.
opportunities.notes: The theme title and the host city were not shown on the call page; check the theme and location pages.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master GLOBE (global change, biodiversity conservation and environmental management) 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: GLOBE Erasmus Mundus consortium (Universidad Rey Juan Carlos)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in biology, environment, forestry or agriculture from any country with B2 English may apply by 4 January 2027 for a fully funded two-year Erasmus Mundus master.
opportunities.description:
GLOBE is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master on global change, biodiversity conservation and environmental management, now in its third edition (2027-2029). It is run by Universidad Rey Juan Carlos in Madrid with the University of Lisbon, Bangor University in Wales and the Autonomous University of Tlaxcala in Mexico, with EU co-funding.

Students spend the first semester in Madrid, the second at Bangor, the third in Lisbon and the fourth on a master's thesis at a partner, with a three-week summer school in Mexico between the two years. Up to 25 students are admitted.

All nationalities can apply for the EU scholarships, so African graduates in biology, environmental science, forestry or agriculture can compete for a fully funded master's across three countries.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover participation costs for 24 months plus a monthly allowance of 1,400 EUR. Without a scholarship, participation costs are 9,000 EUR a year for students from non-associated third countries (4,500 EUR for programme countries), covering tuition, insurance and registration but not travel, visa or living costs. There is no application fee.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS in biology, agriculture, environmental sciences, forestry, earth and environmental geography, natural resources or equivalent

English at CEFR B2 by the Stage 1 deadline: IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72 or Cambridge B2 (160); native speakers and graduates of majority-English countries exempt; medium-of-instruction letters not accepted
Transcript showing the official grading scale
Not a previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship holder (for the scholarship)
documents: Stage 1 online form: personal and passport details, degree and GPA details, English level, a 1 to 2 minute video and two referees

Stage 2 (shortlisted): passport valid for two years, apostilled or certified degree certificates, transcripts in English, English certificate, Europass CV, declaration of veracity, and an eligibility certificate if your university is outside the EHEA
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 academic assessment (77%): academic excellence 35%, CV 32%, programme fit 10%, with a pass mark of 50. Stage 2 personal assessment (23%): video 15% and references 8%. Scholarships also consider geographical balance.
important_dates: Stage 2 documents for shortlisted applicants: January to February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The GLOBE consortium is led by Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (Madrid) with Universidade de Lisboa, Bangor University and Universidad Autónoma de Tlaxcala, co-funded by the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the Stage 1 online form on the GLOBE application platform by 4 January 2027, using a personal email address; all content must be in English. Shortlisted applicants are asked to upload documents in Stage 2. Contact project.globe@urjc.es.
opportunities.notes: Only one application is needed; if you submit twice, the latest counts. Check passport validity early.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development (ILSPSD)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law, politics or international-relations graduates worldwide with C1 English may apply by 4 January 2027 for a fully funded two-year Erasmus Mundus master's starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
ILSPSD is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development, run by a European consortium led by Leuphana University of Lüneburg in Germany. Students choose an LL.M. track or an MA track.

The programme starts in October 2027. The first semester is at Leuphana, the second at IBEI in Barcelona, and the third and fourth at one of four partners: the University of Glasgow, the Université libre de Bruxelles, NOVA University Lisbon or the University of Tartu, where the dissertation is written. Students live in at least three countries.

The EU-funded scholarship pays a monthly allowance and waives tuition, and a share of places is reserved for applicants from targeted regions outside Europe, which makes it a strong option for African law and international-relations graduates.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of 1,400 EUR per month for the full 24 months, meant to cover travel, visa, installation and living costs, plus a full tuition waiver. About 70 scholarships are shared across four intakes, including 18 for targeted regions and 20 for non-associated third countries, with no more than 10% going to one nationality.
requirements: Completed first degree of at least 180 ECTS (or equivalent) by the time of the scholarship application
LL.M. track: at least 60 ECTS in law; MA track: at least 60 ECTS in law, political science, international relations or a related subject
Track rules: Glasgow needs a 2.1 Hons in Law or equivalent; ULB needs at least 240 ECTS in law and French at B2; Tartu needs at least 60 ECTS in law

English at C1: IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT (new scale 5; 95 for tests before 21 January 2026), or Cambridge CAE/CPE, no older than 2 years, unless English is your first language or your degree was taught in English in listed countries
Must hold an offer of a place from Leuphana before entering the scholarship competition
Not a previous Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship holder
documents: English (and, for ULB, French) test results
Proof of residence issued within 12 months before the deadline (residence certificate or employer/institution certificate)
Further documents listed in the official step-by-step application guide
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are checked for eligibility and admission, then a selection committee ranks scholarship candidates. Results are emailed by the end of April. Appeals are possible within 14 days, on procedural grounds only.
important_dates: Scholarship results: by end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The ILSPSD consortium is led by Leuphana University of Lüneburg with IBEI Barcelona, the University of Glasgow, ULB Brussels, NOVA Lisbon and the University of Tartu, and is funded by the European Union through the Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Leuphana awards portal for the 2027 scholarship round (a separate portal exists for self-funded places), following the step-by-step guide on the programme website. Submit language results with the application, since no exemptions are given after the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Emails asking for exemptions are not answered. Your scholarship category depends on your country of residence; check the EU list of eligible countries and regions. Contact: ilspsd@leuphana.de.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Cybersecurity and Assurance (CYBERSURE) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Computing, maths or IT graduates worldwide with IELTS 6.5 may apply by 4 January 2027 for a funded Erasmus Mundus master in cybersecurity.
opportunities.description:
CYBERSURE is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Cybersecurity and Assurance led by NTNU in Norway, with Aalto University, DTU, the University of Tartu, EURECOM, KTH and TU Graz.

The first year is at NTNU (Trondheim, then Gjøvik). In the second year students specialise at one partner: distributed systems security (Aalto), networks and systems security (KTH), cybersecurity and software assurance (DTU), cryptography (Tartu), big data security (EURECOM) or security engineering (TU Graz).

Scholarships are open to all countries, so African computer science and engineering graduates can compete for a funded master's in a fast-growing field across two European countries.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus grant of 16,800 EUR per year for scholarship holders, covering travel, visa, installation and living costs. For the 2026 intake there were 12 scholarships for all countries plus 5 for targeted regions; the 2027 number is not yet published.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or 3 years full time, giving access to a master's in the awarding country
Relevant field preferred: mathematics, computer science, computer engineering, IT or information systems

English: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing, or C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency, or the TOEFL iBT level stated on the page; tests taken from 16 November 2024; exemptions for English-medium degrees in listed countries
Non-EU applicants must submit final degree documents by the deadline
documents: Colour scan of the bachelor's certificate and official transcripts (with certified translations if needed)
Motivation letter (max 500 words) and a one-minute motivation video
Passport or ID copy and proof of residence
Two recommendation letters and course descriptions (recommended)
Country-specific documents for several African countries (including Cameroon, Ethiopia, Ghana, Nigeria and DR Congo)
opportunities.selection_process: Document-based and competitive. Criteria in order: relevance of previous studies, academic performance, quality of the institution, motivation, other achievements and English. Only applicants who meet the first two are assessed further.
opportunities.about_provider: The CYBERSURE consortium is led by the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) and includes six European technical universities, with EU Erasmus Mundus funding.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through NTNU's Søknadsweb as an international applicant by 4 January 2027, ranking all six specialisations, and make sure English test results reach NTNU by 18 January 2027 (not by email).
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are rejected. Check the country-specific document rules for your country on the admission page.

opportunities.title: Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program (FUSRP) 2027
opportunities.provider: Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Strong undergraduate mathematics students who want to spend nine weeks on a supervised research project in Ontario; the page sets no nationality limit.
opportunities.description:
The Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program brings small teams of talented undergraduates together with faculty supervisors to work on genuine research problems in the mathematical sciences. Each project takes a group of up to four students, and around ten projects are on offer for the 2027 edition.

The programme runs for nine weeks, from 1 June to 31 July 2027. Teams are based at the Fields Institute in Toronto or at partner sites such as Western University in London, Ontario. The summer includes an orientation day, a presentation clinic in late July and a final day of project presentations.

For students from African universities this is a rare chance to do research-level mathematics at one of Canada's best-known institutes, build relationships with supervisors and come away with a project to show graduate schools. The Institute pays most travel and on-site costs for selected students.
opportunities.benefits: The Institute covers most of each selected student's travel and on-site expenses for the nine-week programme. The page does not state a stipend amount.
requirements: Current undergraduate student with strong mathematics preparation
Background that matches the chosen project (for example PDEs and matrix theory, or calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and programming in Matlab, Python or R)
Able to be in Ontario from 1 June to 31 July 2027
A referee who will submit a letter by 11 January 2027
documents: One reference letter (submitted separately by the referee)
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is competitive. Students are matched to faculty projects in groups of up to four; the page does not describe the scoring in detail.
important_dates: Student application deadline: 4 January 2027, 1:00 PM EST
Reference letter deadline: 11 January 2027, 1:00 PM EST
opportunities.about_provider: The Fields Institute is a centre for mathematical research and training based at the University of Toronto. It runs thematic programmes, workshops and training schemes in partnership with Canadian universities and sponsors such as Mitacs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the list of 2027 projects on the Fields page and pick those that fit your background. Complete the online student application (linked from the programme page) before 4 January 2027 at 1:00 PM Eastern time, and ask your referee to send a letter by 11 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Projects have their own prerequisite skills, so mention the ones you meet. Questions go to inquiries@fields.utoronto.ca. Fields also lists a Research Exchange Program and other training opportunities on its site.

opportunities.title: IJCAI 2027 Main Track Call for Papers (Kyoto, Aug 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: AI researchers worldwide may submit abstracts by 4 January 2027 (full papers by 11 January) to IJCAI 2027 in Kyoto.
opportunities.description:
IJCAI 2027, the 36th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence, invites papers for its main track on any area of AI that report significant, original and unpublished results.

The conference takes place in Kyoto, Japan, from 7 to 13 August 2027, with a satellite event in Hengqin, China, from 15 to 17 August 2027. Papers go through a two-phase review, with summary rejections first and then full reviews with an author response period.

For African AI researchers and PhD students, IJCAI is one of the most prestigious venues in the field. Note that at least one author must present in person, so plan travel funding and visas early.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the IJCAI 2027 proceedings and presentation at the conference. A 100 USD submission fee applies per paper, waived for primary papers (where no author has another IJCAI 2027 submission).
requirements: Original, unpublished AI research
Maximum 9 pages (7 body pages plus up to 2 pages of references), double-blind
One qualified author designated as a reciprocal reviewer unless exempt
At least one author attends in person (Kyoto or Hengqin) to present
LLMs may only be used to polish text written by the authors
documents: Full paper PDF using the IJCAI authors' kit (by 11 January 2027)
Optional supplementary material up to 50 MB, anonymised
opportunities.selection_process: Two phases: summary rejection, then full review with an author response. Criteria are novelty, correctness, clarity, significance, impact and presentation.
opportunities.about_provider: IJCAI (International Joint Conferences on Artificial Intelligence) is a non-profit that has run the IJCAI conference, one of the oldest and leading AI conferences, since 1969.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register the abstract by 4 January 2027 and upload the full paper by 11 January 2027 following the IJCAI 2027 submission process page. Questions go to pcchair@2027.ijcai.org.
opportunities.notes: Special tracks (AI4Science, AI and Health, AI and the Arts, AI for Social Good) share the same deadlines.

opportunities.title: MIT need-based financial aid for international first-year students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students may apply to MIT for autumn 2027 by 4 January 2027 and receive need-based aid on the same terms as US students.
opportunities.description:
MIT admits international first-year applicants and offers them the same need-based financial aid as US students. This item covers the Regular Action round for entry in autumn 2027.

The admission application is due on 4 January, and the financial aid application (CSS Profile and family income documents) follows by 15 February for Regular Action applicants. Admission decisions for this round come out in mid-March.

MIT has no country quotas and no minimum test scores, and its aid is based only on need, which makes it reachable for strong African science and engineering students from any income background.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based financial aid on the same terms as for US applicants (amounts depend on family finances and are set after admission).
requirements: Not a US citizen or permanent resident (counts as international)
Three years of secondary-school grades plus external exams such as WAEC, IB, A Levels or national exams
SAT or ACT (no cut-off score); taken by 31 December for Regular Action
English test strongly recommended if you have used English for fewer than five years (results by 31 January)
documents: MIT application and 75 USD fee (or waiver)
CSS Profile and parents' income documents via IDOC, with English translations if needed
opportunities.selection_process: Holistic admissions review, with alumni interviews where available. Aid is worked out separately from the CSS Profile and family documents.
important_dates: Regular Action financial aid deadline: 15 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is a private research university known for science and engineering. Student Financial Services runs its need-based undergraduate aid.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the MIT admissions portal by 4 January, then submit the CSS Profile and family income documents through IDOC by 15 February. Parents outside the US provide their own country's tax returns with translations.
opportunities.notes: Do not confuse the admission date (4 January) with the aid date (15 February). The pages do not print the year, but they describe the current open cycle.

opportunities.title: Middlebury College Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students applying for autumn 2027 entry can request need-based aid that meets full demonstrated need; apply by 4 January 2027 with the CSS Profile due 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Middlebury College, a liberal arts college in Vermont, USA, offers need-based financial aid to international first-year students entering in autumn 2027. For admitted undergraduates, Middlebury meets full demonstrated financial need with its own institutional aid.

Admission for international students is need-aware, which means asking for aid can be taken into account in the admission decision. International students must apply for aid at the same time as they apply for admission; aid cannot be requested later.

For strong African secondary-school students, a full-need offer from a highly selective US college can make a four-year degree affordable. The final application round (Regular Decision and Early Decision II) closes on 4 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based institutional aid that meets the full demonstrated need of admitted undergraduates; the page gives no fixed amounts. Offers are released in early summer.
requirements: Applying as a first-year undergraduate for autumn 2027
Must apply for financial aid at the same time as admission
Proof of English unless English is your native language or language of instruction (recommended: TOEFL iBT 105 / 5.5 on the new scale, IELTS 7.0, Duolingo 130 or Cambridge C1 Advanced)
Tests (SAT/ACT) optional
documents: Common App, Coalition or QuestBridge application
Parents' 2025 non-US tax forms or earning statements, translated into English, or a non-filing statement, uploaded via College Board IDOC
School report, counsellor recommendation and transcript
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is need-aware for international applicants. Financial aid is calculated after the CSS Profile and IDOC documents are reviewed; no interview is required.
important_dates: Early Decision II and Regular Decision applications: 4 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Middlebury College is a highly selective private liberal arts college in Middlebury, Vermont, known for its languages, environmental studies and international programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Common App, Coalition or QuestBridge by 4 January 2027, then complete the CSS Profile on the College Board website and upload family financial documents through IDOC (not by email). Middlebury does not accept the ISFAA or a paper CSS Profile from international applicants.
opportunities.notes: The CSS Profile has a fee; fee waivers are decided by College Board. Contact: sfs@middlebury.edu, +1 802 443 5158.

opportunities.title: WashU Need-Based Financial Aid for First-Year International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students applying for autumn 2027 can receive aid meeting full demonstrated need and automatic merit awards; apply by 4 January 2027 with aid forms due 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Washington University in St. Louis (WashU) meets 100 percent of demonstrated financial need for all admitted undergraduates, including international students entering in autumn 2027. Merit scholarships are awarded automatically, with no separate application, and some can cover up to full tuition.

International applicants must ask for aid at the time they apply: those who do not apply for aid during admission cannot receive it later. The application fee of USD 75 is waived for students applying for aid.

For talented African school leavers, WashU combines a top US research university with full-need aid. The Regular Decision and Early Decision II application deadline is 4 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based aid meeting 100% of demonstrated need for admitted undergraduates; automatic merit scholarships that can reach full tuition; application fee (USD 75) waived for aid applicants. The page gives no fixed amounts.
requirements: Non-US citizen or permanent resident applying on a temporary visa
In secondary school or graduated without full-time university study
At least 12 years of primary and secondary schooling and a secondary diploma
English test (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo) for non-native speakers
Must apply for aid during the admission process
documents: Common App or Coalition application with essay
250-word response on intended field of study
School report and official transcript (certified English translations if needed)
Optional SAT/ACT or national exam results
CSS Profile and financial aid documents
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed holistically; aid is set from the financial aid application. Early Decision is binding.
important_dates: ED II and Regular Decision applications: 4 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Washington University in St. Louis is a leading private research university in Missouri, USA.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Common App or Coalition by 4 January 2027 and complete the financial aid application (CSS Profile) by 1 February 2027 for Regular Decision. After submitting you get access to the WashU Pathway portal to track your file.
opportunities.notes: You will not be eligible for aid after receiving your admission decision, so apply for it from the start. Visa documents (F-1/J-1) are issued only after admission and proof of funds. Contact: admissions@wustl.edu, +1 314 935 6000.

opportunities.title: Williams College Need-Based Aid for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants who indicate they need aid are considered for grants meeting 100% of demonstrated need; Regular Decision closes 4 January.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Competitive full or partial tuition waivers for non-EU master's students starting 2027; apply with the admission application by 5 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Bowdoin College need-blind financial aid for international first-year students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students may apply to Bowdoin by 5 January 2027; admission is need-blind and aid meets full need without loans.
opportunities.description:
Bowdoin College in Brunswick, Maine, is need-blind for international applicants: whether you need aid does not affect admission. It meets the full calculated need of every admitted student with grants and no loans.

For entry in autumn 2027, Early Decision 2 and Regular Decision applications are due on 5 January. International students submit aid forms only after they are admitted, within seven days of the offer.

Because few US colleges are need-blind for international students, Bowdoin is an especially good option for African secondary-school students with strong records who need full financial support.
opportunities.benefits: Grants meeting full calculated need with no loans; the average annual aid package is about 72,883 USD. The 70 USD application fee is waived automatically for aid applicants.
requirements: Applying as a first-year student for autumn 2027
No minimum GPA or test score; English tests optional
National exam results (for example WASSCE or KCSE) submitted as official results, transcripts in English
Not already holding a bachelor's degree; international transfer students receive no Bowdoin aid
documents: Common App, Coalition on Scoir or QuestBridge application
Official transcripts and national exam results
After admission: aid forms (CSS Profile, code 3089) within 7 days of the offer
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is decided without regard to need; aid is calculated after admission.
important_dates: Early Decision 2 and Regular Decision deadline: 5 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Bowdoin College is a private liberal arts college founded in 1794 in Brunswick, Maine. It gives need-based aid only, with no merit scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common App, Coalition on Scoir or QuestBridge by 5 January 2027. If admitted, complete the aid forms within seven days of your offer.
opportunities.notes: Bowdoin's pages disagree on whether the ISFAA form is still accepted instead of the CSS Profile; confirm with sao@bowdoin.edu.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Communications and Data Science (CoDaS) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality in communications, computer, electrical or software engineering with excellent grades can apply from 1 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 for this two-year European master's with full Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
CoDaS is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Communications and Data Science, run by five European universities: Aalto University (Finland), Grenoble INP-UGA (France), Tecnico Lisboa (Portugal), TU Braunschweig (Germany) and UPC BarcelonaTech (Spain). Students spend the first year at a home university and the second at a host university, starting in autumn 2027.

The two-year programme combines communications engineering with data science. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover the EUR 8,000 yearly programme fee and pay EUR 1,400 a month, while the consortium's own CoDaS scholarships waive the fee.

The programme is open to all nationalities. African graduates in communications engineering, computer science, electrical or software engineering with excellent grades are well placed to apply when the window opens on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: programme fee of EUR 8,000 per year waived for two years plus EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months. CoDaS scholarship: fee waiver; CoDaS Premium adds monthly support. The fee covers tuition, insurance, summer school and a conference. Non-EM students may get EUR 300 towards travel to the second-year university.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS / three years in communications engineering, computer science, electrical engineering (communications) or software engineering
Excellent grades (examples given: India 8.0/10 or 80%, Pakistan 3.60/4)
No previous master's degree (except long-cycle degrees)
Degree completed by 31 July 2027

English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (writing 6.0), TOEFL iBT 4.5 (writing 4) on the new scale, PTE 62 (writing 54) or Cambridge C1/C2; tests taken on or after 1 December 2024 (South African English-medium degrees are accepted as proof)
Maximum 10% of EM scholarships per nationality
documents: Motivation letter (max 500 words, on the form)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are ranked on the relevance of their previous studies, academic performance, the standing of their institution, suitability and motivation (including the video) and other skills. Scholarships are awarded from the same application.
important_dates: Documents, test scores and video: 12 January 2027, 15:00 GMT+2
opportunities.about_provider: The CoDaS consortium is a partnership of five European technical universities, with admissions managed by Aalto University in Finland, and is co-funded by the European Union.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the single online application on the Aalto portal linked from the CoDaS admission page between 1 December 2026 and 5 January 2027; it cannot be saved as a draft, so prepare everything first. Upload the remaining documents and video by 12 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per person. Late or partial documents are not considered and deadlines are not extended. Contact: codas@aalto.fi.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Plant and Microbe Engineering for Sustainability (N2) Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and early postdocs anywhere who present a poster can apply by 5 January 2027 for up to USD 1,500.
opportunities.description:
Keystone Symposia offers scholarships for early-career scientists to attend its meeting on Plant and Microbe Engineering for Sustainability (N2), held jointly with the Receptor Kinase Signaling meeting at the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver, Canada, from 2 to 5 May 2027. The meeting is organised by Dan Voytas, Ralph Bock and Jennifer Pett-Ridge.

Scholarships pay up to USD 1,500 towards the cost of attending in person, reimbursed against receipts. Applicants must submit an abstract and present a poster. A separate Global Health Award, with an earlier 1 December 2026 deadline, also exists for scientists from low- and middle-income countries.

Graduate students and postdocs anywhere can apply, so African plant scientists and microbiologists can use this to present their work at a leading international meeting.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 1,500 towards airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee, reimbursed with receipts.
requirements: Graduate student, or postdoc within 8 years of the PhD, MD or DVM
Enrolled or employed at the start of the meeting
Attend in person and present a poster
One award per person per meeting year, and one per lab
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers review abstracts for scientific quality, significance, clarity and relevance to the meeting.
important_dates: Scholarship and short-talk abstract deadline: 5 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) organisation that runs scientific conferences around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through Keystone Symposia's abstract system and your scholarship application with a mentor letter through its online scholarship portal by 5 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Keystone Symposia Receptor Kinase Signaling: Fueling Plant Resilience and Development (N1) Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs worldwide may apply by 5 January 2027 for up to 1,500 USD to attend Keystone's plant receptor kinase meeting in Vancouver.
opportunities.description:
Keystone Symposia offers scholarships for graduate students and postdoctoral researchers to attend its meeting "Receptor Kinase Signaling: Fueling Plant Resilience and Development" (N1), held jointly with "Plant and Microbe Engineering for Sustainability".

The meeting takes place from 2 to 5 May 2027 at the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver in British Columbia, Canada, and can also be followed by livestream or on demand. Scholarship holders attend in person and present a poster.

It is a good fit for African plant scientists, agronomists and molecular biologists working on plant signalling, crop resilience or plant-microbe engineering who want to present their work internationally.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 1,500 USD towards in-person attendance, covering airfare, ground transport, lodging and part of the registration fee, reimbursed against receipts.
