requirements: Graduate student, or postdoc within 8 years of receiving a PhD, MD or DVM
Enrolled or in post at the start of the meeting
Attend in person and present a poster
Only one Keystone scholarship per applicant per meeting year (July to June) and one per lab
documents: Abstract (up to 1,000 words) with a refundable 50 USD abstract fee for in-person attendance
Letter from your mentor, submitted on your behalf
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are based on the scientific quality and relevance of the abstract.
important_dates: Scholarship and short-talk abstract deadline: 5 January 2027, 11:59 pm Mountain time
opportunities.about_provider: Keystone Symposia is a US non-profit that organises scientific conferences in molecular and cellular biology around the world and funds scholarships to help early-career scientists attend.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit and pay for your abstract, ask your mentor to send a letter, and complete the scholarship application on the Keystone Symposia SmApply portal by 5 January 2027. Questions go to scholarships@keystonesymposia.org.
opportunities.notes: Submitting an abstract does not guarantee registration. NIH employees can only receive in-kind registration. Keystone also runs Global Health Awards and Early-Career Travel Awards for some meetings.

opportunities.title: NED Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Democracy practitioners and PhD scholars worldwide with good English may apply by 5 January 2027 for a funded five-month fellowship in Washington, DC.
opportunities.description:
The Reagan-Fascell Democracy Fellows Program brings democracy activists, journalists, civil-society leaders and scholars to Washington, DC, for five months of independent research and writing at the National Endowment for Democracy's International Forum for Democratic Studies.

There are two tracks. Practitioners need substantial hands-on experience promoting democracy or human rights, usually mid-career, with no degree required. Scholars need a PhD and publications. Fellows produce a written or audiovisual output and give a presentation.

The programme is aimed mainly at people from developing democracies and non-democratic countries, which makes it an excellent opportunity for African practitioners and researchers working on governance, rights and civic space.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend for living costs and a short-term furnished apartment, basic health insurance, and round-trip travel to Washington at the start and end. Family travel is paid by the fellow.
requirements: Good English
A project on political, social, economic, legal or cultural aspects of democratic development
Available for the full five months in Washington with no other job or fellowship
Practitioner track: substantial practical experience in democracy or human rights; Scholar track: PhD (or equivalent) and a publication record
Not a former Reagan-Fascell fellow; not on a J-1 research scholar programme in the previous 24 months
documents: Project proposal for the chosen track
opportunities.selection_process: Competitive annual review; finalists are chosen by NED's Board of Directors. Deferrals are generally not offered.
opportunities.about_provider: The National Endowment for Democracy (NED) is a US non-profit foundation funding democracy work worldwide. Its International Forum for Democratic Studies runs research and fellowship programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on NED's fellowship application site and submit the forms and proposal by 5 January 2027; referees send letters by 12 January. Questions go to fellowships@ned.org.
opportunities.notes: Fellows need a J-1 visa and usually must return home for two years afterwards. Copying AI-generated answers wholesale is prohibited.

opportunities.title: CENTA NERC Project-Based PhD Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a 2:1 bachelor's or a master's in a relevant science who apply to a listed CENTA project; international places are capped at 30%.
opportunities.description:
CENTA, the Central England NERC Training Alliance, is recruiting for its project-based PhD studentships starting in autumn 2027. CENTA is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and led by the University of Birmingham with partner universities and research centres across central England.

Applicants choose a specific project from CENTA's list, covering environmental and earth sciences, and apply to the host university. Studentships last 3.5 years and include a tax-free stipend and a research training grant. Applications close at 23:59 GMT on Wednesday 6 January 2027.

International applicants, including Africans, can apply, but UK rules limit them to 30% of the cohort, and CENTA only pays fees at the home rate, so international students face a fee shortfall to cover themselves.
opportunities.benefits: For 3.5 years: a stipend of £21,805 a year (2026/27 rate) paid monthly, tuition fees at the UK home rate (international students will likely face a fee shortfall), and a research training support grant of £8,000. Visa, health surcharge, flights and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: At least a 2:1 UK bachelor's or a pass in a UK master's, or equivalent
Application to a specific CENTA project
International students are capped at 30% of the cohort
International students must cover the gap between home and international fees
Only one project per university
documents: CENTA Studentship Application Form (2027 version) - applications without it are rejected
CV with at least two referees
Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) survey receipt number
opportunities.selection_process: Each host university's recruitment team shortlists applicants, online interviews are normally held in early February, and conditional offers go out in late February or early March 2027. Offers depend on the host university's admission offer.
opportunities.about_provider: CENTA is a NERC-funded doctoral training partnership that trains PhD researchers in environmental science. It is hosted by the University of Birmingham with partner universities and research organisations in central England.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pick a project from the CENTA projects list, then apply through the host university's online portal, attaching the CENTA Studentship Application Form, your CV with two referees and the EDI survey receipt. Submit before 23:59 GMT on 6 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The separate CENTA Science Opportunity Scholarships (CSOS) are closed for 2027 and not open to international students. One Cranfield project (2027-C03) starts earlier, by 6 June 2027.

opportunities.title: EdUHK Entrance Scholarship for Non-local Students 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-local school leavers, including African applicants, admitted to EdUHK undergraduate programmes for 2027/28 can receive scholarships of up to 270,000 HKD a year; main round closes 6 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK) awards entrance scholarships to non-local students admitted to its full-time government-funded undergraduate programmes. The scholarships are renewable each year and range from half tuition to a full award that also helps with living costs.

The 2027/28 admission round for international applicants opened on 5 October 2026. The main round closes on 6 January 2027, with a late round to 7 May 2027; interviews and offers run on a rolling basis, and studies begin in early September 2027.

EdUHK accepts many African school qualifications, including WASSCE, the South African NSC and others, so African school leavers interested in education, languages, social sciences or related fields can compete for these awards.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship of 270,000 HKD a year, Tuition Scholarship of 210,000 HKD a year, or Half-tuition Scholarship of 105,000 HKD a year, renewable annually. Amounts may change without notice.
requirements: Non-local applicant admitted to a full-time government-funded undergraduate programme for 2027/28
Meets EdUHK general entrance requirements with an accepted national qualification (for example WASSCE with at least C6 in English for Ghana, Gambia or Liberia)
English: for example IELTS Academic 6.0, PTE Academic 62, or Cambridge C1/C2 grade C (180)
Admission is competitive and usually includes an interview
documents: School transcripts and public exam results (or predicted grades)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed for admission, with interviews from December 2026 to May 2027; the scholarships are offered to admitted non-local students (no separate scholarship form is described).
important_dates: Interviews and offers: December 2026 to May 2027 (rolling)
opportunities.about_provider: The Education University of Hong Kong is a public university in Tai Po, Hong Kong, focused on teacher education and related disciplines in the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through EdUHK's undergraduate application system for non-local students and upload all supporting documents, since an application is incomplete without them. Pending results can be added later.
opportunities.notes: Applicants without an offer by the end of July 2027 may assume they were unsuccessful. Other options for non-local students include the HKSAR Belt and Road Scholarship.

opportunities.title: French Government Eiffel Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International master's candidates aged up to 29 and doctoral candidates aged up to 35 can be nominated by a French higher-education institution for the 2027 Eiffel call.
opportunities.description:
The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' flagship award for bringing top international students to French universities and grandes écoles. Campus France runs the programme on the ministry's behalf, and the 2027 call opened on 2 October 2026.

The award supports two tracks: master's study and doctoral study (usually a mobility period within a co-supervised or co-directed doctorate). Students do not apply to Campus France themselves. Instead, a French institution that has admitted or is admitting the student puts the candidate forward, and the institution files the application with Campus France.

For African students this is one of the most visible French government awards, and it is open to applicants from any country outside France. Because the institution must nominate you, the practical first step is to apply for admission early to a French programme and ask its international office whether it nominates candidates for Eiffel.
opportunities.benefits: The programme funds a monthly allowance and related support for the master's or doctoral stay in France; the exact amounts and coverage are set out in the 2027 programme regulations published by Campus France.
requirements: Nominated by a French higher-education institution (no direct student applications)
Master's track: aged 29 or under
Doctoral track: aged 35 or under
Admitted to, or being admitted to, a programme at the nominating institution
documents: Application file prepared with the host institution (following the Campus France filing guide)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored by expert evaluators drawn from French university teacher-researchers, using separate published grids for the master's and doctoral tracks. Results are announced by Campus France.
opportunities.about_provider: Campus France is the French national agency for promoting higher education, hosting international students and managing government scholarships. It administers the Eiffel programme for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a French institution and ask its international office about its internal Eiffel deadline, which falls before 6 January 2027. The institution prepares and submits the file to Campus France; new institutions contact candidatures.eiffel@campusfrance.org to get access.
opportunities.notes: Check the host institution's own deadline, which is earlier than the Campus France date. An English version of the programme page is available on campusfrance.org.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation AfOx Scholarship 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded graduate study at Oxford for African students.

opportunities.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship and QEII-GSST at University of Windsor 2027-28
opportunities.provider: University of Windsor Faculty of Graduate Studies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate applicants and students at the University of Windsor, including international students, can apply through their department for the Ontario Graduate Scholarship or the QEII Graduate Scholarship in Science and Technology.
opportunities.description:
The Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) and the Queen Elizabeth II Graduate Scholarship in Science and Technology (QEII-GSST) are provincial graduate awards in Ontario, Canada. At the University of Windsor, both competitions for awards held in 2027-28 are run through the Faculty of Graduate Studies, and the university states clearly that they are open to international applicants as well as Canadian citizens and permanent residents.

This matters for African students, because many other Canadian graduate awards on the same Windsor deadlines list (such as the CGS Master's, the Mackenzie King award and the NSERC undergraduate research awards) are limited to Canadians and permanent residents. OGS and QEII-GSST are among the few funding competitions at Windsor that international master's and doctoral students can enter.

Applications are not sent to a central office. Each student applies to their own graduate department at Windsor, which may set an earlier internal deadline; departments then rank their candidates and pass them on to Graduate Studies. Detailed instructions for the competition are published separately on the university's OGS/QEII-GSST web page, which the university said would be updated in mid-November 2026.
important_dates: Instructions expected on the OGS/QEII-GSST web page: mid-November 2026
Application to your graduate department: 6 January 2027, 11:59 p.m. EST
Faculty rankings to Graduate Studies: 24 February 2027
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the University of Windsor Graduate Studies OGS/QEII-GSST web page for the detailed 2027-28 instructions and forms, and ask your graduate department about its internal deadline. Submit your application to your department by 6 January 2027 at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern time). Departments rank applicants and send nominations to Graduate Studies by 24 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Departments can set their own earlier deadlines, so confirm with your programme. Most other external awards on Windsor's 2027-28 list are for Canadians and permanent residents only.

opportunities.title: Yale Young Global Scholars 2027 (Regular Decision)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High-school students aged 16 to 18 from any country may apply by 6 January 2027 for Yale's two-week summer programme, with need-based aid up to full tuition.
opportunities.description:
Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) is a two-week residential summer programme at Yale University for secondary-school students from around the world. Participants take part in lectures, seminars and group work led by Yale faculty and staff in a chosen subject area.

The programme takes place on Yale's campus in New Haven, Connecticut, in summer 2027 in several two-week sessions (one session starts on 18 July 2027). Regular Decision applications close on 6 January 2027.

YYGS accepts applications from all countries and offers need-based aid up to full tuition, so strong African high-school students can attend regardless of family income.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based financial aid of up to the full tuition for domestic and international students. Tuition is 7,500 USD, covering housing, meals and course materials. Travel is not covered. The 100 USD application fee can be waived for students with financial need.
requirements: Aged 16 to 18 by 18 July 2027
Currently a high-school sophomore or junior (or the international equivalent), graduating in May/June 2028 or 2029 (Northern Hemisphere) or November/December 2027 or 2028 (Southern Hemisphere)
Able to follow a demanding curriculum in English
First-time YYGS participant
documents: Online application with the required components
Application fee of 100 USD or a fee waiver form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed as a full pool after the deadline, with decisions by 10 March 2027.
important_dates: Regular Decision deadline: 6 January 2027, 11:59 pm US Eastern time
Accept and pay tuition: by 15 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Yale University is a private Ivy League research university in New Haven, Connecticut. YYGS is its academic enrichment programme for high-school students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online YYGS application, request a fee waiver in the form if needed, and submit by 6 January 2027. Admitted students pay through Slate or Flywire.
opportunities.notes: Tuition is non-refundable except in extreme cases. YYGS runs a free webinar on choosing a deadline.

opportunities.title: ACCE+ NERC Doctoral Landscape Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least a 2:1 or equivalent in a relevant subject can apply for ACCE+ NERC-funded ecology and environmental PhD projects starting in 2027/28; international applicants compete for up to 30% of places.
opportunities.description:
ACCE+ is a NERC Doctoral Landscape Award partnership that trains PhD researchers in ecology, evolution and the wider environmental sciences. It is led by the University of Liverpool with the Universities of Sheffield and York and research partners including the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, the Natural History Museum and the National Oceanography Centre.

For 2027/28 entry the partnership is advertising projects from early November 2026 and funds at least 13 studentships a year. Students join a cohort-based programme with shared training across the partner institutions alongside their individual research project.

International students, including applicants from Africa, may apply, but UKRI rules cap international candidates at 30% of studentships and interview places, and not every ACCE+ department is taking international applicants this year. Check each project advert before applying.
opportunities.benefits: NERC-funded PhD studentship for 2027/28 entry with cohort training across the partnership; the funding package is detailed on the ACCE+ financial-support page.
requirements: Degree in a subject relevant to the project
Liverpool, Sheffield and York generally expect the equivalent of a UK 2:1 or better (exceptions for demonstrated excellence)
International applicants limited to 30% of studentships and interviews
Some departments are not accepting international applicants for 2027/28: check the project advert
English proficiency evidence if requested by the host institution
documents: Host institution's online application form with the ACCE+ proforma questions (replaces CV and personal statement)
Details of referees, including at least one academic
Transcripts, passport and English test certificate if requested
Mandatory equality, diversity and inclusion form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications receive a holistic, contextualised review against the published ACCE+ rubric, followed by interviews in the weeks of 15 and 22 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ACCE+ (Adapting to the Challenges of a Changing Environment) is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK Natural Environment Research Council. It brings together Liverpool, Sheffield and York with national research centres and museums.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose one or two projects at a host institution and apply through that institution's online form, adding the ACCE+ proforma answers, referee details and the EDI form. Applications to different institutions are made separately. Questions go to acce.dtp@liverpool.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: You may apply for up to two projects per institution. The Widening Participation scheme is for Home candidates only.

opportunities.title: CUHK International Undergraduate Admission Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International school leavers admitted to CUHK undergraduate programmes for 2027 are automatically considered for merit entrance scholarships; the Regular Round closes 7 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) gives entrance scholarships to outstanding international students admitted to its full-time undergraduate programmes for 2027 entry. There is no separate scholarship application: admitted non-local students are considered automatically.

CUHK does not offer need-based financial aid to international students, so these merit scholarships are the main support available. Amounts are listed on the university's admission scholarships pages, which were not read for this write-up.

CUHK publishes minimum entry requirements for many African school systems (for example South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, Ethiopia, Cameroon, Mauritius, Uganda, Tanzania and Zimbabwe). The final (Regular) application round closes on 7 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Merit-based entrance scholarships for admitted international undergraduates (amounts on CUHK's admission scholarships pages). For reference, 2027-28 tuition is HK$230,000 a year and living costs are about HK$48,500.
requirements: Non-local applicant needing a student visa (or eligible dependant/IANG visa holder aged 18+)
Meets the minimum requirement for your school system (e.g. IB Diploma 30, South African NSC 70%, Ugandan UACE or Tanzanian ACSE BBB, Cameroon Baccalaureat 14/20)
English: IELTS Academic 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 80 (older scale); home editions and online IELTS not accepted
Some programmes require an interview
documents: Academic transcripts and public exam results
opportunities.selection_process: Admission and scholarships are based on academic results, other achievements and individual merit; some programmes interview. Offers are made on a rolling basis.
opportunities.about_provider: The Chinese University of Hong Kong is one of Asia's top research universities, with a college system and teaching in English and Chinese.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the CUHK Online Application Portal by 7 January 2027 and pay the HK$500 fee at submission; only one application is allowed. Admitted students are considered for entrance scholarships automatically.
opportunities.notes: Financial aid is not available to international students. The application fee cannot be waived. Documents uploaded under 'Identity Document(s)' may not be reviewed, so place academic files in the right sections.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus GrEnFIn Scholarship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality in maths, physics, economics, statistics, IT or engineering with B2 English can apply by 7 January 2027 for this triple-degree European master in green energy and finance, with up to 18 full scholarships.
opportunities.description:
GrEnFIn (Greening Energy Market and Finance) is a 24-month Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of 120 ECTS coordinated by the University of Bologna, with LMU Munich and Universite Paris-Dauphine as full partners. Graduates receive three degrees. Students choose one of three tracks: Renewable Technologies, Environmental Finance, or Climate and Business.

Studies take place in Bologna, Munich and Paris (with a London campus for one track), starting on 6 September 2027. Up to 51 students are admitted for 2027-28, and up to 18 receive full Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400 a month.

The programme is open to all nationalities and suits African graduates in mathematics, physics, economics, statistics, IT or engineering who want to work on the energy transition and green finance.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 18 full Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 2027-28 of EUR 1,400 gross per month, intended to cover travel, visa, installation and living costs. Self-funded students pay tuition (a fixed EUR 157.04 plus an income-based amount).
requirements: Three-year bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, economics, statistics, IT or engineering
Final-year students must graduate by 23 July 2027
English at CEFR B2 (exempt for degrees or nationality from the USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland or the UK)
Competence score of at least 60/100 (academic merit up to 60, experience up to 30, optional GRE/GMAT up to 10); 80+ invited to interview
No more than 10% of scholarships per nationality
documents: ISCED classification template (Excel, from the application page)
Degree certificate and transcript (English translation and Diploma Supplement if available)
opportunities.selection_process: An Admission Board from the three universities scores each file; candidates with 80 or more are interviewed, and a single ranking across tracks decides the scholarships.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Bologna (Alma Mater Studiorum) is one of Europe's oldest universities and coordinates GrEnFIn with LMU Munich and Universite Paris-Dauphine.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in to the University of Bologna's Studenti Online portal, choose 'Admission application' for a second-cycle programme and select one GrEnFIn track. Upload all documents as PDFs before 11:00 CET on 7 January 2027; documents sent by post or email are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Deadlines are final and missing mandatory documents lead to exclusion. Contact: grenfin.emjm@unibo.it.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus International Master in Security, Intelligence and Strategic Studies (IMSISS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a 2:1 or equivalent in politics, IR, law, history and related fields, from any country, can apply by 7 January 2027 for this two-year European security master's with Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
IMSISS is an Erasmus Mundus International Master in Security, Intelligence and Strategic Studies, led by the University of Glasgow with Dublin City University, the University of Trento, Charles University in Prague and the University of Belgrade. It is a full-time, two-year programme taught in at least three cities, starting in September 2027.

Students follow one of three pathways (Glasgow-DCU-Prague, Glasgow-Trento-Prague or Glasgow-DCU-Belgrade). Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover full tuition, insurance and a monthly allowance, and part of the scholarships are targeted at regions that include Africa.

For African graduates in politics, international relations, law, history and related fields, IMSISS is a fully funded route into European security and intelligence studies. Scholarship applications close on 7 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: full tuition, full insurance and a monthly allowance, either EUR 1,275 a month over two years plus three EUR 1,000 travel and installation payments, or EUR 1,400 a month without the travel payment. Part of the scholarships target Erasmus+ partner regions, including African regions; no more than 6 per nationality across four editions.
requirements: A strict 2:1 UK honours degree or international equivalent in a listed field (politics, IR, history, law, sociology, economics, management, computing and others)
Relevant work experience may be considered alongside a lower grade
Conditional or unconditional offer from Glasgow before scholarship consideration
No earlier Erasmus Mundus scholarship
Pathway B (Trento) also needs B2 in a language other than English or Italian
English proof as set by the University of Glasgow
documents: Two signed references on headed paper, at least one academic, dated within 24 months
Transcripts and degree certificates with certified translations
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarship candidates are ranked by the consortium: personal statement 40%, academic merit 30%, other achievements (research, experience, publications) 30%. A reserve list is kept.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow's School of Social and Political Sciences leads the IMSISS consortium and manages its admissions; the programme is funded by the EU's Erasmus+ programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow portal linked from the IMSISS Apply page (admit term 2027/8, programme 'Security') and upload the scholarship form as a PDF. All documents must be in at the time of the scholarship application; files 'held for documents' are not considered.
opportunities.notes: References from personal email addresses are not accepted. A deposit of GBP 2,000 applies; scholarship winners pay after the April results. Contact: imsiss@glasgow.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus MESPOM Environmental Sciences, Policy and Management 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a related degree and GPA 3.5+ may apply; funding applicants must submit by 7 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
MESPOM (Masters in Environmental Sciences, Policy and Management) is a 24-month, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's run by Central European University (coordinator), Lund University, the University of Manchester and the University of the Aegean. The 2027-2029 cohort begins in 2027 with an autumn and winter term at CEU in Vienna and a spring term on Lesvos at the University of the Aegean, followed by summer internships, a second year at Lund or Manchester and a thesis at a consortium partner.

The call invites applicants from all countries. Those who want financial aid must apply by 7 January 2027; self-financing applicants have until 15 April 2027, or 15 July 2027 if they can enter Austria without a visa.

The programme combines science, policy and management of the environment, making it relevant for African graduates aiming at careers in environmental agencies, NGOs, consultancies or international organisations. Funding is competitive and takes the form of partial tuition waivers and living stipends for the strongest applicants.
opportunities.benefits: Partial tuition fee waivers and living stipends for outstanding students (amounts are on the programme's funding pages, not on the call page).
requirements: Good first degree in a related subject with a GPA of 3.5 or above (other degrees considered with evidence of commitment to the field)
English proficiency
Open to applicants from all countries
Apply by 7 January 2027 to be considered for financial aid
documents: Online application via the CEU portal with transcripts, degree, CV, motivation and references as listed on the MESPOM how-to-apply page
opportunities.selection_process: Highly competitive selection based on academic excellence, motivation and prior experience.
important_dates: Self-financing deadline: 15 April 2027 (15 July 2027 for applicants with visa-free entry to Austria)
opportunities.about_provider: MESPOM is delivered by Central European University (Vienna), Lund University (Sweden), the University of Manchester (UK) and the University of the Aegean (Greece), with CEU as coordinator.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the CEU online application system linked from the MESPOM call page, choosing MESPOM 2027-2029, and submit before 7 January 2027 to be considered for funding. Questions go to coordinator@mespom.eu.
opportunities.notes: Check the eligibility, how-to-apply and potential sources of funding pages on mespom.eu for the full document list and stipend amounts.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master of Science in Geospatial Technologies (GeoTech)
opportunities.provider: University of Muenster, Universitat Jaume I, NOVA Lisbon
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any partner country, including African countries, with a finished 180-ECTS bachelor's in geography, GI science, planning or computing can apply by 7 January 2027 for this funded master in Germany, Spain and Portugal.
opportunities.description:
The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Geospatial Technologies (GeoTech) is taught by the University of Munster (Germany), Universitat Jaume I (Castellon, Spain) and NOVA University Lisbon (Portugal). It lasts three semesters and starts at the beginning of September 2027; the programme has been reselected for four more editions from 2027.

Up to 32 students are admitted each year, split between Lisbon and Castellon. Erasmus Mundus scholarships for partner-country students are full scholarships covering tuition, insurance and EUR 1,400 a month for 18 months.

African graduates in geography, planning, geoinformation, computer science and related fields are eligible as partner-country applicants, as long as their bachelor's degree is finished by the deadline.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: EUR 1,400 per month for 18 months, tuition coverage of EUR 1,800 per semester, insurance and diploma fees; it is described as a full scholarship covering all costs. Students need their own laptop.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of six semesters (180 ECTS) completed at the time of application
Relevant degree recommended (geography, planning, GI science; computer science welcome)
English: IELTS Academic 6.0 (6 in each band), TOEFL iBT 3.5 on the new scale (61 older scale), TOEFL PBT 500 or Cambridge FCE, or an English-taught degree; home-based tests not accepted
Not already admitted to or funded by another Erasmus Mundus master
documents: Bachelor's diploma and transcript (official translation if needed)
Europass CV without gaps in the last 5.5 years
Public video link (max 2 minutes) on your CV and motivation
Two recommendation letters uploaded by referees by the deadline
Residence proof if residence differs from nationality
opportunities.selection_process: A formal check of documents, possibly followed by an online interview to clarify them; candidates are then ranked for admission and scholarships.
opportunities.about_provider: GeoTech is run by three European universities with strong geoinformatics departments: the University of Munster, Universitat Jaume I and NOVA University Lisbon.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online application and supporting documents through the GeoTech application system by 18:00 CET on 7 January 2027, choosing the correct scholarship category (partner or programme country). Referees upload their letters through the system by the same date.
opportunities.notes: The site gives conflicting scholarship counts (about 19 for partner-country students in the body text versus a smaller number in the page summary). Self-funded applications for 2027 are already closed.

opportunities.title: IGNITE NERC Doctoral Landscape Award PhD Studentships 2027 (University of Southampton)
opportunities.provider: IGNITE Doctoral Landscape Award, University of Southampton (NERC-funded)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with a 2:1 bachelor's or a merit/distinction master's (or equivalent) can apply for NERC-funded environmental science PhDs; up to 30% of places (about 5 a year) go to international students.
opportunities.description:
IGNITE is a Doctoral Landscape Award funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and hosted by the University of Southampton, with partners such as the British Antarctic Survey, the National Oceanography Centre, the Marine Biological Association and the Natural History Museum. It funds environmental science PhD projects starting in 2027.

Applications are open until 7 January 2027. Shortlisted candidates are invited to online visit days in late February and interviews in the first week of March 2027, with offers made about a week later. Studentships last up to 3.5 years.

International students, including African applicants, can compete for up to 30% of the studentships, usually around five a year, but not every project is open to them. The page advises international applicants to contact the project's lead supervisor before applying, and those proposing their own project need a CASE partner involved.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fees at the UK rate covered in full, a tax-free stipend of GBP 21,805 a year (UKRI 2026/27 rate) and a Research Training Support Grant of GBP 2,200 a year, for up to 3.5 years. The page does not state that the higher international fee is covered.
requirements: Upper second-class (2:1) bachelor's or MSci, and/or a master's at merit or distinction (over 60%), or equivalent professional experience
IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 92 where applicable
International applicants: only projects marked as open to them; contact the lead supervisor first
International applicants proposing their own project need a CASE partner
documents: Research proposal, if proposing your own project
Recommended: degree certificates, two academic references, English test result, CV (maximum 2 pages)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by the faculty admissions team, the supervisors and the IGNITE recruitment panel, with interview decisions within about a month of the deadline. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online.
important_dates: Visit days: 24 February 2027 (online) and 26 February 2027 (in person)
Offers: about one week after interviews
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Southampton is a UK research university with major strengths in ocean and earth sciences. IGNITE brings it together with national environmental research centres and museums to train the next generation of environmental scientists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pick a project from the IGNITE list (checking it is open to international applicants), contact its lead supervisor, then apply through the University of Southampton postgraduate research application portal before 7 January 2027. Questions go to nerc-dla@soton.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Johns Hopkins SAIS Europe MAIA Financial Aid Fall 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality to the Johns Hopkins SAIS Europe MAIA in Bologna for Fall 2027 can be considered for merit and need-based aid by applying by 7 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Johns Hopkins SAIS Europe in Bologna, Italy, offers financial aid to students entering its Master of Arts in International Affairs (MAIA). Awards range from partial tuition funding to a small number of full-tuition scholarships, and the school reports that more than 70% of its entering class receives aid.

The MAIA is a graduate degree in international relations and international economics taught at the SAIS Europe campus. Aid is considered as part of the admission application, so candidates must apply for admission and complete the financial aid section by the Regular Decision deadline.

Aid is open to students of every nationality, which makes it relevant for African applicants interested in diplomacy, development, international economics and policy careers. Some donor-funded awards carry their own nationality restrictions or separate applications.
opportunities.benefits: Merit and need-based awards from partial tuition funding up to a limited number of full-tuition scholarships; second-year support is possible for strong students. No application fee.
requirements: Applying for the SAIS Europe MAIA, Fall 2027 entry
Grade of B- or better in introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics (or one course covering both) before enrolling
English test for non-native speakers
Interview required for all MAIA candidates
GRE/GMAT optional
documents: Online application with the financial aid section completed
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is decided on the full application and an interview; aid is awarded at admission on merit and need. Some donor awards require a separate application.
important_dates: Regular Decision and aid deadline: 7 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) is the graduate school of international affairs of Johns Hopkins University, with campuses in Washington DC, Bologna and Nanjing.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for the MAIA by 7 January 2027 and answer yes to the scholarship question in the financial aid section; otherwise you will not be considered. Send proof of income by 15 February and prepare for the admission interview.
opportunities.notes: Ticking the scholarship consideration box is essential. Check donor awards on the page for any separate application.

opportunities.title: NERC GW4+ Doctoral Landscape Training Partnership 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a 2:1 or better in a related subject can apply for one GW4+ NERC PhD project starting September 2027; a limited number of full studentships go to international students.
opportunities.description:
The Great Western Four+ Doctoral Training Partnership funds PhD research across the environmental sciences. It links the Universities of Bristol, Bath, Cardiff and Exeter with research partners including the British Antarctic Survey, British Geological Survey, UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, Natural History Museum and Plymouth Marine Laboratory.

Studentships start in September 2027 and are funded for three and a half years full time, with up to four years to complete. Students pick a project advertised by one of the partner schools and join a cross-institution training cohort.

The programme is mainly for UK students, but a limited number of full studentships are available to international applicants, which makes it a realistic route for strong African graduates in earth, ocean, climate, ecology and related fields.
opportunities.benefits: Tax-free stipend of £22,437 a year; tuition fees paid (international awardees are charged at the home fee rate); research and training support grant of £11,000; training budget of £1,000. Visa, immigration health surcharge and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: Upper second-class degree or higher (or international equivalent) in a discipline related to the project
Master's degree encouraged but not required
English at University of Bristol profile level E if English is not your first language
Only one project application allowed across all partner institutions
documents: Online application for the PhD linked to the chosen project
Personal statement on the Bristol GW4+ template
Supporting documents listed in the 2027 How to Apply guide (transcripts, references, English evidence)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed by the partner schools hosting each project; shortlisted candidates are interviewed. Full criteria are in the How to Apply guide.
opportunities.about_provider: GW4 is an alliance of four research-intensive universities in the west of England and Wales. The GW4+ partnership is funded by the Natural Environment Research Council and includes national research centres.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a project on the GW4+ site, then apply for the related PhD through the University of Bristol online application (or the host partner's system) by 7 January 2027, attaching the GW4+ personal statement template. Contact uob-pgradmissions@bristol.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: You can only apply for one project across the whole partnership, so choose carefully.

opportunities.title: Tampere University Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students in English-taught degrees. Source lists 7 Jan and 21 Jan 2027; earlier date used to be safe.

opportunities.title: Yonsei Samsung Global Hope Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full scholarship for undergraduates from developing countries.

opportunities.title: AfDB Japan Africa Dream Scholarship at APU (September 2027 Master's)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants from AfDB member countries applying from overseas to an APU graduate programme starting September 2027 can be considered for the AfDB-funded scholarship (AfDB Scholarship 2 round).

opportunities.title: CDC Steven M. Teutsch Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship, Class of 2027
opportunities.provider: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders in economics, public health, modelling or related quantitative fields who are allowed to work in the US can apply by 8 January 2027 for CDC's two-year Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship starting August 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Steven M. Teutsch Prevention Effectiveness (PE) Fellowship is a two-year, full-time postdoctoral programme at the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Fellows assess how effective and how cost-efficient public health interventions are, working on real CDC programmes, mostly at CDC headquarters in Atlanta, Georgia.

There are two tracks: a Traditional track for economics, health services research, public health and related quantitative fields, and an Analytics and Modeling track for epidemiology, infectious disease modelling, applied mathematics, operations research, data science and related fields. About ten fellows are chosen for each track every year, and the Class of 2027 starts in August 2027.

Non-US citizens can apply only if they hold a visa or work authorisation that allows them to work in the US for the fellowship, which matters for African PhD holders already in the US (for example on OPT STEM, J-1 or H-1B status).
opportunities.benefits: A two-year, full-time postdoctoral fellowship in applied public health economics and modelling at CDC. The pages read do not state the stipend; relocation to the duty city is at the fellow's own cost.
requirements: PhD or equivalent, with all degree requirements complete before the start (by July 2027)
Traditional track: economics, agricultural economics, health services research, public health or a related quantitative field
Analytics and Modeling track: epidemiology, disease modelling, disease ecology, applied mathematics, operations research/industrial engineering, biology, data science or related field
US citizen, permanent resident, or non-citizen with valid US work authorisation for the fellowship (e.g. OPT STEM covering two years, J-1, H-1B, TN)
Not a citizen of a country designated a state sponsor of terrorism
Foreign degrees translated into English; a credential evaluation may be requested
documents: Online application through the CDC portal
opportunities.selection_process: Competitive selection of about 10 fellows per track, based on academic preparation, recommendation letters, research and work experience, publications or publication potential, methods and data skills, and the personal statement. Shortlisted candidates have virtual interviews in February-March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The CDC is the national public health agency of the United States. The PE Fellowship is run by its Division of Scientific Education and Professional Development.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the CDC application portal linked from the PE Fellowship 'Apply' page before 11:59 pm ET on 8 January 2027. Non-citizen finalists are contacted about their visa situation. Questions: PEF@cdc.gov.
opportunities.notes: CDC describes the dates as tentative, and acceptance of non-citizens is subject to federal rules. Most placements are in Atlanta, with some in other states or agencies.

opportunities.title: DHET Japan Scholarship Programme at Tokyo Metropolitan University 2027
opportunities.provider: South Africa DHET / Tokyo Metropolitan University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: South African citizens with a strong bachelor's (master's track) or master's (PhD track) can apply to DHET by 8 January 2027 for fully funded study at Tokyo Metropolitan University from October 2027.
opportunities.description:
South Africa's Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) runs this scholarship with Tokyo Metropolitan University (TMU) so that South African graduates can complete a master's or doctoral degree in Japan. Study starts in October 2027; master's degrees last two years and PhDs three years.

The call covers a set list of fields at TMU: Biological Sciences (PhD only), Geography, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Applied Chemistry for the Environment and Tourism Science (master's and PhD).

The award is fully funded and is reserved for South African citizens. Preference goes to applicants from previously disadvantaged backgrounds, and candidates are expected to show interest in Japan and a commitment to contributing to South Africa after their studies.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition; one return economy airfare plus one mid-term airfare; a monthly stipend for living costs, accommodation and local transport; a once-off settlement allowance; health and medical insurance; visa costs; pre-departure orientation and psychosocial support.
requirements: South African citizen in good health (medical examination required)
Master's track: bachelor's or NQF 7 with GPA of at least 2.30 out of 3.00 (about 78%)
PhD track: master's degree with the same GPA
GPA confirmed with the official DHET GPA calculator
Proficient in English and meets TMU programme requirements
Available to start in October 2027
Foreign qualifications evaluated by SAQA or Umalusi
documents: Degree certificate or proof of completion
Publication abstracts and nomination letter, if any
opportunities.selection_process: Five stages: an eligibility check, ranking by academics, an online or in-person interview and questionnaire for shortlisted applicants, nomination by DHET, and a final admission decision by TMU.
opportunities.about_provider: The Department of Higher Education and Training is the South African government department responsible for universities and colleges. Its international scholarships office manages government-to-government and partner-university scholarships for South Africans.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare all documents as clearly named PDFs and send the complete package to DHET by email using the contact on the official page before 8 January 2027. Late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Use the official GPA calculator; applications without it may be rejected. Make sure your passport is ready by April 2027.

opportunities.title: ESERA Early Career Researcher Travel Grants 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and researchers within 3 years of their PhD in science education, including those based in Africa visiting Europe, can apply by 8 January 2027 for up to EUR 1,000 for a research visit.
opportunities.description:
ESERA's Early Career Researcher Travel Grants pay for short research visits abroad by doctoral students and recent PhDs in science education research. A grant of up to EUR 1,000 covers travel, accommodation and/or subsistence for a visit to meet researchers who are relevant to the grantee's work, at any time between 1 February 2027 and 31 January 2028.

Researchers based in Europe may visit an institution anywhere in the world, and researchers based outside Europe, including in Africa, may visit an institution in Europe. Ten grants are available in 2027. The visits must be new contacts: conference or summer school attendance and visits within an existing collaboration are excluded.

For African science education researchers this is a straightforward way to fund a working visit to a European group, with priority for those who have little support from their home institution.
opportunities.benefits: Up to EUR 1,000 per grantee towards travel, accommodation and/or subsistence for a research visit; ten grants in 2027.
requirements: Enrolled in doctoral studies, or PhD awarded no more than 3 years before the deadline (career breaks are taken into account)
ESERA membership (may be bought after selection, before payment)
Based in Europe visiting anywhere, or based outside Europe visiting an institution in Europe
Visit must not be a conference, summer school or part of an existing collaboration
Grantees must be insured
documents: Online application form: research description (max 500 characters), home funding, host details, visit agenda and expected outcomes, budget, previous grants, and confirmation of discussion with host and supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: A panel of three, including at least one ESERA Executive Board member, rates the professional benefit of the visit, the need for financial support and how feasible the planned outcomes are. Geographic spread is considered, and priority goes to applicants with limited home-institution support and no earlier ESERA grant.
important_dates: Grantees notified: by end of January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The European Science Education Research Association (ESERA) is the main European society for research in science education. The 2027 call is published on a page hosted by the biology education institute of Justus Liebig University Giessen.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online form on the ESERA travel grant page before 22:00 CET on 8 January 2027, after agreeing the visit with your host and supervisor. Grantees write a 1-3 page report after the visit for the ESERA website.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to ecr@esera.org.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Public Health (Europubhealth+) 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any country with a 180-ECTS bachelor's and the language level for their chosen pathway can apply by 8 January 2027 for this two-year European public health master with Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Europubhealth+ is a two-year, full-time European Master in Public Health run by an EU-funded consortium and open to graduates from any country. Students spend the first year at one of four universities (Granada, University College Dublin, Liege or Sheffield) and specialise in the second year at partners such as Rennes, Maastricht, Krakow, Bordeaux or Granada.

The programme is multidisciplinary and requires a bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS. Each pathway has its own language rules, including English, French or Spanish requirements depending on the cities chosen.

For African graduates the programme is especially accessible: citizens of French-speaking African countries are exempt from the French test, and applications for Erasmus Mundus scholarships close on 8 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available to the best candidates (amounts on the programme's funding pages). Self-funded students may apply until March 2027.
requirements: Bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) or equivalent
Language requirement for your pathway, e.g. IELTS 6.5 (6.0 per band) for Dublin or Sheffield, IELTS 6.0 for Liege or Granada with most second-year sites
French B2 for Liege or Rennes health promotion (exempt for citizens of French-speaking countries such as Benin, Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal, Mali, Togo, Gabon, DR Congo)
Spanish B2 for Granada first year or health services management
Language proof met at the time of application
documents: Certified degree copies with diploma supplement and English translation
Proof of current residence issued within 12 months
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by the consortium; results are released about nine weeks after the deadline, mid-March for scholarship applicants.
important_dates: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline: 8 January 2027, 13:00 CET
opportunities.about_provider: Europubhealth+ is run by a consortium of European universities and schools of public health and is co-funded by the European Union's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Europubhealth+ application platform (emundus) and submit your application with all documents before 13:00 CET on 8 January 2027 for scholarship consideration. Read the 'Instructions for 2027 applicants' on the platform first.
opportunities.notes: Citizens of Cameroon and Sudan (among others) are advised to choose partner universities other than those in the UK because of visa restrictions. Sheffield checks Nigerian and Ghanaian degrees against national accreditation lists. Liege requires non-EU students to show EUR 10,000 a year at enrolment.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Sustainable Transportation and Electric Power Systems (STEPS) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Engineering graduates of any nationality with a three-year bachelor's and IELTS 6.0 can apply by 8 January 2027 for this two-year Erasmus Mundus master in sustainable transport and power systems.
opportunities.description:
STEPS (Sustainable Transportation and Electric Power Systems) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by the University of Oviedo in Spain with Kiel University, Sapienza University of Rome and the Polytechnic of Coimbra. It runs for two years (120 ECTS), is taught in English and takes students through at least three countries.

Students follow either the Coimbra-Kiel-Oviedo or the Rome-Kiel-Oviedo track, with an internship option, and the programme is supported by 13 universities and 24 companies. Scholarships pay EUR 1,400 a month for up to 24 months, and a tuition waiver option also exists.

For African engineering graduates interested in electric mobility and power systems, STEPS offers a funded European master that starts in September 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship covering tuition and EUR 1,400 per month for the whole programme (up to 24 months), or a tuition waiver. The number of scholarships is set each year.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in engineering of at least three years (180 ECTS)
English for non-native speakers: IELTS Academic 6.0 (5.5 per band), TOEFL 79 (writing 17, reading 18, speaking 20) or PTE Academic 55 (51 per section), taken within two years
Full-time study; no other EU grant for the same course
No more than two scholarship holders of the same nationality
documents: Hard copies sent by post before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: After a formal check, candidates are scored on their CV (40%), professional and research experience (20%) and a personal interview (40%). The best-ranked 40 to 60 are interviewed, possibly by video, and a weak interview can exclude a candidate.
important_dates: Official decision: mid to late May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Oviedo coordinates the STEPS consortium, which also includes Kiel University, Sapienza University of Rome and the Polytechnic of Coimbra.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEPS portal, ticking the scholarship option and attaching your documents in English, then send hard copies by post, postmarked before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: The admission page gives the deadline as 15 January of the starting year, while the home page says 8 January 2027; aim for 8 January to be safe. Contact: info-emmcsteps.eu@uniovi.es.

opportunities.title: ISTA Funded PhD Programme 2027
opportunities.provider: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or master's graduates of any nationality in the sciences, mathematics or computer science can apply to the ISTA PhD programme by 8 January 2027 for a September 2027 start.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) runs an interdisciplinary graduate school near Vienna that admits PhD students in biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer science, neuroscience, earth sciences and related areas. The call for the 2027 intake is open, and the programme starts on 15 September 2027.

Students first join research groups through rotations and coursework before choosing a thesis group, so applicants apply to the programme rather than to a single supervisor. Applicants with a bachelor's degree may enter directly.

No nationality restriction appears on the official pages, which makes ISTA a strong option for African graduates who want a funded, research-intensive PhD in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Funded PhD position at ISTA; employment terms are explained by ISTA on admission.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant field (or about to complete one)
Strong undergraduate record
Documents in English
Available to start on 15 September 2027 (start date not negotiable)
documents: Transcripts and diplomas in English and in the original language
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on undergraduate performance, reference letters (academic referees preferred), the statement of purpose, field-specific and transferable skills, and diversity. A first review runs in February, followed by mostly remote interviews in late February and early March; decisions come by early March.
important_dates: Reference letters due: 12 January 2027, 11:59 PM CET
Interviews: late February to early March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ISTA is a research institute in Klosterneuburg, Austria, dedicated to basic research in the natural and formal sciences, with its own graduate school offering PhD degrees.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Apply@ISTA portal (apply.ista.ac.at) and complete the application on a desktop browser, uploading all documents there; emailed documents are not processed. Enter your referees early so they can submit letters by 12 January.
opportunities.notes: The portal does not work on mobile devices. You can still change referee details until the application deadline.

opportunities.title: Imperial College Global Health PhD Scholarship for Africa
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded global health PhD for African applicants.

opportunities.title: NIMS International Cooperative Graduate Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time graduate students enrolled at an NIMS partner university (none currently in Africa) can be nominated by 8 January 2027 for a 6-12 month research stay in Tsukuba, Japan.
opportunities.description:
The International Cooperative Graduate Program (ICGP) of Japan's National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS) brings graduate students from partner universities to Tsukuba for a research attachment in materials science. The 2027 call is open, with stays starting from July 2027 onward.

Stays last 6 to 12 months and can be split into several visits. Each student works under an NIMS co-supervisor while remaining registered at their home university, and English is the working language.

Partner universities are in North America, Europe and Asia; none is in Africa. African students can benefit only if they are enrolled full time at one of the listed partners.
opportunities.benefits: Living allowance of 120,000 JPY per month, accommodation at Ninomiya House in Tsukuba, and visa support; no training or facility fees. Utilities and insurance are paid by the student.
requirements: Full-time graduate student at an ICGP partner university
Registered as a student for the whole stay
Nominated by the partner university (maximum two per partner per year)
Working knowledge of English
Research insurance and Japanese National Health Insurance
opportunities.selection_process: The partner university selects and nominates candidates, NIMS finds a co-supervisor and may hold online interviews, and the NIMS president gives final approval. Results come in mid-March 2027.
important_dates: Application deadline (documents at NIMS via the home university): 8 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: NIMS is Japan's national research institute for materials science, based in Tsukuba. It runs graduate education programmes with Japanese and international partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Send the application form and transcripts electronically to the ICGP contact at your partner university, who forwards nominations to the NIMS Graduate Program Section by 8 January 2027. Questions go to nims-graduate@nims.go.jp.
opportunities.notes: Family visas are not supported. Check whether your university is on the official partner list before applying.

opportunities.title: Oxford-Pershing Square Graduate Scholarships 2027
opportunities.provider: University of Oxford / Pershing Square Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to an Oxford one-year master's followed by the MBA can be considered for up to five fully funded awards.

opportunities.title: RIKEN Center for Brain Science Summer Internship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students beyond high school worldwide with an institutional affiliation can apply by 8 January 2027 for RIKEN CBS's 2027 summer internship or lecture course near Tokyo, with travel and accommodation support.
opportunities.description:
The RIKEN Center for Brain Science (CBS) Summer Program brings students from around the world to RIKEN's Wako campus near Tokyo for hands-on neuroscience. It has two parts: Plan A, a two-month internship in a CBS laboratory (8 June to 5 August 2027), and Plan B, a five-day lecture course with poster sessions (5 to 9 July 2027). Participants may choose one plan or both, and all lectures are in English.

The programme is open to anyone beyond high school who holds an institutional affiliation (a university or a company) for the whole period, and no previous research experience is required. It is sponsored in part by IBRO.

For African students interested in brain science this is a rare chance to work inside one of Asia's leading neuroscience centres, with airfare and accommodation covered for approved applicants and an airfare cap of JPY 300,000 for travellers from Africa.
opportunities.benefits: For approved applicants: accommodation plus reimbursement of round-trip airfare (or Shinkansen fare), capped at JPY 300,000 for travellers from Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas (JPY 150,000 from India and Oceania, JPY 100,000 from Asia). No registration fee. Tickets are bought first and refunded later; daily living costs are not covered.
requirements: Studying beyond high school (high school students are not eligible)
Official affiliation with a school or company from application until the end of the programme (recent graduates without one are not eligible)
Able to attend the whole programme in person
Valid passport; non-Japanese participants arrange their own visa
Not receiving a salary or other financial support for the stay (to be eligible for support)
Plan A: accident insurance and a medical check within six months before departure
documents: One recommendation letter uploaded by the supervisor via the emailed link
Letter requesting financial support (if support is needed)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on the submitted materials only; results are usually sent by email around mid-February, and no individual feedback is given. Being accepted does not by itself guarantee participation.
important_dates: Deadline: 8 January 2027, 9:00 am JST (no late applications)
opportunities.about_provider: RIKEN is Japan's largest comprehensive research organisation. Its Center for Brain Science in Wako, Saitama, is one of the world's major neuroscience institutes and runs training programmes for junior scientists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the online form linked from the RIKEN CBS Summer Program page before 9:00 am JST on 8 January 2027. Drafts cannot be saved, but you may resubmit until the deadline and only the latest submission counts; your supervisor receives an automatic link to upload the recommendation.
opportunities.notes: Posters for Plan B are A0 portrait (876 x 1643 mm). Questions go through the Summer Program inquiry form. RIKEN CBS also runs a Brain Science Training Program and other programmes for junior scientists.

opportunities.title: RJI Professional Innovation Fellowships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anyone anywhere with an idea for a free, open-source tool or training for journalists can apply by 8 January 2027 for an eight-month RJI fellowship worth USD 75,000-100,000.
opportunities.description:
The RJI Professional Innovation Fellowships fund journalists and other innovators to build a free, open-source tool, platform or workshop that helps newsrooms and journalists. The fellowship lasts eight months, is mostly remote with a couple of visits to the Reynolds Journalism Institute in Columbia, Missouri, and starts with an in-person kickoff on 28 June 2027.

There are three types: Individual, Institutional and Emerging Technology. Fellows receive a large stipend in three instalments tied to their deliverables, and RJI pays for the trips.

RJI places no restrictions on who can apply: applicants can live anywhere, work in journalism or not, and be of any age or experience. The result must be immediately usable by any journalist in the US, but global ideas are welcome, so African media innovators can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Individual fellowship: USD 75,000 stipend; Institutional fellowship: USD 75,000 (to the organisation or fellow); Emerging Technology fellowship: USD 100,000. Stipends are paid in three instalments based on deliverables, and travel for the RJI visits is covered.
requirements: Open to anyone, anywhere, of any age or experience, in or outside journalism
A project idea for a free, accessible, open-source resource for journalists
The resource must be immediately available to any journalist in the US (single-city or single-state tools are unlikely to be funded)
Commitment to monthly articles and meetings during the fellowship
opportunities.selection_process: Selection runs in three stages: a first-round application, an in-depth second round in February for shortlisted applicants, and finalist interviews from 5 to 23 April 2027. RJI looks first for strong ideas and passionate, driven people.
opportunities.about_provider: The Donald W. Reynolds Journalism Institute (RJI) is part of the Missouri School of Journalism at the University of Missouri and funds research and innovation for the news industry.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the first-round application on RJI's Submittable page by 8 January 2027. Shortlisted applicants get two to three weeks in February to complete a second-round application, followed by interviews.
opportunities.notes: Deliverables must be free, open-source and launched within the fellowship. Contact: rji@rjionline.org or Kat Duncan (duncank@rjionline.org). RJI also runs Student Innovation Fellowships.

opportunities.title: Surrey Vice-Chancellor's Future Leaders Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded overseas students domiciled in Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Kenya, Mauritius, Morocco, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda or Zimbabwe with a Surrey offer can apply for a £7,500 first-year fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The Vice-Chancellor's Future Leaders Award is a University of Surrey fee waiver for self-funded international students from a list of priority countries. It is available for full-time undergraduate degrees starting in September 2027 and for postgraduate taught degrees starting in February or September 2027.

Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis and must be secured before the university issues your CAS for the visa, so early application matters. Applications are reviewed monthly.

Eligibility depends on where you live (domicile), not on nationality. Ten African countries are on the list, making this a useful discount for students from those countries applying to Surrey in Guildford, UK.
opportunities.benefits: £7,500 reduction in tuition fees for the first year of study only. It cannot be deferred or combined with other Surrey scholarships, alumni discounts or early-payment discounts.
requirements: Self-funded student paying overseas fees
Domiciled in an eligible country (for Africa: Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Kenya, Mauritius, Morocco, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe)
Offer for a full-time degree at Surrey
Undergraduates: first-year entry with Surrey as firm UCAS choice; Clearing applicants need ABB or equivalent
Apply before your CAS is issued
Not for the International Study Centre, part-time, distance learning, the MBA or some named MSc programmes
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed monthly on prior academic performance, predicted grades where relevant, and the personal statement, until awards run out.
important_dates: Postgraduate February 2027 intake: applications close 8 January 2027
Postgraduate September 2027 intake: applications close 20 August 2027
Undergraduate September 2027 intake: applications close 24 August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Surrey is a public research university in Guildford, England, known for engineering, health, business and hospitality programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your Surrey degree first, then use the 'Apply now' form on the award page for your intake, quoting your offer and student ID. Contact international@surrey.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Applications without both an offer and a student ID are not assessed. Students from non-listed countries can look at Surrey's International Excellence Award (£5,000).

opportunities.title: UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award (UELA) Studentships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants can hold up to 30% of about 50 fully funded engineering and physical sciences PhD studentships at UCL, with the overseas fee difference covered.

opportunities.title: KSJ Fellowship for Advancing Science Journalism in Africa and the Middle East 2027
opportunities.provider: Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists based in Africa or the Middle East with at least three years covering science, health or the environment can apply by 9 January 2027 for a paid autumn-semester fellowship at MIT.
opportunities.description:
The Fellowship for Advancing Science Journalism in Africa and the Middle East is a one-semester fellowship at MIT for a journalist based in Africa or the Middle East. The fellow spends the autumn semester (August to December) in Cambridge, Massachusetts, joining the other Knight Science Journalism fellows in seminars, workshops and field trips.

The fellowship was created with Springer Nature as founding sponsor and is inspired by the Egyptian science journalist Mohammed Yahia. It is meant to strengthen science reporting in the region by giving one journalist time to learn, build networks and develop their work.

It is one of very few international science journalism fellowships reserved for journalists in Africa and the Middle East, with a stipend, travel money and health insurance.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 40,000 paid in instalments over 4.5 months; a USD 5,000 travel and housing payment near the start; health insurance for the fellow and family; a childcare subsidy of USD 500-750 per month for those who qualify; and local transit access. Housing is paid by the fellow.
requirements: Journalist based in Africa or the Middle East
At least three years' experience reporting on science, health or environmental issues in the region
Reporter, writer, editor, producer, illustrator, filmmaker or photojournalist
Proficient in spoken and written English
Able to obtain a US visa (usually J-1)
documents: Three work samples (with translations if needed)
At least one professional reference letter
opportunities.selection_process: A panel of judges reviews the applications between January and March and interviews finalists; the fellow is announced in April.
opportunities.about_provider: The Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT has trained science journalists since 1983 and publishes the magazine Undark. This fellowship was set up with Springer Nature as founding sponsor.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through KSJ's Submittable form for this fellowship (linked from the fellowship page) by 11:59 pm Eastern Time on 9 January 2027. Applications written with AI are disqualified; AI may only be used for minor editing, with disclosure.
opportunities.notes: You may also apply to the KSJ Academic-Year Fellowship in the same cycle, but both applications must be complete. Applicants from countries under US visa suspension should check the visa guidance first. Contact: knight-info@mit.edu.

opportunities.title: Knight Science Journalism Academic-Year Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time science, health, tech or environment journalists with at least three years' experience, from any country and able to get a US visa, can apply by 9 January 2027 for a nine-month paid fellowship at MIT.
opportunities.description:
The Knight Science Journalism (KSJ) Academic-Year Fellowship gives ten experienced science journalists from around the world nine months at MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Fellows work on a journalism research project of their own, audit courses at MIT, Harvard and nearby universities, and join seminars, workshops and field trips designed for them.

Fellows must live in the Boston-Cambridge area for the MIT academic year (mid-August to May). The programme pays a generous stipend plus health insurance and other support, and international applicants are actively encouraged.

For African science, health, technology and environment journalists it is one of the most prestigious mid-career fellowships available. Applications for 2027-28 open on 15 November 2026 and close on 9 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 87,500 paid over 9.5 months; a USD 5,000 travel and housing payment near the start; health insurance for the fellow and family; a childcare subsidy of USD 500-750 per month for those who qualify; and local transit access. Housing is paid by the fellow (about USD 2,000-5,000 per month locally).
requirements: Full-time journalist (staff or freelance); part-time journalists are not eligible
At least three consecutive years covering science, health, technology or the environment
Work as a reporter, writer, editor, producer, illustrator, filmmaker, photojournalist or book author
Able to obtain a US visa (usually J-1)
No residential fellowship of four months or longer in the past two years
English proficiency, checked through the interview and/or a test (IELTS or TOEFL not required to apply)
documents: Five work samples (with translations if not in English)
opportunities.selection_process: A panel of science journalists, including the KSJ director, associate director and the editor of Undark, reviews applications from January to March. Finalists have video interviews in early March and fellows are announced in April. The panel looks for a high level of professional achievement and a long-term commitment to journalism.
opportunities.about_provider: The Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT has trained science journalists since 1983. It is based at MIT and also publishes the science magazine Undark.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through KSJ's Submittable page (linked from the fellowship page) by 11:59 pm Eastern Time on 9 January 2027. Applications must be written by the applicant: AI may only be used for minor editing and must be disclosed.
opportunities.notes: Citizens of countries where the US has suspended visa issuance are advised to wait, unless they hold a second passport from an unaffected country. You can apply to this and the Africa and Middle East fellowship at the same time. Contact: knight-info@mit.edu, +1 617 452 3513.

opportunities.title: 15th Dr. Dahlia Greidinger International Symposium 2027: Call for Abstracts
