opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers, students and practitioners in agriculture and environmental science can submit abstracts by 10 January 2027 to the Technion's March 2027 symposium in Haifa, with free registration for presenters.
opportunities.description:
The 15th Dr. Dahlia Greidinger International Symposium takes place at the Technion - Israel Institute of Technology in Haifa from 1 to 3 March 2027, on the theme 'Agricultural Innovation Under Global Uncertainty'. The three-day meeting combines keynote and invited talks with contributed presentations and poster sessions.

The call for abstracts invites researchers, practitioners, industry and policy makers to submit work in nine areas, including forever chemicals in agriculture, crop nutrition, climate-resilient and precision agriculture, digital agriculture and AI, plant-soil-microbiome interactions, carbon cycling, life-cycle assessment and the valorisation of agricultural waste. Graduate students are especially encouraged to present posters.

Oral and poster presenters do not pay the registration fee, which makes this an affordable venue for African agricultural and environmental scientists to present their work, although the pages read do not mention travel grants.
opportunities.benefits: Oral and poster presenters are exempt from the registration fee (which otherwise ranges from 100 to 850 NIS, including lunch). No travel funding is mentioned.
requirements: Abstract on one of the nine symposium topics (for example forever chemicals, crop nutrition, climate-resilient, precision or digital agriculture, soil carbon, LCA, agricultural waste)
Open to researchers, practitioners, industry leaders and policy makers
Graduate students are especially encouraged to present posters
Presenters attend the symposium at the Technion, Haifa, 1-3 March 2027
documents: Abstract submitted through the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Submitted abstracts are reviewed by the organisers for oral or poster presentation; the pages read give no further detail.
opportunities.about_provider: The Technion - Israel Institute of Technology is Israel's oldest university and a leading science and engineering institution. The symposium is organised and supported by the Dahlia Greidinger Memorial Fund, with support from ICL.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the online form linked from the symposium's abstract submission page by 10 January 2027. Non-presenting participants register through the event's registration page.
opportunities.notes: Registration cancellations are charged 15% until 14 February 2027 and in full afterwards. The secretariat helps with Haifa accommodation; contact hanat@trdf.technion.ac.il.

opportunities.title: BIS 2027: 27th International Conference on Business Information Systems
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers in business information systems from any country can submit papers by 10 January 2027 to BIS 2027, an in-person conference in Poznan, Poland.
opportunities.description:
BIS 2027, the 27th International Conference on Business Information Systems, takes place in Poznan, Poland, from 23 to 25 June 2027. It is organised by Poznan University of Economics and Business and attendance is in person only.

The conference invites research papers on business information systems, of up to 12 pages including the abstract and references, using the Springer LNBIP template. Papers are not anonymised. Proposals for workshops are due earlier, on 15 December 2026.

This is a call for papers, not a funding scheme. It is a well-established European venue for African researchers in information systems, digital business and data-driven management.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are presented in Poznan and published by Springer (LNBIP series). No funding is offered.
requirements: Original paper of at most 12 pages including abstract and references
Springer LNBIP template (LaTeX or Word)
Papers are not blinded
Attendance in person (remote presentation is not supported)
opportunities.selection_process: Peer review by the programme committee; notification on 5 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Poznan University of Economics and Business is one of Poland's leading economics universities and has organised the BIS conference series for over two decades.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Format the paper with the Springer LNBIP template and submit it on the BIS 2027 EasyChair site by 10 January 2027. Contact: bis2027@bisconf.org.
opportunities.notes: The official site and the EasyChair page describe the indexing slightly differently (LNCS/Scopus/DBLP/Web of Science versus LNBIP); check the conference site before submitting.

opportunities.title: Bucknell University Financial Aid and Merit Scholarships for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants can request limited need-based aid through the ISAFA and are considered for a few partial merit scholarships; Regular Decision deadline 10 January, admission need-aware.

opportunities.title: EACL 2027 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Subsidies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers, students and others with financial barriers, especially from developing countries and marginalised groups, who will present at EACL 2027 can ask for registration, travel, care or connectivity support by 10 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The 2027 conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL) runs a subsidy scheme that helps people who would otherwise struggle to take part. Support can take the form of a registration waiver (including virtual registration for authors), help with travel and accommodation, caregiving and accessibility costs, or internet bandwidth and VPN costs for remote participants.

The scheme is aimed especially at researchers from developing countries and marginalised communities, students and anyone facing financial barriers. First-time attendees and members of under-represented groups who are presenting work in the main conference, in Findings or at an EACL workshop are given priority.

For African researchers in natural language processing this is one of the most practical ways to present at a leading European NLP venue. Neither the number of awards nor their size is fixed: both depend on how many people apply and how much funding is available.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on need: a waiver of the conference registration fee (virtual registration for authors included); reimbursement of travel and accommodation costs; support with caregiving and accessibility costs; and help with bandwidth or VPN costs for remote attendance. Amounts are not fixed and depend on demand and available funds.
requirements: Presenting work at EACL 2027 (main conference, Findings or an EACL workshop) gives priority
Open to any nationality; researchers from developing countries and marginalised communities are especially encouraged
Students and people facing financial hurdles are encouraged to apply
First-time *CL attendees and under-represented groups are prioritised
documents: Written justification of the support requested
Receipts for any expenses claimed (after the conference)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the submitted materials and the justification given. Priority goes to first-time attendees and under-represented groups who are presenting at the main conference, Findings or an EACL workshop.
important_dates: Application deadline: 10 January 2027, 23:59 Anywhere on Earth
opportunities.about_provider: EACL is the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics, the main international society for natural language processing research. Its yearly conference is one of the core *CL venues, alongside ACL, NAACL, AACL, EMNLP and COLING.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online form linked from the EACL 2027 subsidies page before 10 January 2027 (Anywhere on Earth time) and explain clearly why you need support. If you are asking for a registration waiver, do not register until you have the decision, unless the registration system offers a 'pending subsidy application' option.
opportunities.notes: Travel and accommodation are refunded only after the conference, against receipts, and refunds take 6 to 8 weeks, so book refundable tickets where possible. ACL does not book travel for grantees. If your visa is refused, the in-person grant lapses. Alcohol is not covered. Questions: eacl2027.deichairs@gmail.com.

opportunities.title: EASO Travel Grants for ECO2027
opportunities.provider: European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career obesity researchers who are EASO members, mainly working in Europe and unable to self-fund, can apply by 10 January 2027 for free ECO2027 registration plus EUR 500.
opportunities.description:
The European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO) offers a limited number of travel grants to help early-career obesity researchers who could not otherwise afford it to present at ECO2027, the European Congress on Obesity. Each grant gives free congress registration plus EUR 500 towards travel and accommodation.

The grants are for EASO members who are working towards, or recently completed, a PhD or MD and who have done most of their work in Europe. Applicants must submit an abstract to ECO2027, and the abstract is assessed as part of the decision.

African researchers based at European institutions who study obesity can use this grant to present at Europe's main obesity congress.
opportunities.benefits: Free registration for ECO2027 plus EUR 500 towards travel and accommodation.
requirements: EASO member, through an EASO-affiliated national obesity association
Unable to attend for financial reasons
Currently working towards a PhD/MD, or PhD within the last 5 years or MD within the last 8 years
Most of your work carried out in Europe
Abstract submitted to ECO2027
Applicants who had an EASO grant or EASO education course in the past 2 years may be unsuccessful
documents: Application on the Reviewr platform: justification of financial need and a short description of your work and contribution to obesity research
opportunities.selection_process: Applications and the submitted abstract are assessed; decisions are emailed in late February 2027.
important_dates: Deadline: 10 January 2027, 23:59 GMT (late applications not considered)
opportunities.about_provider: EASO is a federation of professional associations from 40 European countries working on obesity research, prevention and treatment, and it organises the yearly European Congress on Obesity.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your ECO2027 abstract and complete the travel grant application on the Reviewr platform, linked from EASO's travel grants page, by 23:59 GMT on 10 January 2027. The form can be saved and edited before submission.
opportunities.notes: EASO also runs New Investigator Awards; see the EASO website.

opportunities.title: EEMS 2027 Electromagnetic Engineering Conference Call for Papers
opportunities.provider: EEMS 2027 organising committee (BIT Yangtze Delta Academy)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers in electromagnetic and microwave engineering from any country can submit papers by 10 January 2027 to EEMS 2027 in Hangzhou, China.
opportunities.description:
EEMS 2027, the 2nd International Conference on Electromagnetic Engineering and Microwave Systems, takes place in Hangzhou, China, from 11 to 13 June 2027. It is co-sponsored by the Yangtze Delta Region Academy of Beijing Institute of Technology (Jiaxing), Zhejiang University, Hangzhou Dianzi University and Ningbo University.

The conference invites full papers (4 to 12 pages, double-column) and abstract-only submissions from presenters working on electromagnetic engineering, antennas, microwave and related systems. Review is double-blind and accepted papers are indexed in Ei Compendex and Scopus.

This is a call for papers, not a funding scheme. It is useful for African engineering researchers seeking an indexed international venue in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers are presented in Hangzhou and published in proceedings indexed in Ei Compendex and Scopus. No funding is offered; pages beyond 5 are charged extra.
requirements: Original paper in English, double-column, 4-12 pages (or an abstract-only submission for presenters)
Double-blind anonymised submission
At least one paid full registration per paper by the registration deadline
documents: Anonymised paper or abstract submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review; accepted papers without a paid registration by the deadline are dropped from the proceedings.
opportunities.about_provider: EEMS is an engineering conference co-sponsored by the BIT Yangtze Delta Region Academy in Jiaxing and three Zhejiang universities: Zhejiang University, Hangzhou Dianzi University and Ningbo University.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the paper in the conference template and submit it through the EEMS 2027 EasyChair page by 10 January 2027. Contact: eems_conf@163.com.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master's in Journalism, Media and Globalisation 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a relevant three-year bachelor's, at least three months of journalism work and C1 English can apply by 10 January 2027 for this two-year European master's, with full Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 10-15 students.
opportunities.description:
The Erasmus Mundus Master's in Journalism, Media and Globalisation is a two-year joint master's run by a consortium led by Aarhus University. Students spend the first year in Aarhus, Denmark, and the second year specialising at the University of Amsterdam, City St George's (London), LMU Munich or Charles University in Prague.

The programme is highly competitive, with about 700 applications a year for 80 to 90 places. Between 10 and 15 of the best candidates, of any nationality, receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships that cover tuition for both years plus EUR 1,400 a month.

For African journalists with a relevant bachelor's degree and some professional experience, it offers a fully funded route into a leading international journalism programme. Applications for the 2027-2029 intake are open from 1 November 2026 to 10 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (10-15 awards, all nationalities): full tuition for both years, EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months, and free health and liability insurance. Self-funded non-EU students pay EUR 9,000 in year one and EUR 12,000 in year two. A separate Erasmus+ stipend for year two may be awarded after the course starts.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least three years full-time in a relevant subject
Above-average grades
At least three months of documented full-time journalism work
English at CEFR C1: for most tracks IELTS Academic 7.0 (6.0 per band), TOEFL iBT 100 (20 per section) or C1 Advanced 190; the Amsterdam track needs 6.5 per IELTS band and higher TOEFL section scores
Not eligible for the scholarship if you already hold a two-year master's after a three-year bachelor's or had an Erasmus Mundus scholarship before
documents: One PDF application package in the required order: signed application form with Application Reflections
Transcripts and degree certificates with certified English translations
English test report or proof of exemption
Two signed reference letters on letterhead (one academic, one professional)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic merit, journalistic or media experience and the quality of their Application Reflections. The scholarship shortlist is reviewed by the programme's Advisory Board.
opportunities.about_provider: The Mundus Journalism consortium is coordinated by Aarhus University in Denmark together with four European partner universities, and is funded by the EU's Erasmus+ programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an Aarhus University account through the Mundus Journalism admissions page, then wait for the emailed link to the online registration form, where you upload your complete application package. Allow time, as account activation takes several steps, and submit at least 24 hours before the 13:00 CET deadline on 10 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Only complete packages in the right order are considered, and your choice of second-year track is binding. No African country is on the English-test exemption lists, so plan to take a test in time. Contact for confidential references: band@au.dk.

opportunities.title: Heinz Heinen Fellowships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates near completion, postdocs, professors and non-academic knowledge producers working on slavery and strong dependency can apply by 10 January 2027 for a 2027/2028 fellowship in Bonn.
opportunities.description:
The Heinz Heinen Fellowships are offered by the Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS), a Cluster of Excellence at the University of Bonn. They bring international researchers to Bonn to work on strong asymmetrical dependencies, including slavery, with proposals expected to address periods before 1900 and to take a comparative view.

The 2027/2028 call offers fellowships starting no earlier than 1 October 2027 in several categories: doctoral (up to 6 months), junior postdoctoral and postdoctoral (up to 12 months), senior for full professors (up to 6 months in the call), and alternative knowledge producers such as journalists, artists and curators (up to 6 months).

No nationality limits are stated, and the programme's focus on slavery and dependency makes it highly relevant to African historians and scholars of the African past and its diasporas.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipend of €1,700 (doctoral), €2,600 (junior postdoc), €3,100 (postdoc) or €3,600 (senior); outward and return travel allowance; accommodation lump sum of up to €1,000 per month (€1,250 with children) for fellows from outside Bonn; desk and computer, workshop funding and childcare support.
requirements: Doctoral: close to finishing the PhD and enrolled
Junior postdoc: PhD awarded at most 4 years ago
Postdoc: PhD awarded more than 4 years ago
Senior: full professor
Alternative knowledge producers: journalists, artists, curators and similar
Project on strong dependency or slavery, ideally pre-1900 and comparative
Application in English
documents: Research statement (max 9,000 characters for doctoral, 6,000 for postdoc, excluding spaces)
List of principal publications (postdoc and senior)
Two reference letters (doctoral: one from the supervisor; postdoc: two)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on how well the project fits the BCDSS research areas and on its relevance. Applicants are notified by April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: BCDSS is a Cluster of Excellence funded under Germany's Excellence Strategy at the University of Bonn. It studies slavery and other forms of strong asymmetrical dependency across history and regions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into a single English PDF and email it to application@dependency.uni-bonn.de by 10 January 2027. There is no online portal; questions go to researchandstudy@dependency.uni-bonn.de.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. Check the five BCDSS research areas and make the fit explicit in your statement.

opportunities.title: IIASA Young Scientists Summer Program (YSSP) 2027
opportunities.provider: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students worldwide, ideally 1-2 years from finishing, whose research fits IIASA's systems-analysis themes can apply by 10 January 2027 for the 2027 summer research programme in Austria.
opportunities.description:
The Young Scientists Summer Program (YSSP) at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA) is a full-time, in-person research placement for PhD students from around the world. Each participant works on a research project connected to IIASA's research areas, supervised by two IIASA scientists, at the institute near Vienna, Austria.

The programme suits doctoral students who are ideally one to two years from finishing their PhD and who can work independently with a mentor. The research proposal is the heart of the application.

IIASA has strong links with researchers in Africa, and the YSSP is a respected way for African PhD students in climate, energy, food, water, population and systems research to build international collaborations. Details of funding and dates are on a separate IIASA funding page that was not read.
opportunities.benefits: A supervised summer research placement at IIASA with two supervisors. Funding details are given on IIASA's separate funding page.
requirements: Enrolled in a PhD programme, ideally within 1-2 years of completion
Research connected to an IIASA research area
Able to work independently with a mentor
Sufficient English
Available full-time and in person for the whole programme
Open to PhD students worldwide
documents: Personal data form (citizenship, PhD details, English level, master's thesis description up to 2,500 characters)
First and optional second research group choice with reasons
Research proposal in the set sections (each up to 2,500 characters)
One PDF with CV, motivation letter and publication list
opportunities.selection_process: The research proposal is described as the most important part of the application; applicants are encouraged to contact the relevant IIASA research group before applying.
opportunities.about_provider: IIASA is an independent international research institute in Laxenburg, Austria, that studies global problems such as climate change, energy, food and water using systems analysis.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Before applying, send a half-page outline and your CV to the contact of the research group you want to join. Then submit everything on IIASA's online application platform (Onlyfy) in one session, as progress cannot be saved, before 23:00 CET on 10 January 2027.

opportunities.title: President's International Distinction Scholarship (2027 entrance)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students entering first-year undergraduate study at the University of Alberta with top grades and leadership can apply by 10 January 2027 for up to CAD 120,000 over four years.
opportunities.description:
The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's top entrance award for international undergraduates. It is worth up to CAD 120,000, paid over four years, and 25 awards are made each year to students entering first year on a study permit.

The award is application-based: students first apply for an undergraduate programme and then complete the university's single scholarship application, which considers their background, experiences, academics and interests. Recipients are expected to show a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership.

The University of Alberta, in Edmonton, also gives admission-based awards automatically, so African applicants who apply early can be considered for several awards at once.
opportunities.benefits: Up to CAD 120,000 paid over four years; 25 awards each year. Admitted international students may also automatically receive the International Admission Scholarship (up to CAD 10,000) or the Regional Excellence Scholarship (up to CAD 5,000), based on admission average.
requirements: Entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at the University of Alberta on a study permit
Superior admission average
Demonstrated leadership
Must apply for an undergraduate programme first
documents: Scholarship application on the university's scholarship portal (alberta.academicworks.ca)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on the applicant's background, experiences, academic record and interests, with a focus on superior grades and leadership.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Alberta in Edmonton is one of Canada's leading research universities and awards about CAD 53 million in undergraduate scholarships each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an undergraduate programme, then complete the scholarship application on the University of Alberta scholarship portal by 10 January 2027. One application covers all application-based entrance awards.
opportunities.notes: Other University of Alberta awards include the International Leader Scholarship (up to CAD 15,000), the Cora Martinson International Scholarship at Augustana (up to CAD 56,000 over four years) and the Aga Khan Academies IB Global Citizen Scholarship. Contact for students outside Canada: welcome@ualberta.ca.

opportunities.title: Atlantic Fellows for Social and Economic Equity (AFSEE) 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Activists, policymakers, researchers and practitioners with at least 7 years of experience fighting inequality, from any country, can apply by 11 January 2027 for a funded year at LSE and a Senior Fellowship.
opportunities.description:
The Atlantic Fellows for Social and Economic Equity (AFSEE) programme is a funded fellowship hosted by the International Inequalities Institute at the London School of Economics. It brings together activists, policymakers, researchers, artists and other practitioners who are working to challenge inequality, and most of its fellows come from the Global South.

The fellowship starts with an immersive active year at LSE in London built around learning modules, followed by a Senior Fellowship that offers continued funding and collaborative projects. There are two tracks: a Residential track, whose fellows must also qualify for admission to LSE's MSc in Inequalities and Social Science, and a Non-residential track.

For experienced African change-makers, AFSEE offers time, training and a global network to deepen their work on inequality. The 2027-28 application round opened on 7 October 2026 and closes on 11 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A funded fellowship: an active year of learning at LSE (Residential or Non-residential track) followed by a Senior Fellowship with funding and support for collaborative projects. The pages read do not give amounts.
requirements: At least 7 years of relevant experience
Meet LSE's English language requirements (no test needed before applying)
Residential track: must also qualify for admission to the LSE MSc in Inequalities and Social Science
A university degree is not required (applicants without one submit a statement saying so)
Open to all nationalities
documents: Online application in LSE's Graduate Application System
Transcripts, or a statement that you do not hold an undergraduate degree
Two references, submitted by the reference deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are read for a clear picture of who the applicant is, their values and their work, especially in challenging inequality; the clarity of their vision and its future impact; and their readiness to learn from and contribute to the AFSEE community. Shortlisted applicants are invited to interview.
opportunities.about_provider: The International Inequalities Institute at LSE studies the causes and consequences of inequality worldwide. AFSEE is one of the Atlantic Fellows programmes and is run by the institute.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Start your application through the link on the AFSEE 'How to Apply' page, which opens LSE's admissions system, choose the Residential or Non-residential track and upload all documents before 11 January 2027 at 5 pm UK time. Ask your two referees early, as incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Start early: documents such as transcripts can be slow to obtain over the winter break. Weekly Zoom drop-in sessions run in November and December 2026. Contact: afsee@lse.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: DIS 2027: ACM Designing Interactive Systems Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and practitioners anywhere can submit anonymised papers or pictorials on interactive systems design; the abstract is due 11 January 2027 and the full paper 18 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
DIS 2027 is the ACM conference on Designing Interactive Systems, the main meeting for research on the design of interactive technology, from user experience and design methods to critical and speculative design. The conference takes place from 28 June to 2 July 2027 in a hybrid format, with online presentations held the week before (21 to 25 June 2027).

The call for papers and pictorials invites full research contributions across five contribution areas. Papers are written in the single-column ACM template; there is no strict page limit, but typical papers run to 7,000 to 8,000 words without references, and submissions above 12,000 or under 4,000 words risk being rejected without review. Review is double-blind.

For African researchers in human-computer interaction and design, DIS is a high-profile venue, and the hybrid format with online presentation slots makes participation possible even when travel is difficult. This is a call for papers, not a funding scheme: the page does not mention travel support.
opportunities.benefits: Accepted papers and pictorials are presented at DIS 2027 and published in the ACM proceedings. No travel or registration funding is offered on the call page.
requirements: Original, unpublished work in English
Single-column ACM template; typically 7,000-8,000 words excluding references (under 4,000 or over 12,000 words may be desk-rejected)
Fully anonymised for double-blind review
Related concurrent submissions must be declared
All citations must be real (papers with non-existent references are desk-rejected)
documents: Anonymised full paper or pictorial as PDF
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review by the programme committee. Incomplete or non-anonymised papers, undeclared concurrent submissions, non-English papers, wrong templates and papers with fabricated citations are rejected without review; an 'Assisted Desk Reject' step is new for 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: DIS is organised under ACM SIGCHI, the Special Interest Group on Computer-Human Interaction of the Association for Computing Machinery, the world's largest computing society.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register the title and abstract by 11 January 2027 and upload the full PDF by 18 January 2027 through the Precision Conference system (new.precisionconference.com). Use the single-column ACM template and remove all author details. Adding an ORCID is encouraged.
opportunities.notes: All deadlines are Anywhere on Earth. Questions go to tpc@dis2027.acm.org. The DIS site also runs a Doctoral Consortium, workshops and a call for zines.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence (DEAI) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any country with a 180-ECTS bachelor's (ideally in computer science) and B2 English can apply by 11 January 2027 for Erasmus Mundus grants on this two-year European master in data engineering and AI.
opportunities.description:
DEAI is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, coordinated through the Universite libre de Bruxelles (ULB) in Belgium, with EU funding through Erasmus+. The current call covers the 2027-2029 cohort.

There are two application windows. The first, for applicants seeking an Erasmus Mundus grant, is open from 20 October 2026 to 11 January 2027. The second, for self-funded or partially funded students, opens on 1 March 2027 and closes in May.

African graduates with a strong computer science background are well placed to apply; the programme also has an 'African Ambassadors' page for applicants from the continent. The English requirement (CEFR B2, for example IELTS 5.5) is lower than at many other European master's programmes.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus grants for the best-ranked applicants in the grant window (amounts on the programme's tuition and scholarships page). Self-funded applicants need a financial guarantor for a Belgian student visa able to provide EUR 666 a month.
requirements: Bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS from a university listed in WHED or in the THE, ARWU or QS rankings
Final-year bachelor students may apply before graduating
English at CEFR B2: e.g. IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, TOEFL paper 570 or Cambridge FCE
No more than 10% of selected students from one nationality
documents: Online application (see the programme's application manual)
Reference letters (due 18 January 2027 for the grant window)
opportunities.selection_process: A joint committee ranks applicants on the field of their bachelor's (share of computer science credits), weighted average grade, other studies, professional IT/BI experience, cover letter and reference letters.
opportunities.about_provider: DEAI is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master funded by the EU (EACEA/Erasmus+), with admissions run from the Universite libre de Bruxelles.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the DEAI online application form linked from the admission page before 12:00 GMT on 11 January 2027 if you want an Erasmus Mundus grant, and make sure your referees send their letters by 18 January. Self-funded applicants use the later window.
opportunities.notes: Contact: bdma_admissions@cs.ulb.ac.be.

opportunities.title: FEBS Congress 2027 Mathias Sprinzl Scheme (Riga)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD-holding members of FEBS societies in Hinari countries of the FEBS area, such as Morocco and Tunisia, who present a first-author abstract can get half-price early registration (and possibly a travel grant) for FEBS 2027 in Riga.
opportunities.description:
The Mathias Sprinzl Scheme is a FEBS programme that makes it easier for scientists from lower-income countries in the FEBS area to take an active part in the FEBS Congress. In 2027 the congress takes place in Riga, Latvia, and registration and abstract submission are already open.

The scheme targets scientists from FEBS Constituent Societies in countries covered by Hinari (Research4Life). Within the FEBS area these include Morocco and Tunisia, which makes this one of the few European biochemistry congress schemes open to North African researchers. Selected applicants pay half of the early registration fee, and a small number also receive Sprinzl travel grants.

Applicants must hold a PhD and present an abstract as first author. FEBS also offers other congress support (bursaries for young scientists, the FEBS Neighbours scheme and Young Scientists' Forum grants), described on the same news page.
opportunities.benefits: A 50% reduction of the early registration fee for the FEBS Congress 2027 in Riga; a small number of Sprinzl travel grants are also available.
requirements: Member of a FEBS Constituent Society in a Hinari (Research4Life) country in the FEBS area (including Morocco and Tunisia)
Holder of a PhD
Submitting an abstract to the FEBS Congress 2027 as first author
documents: First-author abstract submitted to the congress
Scheme application (see the scheme page linked from the FEBS news item)
opportunities.selection_process: FEBS selects applicants from eligible countries who submit a first-author abstract; details of the assessment are given on the congress scheme page.
opportunities.about_provider: The Federation of European Biochemical Societies (FEBS) brings together national biochemistry and molecular biology societies across Europe and neighbouring regions. It runs the yearly FEBS Congress, advanced courses, journals and many fellowships and grants.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract to the FEBS Congress 2027 as first author and apply to the Mathias Sprinzl Scheme through the link on the FEBS news page before 11 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Other FEBS support on the same page: FEBS bursaries for PhD students and postdocs within five years of their PhD (early young-scientist fee plus EUR 475 towards travel and accommodation, EUR 850 in total; deadline 1 March 2027; FEBS society membership needed), the trial FEBS Neighbours scheme (50% off registration, deadline 11 January 2027) and Young Scientists' Forum grants (deadline 9 December 2026). FEBS also runs PROBio-Africa Fellowships.

opportunities.title: IEEE ETHICS-2027: Symposium on Ethics in Engineering, Science and Technology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers, educators and practitioners worldwide can submit to IEEE ETHICS-2027 at Duke University by 11 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
IEEE ETHICS-2027 is the International Symposium on Ethics in Engineering, Science and Technology, sponsored by the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology and hosted by Duke University's Pratt School of Engineering in Durham, North Carolina, from 25 to 27 June 2027. The series began in 2014, and the 2027 theme is 'Cultivating Ethical Technology: Character, Leadership, and Education'.

The symposium accepts poster abstracts, short papers of 3-5 pages, regular papers of 6-10 pages, and workshop and panel proposals. All submissions are due on 11 January 2027, with decisions on 15 March 2027 and final camera-ready papers on 10 May 2027. Papers are published in IEEE Xplore.

The call is open to researchers, educators, industry, policy makers and civil society, so African scholars working on technology ethics, responsible AI and engineering education can take part. No funding for authors is mentioned.

Submission by 11 January 2027

opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your abstract, paper or proposal and submit it through the ETHICS-2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=ethics2027) by 11 January 2027. See attend.ieee.org/ethics-2027 for details.
opportunities.notes: The 10 May 2027 date is for final camera-ready papers, not first submissions.

'The maternal-fetal dialogue: from mechanisms to pregnancy outcomes' is a four-day EMBO | EMBL Symposium held from 13 to 16 April 2027 at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, with an option to attend virtually. It brings together researchers and clinicians from all disciplines and career stages working on pregnancy and the interaction between mother and fetus.

Participants can apply for financial help when they submit their abstract: travel grants of up to EUR 1,000 for those travelling from outside Europe, registration fee waivers and childcare grants, with priority for early-career researchers.

For African researchers in reproductive health, obstetrics and developmental biology, the travel grant makes it realistic to present at a leading European symposium.

Registration otherwise costs EUR 650 (PhD) to EUR 950 (industry) on site, or EUR 190-290 virtually.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EDISS Scholarship 2027 (Intake 7)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Computer science or software engineering graduates of any nationality with IELTS 6.5 can apply by 12 January 2027 for EDISS scholarships worth up to EUR 51,600 for a two-year European master's.
opportunities.description:
EDISS is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master on the Engineering of Data-intensive Intelligent Software Systems. The two-year programme is run by a consortium that includes Abo Akademi University (Turku, Finland), the University of the Balearic Islands, the University of L'Aquila and Malardalen University, and intake 7 starts in August 2027.

Applications run in three rounds: round 1 (Erasmus Mundus and EDISS scholarships) is open now and closes on 12 January 2027, round 2 is for tuition fee waivers, and round 3 is for self-funded students. All nationalities may apply.

The full Erasmus Mundus scholarship is worth EUR 51,600 over two years, which makes EDISS one of the best-funded software engineering master's options in Europe for African computer science graduates.

MSc European Forestry is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by the University of Eastern Finland with AgroParisTech, the University of Freiburg, the University of Lleida, BOKU Vienna, Transilvania University of Brașov and Wageningen University. IMLEX is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in Imaging and Light in Extended Reality, led by the University of Eastern Finland in Joensuu with partners including Toyohashi University of Technology (Japan), Universite Jean Monnet (France) and KU Leuven (Belgium). Studies for the 2027 intake start in early September 2027 in Joensuu.

The programme covers optics, imaging, graphics and extended reality. At most 25 students are selected, and the best receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships covering all participation costs, insurance and EUR 1,400 a month.

There is no application fee, and graduates of English-taught degrees in many African countries (including Cameroon, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe, and English-taught programmes in Ghana and Nigeria) can be exempt from the English test. opportunities.title: The Met Emily K. Rafferty Internship in Museum Administration 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduating seniors, current graduate students and recent graduates with US work authorisation can apply for a 12-month rotational internship in museum administration at The Met.
opportunities.description:
The Emily K. Rafferty Internship gives one early-career candidate a year-long, full-time introduction to how a major museum is run. From 4 June 2027 to 26 May 2028 the intern rotates through three administrative departments of The Metropolitan Museum of Art, working with a staff mentor and completing a project in each.

The internship is onsite in New York City and runs 35 hours a week. The start date is fixed and applicants must confirm on the form that they can begin on 4 June 2027.

It suits graduates with a background in arts administration, art history or a related field who want a management career in museums. International applicants are welcome provided they can obtain US work authorisation.
opportunities.benefits: A paid full-time position with access to the benefits offered to non-exempt full-time Met employees, USD 1,500 towards housing or travel to New York City, and a USD 3,000 stipend for research, conferences or other professional development linked to the internship.
requirements: Undergraduate senior graduating before the start date, current graduate student, or recent graduate within 12 months of the deadline (first-year students, sophomores and juniors are not eligible)
Background in arts administration, art history or a related field preferred
Valid US work authorisation by the start date (no visa sponsorship)
Able to start on 4 June 2027 and work full-time for 12 months
Former Met interns only if they have done no more than a one-semester internship
documents: Short essay responses, including the long-term internship essay
Two letters of recommendation (one from a professor or instructor)
opportunities.selection_process: A central review committee screens applications, supervisors then review shortlisted candidates, at least four finalists are interviewed online, and the Director's Office approves the final choice. Candidates are notified by the end of April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met) in New York is one of the world's largest art museums, with collections spanning 5,000 years of world culture. Its college and graduate internship programmes train future museum professionals across curatorial, education, conservation and administrative departments.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use The Met's online internship application and select the MuSe long-term internship track, then complete the essays and arrange your two recommendations before the deadline. Information sessions are listed on engage.metmuseum.org.
opportunities.notes: International students may apply, but every intern must hold valid US work authorisation and The Met does not sponsor visas. Visas take time and can cost more than USD 1,500, and an offer is withdrawn if work authorisation is not in place by the start date. The hourly rate printed on the page appears to contain an error, so confirm the pay with collegeprograms@metmuseum.org.

opportunities.title: ICML 2027 Call for Papers

The 2027 Energy and Climate Economics and Business Days is an academic conference organised by the Centre for Energy Business and Economics Research (CEnBER) and the University of Groningen Business School. It takes place on 23-24 March 2027 in the Duisenberg Building on the Zernike campus in Groningen, the Netherlands.

The organisers invite researchers to submit extended abstracts, full papers or panel proposals on the economics and business of energy and climate. It is a call for papers rather than a scholarship: there is no travel or accommodation support for external participants.

For African energy economists and PhD researchers it is a chance to present work to a specialised European audience and build links with a strong energy research group.
opportunities.benefits: Opportunity to present research at a specialised energy and climate economics conference. Registration costs EUR 125 (EUR 100 for UGBS alumni); five fee waivers are reserved for University of Groningen students. No travel or accommodation funding.
requirements: Extended abstract of at least 500 words, or a full paper, or a panel proposal
Topic in energy or climate economics and business
Presenters must register by 26 February 2027
documents: Extended abstract or full paper, or panel proposal, submitted through the web form
opportunities.selection_process: The organising committee reviews submissions and notifies authors by 25 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: CEnBER is a research centre at the University of Groningen Business School focusing on energy business and economics, in a region long linked to the Dutch gas and energy sector.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract, paper or panel proposal through the web form linked from the event page before 15 January 2027. Questions go to the organiser, Selma Bakker.
opportunities.notes: Plan your own funding for travel, accommodation and the registration fee.

opportunities.title: Aarhus University Danish State Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants who apply for an Aarhus University master's by 15 January 2027 (summer intake) are automatically considered for a Danish State tuition waiver, sometimes with a living grant.
opportunities.description:
Aarhus University awards Danish State Scholarships, funded by the Danish government, to a small number of highly qualified non-EU/EEA students admitted to its master's programmes. The university has no scholarship fund of its own, so these are the main awards available.

There is no separate application. Everyone who applies for a master's by the deadline is assessed automatically, and offers are sent with the admission letter. Typically only one or two awards are made per programme.

What the award covers varies by faculty: Arts and Business and Social Sciences combine a tuition waiver with a monthly grant, while Natural and Technical Sciences give 100% tuition waivers. For African applicants, applying early and presenting excellent grades is key.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver; in some faculties also a monthly living grant, usually for the whole programme.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicant who must pay tuition
Applied for an Aarhus master's by 15 January (summer intake) or 15 September (winter intake)
Excellent academic record
Sufficient funds for any costs not covered (for waiver-only offers)
documents: No extra documents: the regular master's application is used (do not upload scholarship documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculties rank applicants on academic excellence when assessing admission; some faculties focus on particular countries or programmes. Offers have a short acceptance window.
important_dates: Acceptance of tuition waiver: by 1 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Aarhus University is Denmark's second-largest university, founded in 1928, with faculties of arts, natural sciences, technical sciences, health and business and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your chosen Aarhus master's programme through the university's application portal by 15 January 2027. If offered a scholarship, accept it by the stated date or it lapses.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship is tied to one programme and cannot be transferred.

opportunities.title: American Antiquarian Society Short-Term Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates, postdocs and independent scholars of any nationality researching early American history and culture can apply by 15 January 2027 for one- or two-month AAS fellowships in Worcester, Massachusetts.
opportunities.description:
The American Antiquarian Society (AAS) offers 19 different one- to two-month residential fellowships through a single application, for scholars who need to work in its library in Worcester, Massachusetts. The library holds one of the largest collections of printed material from early America.

Fellowships can be taken at any time between 1 June and 31 May; a second month is rarely granted. Most awards are open to doctoral candidates working on dissertations, and several also accept postdocs, independent researchers and holders of terminal degrees such as MLS or MFA.

International scholars are explicitly welcome, so African researchers working on Atlantic history, slavery, print culture or the African diaspora in early America can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $2,400 per month. Rooms in the AAS scholars' housing (about $600 to $1,000 a month) can be deducted from the stipend.
requirements: Doctoral candidate, postdoc, independent scholar or terminal-degree holder (depending on the fellowship)
Project that needs the AAS collections
Preference for applicants without an AAS fellowship in the past three years
Arrange your own visa: AAS cannot sponsor J-1 visas
documents: Statement of previous support and current appointment
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on scholarly qualifications, the significance of the project and how well it fits the AAS collections.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1812, the American Antiquarian Society is a national research library and learned society focused on American history and culture up to 1876.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into one PDF and submit it through the AAS online fellowship form (Breezy portal) by 15 January 2027. One application covers all 19 short-term fellowships.
opportunities.notes: Some named fellowships have extra restrictions (for example one reserved for German citizens or residents).

opportunities.title: American University Emerging Global Leader Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students who need a US student visa and have not started university can apply by 15 January 2027 for American University's EGLS, with two full awards and partial awards up to US$40,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (EGLS) is American University's flagship award for international first-year students who will study in Washington DC on a student visa. It targets young people who have shown leadership, a commitment to social change in their communities and resilience in overcoming obstacles.

For Fall 2027 entry, two students receive a full award covering all billable university costs, and other strong applicants receive partial awards. Awards renew for up to four years with satisfactory progress.

African secondary-school students who are ambitious about public service, international affairs or community leadership are a natural fit for this scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: Full award (two students): full tuition, room and board for up to four years. Partial awards: up to US$40,000 a year, with no separate application. Not covered: health insurance, books, airfare, taxes and personal costs (about US$4,000 a year).
requirements: Not a US citizen or permanent resident, and will need an F-1 or J-1 visa
Has not enrolled in or started university study
Finished secondary school no earlier than 2024 (preference for students graduating by June 2027)
Proof of English proficiency
Evidence of leadership and community commitment
Able to show at least US$4,000 a year for uncovered costs
documents: Common Application with AU's international checklist documents
AU EGLS essays (submitted in the applicant portal)
Official English test score (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE, LanguageCERT or Cambridge) sent by the testing agency
Bank letter and signed AU Declaration of Finances showing at least US$4,000
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed for merit, leadership, commitment to social change and obstacles overcome. Semi-finalists and finalists may be asked for Zoom interviews or extra essays, and winners are told by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: American University is a private research university in Washington DC, known for international service, public affairs, law and communication.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to American University through the Common Application (Regular Decision recommended) before 15 January 2027, then complete the EGLS essays in the AU applicant portal by the same date. Late applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Only two full awards are given, so also present yourself well for the partial awards, which need no extra application.

opportunities.title: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (Amsterdam Law School LLM) 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants with top grades applying to one of four Amsterdam Law School LLM programmes can apply by 15 January 2027 for the single Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (amount to be announced).
opportunities.description:
The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) at the University of Amsterdam's Amsterdam Law School supports one excellent non-EU/EEA student each year in a full-time LLM (Master of Laws) programme. The 2027-2028 call applies to four LLM programmes: International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law and Finance, and International Criminal Law.

The scholarship is meant for applicants with outstanding grades who do not qualify for Dutch student finance. The amount for 2027-2028 has not yet been announced by the faculty, so applicants should treat it as a partial award and plan other funding.

African law graduates aiming at an international or European law career are eligible, provided they meet the grade threshold and can obtain a Dutch study visa.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship towards the LLM year; the amount for 2027-2028 is to be announced by the university. Only one scholarship is awarded each year.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA passport and not eligible for Dutch student finance (studiefinanciering)
Applying for a first master's at the UvA
Full-time enrolment in one of four LLM programmes (International and European Law; Transnational and European Private Law; Law and Finance; International Criminal Law)
Previous degree grades comparable to a 4.0 US GPA, UK first-class honours or 8.0 on the Dutch scale (for a non-law bachelor, only law courses count)
Able to meet Dutch visa requirements
documents: Motivation letter of up to 500 words
All documents required for the LLM application (incomplete files are not considered)
opportunities.selection_process: The award goes by lottery among applicants who meet all the requirements. Results are announced by the end of March.
important_dates: Deadline: 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET (with the LLM application)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Amsterdam is a large public research university in the Netherlands. Its Amsterdam Law School runs English-taught LLM programmes through the Amsterdam Graduate School of Law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for one of the eligible LLM programmes and, on the 'Scholarship' tab of the application, select the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship. Upload your motivation letter on the 'Additional documents' tab. Make sure the whole application is complete by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The same motivation letter can also be used for the Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund scholarship. Because selection is by lottery among eligible applicants, meeting the grade threshold is the key step.

opportunities.title: Bachelor of Applied Computer Science (Thomas More Geel) - VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarship 2027
opportunities.provider: VLIR-UOS and Thomas More University of Applied Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship for nationals of the 25 eligible countries (17 in Africa) who also live in one of them, aged 19 to 35 on 1 January 2027, with no earlier Belgian government study scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Thomas More University of Applied Sciences offers VLIR-UOS full scholarships for its Bachelor of Applied Computer Science at the Geel campus in the province of Antwerp, Belgium. The funded period runs from September 2027 to September 2029, and it is one of only two bachelor-level programmes in the 2027-28 ICP Connect call.

Teaching is hands-on and project-based: you work in teams with students from other specialisations and with real clients and companies, and project management runs through the whole programme. You graduate with a diploma in one of two specialisations: Application Development (leading to jobs such as software, web or full-stack developer and analyst) or Artificial Intelligence (data engineer, machine-learning engineer, data analyst). Thomas More reports that nearly all its graduates find a job within three months.

Citizens of 16 sub-Saharan African countries and Morocco who live in an eligible country and are 19 to 35 years old on 1 January 2027 can apply. Applications for 2027-28 opened at the start of November 2026 and the VLIR-UOS deadline is 15 January 2027, the earliest in this call.
opportunities.benefits: A full scholarship for the whole length of the programme (24 months) and no longer. It is paid mainly as a monthly allowance meant to cover living costs (board and lodging) and tuition; travel to and from Belgium and insurance are also covered. Depending on the institution, tuition, insurance or housing is either paid by you out of the allowance or paid by the university directly and taken off the allowance. There are no partial awards or extensions, and VLIR-UOS pays nothing extra for optional activities such as field trips to the Global South. ICP Connect programmes charge no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of one of the 25 VLIR-UOS ICP Connect countries (in Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe; also Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam)
Living in one of those 25 countries when you apply (it does not have to be your own country)
Aged at least 19 and not older than 35 on 1 January 2027
Never awarded a Belgian government scholarship for study before, and not enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January 2027
Only one ICP Connect scholarship application per year: applying to two or more ICP programmes gets you excluded
No other scholarship or grant for this or any other programme at the same time
Good command of English (all ICP Connect programmes are taught in English; Dutch is not needed)
Meets Thomas More's general admission requirements for degree students
Strong motivation, good academic results, relevant professional and soft skills
An intake interview with the programme
documents: The Thomas More ICP Connect scholarship form (CV, motivation, academic records)
After selection: the regular Thomas More admission file through its Apply procedure
opportunities.selection_process: The host institution first checks and ranks every eligible application, then sends its shortlist to VLIR-UOS, which screens it again. Points that weigh in the ranking: motivation and your potential to act as an agent of change at home; professional experience, with preference for people working in (or heading for) higher education, government or civil society; gender balance, with women strongly encouraged to apply; balance between regions; the Leave No One Behind principle, which favours candidates from vulnerable groups when two files are equally strong; and preference for people who have never had a scholarship to study in a high-income country. VLIR-UOS emails the selected and reserve-list candidates; the programme tells the others. Results are due by mid-May 2027 at the latest. Thomas More pre-selects 16 candidates (8 on a main list and 8 on a reserve list) after an intake interview and sends the list to VLIR-UOS by March.
important_dates: Shortlist sent to VLIR-UOS: by March 2027
Candidates contacted by VLIR-UOS: by end of May 2027
VLIR-UOS online information session: 26 November 2026, 14:30-16:30 CET (register through the Zoom link on the call page)
opportunities.about_provider: VLIR-UOS is the Flemish university network's programme for development cooperation, funded by the Belgian government. Through its ICP Connect scheme it pays full scholarships for a selected set of English-taught degree programmes at universities and university colleges in Flanders and Brussels, so that students from partner countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America can study in Belgium and take their skills back home. For the September 2027 intake it funds 12 programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the ICP Connect scholarship form on https://thomasmore.be/en/vlir-uos-scholarship before 15 January 2027. If you are shortlisted you then complete the normal admission procedure (https://thomasmore.be/en/admissions-application-procedure-general) and receive instructions by email. Questions: ICPConnectScholarships@thomasmore.be.
opportunities.notes: Do not apply to more than one ICP Connect programme in the same year. New graduates or people from the private sector without work experience can still be considered if their motivation is strong. Students may work a few hours a week, but not during compulsory classes, and the scholarship should not be topped up by a job. Some countries need their diplomas legalised through a Belgian embassy or consulate; ask the university early. In mid-November 2026 the Thomas More page said its scholarship form was temporarily unavailable; check back or email ICPConnectScholarships@thomasmore.be if it still does not work.

opportunities.title: Beahrs Environmental Leadership Program Partial Scholarships 2027
opportunities.provider: UC Berkeley Beahrs Environmental Leadership Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Environmental professionals worldwide can apply for the 2027 Berkeley ELP; partial fee scholarships are reviewed by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Beahrs Environmental Leadership Program (ELP) is an intensive professional course run by the Rausser College of Natural Resources at the University of California, Berkeley. The 2027 edition has two required parts: online sessions on Zoom in mid-June 2027 and an in-person course on the Berkeley campus from 1 to 16 July 2027.

The programme gathers environmental professionals from around the world to build skills in leadership, conservation and sustainable resource management, and to join an international alumni network. Because the course fee is high, ELP offers a limited number of partial scholarships to help with programme fees, plus some donor-funded fellowships whose amounts change from year to year.

Applications opened on 4 September 2026. The first scholarship review date (6 November 2026) has passed; the second and last scholarship review date is 15 January 2027. African environmental practitioners who need funding should apply before that second date, since later applicants can still be admitted but are not guaranteed scholarship consideration.
opportunities.benefits: Partial scholarships of various amounts, usable only towards the programme fee (US$9,100, which includes housing and most meals during the in-person part). Some donor-funded fellowships are also offered. Travel, visa costs and about US$500 of incidental expenses are not covered.
requirements: Environmental professional interested in leadership and sustainable resource management
Able to attend both the online sessions in June 2027 and the in-person course in Berkeley, 1-16 July 2027
Scholarship decisions weigh financial need
Professional experience and commitment to positive environmental change are considered
documents: Online application form (via the programme website)
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarship applications are reviewed in rounds; candidates are judged on financial need, professional experience and commitment to positive change. Scholarships are limited and not guaranteed after the review dates.
opportunities.about_provider: The Beahrs ELP is part of the Rausser College of Natural Resources at UC Berkeley, one of the leading US public research universities. It has trained environmental leaders from many countries through its summer course.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the 2027 programme page and indicate that you wish to be considered for a scholarship. Submit before 15 January 2027 for the last scholarship review. Questions go to beahrselp@berkeley.edu or (510) 473-2771.
opportunities.notes: Budget for your own flights, visa and about US$500 for incidentals; the scholarship only reduces the programme fee.

opportunities.title: Boulder School 2027: Machine Learning and Condensed Matter
opportunities.provider: Boulder School for Condensed Matter and Materials Physics, University of Colorado Boulder
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and young researchers can apply by 15 January 2027 for the July 2027 Boulder School on machine learning and condensed matter, with free housing and weekday meals.
opportunities.description:
The Boulder School for Condensed Matter and Materials Physics holds a four-week graduate summer school each year at the University of Colorado Boulder. The 2027 school, on Machine Learning and Condensed Matter, runs from 5 to 30 July 2027 and is directed by Leo Radzihovsky, with partial funding from the US National Science Foundation.

The school combines lectures by leading researchers with discussion, and is meant for graduate students and early-career researchers who want a deep grounding in how machine-learning methods are reshaping condensed-matter physics. Participants must attend for at least three weeks.

The practical support is generous: accepted participants get a free dormitory room and weekday meals. That makes the school realistic for African physics PhD students and postdocs who can cover their airfare, while US-based students can also claim travel money.
opportunities.benefits: Free dormitory accommodation and weekday meals (weekend meals not included). Travel support of up to US$500 is available only to graduate students and postdocs at US universities. Accepted students pay a US$400 registration fee; students from outside the US pay their own airfare.
requirements: Graduate student or early-career researcher in physics or a related field
Must attend at least three of the four weeks
One letter of recommendation
documents: One recommendation letter (the recommender is contacted automatically)
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers review the electronic applications and recommendation letters and select participants.
opportunities.about_provider: The Boulder School for Condensed Matter and Materials Physics is a long-running summer school at the University of Colorado Boulder, partly funded by the US National Science Foundation, that brings graduate students together with leading physicists each summer.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the electronic application linked from the 2027 school page and give your recommender's details so they receive the letter request. Questions go to boulder.organizers@yale.edu.
opportunities.notes: Plan for the US$400 registration fee and your own flight; non-US participants are not eligible for the travel grant.

opportunities.title: Cambridge-Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund 2026/27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral-level researchers at African institutions, applying jointly with a Cambridge partner, can seek GBP 25,000-80,000 for climate resilience research by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Cambridge Africa Climate Collaborative Research Fund supports joint research between a researcher at the University of Cambridge and a researcher at an African university or similar institution, focused on climate resilience and sustainability. The 2026/27 call opened on 15 October 2026 and is run by Cambridge-Africa with partners including the Mastercard Foundation and the universities of Cape Town, Ghana and Makerere.

Three kinds of award are offered: Research Catalyst Grants of up to GBP 25,000 for about a year, Research Project Grants of up to GBP 80,000 for up to 18 months for teams that have already worked together, and Workshop Grants of up to GBP 50,000 for workshops held in Africa.

The scheme is built around equal partnership: the African and Cambridge applicants apply together. Projects that involve young people in Africa (under 35) are given priority, which makes this a strong opening for African early-career and established researchers working on climate questions.
opportunities.benefits: Research Catalyst Grant: up to GBP 25,000 (about 12 months). Research Project Grant: up to GBP 80,000 (up to 18 months). Workshop Grant: up to GBP 50,000 (about 12 months, workshops in Africa). Salaries, overheads and indirect costs are not funded.
requirements: Joint application by a Cambridge researcher and a researcher at an African university or comparable institution
Both applicants at postdoctoral level or above (equivalent experience may be accepted after contacting the organisers)
Both formally employed by their institution for the length of the award
Support from both heads of department
Not open to postgraduate students
Research Project Grants need evidence of earlier collaboration
documents: Letters of support from both departments
CVs of both applicants (max 2 pages each)
opportunities.selection_process: A panel reviews applications; referees are contacted in January-February 2027 and outcomes are announced in March 2027. Projects engaging young people in Africa are prioritised.
opportunities.about_provider: Cambridge-Africa is the University of Cambridge's umbrella programme for research partnerships with African institutions. It runs funding schemes such as the ALBORADA Research Fund and this climate fund with the Mastercard Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The Cambridge applicant registers on the Cambridge-Africa website (a @cam.ac.uk email is required) and submits the joint application with the African partner. Read the 2026-27 guidance for applicants first; questions go to africaclimatecollaborative@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: African researchers without a Cambridge partner should look for one early, since the Cambridge co-applicant must register the application.

Research that requires the Gennadius Library collections
Open to all nationalities

English for the application and the school

Letter of endorsement from a current or former supervisor or senior staff member

opportunities.about_provider: The European Educational Research Association (EERA), based in Berlin, is the umbrella body for European educational research associations and organises the annual ECER conference and season schools.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the EERSS 2027 ConfTool site by 15 January 2027 with your abstract, CV and endorsement letter. If accepted, register and pay by 31 March 2027; registration is binding.
