opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in materials science, physics, chemistry or related fields can apply for a fully funded AMASE Erasmus Mundus master's; deadline 15 January 2027 (Luleå) or 15 February 2027 (other entrances).
opportunities.description:
AMASE (Advanced Materials Science and Engineering) is an Erasmus Mundus joint master's coordinated by the European School of Materials (EUSMAT) at Saarland University. Students spend four semesters at two of six partner universities: Luleå University of Technology (Sweden), Montanuniversität Leoben (Austria), the University of Padua (Italy), Saarland University (Germany), Université de Lorraine in Nancy (France) and UPC Barcelona (Spain).

The application period for the 2027/28 intake opened in October 2026. Candidates choose an entrance university and a second university, and the deadline for Erasmus Mundus scholarship candidates depends on that choice: 15 January 2027 for those starting at Luleå, and 15 February 2027 for all other entrance universities.

Full Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay a monthly allowance for the whole two years and cover all participation costs, which makes AMASE an attractive route for African materials science, physics and chemistry graduates. Several African bachelor's degrees are accepted as proof of English for the Luleå route.
opportunities.benefits: Full Erasmus Mundus scholarship: EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months (EUR 33,600 in total), all participation costs for four semesters and basic EU health insurance. Partial scholarship: tuition (participation fee) waiver only. Self-funded fees: EUR 4,500 per semester for non-EU students (EUR 1,500 for EU students).
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least three years in materials science or engineering, physics, chemistry or a related field (final-year students may apply with proof from the registrar)
Language level set by the entrance university: Luleå B2 English (IELTS 6.5, no part below 5.5); Saarland B1 German; Lorraine B2 French; UPC B2 Spanish
English-test exemption at Luleå for bachelor's degrees from countries including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia and Botswana
documents: Motivation statement (English, PDF, max one page)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed by the consortium against its published selection criteria; scholarship candidates compete in the first rounds.
important_dates: EM scholarship deadline, Luleå entrance: 15 January 2027
EM scholarship deadline, other entrance universities: 15 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: EUSMAT, the European School of Materials based at Saarland University, coordinates international materials science programmes. AMASE is delivered jointly by six European technical universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose your entrance and second university, then apply through the AMASE online portal linked from the EUSMAT application pages, uploading all documents. Questions go to office@eusmat.net.
opportunities.notes: Pick the entrance university carefully, because it decides both your deadline and the language you must prove.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Choreomundus Scholarship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Humanities and social science graduates or dance practitioners from any country can apply by 15 January 2027 for the fully funded Choreomundus Erasmus Mundus master's.
opportunities.description:
Choreomundus is an Erasmus Mundus joint master's in Dance and Movement Practical Knowledge and Heritage. Over 24 months, students are registered at all four partner universities and study dance as cultural heritage and embodied knowledge, combining anthropology, ethnochoreology and heritage studies; an optional final semester can be taken at the University of Roehampton.

The 2027-2028 application campaign is open, with a single deadline of 15 January 2027 for all applicants. There are no self-funded places: every admitted student either holds an Erasmus Mundus scholarship or a tuition waiver, and 17 scholarships are planned.

The programme welcomes graduates in the humanities and social sciences, and also dancers with a strong practical background from other disciplines. It accepts West African school English results (WAEC) and South African results among its English proofs, which makes it accessible to African applicants.
opportunities.benefits: 17 Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months, awarded without a separate application. Other admitted students receive a tuition waiver valued at EUR 18,000. No tuition-paying places are offered.
requirements: Bachelor's (180 ECTS) or master's (120 ECTS) in the humanities or social sciences, preferably related to dance or heritage; strong dance practitioners from other fields may apply
Minimum CGPA of 60% (grade C)
English at B2 level, e.g. IELTS 5.5-6.5 or TOEFL iBT 87-109; WAEC grade 6 (Nigeria, Ghana) or South African grade C also accepted
documents: Degree documents in English or with official translation
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on CGPA (40%), portfolio (30%) and motivation letter (30%). Shortlisted candidates have a 5-minute interview, and the committee balances the class by nationality, residence and gender.
opportunities.about_provider: Choreomundus is run by a consortium of four European universities, with applications handled through the portal of Vytautas Magnus University in Lithuania. It has been an Erasmus Mundus programme for several editions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Vytautas Magnus University DreamApply portal linked from the Choreomundus site, uploading the video, essay and other documents. There is no separate scholarship form.
opportunities.notes: Because there are no paying places, every admitted student is funded, but competition for the 17 scholarships is strong.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EU4M - Joint Master in Mechatronic Engineering
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to engineering bachelor's graduates of any nationality applying for EMJM scholarships through the EU4M portal by 15 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus GEM - Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation for Environmental Modelling
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Strong (2.1 or better) bachelor's graduates from any country can apply for about 17-18 GEM Erasmus Mundus scholarships; English results due 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
GEM is an Erasmus Mundus joint MSc in Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation for Environmental Modelling and Management. It is run by a consortium of four universities: the Faculty ITC of the University of Twente in the Netherlands (the coordinator), the University of Tartu in Estonia, Lund University in Sweden and UCLouvain in Belgium. The programme lasts 24 months, is taught in English and leads to a double degree from the two universities where the student studies.

Students choose one of four tracks, each combining two partner universities: Geospatial Planner (Tartu and Twente), Geospatial Analyst (Tartu and UCLouvain), Geospatial Developer (Lund and Twente) and Geospatial Modeller (Lund and UCLouvain). Across all of them, the course trains students to use remote sensing and geographic information systems to monitor and model environmental change and support land and resource management.

The September 2027 intake is recruiting now, with roughly 17 to 18 Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 2027-2029 spread across the tracks. Each scholarship waives tuition, provides insurance and pays EUR 1,400 a month for up to 24 months. English test results must be submitted by 15 January 2027. For African applicants the programme is especially accessible because graduates of degrees from Botswana, Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Namibia, Nigeria, Zambia and Zimbabwe may qualify for an exemption from the English test.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (about 17-18 for 2027-2029): full tuition waiver, insurance and EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months. Self-funded students pay EUR 19,800 tuition for non-EU students (EUR 5,500 for EU) plus EUR 400 extra, with living costs estimated at about EUR 30,000 for the two years (total about EUR 50,200 for non-EU students; instalments due 1 May 2027 and 1 May 2028).
requirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or three years of full-time study that gives access to master's study in the awarding country
Degree from an institution ranked in the Webometrics top 10,000 at the time of application
First Class or upper second (2.1) result plus the country- or institution-specific minimum CGPA/GPA, which cannot be waived; a 2.2 does not qualify

Relevant background such as geography, geoinformatics, environmental or earth science, engineering or computer science; GIS or remote sensing experience is an advantage (15 ECTS recommended for the Developer and Modeller tracks)

English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (6.0 per section), TOEFL iBT 100 (25 per section; new format 5 overall), Cambridge C1/C2 176 (169 per section), PTE Academic 63 (59 per section) or LANGUAGECERT Academic 70, no more than two years old; IELTS Online, Duolingo and institutional TOEFL are not accepted
Erasmus Mundus scholarship: not previously an Erasmus Mundus master's or joint doctorate scholarship holder, and both study periods must be outside your country of residence
documents: Bachelor's degree certificate (final-year students may apply and submit it, with the final transcript, before 31 July 2027)
English language certificate or proof of exemption
Statement for final-year students on expected completion
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are ranked on their academic results together with an assessment of how relevant their previous courses are to the chosen track. Minimum grade and English thresholds are strictly enforced, and applications missing English results by 15 January 2027 are treated as incomplete.
important_dates: First tuition instalment for self-funded students: 1 May 2027
Degree and final transcript due: 31 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The GEM consortium is coordinated by ITC, the Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation of the University of Twente in the Netherlands, a leading geospatial institute that has trained many professionals from developing countries. Its partners are the University of Tartu (Estonia), Lund University (Sweden) and UCLouvain (Belgium).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a track, check the minimum GPA for your country and whether your degree exempts you from the English test, then apply online through the 'Apply to GEM' section of gem-msc.eu before 15 January 2027 with your degree, transcripts and English results.
opportunities.notes: Only formal exemption categories remove the English test requirement; use the University of Twente self-check. Region-specific scholarships also exist. Results are shared with applicants after ranking; check the 2026 GEM study guide for course details.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus IDOHNext: Infectious Diseases and One Health (2027-2029 intake)
opportunities.provider: IDOHNext Erasmus Mundus consortium (Tours, Barcelona, Hannover and partners)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's graduates (or final-year students) in immunology, microbiology, biomedicine or a related life-science field with upper-second-class grades and B2+ English can apply from 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
IDOHNext is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Infectious Diseases and One Health. Students study in several European universities, with mobility between Tours (France), Barcelona (Spain) and Hannover (Germany), and spend the fourth semester on a traineeship. The programme connects human, animal and environmental health, the One Health approach to infectious diseases.

Applications for the 2027-2029 cohort open on 1 December 2026 and close on 15 January 2027, and the course starts in September 2027. Each intake has about 15 to 25 students, and a few Erasmus Mundus scholarships are given to the best-ranked of the selected candidates; others pay a tuition fee of EUR 4,500 per year.

The programme sets no nationality restriction and welcomes medical doctors, veterinarians, pharmacists and biologists, which makes it a strong option for African graduates working on epidemics, zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.
opportunities.benefits: A few Erasmus Mundus scholarships for the top-ranked selected students (the guideline gives no amount; Erasmus Mundus scholarships normally include a monthly allowance and cover participation costs). Self-funded students pay EUR 4,500 per year.
requirements: Bachelor's degree of three or four years (180 ECTS or equivalent) majoring in immunology, infectious diseases, biomedicine, microbiology or a similar topic
Medical doctors, veterinarians, pharmacists, biologists and related scientists are welcome
Final-year students may apply with a university letter if they graduate before the programme starts
At least upper second-class honours or equivalent (e.g. French "Assez Bien", Spanish "Notable", German "Gut")
English at CEFR B2+ (IELTS Academic from 1 Sept 2025 or later, TOEFL iBT, Oxford tests, Cambridge C1/C2 from 1 March 2024 or later, or an English-taught degree)
Work experience not required; internships count
documents: Degree certificates and transcripts (certified English translations if needed)
At least one reference letter (up to three) on signed, stamped headed paper
All uploads as PDF; documents in English and stamped by a public institution
opportunities.selection_process: After an eligibility check, applicants take a timed online multiple-choice test of 36 questions (up to 60 minutes, one sitting). Two evaluators then score each file, with a third review if they differ by more than 10 per cent. About the top 100 are interviewed by two assessors, who score motivation, career consistency, scientific background and English out of 100.
opportunities.about_provider: IDOHNext is run by a consortium of European universities and is co-funded by the European Union's Erasmus Mundus programme, which supports joint master's degrees taught across several countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: From 1 December 2026, register on the application portal linked from the IDOHNext website, upload all documents as PDFs and submit before 15 January 2027. Wait for the confirmation email, then take the online test when invited.
opportunities.notes: Start gathering stamped translations and your birth certificate in English early, as these take time to obtain in many African countries.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Earthen Architecture and Construction (TERRA) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Architecture and civil engineering graduates of any nationality can apply by 15 January 2027 (first call) for TERRA Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
TERRA is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Earthen Architecture and Construction run by the University of Minho (Portugal), Universitat Politècnica de València (Spain), ENTPE (France) and the University of Florence (Italy), with about 40 associated partners. The academic year runs from September to July and includes three compulsory mobilities between partner universities.

The 2027/2028 edition is only the programme's second. Its first call, which is the main round for EU and consortium scholarships, closes on 15 January 2027; the page says applications will open soon. A second call closes on 15 April 2027 and an optional third on 15 June 2027.

TERRA focuses on building with earth, a low-carbon material with deep roots in African architecture, which makes it highly relevant for African architects and civil engineers. The first call is open to all nationalities.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus and most consortium scholarships are offered only in the first call (amounts not stated on the applications page). Tuition for non-scholarship students is EUR 9,000; a EUR 250 deposit on acceptance is refunded on registration.
requirements: Degree in civil engineering, architecture or equivalent (bachelor's of 240 ECTS, or 300 ECTS)
Final-year students may apply if they graduate by 31 July 2027
English: TOEFL iBT 72, IELTS Academic 6.5 or another recognised certificate
documents: Two recommendation letters (submitted via the portal)
opportunities.selection_process: After an academic review, about 60 top candidates are notified by 15 February 2027 and 5-7 per country are invited to video interviews (22-26 February 2027). Gender balance is used as a tie-break. Admission results by 5 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Minho in Portugal coordinates TERRA together with three European partners specialising in architecture and construction.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply with the online form on the TERRA applications page once the first call opens, uploading all documents before 15 January 2027 to be considered for scholarships.
opportunities.notes: Scholarships are concentrated in the first call, so apply by 15 January if you need funding.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Nuclear Physics Scholarship 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Physics graduates from any country can apply by 15 January 2027 for the NucPhys Erasmus Mundus master's, with automatic consideration for EUR 1,400-a-month scholarships.
opportunities.description:
NucPhys is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree in Nuclear Physics run by six universities in Spain, France and Italy, coordinated from the Universidad de Sevilla, with about 30 associated partners worldwide, including institutions in South Africa and Morocco. The programme lasts two years (120 ECTS) and trains students in experimental and theoretical nuclear physics and its applications.

The application period for the 2027-2029 edition is open until 15 January 2027. Every applicant is automatically considered for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship, with no separate form, and about 12-13 scholarships are expected per edition.

To spread places fairly, the consortium caps scholarships by nationality: for 2027-2029, most nationalities can receive up to two, which leaves real room for strong African physics graduates.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 a month for the full two years, with no tuition for scholarship holders; about 12-13 scholarships per edition. One extra Normandie region scholarship for 2027-2028. Consortium fee waivers are awarded automatically.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in physics (related fields such as chemistry, engineering or applied mathematics accepted with lower priority)
English at B2: TOEFL iBT 78, IELTS Academic 6.0 (min 5.7 per part) or Cambridge FCE 72; waived for degrees taught in English in Canada, USA, UK, Ireland, New Zealand or Australia
Written commitment to full-time study
Scholarship caps by nationality (up to two per nationality for most countries in 2027-2029)
documents: Residence certificate issued within 12 months before the deadline
Work or study certificate issued within 12 months before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are ranked out of 100 by the consortium; scholarships go to the top-ranked candidates within the nationality caps.
opportunities.about_provider: The NucPhys consortium brings together six European universities, coordinated by the Universidad de Sevilla, plus around 30 associated research and academic partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the 'Student Application Form' on the NucPhys website before 15 January 2027 and upload the residence and work/study certificates with your academic documents. Scholarship consideration is automatic.
opportunities.notes: Women in nuclear fields may also look at the IAEA Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellowship Programme, which NucPhys links to.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus MA Euroculture: Society, Politics and Culture in a Global Context (2027-2029)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Arts, humanities and social science graduates from any country can apply by 15 January 2027 for Euroculture Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400 a month.
opportunities.description:
Euroculture is an Erasmus Mundus MA in Society, Politics and Culture in a Global Context, coordinated by Jagiellonian University in Kraków with seven other European partner universities. The two-year programme looks at Europe and European integration from cultural, political and social angles, with study at more than one partner university.

Applications for the 2027-2029 intake opened on 15 October 2026. Applicants who want an Erasmus Mundus scholarship must apply by 15 January 2027; self-funded applicants can apply later, with a recommended date of 1 May 2027 for non-EU passport holders.

Graduates in the arts, humanities and social sciences from Africa are eligible, and the full scholarship covers tuition, health insurance and a monthly allowance for both years.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months (EUR 33,600 in total), full tuition waiver and health insurance.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (arts, humanities or social sciences)
English: IELTS 6.5 overall with no part below 5.5 and writing at least 6.0, TOEFL iBT 92 (PBT 580), or Cambridge CAE/CPE
English test waived for native speakers, a fully English-taught bachelor's, or a year of English-taught study in an English-speaking country
documents: Bachelor's diploma (see the site for the exact date by which it is needed)
Two references, at least one academic
English certificate or university statement of English-medium study
opportunities.selection_process: The consortium assesses academic qualifications, the application documents and references, and interviews shortlisted candidates. Scholarship results are announced by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Euroculture consortium links eight European universities and is coordinated by Jagiellonian University in Kraków; its secretariat can be reached at euroculture@rug.nl.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Euroculture Online Application Tool linked from the admissions page, adding your referees' details and language proof. Apply by 15 January 2027 to be considered for a scholarship.
opportunities.notes: The site gives two dates for submitting the bachelor's diploma (10 and 15 January); aim for the earlier one.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus MSc WAVES - Water Vulnerability Engineering in Spatial Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Engineering graduates of any nationality with the required maths, physics and hydraulics credits can apply by 15 January 2027 for the WAVES Erasmus Mundus master's.
opportunities.description:
MSc WAVES (Water Vulnerability Engineering in Spatial Sciences) is an Erasmus Mundus double master's run by the University of Twente (Faculty ITC), the University of Padova and the University of Ljubljana, with associated partners in countries including South Africa, India and Brazil. The two-year, 120 ECTS programme starts on 1 October 2027, with each year spent at different partner universities.

It trains engineers to assess and reduce water-related risks such as floods and droughts using spatial data and modelling. The application portal opened on 13 October 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027 at 23:59 CET.

The programme is open to all nationalities and charges no application fee, so African engineering graduates with the right foundation courses can apply for Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarships for the two-year programme (number and amounts are on the programme's fees and funding page). No application fee.
requirements: Bachelor's of at least 180 ECTS in a relevant field (final-year students may apply)
Foundation credits: maths 10, physics 8, chemistry 8, hydraulics 6, programming 6, solid mechanics 6 and hydraulic/geotechnical engineering 14 ECTS
English: IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 6.0), TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1/C2, PTE or LanguageCert (check the exact scores on the admissions page)
Open to all nationalities
opportunities.selection_process: Each application is scored by two reviewers on six weighted criteria; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in February-March 2027 and results are confirmed by 17 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The WAVES consortium is led by ITC at the University of Twente in the Netherlands with the universities of Padova (Italy) and Ljubljana (Slovenia).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the University of Twente DreamApply portal for MSc WAVES before 15 January 2027. Questions go to admission-itc@utwente.nl.
opportunities.notes: Check your transcript against the foundation credit list before applying; missing credits are a common reason for rejection.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus MultiDiverse - Multilingualism and Cultural Diversity
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in linguistics, education, psychology and related fields can apply 23 November 2026 to 15 January 2027 for about 12 MultiDiverse Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
MultiDiverse is an Erasmus Mundus joint master's in Multilingualism and Cultural Diversity, coordinated by the University of Konstanz in Germany, with partners including the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki. Over four semesters (24 months), students study how languages and cultures meet in education, society and the mind.

The application window for the 2027-2029 intake runs from 23 November 2026 to 15 January 2027. Around 12 Erasmus Mundus scholarships are awarded each year, and scholarship applicants also apply as self-payers so that they can still be considered for a paying place.

Graduates in linguistics, education, psychology, sociology or speech and language therapy from Africa are eligible; no more than 10% of scholarships go to any one nationality.
opportunities.benefits: About 12 Erasmus Mundus scholarships a year covering participation costs, EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months and insurance. Self-payer fees for 2027-2029: EUR 11,520 in total for students from non-associated countries.
requirements: Bachelor's in linguistics, education, psychology, sociology, speech and language therapy or a related field
Final grade of at least 3.0 on the German scale (or equivalent)
English at C1 level (not needed if the degree was taught in English)
No more than 10% of scholarships per nationality
documents: Motivation letter in English (max one page, written without AI assistance)
opportunities.selection_process: After an eligibility check, applications are scored out of 100: degree grade (20), course fit (30), experience (20), motivation (20) and references (10). Offers are made by mid-April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Konstanz is a German research university on Lake Constance that coordinates the MultiDiverse consortium of European universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Konstanz ZEuS portal once it opens on 23 November 2026, uploading all documents and sending the reference links. Questions go to emjm.multidiverse(at)uni-konstanz.de.
opportunities.notes: The programme asks that the motivation letter be written without AI help.

opportunities.title: Folger Short-Term Scholarly Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars with a PhD, or PhD candidates at the dissertation stage, of any nationality, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a one- to three-month Folger fellowship paying USD 5,000 a month in residence or USD 4,000 virtually.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC offers short-term scholarly fellowships for researchers whose projects need its collections of early modern books, manuscripts and other materials. The 2027-2028 round funds stays of one, two or three months, and fellows may choose to work on site in Washington, virtually, or in a hybrid arrangement.

The fellowships are run by the Folger Institute, the library's research and scholarly programmes arm. They exist to support original research that makes real use of the Folger holdings, and the selection committee aims for a mix of disciplines, methods and geographical backgrounds among fellows.

There is no nationality restriction, so African doctoral candidates who have reached the dissertation stage and early-career or established scholars working on the early modern world, Shakespeare, book history, the Atlantic world or related topics can apply on equal terms with everyone else.
opportunities.benefits: USD 5,000 per month for fellows in residence in Washington, DC, or USD 4,000 per month for virtual fellows, for one to three months. The stipend is meant to cover travel, housing and living costs.
requirements: A terminal degree (such as a PhD), or PhD candidacy at the all-but-dissertation stage, or an international equivalent
A research project that needs the Folger collections
Open to applicants of any nationality
Fellowship of one, two or three months, held on site, virtually or in hybrid form
documents: Project abstract of up to 250 words
Project description of up to 1,500 words, stating the months requested and how each month will be used
One-page list of the Folger primary sources you plan to use
One letter of recommendation submitted through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: An external committee reviews applications for their likely impact, relevance to the field, originality and sophistication, feasibility, and how well they will use the Folger collections. The committee also aims for disciplinary, methodological and geographical diversity.
important_dates: Information sessions: 9 October and 1 December 2026 (12 pm ET, online)
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC holds one of the world's largest collections of Shakespeare and early modern printed and manuscript material. Its Folger Institute runs fellowships, seminars and other programmes for researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the abstract, project description, CV and source list, then apply through the Folger fellowship portal (onlineapplicationportal.com/folgerfellowships). Your recommender uploads their letter through the same portal. Check the Online Catalog and finding aids first so that your source list is specific.
opportunities.notes: Use the Folger catalogue and finding aids to name concrete items in your source list; vague lists weaken an application. The online information session on 1 December 2026 is a good chance to ask questions.

opportunities.title: Fully funded PhD in Management at Rotterdam School of Management (ERIM), September 2027 start
opportunities.provider: Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University (ERIM)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a strong master's (MSc, MA or MPhil) in business, economics or a related field, with high GMAT/GRE scores and TOEFL/IELTS, can apply for fully funded PhD projects starting September 2027.
opportunities.description:
Rotterdam School of Management (RSM) at Erasmus University offers a fully funded, English-taught full-time PhD in Management through its research institute ERIM. The programme lasts four to five years, starts in September, and draws candidates from more than 30 countries. Applicants pick up to two projects from the published vacancy list.

For the September 2027 intake, applications opened in November 2026 and the general deadline is 15 January 2027 (some individual vacancies may have their own dates). Decisions are usually made by mid-March.

The page states no nationality restriction, so African graduates with a strong master's in business or economics and competitive test scores can compete for these funded places at one of Europe's leading business schools.
opportunities.benefits: A fully funded PhD position for four to five years (amounts not stated on the pages read).
requirements: Master's degree (MSc, MA or MPhil) in business, economics or a related field linked to the PhD project
Strong academic record
GMAT or GRE with verbal and quantitative scores at or above the 85th percentile (a 2026 GMAT needs a total of at least 650)
English: TOEFL iBT (from 2026 every section at least 5) or IELTS 7.5 overall with no section below 6.5, unless exempt
Not already holding a PhD
documents: Certified diplomas and transcripts (with certified translations if not in English or Dutch)
Two academic references (a third is optional)
GMAT or GRE score under 5 years old, sent by the test provider (GMAT code QK8-CX-23, GRE code 7103)
English test score under 2 years old
opportunities.selection_process: The PhD office screens the applications, supervisors review them and interview candidates, supervisors nominate their preferred candidates, and ERIM management makes the final decision.
opportunities.about_provider: RSM is the business school of Erasmus University Rotterdam in the Netherlands. ERIM, the Erasmus Research Institute of Management, runs the school's doctoral programme and research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose up to two projects from RSM's full-time PhD vacancy list and apply online (email applications are not accepted). Arrange for the test provider to send your GMAT/GRE score to ERIM and ask your referees for letters in time. Questions go to phdadmissions@erim.eur.nl.
opportunities.notes: Some vacancies may list a deadline other than 15 January 2027, so check each project. Test-score exemptions exist for some degrees taught in English.

opportunities.title: Georgetown University Graduate School Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to Georgetown graduate programmes are considered for tuition aid with their application.

opportunities.title: Graduate Institute Geneva Scholarship for Africa and the Middle East 2027
opportunities.provider: Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (Geneva)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants from Africa and the Middle East applying to a Graduate Institute master's or PhD can request a partial scholarship with their application.

opportunities.title: Hamilton College Need-Based Aid for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Hamilton College who file the CSS Profile and Certification of Finances by 15 January 2027 (Regular Decision) can receive aid meeting full need.
opportunities.description:
Hamilton College, a liberal arts college in Clinton, New York, meets the full demonstrated financial need of the students it admits, and international applicants can apply for this need-based aid. The aid timeline for the current admission cycle lists 15 January 2027 as the financial aid deadline for Regular Decision applicants.

For African students admitted to Hamilton, this can make a US liberal arts education affordable, provided the aid forms reach the college on time.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based aid that meets 100% of demonstrated need, made up of scholarships, loans and work-study (amounts depend on need).

Meet the aid deadline for your admission round

opportunities.title: Houghton Library Visiting Fellowships 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality, from doctoral students to independent scholars and archive professionals, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 4,500 Houghton Library visiting fellowship of at least four weeks at Harvard.
opportunities.description:
Houghton Library, Harvard University's main library for rare books and manuscripts, offers visiting fellowships for researchers who need to work with its collections. For the 2027-2028 fellowship year (July to June), the library is awarding fellowships from 15 endowed funds; applicants submit one application and the committee decides which fellowship fits each project.

Fellows must spend at least four weeks in residence at Houghton Library in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The library is keen on projects with a global outlook and contemporary relevance, and some of the named fellowships have a specific focus, for example the Hyde Fellowship for research on early modern Black lives, including Africa and the African diaspora between 1500 and 1800.

The programme is open to all nationalities and to a wide range of researchers, from doctoral students to independent scholars and museum or archive professionals, which makes it a realistic option for African researchers working with historical, literary or archival sources held at Harvard.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 4,500 for the fellowship, paid two to three weeks after arrival. Fellows pay their own travel, housing and taxes; non-US fellows need a J-1 visa, which Harvard sponsors, but the visa fees are paid by the fellow.
requirements: Open to all nationalities
Doctoral students, postdocs, faculty, independent scholars, curators and library, archive or museum professionals
Aged 18 or over
Must not live within commuting distance of Harvard
Research must use Houghton Library holdings
At least four weeks in residence during July 2027 to June 2028
Past fellows must wait five years before applying again
documents: Project proposal of up to 500 words
Preliminary list of Houghton holdings you will consult
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee reviews all applications and assigns each successful applicant to one of 15 endowed fellowships. Proposals that do not name Houghton materials are not considered; the library favours projects with a global lens and present-day relevance. Some fellowships carry extra conditions, such as ASECS membership for the Bate/Bryant ASECS fellowship.
important_dates: Fellowship year: July 2027 to June 2028 (minimum four weeks in residence)
opportunities.about_provider: Houghton Library is Harvard University's principal repository for rare books, manuscripts and archives. It supports outside researchers through a programme of endowed visiting fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Houghton Library Visiting Fellowship Program 2027-2028 form on Submittable (houghtonlibrary.submittable.com), uploading the proposal, holdings list and CV and arranging one reference letter. You do not need to choose a particular named fellowship. Questions go to Peter X. Accardo at Houghton Library.
opportunities.notes: Search HOLLIS and the Houghton finding aids before applying so that your holdings list is precise. Budget for travel, housing and J-1 visa fees, since the USD 4,500 stipend does not cover everything.

opportunities.title: ICWSM 2027 Call for Papers, January round (Edinburgh)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit web and social media research to ICWSM 2027 (Edinburgh) by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
ICWSM, the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media, is one of the main venues for research on online platforms, social media and their effects on society. The 2027 conference will be held in Edinburgh, and papers are reviewed in several rounds through the year; the January round closes on 15 January 2027.

The conference accepts full papers, posters, demos and dataset papers, and has a Social Science and Sociophysics track alongside computational work. Papers accepted (rather than given a revise-and-resubmit) in this round can be presented at ICWSM 2027 and appear in the official proceedings.

For African researchers studying misinformation, digital politics, online communities or platform data, ICWSM is a high-visibility outlet that welcomes interdisciplinary work.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the ICWSM proceedings (AAAI) and the chance to present at ICWSM 2027 in Edinburgh. No travel grants are mentioned on the submission page.
requirements: Full papers up to 11 pages (8 recommended) including references, AAAI two-column format, double-blind
Posters 5 pages; demos 3 pages (single-blind); dataset papers 2-10 pages with a DOI
Mandatory, unaltered paper checklist (papers without it are desk-rejected)
Use of generative AI must be disclosed
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review; decisions are accept, revise-and-resubmit or reject. Notification on 15 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ICWSM is organised under the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI), which publishes its proceedings.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the Precision Conference System (AAAI > ICWSM 2027) before 15 January 2027 23:59 AoE, with the checklist attached.
opportunities.notes: Only papers accepted outright in this round can be presented at ICWSM 2027; revise-and-resubmit papers move to a later year.

opportunities.title: IEEE IntelliSecAI 2027 Call for Papers

opportunities.description:
IEEE-IntelliSecAI 2027 is the IEEE International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Security and AI, organised by Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd University (PMU) with IEEE-linked committees. It takes place at PMU in Al-Khobar, Saudi Arabia, on 24-25 March 2027, in hybrid format so authors can present in person or online.

The call invites papers on computational intelligence, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, smart cities and related topics. Abstract registration and full submission are both due on 15 January 2027.

The hybrid format makes it practical for African researchers who cannot travel to present work at an IEEE conference.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at an IEEE conference, in person or online. No grants or awards are listed in the call.
requirements: Papers up to 8 A4 pages in the IEEE conference template
Single-blind review; non-conforming papers are rejected without review
Topic within computational intelligence, security or AI

opportunities.about_provider: Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd University is a private university in Al-Khobar, Saudi Arabia, which hosts the IntelliSecAI conference with IEEE support.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and submit your paper on EasyChair (conference intellisecai2027) by 15 January 2027. Questions go to info@intellisecai.org.

opportunities.title: IMPRS for Genome Science PhD Positions 2027 (Göttingen)
opportunities.provider: International Max Planck Research School for Genome Science (University of Göttingen and Max Planck institutes)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a master's in life sciences, mathematics, computer science, statistics, physics or a related field (or finishing before October 2027) can apply by 15 January 2027 for salaried PhD positions in Göttingen.
opportunities.description:
The International Max Planck Research School for Genome Science (IMPRS-GS) is an English-language doctoral programme in experimental and computational genome research in Göttingen, Germany. It is run jointly by the University of Göttingen, the University Medical Center Göttingen, the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization and the German Primate Center, within the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neurosciences, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences (GGNB).

The 2027 recruitment opened on 15 November 2026 and the online application tool stays open until 15 January 2027. Successful candidates start in autumn 2027, or earlier if their project funding allows, and are employed on fully funded contracts.

The programme accepts applicants from any country and is well suited to African biologists, bioinformaticians, statisticians and computer scientists who want to work on genomes at leading German research institutes.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded PhD positions on employment contracts, with a net monthly salary of roughly EUR 1,300 to 1,600.
requirements: Master's degree or equivalent in experimental life sciences, mathematics, computer science, statistics, physics or a closely related field
Applicants expecting to finish their master's before October 2027 are eligible
Good English (the programme language); proof by test, language of instruction or native-speaker status if available
documents: Other relevant exam results such as GRE, if available
Proof of English proficiency, if available
Two referees who complete an online questionnaire (by 18 January 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on academic excellence, research experience, motivation, communication skills, English and the ability to think creatively across disciplines. Supervisors hold online interviews from late January to mid-February 2027, the best candidates are invited at the end of February, and final selection happens at recruitment days in Göttingen on 6 to 8 April 2027.
important_dates: Online interviews: late January to mid-February 2027
Recruitment days in Göttingen: 6 to 8 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: IMPRS-GS is one of the International Max Planck Research Schools, which bring together Max Planck institutes and universities to train doctoral researchers. It is based on the Göttingen Campus and coordinated through the GGNB graduate centre.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the IMPRS-GS online application portal and upload your documents as one PDF; documents sent any other way are not considered. You can name up to five potential supervisors from the published project list and give two referees.
opportunities.notes: The English homepage still shows an old 2026 deadline; the admission page confirms 15 January 2027. Questions go to the programme coordinator at imprs-gs@mpinat.mpg.de.

opportunities.title: ITS 2027 Intelligent Tutoring Systems Conference Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and PhD students worldwide can submit AI-in-education work to ITS 2027 (Rome, hybrid) by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
ITS 2027 is the 23rd International Conference on Intelligent Tutoring Systems, themed 'From ITS to Intelligent Learning Companions'. It is co-hosted by Universitas Mercatorum in Rome, Italy, and runs in hybrid format: tutorials on 14 June, workshops on 15 June and the main conference on 16-18 June 2027.

The call has nine special tracks, covering topics such as generative AI in education, learning analytics and human-AI collaboration. Scientific papers, posters and doctoral consortium submissions are due on 15 January 2027, and the industry track on 15 February 2027.

The hybrid format and the doctoral consortium make it a good venue for African education technology researchers and PhD students.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in Springer LNCS proceedings and presentation in Rome or online.

Double-blind, in English, PDF
Doctoral consortium submissions accepted on the same deadline

opportunities.title: International PhD Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International-fee PhD applicants to Reading for October 2027 can apply by 15 January 2027 for studentships covering fees and, for on-campus students, a UKRI-rate stipend.
opportunities.description:
The University of Reading in England runs an annual competition for International PhD Studentships for doctoral students starting in October 2027. The awards span science, life sciences, social sciences, arts and humanities, and Henley Business School; professional doctorates such as the DBA or EdD are excluded.

Each studentship pays international-rate tuition fees for up to four years of full-time study and a yearly training allowance. Students based at Reading also receive a stipend at the UKRI minimum rate, while distance-based students receive fees and the allowance only.

Applicants do not need an offer of admission or English test results by the deadline, only a submitted PhD application, which makes the scheme accessible to African candidates who are still finalising their plans.
opportunities.benefits: International tuition fees for up to 4 years full-time (6 years part-time), a training and development allowance of GBP 1,000 a year, and for Reading-based students a stipend at the UKRI rate (GBP 21,805 in 2026/27). Immigration costs are not covered.
requirements: Eligible for international tuition fees
PhD application to Reading (on campus or by distance) submitted by 15 January 2027
Meet the academic requirements of the chosen department
Professional doctorates (e.g. DBA, EdD) not eligible
English proof not needed by the deadline
documents: Online PhD application quoting 'International Research Studentship Competition'
If nominated by your school: research proposal of max 700 words
opportunities.selection_process: Two stages: each school nominates its strongest candidates, then a college panel decides around the end of March 2027; award letters are sent around the end of April 2027.
important_dates: Final panel: around end of March 2027
Award letters: around end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university west of London, home to Henley Business School. Its Doctoral and Researcher College runs the studentship competition.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for your PhD place, writing 'International Research Studentship Competition' in the scholarships box, and complete the studentship form linked from the official page by 15 January 2027. There is no application fee.
opportunities.notes: The page mentions both September and October 2027 as start months; confirm with your school.

opportunities.title: KTH Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying international applicants who list a KTH master's as first choice can apply 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 for a full-tuition KTH Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The KTH Scholarship is the main merit award of KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm for fee-paying master's students. It covers the full tuition fee of a one- or two-year master's programme; for two-year programmes, the second year depends on satisfactory results in the first.

The award is very competitive (in 2026, 65 of 718 admitted applicants were nominated), but it is open to fee-paying students of any nationality, including African applicants with outstanding records.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee for the one- or two-year master's programme (second year subject to first-year results). Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Required to pay tuition fees in Sweden (non-EU/EEA)
KTH master's programme as first priority on universityadmissions.se, with the application fee paid
Not for joint Erasmus+/EIT programmes or the Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering programme
Strong academic record (GPA, ranking of bachelor's university)
documents: KTH scholarship application form (no extra documents)
Complete master's application on universityadmissions.se by 1 February 2027

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your KTH master's programme as first priority on universityadmissions.se and pay the fee, then fill in the scholarship form on the KTH page between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Kathryn and Peter Yatrakis Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens, Gennadius Library
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and scholars who earned a PhD in the last five years, of any nationality, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a 2027-28 Gennadius Library fellowship in Athens.
opportunities.description:
The Kathryn and Peter Yatrakis Fellowship supports a full academic year of research that depends on the Gennadius Library of the American School of Classical Studies at Athens. The library holds more than 150,000 titles on Greece from antiquity to the present, with about 90,000 research titles on open shelves.

The fellowship runs from September 2027 to May 2028 in Athens and includes housing and meals at the School's Loring Hall. Fellows must report on their work and acknowledge the School in resulting publications.

It is open to all nationalities, so African doctoral students and early-career scholars working on Byzantine, Ottoman, modern Greek or wider Mediterranean topics can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of US$11,500 plus room and board at Loring Hall (weekday meals) and waiver of School fees.
requirements: PhD candidate, or PhD awarded within the last five years
Research that requires the Gennadius Library
Open to all nationalities
Concurrent employment only with the Director's permission
documents: Project description (up to 750 words) referring to the Gennadius Library or its holdings
Transcripts of all postsecondary study for current students (translated into English if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the application materials; awards are announced in mid-March.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading research centre on Greece. Its Gennadius Library specialises in post-classical Greek history and culture.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the ASCSA Submittable form for the Yatrakis Fellowship by 15 January 2027, uploading your CV, project description and transcripts, and arrange two online reference letters.
opportunities.notes: Research trips outside Athens need advance approval. The same page lists other Gennadius fellowships open to all nationalities, such as the Macricostas and Schwarz fellowships.

opportunities.title: Lalor Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career PhD or MD researchers of any nationality in mammalian reproductive biology can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 67,000 one-year postdoctoral fellowship at a nonprofit research institution.
opportunities.description:
The Lalor Foundation's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program supports early-career scientists who want to do research in mammalian reproductive biology, especially work connected to the regulation of fertility. The foundation funds one year of postdoctoral training at a nonprofit research institution, with the possibility of a second, renewal year.

Fellowships usually begin in May or June and last 12 months. Applicants of any citizenship may apply, and the host institution can be in any country, provided it is a nonprofit research organisation that can prove its status.

For African PhD and MD graduates in reproductive biology, endocrinology, veterinary science or related fields, the fellowship offers a well-funded first postdoc, either at an institution abroad or at an eligible nonprofit institute at home.
opportunities.benefits: USD 67,000 per year, covering the fellow's stipend, fringe benefits and institutional overhead (overhead may not exceed 5%). Other costs are not allowed. One renewal year may be granted.
requirements: Any citizenship
PhD or MD level training (or in the final year of the doctorate, with the degree expected in the application year)
No faculty appointment at instructor level or above
The foundation prefers applicants who received their doctorate no more than two years before
Host must be a nonprofit research institution (US hosts need 501(c)(3) status and an IRS 'not a private foundation' letter; non-US hosts must prove nonprofit status)
Research in mammalian reproductive biology related to fertility regulation
documents: Appendix A: project narrative of up to 5 pages including figures and references
Appendix B: four letters (two independent expert reviews, one reference letter and one sponsor/mentor letter), with NIH-style biographical sketches
Appendix C: signed institutional representation form
opportunities.selection_process: A confidential scientific review committee scores each application on three equally weighted criteria: the host institution and its resources, the applicant's merit, and the scientific merit of the proposal. The top 8 to 12 are ranked for the trustees, who make the final awards.
opportunities.about_provider: The Lalor Foundation is a US private foundation that advances research and innovation in reproductive health. It has long supported early-career researchers in mammalian reproductive biology.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Lalor Foundation online application system and use the access code given on the instructions page, then upload the narrative, letters and signed institutional form. Ask referees and the mentor to submit by 1 January so the file is complete well before the 15 January deadline.
opportunities.notes: The FAQ gives the cut-off as midnight EST and the instructions as 11:59 pm EST on 15 January; submit early. Questions go to the foundation's administrator listed on the site.

opportunities.title: Lingnan University Postgraduate Studentships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a good honours bachelor's or a master's can apply by 15 January 2027 for a full-time MPhil or PhD at Lingnan University, Hong Kong, and are normally awarded a monthly studentship of about HK$19,000.
opportunities.description:
Lingnan University in Hong Kong admits full-time MPhil and PhD students through its Direct Admissions route, and full-time admittees are normally awarded a Postgraduate Studentship that pays a monthly stipend. The main round for September 2027 entry runs from 1 September 2026 to 15 January 2027, with two later clearing rounds.

Lingnan is Hong Kong's liberal arts university, and its research degrees span the humanities, social sciences, business and data-related fields. Applicants may apply to a maximum of two programmes in the online admission system.

Non-local students, including Africans, are eligible for the studentship, although they do not receive the Hong Kong government tuition waiver that local students may get. A separate, more generous route is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, which closed for this round on 1 December 2026 applications.
opportunities.benefits: Postgraduate Studentship (2026-27 rates): MPhil HK$19,010 per month; PhD HK$19,280 per month, rising to HK$19,660 after confirmation of candidature. Holders give up to 12 hours a week of teaching or research support. Further support is available for conferences and field trips, and for overseas research visits.

PhD: a master's degree, or a bachelor's with first or second class honours plus at least one year of master's study and evidence of research, or a first-class bachelor's with substantial research achievement
If your degree was not taught in English: TOEFL iBT 79 (tests before 21 January 2026) or the new-scale 4 (tests from 21 January 2026), or IELTS 6.5, taken at a test centre within the last two years
Full-time study for the studentship
Programme-specific requirements may apply

Research proposal and references as required by the programme

2nd clearing round: 1 May to 31 August 2027 (January 2028 intake)
opportunities.about_provider: Lingnan University is a public liberal arts university in Tuen Mun, Hong Kong. Its School of Graduate Studies runs the research postgraduate (MPhil and PhD) programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Lingnan's online admission system, choosing 'Direct Admissions (2027-28)' and up to two programmes, and pay the non-refundable application fee. Apply in the main round by 15 January 2027 for the best chance of a studentship.
opportunities.notes: You cannot transfer an application between the HKPFS route and direct admission. Lingnan advises its own graduates not to apply for its PhD.

opportunities.title: M. H. Wiener Laboratory Annual Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and holders of a master's or doctorate from any university worldwide can apply by 15 January 2027 for up to nine months of archaeological-science research at the Wiener Laboratory in Athens.
opportunities.description:
The M. H. Wiener Annual Fellowship (formerly the Research Associate Appointment) supports short, focused projects in archaeological science at the Malcolm H. Wiener Laboratory of the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA). Projects should relate to the ancient Greek world or neighbouring regions.

The fellowship term is flexible, up to nine months, with the next term beginning in early September 2027. Fellows work with the laboratory's facilities and become associate members of the School.

Applications are welcome from any college or university worldwide and from independent scholars, so African researchers in bioarchaeology, archaeometry, geoarchaeology and related sciences may apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of up to US$7,000 plus waiver of School and Laboratory fees. Room and board are paid by the fellow; the project budget is capped at US$7,000.
requirements: Enrolled in a graduate programme, or holding a master's or doctorate in a relevant field (independent scholars welcome)
Project in archaeological science linked to the Greek world or adjacent regions
Permits or letters from authorities and excavation directors for the material studied
Past recipients of this fellowship or a Wiener Research Fellowship must wait two years
documents: Results of any previous Wiener-funded work
Facilities, equipment and sample numbers needed
One reference letter from a scholar in the field
Statement of expected contributions to the Laboratory and the School
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed for intellectual merit and broader impacts.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading centre for research on Greece. Its Wiener Laboratory specialises in archaeological science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through the ASCSA Wiener Laboratory fellowships form on Submittable by 15 January 2027 and ask your referee to send the letter by the same date. Applications without the required permits may not be considered.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to the Laboratory Director, Dr Panagiotis Karkanas. Successful applicants receive ASCSA associate membership automatically.

opportunities.title: MPIWG First Research Article Fellowship for PhD students from Africa, Asia and Latin America (2027-28)
opportunities.provider: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students enrolled at African, Asian or Latin American institutions who have finished their thesis research in the history of science, technology or medicine or STS can apply for a six-month Berlin fellowship to write their first article.
opportunities.description:
The First Research Article Fellowship at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Berlin helps doctoral students from institutions in Africa, Asia and Latin America turn their thesis research into a first single-authored research article in English. The fellowship lasts six months, from 1 September 2027 to 28 February 2028, and fellows are hosted by one of two departments (AAK or KSCL).

It is aimed at PhD candidates whose research is already complete and who need time, mentoring and a strong scholarly environment to write and submit a publication. Fellows must stay enrolled in their home doctoral programme throughout.

The deadline is 15 January 2027 at 23:59 CET, with decisions expected by 1 April 2027. Because it is reserved for students at institutions in the Global South, it is a rare, targeted opportunity for African doctoral students in history of science, medicine and technology or STS.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend set according to Max Planck Society guidelines for the six months (amount not stated on the call page), plus a research place and mentoring in Berlin.
requirements: Enrolled as a doctoral student at an institution in Africa, Asia or Latin America, and remaining enrolled until the fellowship ends
Thesis research in the history of science, technology or medicine, or STS, already completed
Aim of writing a first single-authored research article in English
Application tied to one MPIWG department (AAK or KSCL)
documents: Cover letter naming the chosen department (AAK or KSCL)
Certificate of enrolment and proof of continued enrolment
Title, abstract and outline of the planned article (maximum 750 words)
One recommendation letter from the supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Applications in English are reviewed by the institute after the deadline; a decision is expected by 1 April 2027. The number of fellowships is not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG) in Berlin is part of the Max Planck Society and a leading international centre for research on the history of science, technology and medicine.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply electronically through the MPIWG recruitment portal linked from the call, uploading all documents in English, and ask your supervisor for the recommendation letter. The programme FAQ pages explain each department's version.
opportunities.notes: Only electronic applications are accepted. Fellows must keep their PhD enrolment active through February 2028.

opportunities.title: Macalester College Financial Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year Regular Decision applicants can be considered for financial aid, with a 22 January priority date for aid materials.

opportunities.title: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science Fellowships (January 2027 round)
opportunities.provider: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral, research and senior scholars in the history of science, technology and medicine whose main residence is outside Germany (for postdoc and research fellowships) can apply for paid research stays in Berlin.
opportunities.description:
The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Berlin runs a fellowship programme for scholars who want to spend a research stay at the institute. Postdoctoral and research fellowships usually last between three and six months, while senior fellowships can run from one to twelve months. Each project must connect to one of the thematic focuses named by the institute's departments and research groups.

The institute accepts applications twice a year, with deadlines on 15 January and 15 September; the next round closes on 15 January 2027. A stipend committee meets after each deadline, and the earliest possible start is about four months later.

The programme is open internationally, and the Lise Meitner research group on 'China's Science Silk Road' especially encourages applicants from the Global South. For African historians of science, medicine and technology, or STS researchers, it is a well-paid way to work with one of the leading institutes in the field.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipends (for starts from 1 October 2026): EUR 3,000 for postdoctoral fellows, EUR 3,600 for research fellows and generally EUR 4,200 for senior fellows. Postdoctoral fellows can receive a health-insurance subsidy of 50% of the premium, up to EUR 100 a month, for a full-tariff policy. No other significant income is allowed during the stipend.
requirements: Postdoctoral fellows: PhD defended by the fellowship start (certificate can follow)
Postdoctoral and research fellowships: main place of residence outside Germany
Senior fellows: PhD obtained more than ten years ago
A project tied to one of the thematic focuses advertised by an MPIWG department or group
Application in English or German
documents: Online application through the MPIWG portal (project description and CV, as requested in the portal)
opportunities.selection_process: A stipend committee meets twice a year and assesses applications only after each deadline (15 January and 15 September). The number of fellowships is limited and not stated.
important_dates: Earliest start: about four months after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (MPIWG) in Berlin is part of the Max Planck Society and one of the world's main centres for research on the history of science, technology and medicine.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose the thematic focus that fits your project, then apply through the application portal linked from the MPIWG fellowship page in English or German before 15 January 2027. Questions go to the institute's career office.
opportunities.notes: The Lise Meitner group's 'China's Science Silk Road' call especially encourages candidates from the Global South.

opportunities.title: Mr. Julia Henriëtte Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund Scholarship – Amsterdam Law School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Dutch applicants with top grades applying to one of four Amsterdam Law School LLM programmes can apply by 15 January 2027 for this single annual scholarship (amount to be announced).
opportunities.description:
The Mr. Julia Henriëtte Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund Scholarship helps one exceptionally talented and motivated non-Dutch student each year to follow a full-time LLM at the University of Amsterdam's Amsterdam Graduate School of Law. Students from both inside and outside the European Economic Area may apply.

The 2027-2028 award is tied to four LLM programmes: International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law and Finance, and International Criminal Law. The amount for 2027-2028 has not yet been announced.

For African law graduates with very strong grades, this is a second chance at funding alongside the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, since one application and motivation letter covers both.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship towards the LLM year; the amount for 2027-2028 is to be announced. One scholarship is awarded per year.
requirements: Non-Dutch nationality and not eligible for Dutch student finance
Applying for a first master's at the UvA
Full-time enrolment in one of four eligible LLM programmes
Grades comparable to a 4.0 US GPA, UK first-class honours or 8.0 on the Dutch scale
Able to meet Dutch visa requirements
documents: Motivation letter of up to 500 words (the same letter covers the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship)
opportunities.selection_process: According to the full scholarship page, the award is decided by lottery among eligible applicants; a shorter UvA summary says selection looks at academic records and motivation. The decision is announced by the end of May.
important_dates: Deadline: 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET (with the LLM application)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Amsterdam is a public research university in the Netherlands. The Amsterdam Law School administers this fund-based scholarship for its English-taught LLM programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible LLM programme, choose the Jaarsma-Adolfs Fund scholarship on the 'Scholarship' tab, and upload one motivation letter on the 'Additional documents' tab. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Apply for both this award and the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship in the same application to double your chances.

opportunities.title: NYU Abu Dhabi Need-Based Financial Aid for International Undergraduates 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students from any country admitted to NYU Abu Dhabi receive financial aid meeting their demonstrated need, which can cover tuition, housing and travel.

opportunities.title: NYU School of Law Global Fellows Program 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Legal scholars, practitioners and recent law PhDs from outside the US can apply by 15 January 2027 for a 2027-2028 research fellowship at NYU Law (mostly self-funded, rare stipends).
opportunities.description:
The Global Fellows Program of NYU School of Law in New York brings legal scholars and practitioners from around the world for a research stay of a full academic year (1 September 2027 to 31 May 2028), the fall term or the spring term. It has four categories: research fellows (tenured or tenure-track academics), practice and government fellows, postdoctoral fellows, and the separately selected Emile Noël and Hauser/Remarque fellows.

Applications for 2027-2028 are open until 15 January 2027. Most fellows pay a programme fee, but a small number of merit-based stipends are available to recent postdoctoral fellows who do not yet hold a tenure-track post.

The programme is open to foreign nationals, so African legal academics, judges, government lawyers and recent PhDs in law can apply for a year of research in one of the world's leading law schools.
opportunities.benefits: Access to NYU Law's research community for a year or semester. Fellows pay a programme fee of US$7,500 a year (US$3,750 a semester), with partial reductions on request. A very limited merit-based postdoctoral stipend of US$70,000 a year (US$35,000 a semester) may be awarded at the committee's discretion.
requirements: Foreign national, or a US/dual citizen teaching, working or studying outside the US
Postdoctoral applicants: all PhD requirements, including the defence, completed before the start; stipend only for PhDs within 4 years of the deadline without a tenure-track post
Proof of English (native speaker, English-taught degree or TOEFL/IELTS)
For J-1 visa sponsorship: proof of US$3,200 a month for living costs
documents: Two recommendation letters emailed by recommenders to law.global@nyu.edu
opportunities.selection_process: A committee selects fellows for outstanding academic records and a demonstrated commitment to research; decisions are made in April 2027.
important_dates: Late applications: may be considered in mid-April if space remains
opportunities.about_provider: NYU School of Law is a leading US law school in New York City, known for its Hauser Global Law School Program, which runs the Global Fellows scheme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the NYU Law graduate application portal, uploading the proposal, statements and publication, and ask two recommenders to email their letters to law.global@nyu.edu by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Apply for a fee reduction or the postdoctoral stipend in the same application if you need funding; most fellows bring their own funding.

opportunities.title: Planning Practice & Research: Special Issue on Rethinking Planning Practice from the Global South
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Planning researchers and practitioners worldwide can send 500-word abstracts by 15 January 2027 for a Global South special issue of Planning Practice & Research.
opportunities.description:
Planning Practice & Research, a Taylor & Francis (Routledge) journal, is preparing a special issue titled 'Rethinking Planning Practice from the Global South: Conflict, Informality and Knowledge Production'. The guest editors are Fanny Esther Berigüete Alcántara (UNAM), Miguel Mayorga Cárdenas (UPC Barcelona) and Yefer Asprilla Lara (Universidad Distrital, Bogotá).

The issue seeks research articles, review articles and practice reviews on how planning works in contexts of conflict and informality, and how knowledge from the Global South can reshape planning theory and practice. Abstracts of up to 500 words are due on 15 January 2027, and invited authors then submit full drafts by 31 May 2027.

This is a publishing opportunity rather than a funded award, but it is directly relevant to African urban planners and researchers working on informal settlements, land and urban conflict.
opportunities.benefits: Possible publication in a peer-reviewed international planning journal special issue. No funding is attached.
requirements: Abstract of up to 500 words in English
Research article, review article or practice review on the special issue theme
Full paper submitted only after invitation by the guest editors
documents: Abstract (max 500 words) with author details and article category
opportunities.selection_process: The guest editors select abstracts and invite full drafts; invited papers still go through peer review and acceptance is not guaranteed.
opportunities.about_provider: Planning Practice & Research is an international peer-reviewed journal published by Taylor & Francis (Routledge) that links planning research and professional practice.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract, author details and article category to the guest editors as described on the call page by 15 January 2027. If invited, submit the full paper through the journal's Manuscript Central.
opportunities.notes: The page heading also mentions 15 July 2027 as a manuscript deadline, but the call text asks invited authors for drafts by 31 May 2027; follow the earlier date.

opportunities.title: Pomona College need-based financial aid for international students (fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year and transfer applicants to Pomona who apply for aid with their admission application.
opportunities.description:
Pomona College, a liberal arts college in Claremont, California, gives need-based financial aid to international students. There is no separate named scholarship: aid is awarded from the college's own funds based on each family's financial need, and it is set at the time of admission.

Admission for international students is need-aware, which means the admission committee takes financial need into account. Students who do not apply for aid when they apply cannot ask for it later, so applicants who need support must apply for aid at the same time as admission.

The remaining deadlines are 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision (the Early Decision I deadline of 15 November has passed). For African students, Pomona's need-based aid can cover a large part of the cost of a US liberal arts degree.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based grant aid from Pomona College, set at admission according to demonstrated financial need; the amount is not re-assessed each year.
requirements: International first-year applicant (or transfer applicant at the time of admission only)
Apply for aid together with the admission application
Admission is need-aware for international students
documents: CSS Profile (Pomona school code 4607), or the Pomona College International Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a burden
Translated copies of prior-prior year tax or income documents
opportunities.selection_process: Aid is calculated on demonstrated need, and financial need is considered by the Admissions Committee when it decides on international applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Pomona College is a highly selective private liberal arts college in Claremont, California, and a founding member of the Claremont Colleges consortium.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Pomona and, by the same deadline, submit the CSS Profile (or Pomona's international aid form) and translated income documents. Admitted students who did not apply for aid cannot appeal for aid later.
opportunities.notes: The CSS Profile opens on 1 October. The deadlines page does not print a year; the January dates apply to the current admission cycle for fall 2027 entry.

opportunities.title: Reading AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Prospective arts and humanities PhD students, including international applicants, who apply to an eligible Reading PhD by 15 January 2027 can be considered for one of three AHRC studentships paying home fees and a GBP 21,805 stipend.
opportunities.description:
The University of Reading offers three AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award studentships a year for PhD study in the arts and humanities, starting in October 2027. The awards are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council through its Doctoral Landscape scheme and administered by Reading's Doctoral and Researcher College.
