Applicants first apply for a place on an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027 and then complete an expression of interest. Departments nominate their strongest candidates to a university panel.

International applicants, including Africans, can win up to 30% of the awards, but the studentship pays fees only at the home rate, so they must find the difference between home and international fees themselves.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fees at the UK/Republic of Ireland rate, a tax-free stipend (2026/27 rate GBP 21,805 a year) and limited research and training funds. Visa costs and the immigration health surcharge are not covered.
requirements: Apply for a place on an eligible arts and humanities PhD programme at Reading by 15 January 2027
Full-time or part-time study, not by distance learning
Not already a Reading PhD student
International applicants must pay the difference between home and international fees (at least GBP 16,512 a year full-time)
documents: Expression of interest form for the studentship
Revised research proposal if invited (by 1 March 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: Departments review applicants and nominate candidates to a university panel, which judges academic excellence and readiness for research, the quality of the proposal and the supervision arrangements. Nominated applicants are asked to revise their proposal by 1 March 2027.
important_dates: Revised proposals from nominees: by 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university. Its Doctoral and Researcher College manages doctoral funding, including UKRI-funded studentships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027, then complete the studentship expression of interest form linked from the funding page. Discuss your proposal with a potential supervisor first.
opportunities.notes: Only three awards are made each year. International applicants should plan how they will cover the fee difference before applying.

opportunities.title: Rider University First-Year Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants for 2027 entry who apply to Rider University by 15 January 2027 with at least a 2.7 GPA are automatically considered for merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Rider University, a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, awards merit scholarships to first-year students entering in Spring 2027, Fall 2027 or Spring 2028. The awards are given automatically on admission, with no separate application, and can be renewed for up to four years.

Rider is test-optional and considers students for most merit awards without SAT or ACT scores. To be considered for the merit scholarships, students should submit their admission application by 15 January.

The official pages do not describe a separate scholarship just for international students, but they also set no citizenship condition on the merit awards, so international applicants who meet the grade threshold are considered as part of admission. African applicants should confirm with Rider's international admissions office.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 per year, renewable for up to four years. Smaller awards include a USD 1,000-a-year Bronc Visit Award for eligible campus visitors and subject awards such as USD 2,000 a year in accounting and up to USD 5,000 a year in teacher education.
requirements: Admissible as a full-time first-year student
Minimum unweighted cumulative GPA of 2.7 on a 4.0 scale
Audition where the programme requires one
Test-optional: SAT/ACT not needed for most merit awards
Keep a 2.0 cumulative GPA to renew
documents: Audition materials for performing arts programmes
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted first-year students are automatically reviewed for merit awards based on their academic record; no separate scholarship application is required.
important_dates: Musical Theatre and Acting applicants: by 15 November
Application for merit consideration: by 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Rider University is a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, offering undergraduate and graduate programmes in business, education, arts and sciences, and the performing arts.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission through Rider's international admissions process by 15 January 2027; scholarship decisions arrive with the admission offer. Contact Rider One Stop (onestop@rider.edu) with aid questions.
opportunities.notes: The New Jersey Tuition Guarantee applies only to New Jersey residents. Need-based aid at Rider uses the FAFSA, which is generally for US citizens.

opportunities.title: Schwarz Fellowship for Research on Music 2027-28 (Gennadius Library)
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD, of any nationality, researching music; apply by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Schwarz Fellowship supports research on music, including Greek and Byzantine musical traditions, carried out with the collections of the Gennadius Library at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA).

The award supports research in Athens during the 2027-28 academic year, and fellows are expected to make full use of the library's rare books, archives and open-stack collections.

The ASCSA states that the fellowship is open to all nationalities, so African doctoral students and early-career researchers working on Greek, Byzantine, Ottoman or Mediterranean topics can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of US$11,500 for the academic year, as listed on the ASCSA fellowships page.
requirements: Eligible career stage: career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD
Research that requires the Gennadius Library collections
Open to all nationalities
documents: Online application on the ASCSA Submittable portal
Reference letters as requested on the form
opportunities.selection_process: A School committee reviews the applications; awards are announced in the spring.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading research centre on Greece. Its Gennadius Library holds more than 150,000 titles on Greece from antiquity to the present.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the fellowship form on the ASCSA Submittable portal before the deadline, uploading your CV and project description and arranging the requested references.
opportunities.notes: Application form: https://ascsa.submittable.com/submit/189405/schwarz-fellowship-at-the-gennadius-library-for-research-on-music

opportunities.title: Smith College Need-Based Financial Aid for International First-Year Students (Fall 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens applying as first-year (or transfer) students for September 2027 can receive need-based aid that meets their full documented need, but only if they apply for aid together with their admission application and by the aid deadlines.
opportunities.description:
Smith College, a private liberal arts college for women in Northampton, Massachusetts, offers need-based financial aid to international students who are not US citizens. Aid for the September 2027 entry is awarded alongside the admission decision, and for admitted students who applied for aid on time the college commits to covering their full documented financial need with grants rather than loans.

The main award is the Smith Grant, which is sized from the family's assessed ability to pay against the full cost of attendance (tuition, housing, food, fees, insurance, books, travel and personal costs). The college adjusts the grant over the years so that the family's expected contribution stays broadly stable. International students who receive need-based aid also get a grant covering the college health insurance.

The programme matters for African applicants because Smith is one of a small group of US colleges that meet full need for international students, which can make a degree costing over USD 100,000 a year affordable. The pool is very competitive, and the college states that the level of support varies widely between students. The timing rule is strict: an international student who does not ask for aid before being admitted can never receive institutional aid at Smith later.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based Smith Grant that, together with any outside support, meets 100% of the documented need of admitted students who applied for aid by the deadlines; undergraduate institutional packages contain no loans. Recipients also receive a health grant that covers the college health insurance. For reference, the published 2026-27 cost of attendance is: tuition USD 70,460; food and housing USD 24,520; student activities fee USD 308; health insurance USD 4,030; books USD 800; international transport (average) USD 1,000; personal costs USD 1,910.
requirements: Not a US citizen (international applicant)
Applying for first-year (or transfer) entry in September 2027
Must apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission and by the aid deadlines; no institutional aid is ever offered to international students who did not apply before admission

English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo) unless English is the first language, secondary school was taught in English, the student had two years of US English-medium schooling, or holds an IB Diploma or A-levels taught in English
SAT/ACT scores are optional
Women's college: applicants apply under Smith's admission policy for women
documents: Secondary school report with official transcript
Midyear report (by 15 February for Regular Decision)
CSS Profile 2027-28 (Smith code 3762; fee waivers available)
Translated and signed 2025 parent tax return, or the International Parent Non-Filer form plus a translated employer statement of income
Optional standardised test scores and English test results where required
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is holistic, looking at the student's academic record, recommendations, writing and activities. Financial aid staff then review the CSS Profile and income documents using federal and institutional methods to work out the family contribution and the student's need against the cost of attendance. Admission of international applicants is competitive and aid amounts differ widely between students.
important_dates: Early Decision I application and CSS Profile: 15 November 2026
Early Decision II application: 5 January 2027 (aid forms 6 January 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Smith College is a private women's liberal arts college in Northampton, Massachusetts, USA. It admits first-year and transfer students and awards both need-based aid and merit awards, with merit decided only at the time of admission.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or Coalition on Scoir (no application fee) and mark that you are applying for aid. Complete the 2027-28 CSS Profile on the College Board site and upload translated tax or income documents through IDOC; Smith then emails instructions for its Net Partner aid portal. Meet the deadline for your chosen round (Early Decision I, Early Decision II or Regular Decision).
opportunities.notes: Early Decision is binding, but a student can be released if the aid offered makes attendance impossible. Outside scholarships first reduce the work-study portion and then the Smith Grant; state or federal grants reduce the Smith Grant dollar for dollar. International students may not take off-campus jobs. Contact Student Financial Services at sfs@smith.edu or +1 413-585-2530.

opportunities.title: South Coast Doctoral Training Partnership (ESRC) PhD Studentships 2027/28
opportunities.provider: South Coast Doctoral Training Partnership (Universities of Brighton, Chichester, Portsmouth and Southampton)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with a first or upper-second honours degree (or equivalent) can apply for ESRC-funded social science PhD studentships; non-UK residents can take up to 30% of the places.
opportunities.description:
The South Coast Doctoral Training Partnership (SCDTP) is an ESRC-funded consortium of the Universities of Brighton, Chichester, Portsmouth and Southampton. It is now taking applications for social science doctoral studentships starting in 2027/28, offered as 1+3.5 (master's plus PhD), +3.5 and +4.5 awards.

The SCDTP deadline is 16:00 GMT on 15 January 2027. Applicants must also apply to their host university, and some host deadlines are earlier (Brighton's is 3 January). The awards committee meets in March 2027 and results are expected by mid-April.

Both UK and international applicants may apply, with non-UK residents capped at 30% of the partnership's allocation. For African graduates in the social sciences, this is a fully funded route to a UK PhD, though travel, visa and health-surcharge costs are not covered.
opportunities.benefits: Programme fees plus a tax-free maintenance grant of GBP 21,805 a year (2026/27 UKRI rate) and access to a Research Training Support Grant. Travel to the UK, visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge are not covered.
requirements: First or upper-second class honours degree from a UK university, or an equivalent non-UK qualification
An offer or application at one of the four partner universities
Non-UK residents are limited to 30% of the overall allocation
documents: Research proposal (750 words for 1+3.5 awards, 1,500 words for +3.5 awards)
opportunities.selection_process: The SCDTP committee assesses academic potential, the proposed research, and feasibility, aptitude and fit with the supervisory team. It meets in March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The SCDTP is one of the UK Economic and Social Research Council's doctoral training partnerships, linking four universities on England's south coast to train social science researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your chosen partner university's PhD programme and also complete the SCDTP funding form on the SurveyMonkey Apply portal by 15 January 2027 (or earlier if your host university sets an earlier date). Questions go to scdtp@soton.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying non-EU/EEA applicants who apply to a Stockholm University master's by 15 January 2027 and are admitted can receive a full tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Stockholm University's Scholarship Scheme pays the full tuition fee for selected fee-paying students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are admitted to a master's programme starting in autumn 2027. It does not cover living costs.

To be considered, students must apply in the first, international admission round on universityadmissions.se, which closes on 15 January 2027. After the selection results on 1 April, eligible admitted students receive an electronic scholarship application form in their University Admissions account.

Awards are based on academic merit, and priority goes to students who ranked Stockholm University as their first choice, which is a useful tip for African applicants choosing between Swedish universities.
opportunities.benefits: Covers the whole tuition fee for the master's programme. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who must pay tuition fees
Admitted to a master's programme in the first (international) admission round for autumn 2027
Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or equivalent
English equivalent to Swedish upper-secondary English 6/B
Stockholm University listed as first choice gives priority
documents: Application on universityadmissions.se with degree certificates, transcripts and English proof
Application fee paid and documents uploaded by 1 February 2027
Scholarship form sent after admission results
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on academic merit among admitted fee-paying students, with priority for those who ranked Stockholm University first.
important_dates: Scholarship results: by end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Stockholm University is one of Sweden's largest universities, with a broad range of English-taught master's programmes in the sciences, humanities, social sciences and law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and rank Stockholm University first. Pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February; if admitted and eligible, complete the scholarship form that appears in your account.
opportunities.notes: Business programmes may require GMAT or GRE. Also look at the Swedish Institute scholarships, which are limited to citizens of selected countries.

opportunities.title: Swedish Institute Pioneering Women in STEM Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women from Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda or South Africa with work and leadership experience can apply for fully funded STEM master's in Sweden (programmes by 15 January 2027, scholarship 9-25 February 2027).
opportunities.description:
The Swedish Institute's Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship pays for women from selected countries in Africa and Asia to take a one- or two-year English-taught master's in science, technology, engineering or mathematics in Sweden, starting in autumn 2027. It covers full tuition, a monthly living allowance and a travel grant.

The 2027 cycle has two steps. First, applicants apply to eligible master's programmes through University Admissions in Sweden by 15 January 2027. Then, between 9 and 25 February 2027, they apply for the scholarship in the SI portal. Each university publishes its own list of eligible programmes; for example, Karlstad University lists ecology and conservation biology, computer science, cybersecurity and data-driven mechanical engineering.

In Africa, women who are citizens of Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda or South Africa can apply. The scheme looks for applicants with documented work and leadership experience who want to become leaders in STEM.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition paid by SI directly to the university each semester, a living allowance of SEK 12,000 per month, a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (not for those already in Sweden), and membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals and then the Sweden Alumni Network. Insurance, family grants and the University Admissions application fee are not covered.
requirements: Woman and citizen of an eligible country (in Africa: Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda or South Africa; others are Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam)
Admitted to an eligible English-taught STEM master's by the admission results (reserve places do not count)
Liable to pay tuition in Sweden and paid the University Admissions fee on time
Documented work experience (SI's last cycle required at least 3,000 hours) and leadership experience, certified on SI templates
No previous SI study scholarship, no Swedish degree, and less than two years' residence in Sweden
Not an EU/EEA or Swedish citizen and no Swedish residence permit
documents: University Admissions application to eligible programmes
SI scholarship application in the SI portal
Certificates of work and leadership experience on SI template forms
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants must first be admitted to an eligible programme. SI then assesses the scholarship applications and announces results on 23 April 2027.
important_dates: Apply to master's programmes via University Admissions: 15 October 2026 to 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Swedish Institute (SI) is a Swedish public agency that promotes interest and trust in Sweden abroad. It funds master's scholarships for future leaders from selected countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to one or more eligible STEM master's programmes through universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and pay the fee. Then, between 9 and 25 February 2027, submit the scholarship application in the SI scholarship portal (apply-scholarships.si.se) with your work and leadership certificates.
opportunities.notes: Eligible programmes differ by university (Gothenburg lists 12, Karlstad 4, Örebro 1), so check each university's list. Dual citizens must choose one citizenship for one application.

opportunities.title: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Professionals from 12 African countries with work and leadership experience can apply (programmes by 15 January 2027, scholarship 9-25 February 2027).
opportunities.description:
The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP) fund professionals from 34 countries to take a master's degree in Sweden starting in autumn 2027. The scholarship pays full tuition, a monthly living allowance and a travel grant, and connects scholars to SI's network of global professionals.

Applicants first apply to eligible master's programmes through University Admissions by 15 January 2027, and then submit the SI scholarship application between 9 and 25 February 2027. University Admissions results come on 26 March 2027 and SI results on 23 April 2027.

Twelve African countries are on the list: Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia. The scheme looks for people with work and leadership experience who want to contribute to sustainable development at home.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition, SEK 12,000 per month living allowance and a travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for some Eastern European countries), plus membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals.
requirements: Citizen of an eligible country (in Africa: Egypt, Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia)
Admitted to a master's programme that is eligible for SISGP
Liable to pay tuition in Sweden
Documented work experience and leadership experience
documents: University Admissions application to eligible programmes
SI scholarship application in the SI portal
Work and leadership experience certificates on SI templates
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants must be admitted to an eligible programme; SI then assesses scholarship applications and announces results on 23 April 2027.
important_dates: Apply to master's programmes via University Admissions: 15 October 2026 to 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Swedish Institute (SI) is a Swedish public agency that promotes interest and trust in Sweden abroad. Its SISGP programme funds master's study for future global leaders from selected countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for eligible master's programmes at universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027. Then submit your SISGP application in the SI scholarship portal (apply-scholarships.si.se) between 9 and 25 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Ghana is not on the eligible list. Check each Swedish university's list of SISGP-eligible programmes.

opportunities.title: Trinity College (Connecticut) Full-Need Financial Aid for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Admitted international students have their full demonstrated need met; Regular Decision applicants apply and submit the CSS Profile by 15 January.

opportunities.title: Tulane University Merit Scholarships for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens admitted to Tulane are considered for merit awards from $1,000 up to full tuition, including Dean's Honor, Paul Tulane and Stamps scholarships.

opportunities.title: UNDP Washington Representation Office Internships (Spring 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students in communications or development fields from any country can apply for a 3-6 month stipended internship at UNDP's Washington office; spring deadline 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The UNDP Washington Representation Office runs a stipended internship scheme for graduate students in 2027, with two profiles: a General Intern and a Communications and Outreach Intern. Interns are placed in the office in Washington, DC, which handles UNDP's relations with the US Congress, the State Department and the World Bank Group.

There are two intakes. The spring term runs from March to 15 June 2027 and the fall term from September to 15 December 2027; there is no summer intake. An internship lasts at least three consecutive months and at most six, with a minimum of three days (24 hours) of work per week.

UNDP says its interns are chosen from around the world and the page sets no nationality limit, so African graduate students in communications or development-related fields can apply. It is a practical way to see how a UN development agency works with Washington's policy and finance institutions.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend whose amount depends on the duty location (not stated on the page) and is pro-rated for part-time interns. Interns pay all other costs themselves, including travel, visas, accommodation and health insurance.
requirements: Enrolled in a graduate programme in communications or a development field such as economics, public or business administration or environmental studies
Will return to studies after the internship
Available for at least three consecutive months, at least three days (24 hours) a week
Fluent written and spoken English
Commitment to the values of the UN Charter
Experience on Capitol Hill or in the field is an advantage
documents: One reference letter, sent by the applicant
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened by the Washington office and only short-listed candidates are contacted.
important_dates: Spring 2027 deadline: 15 January 2027, 11:59 pm US Eastern time
opportunities.about_provider: The United Nations Development Programme is the UN's main development agency, working in about 170 countries on poverty, governance and climate. Its Washington Representation Office is the liaison between UNDP and US government bodies and the Washington-based international financial institutions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the cover letter, CV, signed application form and reference letter to undp.washington@undp.org and Ebru.Kuran@undp.org. Use the subject line 'Internship Application – Spring Internship – [Full Name]' (or Fall for the later intake).
opportunities.notes: Interns must arrange their own visa and health insurance. Contact: UNDP.Washington@UNDP.org, +1 202 524 4998.

opportunities.title: Umea University Scholarship for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA citizens who apply by 15 January 2027 to an English-taught Umeå University programme as first priority can register for a full or partial tuition waiver.
opportunities.description:
Umeå University in northern Sweden offers tuition fee waivers to talented students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who start an English-taught bachelor's or master's programme in autumn 2027. Selected students receive a full or partial waiver of their tuition fee.

The process has several steps. Applicants must put an Umeå programme as priority 1 in the first international round on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and pay the application fee by 1 February. Eligible applicants then receive a personal email invitation in early February and must register their interest by 5 March 2027.

African applicants from any country outside the EU/EEA can take part, so this is worth planning for early.
opportunities.benefits: A full or partial waiver of the programme tuition fee. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland
Application to a full English-taught bachelor's or master's programme in the first international round
Umeå programme ranked as priority 1 on universityadmissions.se
Application fee paid by 1 February 2027 (or fee-exempt but tuition-paying)
Not open to the double-degree Master's in Sustainability Reporting and Financial Analysis
documents: Scholarship interest registration form (sent by email invitation)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculty committees choose recipients on academic merit and other information given in the registration form. Results are emailed in late April 2027.
important_dates: Programme application with Umeå as priority 1: 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Umeå University is a comprehensive Swedish university founded in 1965, with about 37,000 students and strong programmes in medicine, design, social sciences and IT.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 with an Umeå programme as your first priority and pay the fee by 1 February. Watch for the invitation email and complete the scholarship registration form by 5 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: Only priority-1 applicants receive the invitation, and scholarships cannot be deferred. Contact: tuitionfees@umu.se.

opportunities.title: Universite Laval Citizens of the World Scholarship, Commitment Component 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying to a research master's or doctorate at Université Laval for 2027 can apply by 15 January 2027 for CAD 20,000-30,000 awards for civic engagement.
opportunities.description:
The Citizens of the World Scholarship, Commitment component (award 3423G) is offered by Université Laval in Quebec City to international students starting a research master's or a doctorate. It rewards candidates who stand out for civic engagement, leadership and innovation, and is funded by the university's Fonds citoyennes et citoyens du monde.

The current call, published for winter 2027, closes on 15 January 2027 and covers students admitted for the winter, summer or fall 2027 terms. Several awards are given: CAD 20,000 for a research master's and CAD 30,000 for a doctorate, paid in instalments of CAD 5,000 per term.

No nationality is excluded, so African students with a record of community or civic involvement who are applying to a thesis-based programme at Laval (which teaches in French) are strong candidates.
opportunities.benefits: Research master's: CAD 20,000 (CAD 5,000 per term for up to four terms). Doctorate: CAD 30,000 (CAD 5,000 per term for up to six terms). Several awards are available.
requirements: International student
New admission application to Université Laval for winter, summer or fall 2027 in a research master's (with thesis) or a doctorate, processed and with fees paid
Taught master's, bachelor's, certificates and postdocs are not eligible
Full-time enrolment throughout and study in Canada with a valid study permit
Follow-up with a regulated immigration consultant (CRIEE) for a first study permit application
documents: Online application form (documents sent by email are not accepted)
Official transcript as one PDF showing the cumulative average
One referee (professor, employer or supervisor) who completes their own online section
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on involvement and engagement, the global citizenship dimension, leadership, academic record and quality of presentation. Results are sent by email in early March 2027, and the admission offer must be accepted within 15 days of the scholarship offer.
opportunities.about_provider: Université Laval is a large French-language public university in Quebec City, Canada. Its Bureau des bourses et de l'aide financière (BBAF) runs its scholarship directory.
opportunities.how_to_apply: After applying for admission to a research master's or doctorate at Laval, complete the online scholarship form in the BBAF directory and invite your referee before 15 January 2027. Questions go to engagement@bbaf.ulaval.ca or 1 877 785-2825.
opportunities.notes: An English version of the award sheet is linked from the official page. Laval programmes are mainly taught in French.

opportunities.title: University of Copenhagen Danish Government Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants admitted to a University of Copenhagen master's who apply by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for a full tuition waiver plus living allowance.
opportunities.description:
The University of Copenhagen awards a limited number of Danish Government Scholarships each year to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its MA and MSc programmes. The scholarships are funded by the Danish state and are given purely on academic merit; financial need is not considered.

There is no separate application. Every eligible non-EU/EEA applicant to a master's starting in September 2027 is considered automatically, provided they apply in the round that closes on 15 January 2027.

For African students, this is one of the most generous master's awards in the Nordic countries, covering both tuition and basic living costs for the whole two-year degree.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver and basic living costs for 22 months (DKK 11,225 per month at the 2026 level).
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland
Admitted to a University of Copenhagen MA or MSc programme
Granted a time-limited Danish residence permit for study
Not entitled to Danish citizen rights or the Danish SU state grant
Strong academic record (merit-based)
documents: Regular master's application documents (no separate scholarship application)
Payment of the DKK 1,120 application fee
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic criteria during the admission assessment. Offers must be accepted by the stated deadline or they are withdrawn.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1479, the University of Copenhagen is Denmark's oldest and largest university and one of the leading research universities in Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pay the application fee, then apply for your chosen master's through the University of Copenhagen application portal by 15 January 2027. Eligible applicants are considered automatically and must accept any scholarship offer by the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Estimated living costs are €1,280-1,800 a month; the allowance covers basic costs only.

opportunities.title: University of South Florida Green and Gold International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants for Summer or Fall 2027 who complete their USF application by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for Green and Gold tuition waivers worth up to USD 11,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The University of South Florida (USF), a large public research university in Tampa, Florida, gives Green and Gold tuition waivers to international first-year students it admits for Summer or Fall 2027. These are merit awards that reduce tuition each year for up to four years.

There is no separate scholarship form. Every international first-year applicant who submits a complete application by the scholarship consideration date is automatically reviewed, using the same academic record that the admissions team uses. The number of awards is limited, so applying early and completely matters.

For African school leavers who want a US bachelor's degree, the waivers can cut the cost of an international tuition bill substantially, but they do not cover the full cost of study, so applicants should plan for the remaining tuition, housing and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: Green and Gold Presidential Waiver of about USD 44,000 in total (up to USD 11,000 a year); Directors Waiver of about USD 36,000 (up to USD 9,000 a year); Scholars Waiver of about USD 20,000 (up to USD 5,000 a year). These cannot be combined with USF's out-of-state merit tuition waivers.
requirements: International applicant for first-year (freshman) entry in Summer or Fall 2027
Complete application, including test scores, transcripts and fee, by 15 January 2027

For applicants whose first language is not English: SAT Reading and Writing 490+, or ACT English 17+ and Reading 19+, or CLT Verbal Reasoning and Writing 38+ (TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo are not accepted in place of these for this purpose)
Awards are based on the academic record used for admission
documents: USF online application or Common App
STARS self-reported record or official secondary school transcripts
Official SAT, ACT or CLT scores sent by the testing agency (SAT code 5828, ACT code 0761)
opportunities.selection_process: All admitted international first-year students who completed their file on time are considered automatically. Awards are made on academic merit from the admission file, and numbers are limited.
important_dates: Take SAT/ACT before December so scores arrive in time for Fall decisions
Award notice: by post, also visible in the Student Self-Service portal
opportunities.about_provider: The University of South Florida is a public research university based in Tampa, Florida, with campuses in St. Petersburg and Sarasota-Manatee. Its Office of Admissions handles international first-year applications and merit awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for Summer or Fall 2027 through the USF application or the Common App, pay the USD 30 fee, and submit your transcripts and test scores before 15 January 2027. No extra scholarship form is needed; track your file and any award in the USF applicant and Self-Service portals.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to USF International Admissions (international@usf.edu). Because English is assessed through SAT, ACT or CLT section scores, plan your test dates early.

opportunities.title: Wesleyan University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants who apply for aid with admission get 100% of demonstrated need met; African citizens are automatically considered for about 10 full-cost African Scholars awards; Regular Decision 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Wesleyan University, a private liberal arts university in Middletown, Connecticut, promises to meet 100% of the demonstrated financial need of every student it admits, including international students. For the 2027-28 year, international first-year applicants apply for aid at the same time as they apply for admission.

The aid decision is tied to the admission round: Early Decision I closes on 15 November, Early Decision II on 1 January and Regular Decision on 15 January. Students must request aid when they apply, because eligibility is fixed at that point.

Of special interest to African applicants is the Wesleyan African Scholars Program. Citizens or permanent residents of an African country who need aid and have not studied full time at a college before are considered automatically, with no extra form. The award covers the full cost of attendance for four years, and about ten are given each year.
opportunities.benefits: Aid that meets 100% of each admitted student's demonstrated need. Through the African Scholars Program, about 10 African students a year receive the full cost of attendance for four years.
requirements: Apply for first-year admission through the Common App or Coalition/Scoir
Request financial aid at the time of applying (aid is not available later to those who did not apply)
For the African Scholars Program: citizen or permanent resident of an African country, not a US citizen or permanent resident
For the African Scholars Program: demonstrated financial need and no previous full-time college enrolment
documents: International Student Financial Aid Application (ISFAA), emailed to internationalaid@wesleyan.edu, if the CSS Profile cannot be submitted
opportunities.selection_process: Admission decisions come first; aid packages are built from the CSS Profile or ISFAA to meet demonstrated need. African Scholars are chosen automatically from admitted African applicants who need aid.
opportunities.about_provider: Wesleyan University is a private liberal arts university in Middletown, Connecticut, USA. Its Financial Aid Office (860-685-2800, finaid@wesleyan.edu) runs need-based aid for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the admission application and the CSS Profile (or the ISFAA by email) by the deadline of your admission round. Track documents and decisions in the WesCheck portal.
opportunities.notes: There is no separate application for the African Scholars Program. The Freeman Asian Scholarship on the same page is only for Asian countries.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Postgraduate Research Scholarships for funded PhD projects (2027 intakes)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a bachelor's and master's (or equivalent) and an English test who apply to a listed XJTLU PhD project.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) in Suzhou, China, funds full-time PhD students through its Postgraduate Research Scholarships. Students join a listed research project, study for three years, and receive a University of Liverpool PhD degree after a final review by Liverpool.

There are three levels of award: a full scholarship (tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend), a fees-only scholarship, and a partial award that cuts tuition by up to half. Funded projects are advertised across areas such as AI and advanced technology, life and natural sciences, design and semiconductors, and each stays open until filled.

For 2027 entry, applications for existing funded projects close on 15 January 2027 (start 1 June 2027) and 30 April 2027 (start 1 September 2027). The scheme sets no nationality limit, so African master's graduates can compete for a funded PhD with a UK degree while living in China.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000 over three years plus a stipend of RMB 5,000 per month for three years (RMB 180,000 in total); holders must take a teaching or research assistant role. Fees-only scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000. Partial scholarship: up to 50% off tuition for three years (worth RMB 148,500). Paid TA/RA roles may also be offered to other award holders.
requirements: Full-time PhD study at XJTLU in Suzhou
Bachelor's and master's degree (or enrolment statement if not yet completed)
English test certificate (IELTS or equivalent)
Application to a specific advertised funded project, ideally after contacting the supervisor
documents: Two references, at least one academic, on letterhead with a handwritten signature
Master's dissertation (Business, Humanities and Social Sciences applicants)
opportunities.selection_process: XJTLU reviews the application first and the University of Liverpool makes the final decision. Merit-based awards are judged on academic excellence, research potential, research experience and achievements.
important_dates: Self-funded / merit scholarship round 2: 15 January 2027 (start 1 September 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University is a joint-venture university in Suzhou, China, founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool. Its PhD degrees are awarded by the University of Liverpool.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a funded project on the scholarships page and contact the supervisor, then apply through XJTLU's online 'Apply Now' form, uploading the proposal, transcripts, English test and references (each file under 2 MB, in English or with certified translations). Questions go to doctoralstudies@xjtlu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: Projects close once filled, so apply early. Minimum English scores are on XJTLU's PhD entry requirements page.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-IAEA School on Nuclear Security (Apr 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: School in Trieste, 12 to 22 April 2027, for early-career professionals from developing countries with one to three years of experience who first complete eight IAEA e-learning modules; no fee and limited grants.
opportunities.description:
The Joint ICTP-IAEA School on Nuclear Security is a two-week training school held from 12 to 22 April 2027 at the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy, in the Kastler Lecture Hall of the Adriatico Guest House. It is run with the International Atomic Energy Agency, which co-sponsors it.

The school is aimed at early-career professionals from developing countries, ideally with one to three years of experience in an institution at home that deals with nuclear security. People with a scientific or technical background are especially encouraged.

There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants is available, with priority for participants from developing countries, which makes it a strong option for African professionals in regulators, research reactors, customs, border or radiation-protection agencies.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants (amounts not stated) is available, with priority for participants from developing countries.
requirements: Early-career professional, ideally 1-3 years of experience at a relevant institution in the home country
Preferably a scientific or technical background
Priority for applicants from developing countries
Must first complete at least 8 of the 22 IAEA nuclear security e-learning modules
documents: Online application on the ICTP e-applications portal
Proof of completion of at least 8 IAEA nuclear security e-learning modules
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers (Muzna Assi of the IAEA and Sandro Scandolo of ICTP) select participants from the online applications; grants go first to candidates from developing countries.
opportunities.about_provider: ICTP is an international research centre in Trieste, governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and the Government of Italy, that supports science in developing countries. The IAEA is the UN-linked agency for the peaceful use of nuclear technology and nuclear security.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the required IAEA e-learning modules, then apply online at https://e-applications.ictp.it/applicant/login/4346 before 16 January 2027. Questions go to smr4346@ictp.it.
opportunities.notes: The e-learning modules are free on the IAEA learning platform; finish them early, since they are a prerequisite.

opportunities.title: CEGA Visiting Fellowship for African Researchers 2027/2028
opportunities.provider: Center for Effective Global Action (UC Berkeley)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science researchers and practitioners from East and West Africa with at least a master's can apply by 17 January 2027 for a 16-week CEGA impact-evaluation fellowship at Berkeley or online.
opportunities.description:
The Center for Effective Global Action (CEGA) at the University of California, Berkeley runs a 16-week Visiting Fellowship that trains East and West African researchers and practitioners in impact evaluation. The 2027-2028 cohort can join in Fall 2027 (August to December) or Spring 2028 (January to May), either as Resident fellows at Berkeley or as Non-Resident fellows working online.

There are two tracks: a Practitioner track (about 7 places) for staff of NGOs, think tanks and ministries, and an Academic track (about 4 places) for doctoral students and university or research staff. Fellows build skills in rigorous evaluation, research design and evidence use, and are expected to return to an institution in East or West Africa.

Alumni can later compete for CEGA's catalyst, pilot and research grants, so the fellowship is also an entry point into a wider research network on development economics.
opportunities.benefits: Resident fellows: round-trip flights, accommodation, meals, visa fees, health insurance and a stipend. Non-Resident fellows: a stipend for internet and data costs. No salary or family support is provided.
requirements: National of an East or West African country (not open to Southern, Central or North Africa)
Completed at least secondary school in Africa
At least a master's degree, or enrolled in a PhD, or PhD completed within the last 8 years, in a social science
Fluent English
Plan to return to an institution in East or West Africa
Resident track only: national of a J-1-eligible country (Djibouti, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Rwanda, Seychelles, Uganda)
Practitioner track: works for an NGO, think tank or ministry; Academic track: doctoral student or university/research staff
Employer leave or support for 40 h/week (Resident) or 15-20 h/week (Non-Resident) for four months
documents: Policy statement (Practitioner) or research proposal (Academic), max 2 pages
Letter from employer approving leave or time commitment
opportunities.selection_process: CEGA reviews applications by track, looking at academic and professional background, quantitative preparation, the policy statement or research proposal, and the applicant's plans to apply evaluation skills in East or West Africa.
opportunities.about_provider: CEGA is a research centre at UC Berkeley that connects researchers and policymakers to generate rigorous evidence on poverty and development. Its African fellowship programme builds evaluation capacity among researchers from the region.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through CEGA's Submittable portal (2027-28 CEGA Visiting Fellowship). Prepare the statements, CV and employer letter in advance, and register for the 2 December webinar from the call page. Questions go to global-networks-cega@berkeley.edu.
opportunities.notes: Non-Resident priority countries include Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Togo, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The full call is also available as a PDF from the CEGA page.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus European Master in Law, Data and Artificial Intelligence (EMILDAI)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law and computing graduates of any nationality can apply by 17 January 2027 for EMILDAI Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
EMILDAI, the Erasmus Mundus European Master in Law, Data and Artificial Intelligence, is coordinated by Dublin City University with partner universities across Europe; Erasmus University Rotterdam and FGV in Rio de Janeiro have joined the consortium. The 2027-2029 edition starts on 1 September 2027 at DCU.

The master's trains lawyers and computer scientists together on the legal and ethical regulation of data and AI, with study tracks that combine different partner universities. The first application round, the only one with scholarships, closes on 17 January 2027; a second, self-funded round runs from 21 March to 28 May 2027.

About 25 students are selected per intake and no more than 10% can share a nationality, so African law and computing graduates have a fair chance at full and partial scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: Full and partial Erasmus Mundus scholarships (amounts on the programme's scholarships page). No application fee. Self-funded offer holders pay a EUR 500 deposit.
requirements: Computing track: at least a 2.2 honours degree in computer science or a related field
Law track: at least a 2.1 honours degree in law or a law-heavy degree
English at C1 (IELTS 6.5 or equivalent) or a previous degree taught in English
Tracks A and B also need French or Spanish at C1
documents: Diplomas and transcripts (certified English translations if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are scored on academic merit (70%), professional experience (20%) and personal statement (10%); about 25 students are selected, with round 1 results in March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Dublin City University in Ireland coordinates the EMILDAI consortium of European and international universities in law and computing.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the DCU online application portal linked from the EMILDAI how-to-apply page before 17 January 2027, choosing your study track.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus MITRA - International Master in Transnational Migrations
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science and humanities graduates fluent in French and English can apply by 17 January 2027 for MITRA Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400 a month.
opportunities.description:
MITRA, the International Master in Transnational Migrations, is an Erasmus Mundus programme coordinated by the Université de Lille in France. Its consortium includes universities in Granada, the Aegean, Wrocław, Cluj (Babeș-Bolyai), Brussels, Cork, Rio de Janeiro, Istanbul (Galatasaray), Budapest (Károli Gáspár) and Université Cheikh Anta Diop in Dakar.

The programme is bilingual, taught in French and English, and starts in September 2027. Applications opened on 16 October 2026 and close on 17 January 2027 at midnight Paris time; scholarship applications are made inside the same master's application.

With a Senegalese partner and a focus on migration, MITRA is especially relevant to African social science graduates who are comfortable in both French and English.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 a month for 24 months (limited number). Other University of Lille mobility scholarships are also listed on the programme site.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in the social sciences and/or humanities
French and English each at B2 to C2 level
Scholarship eligibility follows the Erasmus Mundus rules
opportunities.selection_process: Administrative check and pre-selection, Zoom interviews in February 2027, then an admission jury in March 2027; criteria are academic background, motivation, research or internship project and language level. Results in April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Université de Lille is a large public university in northern France that coordinates the MITRA consortium of European, African and Latin American universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online on the MITRA application platform before 17 January 2027, requesting the Erasmus Mundus scholarship within the same application.

opportunities.title: New Europe College (NEC) Fellowships 2027-2028, Bucharest
opportunities.provider: New Europe College - Institute for Advanced Study
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral-level scholars of any nationality in the humanities and social sciences (including law and economics) can apply for a funded research stay of one term or a full academic year in Bucharest.
opportunities.description:
New Europe College (NEC), an institute for advanced study in Bucharest, has opened its annual competition for the 2027-2028 fellowships. About 25 fellowships are offered across eight programmes for scholars who already hold a PhD and work in the humanities or social sciences, including law and economics.

Fellows spend either a full academic year (ten months, October 2027 to July 2028) or, for foreign citizens, one term of five months in Bucharest, working on their own research project in an interdisciplinary community. Applications can be written in English, French or German and are due on 17 January 2027.

The general programme is open to international applicants, so African scholars in the humanities and social sciences can apply for a paid, residential research fellowship in Central and Eastern Europe. Some programmes inside the call are restricted by nationality or region, so applicants should read the full call.
opportunities.benefits: A tax-free monthly allowance of EUR 1,000, accommodation in Bucharest, reimbursement of travel from home to Bucharest and back, free library access, and a lump sum towards a research trip or conference.
requirements: PhD holder (postdoctoral level)
Field in the humanities or social sciences, including law and economics

Romanian or international scholars (some programmes have extra nationality or career-stage limits, e.g. Mattei Dogan requires a PhD within the last five years and Central/Eastern European or Black Sea nationality)
Application in English, French or German
documents: Research project description of up to 12,000 characters
One or two reference letters (optional, recommended by 24 January 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the academic track record and publications, the originality of the research proposal, and an interdisciplinary or comparative approach. Pre-selected candidates are interviewed by Zoom.
important_dates: Fellowship period: October 2027 to July 2028 (or one five-month term)
opportunities.about_provider: New Europe College is an independent institute for advanced study in Bucharest, Romania. It hosts Romanian and international fellows each year in the humanities and social sciences and runs several sponsored fellowship programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through NEC's online application portal before 17 January 2027, including the project description and PhD diploma. Read the full call PDF linked on the page to see which of the eight programmes you fit. Questions go to applications@nec.ro.
opportunities.notes: Ameropa fellowships are for Romanian researchers and Gerda Henkel fellowships for certain post-Soviet and Asian countries, so African applicants should target the general programmes.

opportunities.title: <Programming> 2027 Student Research Competition
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate and graduate ACM student members can submit by 18 January 2027 to the <Programming> 2027 SRC in Kyoto, with prizes up to US$500.
opportunities.description:
The <Programming> 2027 Student Research Competition (SRC) is an ACM-sponsored contest held at the <Programming> conference at Kyoto University, Japan, from 15 to 19 March 2027. Students present their research in programming languages and software, first as an extended abstract, then as a poster and, for finalists, a talk.

Submissions close on 18 January 2027 (Anywhere on Earth), with notification on 5 February 2027. Prizes are awarded separately in undergraduate and graduate categories, and winners go on to the ACM SRC Grand Finals.

African undergraduate and graduate students working on programming research can compete; ACM student membership is required.
opportunities.benefits: Prizes in each of the undergraduate and graduate categories: first US$500, second US$300, third US$200. Winners advance to the ACM SRC Grand Finals, which award the same prizes again.
requirements: Current ACM student member
Enrolled undergraduate or graduate student at submission time
Must register for the conference if selected
Group projects allowed only for undergraduates
documents: Extended abstract, max 800 words and 2 pages excluding references, ACM SIGPLAN acmart sigconf 10pt PDF
opportunities.selection_process: Judges review the abstracts; selected students present posters, then the best present in semi-finals and finals.
opportunities.about_provider: The <Programming> conference is an international conference on the art, science and engineering of programming; the ACM Student Research Competition runs at many ACM-sponsored events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your extended abstract to programming.src.utsc@utoronto.ca before 18 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Bayer Foundation Scientific Fellowships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's, PhD, MBBS and PharmD students can apply by 18 January 2027 for up to EUR 10,000 for a research stay or placement of up to six months.
opportunities.description:
The Bayer Foundation Scientific Fellowships fund master's, PhD and medical or pharmacy students for a placement or research stay that complements their current degree. Stays last up to six months and, in the 2027 call, must start on or after 1 August 2027 and end by 31 December 2028.

The application window runs from 10 November 2026 to 18 January 2027. Eligibility depends on the country where the student is enrolled rather than on nationality, and each applicant may submit one application per call.

African students enrolled in qualifying master's, PhD, MBBS or PharmD programmes can use the fellowship to spend time in a lab or institution abroad, with extra support for those caring for children or relatives.
opportunities.benefits: Up to EUR 10,000 for the stay; caregiver support of EUR 500 a month (max EUR 3,000); exceptional costs of up to EUR 2,500 on request.
requirements: Currently enrolled in an MSc, PhD, MBBS or PharmD programme
Bachelor's students and holders of a PhD or MD are not eligible
Very good to excellent academic record
Host institution willing to receive you; placement country rules depend on where you are enrolled
Project starting on or after 1 August 2027 and ending by 31 December 2028
opportunities.selection_process: An eligibility check is followed by an independent jury, which weighs the quality and relevance of the project, the applicant's motivation and potential, and the value of the stay; applicants are told the outcome by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Bayer Foundation is the philanthropic foundation of the German life-science company Bayer, supporting science, education and social innovation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the online form linked from the Bayer Foundation fellowships page before 18 January 2027, uploading all documents and the video. Questions go to bayer.fellowship@bayer.com.
opportunities.notes: Only one application per call is allowed. The Bayer Foundation also supports a Lindau fellowship for early-career researchers.

opportunities.title: CUHK School of Journalism and Communication Internationalization Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, School of Journalism and Communication
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to a postgraduate programme of CUHK's School of Journalism and Communication for September 2027 can be nominated for one of five HK$80,000 awards.
opportunities.description:
CUHK's School of Journalism and Communication offers five Internationalization Scholarships each year to international students admitted to its taught postgraduate programmes. The awards recognise students who will add an international perspective to the school's classes in Hong Kong.

There is no separate scholarship form. A selection panel nominates winners on academic merit from the admission materials of applicants to the September 2027 intake. Programme deadlines are 7 December 2026 for the priority round and 18 January 2027 for the final round; the MSc in AI and Communication accepts applications until 31 March 2027. Applying in the priority round gives the best chance of being considered.

For African journalists and communication graduates the award offers a useful contribution towards the cost of a one-year master's at one of Asia's leading communication schools.
opportunities.benefits: HK$80,000 per award; five awards are available each year.
requirements: International student
Admitted to a taught postgraduate programme of the CUHK School of Journalism and Communication for the September 2027 intake
Strong academic merit
Able to add to the international mix of the class
Must start studies in September 2027
documents: Supporting documents sent by courier to the school as requested by the programme
opportunities.selection_process: The school's selection panel nominates awardees on academic merit, judged from the admission application. No separate interview for the scholarship is described.
important_dates: MSc in AI and Communication deadline: 31 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The School of Journalism and Communication at CUHK is one of the oldest journalism schools in Asia and offers MA and MSc programmes in journalism, global communication, new media and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for one of the school's postgraduate programmes through the CUHK Graduate School system, preferably by the 7 December 2026 priority round, and courier any required supporting documents to the school. All admitted international applicants are considered for the scholarship.
opportunities.notes: A separate scholarship for practising Hong Kong journalists is open to local applicants only.

opportunities.title: UQO International Tuition Surcharge Exemption (Winter 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students in research master's or PhD programmes can win a competitive exemption from the international tuition surcharge for a term.

opportunities.title: AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award Studentships at Birmingham City University 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Home and international arts and humanities graduates can apply by 20 January 2027 for six fully funded AHRC PhD studentships at Birmingham City University.
opportunities.description:
Birmingham City University (BCU) is offering six fully funded PhD studentships for September 2027 under the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) Doctoral Landscape Awards: three funded by the AHRC and three matched by BCU. Projects must fall at least 50% within AHRC subject areas such as arts, design, media, music and the humanities.

Studentships cover tuition fees for three and a half years plus a tax-free stipend at the UKRI minimum rate. Both home and international applicants can apply, and one award each year is reserved for an international student with a full fee waiver.

The full application deadline is 20 January 2027 at noon UK time, so African arts and humanities graduates with a strong project idea still have time to apply.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees for 3.5 years and a tax-free stipend at the UKRI minimum (GBP 21,805 a year in 2026/27). One international award a year includes a full international fee waiver.
requirements: Home or international applicant with no previous doctoral qualification and not already on a PhD
Research project at least 50% within AHRC subject areas
International applicants need an English test (offers can be conditional)
documents: Two references on the DLA reference form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored against BCU's published DLA scoring criteria by a selection panel.
important_dates: Full application deadline: 20 January 2027, 12 noon UK time
opportunities.about_provider: Birmingham City University is a large UK university known for art, design, media and music. The AHRC is the UK's main public funder of arts and humanities research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the BCU online application and upload the DLA funding form, references and degree documents before noon on 20 January 2027. Questions go to DLA@bcu.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Only one studentship a year is set aside for international applicants, so make the project fit with BCU's research strengths clear.

opportunities.title: European Youth Summit 2027 (Madrid, Apr 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: People aged 18 to 50 of any nationality with working English can apply by 20 January 2027 for 300 funded or part-funded places at the Madrid summit.
opportunities.description:
The European Youth Summit 2027 is a four-day youth diplomacy and leadership event run by the Centre for Diplomatic Advancement (CDA) in Madrid, Spain, from 13 to 16 April 2027. This second edition is themed 'Diplomacy in Action: From Dialogue to Delivery' and gathers young people for sessions, simulations and mentoring on international cooperation.

CDA is offering 300 scholarships in three tiers: 50 fully funded places with round-trip airfare, shared accommodation, meals, visa fee reimbursement and mentorship; 100 partially funded places where the delegate pays the flight; and 150 forum-access places where the delegate arranges travel and accommodation. Scholarship applications close on 20 January 2027 at 23:59 CET and results are emailed on 5 February 2027. Five participant projects can also win funding of up to US$5,000.

Applicants aged 18 to 50 of any nationality and educational background may apply, and the organisers strongly encourage people from developing countries, so young Africans interested in diplomacy and public service are a core target group.
opportunities.benefits: Fully funded: round-trip airfare, shared accommodation, meals, visa fee reimbursement, mentorship and eligibility for project funding. Partially funded: same except airfare. Forum access: participation only. Five projects can receive up to US$5,000.
requirements: Aged 18 to 50
Any nationality (developing-country applicants strongly encouraged)
Any educational background, no minimum experience
Working knowledge of English
Available for all four days, 13-16 April 2027
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored 45% on motivation and clarity of purpose, 45% on leadership and community impact and 10% on diversity of region, gender and background. One application is considered for all three scholarship tiers.
opportunities.about_provider: The Centre for Diplomatic Advancement (CDA) is an organisation that runs international youth summits on diplomacy and leadership, including events in Madrid and Berlin.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application at https://thecda.co/product/eys-2027-scholarships/ with the two essays before 20 January 2027. Selected applicants are told by email on 5 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: The page's countdown widget showed 'applications closed' on 19 November 2026 while its timeline gives the 20 January 2027 deadline; check the form is accepting entries. Paid options (invitation letter US$99, summit pass US$249, pass with accommodation US$499) are not needed for a scholarship.

opportunities.title: IJP Southern Africa Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists aged 25-40 from SADC countries or Kenya can apply by 20 January 2027 for a two-month placement in a German newsroom with a EUR 3,500 bursary.
opportunities.description:
The International Journalists' Programmes (IJP) run the Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship, an exchange that places journalists from Southern Africa in German newsrooms for about two months. In 2027 the Southern African fellows are expected to travel in July and August (to be confirmed), starting with an introductory conference in Berlin.

During the placement, fellows work at a German media outlet and produce stories for their home newsroom, building contacts and reporting on Germany and Europe. German journalists take part in the reverse exchange to Southern Africa.

The programme is mainly funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. It is open to journalists from SADC member states and Kenya, and up to five Southern African journalists are chosen each year.
opportunities.benefits: A fixed bursary of EUR 3,500, expected to cover most travel, accommodation and living costs during the fellowship. The full grant depends on a report of at least three pages and copies of published work after the fellowship.
requirements: Journalist from a SADC member state or Kenya
Aged 25 to 40
Working regularly for a media organisation
Strong English; German is an advantage
Employer must agree to the leave of absence
documents: CV with passport photo (and language certificates if available)
Essay of about 800 words: why Germany, three research topics, future role at your home outlet, planned use of the bursary
Reference from your editor-in-chief or head of department that also confirms leave
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee chooses up to five fellows, and its decision is final. Applicants rank preferred host outlets, and IJP agrees the final placement with each fellow.
important_dates: Fellowship: July and August 2027 (to be confirmed), starting in Berlin
opportunities.about_provider: IJP is a German non-profit organisation that runs exchange programmes for journalists from many world regions. Its Southern Africa programme is named after former German Federal President Horst Köhler.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the CV, essay, work samples and editor's reference to IJP (office@ijp.org) between 1 November 2026 and 20 January 2027. Read the 2027 call PDF on the programme page for the list of eligible countries.
opportunities.notes: Programme coordinator: Marco Vollmar at IJP. Plan research topics that suit German host outlets, as they influence placement.

opportunities.title: Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Science, maths and computer science bachelor's or master's students of any nationality with GPA 3.6/4.0 may apply 20 December 2026 - 20 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program places undergraduate and master's students in research laboratories at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, for eight weeks, from 16 June to 12 August 2027. Participants work on a real research project under a Weizmann scientist and also attend a mini-symposium and a safety seminar.

The online application opens on 20 December 2026 and closes on 20 January 2027; results usually come by the end of March 2027. There are no application or tuition fees. Students choose up to five research topics in the physical, chemical and life sciences, mathematics or computer science.

No nationality restriction is stated, so strong African science students with a high GPA can use the programme to gain hands-on research experience at one of the world's leading research institutes, often a decisive step towards a funded PhD.
opportunities.benefits: No fees; stipend of US$1,100 paid in two instalments; flight subsidy of up to US$400; free accommodation in student dormitories; medical insurance; partial meal subsidies.
requirements: Current bachelor's or master's student (not PhD) in physical, chemical or life sciences, mathematics or computer science, after the first year (recent bachelor's graduates and combined BSc/MSc students also eligible)
GPA of 3.6/4.0 or equivalent
Fluent English
At least one academic reference
documents: Official transcript (with registrar-signed English translation if needed)
At least one academic reference uploaded by the referee
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened on CV, transcripts, references and motivation. The strongest files are matched to Weizmann scientists according to the chosen topics, and the scientists make the final decisions. Places are limited.
important_dates: Results: usually by end of March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, is a leading multidisciplinary research institute in the natural and exact sciences with a graduate school but no undergraduate teaching.
opportunities.how_to_apply: From 20 December 2026, start the application through the form linked on the programme page; the full application form is then sent by email. Submit all documents in English and ask your referee to upload the letter by 20 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The 2027 lab list was marked 'coming soon' in November 2026. Contact: undergraduate.summer@weizmann.ac.il, +972-8-934-4536.

opportunities.title: LISS DTP ESRC Open Competition 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science graduates with strong grades, including international applicants, can apply by 20 January 2027 for ESRC-funded doctoral studentships at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial through LISS DTP.
opportunities.description:
The London Interdisciplinary Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (LISS DTP) is funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council and led by King's College London with Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London. Its open competition offers social science doctoral studentships starting in October 2027.

Applicants choose one of two formats: 1+3.5 (a master's year followed by a PhD) or +3.5 (PhD only). They must also apply to a relevant programme at one of the three partner universities and secure supervisor support.

Both home and international students may apply, but UKRI rules cap international awards at 30%, so competition for those places is strong. African social scientists with excellent grades and a well-developed project are eligible.
opportunities.benefits: ESRC studentship covering tuition fees and a stipend for the length of the award; the international fee difference is covered only for a limited number of international students. Visa, immigration health surcharge and travel costs are not covered.
requirements: First degree at first class or upper second (average of 65% or above)
For the +3.5 route, a master's at distinction or high merit
Apply to a relevant programme at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial
Not already holding a PhD, and at least 50% of study time remaining if already enrolled
Live within reasonable travel distance of London once funded
Home and international applicants eligible (international awards capped at 30%)
documents: Online application in the LISS DTP portal (liss-dtp.flexigrant.com)
Official transcripts showing modules, credits and grades (certified translations if needed)
One reference from someone who is not your supervisor, on letterhead
KCL fee-waiver form (by 18 January) or Imperial departmental support form where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Academic reviewers longlist applications, which are then scored, discussed by research-area panels and finalised by a high-level panel. No individual feedback is given.
important_dates: Final outcomes: end of April 2027 (offers week of 27 April)
opportunities.about_provider: LISS DTP is one of the ESRC's doctoral training partnerships, bringing together King's College London, Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London to train social science researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with a supervisor at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial, apply for the PhD (or master's plus PhD) there, and submit the LISS DTP application in its portal by 20 January 2027. Contact liss-dtp@kcl.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Apply for one format only (1+3.5 or +3.5). LISS also offers CASE studentships with partner organisations.

opportunities.title: University of York AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the Arts and Humanities 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with an outstanding record and a York PhD offer in an AHRC subject can apply by 20 January 2027; international winners must cover the gap between home and international fees.
opportunities.description:
The University of York awards six AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards for PhD students in the arts and humanities who start in September 2027. The studentships are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council, part of UK Research and Innovation, and cover research within the AHRC's remit, whether based in York's Faculty of Arts and Humanities or in its science and social science faculties.

Each award pays a tax-free living stipend and waives tuition at the UK (home) rate. International applicants, including those from Africa, are eligible, but the award does not pay the difference between home and international fees, so they need other funds to cover it.

York runs an online information session on 18 November 2026 and an application-writing workshop on 25 November 2026 for interested applicants.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of GBP 21,805 a year (2026/27 rate; 2027/28 rates published early 2027) plus a tuition fee waiver at the UK home rate. International students must pay the difference between home and international fees themselves.
requirements: An offer of a PhD place in a relevant York department, starting September 2027 (no deferrals)
