Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class degree and a master's Distinction or equivalent experience
Research within the AHRC subject remit
Must live in the UK within reasonable distance of York during the PhD; distance learning is not funded
Not already a doctoral student and not in full-time employment at the start
documents: Separate PhD application to York (advised by early December 2026)
opportunities.selection_process: Each department ranks its candidates, and a Faculty of Arts and Humanities panel then ranks the whole group. The process finishes by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a UK research university and member of the Russell Group. The AHRC is UK Research and Innovation's council for arts and humanities research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a PhD place at York, ideally by early December 2026, and complete the AHRC DLA online studentship form by 20 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Six awards are available. Part-time paid work of up to about six hours a week is allowed with supervisor approval. Contact: pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities, University of York 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding humanities graduates of any nationality applying for a York PhD in history, literature or languages can apply by 20 January 2027 for a Wolfson scholarship worth GBP 38,000 a year for three years.
opportunities.description:
The University of York, with funding from the Wolfson Foundation, offers three doctoral scholarships in the humanities for PhD study starting in September 2027. The awards cover history, literature and languages, and are among the most generous humanities PhD awards in the UK.

Each scholarship provides GBP 38,000 a year for three years. It pays home-rate tuition fees and the rest goes towards maintenance, research, travel and training. Overseas students receive the home fee rate only, so they need to cover the difference between home and international fees.

The scholarships are open to all nationalities, so outstanding African humanities graduates with a master's can apply, provided they can arrange the extra fee funding.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 38,000 per year for three years (GBP 114,000 in total), covering home-rate tuition fees and, from the balance, maintenance, research, travel and training costs. Overseas students receive home-rate fees only.
requirements: Applied for (ideally holding an offer for) a PhD in a relevant York department in history, literature or languages, starting September 2027 (no deferral)
Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class undergraduate degree and a master's
Live in the UK for the duration of the award
Open to all nationalities; full-time or part-time
International students must fund the gap between home and international fees
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are passed to scholarship panels, which choose three scholars on academic excellence and the strength of the research project.
important_dates: Submit PhD application: ideally by early December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a research-intensive UK university. The Wolfson Foundation is a UK charity that supports excellence in research and education, including its Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your PhD at York (ideally by early December), then complete the online Wolfson scholarship form by 20 January 2027. Questions on funding go to pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: York also offers AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the arts and humanities in the same window.

opportunities.title: ACM CHI 2027 Posters, Demos and Student Research Competition (Pittsburgh)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality may submit posters, and students with ACM student membership may enter the SRC, by 21 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
ACM CHI 2027, the leading international conference on human-computer interaction, takes place at the David L. Lawrence Convention Center in Pittsburgh, USA, from 10 to 14 May 2027. Two of its lighter-weight tracks close on 21 January 2027 (Anywhere on Earth): Posters, for late-breaking work presented as a 4-page extended abstract and an A0 poster, and the Student Research Competition (SRC), where students present their own research for prizes.

SRC entrants submit a non-anonymous extended abstract of up to five pages; graduate entries must be single-authored and advisors cannot be co-authors. Winners in the undergraduate and graduate categories receive US$500, US$300 or US$200, a medal and a year of ACM student membership. Posters can be presented on site or remotely, while SRC requires attendance in person. Notifications for both are sent on 18 February 2027.

CHI also runs a student volunteer lottery (closing 1 February 2027) that waives the registration fee, and SIGCHI's Gary Marsden Travel Awards help students from under-represented regions, so African HCI students can combine these routes to attend.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted extended abstracts; presentation at CHI 2027. SRC prizes: US$500, US$300 and US$200 in each category plus a medal and one-year ACM student membership. Student volunteers get free registration and daily breakfast and lunch.
requirements: Posters: extended abstract up to 4 pages plus A0 poster, anonymised; one author must register
SRC: presenter must be a student at the deadline with active ACM student membership
SRC: extended abstract up to 5 pages, not anonymous; graduate entries single-author; advisors cannot be co-authors
SRC: in-person attendance and registration required
documents: Proof of student status: letter from school or note from supervisor (SRC)
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed through PCS; SRC finalists present at the conference and are judged for the prizes.
opportunities.about_provider: CHI is organised by ACM SIGCHI, the Special Interest Group on Computer-Human Interaction of the Association for Computing Machinery.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the PCS system (https://new.precisionconference.com/) choosing the Posters or Student Research Competition track before 21 January 2027 AoE. Contacts: posters@chi2027.acm.org and studentresearch@chi2027.acm.org.
opportunities.notes: The SRC track itself gives no travel funding; apply separately for the SIGCHI Gary Marsden Travel Award. Student volunteers work about 20 hours and must arrive for orientation on 9 May 2027.

opportunities.title: CERN Summer Student Programme 2027 (Member and Non-Member States)
opportunities.provider: CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and master's students of any nationality in physics, engineering, computer science or maths, with at least three years of full-time study by the start date, can apply by 21 January 2027 for a paid summer at CERN.
opportunities.description:
Every summer CERN, the particle physics laboratory near Geneva, hosts several hundred university students from around the world for its Summer Student Programme. Students spend between eight and thirteen weeks working on a research or technical project in one of CERN's teams, attend a lecture series given by CERN scientists, visit the facilities and write a short final report. The 2027 programme ideally starts on 14 June 2027 and is fully on site.

The programme is open to students of all nationalities, with separate funding channels for member and non-member states; in 2025 CERN's donor-funded programme alone supported 60 students from non-member states. Projects span experimental and theoretical physics, computing, engineering and mathematics.

For African science and engineering students it is one of the best-known paid research placements in Europe, combining hands-on work at the world's largest physics laboratory with an international network of peers.
opportunities.benefits: A net subsistence allowance of 94 CHF per calendar day, health insurance (the contribution is deducted from the allowance), travel expenses depending on individual circumstances, help finding accommodation on or near site, and the summer lecture programme.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's student (not PhD)
At least 6 semesters (3 academic years) of full-time university study in a relevant field by the start date
Field: physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics
Enrolled full time for the whole stay
Good knowledge of English
Not previously a CERN summer student and not at CERN for more than 3 months under another status
Open to all nationalities
documents: Official transcripts in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: CERN reviews the applications and may invite candidates to an online interview, followed by an offer and onboarding.
opportunities.about_provider: CERN is the European Organization for Nuclear Research, an intergovernmental laboratory on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. It operates the Large Hadron Collider and hosts scientists from more than 100 countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'CERN Summer Student Programme 2027' posting on CERN's careers site, which opens an online form (allow about 15 minutes). Upload your CV, transcripts and enrolment certificate, and arrange your academic reference letter.
opportunities.notes: CERN's general page says applications should arrive by the end of January, but the job posting gives 21 January 2027; use the earlier date. A separate CERN openlab summer programme in computing also runs in 2027.

opportunities.title: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or Master's students of any nationality with at least six semesters completed can spend two paid summer months in Geneva working on computing projects.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master SpaceMed (Space Medicine) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality in life sciences, medicine, psychology, kinesiology or engineering with B2 English may apply by 21 January 2027 for SpaceMed and a €1,400/month scholarship.
opportunities.description:
SpaceMed is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in space medicine, co-funded by the European Union and delivered by a consortium of European universities. Over two years it trains students in human physiology and health in space and extreme environments, preparing them for careers in space agencies, research and the space industry.

The campaign for the 2027 intake opened on 21 October 2026 and closes on 21 January 2027 at 23:59 CET. Files are reviewed in February and March 2027, admission letters go out in early April, and the academic year starts in early October 2027.

About 20 Erasmus Mundus scholarships are awarded each year, open to all nationalities with no more than two holders from the same country, so African graduates in life sciences, medicine, psychology, kinesiology or engineering have a real chance of a fully paid place.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of €1,400 a month for 24 months plus a waiver of the participation fee. No separate travel, visa or installation money is mentioned.
requirements: Bachelor's (180 ECTS) in life sciences, psychology or kinesiology; or a master's in engineering; or a medical degree; or a degree with substantial study of humans in space or extreme environments
English at B2: IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 87 (paper 580), Cambridge B2 First, certificate under 3 years old (OLS not accepted)
No previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship
At most two scholarship holders per nationality
documents: Two recommendation letters (one academic, one from an employer or supervisor)
Motivation video in English (MP4, under one minute)
Proof of residence issued within 12 months of the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on academic excellence (40 points), relevance of background (15), quality of the previous institution (15), motivation video (10), relevant work experience (9), recommendation letters (8) and extra languages (3). Admission and scholarship decisions are separate.
opportunities.about_provider: SpaceMed is run by a consortium of European universities under the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scheme, co-funded by the European Union.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account at https://apply-space-med.tchooz.app/connexion, select 'Application EMJM SpaceMed' under all campaigns and upload every document in English before 21 January 2027. Incomplete applications are rejected; documents cannot be sent by post or email.
opportunities.notes: Only certified translations are accepted. Self-funded admission is also possible.

opportunities.title: Hanken GBSN Scholarship for Students from Developing Countries 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students or alumni of listed GBSN member schools in countries including Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia can apply by 21 January 2027 for one of two two-year tuition waivers at Hanken.
opportunities.description:
Hanken School of Economics in Finland awards two GBSN scholarships each year to master's applicants who are students or alumni of specific Global Business School Network (GBSN) member schools in listed developing countries. The scholarship waives the full tuition fee for two academic years of an English-taught master's programme.

The award is made only within Hanken's main admission round for English-taught master's degrees, which runs from 7 to 21 January 2027. Applicants are ranked on academic merit, and the best-ranked eligible applicants receive the scholarship.

African countries on the list are Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia, so graduates of GBSN member business schools there should check whether their school qualifies.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for two academic years, equivalent to EUR 15,000 a year. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Student or alumnus/alumna of a specified GBSN member school in a listed developing country
Applying in the main admission round for an English-taught Hanken master's
Bachelor's degree with at least 25-30 ECTS in relevant subjects
English language requirement met
GMAT, GRE or GTEBS aptitude test, or the GPA route, as required
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic success and skills from previous studies, scored from 1.00 to 5.00 (minimum 3.00) and ranked; the two scholarships go to top-ranked eligible applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Hanken School of Economics is a business school in Helsinki and Vaasa, Finland. It is a member of the Global Business School Network, which links business schools working on management education in developing regions.

opportunities.notes: Only two scholarships are awarded a year, so meet all main-round requirements, including the aptitude test, early.

opportunities.title: McGill Major Entrance Scholarships (applicants from outside Canada)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top international secondary-school leavers, including Africans, starting a McGill undergraduate degree in Fall 2027 may apply by 21 January 2027 for awards up to $10,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
McGill University in Montreal, Canada, awards Major Entrance Scholarships to outstanding students starting full-time undergraduate study for the first time in Fall 2027. They are merit-based, judged first on academic achievement and then on outstanding leadership, and can be renewed for three or four years if the renewal conditions are met.

Applicants from outside Canada must apply for admission by 15 January 2027 and submit the separate major scholarship application by 21 January 2027 (midnight Montreal time) through the Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal, where applications opened on 1 October. Committees choose the winners and may interview finalists; those not chosen are automatically considered for a one-year award.

International students, including Africans, are eligible for the $3,000, $5,000 and $10,000 tiers (the $12,000 tier is for Canadian citizens and permanent residents). The competition is intense: McGill suggests averages of about 97% over the last two years of secondary school for overseas systems.
opportunities.benefits: Renewable awards of $3,000, $5,000 or $10,000 a year for applicants from outside Canada (the $12,000 tier is limited to Canadian citizens and permanent residents), plus a non-renewable $3,000 one-year award considered automatically.
requirements: First-time, full-time undergraduate entering McGill in Fall 2027 (not transfer, mature, diploma, exchange or part-time)
Outstanding academic record (indicative: about 97% average or top 1% for overseas secondary systems; A*A*A*A at A-level; IB 41)
Outstanding leadership in school and community
Admission application by 15 January 2027
documents: Two reference letters (one academic, one activity-related) uploaded by referees
School statement of class size and rank, if available
List of activities over the last three years
One-page self-written reference in the third person
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarship committees assess academic achievement first and then leadership; finalists may be interviewed. Applicants not chosen for a major award are automatically considered for the one-year award.
important_dates: Scholarship deadline: 21 January 2027, midnight Montreal time
opportunities.about_provider: McGill University in Montreal is one of Canada's leading research universities, with a large international student body.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission through McGill's Undergraduate Admissions Applicant Portal, then complete the major entrance scholarship application there and ask referees to upload their letters by 21 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Students can hold only one centralised entrance scholarship. Contact: scholarships@mcgill.ca, +1 514 398 6013.

opportunities.title: University of Eastern Finland Early-Bird Tuition Discount 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a UEF international master's for September 2027 get 30% off first-year tuition if they accept and pay within 21 days; applications close 21 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Eastern Finland (UEF) gives a 30% early-bird discount on first-year tuition to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its English-taught master's programmes starting in September 2027. Tuition is EUR 10,000 to 12,000 a year, so the discount is worth EUR 3,000 to 3,600.

The discount applies automatically if the student accepts the study place and pays the fee (or the first instalment) within 21 days of the admission results. A further 30% waiver for the second year is available to students who complete at least 55 ECTS in year one and apply separately.

UEF does not offer full tuition waivers or humanitarian scholarships, so African applicants should budget for the remaining fees and living costs of about EUR 900 to 1,000 a month.
opportunities.benefits: 30% off first-year tuition (EUR 3,000 on a EUR 10,000 fee or EUR 3,600 on EUR 12,000); a possible 30% second-year waiver; Finnish Proficiency waivers of EUR 2,500 (A) or EUR 1,500 (B) from 2027-28.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss student liable for tuition fees
Admitted to a UEF international master's for the September 2027 intake
Accept the offer and pay the fee or first instalment within 21 days of results
Second-year waiver: at least 55 ECTS completed in year one and a separate application
documents: Studyinfo.fi application with degree certificates, transcripts and English proof
Non-refundable application fee for non-EU applicants
opportunities.selection_process: No separate scholarship selection for the first year: the discount applies to every fee-liable admitted student who accepts and pays on time.
important_dates: Payment for the discount: within 21 days of admission results
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Eastern Finland is a multidisciplinary university with campuses in Joensuu and Kuopio. It offers international master's programmes in fields such as forestry, health sciences, computing and education.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a UEF international master's on Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027. When admitted, accept the place and pay within 21 days to receive the early-bird discount automatically.
opportunities.notes: Finnish immigration requires proof of EUR 800 a month for living costs; UEF recommends EUR 900-1,000.

opportunities.title: Åbo Akademi University International Master's Tuition Fee Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants, including Africans, admitted to an Åbo Akademi international master's for autumn 2027 get €4,000 off each year; apply 7-21 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Åbo Akademi University in Turku, Finland, reduces the tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students in its international master's programmes. For students admitted from 2026 onwards there is no separate scholarship competition: everyone who accepts their place and pays the fee by the deadline in the admission letter gets a €4,000 early-commitment discount in year one (paying €8,000 instead of €12,000), and all admitted students get a further €4,000 reduction in year two without applying.

The joint application period for autumn 2027 runs from 7 to 21 January 2027 (closing at 15:00 Helsinki time) through Studyinfo.fi, with supporting documents due by 28 January 2027. Admission results and scholarship offers arrive by email in early April 2027, places must be accepted by 13 July 2027, and studies start in August 2027.

For African applicants this means a predictable, automatic fee cut of €8,000 over two years at a Swedish-speaking Finnish university that teaches its international master's programmes in English.
opportunities.benefits: €4,000 off the first-year tuition fee (€8,000 instead of €12,000) for accepting the place and paying on time, plus a further €4,000 reduction in the second year for all admitted fee-paying students.
requirements: Admitted to an Åbo Akademi international master's programme for autumn 2027
Liable to pay tuition fees (non-EU/EEA)
Accept the study place and pay the fee by the deadline in the admission letter
Meet the programme's academic and English requirements
documents: Official translations if not in English, Swedish or Finnish
Residence permit if already living in Finland/EU
opportunities.selection_process: No separate scholarship selection: the fee reductions apply automatically to admitted fee-paying students. Admission itself is decided by each programme.
important_dates: Results and scholarship offers: early April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Åbo Akademi University is Finland's Swedish-language university, based in Turku and Vaasa, offering international master's programmes taught in English.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to up to six programmes in the joint application on Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027 and upload scanned documents as PDFs by 28 January 2027. Non-EU/EEA applicants pay an application fee.
opportunities.notes: Questions: admission@abo.fi. The older 100% and 80% waivers apply only to students admitted in 2025 or earlier.

opportunities.title: ACM UMAP 2027 call for papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality may submit; abstracts due 22 January 2027 and papers 29 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
ACM UMAP 2027, the 35th ACM Conference on User Modeling, Adaptation and Personalization, will be held in Chicago, USA, from 9 to 12 June 2027. The call for full and short papers covers user modelling, recommender systems, personalisation, large language models for adaptive systems, fairness and related topics.

Authors must register an abstract by 22 January 2027 and submit the paper by 29 January 2027 (11:59 pm AoE). Long papers may have 8 pages of content and short papers 4, each plus up to 2 pages of references, in the ACM double-column format under double-blind review. Accepted papers appear in the ACM proceedings, and at least one author must register early and present in person.

UMAP is a central venue for personalisation research, and its student funding support and visa information pages make it reachable for African students working on recommender systems or adaptive learning.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the ACM conference proceedings and presentation in Chicago. The conference site has a student funding support page; authors outside ACM Open institutions may face an article processing charge.
requirements: Original work not under review elsewhere
Long paper up to 8 pages or short paper up to 4 pages, plus up to 2 pages of references, ACM sigconf anonymous format
Abstract registered by 22 January 2027 (author list fixed after that)
At least one author registers by the early deadline and presents in person
Disclose any AI use in the methods
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review with a rebuttal phase (2-8 March 2027); notification on 15 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: UMAP is the premier ACM conference on user modelling and personalisation, organised under the User Modeling Inc. umbrella with ACM SIGCHI and SIGWEB.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register the abstract and then upload the paper in the 'Full and Short Papers' track of the UMAP 2027 EasyChair before the deadlines. Questions go to umap2027-programchairs@um.org.
opportunities.notes: Check https://um.org/umap2027/student-funding-support/ for student grants and the visa information page early, as US visas take time.

opportunities.title: Copernicus Master in Digital Earth Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality in geospatial or related fields with B2/C1 English may apply by 22 January 2027 for CDE and a €1,400/month scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Copernicus Master in Digital Earth (CDE) is a two-year, full-time Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in Earth observation and geoinformation, taught in English by Paris Lodron University Salzburg (Austria), Université Bretagne Sud (France) and Palacký University Olomouc (Czech Republic). Students study in at least two countries and specialise either in GeoData Science and AI for Earth Observation or in GeoVisualisation and Geocommunication.

Call 4 is open from 2 November 2026 to 22 January 2027 (23:59 CET) for applicants worldwide. European applicants also have a separate March-May period without scholarships.

All selected students receive a waiver of participation costs, and the best ranked receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships of €1,400 a month. With no more than 10% of scholarships per nationality, it is well suited to African graduates in geography, environmental science, geology, computer science or surveying who want a career in satellite data and GIS.
opportunities.benefits: Participation-cost fee waiver for all selected students; Erasmus Mundus scholarships of €1,400 a month for top-ranked applicants.
requirements: Bachelor's degree (at least 180 ECTS) in a geospatial or closely related field, or a related discipline with evidence of EO/GI competence
English certificate at C1/B2 no older than 2 years, or at least four semesters of English-medium study
Programming, GIS and basic maths for the GeoData Science track; GIS visualisation skills for the GeoVisualisation track
Certified (legalised/apostilled) degree documents for international applicants
Non-European applicants must already hold the degree
No previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship
documents: Evidence of EO/GI skills and experience
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are ranked on their EO/GI foundations, geospatial work experience, programming and software skills, English, grades and the quality of their letters, with extra credit for publications, teaching or outreach. Eligible candidates outnumber places.
opportunities.about_provider: CDE is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the European Union and run by Paris Lodron University Salzburg (Department of Geoinformatics, Z_GIS), Université Bretagne Sud and Palacký University Olomouc. It is accredited by AQAS.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the Call 4 PDF on master-cde.eu, then apply through the online application form linked from the calls page before 22 January 2027. Questions go to msc-cde@plus.ac.at.
opportunities.notes: Applicants with more than one nationality must choose one for the scholarship.

opportunities.title: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships (January 2027 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Life scientists of any nationality within two years of their PhD, with a first-author paper and moving to another country, may apply by 22 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support internationally mobile postdocs in the life sciences for up to two years. Fellows receive a salary or stipend, a relocation allowance and support for children, attend the EMBO Laboratory Leadership course and join the EMBO Fellows network. Host labs can be in Europe or elsewhere, but every fellowship must involve moving between countries.

Applications are accepted all year with two cut-offs. The spring round closes on Friday 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET, with results around mid-June 2027; the autumn round closes on the second Friday of July.

There is no nationality restriction, so African life scientists with a recent PhD and a first-author paper can use the fellowship to move to a leading lab, for example in Europe. Applicants should note the strict mobility rules and that re-applications will no longer be allowed from the autumn 2027 round.
opportunities.benefits: Up to two years of funding including salary or stipend, relocation allowance, child allowance/support, the EMBO Laboratory Leadership course and membership of the EMBO Fellows network.
requirements: Doctorate in hand at the start of the fellowship, obtained no more than two years before submission if already awarded
At least one first-author research paper accepted or published in a peer-reviewed journal (or first-author preprint with public independent reviews)
Move between countries: not to the country of the PhD or to a lab where you spent more than six months
Not the PhD lab or a continuation of the PhD project
One application per round; a host lab may support only one candidate per round
opportunities.selection_process: Merit-based evaluation of the candidate, the project and the host lab by EMBO's selection process; results around mid-June for the January round.
important_dates: Autumn deadline: second Friday of July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: EMBO (the European Molecular Biology Organization), based in Heidelberg, Germany, is an organisation of more than 2,000 leading life scientists that promotes excellence in research through fellowships, courses and networks.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and apply through the EMBO online application system linked from the fellowship page, get both referees and the host to complete their parts, and confirm the application is complete before 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET.
opportunities.notes: Exceptions to eligibility are only for extraordinary circumstances and must be discussed with the Fellowship Office before applying. From the autumn 2027 round re-applications will not be accepted.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus CLMCE - Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a first degree and good English may apply by 22 January 2027 for a fully funded two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in children's literature, media and cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.description:
Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship (CLMCE) is a two-year, full-time Erasmus Mundus International Master that looks at books, media and creative industries made for young audiences, combining literary and cultural study with the business side of producing and selling cultural content. The University of Glasgow coordinates the programme on behalf of a European university consortium, and the course is co-funded by the European Union through the Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scheme.

Students spend their study periods at different partner universities in at least two countries; the third semester is taken at a consortium institution allocated according to the student's ranking. The intake covered here is the fourth edition (2027-2029), starting in September 2027.

Across its four editions the consortium can offer up to 90 Erasmus Mundus scholarships (60 regular and 30 targeted places). These awards pay all tuition plus a monthly allowance, which makes the programme a fully funded route into Europe for African graduates interested in publishing, children's media, storytelling, education or cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders have all tuition fees and travel insurance covered and receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months (up to EUR 33,600 in total). Students can instead choose three advance payments of EUR 1,000 (to help with visa and travel costs) followed by EUR 1,275 per month.
requirements: A first higher-education degree (bachelor's or recognised equivalent); final-year students may apply if they graduate before the course starts
Proof of English for applicants whose first language is not English, uploaded by the scholarship deadline (minimum score set by the University of Glasgow)
Must not have held an Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship before
At most six scholarships per nationality across the four editions; dual nationals must say which nationality they apply under
Study must take place in at least two countries different from the country of residence at enrolment
documents: CLMCE scholarship application form (uploaded as PDF)
Degree certificate(s), if completed, in the original language
Transcripts with grades, plus official English translations
Two reference letters on letterhead (one academic; the second academic or professional)
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 checks eligibility and shortlists candidates on academic excellence. Stage 2 ranks shortlisted applicants on their personal statement and motivation, academic record and English, other relevant experience, and references. Results are emailed in April 2027; appeals are possible within 14 days on procedural grounds only.
important_dates: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline: 22 January 2027, 13:00 UK time
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the UK's oldest universities and acts as coordinating institution for the CLMCE consortium. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are flagship EU-funded programmes run jointly by several universities in different countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate application portal using the Apply Now link on the CLMCE how-to-apply page, and upload the scholarship form and all documents. Once started, an application must be completed within 42 days. Questions go through the university's online enquiry form, choosing Erasmus as the level of study.
opportunities.notes: Applicants without a master's degree may be preferred when required. Leave time for referees to prepare letters on letterhead before the January deadline.

opportunities.title: Fordham University International Student Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Fordham are automatically considered for merit awards of USD 10,000-25,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Fordham University in New York City considers every complete first-year application from international students for merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 a year. No separate scholarship application is needed: the award, if any, is shown in the online admission letter.

Awards are renewed at the same amount for up to four years as long as the student keeps the required GPA and satisfactory academic progress. Fordham also gives a limited amount of need-based aid to international students, but its admission is need-aware and need-based awards do not cover the full cost.

For the current admission cycle, the Regular Decision deadline has been extended from 3 January to 22 January, and Early Decision II to 15 January. African students applying to a US university in New York can be considered for these merit awards simply by applying on time.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 per year for highly qualified first-year international applicants, renewable at the same amount for up to four years. Transfer students can receive up to USD 25,000. Separate need-based aid is limited and does not cover the full cost.
requirements: International applicant on a non-immigrant visa (US citizens and permanent residents use the domestic process)
Complete first-year application through the Common Application
English test (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson) for non-native speakers without four years of recent English-medium schooling
For need-based aid: CSS Profile and an expected family contribution of at least USD 50,000 a year
Keep the required GPA to renew the award
documents: CSS Profile (school code 2259) if applying for need-based aid
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are decided automatically from the complete admission file; there is no separate merit application. Need-based aid is awarded to about 5% of aid applicants.
important_dates: Early Decision II: 3 January, extended to 15 January
Regular Decision: 3 January, extended to 22 January
CSS Profile: 15 January for Regular Decision
opportunities.about_provider: Fordham University is a private Jesuit university in New York City, with campuses at Rose Hill in the Bronx and Lincoln Center in Manhattan.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Fordham through the Common Application by the Regular Decision or Early Decision II deadline; you are then considered for merit awards automatically. If you also need need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile by its deadline.
opportunities.notes: Fordham does not give CSS Profile fee waivers or loans in international aid packages. Applying for need-based aid can affect admission, because admission is need-aware for international students.

opportunities.title: INTERACT MSCA PhD Fellowships in Interdisciplinary Health Research, 3rd Call (Copenhagen)
opportunities.provider: University of Copenhagen, Biotech Research & Innovation Centre (BRIC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Candidates of any nationality with a relevant master's obtained no more than 4 years before the deadline, no PhD, and no more than 12 months spent in Denmark in the previous 36 months.
opportunities.description:
INTERACT is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND doctoral programme led by the Biotech Research & Innovation Centre (BRIC) at the University of Copenhagen, offering PhD fellowships in interdisciplinary health research. Its third call will offer up to 22 fellowships, hosted at the University of Copenhagen, DTU or the Danish Cancer Institute.

The call opens on 11 December 2026 and closes on 24 January 2027. Evaluation takes place in February and March, online interviews in March and April, and host interviews in late April and May, with answers due by the end of May and fellowships starting on 1 September 2027. Fellows get a three-year employment contract on Danish salary terms.

The programme is open to all nationalities, provided the MSCA mobility rule is met. Competition is stiff (the first two calls drew 744 and 1,100 applications), so African applicants should prepare their documents with the official templates once the call opens.
opportunities.benefits: A 36-month employment contract with a monthly gross salary from about DKK 31,424 (about EUR 4,193, at 1 November 2025 rates) plus pension contributions, five weeks' holiday and five extra days off. Visa costs and family allowances are not covered.
requirements: Any nationality
Must not have lived or worked in the host country for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the deadline (MSCA mobility rule)
Master's degree in a relevant field obtained no more than 4 years before the deadline (career breaks may be taken into account)
No doctoral degree
Master's fully completed, including thesis defence, by 1 September 2027
English test meeting University of Copenhagen rules
documents: Certified master's and bachelor's diplomas and transcripts with English translations
Evidence of career breaks, if relevant

important_dates: Host interviews: late April to May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: BRIC is a biomedical research centre at the University of Copenhagen. It coordinates INTERACT, a doctoral programme run under the EU's Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions with partner hosts DTU and the Danish Cancer Institute.
opportunities.how_to_apply: When the call opens on 11 December 2026, download the templates from the INTERACT site, complete them and apply through the online application linked to the University of Copenhagen job portal before 24 January 2027. Questions go to interact-msca@bric.ku.dk.
opportunities.notes: Templates only become available when the call opens. Check the mobility rule carefully, as it is the most common reason for ineligibility in MSCA programmes.

opportunities.title: Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships 2027 (master's plus PhD in mathematics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women of any nationality who are finishing a bachelor's or first year of master's, preferably in mathematics, and plan to join an eligible Paris-Saclay or IP Paris mathematics master's can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships are part of the Women in Mathematics programme of the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH). They fund talented female students from anywhere in the world through a master's in mathematics and then a three-year PhD at the Hadamard Doctoral School (EDMH) in the Paris region.

Winners join the master's 'Mathematics and Applications' at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris, entering in the first or second year depending on their background. They receive an excellence scholarship of €11,000 a year during the master's and a commitment of doctoral funding worth a minimum of about €82,800 gross over three years.

The call for 2027 opened on 21 October 2026 and closes on 24 January 2027. Because it is open to every nationality, it is an outstanding route for African women in mathematics into one of Europe's strongest mathematical communities.
opportunities.benefits: A master's excellence scholarship of €11,000 per year for one or two years, followed by three years of doctoral funding with a minimum total gross amount of about €82,800. A contribution to master's and PhD tuition is included.
requirements: Female applicant of any nationality
Completing a bachelor's degree or the first year of a master's at the time of application, preferably in mathematics
Intends to enrol in an eligible M1 or M2 of the 'Mathematics and Applications' master's at Paris-Saclay or IP Paris
Plans to continue to a PhD at EDMH
documents: Referee letters (submitted by referees by 31 January 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: An award jury makes a preliminary selection, then shortlisted candidates have a video interview in English or French.
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard brings together the mathematics departments and laboratories of Université Paris-Saclay, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and partner institutions. It funds students, researchers and programmes and runs the Hadamard Doctoral School of Mathematics (EDMH).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the list of eligible master's courses on the FMJH site, then complete the online Maryam Mirzakhani application form before 24 January 2027. Ask your referees to submit their letters by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The number of awards is not stated. Questions go to the FMJH contact email.

opportunities.title: Sophie Germain Master Scholarships 2027 (Wave 1)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematics students of any nationality entering the Paris-Saclay Mathematics and Applications master's may apply by 24 January 2027 for EUR 11,000 a year plus travel and housing support.
opportunities.description:
The Sophie Germain Master Scholarships fund talented students from around the world who join the Mathematics and Applications master's programme in the Paris-Saclay area, either at Université Paris-Saclay or at Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Around fifty scholarships are given each year, and selection is made without regard to where applicants come from.

The awards are run by the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH) and cover either the first (M1) or second (M2) year of the master's in one of the listed research-oriented courses. The 2027 Wave 1 call is reserved for students who are currently outside the Paris-Saclay institutions.

For African mathematics students the scholarship is a strong route into one of Europe's largest mathematics research clusters: it pays a living allowance, helps with registration fees and travel, and offers housing to first-time international students. English-speaking students can follow the English-taught Jacques Hadamard M1 tracks.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 11,000 net per year; a flat-rate contribution to university registration fees; for first-time international students, up to EUR 2,000 (depending on country) towards one return trip and visa costs, an offer of an individual studio in Orsay or Evry and a housing kit worth about EUR 100; access to French language courses.
requirements: Admission to one of the listed research courses of the Mathematics and Applications master's (M1 or M2) at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Wave 1 is only for students coming from outside the Paris-Saclay institutions
Strong academic record in mathematics, shown by transcripts and references
Non-European students must obtain a French student visa and a Campus France file number
Cannot be combined with another excellence scholarship
documents: Transcripts for each year of the bachelor's and first year of master's (or equivalent)
Names and emails of two referees, who upload their letters
opportunities.selection_process: A jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee together with the heads of the master's programmes judges applications on academic criteria, mainly transcripts and recommendation letters. Results are announced about five weeks after the closing date.
important_dates: Results: about five weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard is a research foundation that brings together the mathematics laboratories of the Paris-Saclay area. It runs graduate programmes and scholarships, including the Sophie Germain master's awards and the Maryam Mirzakhani doctoral scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the FMJH online scholarship form and, separately, apply for admission to the chosen master's through Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Give the names of two referees, who must send their letters by 31 January 2027.

opportunities.title: COLT 2027 Call for Papers (Conference on Learning Theory)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality, including students, may submit original learning-theory papers by 29 January 2027; one author must present in person in Tokyo.
opportunities.description:
The Conference on Learning Theory (COLT) is the main international meeting for the theoretical side of machine learning, and its 40th edition will be held in Tokyo, Japan, from 28 June to 2 July 2027. The call for papers invites original research on the mathematical and statistical foundations of learning: learning algorithms and their guarantees, statistical and computational limits, online learning, bandits and reinforcement learning theory, optimisation for learning and related areas.

Papers are submitted as a single anonymised PDF by 29 January 2027 (Anywhere on Earth). The main body may run to 12 pages in the PMLR format, while references and appendices are not limited. Accepted papers appear in the Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, and at least one author of every accepted paper must attend the conference in person.

COLT explicitly welcomes authors who have never submitted to it before, which makes it a realistic target for African doctoral students and early-career researchers working on learning theory. Full-time students who are the main contributors to a paper can compete for the best student paper award, and a strong COLT paper is a valuable entry on the CV of anyone aiming for research posts in machine learning.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted papers in the Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (PMLR); a talk or poster at COLT 2027 in Tokyo; eligibility for the best student paper award. The call page does not mention travel grants or fee waivers.
requirements: Original research on learning theory not under review elsewhere (dual-submission policy applies)

At least one author must attend COLT 2027 in person if accepted
For the best student paper award, the main contributors must be full-time students at submission time

opportunities.title: Institute for Law & AI Summer Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law graduates and researchers from any country can apply by 29 January 2027 for a paid 2027 AI law summer fellowship in Cambridge (UK) or a remote-first track with a Washington, DC convening.
opportunities.description:
The Institute for Law & AI (LawAI) runs paid summer research fellowships for people who want to work on the legal questions raised by advanced artificial intelligence. For 2027 there are two tracks. The EU Law fellowship runs from 28 June to 3 September 2027, mostly in person in Cambridge, United Kingdom, and starts with a Convening Week there on 5-9 July. The Legal Frontiers fellowship is remote-first and lasts ten weeks, from 14 June to 20 August 2027, with a Convening Week in Washington, DC on 21-25 June.

Fellows carry out a research project with guidance from LawAI staff, take part in seminars and meet others working on AI law and policy. Applicants from all countries are welcome, and prior AI research is not required.

The fellowship is a well-paid way for African law graduates and researchers with an interest in technology regulation to build a network and a publication record in a fast-growing field.
opportunities.benefits: EU Law track: GBP 1,000 per week (more for exceptional candidates), a GBP 7,000 relocation payment for fellows who move to Cambridge for the whole fellowship, travel for the Convening Week for those who cannot relocate, and the UK visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge. Legal Frontiers track: a weekly subsidy of USD 1,800 (US-based) or GBP 1,000 (EU/UK-based), travel, accommodation and meals for the Washington Convening Week, and admission to the 2027 Workshop on Law-Following AI.

opportunities.title: Novo Nordisk Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowships at MIT 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers within 5 years of their PhD in science, biomedicine or biotechnology who have a Danish degree, citizenship or research history, an MIT host and a Danish host institution, by 29 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation's Postdoctoral Fellowships at MIT fund a three-year interdisciplinary postdoc. Fellows spend the first two years in a research group at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the United States and then up to one year back at a public or non-profit research institution in Denmark, which employs the fellow and administers the grant.

The 2027 call opened on 30 September 2026 and closes on 29 January 2027 at 14:00 Copenhagen time. Projects must be interdisciplinary within the natural and technical sciences, biomedicine or biotechnology and have potential impact on human health or sustainability. Fellowships can start between 1 October 2027 and 30 September 2028.

There is no nationality rule, but applicants need a real connection to Danish research: a Danish university degree, Danish citizenship or several years of research at a Danish institution. African researchers who did their PhD or a postdoc in Denmark are therefore eligible and can use the scheme to work at MIT with generous funding.
opportunities.benefits: Up to DKK 3.6 million per fellowship (about DKK 1.2 million a year), covering salary and at least DKK 240,000 a year for project costs at MIT; relocation up to DKK 110,000 in total; living-abroad allowance up to DKK 70,000 a year plus DKK 55,000 a year for dependants; conferences up to DKK 50,000 per budget year; MIT administration DKK 25,000 a year; bench fees up to DKK 8,000 a month per FTE; equipment up to 20% of the budget.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide with a space-related project may apply by 29 January 2027 (or 28 May 2027) for up to EUR 1,200 a month to study or intern in the Paris region.
opportunities.description:
The Space Academy of Île-de-France offers incoming international mobility scholarships for students who want to come to the Paris region for space-related study or research. The scholarship gives a monthly living stipend either to follow one semester or one year of a master's programme belonging to the Academy, or to do a research internship in one of its laboratories while still enrolled at a university abroad.

The Academy is a France 2030 project that links eight Île-de-France institutions working in space science and engineering, including Université Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne Université, ONERA, Université Paris Cité, UPEC, UVSQ, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and PSL. The 2027 call has three deadlines; the first (30 October 2026) has passed, so the next one is 29 January 2027, followed by 28 May 2027.

The programme is open to third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide, so African students in physics, engineering, Earth observation or related fields can use it to join a French space master's or gain lab experience in Paris.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly living stipend of up to EUR 1,200 for one semester or one academic year (master's study can be supported for up to two years if the student re-applies for M2). Tuition may be waived only under specific exchange agreements; research interns pay no tuition. Flights and travel are not covered, and an intern's total income including other grants must not exceed the stated amount.

opportunities.benefits: Up to £200 towards travel and/or accommodation for attending BNA2027 in Belfast, paid in pounds sterling before the meeting.

Already registered to attend BNA2027

opportunities.title: Bachelor of Hotel Management (VIVES) - VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarship 2027
opportunities.provider: VLIR-UOS and VIVES University of Applied Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship for nationals of the 25 eligible countries (17 in Africa) who also live in one of them, aged 19 to 35 on 1 January 2027, with no earlier Belgian government study scholarship.
opportunities.description:
VLIR-UOS is paying full scholarships for students from its partner countries to take the three-year, English-taught Bachelor of Hotel Management at VIVES University of Applied Sciences (VIVES Noord) in West Flanders, Belgium. The award runs from September 2027 to September 2030 and is one of only two bachelor's programmes in the 2027-28 ICP Connect call.

At the very start you choose one of two specialisations: Hospitality Management, which prepares you to run hotels, restaurants and other hospitality businesses, or Culinary Arts, which trains you as a professional chef. Both tracks share a core of management, communication and teamwork, then add specialised courses. VIVES points out that hotel and restaurant managers are a shortage occupation in Belgium.

Applicants from 16 sub-Saharan African countries and Morocco can apply, provided they live in one of the 25 eligible countries and are between 19 and 35 years old on 1 January 2027. The scholarship pays travel, insurance, tuition and a monthly living allowance for the full three years. Applications through VIVES opened on 10 November 2026 and close on 31 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A full scholarship for the whole length of the programme (36 months) and no longer. It is paid mainly as a monthly allowance meant to cover living costs (board and lodging) and tuition; travel to and from Belgium and insurance are also covered. Depending on the institution, tuition, insurance or housing is either paid by you out of the allowance or paid by the university directly and taken off the allowance. There are no partial awards or extensions, and VLIR-UOS pays nothing extra for optional activities such as field trips to the Global South. ICP Connect programmes charge no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of one of the 25 VLIR-UOS ICP Connect countries (in Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe; also Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam)
Living in one of those 25 countries when you apply (it does not have to be your own country)
Aged at least 19 and not older than 35 on 1 January 2027
Never awarded a Belgian government scholarship for study before, and not enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January 2027
Only one ICP Connect scholarship application per year: applying to two or more ICP programmes gets you excluded
No other scholarship or grant for this or any other programme at the same time
Good command of English (all ICP Connect programmes are taught in English; Dutch is not needed)
A secondary school qualification that gives access to higher education (VIVES checks equivalence; the VLIR-UOS page gives no further detail)
documents: The VIVES online application with your identity, school-leaving certificate and transcripts
A motivation statement explaining how the degree will help you contribute at home
Proof of English proficiency if VIVES asks for it
The exact list is set by VIVES on its ICP Connect application page
opportunities.selection_process: The host institution first checks and ranks every eligible application, then sends its shortlist to VLIR-UOS, which screens it again. Points that weigh in the ranking: motivation and your potential to act as an agent of change at home; professional experience, with preference for people working in (or heading for) higher education, government or civil society; gender balance, with women strongly encouraged to apply; balance between regions; the Leave No One Behind principle, which favours candidates from vulnerable groups when two files are equally strong; and preference for people who have never had a scholarship to study in a high-income country. VLIR-UOS emails the selected and reserve-list candidates; the programme tells the others. Results are due by mid-May 2027 at the latest.
important_dates: VLIR-UOS online information session: 26 November 2026, 14:30-16:30 CET (register through the Zoom link on the call page)
opportunities.about_provider: VLIR-UOS is the Flemish university network's programme for development cooperation, funded by the Belgian government. Through its ICP Connect scheme it pays full scholarships for a selected set of English-taught degree programmes at universities and university colleges in Flanders and Brussels, so that students from partner countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America can study in Belgium and take their skills back home. For the September 2027 intake it funds 12 programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the eligibility rules on the VLIR-UOS page, then apply for both admission and the scholarship through the VIVES ICP Connect page (https://www.vives.be/en/study/icp-connect-scholarships) before 31 January 2027. Choose your specialisation (Hospitality Management or Culinary Arts) when you apply.
opportunities.notes: Do not apply to more than one ICP Connect programme in the same year. New graduates or people from the private sector without work experience can still be considered if their motivation is strong. Students may work a few hours a week, but not during compulsory classes, and the scholarship should not be topped up by a job. Some countries need their diplomas legalised through a Belgian embassy or consulate; ask the university early. Specialisation details: https://www.vives.be/en/commercial-sciences-business-management-and-informatics/bachelor-hotel-management-hospitality and .../bachelor-hotel-management-culinary-arts.

opportunities.title: Black Histories: Dialogues special issue: Medical histories in the Black Atlantic: Transversal perspectives

opportunities.title: Bristol Applied Economics Meetings 2027 Call for Papers

opportunities.description:
The University of Bristol's School of Economics is calling for papers for the Bristol Applied Economics Meetings 2027, two back-to-back workshops at Bristol, United Kingdom, from 4 to 7 May 2027. The first, on the Economics of Crime, Violence and Conflict, runs on 4-5 May; the second, on Development Economics, runs on 6-7 May and covers topics such as agriculture, education, health, inequality, migration, poverty and trade.

Researchers send either a full paper or an extended abstract by 31 January 2027. There is no registration fee, which keeps the meetings accessible to doctoral students and early-career economists.

The development economics day is especially relevant to African economists whose applied work studies their own countries, and presenting at a UK workshop of this kind is a good way to get feedback and meet researchers in the field. Note that the call does not offer travel or accommodation funding.
opportunities.benefits: A slot to present applied economics research at a specialist workshop in Bristol with no registration fee. No travel or accommodation support is mentioned.

Full paper or extended abstract
Able to attend in Bristol on 4-5 or 6-7 May 2027 at your own cost

opportunities.title: CDU Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship 2027

The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarships (VCIHAS) at Charles Darwin University reward international students with outstanding grades by paying half of their tuition fees for the full length of an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree. A limited number are awarded for each intake.

Charles Darwin University is based in Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory. For 2027 there are two rounds: Semester 1 (closing 31 January 2027) and Semester 2 (closing 4 July 2027). The scholarship has no living allowance, and scholars must keep a good GPA to keep it.

African students with excellent results can use it to halve the cost of an Australian degree; the same page also lists automatic awards such as the 30% CDU Global Merit Scholarship.

opportunities.title: ESEB Conference Travel Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: ESEB members from Master's student to young lecturer level who work in a country that is not high-GDP can request travel support to present at one of three 2027 evolution meetings.
opportunities.description:
The ESEB Conference Travel Award is a travel stipend from the European Society for Evolutionary Biology for students and early-career scientists who are based in lower-income countries. It helps them attend and present their work at one of three meetings in 2027: the EMPSEB student meeting in Zreče, Slovenia (31 May to 4 June 2027), the ESEB Hub Congress 2027 (16 to 20 August, held across four locations), or the joint Evolution meeting of ASN, SSB and SSE in San Juan, Puerto Rico (25 to 29 June 2027).

The award is meant to cover travel, living costs during the meeting and the early-bird registration fee. It is paid back to the winner after the meeting, on the basis of receipts, so applicants should plan to pay their costs up front.

For evolutionary biologists working at African universities and research institutes, this is one of the few society travel schemes that is aimed squarely at scientists outside high-income countries. It is open from Master's level through PhD and postdoc to young lecturers, and the society coordinates it with the SSE award, so one application is enough.
opportunities.benefits: Support towards travel costs, living expenses during the meeting and the early-bird registration fee for one of the three eligible 2027 meetings. The money is reimbursed after the meeting against receipts. The page does not state a fixed amount or the number of awards.
requirements: ESEB membership taken out before the deadline
Career stage from Master's or PhD student to postdoc or young lecturer
Working in a country that is not classed as high-GDP by the World Bank (scientists in high-GDP countries are not eligible)
No ESEB travel stipend received in the last five years
Must apply to give an oral talk or poster at the chosen meeting (acceptance is checked before reimbursement, not at application)
documents: One PDF of no more than 2 pages with name, ESEB membership number, budget in euros (including other funding sources), how attending supports your career goals, and a short CV

Submit your abstract to the meeting you want to attend as well.
opportunities.notes: ESEB and SSE coordinate their awards, so there is no need to apply to both. The ESEB Congress Attendance Aid Grant is a separate scheme with its own rules. Keep all receipts, since payment is only made after the meeting.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EMship Master in Sustainable Ship and Offshore Design 2027-2029

opportunities.description:
EMship, the International Master in Advanced Design of Sustainable Ships and Offshore Structures, is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by Ghent University in Belgium. The two-year, English-taught programme (120 ECTS) is delivered by seven universities in six countries: Ghent and Liège (Belgium), Galati (Romania), Rostock (Germany), Centrale Nantes (France), IST Lisbon (Portugal) and UPM Madrid (Spain).

Applications for the 2027-2028 intake are open. Erasmus+ scholarship holders have their tuition waived and receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months, intended to cover living costs including travel, visa, installation and rent. The consortium will award 95 scholarships over four cohorts: 60 open to all nationalities and 35 reserved for targeted regions, with no more than 10% of recipients from any one country.

African engineering graduates count as partner-country applicants. Self-funded places cost EUR 9,000 a year for partner-country students, with up to 20 high-potential self-funded students receiving a 50% discount.

Students move between partner universities, including La Rochelle University in France, with further partners in Croatia, Lithuania, Romania and Greece.

The programme trains students to use marine organisms and resources in biotechnology for health, food, materials and the environment. Around 40 students start in September 2027 (registration from 6 September and classes from 8 September, both still to be confirmed).

The first call for applications, which is the only round with Erasmus Mundus scholarships, opens on 1 December 2026 and closes on 31 January 2027. About 17 to 20 scholarships are awarded each year, with 4 to 5 planned for the group of countries that includes Africa. Selection does not favour any nationality, but no more than 10% of the scholarships may go to one nationality.

English at CEFR B2 or IELTS 6.5 (at least 6 in each skill) unless English is your native language; certificate issued within the last 2 years
Strong motivation for marine biotechnology

Two academic recommendation letters (less than 6 months old)

opportunities.notes: The conference is in person only; no online option is mentioned. Registration fees were not shown on the pages read.

opportunities.title: IBSA Foundation Fellowships 2026-2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Biomedical researchers of any nationality under 40 (PhD students to postdocs) may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of seven EUR 32,000 one-year fellowships.
opportunities.description:
The IBSA Foundation Fellowships give young biomedical researchers a year of funding to carry out a research project in a host laboratory, university, hospital or research centre of their choice. The 2026 call offers seven fellowships in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility and urology, orthopaedics and pain medicine, and healthy ageing. Projects must start by 2027 and last 12 months.

The programme is run by the IBSA Foundation for scientific research in Lugano, Switzerland. It is open to researchers of any nationality under 40, from PhD students and residents to postdocs, who hold a degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering.

Alongside the fellowships, a separate Research Equity Prize of EUR 5,000 rewards the best project hosted in a developing country, including any African country, which gives African-based labs and researchers an extra chance of support.
opportunities.benefits: Each fellowship is worth EUR 32,000 gross (before tax), meant to cover salary and mobility costs for 12 months, paid half before the project starts and half by the end of 2027. It does not cover bench fees, overheads or consumables. The Research Equity Prize pays EUR 5,000 in one instalment.
requirements: Any nationality
Under 40 years old on the deadline
Degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering
PhD students, PhD holders, postdocs and medical residents may apply; holders of permanent positions such as professors may not
Must be based at the host institution for the whole grant
Project in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility/urology, orthopaedics/pain medicine or healthy ageing
documents: List of one to three best peer-reviewed publications
Project proposal entered on the online platform
Acceptance letter from the host institution (within one week of being notified as a winner)
opportunities.selection_process: The IBSA Scientific Board peer-reviews proposals for feasibility, originality and scientific value, along with the candidate's CV (especially research experience) and the suitability of the host lab. Projects carried out at an institution other than the candidate's home lab earn extra merit. Results usually come within three months of the deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: The IBSA Foundation for scientific research is a Swiss non-profit foundation in Lugano linked to the pharmaceutical company IBSA. It promotes biomedical research and science communication through fellowships, scholarships and events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the proposal and the three documents as separate files on the foundation's application platform (ibsafoundation.poliresearch.com). Only online applications are accepted.
opportunities.notes: Winners must answer a yearly survey and acknowledge the foundation in publications. Contact: info@ibsafoundation.org, +41 58 360 10 00.

opportunities.title: ITC Faculty Early Bird Programme (40% tuition waiver), University of Twente, September 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students unconditionally admitted to the ITC MSc in Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation or MSc Spatial Engineering for September 2027 who can pay the remaining tuition by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
The ITC Faculty Early Bird Programme gives a limited number of new master's students a 40% reduction of the tuition fee for each academic year. It is offered by the Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) at the University of Twente in Enschede, the Netherlands, for programmes starting in September 2027.

It applies to two master's degrees: Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation, and Spatial Systems and Society (Spatial Engineering). Applicants must first be unconditionally admitted, then submit a separate Early Bird form by 31 January 2027, and results follow by 5 February 2027.

Because the waiver covers only part of the costs, the scheme suits African applicants who can fund the rest of their tuition and living costs, for example through an employer. The university's page lists a long set of eligible countries that includes many African nations.
opportunities.benefits: A 40% tuition waiver per academic year: on a tuition fee of EUR 45,260 the waiver is EUR 18,104, leaving EUR 27,156 to pay. The student must also cover insurance (about EUR 1,400), the residence permit (EUR 270) and living costs (about EUR 28,750), for an own contribution of about EUR 57,576 (university figures; second-year figures are indicative).
requirements: Unconditional admission to a participating ITC master's programme starting September 2027
First-time enrolment at the University of Twente
Not eligible for Dutch study grants or loans
Meet Dutch entry visa conditions if applicable
Able to pay the remaining tuition by 1 March 2027
opportunities.selection_process: An Early Bird selection committee reviews the applications after the 31 January 2027 deadline and announces results by 5 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Twente is a Dutch technical university in Enschede. Its ITC faculty is an international centre for education and research in geo-information science and Earth observation, with many alumni from Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for the master's programme through the University of Twente's online system first. Once unconditionally admitted, submit the Early Bird form on the ITC scholarship page before 31 January 2027 and wait for the committee's decision.
opportunities.notes: Late applications and late payments are not accepted. Contact: esp-itc@utwente.nl.

opportunities.title: International Women's Day Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women of any nationality who are already studying full time on an SCU campus in 2027 and have completed at least one full-time on-campus term can apply.
opportunities.description:
Southern Cross University marks International Women's Day each year with three scholarships of $5,000 for female students who are already enrolled at the university. The 2027 awards support women who are doing well academically and who can describe, in a short statement, who they are and what drives them.

The scholarship is for current students, not for people applying to the university for the first time. Recipients must be studying full time in 2027 at the Coffs Harbour campus (including the National Marine Science Centre), Lismore or the Gold Coast, and must already have completed at least one full-time term on campus.

There is no nationality rule, so African women who are already enrolled at SCU as international students can apply. Each winner's introductory statement is shared publicly during the university's International Women's Day events.
opportunities.benefits: A one-year scholarship of $5,000. Three awards are available for 2027.
requirements: Female student
Currently enrolled and studying full time at SCU in 2027
Studying at Coffs Harbour (including the National Marine Science Centre), Lismore or Gold Coast
Has completed at least one full-time on-campus term
Excellent GPA
documents: Personal introductory statement of up to 200 words
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic merit and on the introductory statement. Selection takes place in the weeks after the closing date and can take up to a month.
important_dates: Selection: up to one month after closing
Statements shared: International Women's Day, March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Southern Cross University is a public Australian university with campuses in Lismore, Coffs Harbour and the Gold Coast in New South Wales and Queensland. It is known for marine science, environmental science, health and education.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form linked from the scholarship page before 31 January 2027 and include your 200-word introductory statement. Questions go to the SCU scholarships team by email or on 1800 72 4357.
opportunities.notes: Not open to prospective students who have not yet started at SCU. Your statement will be published if you win.

opportunities.title: J. S. Lee Memorial Fellowship Programme 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates working on Chinese art or museum research of any nationality can apply for a 4 to 12 month fellowship abroad with flights, visa, insurance, accommodation and living costs covered.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-IAEA Nuclear Energy Management School (Jul 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young nuclear professionals who have not attended an IAEA Nuclear Energy Management School before can apply by 31 January 2027 for the free two-week school in Trieste, with limited grants for developing-country participants.
opportunities.description:
The Joint ICTP-IAEA Nuclear Energy Management School is a two-week certificate course held at ICTP in Trieste, Italy, from 19 to 30 July 2027. It teaches new and young professionals the basic knowledge and skills needed to manage and lead a national nuclear energy programme.

Topics include IAEA services, nuclear safety, security and safeguards, nuclear power technology, the fuel cycle and nuclear law. The school is organised by the International Atomic Energy Agency with ICTP, which is governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and Italy.

There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants are available, with priority for participants from developing countries. Several African countries are building nuclear energy programmes, so the school is directly relevant to young African engineers, regulators and policy staff.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants support the attendance of selected participants, with priority for those from developing countries; amounts are not stated.
requirements: Open only to people who have not previously attended an IAEA Nuclear Energy Management School
Aimed at new and young nuclear professionals
Women and candidates from developing countries are strongly encouraged to apply
documents: Online application in the ICTP e-portal (the page does not list documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Participants are selected by the organisers after the deadline; criteria are not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste is a UNESCO Category 1 institute governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and Italy that trains scientists from developing countries. The IAEA is the UN agency for the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create a profile on the ICTP e-portal and apply through the school's application page (activity smr 4374) once the call opens; the page says it will open soon. Questions go to smr4374@ictp.it.
opportunities.notes: As of 19 November 2026 the application form was not yet accepting entries, so check back. Request a grant in the application if you need travel support.

opportunities.title: Knight-Bagehot Fellowship in Economics and Business Journalism 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists with at least four years of business, economics or finance reporting experience can apply for a fully funded academic year at Columbia.

opportunities.title: Mercedes-Benz beVisioneers Fellowship 2027
