opportunities.eligibility_summary: Residents aged 18-28 of Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe and other listed countries may apply by 31 January 2027 for a two-year environmental innovation fellowship with up to EUR 15,000 in project funding.
opportunities.description:
beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship is a two-year programme for young people who want to turn an early idea for an environmental solution into a working project. The first year is an intensive, mostly online training year (at least 24 hours a month) in which fellows build a prototype with venture coaching, mentoring and project scholarships. The second year is an acceleration year with continued support and a cost-of-living stipend.

The fellowship is funded by Mercedes-Benz and run by The DO School Fellowships in Hamburg, Germany. It is delivered in English in a hybrid format and includes regional summits where fellows meet in person. Applications are now open for the 2027/28 fellowship year.

Eligibility depends on where you live, not your passport. In Africa, residents of Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zimbabwe can apply, alongside residents of Europe, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Türkiye, the UK and the US.
opportunities.benefits: Project scholarships of up to EUR 15,000, available at the end of the first year; a cost-of-living stipend in the second year (amount not stated); innovation training, one-to-one mentoring and travel to regional summits.
requirements: Aged 18 to 28 on 31 January 2027
Resident in one of the listed countries (in Africa: Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda or Zimbabwe)
Strong command of English
Has identified an environmental problem to solve
Neither you nor a parent or guardian works for Mercedes-Benz
Able to commit at least 24 hours a month in year one
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on their written answers and their recorded interview video, which is also used to judge English ability. The number of fellows is not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: beVisioneers was launched in 2023 by Mercedes-Benz and is delivered by The DO School Fellowships gGmbH, a Hamburg-based organisation that trains young changemakers to launch social and environmental projects.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply on the beVisioneers DreamApply portal (applications.bevisioneers.world), answering the written questions and recording the video interview before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Check the full residence list on the official eligibility page before applying; residents of countries such as Nigeria and Ghana are not eligible in this round.

opportunities.title: Morgan State University Martin D. Jenkins Honors Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Incoming honors college students, including international applicants, compete for a renewable tuition scholarship.

opportunities.title: NL Scholarship at Radboud University 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students with a non-Dutch bachelor's who apply to an English-taught Radboud master's for 2027-28 and to the Radboud Scholarship Programme can be considered for €5,000.
opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship at Radboud University in Nijmegen is a one-off award of €5,000 for students from outside the EU/EEA who start an English-taught master's programme. It is paid for jointly by the Dutch Ministry of Education and the university, and up to 32 awards are available for 2027-28.

It is a partial award, not a full scholarship, and can only be given together with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP), so applicants must apply for both. Faculties judge candidates on academic excellence and ambition.

African students who hold a bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands and are fully admitted to a regular English-taught master's (not an Erasmus Mundus or joint degree) can apply. The application must be in OSIRIS by 31 January 2027 and complete by 14 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €5,000, awarded once for one year. It does not cover the full cost of study.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA passport and not eligible for the lower EU/EEA fee
Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch education
Meet the English proficiency requirement
Full admission to an English-taught Radboud master's (not Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree)
Apply also for the Radboud Scholarship Programme
Full-time enrolment and compliance with visa rules
documents: Master's application in OSIRIS with the NL Scholarship indicated
opportunities.selection_process: Each faculty assesses academic excellence (grades, test scores, publications, relevance of the degree, standing of the university) and ambition (motivation, promise, life experience and extracurricular activities). Decisions are expected around mid-April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Radboud University is a public research university in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, with about 24,000 students. It offers many English-taught master's programmes and runs its own scholarship programme for talented non-EU students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your English-taught master's in OSIRIS and indicate the NL Scholarship by 31 January 2027, then make sure the application is complete by 14 February 2027. Apply for the Radboud Scholarship Programme at the same time, since the NL Scholarship cannot be awarded on its own.
opportunities.notes: Part of the page still refers to 2026 admission; confirm details with the scholarships office by email.

opportunities.title: NNPC Ltd / TotalEnergies International Master's Scholarship 2027/2028 (France)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded master's study in France for Nigerian graduates sponsored by NNPC Limited and TotalEnergies.

opportunities.title: Nanyang Business School PhD Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with a strong Honours (Distinction) bachelor's degree can apply by 31 January 2027 for a funded Nanyang Business School PhD starting August 2027.
opportunities.description:
Nanyang Business School at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore admits PhD students once a year, for an August intake. For August 2027, applicants are considered for several funding routes: the NTU Research Scholarship, the Provost Graduate Award and the Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship, as well as self-funding.

The scholarships pay tuition and a living allowance for the whole scholarship period, with tuition covered for up to four years subject to yearly renewal. The school says there is no age or nationality restriction and that scholarships are open to international applicants and people without a business background.

For African graduates aiming at an academic career in business, finance, accounting or management, this is a fully funded PhD at one of Asia's top business schools.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fees and a monthly living allowance for the entire scholarship period, with tuition covered for up to 4 years subject to yearly renewal. The stipend amount is not stated on the school's pages.
requirements: Strong bachelor's degree with Honours (Distinction) or equivalent, and a master's if applicable
No age or nationality restriction
GMAT or GRE for most international applicants (guide scores: GRE verbal plus quantitative 319 or more and writing 3.5; GMAT 650 or GMAT Focus 595); waivers only in exceptional cases
TOEFL 100 or IELTS 7 (guides) if the bachelor's was not taught in English
Full-time study
documents: Passport or ID and a passport photo
GMAT or GRE score report (taken within 5 years)
TOEFL or IELTS report (within 2 years) if needed
Degree certificates and official transcripts with grading scale
Two academic references sent through the portal from official institutional emails
Research proposal of about 2 to 3 pages
Publications, awards or employment certificates if any
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed from January and shortlisted candidates are interviewed (January to February or March for the NTU Research Scholarship and self-funded routes; December to mid-January for the President's Graduate Scholarship). Outcomes are released between February and May.
important_dates: Enrolment: July 2027 for the August 2027 intake
opportunities.about_provider: Nanyang Business School is the business school of Nanyang Technological University, a leading public research university in Singapore. Its full-time PhD programme trains researchers in the main business disciplines.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through NTU's graduate admissions portal for the Nanyang Business School PhD, choosing your specialisation and funding route, and pay the application fee after submitting. Your referees receive a link and have 14 working days to send their reports.
opportunities.notes: Submit only one application; incomplete or late applications are rejected. The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship has its own earlier timeline, so check its page.

opportunities.title: Nova SBE PhD Research Fellowships
opportunities.provider: Nova School of Business and Economics
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to Nova SBE's 2027/28 PhD programmes are automatically considered for four-year fellowships paying EUR 1,400 a month; apply by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Nova School of Business and Economics in Lisbon automatically offers its strongest PhD applicants a four-year research fellowship. The fellowships come with the PhD programmes in economics, finance and management for the 2027/28 intake, and no separate scholarship application is needed: applying to the PhD is enough to be considered.

The fellowship pays a tax-free monthly stipend, waives most of the tuition and adds a yearly research allowance from the second year for conferences. It is renewed each year if progress is satisfactory, and a fifth year can be requested on academic merit.

For African graduates aiming at an academic or research career in economics or business, it is a funded doctorate at an internationally accredited European school. The same page also lists other funding sources for PhD students, such as FCT studentships, La Caixa INPhINIT and Camões Institute cooperation scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: A tax-free stipend of EUR 16,800 per year (EUR 1,400 per month), a 90% annual tuition waiver (worth about EUR 2,700), and from the second year a EUR 1,000 research allowance for conferences, for four years.
requirements: Apply to a Nova SBE PhD programme for the 2027/28 intake
Fellowships go to the top-ranked applicants
Renewal each year depends on satisfactory progress
documents: Nova SBE PhD online application (documents listed on the PhD admission page)
opportunities.selection_process: The top applicants to the PhD programmes are offered the fellowship automatically. Applicants may be invited to an online interview, and decisions are sent by email.
opportunities.about_provider: Nova SBE is the business and economics school of NOVA University Lisbon, Portugal, and holds AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA accreditation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit an online application to the chosen Nova SBE PhD programme between 1 October and 31 January via the PhD admission page; there is no separate fellowship form.
opportunities.notes: Contact the PhD Office at phd@novasbe.pt. Other external PhD funding options are listed on the same page with their own deadlines.

opportunities.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship at Laurentian University (International Applicants) 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students enrolled, or planning to enrol, full-time in a master's or doctoral programme at Laurentian University in 2027-2028 can apply through the international application form.
opportunities.description:
The Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) is a merit-based award funded through the Province of Ontario for students in research master's and doctoral programmes. Laurentian University in Sudbury, Ontario, runs its own OGS competition and has opened applications for the Fall 2027-2028 award year.

The award is for students who are already enrolled, or will be enrolled, full-time in graduate studies at Laurentian in 2027-2028. Laurentian provides a separate International Student Application Form, which confirms that international students can compete, making it one of the few provincial graduate awards in Canada open to African applicants.

The Laurentian page does not give the award value or minimum grades, so check the OGS rules or contact the graduate studies office before you apply.
opportunities.benefits: A merit-based Ontario Graduate Scholarship for the 2027-2028 academic year. The amount is not stated on Laurentian's page.
requirements: Enrolled, or planning to enrol, full-time in a master's or doctoral programme at Laurentian University in 2027-2028
International applicants use the International Student Application Form
Strong academic merit (the award is merit-based)
Two referees willing to submit references
documents: Completed OGS International Student Application Form
Two references, each sent directly by the referee through the Referee Submission Form
opportunities.about_provider: Laurentian University is a bilingual public university in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada, teaching in English and French. Its Faculty of Graduate Studies offers master's and doctoral programmes and manages internal and external graduate awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose the International Student Application Form on Laurentian's graduate scholarships page, complete it, and ask two referees to send the Referee Submission Form directly. Send questions to graduatestudies@laurentian.ca.
opportunities.notes: Laurentian also gives an automatic Dean's Entrance Scholarship to new graduate students (CAD 1,500 for master's and CAD 3,000 for doctoral students), with no application needed.

opportunities.title: RCELL International Conference 2027: Literature in the Age of AI (online)
opportunities.provider: Research Centre for English Language and Literature (RCELL)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Faculty, researchers, doctoral and postdoctoral scholars and independent scholars in English studies can register and send an abstract by 31 January 2027 for this two-day online conference (international fee USD 25 to 30).
opportunities.description:
The RCELL International Conference 2027, "Literature in the Age of AI: Posthumanism, Digital Humanities, and Ecological Futures", is a two-day online conference on 13 and 14 February 2027. It is held on Zoom, with keynotes also streamed on YouTube, so participants can join from anywhere.

It is organised by the Research Centre for English Language and Literature (RCELL) in India with two partner institutions, Sahrdaya College of Advanced Studies in Kerala and Sri Guru Granth Sahib World University in Punjab. Presenters give a 5 to 10 minute live talk, and selected full papers may be invited for a special issue of the journal The Criterion after peer review.

Because it is fully online and the fees are low, it is an easy way for African literature and English studies scholars to present work internationally without travel costs. This is a conference call rather than a funded award.
opportunities.benefits: An online presentation slot, written feedback on every abstract, an e-certificate, inclusion in an ISBN Book of Abstracts and a possible invitation to submit a full paper to The Criterion. No fee waivers or grants are mentioned.
requirements: Faculty, researchers, doctoral and postdoctoral scholars or independent scholars in English studies and related fields
Abstract of 250 to 300 words with 4 to 6 keywords and a bio of up to 75 words
Each co-author registers and pays separately (up to two co-authors)
Up to two papers per person
Disclosure of any generative AI use
documents: Online registration and abstract form with payment ID
Abstract, keywords, short bio and choice of one of four streams
Slides and a backup video by 8 February 2027 (presenters)
opportunities.selection_process: Every abstract receives written feedback within 15 days (7 days for those sent after 31 December). Full papers invited after the conference go through independent peer review, and an invitation does not guarantee publication.
opportunities.about_provider: The Research Centre for English Language and Literature (RCELL) is an Indian research and events organisation in English studies that runs international conferences with academic partner institutions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the single Google Form linked on the conference site, paying the fee through Razorpay and entering the payment ID, and submit your abstract in the same form. International presenters pay USD 25 by 31 December 2026 or USD 30 by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Fees are non-refundable except for duplicate payments. Contact conference@rcell.co.in.

opportunities.title: Radboud Scholarship Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to an English-taught Radboud master's starting September 2027 may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of 32 tuition-reduction scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Radboud Scholarship Programme helps highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA take a full English-taught master's at Radboud University in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. It is very selective: for 2027/2028 there are at most 32 scholarships spread across the faculties of Arts, Law, Management, Philosophy and Theology, Science and Social Sciences.

The scholarship does not pay living costs, but it cuts the tuition fee to the much lower Dutch statutory level and covers the costs of the visa and residence permit as well as health and liability insurance. It is funded from the university's Profiling Fund and lasts for the nominal length of the master's; the second-year grant requires all first-year courses to be passed.

For African students who can fund their living costs, it turns a costly Dutch master's into an affordable one. Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree master's are excluded.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition reduced from the full non-EU rate (around EUR 19,000, depending on the programme) to about EUR 2,771 (amount to be confirmed), plus the costs of the visa and residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance through Aon Student Insurance. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Passport from a non-EU/non-EEA country and not eligible for EU fees
Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch degree or education
Meets the English requirement of the chosen master's
Full admission to an English-taught master's starting 1 September 2027
Able to meet Dutch visa conditions and study full time
documents: Master's application in OSIRIS with all required documents
opportunities.selection_process: Faculties judge academic excellence (grades, test scores, publications, relevance and ranking of previous university), ambition (motivation letter, promise, life and extracurricular experience) and the quality of the reference letters. Some programmes interview candidates. The final decision comes before mid-April 2027.
important_dates: Submit application in OSIRIS: 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET
Application complete (including references and CV): 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET
opportunities.about_provider: Radboud University in Nijmegen is a Dutch research university with about 20 English-taught master's areas across seven faculties. Its scholarships are paid from the university's own Profiling Fund.
opportunities.how_to_apply: When applying for your master's in OSIRIS Application, indicate that you want to be considered for the Radboud Scholarship, then upload two reference letters and your CV. Master's admission and the scholarship are handled separately, and incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Places by faculty: Science 10, Social Sciences 8, Management 6, Arts 3, Law 3, Philosophy/Theology/Religious Studies 2. The NL Scholarship can be combined with it. Contact: scholarships@ru.nl.

opportunities.title: SampTA 2027: 16th International Conference on Sampling Theory and Applications (call for papers)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematicians, engineers and applied scientists can submit four-page papers by 31 January 2027 for SampTA 2027 in Utrecht (26 to 30 July 2027).
opportunities.description:
SampTA 2027 is the 16th International Conference on Sampling Theory and Applications, a biennial meeting for mathematicians, engineers and applied scientists working on sampling, signal processing and related mathematics. It takes place in Utrecht, the Netherlands, from 26 to 30 July 2027, with nine plenary speakers.

The conference is hosted by Utrecht University with sponsors including IEEE and URASIP. Accepted papers are presented as a talk or poster, and papers from authors who attend are published in IEEE Xplore.

This is a call for papers rather than a funded award. It suits African researchers in applied mathematics, signal processing and data science who want a specialised, IEEE-indexed venue.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at SampTA 2027 and publication in IEEE Xplore for attending authors. Fees, travel grants or waivers are not stated.
requirements: Original research on sampling theory and applications
Paper of no more than 4 pages including figures and tables, in IEEE conference style (IEEEtran LaTeX); references do not count
Accepted papers must be presented as a poster or talk
Keep LaTeX sources for the final version
documents: PDF paper of up to 4 pages in IEEE format
opportunities.selection_process: Papers go through single-blind peer review, with acceptance announced on 15 April 2027. Publication in IEEE Xplore depends on attendance and on IEEE scope and quality checks.
opportunities.about_provider: Utrecht University is a leading Dutch public research university, here hosting the SampTA conference series on sampling theory with support from IEEE and URASIP.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper in the IEEE conference template and submit it through the link that will be posted on the SampTA 2027 call for papers page. Check the page regularly, since the submission link was not yet live on 19 November 2026.
opportunities.notes: The submission portal had not been published as of 19 November 2026.

opportunities.title: Scripps College Financial Aid for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Scripps College for fall 2027 who need help paying can apply for limited need-based aid by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Scripps College, a liberal arts college for women in Claremont, California, offers a limited amount of need-based financial aid to international students. Aid is only awarded at the moment of admission, so students who want help must apply for it together with their application for fall 2027 entry.

This is not a fixed-amount scholarship. The college assesses each family's finances through the College Board CSS Profile and IDOC service and builds an aid package from that. Once awarded, aid can be renewed each year for up to eight semesters, as long as the student stays full time and makes satisfactory academic progress.

Scripps is need aware for international applicants, which means asking for aid can affect the admission decision. African applicants who need support should still apply for it at the start, because aid cannot be requested later.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based institutional aid towards the cost of attending, renewable for up to 8 semesters with full-time study and satisfactory progress. The page does not state amounts or the number of awards.
requirements: International applicant for first-year entry in fall 2027 (Early Decision II or Regular Decision)
Must show financial need through the CSS Profile and IDOC
Must show resources to cover the cost of attendance not met by aid
Aid must be requested at the time of admission; it is not offered later
documents: Parents' signed 2025 foreign income tax returns, uploaded to IDOC
Professional translations of the parents' latest tax return and wage statements (or an employer wage statement if no return is filed)
2027-2028 Parent and Student Non-Tax Filer Statements, where applicable
Scripps International Student Financial Form, uploaded to the Admission Applicant Status Page
opportunities.selection_process: The financial aid office reviews the CSS Profile and IDOC documents to work out need. Because Scripps is need aware for international students, the admission decision may take the aid request into account. Detailed criteria are not stated.
important_dates: Early Decision I aid deadline: 15 November 2026 (passed)
Early Decision II and Regular Decision: all documents to IDOC by 31 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Scripps College is a private liberal arts college in Claremont, California, and a member of the Claremont Colleges consortium. Its financial aid office handles need-based aid for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the CSS Profile, then upload the tax and wage documents to College Board IDOC, which takes 7 to 10 business days to process. Upload the Scripps International Student Financial Form to your Admission Applicant Status Page rather than to IDOC. Check the Financial Aid Checklist on your status page to make sure everything has arrived.
opportunities.notes: Documents sent after the deadline can lead to less aid or none at all. Translations are at the family's own cost. Aid is limited, so apply early and complete every document.

opportunities.title: University of Glasgow Computing Science PhD Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a good computing degree, including international students, can apply by 31 January 2027 for Glasgow Computing Science PhD funding starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The School of Computing Science at the University of Glasgow funds PhD students who start in October 2027 or soon after through one competition that covers several scholarship schemes. Applicants are considered for whichever schemes suit them, including the College of Science and Engineering Graduate School Scholarships, College Scholarships, Excellence Bursaries and the part-time Minerva Scholarships.

Coverage differs between schemes. The Graduate School Scholarships pay fees (home or international) and a stipend for three years, while the Excellence Bursary for international students is a fee discount of GBP 10,000 a year. Stipends usually follow the UKRI rate, which is GBP 22,437 for 2027-28.

International applicants, including those from Africa, apply through the normal PhD admission system and simply select the university scholarship as their funding source. The school suggests PhD projects on its website, and contacting a potential supervisor first helps.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: tuition fees (home or international) plus a stipend of GBP 22,437 for 2027-28 for three years (Graduate School Scholarships); home-level fees plus UKRI stipend (College Scholarships); a GBP 10,000 a year fee discount for three years for international students (Excellence Bursaries); or a five-year part-time Minerva post with home-level fees and pay of at least GBP 24,000 a year.
requirements: Upper second-class honours undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree in computing science or a related field
Applying for a PhD in the School of Computing Science starting October 2027 or shortly after
Meets the University of Glasgow English requirements
documents: Documents listed on the university's before-you-apply page (transcripts, references, research proposal or statement)
opportunities.selection_process: Academic admission and scholarship applications are processed separately; scholarship decisions are confirmed with candidates around April 2027. The number of awards and detailed criteria are not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow is one of the UK's oldest universities and a member of the Russell Group. Its School of Computing Science is consistently ranked among the top ten in the UK.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate research application, and choose 'Univ of Glasgow Scholarship' as your funding source. Look at the school's suggested PhD projects and contact a supervisor before applying.
opportunities.notes: Contact: socs-pgr-enquiries@glasgow.ac.uk. The James McCune Smith scholarship listed on the same page is for Black UK-domiciled students only.

opportunities.title: Anders Wall's Scholarship for Studies at Uppsala University 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of African countries who apply to an Uppsala bachelor's or master's programme as first choice for autumn 2027 and must pay tuition can apply for a full tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Anders Wall's Scholarship for Studies at Uppsala University is a tuition award reserved for citizens of African countries. It covers the full tuition fee for a bachelor's or master's programme at Uppsala University in Sweden, starting in autumn 2027.

The award is merit-based; financial need is not considered, but recipients must be able to pay their own living costs, as required for a Swedish residence permit. Applicants must rank their Uppsala programme first on universityadmissions.se before the national admissions deadline.

The scholarship application itself is short: an online form and a motivation letter of no more than 350 words, with no documents and no fee. The window is open from 16 January to 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee for the bachelor's or master's programme. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of an African country
Liable to pay tuition fees in Sweden
Uppsala programme ranked first on universityadmissions.se, applied for before the national deadline
Meet the programme's entry requirements
Strong academic record
Some programmes are excluded (see the official list)
documents: Online scholarship form with your 8-digit application number
Motivation letter of up to 350 words
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on academic merit; financial need is not a factor.
opportunities.about_provider: Uppsala University, founded in 1477, is the oldest university in the Nordic countries and one of Europe's leading research universities. Its tuition scholarships are funded partly by donors such as the businessman Anders Wall.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your Uppsala programme as first priority on universityadmissions.se and note your application number. Then fill in the online scholarship form between 16 January and 1 February 2027 and add your motivation letter.
opportunities.notes: No application fee and no extra documents. You must show you can fund living costs to get a residence permit.

opportunities.title: Brown University Need-Blind Financial Aid for International First-Year Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying to start at Brown as first-year undergraduates are admitted need-blind and can request need-based aid; Regular Decision aid forms are due 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island, admits international first-year undergraduates on a need-blind basis, which means asking for financial aid does not count against an applicant in admission. Students apply for need-based aid at the same time as they apply for admission, and Brown builds an aid package from the family's financial information.

The aid application runs through the College Board CSS Profile, which opens on 1 October, with supporting tax or earnings documents sent through IDOC when requested. If the aid documents arrive by the deadline, the student receives a provisional aid offer together with the admission decision.

For talented African students, need-blind admission at an Ivy League university is a rare opening, because it removes money from the admission decision. The current aid deadlines are 2 November 2026 for Early Decision (passed) and 1 February 2027 for Regular Decision.
opportunities.benefits: Institutional need-based aid based on the family's demonstrated need. Amounts are not stated; they depend on each family's finances.
requirements: Applying for first-year undergraduate entry as an international student
Must apply for aid at the time of admission through the CSS Profile
Each parent completes a CSS Profile if parents are divorced or separated
Applicants from Iran or North Korea, who cannot use the CSS Profile, must email the aid office
documents: Parents' income tax returns or non-tax-filer statements if requested through IDOC
Employer earnings statements if no tax return is filed
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is need-blind, so the aid request does not affect the admission decision. The aid office reviews the CSS Profile and documents to calculate need and sends a provisional offer with the admission decision when materials arrive on time.
opportunities.about_provider: Brown University is a private Ivy League research university in Providence, Rhode Island, founded in 1764. Its Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid handles need-based aid for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the CSS Profile online and list Brown (code 3189). Upload any documents the College Board IDOC service asks for. Contact financial_aid@brown.edu or +1 401-863-1000 with questions.
opportunities.notes: Brown does not give CSS Profile fee waivers. The ISFAA form and paper CSS forms are not accepted in place of the online CSS Profile.

opportunities.title: Centre College Language Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International and domestic first-year applicants to Centre College for Fall 2027 who want to study Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Latin or Spanish can apply for a renewable language scholarship of up to USD 5,000 a year on top of general merit aid.
opportunities.description:
Centre College, a private liberal arts college in Danville, Kentucky, offers Language Scholarships to incoming first-year students who want to pursue a language and its culture. The award is open to both international and domestic students entering in Fall 2027, and no major or minor in the language is required.

The scholarship is worth up to USD 5,000 a year, is renewable, and can be combined with Centre's general merit scholarships, which for international applicants are typically USD 15,000 to 30,000 a year and awarded automatically. Recipients must keep at least a 3.0 GPA in their language courses and are expected to study abroad.

For African students this is a way to reduce the cost of a US liberal arts education, especially combined with general merit aid. Applicants may even apply in their native language, but only one language scholarship can be held, and Spanish applicants must record a short video in Spanish.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 per year, renewable, stackable with general merit scholarships (USD 15,000-30,000 per year for international applicants). International students should plan for roughly USD 25,000 a year in remaining costs according to the college.
requirements: First-year applicant for Fall 2027 (international or domestic)
Interest in Chinese (Mandarin), French, German, Japanese, Latin or Spanish
Complete Common App or Coalition App and all admission items
Only one language scholarship per student
English proficiency for international applicants: TOEFL iBT 93, IELTS 7.0, PTE 64, Duolingo 125, TOEFL Essentials 9.5, or a waiver request
To renew: minimum 3.0 GPA in target-language courses and study abroad
documents: Common App or Coalition App with 500-650 word essay
Official transcripts (with certified literal translations if not in English)
Language scholarship form: language course list, AP/IB results, 500-word essay, weighted and unweighted GPA
Spanish applicants: YouTube video answering three prompts in Spanish (about one minute each)
opportunities.selection_process: After reviewing all application materials, Centre judges applicants' interest in the language and its culture; Spanish videos are assessed for conversational ability. Scholarship decisions are sent by mid-March.
opportunities.about_provider: Centre College is a private liberal arts college in Danville, Kentucky, USA. It awards merit, premier and special-interest scholarships, and gives international applicants general merit awards automatically.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Centre through the Common App or Coalition App, then complete the online Language Scholarship form for the Fall 2027 term with your essay and language details. Submit by the deadline of your admission round.
opportunities.notes: Centre also runs the Lincoln Scholars Program (full funding, separate application due 1 December) and Performing Arts and Studio Arts scholarships of up to USD 5,000. Contact intladmission@centre.edu.

opportunities.title: Dartmouth College Need-Blind Aid for International Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Dartmouth admits international applicants need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated need; Regular Decision aid forms are due 1 February.

opportunities.title: EMBL EIPOD-LinC Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality with a PhD by 1 February 2027 and up to eight years of research experience can apply for a fully funded three-year interdisciplinary postdoc at EMBL with a partner secondment.
opportunities.description:
EIPOD-LinC (Exploring Life in Context) is EMBL's interdisciplinary postdoctoral fellowship programme. Fellows design their own three-year project with an EMBL host group and an external partner, and spend between three months and one year on secondment at the partner lab. Projects are based at one of EMBL's sites in Heidelberg, Barcelona, Grenoble, Hamburg, Rome or EMBL-EBI near Cambridge.

The programme is co-funded by the EU's Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions and offers fully funded contracts. The current call (named the 2026 call) opens on 25 November 2026 and closes on 1 February 2027, with the latest start date in September 2027.

The fellowship is open to experienced researchers of all nationalities, so African scientists in molecular biology, computation, ecology and related fields can apply, although the external partner must be in an EMBL member, associate or prospect state.
opportunities.benefits: A fully funded three-year postdoctoral contract at EMBL, including a secondment of 3 months to 1 year with the external partner. Salary rates are given in a separate EMBL rates document and are not stated on the page.
requirements: Open to experienced researchers of all nationalities
PhD held by 1 February 2027 (defended but not yet awarded is accepted)
No more than eight years of research experience since the PhD (career breaks do not count)
No more than 12 months spent at EMBL or the partner in the last 3 years
An EMBL host group and an external partner in an EMBL member, associate or prospect member state
documents: Project proposal on the official template (one project only)
Two reference letters with the cover page
All files combined into one PDF
opportunities.selection_process: Three external experts assess each proposal for excellence, impact and implementation. A committee then shortlists candidates, who are interviewed on Zoom with a 10-minute talk and a 30-minute panel discussion. Applications may be screened with AI-detection tools and AI use must be declared.
opportunities.about_provider: The European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) is Europe's flagship intergovernmental laboratory for the life sciences, with six sites across Europe. It runs research, services, training and international postdoctoral programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the applicant guide, agree a project with an EMBL host and an external partner, and complete the application form and project template. Submit everything through the EMBL portal once the call opens on 25 November 2026, and ask your referees to send their letters. Questions go to eipod@embl.org.
opportunities.notes: Only one project proposal per applicant is allowed. EMBL also runs the EIPOD4 and ARISE2 fellowship programmes.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Smart Cities and Communities (SMACCs) 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: SMACCs Erasmus Mundus consortium (UMONS, IHU, University of Vaasa, UPV/EHU)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Engineering and science graduates (minimum 180 ECTS) with English at IELTS 6.5 or equivalent can apply by 1 February 2027 for SMACCs 2027-2029 and its Erasmus Mundus scholarships of EUR 1,400 a month.
opportunities.description:
SMACCs is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in Smart Cities and Communities, taught in English and co-funded by the European Union. Students move between partner universities: the Université de Mons in Belgium (coordinator), the International Hellenic University in Greece, the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) in Spain, which awards the degree, and the University of Vaasa in Finland.

The programme trains engineers and scientists to design energy-efficient, connected and sustainable cities. The 2027-2029 edition starts in September 2027, and applicants who want an Erasmus Mundus or other scholarship must apply by 1 February 2027; self-funded applicants have later deadlines.

African applicants have good chances: part of the scholarships are reserved for nationals of listed regions that include Sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa, with priority for least-developed countries.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months, with no tuition fees, covering travel, visa, installation and living costs. Consortium and associated partner scholarships cover part of the tuition. Erasmus+ grants for inter-semester mobility are also available. 95 EMJM scholarships across four editions, including 35 for listed regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in engineering or science (such as physics, chemistry, mathematics or computer science) of at least 3 years / 180 ECTS; arts, social science, business and law degrees are not eligible except case by case
Final-year students can apply if the degree is awarded before 15 September 2027
English: TOEFL iBT 90, TOEIC 850, IELTS 6.5 (at least 5.5 per band), Cambridge CPE/CAE/FCE or B2; degrees taught in English in South Africa, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia or New Zealand are accepted
No more than 10% of the open scholarships go to one nationality
documents: Online application form with language certificate
CV with work and R&D experience
Originals at registration and UPV/EHU recognition of foreign qualifications before enrolment
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants receive a merit score based on academic records, motivation letter, work and research experience and references. The best scholarship applicants are interviewed online in April 2027, and awards depend on the interview, funds and geographic balance.
opportunities.about_provider: SMACCs is run by a consortium led by the Université de Mons (UMONS) in Belgium with the International Hellenic University, the University of the Basque Country and the University of Vaasa, and is co-funded by the EU's Erasmus+ programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the SMACCs application page before 1 February 2027; applying by this date automatically puts you forward for a scholarship unless you untick the box. Send TOEFL scores directly to UMONS (code C194) and start the UPV/EHU foreign qualification process early.
opportunities.notes: Students must complete the programme in two consecutive academic years. Contact is through the SMACCs contact form.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus SARENA Master in Safe and Reliable Nuclear Applications 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates in nuclear engineering, engineering, physics or chemistry can apply by 1 February 2027 for the SARENA 2027-2029 Erasmus Mundus master's and its scholarships.
opportunities.description:
SARENA (SAfe and REliable Nuclear Applications) is a two-year, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in nuclear engineering, taught fully in English. It covers radioactive waste management and decommissioning, and nuclear reactor operation and safety.

The programme is coordinated by IMT Atlantique in Nantes, France, with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, LUT University in Finland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia. Students choose one of two tracks, each leading to a double degree: Radioactive Waste Management and Decommissioning (France and Spain) or Nuclear Reactor Operation and Safety (Finland and Slovenia).

Applications for the 2027-2029 intake opened on 16 October 2026 and close on 1 February 2027, for both scholarship and self-funded applicants. African science and engineering graduates interested in nuclear safety and energy can compete for the EU-funded Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: Scholarship options include the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship and a Top-Excellence fee waiver, among others; amounts are not stated on the pages read.
requirements: Bachelor's or equivalent in nuclear engineering, engineering or sciences such as physics or chemistry
Programme taught fully in English
Open to scholarship and self-funded applicants
documents: Online application in the SARENA portal (the pages read do not list documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed after the February deadline and results are usually released by early April.
opportunities.about_provider: IMT Atlantique is a French graduate engineering school (grande école) that coordinates SARENA, an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master funded by the European Union with partners in Spain, Finland and Slovenia.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the SARENA application portal at IMT Atlantique and submit the course application for the 2027-2029 intake before 1 February 2027. Check the programme's fees and scholarship, admissions and FAQ pages for document and language requirements.
opportunities.notes: The same campaign covers both EMJM scholarship and self-funded applicants, so tick the scholarship option if you need funding.

opportunities.title: Ernst Mach Follow-up Grant for Non-European Developing Countries 2027
opportunities.provider: OeAD (Austrian Agency for Education and Internationalisation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Postdocs and university lecturers from non-European developing countries who once held an OeAD scholarship, and whose last OeAD stay ended at least three years earlier, can apply by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Ernst Mach Follow-up Grant lets former OeAD scholarship holders from non-European developing countries come back to Austria for a research stay in the 2027-28 academic year. It is aimed at alumni who now work as postdoctoral researchers or lecturers at a university or other higher education institution at home.

The grant is part of the OeAD's family of Ernst Mach grants, which are mainly financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Women, Science and Research. The OeAD announced the 2027-28 round in a notice published on 28 September 2026, with an application deadline of 1 February 2027.

For African academics who studied or researched in Austria with OeAD support in the past, this is a way to renew links with Austrian colleagues and institutions.
opportunities.benefits: A research grant for a stay in Austria in 2027-28. The OeAD notice does not give the monthly amount or the length of the stay; these are in the grant's entry in the grants.at database.
requirements: Postdoctoral researcher or lecturer from a non-European developing country
Employed at a university or higher education institution
Previously held an OeAD scholarship
At least three years must have passed since the last OeAD-funded stay in Austria when the new grant starts
documents: Application through the OeAD online system as described in the grants.at entry (the notice does not list documents)
opportunities.selection_process: The notice does not describe the selection process.
opportunities.about_provider: The OeAD is Austria's agency for education and internationalisation, a non-profit company owned by the Republic of Austria. It runs Austria's government scholarship programmes for international students and researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the Ernst Mach Follow-up Grant entry in the grants.at scholarship database for the full conditions, amount and application link, and submit before 1 February 2027. The OeAD notice links to that entry.
opportunities.notes: The OeAD also offers the Ernst Mach Grant worldwide (deadline 1 December 2026) and the Ernst Mach Grant for study at an Austrian university of applied sciences (deadline 1 February 2027).

opportunities.title: Ernst Mach Grant for Studying at an Austrian University of Applied Sciences 2027-28
opportunities.provider: OeAD (Austrian Agency for Education and Internationalisation)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and Master's students from non-European countries can apply by 1 February 2027 for a 4 to 10 month study stay at an Austrian university of applied sciences in 2027-28.
opportunities.description:
This Ernst Mach Grant lets Bachelor's and Master's students from countries outside Europe spend between four and ten months studying at an Austrian university of applied sciences (Fachhochschule) during the 2027-28 academic year. Extensions are not possible.

The grant is run by the OeAD, Austria's agency for education and internationalisation, as part of the Ernst Mach family of grants, which are mainly funded by Austrian federal ministries. The OeAD announced the 2027-28 round on 28 September 2026 with a deadline of 1 February 2027.

For African students already enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's at home, it offers a practical semester or year in Austria's applied, industry-linked universities.
opportunities.benefits: A study grant for 4 to 10 months at an Austrian university of applied sciences. The OeAD notice does not state the monthly amount; it is given in the grant's grants.at entry.
requirements: Bachelor's or Master's student from a non-European country
Study stay at an Austrian university of applied sciences in 2027-28
Stay of 4 to 10 months, with no extension
documents: Application through the OeAD system as described in the grants.at entry (the notice does not list documents)
opportunities.selection_process: The OeAD notice does not describe the selection process.
opportunities.about_provider: The OeAD is Austria's agency for education and internationalisation, a non-profit company owned by the Republic of Austria. It manages Austria's government scholarships, funded mainly by federal ministries, the Austrian Development Agency and the European Commission.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the grant's entry in the grants.at database, which the OeAD notice links to, for the amount, documents and online application link, and apply before 1 February 2027. Contact the host university of applied sciences early about your study plan.
opportunities.notes: The OeAD also offers the Ernst Mach Grant worldwide for PhD students and researchers (deadline 1 December 2026).

opportunities.title: HBKU Graduate Admission and Scholarships (Master's and PhD)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to HBKU master's and PhD programmes are automatically considered for tuition waivers and monthly stipends if they apply by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) in Doha, Qatar, considers every graduate applicant for funding as part of the admission process, so there is no separate scholarship form. Awards are based on merit or need and depend on the funds available, and they are not guaranteed.

Funding has two parts. Tuition waivers range from 100% for PhD programmes to 60% or 75% for many master's degrees, and some programmes (LL.M., MS Economics and certificates) have no waiver. International students who are selected also receive a monthly stipend for the length of the programme and one round-trip air ticket.

The online application for the next intake opened on 1 October 2026, and international applicants must apply by 1 February 2027. For African graduates, this is one of the most generous funded routes in the Gulf, especially for PhD study in STEM and the social sciences.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition waivers of 100% for PhD (STEM, SHAPE) and S.J.D., 75% for STEM MS, 60% for SHAPE MS/MA and J.D., and 0% for LL.M., MS Economics and certificates. International PhD students receive QAR 9,000 a month (QAR 108,000 a year) for up to 45 months; international master's students receive QAR 7,000 a month (QAR 84,000 a year) for up to 21 months. One round-trip airfare for international students. Students pay for their own housing.
requirements: Admission to an HBKU master's or PhD programme
International applicants must apply by 1 February 2027
Funding is merit or need based and subject to available funds
Stipend holders work about 10 hours a week as research assistants
Up to two applications per academic year
documents: Supporting documents uploaded in the portal (the pages read do not list them)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications pass a preliminary review by the college and the admissions office, followed by an offer letter. Scholarship decisions are made at the same time, based on merit, need and the funds available.
important_dates: Deadline for Qatari and resident applicants seeking funding: 15 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Hamad Bin Khalifa University is a research university in Education City, Doha, founded by Qatar Foundation. It offers multidisciplinary graduate programmes in science, engineering, health, law, policy, Islamic studies and the humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the HBKU application portal, choose your college and programme, upload your documents and invite your referees. You do not need a separate scholarship application. Ask your chosen college about funding questions, or write to admissions@hbku.edu.qa.
opportunities.notes: Housing is not covered, so budget for it. Teaching assistant and other paid campus work can add to the stipend.

opportunities.title: HIAS Fellowships 2028-29
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars with a doctorate and artists at any career stage, of any nationality and with excellent English, can apply for a residential fellowship in Hamburg between October 2028 and June 2029.
opportunities.description:
The Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study (HIAS) offers residential fellowships that bring scholars and artists to Hamburg to work on their own projects in dialogue with partners in the city. The 2028-29 fellowship year runs from 1 October 2028 to 30 June 2029, and the preferred stay is at least three months.

Each fellow works with a 'tandem partner' at a Hamburg institution. Applicants only need to name a possible partner; prior contact is not required. HIAS values interdisciplinary profiles and aims for a diverse group of fellows.

The call is open to all nationalities, so African researchers and artists can apply. The deadline is 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET.
opportunities.benefits: Either a stipend paid to the fellow or partial reimbursement to the home institution for the cost of a teaching replacement (amount not stated). Office space is provided, and guesthouse accommodation may be available.
requirements: Scholars: a doctorate
Artists: any career stage
Excellent command of English
Name a tandem partner at a Hamburg institution
Applicants based in the Hamburg metropolitan region are not eligible
Preferred stay of at least three months within October 2028 to June 2029
documents: Letter of intent from the tandem partner, if already agreed (max 1 page)
opportunities.selection_process: HIAS weighs the doctorate and publications (scholars) or exhibitions and performances (artists), interdisciplinary profile, prizes, English, fit of the project with Hamburg partners, and the diversity of the fellow group.
opportunities.about_provider: The Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study is an institute for advanced study founded by Hamburg's universities and cultural institutions. It hosts international fellows from the sciences, humanities and arts and links them with partners across the city.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the documents listed on the HIAS application page and submit them through the online application form before 1 February 2027. The form also asks whether AI tools were used.
opportunities.notes: HIAS also runs a joint fellowship with IFSH on peace and security (deadline 16 November 2026).

opportunities.title: Hilary and Galen Weston International Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students entering Huron University College who have overcome serious hardship, especially those coming directly from challenging environments abroad, can apply by 1 February 2027 for a full-ride award.
opportunities.description:
The Hilary and Galen Weston International Scholarship is a full-ride, four-year award at Huron University College in London, Ontario. It is part of the Weston International Scholars Program, funded by a CAD 1.8 million gift from The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation, which will support twelve international students from underserved regions between 2025 and 2030.

The award pays for tuition, fees, housing, meals, books and supplies, so it covers almost the full cost of study. It is aimed at students who have shown resilience and perseverance in the face of real adversity, with preference for those coming straight from difficult environments overseas.

This makes it one of the most relevant Canadian awards for African students from low-income or crisis-affected backgrounds. Huron even lists an admissions adviser for Africa and Europe on the programme page.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition, ancillary and student fees, housing, meals, books and supplies, renewable for up to four years.
requirements: Entering international undergraduate student for 2027-28
Evidence of resilience and perseverance in overcoming significant adversity
Academic potential and achievements
Community involvement and clear future goals
Preference for students coming directly from challenging environments overseas
documents: Common Scholarship Application in the Huron Connect Portal
Letter of recommendation from your school counsellor
List of extracurricular activities and achievements
Statement of purpose of up to 1,000 words
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on resilience and determination, academic potential and achievements, and community involvement and aspirations. Only a small number of awards are made.
important_dates: Common Scholarship Application opens in the Huron Connect Portal: late November 2026
opportunities.about_provider: Huron University College is a liberal arts university college affiliated with Western University in London, Ontario, Canada. Its Weston International Scholars Program is funded by The Hilary and Galen Weston Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Huron first, then complete the Common Scholarship Application in the Huron Connect Portal, which opens to Huron applicants in late November 2026. Submit it with your counsellor's letter, activity list and statement of purpose by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Huron's International Admissions Advisor for Africa and Europe is Zayn Nasser (zayn.nasser@huron.uwo.ca). The same application also covers the Wes Hall Student Support Fund for eligible students.

opportunities.title: Huron International Presidential Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Incoming international undergraduates at Huron University College with a mid-year average of 90% or more and strong community involvement can apply by 1 February 2027 for full tuition and fees.
opportunities.description:
The International Presidential Scholarship is Huron University College's top entrance award for international students. It pays full tuition and ancillary fees and can be renewed for up to four years, covering a whole undergraduate degree.

Huron is a liberal arts college affiliated with Western University in London, Ontario, Canada. Applicants are considered through Huron's Common Scholarship Application for the 2027-28 academic year, which closes on 1 February 2027.

The award looks for top students with an average of at least 90% who are also very active outside the classroom. For high-achieving African school leavers, it is a route to a Canadian degree with tuition fully paid.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition and ancillary fees, renewable for up to four years.
requirements: Incoming international student starting in 2027-28
Mid-year average of 90% or higher, as calculated by Huron
Outstanding extracurricular and community involvement
A clear wish to contribute to global society
documents: Letter of recommendation from your school counsellor
List of extracurricular activities and achievements
Statement of purpose of up to 1,000 words, using the guiding questions in the application
opportunities.selection_process: Huron reviews applications through its Common Scholarship Application, looking at grades, community involvement and the statement of purpose. Detailed criteria are not stated.
important_dates: Common Scholarship Application opens in the Huron Connect Portal: late November 2026
opportunities.about_provider: Huron University College is a small liberal arts university college in London, Ontario, affiliated with Western University, whose students earn Western degrees. It offers several major entrance scholarships for international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Huron first, then complete the Common Scholarship Application in the Huron Connect Portal, which opens to Huron applicants in late November 2026. Submit it with your counsellor's letter, activity list and statement of purpose by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Contact admissions@huron.uwo.ca or financial.aid@huron.uwo.ca. The Common Scholarship Application also considers you for other Huron awards, such as the Hilary and Galen Weston International Scholarship.

opportunities.title: ICA 2027 Pre-conference: Centring Creators across Intersecting Ecosystems: Labour, Agency, and Collaboration (London)
opportunities.provider: ICA pre-conference organisers, King's College London
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers, creators and practitioners, especially early-career researchers and MA and PhD students, can submit abstracts and apply for a limited conference scholarship by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
This one-day pre-conference to the 2027 International Communication Association (ICA) conference takes place at King's College London on 2 June 2027. It focuses on content creators and the creator economy, looking at labour, agency and collaboration across platforms, media industries and communities.

The call is hosted by King's College London Digital Humanities, with organisers from LSE, KCL, USC Annenberg, the Hebrew University, City St George's, SOAS, UAL and Chulalongkorn University, among others, and is sponsored by KCL and the Content Creator Scholar Network.

A limited number of conference scholarships support participation, and early-career researchers and students are especially encouraged. African media and communication scholars studying creators, influencers and digital work can apply, and there is an email route for regions where Microsoft Forms is not available.
opportunities.benefits: A limited number of conference scholarships to support participation; amounts are not stated.
requirements: Open to researchers, creators, practitioners and industry professionals
Early-career researchers and MA and PhD students are specially encouraged
Abstracts of up to 500 words for papers or posters, or 800 words for panels, roundtables or sessions, excluding references
Up to six contributors per submission
A statement on use of generative AI
documents: Abstract with title, contributor names, affiliations, contact email, preferred format and 3 to 5 keywords
For scholarships: a statement of up to 200 words on why you need support and how attending helps your research or career
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are reviewed by the organising committee and authors are notified on 1 March 2027. Scholarship requests are reviewed alongside.
opportunities.about_provider: King's College London is a major public research university in London; its Department of Digital Humanities hosts this call. The International Communication Association is the leading global academic association for communication research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the Microsoft Forms link on the call page and, if you need support, the separate scholarship form, both by 1 February 2027. If Microsoft Forms is blocked in your country, email creatorcon@kcl.ac.uk with "Submission" or "Scholarship Application" in the subject line.
opportunities.notes: The ECREA notice header shows the deadline as 2026 by mistake; the organisers' page gives 1 February 2027.

opportunities.title: ICCCI 2027: 19th International Conference on Computational Collective Intelligence (call for papers)
opportunities.provider: University of Cadiz with Wroclaw University of Science and Technology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers working on computational collective intelligence can submit 12 to 15 page papers by 1 February 2027 for ICCCI 2027 in Cádiz, Spain (in-person presentation required).
opportunities.description:
ICCCI 2027 is the 19th International Conference on Computational Collective Intelligence, held at the University of Cádiz in Spain from 15 to 17 September 2027. It is organised jointly by Wroclaw University of Science and Technology in Poland and Complutense University of Madrid, in cooperation with the IEEE SMC Technical Committee on Computational Collective Intelligence and ERCIS.

The conference covers multi-agent systems, collective decision making, machine learning, knowledge engineering, social networks and related areas. Accepted papers appear in Springer's LNCS/LNAI and CCIS series, and the conference is ranked category B in the 2026 ICORE rankings.

This is a call for papers, not a funded award: authors must register, pay the fee and present in person. It is useful for African computer science researchers who want an indexed, well-ranked venue.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted papers in Springer LNCS/LNAI or CCIS, eligibility for best paper awards and possible invitations to extended journal special issues. Registration fees and any waivers are not stated.
requirements: Original work not under review elsewhere, written in English
Paper of 12 to 15 pages in Springer LNCS/LNAI style, as one PDF
At least one author must register, pay the fee and present in person
documents: Full paper PDF in Springer format submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed and authors are notified by 15 April 2027. Only papers presented in person can be nominated for the best paper award.
opportunities.about_provider: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology is a leading Polish technical university that has run the ICCCI series for many years with international partners; the 2027 edition is hosted by the University of Cádiz.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper in the Springer LNCS template and submit it through the ICCCI 2027 EasyChair page by 1 February 2027. Questions go to iccci@pwr.edu.pl.
opportunities.notes: The conference is on-site only, so plan visa and travel early if your paper is accepted.

opportunities.title: IEEE NEWCAS 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students worldwide working on circuits and systems.
opportunities.description:
The 25th IEEE Interregional NEWCAS Conference is a flagship conference of the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society, held in Cork, Ireland, from 20 to 23 June 2027 and organised with Tyndall National Institute and University College Dublin. The 2027 theme is AI-assisted design of circuits and systems.

The call covers analog and mixed-signal circuits, data converters, digital and embedded systems, biomedical and wearable devices, RF to terahertz circuits, power management, photonics, EDA, neuromorphic and AI hardware, hardware security, quantum and cryo-CMOS and emerging technologies. Papers are four pages in IEEE double-column format, plus an optional page of references.

It is a strong venue for African electronics and microelectronics researchers to present work and connect with the IEEE CAS community in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at the conference and publication of accepted papers through IEEE. Fees, travel grants and awards are not stated on the call.
requirements: Complete 4-page paper in IEEE double-column format, plus an optional page for references
PDF format only
Fits one of the listed tracks or a special session
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are reviewed by the technical programme committee, with decisions on 9 April 2027.
important_dates: Paper submission: 1 February 2027 on the conference website (the CFP PDF says 8 February 2027)
Final papers and early registration: 30 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Circuits and Systems Society is the IEEE body for the theory, design and application of circuits and systems. NEWCAS is one of its interregional flagship conferences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the submission site linked from ieee-newcas.org once it opens on 1 December 2026. Use the earlier 1 February 2027 date to be safe, then submit the final version and register by 30 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: The conference website and the CFP PDF give different paper deadlines (1 vs 8 February 2027); plan for the earlier one.

opportunities.title: ITM-DGD Predoctoral Research Training Grants 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers living in a low- or middle-income country, mainly nationals of DGD partner countries, with an ITM supervisor and a home-institute supervisor, can apply for 3 to 6 months of pre-PhD training in Antwerp.
opportunities.description:
The ITM-DGD Predoctoral Research Training Grants let promising early-career researchers from low- and middle-income countries spend three to six months at the Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM) in Antwerp, Belgium, to prepare a PhD project. The training is not a degree; it is meant to build the skills and proposal needed to start doctoral research.

The grants are funded by the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (DGD). At most five grants are available in the 2027 call, to be taken up between 15 June 2027 and 14 June 2028, preferably before the end of 2027.

Most eligible countries are in Africa, including Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda. Applicants need both an ITM supervisor and a supervisor at their home institute.
opportunities.benefits: A living allowance of €28 per day (up to 6 months in Antwerp), a housing allowance, a bench fee of €1,470 per month, a return ticket, insurance (€63 per month) and €200 for indirect travel costs. Grantees have student status, not employee status.
requirements: Primary residence in a low- or middle-income country
Nationality of a DGD-eligible country (a limited number of grants for other LMIC nationals)
Formal supervisor at ITM and at the home institute
Early-career researcher with strong potential for PhD research
Not a dual national of a high-income country
No more than one year of employment in a high-income country in the three years before 1 February 2027
Never on the ITM payroll
documents: CV with master's and postgraduate transcripts and current employment
Letters of support from both supervisors
opportunities.selection_process: The ITM PhD Committee evaluates applications, followed by a decision by the ITM Management Committee. Proposals limited to a single course are not considered a good fit.
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp is one of the world's leading institutes for research, training and services in tropical medicine and global health. It has long-standing partnerships with institutions in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree on a training plan with an ITM supervisor and your home supervisor, then complete the application form from the ITM website. Email the full application to the ITM contact named in the call before 1 February 2027, 17:00 Belgian time.
opportunities.notes: At most 5 grants. ITM also offers DGD postdoctoral and sandwich PhD grants with March and September deadlines.

opportunities.title: IntRob'27: Intelligent Robotics FAIR 2027 (call for papers)
opportunities.provider: ELTE and Bosch Budapest Innovation Campus
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Robotics researchers can submit original English papers by 1 February 2027 to IntRob'27 in Budapest (27 to 28 May 2027); an author must register and present.
opportunities.description:
IntRob'27, the third Intelligent Robotics FAIR, is a two-day conference with an exhibition and a public "Meet a Robot Day", held on 27 and 28 May 2027 in Budapest, Hungary. It is hosted by Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) at its Lágymányosi Campus and at the Bosch Budapest Innovation Campus, with Bosch as a sponsor.

The call invites original papers on intelligent robotics. Reviews are single-blind and run in two phases, and each accepted paper must be presented by a registered author.

This is a call for papers, not a funded award. It offers African robotics and AI researchers a smaller, industry-linked venue in Central Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Presentation at the conference and publication in the proceedings (publisher to be announced). Registration fees, travel grants and waivers are not yet published.
requirements: Original work in English
ORCID iDs for authors in the manuscript
LaTeX template (to be released)
Manuscripts written by generative AI are not allowed; light AI editing must be acknowledged
At least one registered author presents each accepted paper
documents: Paper in the conference LaTeX template, submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind peer review in two phases, with notification on 15 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) is Hungary's oldest and largest university, based in Budapest; its Faculty of Informatics hosts the Intelligent Robotics FAIR.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the IntRob'27 EasyChair page by 1 February 2027, once the template is released on the conference site.
opportunities.notes: Fees, page limits and the template were still marked as coming soon on 19 November 2026.

opportunities.title: Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Very early postdocs (PhD within 24 months, MD within 3 years) of any nationality with a sponsoring lab can apply by 1 February 2027; non-US citizens must be placed at a US institution.
opportunities.description:
The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research awards postdoctoral fellowships to young scientists who want to do basic biomedical research. The 2027 cycle is for fellows who will start on 1 July 2027, and the online application has been open since 1 October 2026.

Applicants must already have found the lab and institution where they will do their postdoc. The fund wants people at the very start of their postdoctoral careers, so there are strict limits on how long ago the PhD or MD was awarded and on how much postdoc experience the applicant already has.

The fellowship is open to citizens of any country, which makes it relevant to African life scientists. The one condition for non-US citizens is that the fellowship must be held at a sponsoring institution in the United States.
opportunities.benefits: A postdoctoral fellowship paid through the sponsoring institution. The pages read do not state the stipend amount or duration; the fund's FAQ and award terms give those details.
requirements: No more than 12 months of postdoctoral experience at the deadline
PhD awarded no earlier than 1 February 2025, or MD awarded no earlier than 1 February 2024
PhD candidates may apply if the degree is conferred and the lab position starts before 1 July 2027
Must not have already accepted another postdoctoral fellowship (T32 support is allowed but not at the same time)
A sponsoring lab and institution must be identified before applying
Non-US citizens can only hold the award at a sponsoring institution in the United States
Postdoc in the same lab as the PhD is not funded, and staying at the same institution is discouraged
documents: Research proposal submitted in the application portal
Three reference letters (not from the proposed postdoc advisor or co-advisor)
Proposed Postdoctoral Advisor Form, completed by the advisor
Fiscal Officer form signed by the sponsoring institution's grants or financial officer
opportunities.selection_process: The fund reviews all complete applications after the deadline and sends award decisions by email in mid-May 2027. The pages read do not describe the scoring criteria.
opportunities.about_provider: The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research is a US charitable fund, administered from Yale, that has supported postdoctoral research in the medical and related sciences for decades through its competitive fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register in the fund's Temelio application portal as an individual (not as an organisation), complete the proposal and invite your referees, advisor and fiscal officer, who must sign up with the same email address you give for them. Everything must be in the portal by 3:00 pm Eastern Time on 1 February 2027, with no exceptions.
opportunities.notes: Do not follow older guidelines, including the 2026 version. Questions go to jccfund@yale.edu. Read the FAQ and the terms of award for stipend details.

opportunities.title: Khalifa University PhD Scholarships (Fall 2027)
opportunities.provider: Khalifa University of Science and Technology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International PhD applicants who flag scholarship interest in their Fall 2027 admission application can get full or partial tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend; a 3.25 GPA is needed with a master's, 3.5 for direct PhD entry.

opportunities.title: Kyoto University Amgen Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate science students enrolled at a university in Asia (any nationality) who plan a PhD can apply by 1 February 2027 for a funded nine-week research placement in Kyoto.
opportunities.description:
The Kyoto University Amgen Scholars Program is a nine-week summer research programme for undergraduates who are thinking about a PhD in science or biotechnology. Scholars spend about eight weeks working full time in a Kyoto University laboratory and then attend the compulsory Amgen Scholars Asia Symposium.
