The 2027 programme runs from 4 June to 5 August 2027 and takes about 10 students.

The programme is run by Kyoto University's Division of Graduate Studies with support from the US-based Amgen Foundation. It pays a scholarship and covers travel and housing, so participants can focus on research.

Nationality is not restricted, but applicants must be studying at a college or university in Asia. African students enrolled in a bachelor's degree at an Asian university (for example in Japan, China, Korea, India or Malaysia) can therefore apply.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship of JPY 180,000 paid in two instalments of JPY 90,000, economy airfare on the set route, accommodation in Kyoto (not for Kyoto University's own students) and fees for official events. Participants must buy private health insurance and the Kyoto University Co-op liability insurance.
requirements: Undergraduate enrolled at a degree-granting college or university in Asia (UN regional list); nationality is open
At least the first year of study completed by the start
Must not graduate before the programme ends and must return to undergraduate study for at least one more term
Strong academic record and interest in doing a PhD
English: TOEFL iBT 72, IELTS 5.5, Cambridge FCE, TOEIC 1095 (or L&R 785 or S&W 310), unless a native speaker or in an English-taught programme
Master's and doctoral students are not eligible
documents: Online application form with application details and a statement of purpose
Two recommendation letters uploaded by your recommenders before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: First-stage screening results come by mid-February 2027, after which shortlisted applicants send a short video. Final results are announced in late March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Kyoto University is one of Japan's leading national research universities, founded in 1897. The Amgen Scholars Program is a global undergraduate research network funded by the Amgen Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Kyoto University's international student application system linked from the programme page, after reading the guidelines and FAQ. Nominate your two recommenders early so their letters are in by 1 February 2027. Questions go to amgenscholars@mail2.adm.kyoto-u.ac.jp.
opportunities.notes: The Asia Symposium is compulsory. Airfare is not provided if you cannot arrive on the set dates.

opportunities.title: Leiden Children's Rights Scholarship 1 (LL.M. Advanced Studies in International Children's Rights, 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of countries with a medium or low UNDP Human Development Index ranking (positions 113-189), who need financial help and plan to return home, can apply for a EUR 17,900 tuition contribution for Leiden's children's rights LL.M.
opportunities.description:
Leiden University's Faculty of Law offers two private scholarships, each worth EUR 17,900, towards tuition for its one-year Master of Laws: Advanced Studies in International Children's Rights. The scholarship applies only to this programme and is not a full scholarship: the programme's tuition is EUR 22,900, and recipients must still fund the rest of their fees and their living costs.

The scholarship deadline is 1 February 2027, and decisions are made in the first week of May. To be considered, applicants must also have applied for admission to the programme and paid the application fee.

The award targets students from countries ranked medium or low on the UNDP Human Development Index, which includes many African countries. Priority goes to applicants from single-parent families or families on social assistance, and applicants must intend to return home after graduating.
opportunities.benefits: A contribution of EUR 17,900 towards the EUR 22,900 tuition fee for one year. Two scholarships are available. Non-EEA recipients must still show proof of sufficient funds for the visa or residence permit.
requirements: National of a country ranked medium (113-151) or low (152-189) on the UNDP Human Development Index
Admission application to the LL.M. Advanced Studies in International Children's Rights
Proof that you cannot fund the studies without the scholarship
High motivation and intention to return home after graduation
Valid English test result
documents: Online admission application in uSis with the EUR 100 application fee
Separate scholarship motivation letter with your student number, describing your financial situation, why you need the scholarship and how you will cover the remaining costs
opportunities.selection_process: The programme's Admission Board and the scholarship provider decide. Priority is given to applicants from single-parent families and families on social assistance.
important_dates: Programme admission deadline: 1 April (visa needed) or 15 May (no visa)
opportunities.about_provider: Leiden University is the oldest university in the Netherlands, with its law faculty based in Leiden and The Hague. Its LL.M. in International Children's Rights is a specialised one-year advanced master's programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to the programme in uSis and pay the fee, then submit the scholarship application through the scholarship tab in uSis with your scholarship motivation letter before 1 February 2027. Contact ICRscholarships@law.leidenuniv.nl with questions.
opportunities.notes: Housing in Leiden and The Hague is hard to find, so start looking early.

opportunities.title: Leiden Children's Rights Scholarship 2 for Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda and Malawi (2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda or Malawi who cannot fund their studies and plan to return home can apply for a EUR 50,543 full scholarship for Leiden's LL.M. in International Children's Rights.
opportunities.description:
Leiden University's Faculty of Law offers a private, full-cost scholarship for nationals of Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda and Malawi to take its one-year Master of Laws: Advanced Studies in International Children's Rights. The award is worth EUR 50,543 and covers tuition, travel, living costs and accommodation.

The scholarship deadline is 1 February 2027, and decisions are expected in the first week of May 2027. Applicants first apply for admission to the programme, then email their scholarship application with a short video, and a brief online interview may be part of the process.

This is one of the few fully funded master's scholarships reserved specifically for East and Southern African applicants, aimed at people who want to work on children's rights and intend to return home after graduating.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 50,543 for one year, covering tuition, travel, living expenses and accommodation. It cannot be used for the application fee or English test costs.
requirements: Nationality of Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda or Malawi
Admission application to the LL.M. Advanced Studies in International Children's Rights
Insufficient funds to study without the scholarship
High motivation and intention to return home after graduation
Sufficient English language test result
documents: Online programme application in uSis with the non-waivable EUR 100 fee
Scholarship motivation letter with your full name and student number, describing your financial situation and why you need the scholarship
opportunities.selection_process: The programme's Admission Board selects the recipient after the admission application, the scholarship application and the fee are all complete. A short online interview may be held.
opportunities.about_provider: Leiden University is the oldest university in the Netherlands, with its law faculty based in Leiden and The Hague. Its LL.M. in International Children's Rights is a specialised one-year advanced master's programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the programme application in uSis and pay the fee, then email ICRscholarships@law.leidenuniv.nl stating your interest, with your scholarship letter and video attached, before 1 February 2027.

opportunities.title: Maastricht University NL High Potential Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Excellent non-EU/EEA students aged 35 or under who have not studied for a degree in the Netherlands can apply for a fully funded master's at Maastricht.

opportunities.title: Massey University Alumni Doctoral Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Massey University graduates of any nationality who hold a doctoral offer at Massey (or are in their first 12 months of enrolment) can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Massey University Alumni Doctoral Scholarship supports Massey graduates who return to the university for a PhD or named doctorate. It is worth $90,000 plus tuition fees over three years, and several awards are made.

Both international and domestic candidates are eligible, and the scholarship can support full-time or part-time study. Applicants must already hold a conditional or unconditional doctoral offer, or be within their first 12 months of enrolment at the closing date, and must enrol by 1 June of the award year.

African graduates of Massey University who want to continue to doctoral research in New Zealand can apply between 1 December 2026 and 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: $90,000 over three years plus tuition fees.
requirements: Graduate of Massey University
Conditional or unconditional offer of a Massey doctoral place, or enrolled for no more than 12 months at the closing date
Enrol by 1 June of the award year
Open to international and domestic, full-time and part-time candidates
documents: Supervisor Support Template completed by the primary supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are assessed on academic achievement and on how well the research fits the strategic priorities of the university, the college and the supervisor.
opportunities.about_provider: Massey University is a public New Zealand university with campuses in Auckland, Palmerston North and Wellington and a large distance-learning programme. It is known for agriculture, veterinary science, design and business.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Massey Student Portal between 1 December 2026 and 1 February 2027, uploading the research outline and the supervisor template. Contact Massey by email for help.
opportunities.notes: The page currently shows the status as closed because the round has not opened yet.

opportunities.title: Master Mind Scholarship at the University of Antwerp 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: University of Antwerp (Flemish Government Master Mind scheme)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality except Russia, with a previous degree from outside Flanders and admission to one of 15 eligible UAntwerp master's programmes, can apply.
opportunities.description:
Master Mind is a Flemish Government scholarship that the University of Antwerp uses to attract outstanding international students to its master's programmes. For 2027-28 the university can award five scholarships across 15 eligible one- and two-year programmes.

Each winner receives a one-time grant of €5,375, and non-EEA winners pay the much lower EEA tuition fee instead of the international rate (€1,181.40 for 60 credits in 2026-27). Winners are chosen for their academic record and potential, motivation, maturity and relevant work experience.

African applicants are eligible provided this is their first master's and their previous degree comes from outside Flanders. The page notes that the Flemish scheme is under review, with new conditions expected in December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time grant of €5,375, and for non-EEA students the reduced EEA tuition fee (€1,181.40 for 60 ECTS in 2026-27, subject to change) instead of the international fee.
requirements: Any nationality except Russian citizens
First master's degree
Previous degree from a higher education institution outside Flanders
Admission to one of the 15 eligible UAntwerp master's programmes
Meet the programme's academic and language requirements
Cannot be combined with another Flemish government or Erasmus Mundus scholarship
documents: Motivation letter that explicitly addresses the Master Mind scholarship
Hard copies of documents to the Registrar's Office by 31 May
opportunities.selection_process: Programmes shortlist one or two candidates each, who complete an extra screening task in early April. A central board then selects winners on academic performance, motivation, attitude, maturity and relevant work experience. Results come in May.
important_dates: Screening task for shortlisted candidates: early April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Antwerp is a public research university in Antwerp, Belgium, with about 20,000 students. It offers a range of English-taught master's programmes and hosts several international scholarship schemes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible UAntwerp master's before 1 February 2027 and tick the Master Mind box in the application. Your motivation letter must include a section on why you deserve the scholarship, or it will not be considered.
opportunities.notes: Only five awards. The Flemish scheme's conditions may change in December 2026, so check the page again.

opportunities.title: Master of Development Evaluation and Management (University of Antwerp, IOB) - VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarship 2027
opportunities.provider: VLIR-UOS and University of Antwerp (Institute of Development Policy)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship for nationals of the 25 eligible countries (17 in Africa) who also live in one of them, aged 45 or younger on 1 January 2027, with no earlier Belgian government study scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Development Policy (IOB) at the University of Antwerp offers six VLIR-UOS full scholarships for its one-year advanced Master of Development Evaluation and Management, starting in September 2027. Because it is an advanced master's, the age limit is 45 rather than 35.

The programme examines competing ideas of development and the roles that international and local actors play in it. Students learn to research and evaluate development policies and programmes using qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods. The 60-credit year combines a common core (Theories of Development, two Research Methods courses and an 18-credit master's dissertation defended orally) with a 12-credit course on Evaluating Development Effectiveness and a choice between Local Institutions, Structure and Agency or (Inter)national Institutions and Global Public Goods. Electives touch on natural resources, migration, gender, land tenure, climate finance and public services.

Candidates must be citizens and residents of one of 25 eligible countries (16 in sub-Saharan Africa plus Morocco) and no older than 45 on 1 January 2027. Applications opened on 1 November 2026 and close for scholarship candidates on 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A full scholarship for the whole length of the programme (12 months) and no longer. It is paid mainly as a monthly allowance meant to cover living costs (board and lodging) and tuition; travel to and from Belgium and insurance are also covered. Depending on the institution, tuition, insurance or housing is either paid by you out of the allowance or paid by the university directly and taken off the allowance. There are no partial awards or extensions, and VLIR-UOS pays nothing extra for optional activities such as field trips to the Global South. ICP Connect programmes charge no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of one of the 25 VLIR-UOS ICP Connect countries (in Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe; also Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam)
Living in one of those 25 countries when you apply (it does not have to be your own country)
Not older than 45 on 1 January 2027
Never awarded a Belgian government scholarship for study before, and not enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January 2027
Only one ICP Connect scholarship application per year: applying to two or more ICP programmes gets you excluded

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship for nationals of the 25 eligible countries (17 in Africa) who also live in one of them, aged 35 or younger on 1 January 2027, with no earlier Belgian government study scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Hasselt University (UHasselt) in Belgium offers VLIR-UOS full scholarships for its two-year (120 ECTS), English-taught Master of Transportation Sciences with a focus on road safety in low- and middle-income countries. The scholarship runs from September 2027 to September 2029.

The programme looks at road safety from three angles: the person (behaviour in traffic, such as drink-driving or impaired attention), the environment (for example roads designed so that drivers instinctively behave safely) and society (social norms, policy and enforcement). It brings together psychology, economics, urban planning, environmental studies and engineering. The Traffic Safety track includes courses such as Road Safety in the South and Road Safety Audit, a research portfolio, a 10-week internship (which ICP students may do in their home country) and a master's thesis. Teaching takes place mainly in Hasselt, with some activities in Diepenbeek.

Applicants from the 25 eligible countries (16 in sub-Saharan Africa, plus Morocco) aged 35 or younger on 1 January 2027 can apply. Applications opened in mid-October/November 2026 and must be complete by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A full scholarship for the whole length of the programme (24 months) and no longer. It is paid mainly as a monthly allowance meant to cover living costs (board and lodging) and tuition; travel to and from Belgium and insurance are also covered. Depending on the institution, tuition, insurance or housing is either paid by you out of the allowance or paid by the university directly and taken off the allowance. There are no partial awards or extensions, and VLIR-UOS pays nothing extra for optional activities such as field trips to the Global South. ICP Connect programmes charge no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of one of the 25 VLIR-UOS ICP Connect countries (in Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe; also Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam)
Living in one of those 25 countries when you apply (it does not have to be your own country)
Not older than 35 on 1 January 2027
Never awarded a Belgian government scholarship for study before, and not enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January 2027
Only one ICP Connect scholarship application per year: applying to two or more ICP programmes gets you excluded
No other scholarship or grant for this or any other programme at the same time
Good command of English (all ICP Connect programmes are taught in English; Dutch is not needed)

Academic bachelor's degree in a related field: behavioural, political or social sciences, mathematics or statistics, (transport) economics, transport or traffic planning, urban planning or design, geography, architecture, transport or civil engineering (a Bachelor of Technology or HND is not enough)
Good grades: UHasselt asks for at least a distinction-level result (around 75%, a B or CGPA 3.0/4.0)
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 89, Duolingo 120 or Cambridge CAE (some exemptions)
Work experience is not compulsory but preferred in higher education, government or civil society
opportunities.selection_process: The host institution first checks and ranks every eligible application, then sends its shortlist to VLIR-UOS, which screens it again. Points that weigh in the ranking: motivation and your potential to act as an agent of change at home; professional experience, with preference for people working in (or heading for) higher education, government or civil society; gender balance, with women strongly encouraged to apply; balance between regions; the Leave No One Behind principle, which favours candidates from vulnerable groups when two files are equally strong; and preference for people who have never had a scholarship to study in a high-income country. VLIR-UOS emails the selected and reserve-list candidates; the programme tells the others. Results are due by mid-May 2027 at the latest. UHasselt ranks all complete files: the top 7 get scholarships and ranks 8 to 14 form the waiting list.
important_dates: Applications open: 15 October 2026 (VLIR-UOS page) / 15 November 2026 (UHasselt page)
Results: end of May to mid-June 2027
VLIR-UOS online information session: 26 November 2026, 14:30-16:30 CET (register through the Zoom link on the call page)
opportunities.about_provider: VLIR-UOS is the Flemish university network's programme for development cooperation, funded by the Belgian government. Through its ICP Connect scheme it pays full scholarships for a selected set of English-taught degree programmes at universities and university colleges in Flanders and Brussels, so that students from partner countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America can study in Belgium and take their skills back home. For the September 2027 intake it funds 12 programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Follow the ICP Connect application procedure on the UHasselt programme page (https://www.uhasselt.be/Master-of-Transportation-Sciences#icp-application-procedure) and submit a complete application before 1 February 2027. Admin contact: admissionformaster@uhasselt.be.
opportunities.notes: Do not apply to more than one ICP Connect programme in the same year. New graduates or people from the private sector without work experience can still be considered if their motivation is strong. Students may work a few hours a week, but not during compulsory classes, and the scholarship should not be topped up by a job. Some countries need their diplomas legalised through a Belgian embassy or consulate; ask the university early.

opportunities.title: NL MPP Scholarship 2027/28 (Master of Public Policy)

opportunities.title: New America Fellows Program (Class of 2028)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists, writers, filmmakers and other creators of any nationality with a nonfiction project already under way can apply by 1 February 2027 for a USD 15,000 to 30,000 stipend.
opportunities.description:
The New America Fellows Program funds writers, journalists, filmmakers, podcasters and other thinkers who are working on a big nonfiction project, such as a book, film, podcast, long article or multimedia piece. The Class of 2028 fellowship runs from September 2027 to May 2028 and is non-residential, so fellows keep living and working where they are.

Fellows come together three times: a three-day opening gathering in Washington, DC in the week of 4 October 2027, monthly online meetings from November to April, and a closing gathering in Washington in May 2028. In between they receive editorial and professional support from New America and its network.

The programme accepts applicants who are not US citizens and who live outside the United States, so African journalists and authors with a project already in progress can apply. Competition is strong: the Class of 2027 drew 538 applications for 14 places.
opportunities.benefits: An unrestricted stipend of USD 15,000 to 30,000, usually paid in three instalments directly to the fellow. Travel, lodging and most meals for the opening and closing gatherings in Washington, DC are covered.
requirements: Open to all nationalities, including people based outside the United States
Substantial reporting or significant professional experience in your field
A nonfiction project that is already under way (projects still at the concept stage are advised to wait)
Application materials and reference letters in English
Team applications are allowed, but the funding is the same as for one person
documents: Online application with a statement of interest, plan of approach and written answers, all written by the applicant
Up to three work samples (written or audiovisual) with the cover page template
Two reference letters requested through the portal, from people who know your work (not relatives)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed from February to April 2027 and narrowed to 40 to 50 finalists, who are interviewed. A selection committee then chooses about 10 to 15 fellows, looking for a fresh perspective, a link to New America's mission, a clear production plan, proof from past work that the applicant can finish, and a project where the support will make a real difference.
important_dates: Reference letters due: 8 February 2027, 11:59 pm EST
Opening gathering: week of 4 October 2027, Washington, DC
opportunities.about_provider: New America is a Washington, DC based think tank and civic organisation that works on public policy, technology and media. Through its fellowships it invests in journalists, scholars, filmmakers and policy analysts who produce work for a wide public.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through New America's SurveyMonkey Apply portal for the Class of 2028, following the application instructions PDF. Upload your work samples with the cover page and request your two references in the portal early so they can submit by 8 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Generative AI may not be used to draft or rewrite the narrative answers; breaking this rule can lead to disqualification. New America does not take phone calls or give feedback on projects. Its other fellowships (such as Future Security) need separate applications.

opportunities.title: New England Regional Fellowship Consortium 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers who are US citizens or foreign nationals with the required US documents can apply for a $5,000 stipend for at least six weeks of research across several New England archives.
opportunities.description:
The New England Regional Fellowship Consortium (NERFC) is a group of 29 libraries, archives and historical societies coordinated by the Massachusetts Historical Society. Each year it funds researchers to work in the collections of several member institutions.

Each fellowship pays $5,000 for at least six weeks of research between 1 June 2027 and 31 May 2028. The plan must include at least two weeks at each of two institutions and at least one week at a third, with the remaining time at any member institution. The consortium expects to make at least two dozen awards.

Foreign nationals may apply if they hold the necessary US government documents, and should talk to MHS staff about stipend eligibility before applying. Applicants without a doctorate need a recommendation letter from a faculty member.
opportunities.benefits: A $5,000 stipend for a minimum of six weeks of research.
requirements: US citizen, or foreign national holding the necessary US government documents
Foreign nationals must consult MHS staff about stipend eligibility before applying
Research at at least three member institutions (2 weeks, 2 weeks, 1 week minimum)
Applicants without a doctorate need a faculty recommendation letter
One award per project
documents: List of staff contacts at the institutions
Short project description of about 100 words
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are scored against a published rubric. Applicants are encouraged to contact repository staff in advance. Results are sent about eight weeks after the deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: The Massachusetts Historical Society, founded in 1791, is an independent research library and the oldest historical society in the United States. It administers the NERFC on behalf of 29 member institutions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the MHS SlideRoom portal by 1 February 2027. Questions go to the MHS fellowships email address.
opportunities.notes: Check visa and stipend rules early if you are not a US resident.

opportunities.title: St. Gallen Symposium Global Ideas Competition 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's and PhD students of any nationality born in 1997 or later can enter by 1 February 2027; the top 100 attend the St. Gallen Symposium free and three winners share CHF 20,000.
opportunities.description:
The Global Ideas Competition, which replaces the St. Gallen Symposium's long-running Global Essay Competition, invites graduate students to propose solutions to big economic, political and social questions. Entrants send a short written solution brief and a three-minute video explaining their idea.

The best 100 entrants become "Leaders of Tomorrow" and are invited to the 56th St. Gallen Symposium in St. Gallen, Switzerland, from 27 to 29 April 2027, with travel, board and lodging paid. Three winners also share a prize fund of CHF 20,000.

The competition is open to students from every country and any field of study, so it is a strong chance for African graduate students to join a leading forum where young people debate with business, political and academic leaders.
opportunities.benefits: Top 100 entrants attend the 56th St. Gallen Symposium free of charge, with travel, board and lodging covered and a free public transport ticket for the week. Three awardees share a CHF 20,000 prize fund. Participants should bring CHF 100 to 200 pocket money and arrange their own visa (support letters are provided).
requirements: Enrolled at Master's level or higher at a regular university (one that does research and offers a PhD programme) on 1 February 2027
Born in 1997 or later
Any nationality and any field of study
Individual entries only
Bachelor's students are not eligible unless their current year equals graduate level (such as a fourth honours year), confirmed in writing by the university
Entries in English
documents: Passport or other government ID (not a driving licence)
Confirmation of enrolment valid on 1 February 2027
Solution Brief of up to 1,000 words using the official template, with no name in the file or metadata
Video Explainer of up to 3 minutes (MP4/MOV or YouTube/Vimeo link, at least 720p)
Abstract of 200 to 300 words entered in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: In round one the Award Jury judges the anonymous Solution Briefs on originality and the strength of argument and evidence. In round two the jury reviews the videos. The top 100 become Leaders of Tomorrow and three winners are chosen. AI use must be declared, and plagiarism is checked.
opportunities.about_provider: The St. Gallen Symposium is an annual meeting in St. Gallen, Switzerland, organised by students, that describes itself as the world's leading initiative for intergenerational debate on economic, political and social developments.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the Solution Brief template from the competition page, write your brief and record your video, then sign up and submit through the competition's online portal before the deadline. Make sure your file has no name in the text or metadata.
opportunities.notes: Undeclared use of AI leads to disqualification. Eligibility is judged on your status on 1 February 2027.

opportunities.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) PhD Scholarship Fall 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants worldwide can apply to one of TIGP's 14 English-taught PhD programmes at Academia Sinica for Fall 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) is a doctoral programme run by Academia Sinica, Taiwan's national research academy, together with leading Taiwanese universities. It offers 14 PhD sub-programmes, all taught in English, in which students do their research in Academia Sinica's laboratories and receive their degree through a partner university.

Applications for Fall 2027 entry are open to applicants worldwide through the TIGP online portal from 1 November 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59, Taiwan time). Each applicant may apply to only one TIGP programme.

TIGP is an attractive route for African graduates who want an English-language PhD in a strong research setting in Asia. Check the programme pages for the funding package offered to admitted students, as the portal page does not list it.
opportunities.benefits: The official portal page read does not state the funding package; check the TIGP programme pages or contact the TIGP office for the current stipend and support for admitted students.
requirements: Open to applicants of any nationality
Apply to only one of the 14 TIGP PhD programmes
Meet the admission requirements of the chosen programme (see programme pages)
documents: Online application in the TIGP portal (register an account first)
Programme-specific documents listed in the portal
opportunities.selection_process: Each TIGP programme reviews its own applicants; see the programme pages for interview and selection details.
opportunities.about_provider: Academia Sinica is Taiwan's leading national research institution, with institutes in the mathematical and physical sciences, life sciences and humanities and social sciences. TIGP is its international doctoral programme, run with partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register an account on the TIGP application portal, choose one programme and submit the online application before 1 February 2027 (Taiwan time). Questions go to the TIGP office by email (tigp@as.edu.tw) or phone.
opportunities.notes: Applying to more than one TIGP programme is not allowed.

opportunities.title: Tufts University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Tufts for 2027-28 who request aid when applying can receive aid meeting 100% of demonstrated need; the Regular Decision CSS Profile is due 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Tufts University near Boston meets 100% of the demonstrated financial need of every admitted undergraduate, whatever their citizenship. International applicants who want aid must say so when they apply for admission, because aid is not offered later to students who did not request it.

Tufts gives only need-based aid to undergraduates and has no merit scholarships. Aid can continue for up to eight semesters or until the bachelor's degree is finished, but students must reapply each year.

For the 2027-28 year, Regular Decision applicants submit the CSS Profile by 1 February 2027 and their supporting tax documents by 15 February 2027. For African families, full need coverage at a selective US university can make study there possible.
opportunities.benefits: Need-based aid that meets 100% of demonstrated need, for up to eight semesters or until the bachelor's degree is completed. Amounts depend on need. No merit scholarships are offered.
requirements: International (non-US citizen) applicant for first-year entry in 2027-28
Must state interest in aid on the admission application
Must reapply for aid every year
The Tufts Tuition Pact (free tuition under USD 150,000 income) applies to US students only
documents: CSS Profile, or the International Student Financial Aid Application (ISFAA) if the CSS Profile is not available
2025 foreign tax documents in English and US dollars, uploaded through IDOC
opportunities.selection_process: Aid is based on demonstrated need, calculated from the CSS Profile and documents. Tufts meets the full need of every admitted student.
important_dates: Early Decision I CSS Profile: 16 November 2026 (passed)
Early Decision II CSS Profile: 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Tufts University is a private research university in Medford and Somerville, Massachusetts, near Boston. Its Student Financial Services office manages undergraduate aid.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission and indicate that you want financial aid, then complete the CSS Profile and upload the requested documents through IDOC. Check your Tufts admissions account for missing items. Tufts does not accept documents by email.
opportunities.notes: Contact Student Services at studentservices@tufts.edu or +1 617-627-2000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants with financial need who are admitted to Maastricht's BA Global Studies can receive tuition, a living allowance, insurance and visa support.

opportunities.title: UTokyo Amgen Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate science students enrolled at a university in the Asia region (any nationality) who plan a PhD can apply by 1 February 2027 for a funded eight-week research internship in Tokyo.
opportunities.description:
The UTokyo Amgen Scholars Program is an eight-week summer research internship in the laboratories of the University of Tokyo, for undergraduates interested in biomedical and life science research. The 2027 programme runs from 3 June to 30 July 2027 and is followed by the Amgen Scholars Asia Symposium in Kyoto from 3 to 5 August 2027. About ten students are chosen.

Scholars work on a project with a host professor, take online Japanese classes and join the symposium. The programme is run by the university's Center for Global Education with support from the Amgen Foundation, and it covers housing, airfare and a stipend.

Since 2024, applicants must be studying at a college or university in the Asia region. African students enrolled in a bachelor's degree at an Asian university can apply, but those studying in Africa cannot.
opportunities.benefits: Off-campus accommodation during the programme, round-trip economy airfare on the most direct route for international participants, a stipend of JPY 280,000 for meals, personal costs and local transport, and the costs of the Asia Symposium. Health and travel insurance are not covered.
requirements: Undergraduate enrolled at a college or university in the Asia region (applications from outside the region are no longer accepted)
At least the first year completed; must not graduate before the programme and must continue undergraduate study for at least one term afterwards
Strong academic record and interest in a PhD; no previous bachelor's degree
English: TOEFL iBT 72, IELTS 5.5, Cambridge FCE or TOEIC 1,095 (L&R 785 or S&W 310) unless English is your first language or your degree is taught in English
documents: Academic transcript in English (all pages, unencrypted PDF)
Two recommendation letters, one from a faculty member at your institution, on letterhead, signed and dated
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed after the deadline (not on a rolling basis) and results are sent in mid to late March 2027. Applicants choose one project from the list of host professors.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Tokyo is Japan's leading national research university. The Amgen Scholars Program is a global undergraduate research network funded by the Amgen Foundation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on The Admissions Office (TAO) portal and apply to the UTokyo Amgen Scholars Program under the Center for Global Education. Nominate your two recommenders early, because you cannot submit until both letters are in, and no changes are allowed after submission.
opportunities.notes: Late submissions are not accepted under any circumstances. Participants who do not complete the programme may have to repay travel and stipend. Contact amgenscholars.adm@gs.mail.u-tokyo.ac.jp.

opportunities.title: UW-Milwaukee International Student Scholarship (Fall start) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Newly admitted international first-year and transfer undergraduates with strong grades and financial need are considered by 1 February 2027 for up to $6,000 a year at UW-Milwaukee.
opportunities.description:
The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee awards its International Student Scholarship to newly admitted international undergraduates, both first-year and transfer students, who have strong academic records and financial need. The award is worth up to $6,000 a year, paid as $3,000 per semester.

This listing is for students starting in the fall, with a scholarship deadline of 1 February 2027. Students are considered automatically once they complete UWM's general scholarship application.

African students admitted to UWM can apply, and the combination of merit and need makes it a good fit for capable students with limited family funds.
opportunities.benefits: Up to $6,000 a year ($3,000 per semester). Number of awards not stated.
requirements: Newly admitted international undergraduate (first-year or transfer) starting in fall
Strong academic record
Financial need
documents: UWM General Scholarship Application on the AcademicWorks portal
opportunities.selection_process: Students are considered automatically from the completed general application, based on academic record and financial need.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee is a public research university in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and part of the Universities of Wisconsin system.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to UWM as an international undergraduate, then sign in to UWM's AcademicWorks scholarship portal (uwm.academicworks.com) and complete the General Application by 1 February 2027. No separate form is needed for this award.
opportunities.notes: The official page does not state the entry year directly; a 1 February 2027 deadline for a fall start corresponds to fall 2027.

opportunities.title: University of Groningen NL Scholarship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EEA students with excellent Bachelor's grades who hold an offer for an eligible Groningen Master's starting in 2027-28 can apply for a one-time EUR 5,000 grant by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship at the University of Groningen is a one-time grant of EUR 5,000 for students from outside the European Economic Area who are starting a Master's programme in the 2027-2028 academic year. It is paid during the first year to help with living costs and is co-funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the university.

The grant does not cover full tuition or living costs, so it works best alongside savings or other funding. It is linked to an admission offer, which means students must first apply to and be admitted (conditionally or unconditionally) to one of the Master's programmes on the university's list of eligible programmes.

For African students with strong undergraduate results who are heading to the Netherlands, it is a useful extra source of money at one of the country's oldest research universities, and the application is short.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time grant of EUR 5,000, paid in the first year of study to help with living expenses. It can only be received once in a lifetime. The number of awards is not stated.
requirements: Nationality from outside the EEA and not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee
Full-time enrolment in an eligible Master's programme at the University of Groningen in 2027-28
Bachelor's degree obtained (or to be obtained) outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch diploma or Dutch education (exchange stays excepted)
Excellent academic results in the Bachelor's degree
An admission offer (conditional or unconditional) for a listed programme
Eligible for a Dutch student visa
Never held the NL Scholarship before
documents: Motivation letter on your academic goals and why you chose to study in the Netherlands
Transcript of records for all undergraduate courses so far
Admission letter (conditional or unconditional) for an eligible programme
opportunities.selection_process: A faculty selection committee ranks applicants on academic excellence, ambition and relevant experience, looking at grades, test scores, research and publications, the motivation letter and extracurricular or volunteer work.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Groningen is a public research university in the north of the Netherlands, founded in 1614. It teaches many Master's programmes in English and welcomes large numbers of international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your Master's programme first and wait for the admission offer. Then submit the NL Scholarship application form on the university website with your motivation letter, transcript and admission letter before 1 February 2027. Check the list of eligible programmes before you apply.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not considered. The page calls the grant the NL Scholarship; it replaced the older Holland Scholarship name.

opportunities.title: University of Waterloo International Master's Award of Excellence (IMAE) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to a research-based master's at Waterloo are considered for CAD 2,500 per term for up to five terms, with no separate application.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying to a Paris-Saclay master's programme can be considered for a stipend scholarship.

opportunities.title: Uppsala University Global Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who rank an Uppsala programme first for autumn 2027 can apply from 16 January to 1 February 2027 for a full tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Uppsala University Global Scholarship pays the full tuition fee for international students starting a programme at Uppsala University in autumn 2027. It is funded by the Swedish Council for Higher Education and is very competitive: the university says only about 2% of applicants receive one.

The scholarship does not cover living costs, so winners need their own funds for housing and daily expenses in Sweden. Selection is based on merit, using the documents from the programme application plus a short motivation letter; financial need is not considered.

African applicants should also note the Anders Wall Scholarship on the same page, which is reserved for citizens of African countries and covers full tuition with the same window and conditions.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee for the programme. Living expenses are not covered. No application fee for the scholarship.

Applied to an Uppsala programme at universityadmissions.se before its deadline, with the Uppsala programme ranked first
Meets the programme's entry requirements
Shows academic talent and interest in the learning environment
documents: Online scholarship form with personal details, chosen scholarship(s) and your 8-digit universityadmissions.se application number
Motivation letter of up to 350 words
No other documents are uploaded; academic records come from your programme application
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is merit-based, combining academic performance from the programme application documents with the motivation letter. Financial need is not a factor, and selection runs alongside admissions.
opportunities.about_provider: Uppsala University, founded in 1477, is Sweden's oldest university and a leading research university with many English-taught Master's programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for your programme at universityadmissions.se before its deadline and rank Uppsala first. Then fill in Uppsala's online scholarship form during the window of 16 January to 1 February 2027; the link is published on the scholarships page when it opens. Questions go to tuitiongrants@uu.se.
opportunities.notes: Late applications are not accepted. Students admitted to certain programmes, such as the Master's in Euroculture, cannot hold the Anders Wall Scholarship.

opportunities.title: Utrecht University Law, Economics and Governance International Talent Scholarship (LEGITS) 2027
opportunities.provider: Utrecht University, Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with a non-Dutch secondary qualification and non-Dutch bachelor's, admitted to an English-taught master's in Utrecht's School of Law or School of Economics starting September 2027, can apply for a full tuition-fee scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Utrecht University's Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance awards about four LEGITS scholarships each year to talented international students starting an English-taught master's programme in its School of Law or School of Economics on 1 September 2027. The scholarship pays the tuition fee and can be renewed for the second year of a two-year master's if progress is good.

Applicants first apply for the master's, and from 1 November 2026 the scholarship application appears in the Osiris application dashboard. The deadline is 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET; information submitted between 26 January and 1 February cannot be corrected later, so applying early is wise. Results come by email by mid-April.

Both EU and non-EU students can apply, so African graduates with a strong record and evidence of social engagement are eligible, provided this is their first master's in the Netherlands.
opportunities.benefits: Covers the tuition fee (the institutional fee for non-EU/EEA students), renewable for the second year of a two-year programme subject to satisfactory progress. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Non-Dutch secondary education qualification and non-Dutch bachelor's degree
First master's degree in the Netherlands
Admission to an English-taught master's in the School of Law or School of Economics starting 1 September 2027
English at the level (EMI) set by the programme
documents: Master's application in Osiris with transcripts, educational background, career achievements and motivation letter
Answers to the questions in the scholarship tab
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on academic quality and fit with the master's, societal engagement and initiative and potential contribution to a diverse international environment, and the quality and completeness of the application.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET (no corrections possible for submissions from 26 January)
opportunities.about_provider: Utrecht University is a large public research university in the Netherlands. Its Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance offers a range of English-taught master's programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your master's application in Osiris Online Application, then open the linked LEGITS scholarship process in your Osiris dashboard and upload the personal statement and answers before 1 February 2027. Questions go to scholarships.rebo@uu.nl.

opportunities.title: Utrecht University NL Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EEA students applying to a participating Utrecht University international Master's that starts on 1 September 2027 can be awarded EUR 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000 if they apply by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
Utrecht University offers the NL Scholarship to students from outside the EU/EEA who are starting an international Master's programme on 1 September 2027. The grant is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch universities, and it is a contribution towards costs rather than a full scholarship.

Awards are worth EUR 5,000, EUR 10,000 or EUR 15,000 and are paid in the first year of study, even when the Master's lasts two years. Not every programme takes part, so applicants should check the tuition and financial support section of their chosen programme page.

For African students, the grant can make a Utrecht Master's more affordable, but the university also asks for a realistic financial plan showing how the rest of the costs will be paid for the whole programme.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of EUR 5,000, EUR 10,000 or EUR 15,000, paid during the first year of study. The number of awards is not stated.
requirements: No EU/EEA passport and not eligible for Dutch student finance
Not eligible for the statutory (EU) tuition fee
Never enrolled at a Dutch higher education institution (exchange excepted)
Applied to an international Master's at Utrecht University that takes part in the scheme and starts on 1 September 2027
A financial plan showing the remaining costs are covered for the full programme
documents: Your Master's application to Utrecht University
NL Scholarship application form in OSIRIS Online Application
Statement of Financial Resources showing how you will pay the remaining costs
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on three points: their academic background (taken from the Master's application), their motivation, including why the Netherlands and Utrecht fit their goals, and the quality and feasibility of their financial plan.
important_dates: Applications sent between 27 January and 1 February cannot be corrected afterwards
opportunities.about_provider: Utrecht University is a large public research university in the centre of the Netherlands, founded in 1636, with many English-taught international Master's programmes across the sciences, humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible Master's first. Then log in to OSIRIS Online Application, find "NL Scholarship" on your dashboard, choose View/Edit, fill in the scholarship form and submit it before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET. Upload the Statement of Financial Resources with it.
opportunities.notes: Submit well before the last week, because applications sent from 27 January can no longer be updated. Utrecht also runs other awards such as Bright Minds Fellowships and Utrecht Sylff Scholarships.

opportunities.title: VU Amsterdam Fellowship Programme (VUFP) 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students with a Bachelor's GPA equal to a Dutch 8 who are admitted to a full-time English-taught VU Master's starting September 2027 can apply for a full tuition waiver by 1 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) is Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam's merit scholarship for strong students from outside the EU/EEA. It waives the full higher tuition fee for a full-time English-taught Master's programme that starts in September 2027. VU sets aside about one million euros a year for these awards.

The VUFP covers tuition only and does not include money for living costs. By applying for it, students are also automatically considered for the NL Scholarship, a separate EUR 5,000 contribution towards living costs in the first year, of which only about 20 to 25 are given each year.

For high-achieving African graduates, the waiver can remove the largest cost of studying in Amsterdam. Students on two-year programmes keep the waiver in the second year only if they pass all first-year credits.
opportunities.benefits: Full waiver of the tuition fee for the Master's programme (no living allowance). Applicants are also considered for the NL Scholarship, a one-off EUR 5,000 towards living costs in the first year (about 20 to 25 awards a year).
requirements: Non-EU/EEA passport and not eligible for the statutory tuition fee
Not of Dutch nationality
Bachelor's GPA equal to a Dutch 8 on the 1 to 10 scale (only the Bachelor's GPA is assessed)
Conditional or unconditional admission to the first year of a full-time English-taught VU Master's starting September 2027 (February starters cannot apply)
Degree not obtained in the Netherlands and not currently enrolled in a Dutch Bachelor's or Master's
No preparatory programme required before the Master's
documents: VUFP-NLS application form 2027-2028 (older forms are refused)
Bachelor's transcript or proof of GPA with an explanation of the grading scale
All files combined into one PDF
opportunities.selection_process: The faculty reviews applications first, then the Central Scholarship Committee makes the final choice based on academic results and motivation, also weighing future ambitions and extracurricular activities.
important_dates: Accept or decline: within two weeks, by end of March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is a public research university in Amsterdam, founded in 1880, with a broad range of English-taught Master's programmes. Part of its NL Scholarship funding comes from the VUvereniging association.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register for your Master's in Studielink and finish the application in the VU dashboard. Once admitted, submit the VUFP application in the dashboard for one Master's programme only, uploading the form and GPA proof as a single PDF. Results come by email and you accept or decline in the dashboard.
opportunities.notes: You can submit only once, and incomplete applications are not assessed. GPA proofs emailed in advance are not checked. Contact: scholarships.incoming@vu.nl.

opportunities.title: Waterloo Faculty of Environment International Doctoral Student Award and Funding Guarantee, Fall 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International full-time PhD applicants to Waterloo's Faculty of Environment programmes with a complete application by 1 February 2027 are guaranteed at least CAD 29,145 a year, plus the IDSA for most.
opportunities.description:
The University of Waterloo's Faculty of Environment guarantees a minimum funding package to full-time doctoral students in good academic standing. For students starting in fall 2027, international PhD students receive at least CAD 29,145 a year, most of which comes from their supervisor's research funds.

On top of this, eligible international doctoral students are automatically considered for the International Doctoral Student Award (IDSA), and most receive CAD 5,100 per term. To be sure of funding, applicants must have a complete application in by 1 February 2027; later applications may still be funded at the department's discretion.

The guarantee applies to the PhD programmes in Geography, Planning, Social and Ecological Sustainability, and Sustainability Management, which suits African researchers working on environment, cities and sustainability.
opportunities.benefits: Guaranteed minimum funding of CAD 29,145 per year (rate effective 1 May 2026) for full-time doctoral students in good standing, mostly from the supervisor. Most eligible international students also receive the International Doctoral Student Award of CAD 5,100 per term.
requirements: International student holding a Canadian study permit
Full-time PhD in Geography, Planning, Social and Ecological Sustainability, or Sustainability Management
Good academic standing
Completed application by 1 February 2027 to be sure of funding
documents: Complete PhD application to the chosen programme (the funding page does not list the documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Funding follows admission: admitted full-time doctoral students receive the guarantee, and the IDSA is given automatically to eligible students. Admission decisions are made by each programme.
important_dates: Deadline for guaranteed funding consideration: 1 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Waterloo is a public research university in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. Its Faculty of Environment offers graduate programmes in geography, planning, sustainability and related fields and lists more than 100 awards for its students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact possible supervisors before applying to confirm they can fund you, then submit a complete PhD application to your chosen Faculty of Environment programme by 1 February 2027. Funding questions go to env-grad-info@uwaterloo.ca.
opportunities.notes: Applications after 1 February 2027 can still be funded, but only at the unit's discretion.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: AI and Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scientists working on AI in biology can submit an abstract by 2 February 2027 for the EMBO | EMBL Symposium in Heidelberg (11 to 14 May 2027) and request a fee waiver or travel grant of up to EUR 1,000 from outside Europe.
opportunities.description:
The EMBO | EMBL Symposium "AI and biology" brings together researchers who use artificial intelligence to understand living systems. It takes place from 11 to 14 May 2027 at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, with a virtual option, and includes invited and selected talks, poster sessions and a day of workshops and tutorials.

The scientific organisers are Mor Nitzan (Hebrew University of Jerusalem), Fabio Petroni (EMBL Rome) and Oliver Stegle (EMBL Heidelberg). Participants who register on site can submit an abstract for a talk or poster until 2 February 2027.

EMBL offers limited financial help, including registration fee waivers and travel grants of up to EUR 1,000 for people travelling from outside Europe, which makes the meeting reachable for African computational biologists and data scientists.
opportunities.benefits: Limited financial help: registration fee waivers, travel grants of up to EUR 400 within Europe or EUR 1,000 from outside Europe, and childcare grants. On-site fees (with meals): EUR 675 academia, EUR 575 PhD students, EUR 875 industry. Virtual: EUR 240 academia, EUR 190 PhD students, EUR 290 industry. Travel and accommodation are not included in fees.
requirements: Abstracts are accepted only from on-site registrants, not virtual participants
Abstract body of up to 2,000 characters (excluding spaces) and a title of up to 20 words
Financial help is requested within the abstract submission
documents: Abstract with name, organisation, country, email and choice of oral or poster
Grant request answers in the abstract form, if needed
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts are selected on scientific merit, with results about three weeks after the deadline. Grants consider need for funding and the career impact of attending.
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL is Europe's intergovernmental laboratory for the life sciences, and EMBO is an organisation of leading life scientists that supports research and training. Together they fund and organise the EMBO | EMBL Symposia series.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register for on-site attendance through the EMBL registration portal linked on the event page; you then receive a link to submit your abstract and grant request by 2 February 2027. Registration is confirmed only after payment of the invoice.
opportunities.notes: EMBL never asks for card details by email or phone; beware of sponsorship scams. Contact catherine.casas@embl.org.

opportunities.title: Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tuition plus a UKRI-rate stipend for outstanding new PhD applicants of any nationality starting in 2027-28, with school deadlines ranging from 16 November 2026 to 2 February 2027.

opportunities.title: Northwestern University Need-Based Financial Aid for International First-Year Students (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Northwestern who tick the aid box by 2 January 2027 can receive grant-only aid meeting full need; the CSS Profile or ISAFA is due 2 February 2027 (Regular Decision).
opportunities.description:
Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, gives need-based financial aid to a small group of first-year international students each year. Aid packages meet 100% of the student's demonstrated need and are made up only of grants and scholarships, with no loans or work requirement, covering the full cost of attendance.

Northwestern is need aware for international applicants, so asking for aid can affect the admission decision. Students must tick the financial aid interest box on their admission application by the aid request date, then send the CSS Profile or ISAFA and their parents' tax documents.

For admitted African students from families who cannot pay, a full-need, loan-free package at a top US university is life-changing, but places are limited. International transfer students cannot receive this aid.
opportunities.benefits: Grant and scholarship aid meeting 100% of demonstrated need, with no loans or work, covering tuition, room and board, fees, health insurance, books, personal expenses, visa renewal costs and a travel allowance. Four-year aid awards are made.
requirements: International first-year applicant (not for transfer students)
Must request aid on the admission application by 2 January 2027 (Regular Decision)
Admission is need aware for international students
Students without US permanent residency cannot receive US federal aid
documents: CSS Profile (code 1565) or the Northwestern ISAFA form
Parents' most recent tax forms, or an official earnings letter if no annual tax form
English translations with amounts converted to US dollars and the rate stated
Cover sheet, with your full name and date of birth on every document
opportunities.selection_process: Aid is need-based and competitive among international applicants because funds are limited and admission is need aware. Aid offers are sent with or soon after the admission decision.
important_dates: Regular Decision aid request on admission application: 2 January 2027
CSS Profile or ISAFA due: 2 February 2027
Admission decisions and aid offers: late March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Northwestern University is a private research university in Evanston, Illinois, near Chicago. Its Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid manages need-based aid for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Tick the financial aid interest box on your Northwestern application, then complete the CSS Profile or ISAFA and upload your family's documents through the Undergraduate Financial Aid secure document upload. Contact undergradaid@u.northwestern.edu or +1 847-491-7400 with questions.
opportunities.notes: CSS Profile fee waivers are not available to international students. If you forgot to tick the aid box, email nuinternational@northwestern.edu before the aid deadline.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus STRAINS Master in Solid Mechanics 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: STRAINS Consortium (Université de Lille and Centrale Lille, coordinator)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Science or engineering graduates in mechanics, mechanical or civil engineering with B2 English can apply; all applicants are considered for Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
STRAINS is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Solid Mechanics coordinated by the Université de Lille and Centrale Lille in France, with partners NTUA in Athens (Greece), UCLouvain (Belgium), the University of Calabria (Italy) and Wrocław University of Science and Technology (Poland), plus associated partners.

The programme trains students in the mechanics of solids and structures over up to 24 months of study across partner universities. The call for the 2027-2029 intake opened on 3 November 2026 at 10:00 Brussels time and closes on 3 February 2027 at 23:59 Brussels time.

Every applicant is automatically considered for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship, and there is no nationality restriction, which makes it a strong option for African mechanical and civil engineering graduates.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of up to EUR 1,400 per month for full-time enrolment, for up to 24 months, covering travel, visa, installation and living costs.
requirements: Bachelor of Science or Engineering in mechanics, mechanical or civil engineering, or equivalent
Strong background in mechanics, physics and mathematics
English at least B2 (CEFR)
No previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship
documents: English certificate (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, EF SET or a B2+ letter)
Proof of current residence dated within 12 months before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Files are evaluated first, and shortlisted applicants are invited to an online interview before scholarships are awarded.
opportunities.about_provider: The STRAINS consortium is led by the Université de Lille and Centrale Lille in northern France and includes leading engineering universities in Greece, Belgium, Italy and Poland under the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply in English on the STRAINS application platform (plateforme.master-strains.eu) before 3 February 2027; this application also counts as your scholarship application. Questions go to master-strains@univ-lille.fr.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship page refers to the 2027-2029 intake call opening in autumn 2026, matching the open call on the application page.

opportunities.title: IPSA Travel Grants, 29th World Congress of Political Science (WC2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Political scientists living, working or studying in, or citizens of, developing economies who have a role in the 2027 IPSA World Congress programme can apply for a travel grant (USD 1,000 for Africa) from 4 December 2026 to 3 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The International Political Science Association (IPSA) offers travel grants to help scholars from emerging and developing economies attend its 29th World Congress of Political Science in Rome, Italy, from 24 to 28 July 2027. The theme is "Uncertain Democracies: Rethinking Governance in a Changing Global System", and the congress is organised with LUISS and the Italian political science association SISP.

Grants are for people who already have a role in the congress programme, such as a paper author, chair or discussant, and who will attend in person. They include a cash grant paid at the congress, free registration and a year of IPSA membership.

African political scientists receive the highest grant level (USD 1,000). Because a programme role is needed and the paper deadline (11 November 2026) has passed, the grant is mainly for those whose proposals are already in.
opportunities.benefits: A cash grant paid at the congress in Rome: USD 1,000 for Africa, Asia and Latin America and USD 700 for Europe. Free congress registration and one year of free IPSA membership. No advance payments are made.
requirements: Live, work or study in, or be a citizen of, an emerging or developing economy (IPSA list based on 2023 GNI per capita)
Hold a role in the congress programme, such as author, chair or discussant
Attend the congress in person
Apply online through an IPSA account (email requests are not accepted)
documents: Proof of citizenship (passport ID page or national ID)
Proof of work or study in an emerging or developing economy (student card, staff card or employment letter with dates)
Reference letter from an employer, colleague, supervisor or teacher
opportunities.selection_process: IPSA scores applications with a points system set out in its rules, considering the applicant's role in the programme, region of citizenship and work or study, whether they received a grant before, gender, age, contribution to IPSA membership and the status of their national association.
opportunities.about_provider: The International Political Science Association (IPSA) is the worldwide body of political science, founded under UNESCO in 1949. It brings together national associations and individual members and holds a World Congress every two years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in to your IPSA account and complete the travel grant application on the WC2027 website between 4 December 2026 and 3 February 2027, uploading the documents listed. Contact wc2027@ipsa.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: A separate LOC Solidarity Fund supports a limited number of paper presenters in local organising committee panels. IPSA also runs other awards, such as the Global South Award, with a 1 March 2027 deadline.

opportunities.title: Linköping University International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying master's applicants who rank Linköping University first and are admitted in the first round can get a 25, 50 or 75 percent tuition reduction.

opportunities.title: Washington College of Law Human Rights Essay Award 2027
opportunities.provider: American University Washington College of Law
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Licensed lawyers with a law degree, of any nationality, writing on international human rights law in English or Spanish.
opportunities.description:
The Human Rights Essay Award is an annual writing competition run by the Academy on Human Rights and Humanitarian Law at American University Washington College of Law. Lawyers submit an unpublished legal article on international human rights law (including humanitarian and international criminal law) on a set topic; for 2027 the topic is "Democracy, Human Rights and Participation", and essays that stray from it are disqualified.

The best article in English and the best in Spanish each win a full-tuition place on the Academy's Advanced Studies Program in Washington, D.C., and the winning work may be considered for the American University International Law Review. Four honourable mentions are also given.

The award is open to any nationality, so African lawyers working on democracy, elections, civic participation or related rights can use it to gain recognition and a funded course at a well-known US law school.
opportunities.benefits: For each winner (best English and best Spanish article): a full-tuition scholarship to the Academy's Advanced Studies Program, covering application and administrative fees and up to four courses. Travel, housing and daily expenses are not covered. Four honourable mentions. Possible publication in the American University International Law Review.
requirements: Must hold a law degree (J.D., LL.M., LL.B., S.J.D. or equivalent, with proof); the 2027 call says only licensed attorneys are eligible
Experience in or interest in international human rights law
Current law students are not eligible; those awaiting a diploma should consult the Academy
Past winners cannot enter
Any nationality
Essay in English or Spanish; one submission per person
Essay must address the 2027 topic "Democracy, Human Rights and Participation"
documents: Unpublished essay of up to 35 pages including footnotes, in Word format, anonymous (Times New Roman 12 pt double-spaced, 10 pt single-spaced footnotes, Bluebook or Indigo Book citations, no bibliography or annexes)
Separate CV of up to three pages
opportunities.selection_process: Entries are checked for plagiarism, then a pre-selection committee shortlists essays and an Honor Jury chooses the winners. The jury's decision is final.
important_dates: Deadline: 3 February 2027, 11:59 pm Washington, D.C. time
opportunities.about_provider: The Academy on Human Rights and Humanitarian Law is a programme of American University Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C. It runs specialised courses, the Advanced Studies Program, moot courts and publications on international human rights law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the essay and CV through the Academy's online Google Form linked on the call page, then send the confirmation email without attachments as instructed. Entries sent only by email are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Follow the formatting rules exactly and keep the essay anonymous. Stay tightly on the 2027 topic, as off-topic essays are disqualified.

opportunities.title: ESHG 2027 Conference Fellowships (Rotterdam)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career human genetics researchers (students or within four years of their last degree, not PIs) who are ESHG members and submit an abstract; 10 places are reserved for Africa.
opportunities.description:
The European Society of Human Genetics offers conference fellowships so that early-career researchers can attend its 2027 conference, held in hybrid format in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, from 12 to 15 June 2027. The fellowship pays towards travel and gives free registration.

There are four types. One is reserved for researchers from non-European low and lower-middle income countries: 40 fellowships of EUR 600 each, with ten set aside for Africa. There are also up to 140 fellowships for Europe, ten Fellowships of Excellence for the best-rated abstracts from any country, and national fellowships nominated by national genetics societies.

Applicants apply at the same time as they submit an abstract, so this is a strong route for African students and young geneticists who want to present their research at one of the largest human genetics meetings in the world.
opportunities.benefits: Free conference registration (including lunches) plus a travel contribution: EUR 400 for European fellows; EUR 600 for fellows from non-European low and lower-middle income countries (10 places each for Central/South America, Africa, the Middle East and Asia); EUR 600 for Fellowships of Excellence and National ESHG Fellowships.
requirements: Early-career investigator on 4 February 2027: a student, a medical doctor who finished specialisation no more than four years ago, or another researcher whose last degree is no more than four years old
Not a principal investigator
ESHG member for 2027
Must submit an abstract (types 1 to 3)
Only one conference fellowship per year, not in two consecutive years, and not combined with an ESHG Mentorship
documents: Proof of graduation or current studies in PDF (for example a diploma or a dated enrolment letter), uploaded during abstract submission
opportunities.selection_process: The Scientific Programme Committee selects fellows for types 1 to 3, with Fellowships of Excellence going to the best-rated abstracts. National fellowships are nominated by each national human genetics society under its own deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: The European Society of Human Genetics (ESHG) is a professional body that promotes research and good practice in human and medical genetics. Its annual conference is organised with the Vienna Medical Academy (Wiener Medizinische Akademie).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the ESHG 2027 online abstract system and tick the fellowship boxes at the "Fellowships & Awards" step, uploading your proof of status. For a national fellowship, apply through your national society. Late applications are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Join ESHG for 2027 before applying. The organiser may withdraw offers if the conference format changes. Contact: conference@eshg.org.

opportunities.title: Emory University Need-Based Aid for International First-Year Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Emory who apply Regular Decision and show financial need.
