Emory University in Atlanta offers need-based financial aid to a select group of international first-year students each year. The aid is meant for admitted students who cannot pay for their studies from other sources, and it is assessed through the College Board CSS Profile and tax documents submitted through IDOC.

International students who want to be considered for need-based aid must apply under Regular Decision and tell Emory on the Common App or Coalition App that they are seeking aid. Emory also runs merit scholarships through its Emory Scholar programmes, which have an earlier deadline.

For African students aiming at a top US research university, this is one of the few routes to financial help as a non-citizen, but places are limited, so the finance documents must be complete and on time.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based financial aid package for admitted international first-year students; the page does not state amounts.
requirements: Not a US citizen or permanent resident (some non-citizen categories such as refugees and asylees are treated as US-aid eligible)
Apply as a first-year student under Regular Decision
Meet Emory's first-year admission requirements
Show English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo)
Complete the financial certification
Aid is for students with no other resources to pay
documents: Common App or Coalition App with the financial aid question answered yes
Parents' tax returns or income documents via IDOC, translated into English and converted to US dollars with the exchange rate
