Merit scholarship consideration: apply before December
opportunities.about_provider: Emory University is a private research university in Atlanta, Georgia, with undergraduate study at Emory College and Oxford College. Its Office of Financial Aid manages need-based aid and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Emory under Regular Decision and indicate on the application that you want financial aid. Submit the CSS Profile and upload your family's tax documents through IDOC before 5 February, and complete the Documentation of Finances form. Contact finaid@emory.edu with questions.
opportunities.notes: Missing the February deadline or applying Early Decision without planning can cost you aid eligibility. Translate and convert all financial documents before uploading.

opportunities.title: IASR Travel Grants for Historically Marginalized Groups and Geographies 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students from marginalised groups or low and middle income countries who will present at the IASR annual meeting.
opportunities.description:
The International Academy of Sex Research (IASR) offers up to three travel grants so that researchers from historically marginalised groups and geographies can attend and present at its annual meeting. The grants cover registration, hotel and part of the travel cost.

There are three categories: established researchers (more than five years after their postgraduate degree), early-career researchers (within five years) and current students. Priority goes to people who are under-represented in the field, including researchers based outside North America, Europe and Australia and those living in low and middle income countries.

This makes the grants directly relevant to African researchers in sexual health, sexuality, gender and related fields who have work to present but lack conference funding.
opportunities.benefits: Free conference registration, four nights in the conference hotel and up to USD 750 in travel support, reimbursed through PayPal after the meeting.
requirements: Must present scientific work at the meeting (symposium, brief communication, data blitz or poster)
IASR membership is encouraged but not required
Priority for BIPOC, first-generation, disabled and gender-diverse researchers, researchers outside North America, Europe and Australia, and residents of low and middle income countries
Category depends on career stage: established, early career (within 5 years of postgraduate degree) or student
opportunities.selection_process: IASR reviews applications and notifies applicants between mid-February and early March. Awards are confirmed only once the applicant's presentation has been accepted.
important_dates: Presentation submissions: symposia in December, brief communications and data blitz in March, posters in April
opportunities.about_provider: The International Academy of Sex Research is a scholarly society for researchers who study sexuality and sexual health. It holds an annual scientific meeting and publishes the journal Archives of Sexual Behavior.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the travel grant application form on the IASR website before 5 February 2027 and submit your presentation through the normal call for the annual meeting.
opportunities.notes: Only three grants are available, so make your essay specific about your research and why the meeting matters for your career.

opportunities.title: ICCS 2027: 27th International Conference on Computational Science
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and graduate students worldwide working in computational science.
opportunities.description:
ICCS 2027, the 27th International Conference on Computational Science, invites papers on computational methods, modelling and simulation across science and engineering. It will be held fully in person from 12 to 14 July 2027 at the Faculty of Computer Science of AGH University of Krakow, Poland, with proceedings published by Springer in the Lecture Notes in Computer Science series.

Authors can submit full papers, short papers or abstracts of up to 15 pages in LNCS format. Accepted authors who cannot travel can choose a registration-only option. The conference also runs thematic workshops and a student competition.

For African researchers and graduate students in computational science, ICCS is a well-established venue to publish in an indexed series and meet the international community; check the registration page for fees, as the call itself does not state any travel funding.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted papers in Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science and the chance to present at the conference. No travel or fee support is stated in the call.
requirements: Original paper in English, up to 15 pages in LNCS format (full paper, short paper or abstract)
At least one author must register and present the paper
Registration-only option available for accepted authors who cannot attend
documents: Paper in LNCS format submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed by the programme committee, with acceptance notices sent on 5 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ICCS is an annual international conference series on computational science, organised in 2027 by AGH University of Krakow with a general chair from Brunel University London. Its proceedings appear in Springer's LNCS series.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper in the LNCS template and submit it through the ICCS 2027 EasyChair site by 5 February 2027. After acceptance, register by 23 April 2027 and upload the camera-ready version.
opportunities.notes: Look at the conference's student competition and thematic workshops, which may suit early-stage work. Contact: iccs@computationalscience.nl.

opportunities.title: International Court of Justice Judicial Fellowship Programme 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law graduates aged 31 or under with excellent results and strong English or French can be nominated by their university by 5 February 2027 for a ten-month fellowship at the ICJ in The Hague.
opportunities.description:
The Judicial Fellowship Programme of the International Court of Justice, which used to be called the University Traineeship Programme and dates from 1999, lets young lawyers spend about ten months, from early September to June, working at the principal judicial organ of the United Nations in The Hague. Each fellow is assigned to a Member of the Court and works alongside that judge's legal assistant, carrying out legal research, drafting memoranda and attending public hearings and sittings of the Court.

Up to 16 fellows are chosen each year. Candidates cannot apply on their own: a university must nominate them, register through the Court's online pre-screening questionnaire and send the full nomination file by 5 February 2027. The Court makes its decisions by April 2027.

From the 2027-2028 edition, sponsoring universities must give each fellow a stipend of at least EUR 3,500 net for the whole fellowship, plus health insurance and travel. For African candidates this matters: the Court keeps a trust fund that can support nationals of developing countries who are nominated by universities in developing countries that cannot pay for them.
opportunities.benefits: The nominating university must provide a stipend of at least EUR 3,500 net of tax for the full fellowship, health insurance and travel. A trust fund run by the Court can help nationals of developing countries nominated by universities in developing countries that cannot sponsor them.
requirements: Nomination by a university (individual applications are not accepted)
Aged 31 or younger at the start of the fellowship (waived only in special circumstances)
Excellent academic results in law
Strong interest in public international law
Excellent spoken and written English or French; working knowledge of the other is an asset
opportunities.selection_process: The nominating university first completes an online pre-screening questionnaire and names a focal point, who then emails each candidate's complete file in the set order. The Court reviews the nominations and announces its decisions by April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, based in the Peace Palace in The Hague. It settles legal disputes between states and gives advisory opinions on questions of international law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Ask your law school or university to nominate you. The university registers through the Court's online form, appoints a focal point and emails the nomination letter, personal history form, references, transcripts, writing sample and summary table for each candidate before 5 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Check the Court's eligibility list for the trust fund if your university cannot pay the stipend. All documents must be complete by the deadline.

opportunities.title: EUSIPCO 2027 Call for Papers (Darmstadt, Aug 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students worldwide working in signal processing.
opportunities.description:
EUSIPCO 2027, the 35th European Signal Processing Conference, invites papers in all areas of signal processing. It is organised by the European Association for Signal Processing (EURASIP) and will take place from 30 August to 3 September 2027 at the darmstadtium congress centre in Darmstadt, Germany.

Papers are five pages long and are reviewed single-blind; accepted papers that are presented appear in IEEE Xplore and in open-access proceedings. The conference also accepts presentations of recently published journal papers and runs special sessions, tutorials and a Three Minute Thesis contest.

For African students and researchers in signal processing, communications, machine learning or audio and image processing, EUSIPCO is a leading European venue. The organisers list a student travel grant and a best student paper contest as "coming soon", so watch the site for details.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in IEEE Xplore and the open-access EUSIPCO proceedings for papers that are presented. A student travel grant, best student paper contest and 3MT contest are announced as coming soon; details not yet published.
requirements: Five-page paper (10 pt font, including figures, references and appendices) in the IEEE template, PDF with embedded fonts
Abstract of up to 200 words
At least one author must register at the full rate by 2 June 2027; one registration covers up to three papers
Papers not presented are treated as no-shows
documents: Five-page paper in PDF submitted through the conference management system
opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind peer review by the technical programme committee across the conference's topic areas.
important_dates: Author registration and early bird: 2 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: EURASIP, the European Association for Signal Processing, is a non-profit body that promotes signal processing research and education and runs the annual EUSIPCO conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Write your paper in the IEEE template and submit it through the EUSIPCO 2027 conference management system, which will be linked from the conference papers page. Register at least one author by 2 June 2027.
opportunities.notes: The submission link was not yet live when checked on 19 November 2026. Contact: info@eusipco2027.de.

opportunities.title: FENS Travel Grants for the FENS Regional Meeting 2027 (Istanbul)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: FENS members who are PhD students or postdocs within five years of their PhD and present a first-author poster at FRM 2027 in Istanbul.
opportunities.description:
FENS, the Federation of European Neuroscience Societies, offers travel grants so that early-career neuroscientists can attend the FENS Regional Meeting 2027 (FRM 2027). The meeting takes place in person in Istanbul, Türkiye, from 26 to 29 May 2027 and is organised by the Turkish, Greek, Serbian and Slovenian neuroscience societies with FENS support.

Grants range from EUR 500 to EUR 800 depending on how far the applicant travels, and are paid by bank transfer after the meeting. Each grantee must present a first-author poster in person, based on an abstract already submitted to the meeting.

The grants are open to FENS members who are PhD students or postdocs up to five years after their PhD, which includes African researchers who are members of a FENS-affiliated society or individual FENS members. Note that nationals of Sudan, among other sanctioned countries, cannot be accepted.
opportunities.benefits: A travel grant of EUR 500 to EUR 800, depending on the distance to Istanbul, paid by bank transfer after the meeting. The registration fee still has to be paid.
requirements: FENS member (log in to apply)
PhD student or postdoc no more than 5 years after the PhD at the deadline (parental or documented health leave excluded)
Must attend in person and present a poster as first author, based on an abstract already submitted to FRM 2027
Not resident or working in Türkiye
No travel grant for another 2027 FENS meeting or SfN 2027
FENS cannot accept nationals of Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Sudan or Syria
documents: Contact details of one referee, who submits a recommendation form within five working days after the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: FENS checks eligibility and selects grantees; the call does not publish scoring criteria or the number of grants. Results are announced on 1 March 2027, and grantees must check in at the FENS booth at the meeting.
opportunities.about_provider: FENS is the umbrella federation of national and single-discipline neuroscience societies in Europe. It runs the FENS Forum and regional meetings, training schools and grants for neuroscientists.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract to FRM 2027 first, then log in to your FENS member account and complete the travel grant form on the FENS grant page. Name a referee, who receives an automatic email and must send the recommendation within five working days after the deadline. Questions go to grants@fens.org.
opportunities.notes: The travel grant application is separate from meeting registration and abstract submission. Your application is incomplete until the referee form arrives.

opportunities.title: IEEE SSP Workshop 2027 Call for Papers (Annecy, Jun 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students worldwide working in statistical signal processing.
opportunities.description:
The 2027 IEEE Statistical Signal Processing Workshop (SSP 2027), the 24th in the series, invites full papers on statistical signal processing theory, methods and applications. It is organised under the IEEE Signal Processing Society and will be held from 28 June to 1 July 2027 in Annecy, a lakeside town in the French Alps, with plenary talks and special sessions.

Papers are four pages of technical content plus an optional fifth page for references, and accepted papers are presented as posters and published in IEEE Xplore. Best student paper awards will be given.

For African graduate students and researchers working on estimation, detection, learning or statistical methods for signals, SSP is a focused, well-regarded workshop that is a good first international venue.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted papers in IEEE Xplore and a poster presentation at the workshop; best student paper awards. Travel grants and fees are not stated on the call.
requirements: Paper of 4 pages of technical content plus an optional 5th page for references only
IEEE conference template (LaTeX or Word), submitted as PDF
An author must register by 30 April 2027 and present an A0 portrait poster
documents: IEEE copyright form with the camera-ready version
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed by the technical programme committee, with decisions sent on 14 April 2027.
important_dates: Special session and tutorial proposals: 7 December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Signal Processing Society is the world's largest professional body for signal processing engineers and scientists. It sponsors conferences, workshops and journals in the field.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your paper with the IEEE template and submit it through the online submission system linked from the workshop's Submit a Paper page before 7 February 2027. After acceptance, upload the camera-ready paper and copyright form and register by 30 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: Deadlines are Anywhere on Earth time. Check the site for registration fees and visa information.

opportunities.title: AE Scholarship Fund for International Undergraduates 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Current international undergraduates at Michigan can apply for USD 3,000 to 5,000 toward tuition, housing, food or emergency needs.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus NavigAIte EU – AI for Business Transformation scholarship 2027
opportunities.provider: NavigAIte EU (Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences consortium)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality admitted through the entrance exam; scholarships allocated by merit with EU regional quotas.
opportunities.description:
NavigAIte EU's Degree Programme in AI for Business Transformation is a two-year, English-taught Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's leading to a Master of Business Administration. It is coordinated by Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences in Helsinki, Finland, with the Technical University of Košice (Slovakia) and the University of Seville (Spain) as partners in the Ulysseus European University alliance.

Students spend the first year in Helsinki, the third semester in Košice or Seville and write their thesis at the other partner. The programme received Erasmus Mundus status in 2026 and has 50 EU-funded scholarships over its six-year funding period, each paying EUR 1,400 a month for the full two years plus a tuition waiver.

The next application round runs from 25 January to 8 February 2027 for studies starting in January 2028. Scholarships are awarded on entrance exam results with EU regional quotas, so African applicants compete for places alongside other world regions.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: EUR 1,400 per month for the full two-year programme and exemption from tuition (non-EU/EEA tuition is otherwise EUR 12,000 per year). 50 scholarships in total over six years; some admitted students get a study place without financial aid.
requirements: Apply in the national Studyinfo admissions round (25 January to 8 February 2027)
Pass a two-phase online entrance exam
Previous Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship holders cannot get another
Further admission criteria are published on Studyinfo
documents: CV in the template published by Haaga-Helia
Preliminary materials for the entrance exam (published 25 January 2027)
Other documents as listed on Studyinfo
opportunities.selection_process: Admission and scholarships are decided on entrance exam performance, taking into account Erasmus Mundus regional quotas. Phase 1 is online on 16 March 2027 and phase 2 online on 6 to 7 April 2027.
important_dates: Application period: 25 January to 8 February 2027, 23:59 Finnish time
opportunities.about_provider: Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences is a Finnish business-focused university of applied sciences in Helsinki. It coordinates the NavigAIte EU project within the Ulysseus European University alliance.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Studyinfo (opintopolku.fi), Finland's national admissions portal; the programme application also counts as the scholarship application. Prepare with the preliminary materials and CV template that Haaga-Helia publishes on 25 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The application window is short (two weeks). Not every admitted student gets a scholarship, so check whether you can self-fund if offered a place without aid.

opportunities.title: ICGC Scholar Fellowships 2027-28, University of Minnesota
opportunities.provider: University of Minnesota, Interdisciplinary Center for the Study of Global Change (ICGC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New doctoral students (and Master of Development Practice students) admitted to participating University of Minnesota programmes, nominated by their department, with interests in the Global South, equity, justice and global change.
opportunities.description:
The ICGC Scholar Fellowships support new graduate students at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities who are committed to the interdisciplinary study of the Global South in the context of global change. They are open to students entering doctoral programmes in several colleges (CBS, CEHD, CFANS, CLA, the School of Public Health and the Humphrey School) and the Master of Development Practice.

Students cannot apply directly: they apply for admission to their programme and are nominated by the department, usually with the admission application before mid-December. The ICGC nomination deadline for 2027-28 fellowships is 4 p.m. Central Time on 8 February 2027.

ICGC gives priority to students whose interests relate to equity, justice and global change in the Global South, which it interprets broadly. This makes it a good fit for African applicants planning a PhD on development, environment, health or social change in their region.
opportunities.benefits: First-year fellowship support that varies in amount, duration and format. The home department typically guarantees a 50% teaching or research assistantship in years two and three, plus tuition and health insurance for four years. Dissertation research support and optional predissertation grants are also mentioned. Travel to Minnesota is not covered.
requirements: At least a bachelor's degree
Applied and admitted to a participating doctoral programme or the Master of Development Practice at the Twin Cities campus
Newly entering the programme in 2027-28 (current UMN doctoral students are not eligible)
Nominated by the programme, department or college
documents: Admission application to the graduate programme
Department nomination form (submitted by the department)
opportunities.selection_process: ICGC reviews the nominees for interest in equity, justice and global change, academic excellence, and commitment to interdisciplinary work.
important_dates: Department nomination forms: generally before mid-December 2026
ICGC nomination deadline: 8 February 2027, 4 p.m. CT
opportunities.about_provider: ICGC is a unit of the University of Minnesota's Research and Innovation Office that supports graduate students and research on the Global South and global change.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a participating UMN doctoral programme or the MDP and ask the department to nominate you for an ICGC Scholar Fellowship, usually by filling in the department's nomination form with your admission application before mid-December.

opportunities.title: ISU Bocconi Scholarship 2027-28 for International MSc Applicants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year MSc applicants to Bocconi whose family income and assets fall within the ISU thresholds.
opportunities.description:
The ISU Bocconi Scholarship is Bocconi University's need-based award under Italy's right-to-education (diritto allo studio) scheme. For the 2027-28 academic year, first-year MSc applicants from abroad can apply in rounds that match Bocconi's international admission rounds, and eligibility is judged on the family's economic situation measured by the ISEEU Parificato indicator.

International MSc applicants in the first round apply between 28 January and 8 February 2027, with later rounds in March, April and June 2027. The application is made online with income and asset documents for the whole household, and a certificate issued by a tax assistance centre (CAF) partnered with Bocconi.

For African students admitted to a Bocconi MSc in Milan, this is the main route to need-based support, but it is paperwork-heavy, so start gathering family financial documents early.
requirements: First-year applicant to a Bocconi MSc programme for 2027-28
Family economic indicator (ISEEU Parificato) and assets within the ISU thresholds
Apply in the window that matches your admission round
Documents signed by hand, matching your ID
documents: ISEEU Parificato certificate issued in 2027 by a CAF partnered with Bocconi
Financial statement signed by an accountant if the family had business activity at 31/12/2025, or a declaration that it had none
Extra income and residence documents for independent students
opportunities.selection_process: Bocconi checks the economic and asset data and the completeness of the documents. Feedback on completeness is given by 30 September 2027 at the latest. Late or incomplete applications are not evaluated.
important_dates: International MSc round 1: 28 January to 8 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Bocconi University is a private university in Milan, Italy, specialising in economics, management, finance, law and data science. Its Fees, Funding and Housing Office runs the ISU Bocconi benefits.
opportunities.how_to_apply: During your round's window, open the online application from the ISU Bocconi page, fill in the household, income and business data, upload the documents and click Complete data and then Submit application. Follow your notifications in MyApplication.
opportunities.notes: The official page is marked as being updated, so dates may change. Amounts and thresholds are not shown on the deadlines page.

opportunities.title: NYU CSAAD Pre-Doctoral Research Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: New York University, Center for the Study of Africa and the African Diaspora (CSAAD)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates in the dissertation-writing stage in the humanities or social sciences, researching Africa or its diaspora, can apply by 8 February 2027 for a year at NYU with a $30,000 stipend and health insurance.
opportunities.description:
New York University's Center for the Study of Africa and the African Diaspora (CSAAD) offers a pre-doctoral research fellowship for the 2027-28 academic year. It is designed for PhD candidates who have reached the writing phase of their dissertation and need a year of focused time to complete it.

The fellow is based at CSAAD's offices at 20 Cooper Square in Manhattan for the full academic year and joins the intellectual life of a centre dedicated to Africa and the African diaspora. Projects must be in the humanities or social sciences and must deal with Africa or its diaspora.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African doctoral candidates enrolled at universities in Africa or elsewhere can apply. The fellowship offers a stipend, health insurance and a base in New York to finish writing.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$30,000 and health insurance for the 2027-28 academic year.
requirements: PhD candidate in the dissertation-writing phase
Field in the humanities or social sciences
Dissertation research on Africa or the African diaspora
Must disclose any other fellowship support for 2027-28
Able to be in residence at NYU in New York for the academic year
documents: Statement of other fellowship support for 2027-28
One recommendation letter emailed to csaad@nyu.edu
opportunities.selection_process: CSAAD reviews the applications; the page does not describe further stages or the number of awards.
opportunities.about_provider: CSAAD is a research centre at New York University that supports scholarship, teaching and public programmes on Africa and the African diaspora. It hosts pre-doctoral and post-doctoral fellows each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked as 'Apply here' on the CSAAD fellowship page and upload the letter, summary, chapter, CV and support statement. Ask your referee to email the recommendation letter to csaad@nyu.edu before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to csaad@nyu.edu or +1 212-998-8624. CSAAD also runs a post-doctoral fellowship for scholars based in Africa and the diaspora outside North America and Europe; its 2026-27 round closed in March 2026, so watch for the next call.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus RADMEP+ (Radiation, Microelectronics and Photonics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Physics, electronics or photonics graduates of any nationality with a 180-ECTS bachelor's and B2 English.
opportunities.description:
RADMEP+ is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Radiation, Microelectronics and Photonics, taught in English and co-funded by the EU. Students start at the University of Jyväskylä in Finland and continue at partner universities including KU Leuven, Ghent University, Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Université Jean Monnet and the University of Montpellier.

The 2027-2029 call is open from 16 October 2026 to 9 February 2027 (12:00 UTC) for scholarship consideration. Around 70 EMJM scholarships are offered over four intakes, plus up to 20 extra scholarships for targeted world regions and fee waivers for up to 50 self-funded students.

The programme states that it does not discriminate by nationality and welcomes students from all regions, so African physics, electronics and photonics graduates can compete for full scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: EMJM scholarship: up to EUR 1,400 per month for two years (up to EUR 33,600) plus a 100% waiver of participation costs. RADMEP+ fee waiver for self-funded students: EUR 1,000 per year (EU) or EUR 2,000 per year (non-EU). Participation costs otherwise EUR 9,000 per year for non-EU students. Accommodation and travel are not covered.
requirements: Bachelor of Science or equivalent first-cycle degree of 180 ECTS, preferably in microelectronics, photonics or physics (final-year students may apply)
Solid background in physics, photonics, semiconductor physics and microelectronics
English at CEFR B2, checked through scores, cover letter and interview
Self-funded students must prove full financial support
No nationality restriction; no more than 10% of scholarships to one nationality
documents: Authentic, complete, certified documents (scans of originals or certified translations into English)
Full list on the programme's how-to-apply page
opportunities.selection_process: Admission and scholarships use the same merit-based process. Shortlisted applicants may be interviewed remotely; the selection committee meets in mid-March and outcomes (main or reserve list) are sent on 22 March 2027.
important_dates: Induction in Jyväskylä: end of August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: RADMEP+ is run by a consortium of European public universities led by the University of Jyväskylä, Finland. It trains specialists in radiation effects on electronics, microelectronics and photonics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the admissions link on master-radmep.org before 9 February 2027, 12:00 UTC, to be considered automatically for scholarships. Upload certified documents and be ready for a possible remote interview.
opportunities.notes: Applications after the scholarship deadline are not considered for scholarships. Dual nationals must choose one nationality.

opportunities.title: Ghent University BOF Doctoral Scholarships for Candidates from the Global South 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates from listed Global South countries, including many in Africa, can apply with a Ghent supervisor by 9 February 2027 for a 48-month sandwich PhD.
opportunities.description:
Ghent University's Special Research Fund (BOF) offers 15 sandwich PhD scholarships each year to candidates from the Global South. Under the 2027 call, the doctorate lasts 48 months: 24 months are spent at Ghent University in Belgium and 24 months at a partner institution in the candidate's home region, starting from 1 October 2027.

Ghent funds the Belgian half of the PhD, while the home institution must guarantee 24 months of full-time local funding. Each candidate needs a Ghent professor as supervisor, and the application is submitted together with that promoter.

The list of eligible countries includes many African nations, among them Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Morocco, South Africa, Ethiopia, Uganda and Tanzania, which makes this one of the main Belgian routes into a joint PhD for African researchers.
opportunities.benefits: Funding for the 24 months spent at Ghent University. The Ghent promoter receives a bench fee of EUR 310 a month and a travel budget of EUR 8,000.
requirements: Nationality of a country on the BOF Global South list (includes many African countries)
Enrolled or to enrol as a doctoral student with at least 36 months of the PhD remaining at the start
A Ghent University professor as supervisor (max two candidates per supervisor, of different genders)
A partner institution guaranteeing 24 months of full-time local funding
First stay at Ghent between 1 October 2027 and 28 February 2028
documents: Ethics or biosafety advice where relevant
Statement from the partner institution on local funding
opportunities.selection_process: Ghent University's research council reviews the applications submitted by promoters; results are released from 12 May 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Ghent University is one of Belgium's largest research universities. Its Special Research Fund (BOF) finances research and doctoral scholarships, including this scheme for Global South candidates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a Ghent professor willing to supervise you and agree a joint research plan, then submit the application with your promoter by email to BOFapplication@ugent.be before 9 February 2027. Questions go to BOF@ugent.be.
opportunities.notes: Start contacting Ghent supervisors well before the deadline, since the promoter must prepare and submit the application with you.

opportunities.title: ZiF Fellowships: Practices of Interdisciplinary Research
opportunities.provider: Center for Interdisciplinary Research (ZiF), Bielefeld University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality with a doctorate and an institutional affiliation whose work studies interdisciplinary research.
opportunities.description:
The Center for Interdisciplinary Research (ZiF) at Bielefeld University has a special call for 8 to 10 fellowships in a research group on "Practices of Interdisciplinary Research". Fellows will spend six months in residence in Bielefeld, Germany, from 1 October 2028 to 31 March 2029, studying how interdisciplinary research works in practice.

The group starts with a compulsory on-site kick-off workshop from 13 to 17 March 2028. ZiF provides accommodation, travel and support for families, and can pay for teaching replacement at the fellow's home institution.

There is no nationality limit, so African researchers with a doctorate who study interdisciplinarity, science studies or collaborative research can apply; they need an institutional affiliation and permission for leave.
opportunities.benefits: Buy-out options such as teaching replacement, or allowances; travel to and from Bielefeld; free accommodation on campus or in Bielefeld; workshop funding; support for accompanying family members. No stipend amount is stated.
requirements: Doctoral degree
Affiliation with a university or research institute, especially during the fellowship
Confirmation from the home institution that leave will be granted
Research that advances the study of interdisciplinary research
documents: Project outline (up to 12,000 characters plus references)
Answers to four questions on reflection, collaboration, support and 2-3 workshop collaborators (6,000 characters in total)
opportunities.selection_process: A committee appointed by ZiF reviews applications on scholarly quality, originality, fit with the group's theme, prior research on interdisciplinarity, reflective approaches and experience of interdisciplinary collaboration. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online in June 2027 and decisions are made in July 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ZiF is Bielefeld University's Institute for Advanced Study, founded in 1968. It hosts research groups, workshops and fellows from all disciplines and countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into one PDF addressed to ZiF's Executive Director and upload it through the ZiF application form. Content questions go to Prof. Dr. Marie I. Kaiser; organisational questions to zif-proposalsupport@uni-bielefeld.de.
opportunities.notes: Applications that do not follow the formal requirements are not considered.

opportunities.title: ACM MobileHCI 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: HCI researchers and students worldwide working on mobile and ubiquitous interaction.
opportunities.description:
ACM MobileHCI 2027, the International Conference on Mobile Human-Computer Interaction, invites research papers on interaction with mobile, wearable and ubiquitous technologies. The 2027 theme is "Connecting Realities", and the conference takes place from 20 to 23 September 2027 at the St. Raphael Resort in Limassol, Cyprus, under ACM SIGCHI.

Full papers are published in the Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (PACMHCI) and reviewed double-anonymously. Authors first submit an abstract by 10 February 2027 and the full paper by 17 February 2027, with a revise-and-resubmit stage.

For African HCI researchers studying mobile technology, MobileHCI is the main specialised venue; note the open-access publishing charge, which institutions in ACM Open or waivers may cover.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in PACMHCI and presentation at the conference. Authors pay an ACM Open article charge of USD 500 (ACM/SIG members) or USD 750 (non-members) unless their institution is in ACM Open or a waiver applies.
requirements: Original paper, 5,000 to 8,000 words encouraged (over 12,000 words desk-rejected)
Anonymised for double-anonymous review
Abstract registered by 10 February 2027
opportunities.selection_process: Double-anonymous peer review with a first decision on 15 April 2027, a revision round and a final decision on 17 June 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ACM SIGCHI is the Association for Computing Machinery's Special Interest Group on Computer-Human Interaction, which sponsors the major HCI conferences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the Precision Conference System (SIGCHI > MobileHCI 2027 > MobileHCI 2027 papers): register the abstract by 10 February and upload the full paper by 17 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Check whether your institution is part of ACM Open or eligible for an article charge waiver before submitting.

opportunities.title: Heidelberg Laureate Forum 2027 (Young Researchers)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduates, master's and PhD students and postdocs in mathematics or computer science, of any nationality.
opportunities.description:
The Heidelberg Laureate Forum (HLF) brings about 200 young mathematicians and computer scientists together for a week with winners of the Abel Prize, ACM A.M. Turing Award, ACM Prize in Computing, Fields Medal, Nevanlinna/IMU Abacus Medal and other top awards. The 14th HLF takes place at the Heidelberg Congress Center in Germany, from arrival on 11 September to departure on 18 September 2027.

The forum covers hotel and meals for selected participants and offers travel grants to those whose institutions cannot pay. Applications are open from 11 November 2026 to 11 February 2027.

Undergraduates, master's students, PhD students and postdocs of any nationality can apply, which makes it an outstanding networking opportunity for African students in mathematics and computer science.
opportunities.benefits: Hotel with breakfast from 11 to 18 September 2027 and meals during the week, booked and paid by the foundation. Travel and visa costs can be reimbursed through a travel grant if your institution or national agency cannot pay (a rejection letter is required). Visa support letters are provided.
requirements: Student or researcher in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field
Undergraduate or master's student without a master's degree, PhD student, or postdoc within 5 years of the PhD (plus 1 year per child)
Each person may attend once per academic level
Good English
documents: Recommendation letter from a professor or supervisor, uploaded by the referee
PhD students and postdocs: thesis summary, transcripts and publications
Diplomas in the original language with English translations
opportunities.selection_process: Each application is rated by at least three reviewers from the award-giving institutions, and the top 100 applicants per discipline are invited. The foundation itself does not choose participants.
important_dates: Travel grant applications: 3 May to 23 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Heidelberg Laureate Forum Foundation organises the annual forum and is founded and funded by the Klaus Tschira Stiftung. Participants are selected by experts nominated by ACM, IMU and the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the HLF online application portal linked from the young researchers pages, uploading your CV, statement and documents, and ask your referee to submit the recommendation directly. If selected, apply for a travel grant between 3 May and 23 June 2027 if you need one.
opportunities.notes: Accompanying persons cannot join the programme. Contact: yr@heidelberg-laureate-forum.org.

opportunities.title: Ontario Tech International Emergency Bursary 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International-fee students coming to Canada because of war or environmental catastrophe can receive one of ten CAD 20,000 awards, renewable up to four years.

opportunities.title: ACAP International Merit Scholarship, Trimester 2 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students starting an eligible ACAP bachelor's or master's course in Trimester 2, 2027 can apply for a 20% tuition reduction.
opportunities.description:
The International Merit Scholarship is a tuition reduction offered by ACAP University College to new international students who enrol in one of its eligible bachelor's or master's courses. For the Trimester 2, 2027 intake it takes 20% off the published tuition fees, spread evenly across all the units of the course.

ACAP teaches in Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, and the award applies to courses in psychology, counselling, social work, management and criminology. It can run for the full normal length of the course: up to four years (12 trimesters) for a bachelor's degree and up to two years (6 trimesters) for a master's degree of full-time study.

The official page places no limit on nationality, so African students who apply to ACAP as international students can compete. Candidates are judged on their academic record and on a written statement about leadership, community contribution and their future goals.
opportunities.benefits: A 20% reduction on published tuition fees, applied evenly to every unit needed to complete the course, for up to 12 trimesters (bachelor's) or 6 trimesters (master's) of full-time study. Only one scholarship, bursary or discount can apply to a unit; if several apply, the highest one is used.
requirements: Be a new international student
Hold an offer for an eligible ACAP course starting in Trimester 2, 2027
Assessment considers completion of an Australian university degree at AQF level 7 or above with a minimum GPA of 80% (check the scholarship policy for how this applies to you)
Submit a written statement on leadership, community contribution, personal development and future impact
Study full time
documents: Written statement (leadership examples, skills, career goals, challenges overcome)
Evidence of completed degree and GPA
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed against two criteria: the academic record (degree level and GPA) and the written statement describing leadership, contribution to the community, personal growth and the impact the applicant hopes to have.
opportunities.about_provider: ACAP University College is an Australian higher education provider, part of the Navitas group, that specialises in applied professions such as psychology, counselling, social work, criminology and management. It runs campuses in five Australian cities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply to ACAP as an international student for an eligible course. Then complete the International Merit Scholarship online form linked from the scholarship page before 12 February 2027 and attach your written statement. Read the scholarship policy linked on the page before applying.
opportunities.notes: The award is a fee reduction, not a cash payment. It cannot be combined with another ACAP discount on the same unit. Phone enquiries: 1800 039 139.

opportunities.title: Beit Strathclyde (BStrath) Engineering Master's Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals and residents of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe with a good engineering degree and an offer for a one-year engineering master's at Strathclyde in 2027/28 can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Beit Strathclyde (BStrath) Scholarship is a full award for one-year taught master's study in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. It is run jointly by the university and the Beit Trust, and one scholarship is offered for the 2027/28 academic year.

The award covers the whole cost of the course, including tuition and living costs, for the one-year programme. Eligible departments are Architecture; Biomedical Engineering; Chemical and Process Engineering; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Design, Manufacturing and Engineering Management; Electronic and Electrical Engineering; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; and Naval Architecture, Ocean and Marine Engineering.

The scholarship is aimed at future leaders from Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe, the three countries the Beit Trust serves. Applicants are expected to return home after their studies and use what they have learned for the benefit of their country.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees; a living allowance; UK visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, TB test and biometrics costs; arrival, laptop and departure allowances; and economy return flights. Dependants are not funded.
requirements: National and permanent resident of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe at the time of application
A good engineering degree from a recognised university (Distinction or Upper Second preferred)
An offer for a one-year taught master's in one of the eight eligible Strathclyde engineering departments for 2027/28
International fee status
About three years of work experience is a guide
Commitment to return home after the course
Must not have started the course already
documents: Offer letter from the University of Strathclyde
Personal statement of up to 300 words on how the study will benefit your country
Three references (academic, character and employer if applicable)
opportunities.selection_process: The Beit Trust selects on merit and eligibility, looking at degree results, work experience, leadership potential, commitment to return home and the relevance of the course. Shortlisted candidates are usually interviewed in person in April in Lusaka, Harare or Blantyre.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a public technological university in Glasgow, Scotland, with a large engineering faculty. The Beit Trust is a UK charity that has supported education and development in Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe for over a century, including postgraduate scholarships at partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Secure an offer for an eligible Strathclyde engineering master's first. Then complete the Beit Trust online application form in one sitting, uploading all documents at once, between 1 December 2026 and 12 February 2027. Referees can also send forms to the Beit Trust scholarships email address.
opportunities.notes: Only one award is available. You can submit only one Beit Trust application and cannot save and return to the form. Strathclyde contact: Robert Graham. Late applications are not processed.

opportunities.title: Beit Trust and University of Edinburgh Masters Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of Zambia, Zimbabwe or Malawi with a strong first degree and an Edinburgh master's offer, who plan to return home.
opportunities.description:
The Beit Trust and the University of Edinburgh jointly fund full postgraduate scholarships for students from Zambia, Zimbabwe and Malawi. The Edinburgh award is for a one-year taught master's starting in September 2027, and it is part of the Beit Trust's wider scholarship scheme with partner universities in the UK and South Africa.

The scholarship pays tuition, a living allowance, visa and health surcharge costs, a laptop allowance and return economy flights. Applications open on 1 December 2026 and close on 12 February 2027, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in person in Lusaka, Harare or Blantyre, usually in April.

The Trust favours applicants who will return home to contribute to development in medicine, engineering, education, economic growth, agriculture or conservation.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition and academic fees; a living allowance; UK visa, Immigration Health Surcharge, TB test and biometric costs; arrival, laptop and departure allowances; economy return flights. No support for spouses or dependants.
requirements: National or permanent resident of Zambia, Zimbabwe or Malawi, living in and intending to return to that country
Holds an offer from the University of Edinburgh for a one-year taught master's (UK applicants need the offer before applying)
Preferably a Distinction or Upper Second (Merit) honours degree
Generally no existing postgraduate degree
About three years of work experience preferred, not compulsory
Not already started the course; MBAs are not funded
documents: Three references (academic, character and employer) on Beit Trust forms
opportunities.selection_process: The Trust shortlists on merit, eligibility and fit with its development priorities, also weighing leadership and commitment to return. Interviews are usually held in April in Lusaka, Harare and Blantyre; not every interviewee is funded.
opportunities.about_provider: The Beit Trust is a UK charity founded in 1906 that funds education, health, conservation and development in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Malawi. The University of Edinburgh is one of its UK partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to the University of Edinburgh for your master's first. Then complete the Beit Trust's single online application, linked from its scholarships page, between 1 December 2026 and 12 February 2027. Contact scholarships@beittrust.org.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: The Trust awarded 19 scholarships across all partner universities in 2026. Some Trust FAQ text still shows an old 2026 deadline; use 12 February 2027.

opportunities.title: Reuters Journalist Fellowship 2027/28
opportunities.provider: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career journalists with at least five years of experience and good English can spend a funded term at Oxford with a monthly stipend, fees and travel covered.

opportunities.title: Bath International Excellence Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New first-year undergraduates assessed as overseas fee payers who hold an offer for a Bath degree starting in September 2027 and make Bath their firm choice can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Bath International Excellence Scholarship is a tuition fee discount for new international undergraduates at the University of Bath in England. For entry in September 2027 the university plans to make up to 300 awards, each worth £8,000 per year for up to three years of full-time study.

The scholarship rewards academic and personal merit rather than financial need. Applicants answer three short questions in the Bath Application Tracker after receiving an offer, and their answers are read alongside their UCAS academic profile.

Any student classed as paying overseas fees can apply, which includes most African applicants. There are two application rounds, closing on 14 February and 31 March 2027, and decisions are sent before the May UCAS reply deadline.
opportunities.benefits: A tuition fee discount of £8,000 per academic year for up to three years of full-time study (up to £24,000 in total). It is not a cash award or living allowance, and no discount applies in placement or study-abroad years.
requirements: New first-year undergraduate applicant
Assessed as an overseas fee-paying student
Offer for any Bath undergraduate degree starting in September 2027 (not the two-year MArch)
Bath must be your firm UCAS choice
documents: Answers to three questions of up to 1,000 characters each, submitted in the Bath Application Tracker
opportunities.selection_process: A competitive review of the three written answers and the applicant's UCAS academic profile, based on academic and personal merit. Each applicant is considered once.
important_dates: Outcomes: before the May 2027 UCAS reply deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Bath is a public research university in south-west England, known for engineering, management, science and sport. It is consistently ranked among the leading UK universities for student experience.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Bath through UCAS and get your fee status confirmed. Once you hold an offer, open the Bath Application Tracker and answer the three scholarship questions before your chosen round closes. Questions go to the undergraduate international scholarships email on the page.
opportunities.notes: The discount stops if your fee status changes to Home. Deferring your place cancels the award. Full 2027/28 terms are to be published when applications open.

opportunities.title: IFSA-EUSFLAT 2027 joint world congress on fuzzy logic
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students worldwide working on fuzzy logic and soft computing.
opportunities.description:
IFSA-EUSFLAT 2027 is the joint 22nd World Congress of the International Fuzzy Systems Association and 15th Conference of the European Society for Fuzzy Logic and Technology. It will be hosted by Bari Polytechnic in Bari, Italy, from 13 to 17 September 2027 and covers fuzzy logic, computational intelligence and soft computing.

Authors can submit full papers of 12 to 15 pages plus references, published by Springer in Lecture Notes in Computer Science, or shorter communications of at least 6 pages in a separate open collection. Both the abstract registration and the full paper are due on 14 February 2027.

For African researchers in fuzzy systems, decision-making, control or AI, this is the main world meeting of the field. EUSFLAT also runs a general student grants programme, worth checking for travel help.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of full papers in Springer LNCS or of communications in an open collection, and presentation at the congress. Fees and specific student support for this congress are not stated; EUSFLAT runs a separate Student Grants Program.
requirements: Full paper of 12 to 15 pages plus references, or a communication of at least 6 pages
Abstract registered by the deadline
Submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed, with notification on 16 April 2027.
important_dates: Abstract registration and full paper: 14 February 2027 (23:59 AoE)
opportunities.about_provider: The International Fuzzy Systems Association (IFSA) is the worldwide body for fuzzy set theory and its applications, and EUSFLAT is the European society for fuzzy logic and technology. They hold this joint congress every few years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract and upload the paper through the IFSA-EUSFLAT 2027 EasyChair site by 14 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: See the EUSFLAT students grant programme page for possible travel support.

opportunities.title: Western University International President's Entrance Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Entrance award for international undergraduates.

opportunities.title: ASCSA Cotsen Traveling Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders and graduate students of any nationality whose research needs the Gennadius Library in Athens.
opportunities.description:
The Cotsen Traveling Fellowship is a short-term research grant from the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA) for work that needs the collections of its Gennadius Library, one of the world's great libraries on Greece from late antiquity to modern times. It is named after Lloyd E. Cotsen.

Fellows spend at least one month in Athens during the academic year (1 September to 1 June) and receive a USD 2,000 stipend, with School fees waived for up to two months. The fellowship is open to senior scholars with a PhD and to graduate students of any nationality.

African historians, classicists and researchers in Byzantine, Ottoman or modern Greek studies whose project depends on Gennadius materials can use it to fund a focused research stay.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of USD 2,000 for travel, housing, board, residence permits and other living costs, and a waiver of School fees for up to two months.
requirements: PhD holder (senior scholar) or graduate student
Any nationality
Project related to the Gennadius Library or its collections
Residence in Athens of at least one month between 1 September and 1 June
documents: Project description of up to 750 words (link to the Gennadius and proposed dates)
Budget of no more than one page
Two letters of recommendation submitted by the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: ASCSA reviews applications; the page does not list scoring criteria. Fellows submit a final report and acknowledge the School in publications, depositing a copy at the Gennadius.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading centre for research on Greece from antiquity to today. It runs excavations, the Blegen and Gennadius libraries and many fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the ASCSA Submittable portal (Cotsen Traveling Fellowship form) by 15 February 2027 and ask both referees to submit their letters before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: ASCSA lists other Gennadius fellowships open to all nationalities with 15 January 2027 deadlines (Macricostas, Yatrakis, Schwarz).

opportunities.title: Allegheny College Trustee Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Incoming undergraduates, including international applicants, are considered for a renewable partial academic merit award.

opportunities.title: Call for Papers: Decolonizing the Ethics of AI in Journalism, Perspectives from Asia and Africa (African Journalism Studies)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide working on AI ethics in journalism with an Asian or African focus.
opportunities.description:
African Journalism Studies, a Taylor & Francis (Routledge) journal, is preparing a special issue on "Decolonizing the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Journalism: Perspectives from Asia and Africa". It is edited by Dr Sadia Jamil (University of Nottingham Ningbo China) and Dr Mbongeni Msimanga (Namibia University of Science and Technology).

The issue looks at epistemic erasure, algorithmic inequality, transparency and AI governance in newsrooms, misinformation and related questions from Asian and African points of view. The abstract stage closed in August 2026, and full manuscripts of up to 8,000 words are due in February 2027.

The topic speaks directly to African media scholars and journalism researchers; check with the editors if you did not submit an abstract.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in a peer-reviewed special issue of African Journalism Studies. The call does not state an article charge; Taylor & Francis offers open-access discounts and waivers for authors in developing regions.
requirements: Original research on the ethics of AI in journalism from Asian or African perspectives
Full paper of up to 8,000 words including references
Structure: introduction, literature review, theoretical framework, methodology, findings, discussion, conclusion
documents: Full manuscript submitted in ScholarOne under the special issue title
opportunities.selection_process: Manuscripts go through the journal's peer review, handled by the guest editors.
important_dates: Full manuscripts: 15 February 2027 (the instructions also mention 25 February 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: African Journalism Studies is a peer-reviewed journal on journalism and media in Africa, published by Routledge (Taylor & Francis). Taylor & Francis is one of the largest academic publishers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the full paper through the journal's ScholarOne site and choose the special issue title. Contact the guest editors (emails on the call page) with questions.
opportunities.notes: The call page gives two manuscript dates (15 and 25 February 2027); aim for the earlier one.

opportunities.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (University Program) at Shanghai Jiao Tong University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese master's (up to 35) and doctoral (up to 40) applicants to SJTU for September 2027 who meet degree and language rules.
opportunities.description:
Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) nominates international students for the Chinese Government Scholarship through its own channel (the University Program). Applicants for English-taught and other master's and doctoral programmes starting in September 2027 apply through SJTU's online system and choose the option to apply for scholarships through the university.

Applications opened on 5 November 2026. The first-round deadline for the Chinese Government Scholarship is 15 December 2026 and the final deadline is 15 February 2027. SJTU also offers Shanghai Government and SJTU scholarships until 31 March 2027, and self-funded applicants can apply until 31 May 2027.

African applicants can alternatively apply via a Chinese embassy, but only one channel may be used, so pick one and follow its rules.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen with a foreign ordinary passport
Good health and conduct
Master's: degree equivalent to a Chinese bachelor's; doctoral: degree equivalent to a Chinese master's (final-year students can apply with expected-graduation proof)
Meets SJTU's language requirements
Not receiving other scholarships
Age: up to 35 for master's, up to 40 for doctoral
documents: Degree certificates with verification (CSCSE for degrees outside mainland China)
Passport valid at least 12 months beyond enrolment
Two recommendation letters from associate professors or senior professionals
Supervisor's letter of intent for listed schools
opportunities.selection_process: After the deadline SJTU assesses the documents and decides award levels under the scholarship rules. Results appear in the application system without a separate letter.
important_dates: Shanghai Government and SJTU Scholarship deadline: 31 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Shanghai Jiao Tong University is one of China's top research universities, under the Ministry of Education and the Shanghai government, with strengths in engineering, medicine, science and management.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply at apply.sjtu.edu.cn, complete the form, upload colour scans of all documents and select "Apply for scholarships through the University". Type B applicants must also enter SJTU's agency number 10248 in the CSC system. Contact gs.admission@sjtu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: Apply in the first round (15 December 2026) for the best chance. Amounts and funding periods are shown only in the application system.

opportunities.title: Choose Dalarna First Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying master's applicants who rank a Dalarna University master's first on universityadmissions.se for autumn 2027, apply for the scholarship and are admitted receive a 5,000 SEK reduction.
opportunities.description:
The Choose Dalarna First Scholarship is a small tuition reduction for fee-paying students who make Dalarna University in Sweden their first choice for a master's programme. It takes 5,000 SEK off the first-semester tuition invoice.

The award is not competitive: everyone who ranks a Dalarna master's programme first on universityadmissions.se by the on-time deadline, submits the scholarship application by 15 February and is admitted receives it. The form for the autumn 2027 intake opens in January 2027.

There is no nationality rule, so African students who must pay Swedish tuition fees can benefit. It cannot be combined with a Swedish Institute scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off reduction of 5,000 SEK on the first-semester tuition fee, applied automatically to the invoice.
requirements: Fee-paying master's applicant
Rank a Dalarna master's programme first on universityadmissions.se by the on-time deadline
Submit the scholarship application by 15 February
Be admitted to a Dalarna master's programme
Not combinable with a Swedish Institute scholarship
opportunities.selection_process: No competition: all applicants who meet the conditions receive the reduction.
opportunities.about_provider: Dalarna University is a Swedish public university with campuses in Falun and Borlänge, known for flexible and online learning, energy and environmental studies, and tourism.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme on universityadmissions.se and rank Dalarna first. When the form opens in January 2027, submit the Choose Dalarna First application from the scholarships page by 15 February.
opportunities.notes: Not available for bachelor's programmes or single courses. Dalarna also has an Academic Excellence Scholarship for enrolled students.

opportunities.title: Dalhousie University General Entrance Awards 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New first-year undergraduates, domestic or international, entering Dalhousie in fall 2027, typically with an 80% average.
opportunities.description:
Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, uses one General Entrance Award (GEA) application to consider new undergraduates for more than 2,000 entrance scholarships, bursaries and hybrid awards each year. Awards range from about CAD 1,000 to CAD 80,000 over four years, and some are renewable.

The 2027-28 GEA application opens on 1 October 2026 and closes on 15 February 2027 for students starting in the fall term. Both Canadian and international students may apply, and the university looks at grades, leadership, involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity.

Several awards target particular groups, such as the Sankofa Scholarships (CAD 48,000 for international students of Black/African descent from the Caribbean). For African applicants the GEA is the single most important form to complete when applying to Dalhousie.
opportunities.benefits: Entrance awards worth about CAD 1,000 to CAD 80,000 over four years, as one-time or renewable scholarships, bursaries or hybrid awards, paid in two instalments (mid-August and mid-December).
requirements: Entering undergraduate directly from high school, or a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study
Starting in the fall term
Typically an 80% average or 26 predicted IB points (in the five courses required for the programme)
Domestic and international students are eligible; transfer students generally are not
Full-time registration (at least 9 credit hours per term)
documents: Official Grade 12 first-semester transcript (or predicted or mid-term grades for non-semester systems)
Financial documents for need-based awards (tax assessment, home-country income documents or employer letter, translated into English)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are reviewed after the deadline on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, using first-semester Grade 12 results. Students are notified in spring.
opportunities.about_provider: Dalhousie University is a research university in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, and a member of the U15 group of research-intensive Canadian universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission at apply.dal.ca (CAD 70 application fee), then complete the GEA application in the applicant portal by 15 February 2027. Send transcripts directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca.
opportunities.notes: Some awards need a separate application or reference letters. Many awards for Black African students are limited to Canadian students; read each award's conditions.

opportunities.title: ECREA Conference: Beyond Deficit Narratives: Media Representation, Voice, and the Diversity of Ageing (Porto, 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Media and communication researchers and students worldwide working on ageing.
opportunities.description:
The Aging and Communication working group of the European Communication Research and Education Association (ECREA) invites abstracts for its third international conference, "Beyond Deficit Narratives: Media Representation, Voice, and the Diversity of Ageing". It will be held at Lusófona University's Porto University Centre in Portugal on 8 and 9 July 2027, including a joint session with ECREA's Audience and Reception Studies section.

The conference looks at how media and communication build or challenge the idea of ageing as decline, and welcomes work from media studies, sociology, critical gerontology, cultural and gender studies, science and technology studies and related fields.

African researchers studying ageing, media representation, older people's voices or intergenerational communication can submit; the call has no geographic limit.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present research at an international ECREA conference. Registration fees and travel support for this event are not stated; ECREA has a Support Young Scholars Fund for its main conference.
requirements: Abstract on media, communication and ageing related to the call's themes
Presenters must register by 31 May 2027
documents: Abstract submitted via the conference form
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts are reviewed by the organisers, with acceptance and a waiting list announced on 15 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ECREA is Europe's main association for media and communication researchers, with sections and working groups on many themes. It organises the European Communication Conference and thematic events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your abstract through the online form linked from the ECREA call page by 15 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Abstract length and format are not specified on the call page, so keep it concise and clearly linked to the theme.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Chemical NanoEngineering (CNE) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Science and engineering graduates of eligible nationalities with at least 75% GPA and IELTS 6.2 or TOEFL 91.
opportunities.description:
Chemical NanoEngineering (CNE) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master run by three partner universities in France, Poland and Italy, with Aix-Marseille University as coordinator. It trains chemists, physicists and engineers in nanoscale materials and chemical engineering.

Applications for the next intake are open from 1 November 2026 to 15 February 2027 and are free of charge. Selected students can receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships funded by the EU's European Education and Culture Executive Agency, with a subsistence allowance of EUR 1,400 a month.

African science and engineering graduates with good grades and English can apply; those not selected for a scholarship can choose to join as self-funded students.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship with a subsistence allowance of EUR 1,400 per month. The pages read do not state tuition, travel or insurance coverage or the number of scholarships.
requirements: Bachelor's or equivalent in science or engineering (chemistry, physics, mechanical, chemical or electronic engineering, materials science); biomedical and polymer engineering assessed case by case
GPA of at least 75% of the scale maximum
IELTS 6.2 or TOEFL iBT 91
Proof of residence issued within 12 months before the deadline
Previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders are not eligible for another; full-time enrolment only
documents: Proof of residence (notarised or official English copy)
Other documents on the programme checklist
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee meets in March; results are known in May and a waiting list stays open until the end of August. Appeals are possible, and applicants not selected for a scholarship may opt for self-funded status.
opportunities.about_provider: The CNE Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is delivered by a consortium of three European universities coordinated by Aix-Marseille University in France. It is funded by the EU through EACEA.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online, free of charge, through the CNE application portal (application.master-cne.eu) before 15 February 2027, uploading the documents on the checklist and two recommendation letters on the programme template.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship cannot be postponed to a later intake or combined with other EU grants. Contact: sciences-master-cne@univ-amu.fr.

opportunities.title: International Special Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted for spring 2027 are considered automatically for CAD 1,000 to 3,000 off first-term tuition based on grades.

opportunities.title: KU Leuven Science@Leuven Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Strong applicants with a non-Belgian bachelor's degree applying to a KU Leuven Faculty of Science master's can receive up to EUR 12,000 a year, renewable for a second year.

opportunities.title: NBER Innovation in the Agricultural and Food System Conference 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Economists worldwide, including early-career researchers, with papers on agricultural and food-system innovation.
opportunities.description:
The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), with support from the USDA Economic Research Service, invites papers for a research conference on innovation in agriculture and the food system. The conference takes place in Washington, DC, on 21 May 2027 and is organised by GianCarlo Moschini (Iowa State University) and Paul Rhode (University of Michigan).

Topics include the institutions and incentives behind agricultural innovation, markets, adoption and diffusion of new technologies, emerging technologies, productivity and wider social impacts. Early-career researchers and people outside the NBER network are welcome.

NBER pays hotel and economy travel for up to two authors per accepted paper, which makes it a funded opportunity for African agricultural and development economists with complete or near-complete papers.
opportunities.benefits: NBER covers hotel accommodation and economy-class travel to the conference for up to two authors per paper. Other costs are not stated.
requirements: Original economic research, empirical or theoretical, on innovation in agriculture or the food system
Complete or nearly complete paper ready by May 2027
Disclose any agricultural-industry ties on the first page
Papers already accepted and appearing by May 2027 should not be submitted
NBER papers may not make policy recommendations
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers select papers, and authors are notified in early March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The NBER is a private, non-partisan research organisation in the United States that brings together leading economists to study the economy. Its conferences and working papers are widely followed.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Upload your paper through the NBER conference submission system linked from the call page by 15 February 2027. Questions go to confer@nber.org.
opportunities.notes: Early-career researchers and non-NBER affiliates are explicitly encouraged to apply.

opportunities.title: UNU-MERIT Full-time PhD Programme and Fellowships 2027 (Maastricht)
opportunities.provider: UNU-MERIT (United Nations University) and Maastricht University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a relevant master's degree (or finishing one by spring 2027) with strong English can apply by 15 February 2027, and up to 10 applicants receive a funded PhD fellowship.
opportunities.description:
UNU-MERIT, the Maastricht-based research and training institute of the United Nations University, runs a four-year, full-time residential PhD programme in innovation, governance and development. Students spend the first year on structured courses taught in English, starting in September, and then work on their thesis in Maastricht. The doctorate is awarded by Maastricht University.

The 2027 application round opened on 1 November 2026 and closes on 15 February 2027. Up to ten admitted candidates receive a UNU-MERIT PhD fellowship, which pays a monthly allowance, a research budget and the tuition fees. Candidates do not need a separate fellowship application; they simply tick the fellowship box on the form.

The programme openly encourages applications from the Global South, which makes it a strong option for African economists, political scientists and social scientists who want to research development, innovation and policy questions. Competition is intense: more than 250 people apply each year for about ten places.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 10 UNU-MERIT PhD fellowships: a monthly net allowance of about EUR 1,650 to 1,700 (the page gives both figures), a research budget of EUR 3,500 and full tuition fees. Admitted students without a fellowship pay tuition of EUR 9,000 in the first year and EUR 7,000 in later years (2027-28 rates); tuition does not cover books, travel, accommodation or visa costs.
requirements: Master's degree (MSc or MA) in a relevant field such as economics, political science, social sciences or computational social sciences, or completion by spring 2027
Strong background in one of the institute's disciplines
English: TOEFL iBT 100, IELTS 7.0 or higher, Cambridge CAE 185, or UN language level 4, unless a native speaker or your bachelor's or master's was taught in English
Indicative age limit of 32 for full-time fellows (not a strict rule); earlier career stage preferred
documents: Degree certificates and transcripts with an explanation of the grading system
English test result (can follow after the deadline)
One recommendation letter in English (due by 22 February 2027)

opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form on the UNU-MERIT portal, upload your letter, proposal, CV and certificates, and tick the box to be considered for a fellowship. Ask your referee to send the letter by 22 February 2027.

opportunities.title: VISTEC Admission Scholarship 2027
