VISTEC is research-intensive and teaches in English, making it a strong option for African students interested in science and engineering research in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: University fees; on-campus housing; a stipend of up to 20,000 baht per month; a research budget of up to 500,000 baht; and up to 30,000 baht for equipment. PhD students can receive 1 million baht for up to a year of overseas research.

Maximum of two application forms

opportunities.about_provider: VISTEC is a research university in Rayong, Thailand, founded with support from the PTT group. It focuses on graduate research in energy, materials, molecular science, biomolecular science, information science and engineering.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the VISTEC admissions portal and submit your application with all documents by 15 February 2027. Make sure an official English score reaches VISTEC before the interview.
opportunities.notes: Contact the admissions office by email or on +66 33 014 116.

opportunities.title: ISCB UK 2027 Call for Abstracts: Biology in the Age of AI
opportunities.provider: International Society for Computational Biology (ISCB) UK

The organisers are inviting abstracts for talks and posters, and the first day includes a student symposium for PhD students and postdocs.

Topics include artificial intelligence and machine learning in biology and medicine; bioinformatics infrastructure, training and community; genomics, evolution and multi-omics; structural, molecular and systems biology; translational and precision medicine; and emerging areas of computational biology.

The call is open to anyone, so African bioinformaticians and data scientists can use it to present work to a European audience. Note that presenters must register and pay to attend, and the call does not mention travel grants or fee waivers.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present a talk or poster (in person, or a virtual poster with a short flash-talk video) at an international computational biology meeting. Presenters pay registration; no travel grants or fee waivers are mentioned.

Abstract without title or affiliation in the text (these are entered separately)
Presenters must register for the conference
Student symposium option for PhD students and postdocs

Printed poster up to 46 x 46 inches, or a PDF poster and 5-7 minute video for the virtual hall, if accepted

important_dates: Conference: 20-22 April 2027, University of Strathclyde, Glasgow
opportunities.about_provider: ISCB is the leading international professional society for computational biology and bioinformatics. ISCB UK is its regional community, which runs an annual UK conference.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the ISCB UK 2027 page on EasyChair, choosing talk only, talk and poster, or poster only, and tick the student symposium option if eligible. Questions go to events@iscb.org.
opportunities.notes: If you need a UK visa, apply soon after the 9 March notification. Ask ISCB about any student or regional support, since none is listed in the call.

opportunities.title: Toronto Metropolitan University International Student Leadership Award – Fall 2027

opportunities.description:
The International Student Leadership Award (ISLA) is a one-time C$10,000 entrance award for international students starting a full-time four-year (or five-year co-op) undergraduate degree at Toronto Metropolitan University in fall 2027. Up to 53 students receive it.

Applicants need a final average of at least 86% (an A or equivalent) and must write a personal statement about their leadership. Students can have taken at most one gap year after secondary school.

African students applying to TMU as international first-year students are eligible. Applications go through TMU's AwardSpring portal, which opened on 2 November 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time entrance award of C$10,000 (not renewable). Up to 53 recipients.

Starting a full-time four-year or five-year co-op degree at TMU in fall 2027
Final average of 86% (A) or equivalent
No more than one academic year's gap since secondary school
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on academic results and the leadership shown in the personal statement.
opportunities.about_provider: Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly Ryerson University) is a public university in downtown Toronto, Canada, known for career-focused programmes, innovation and entrepreneurship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a TMU undergraduate programme for fall 2027, then complete the scholarship application on TMU's AwardSpring portal with your personal statement by 16 February 2027 at 11:59 pm Eastern Time. Late applications are not accepted.

The award recognises academic achievement, leadership, original thought and creative ability. Applications are made through TMU's AwardSpring portal between 2 November 2026 and 16 February 2027, and no late applications are accepted.

International students, including those from African secondary schools, are eligible if they meet the 90% average and other conditions. TMU also offers the International Student Leadership Award with the same deadline.

Final admission average of 90% or higher in the best six Grade 12 courses
No gap in studies longer than one year; first-time post-secondary student
Entering a four-year (or five-year co-op) full-time undergraduate programme
Canadian citizens, permanent residents, protected persons or international students with study permits

List of leadership activities in the last two years of secondary school

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus InterMaths (Interdisciplinary Mathematics) Scholarship 2027

InterMaths is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Interdisciplinary Mathematics, coordinated by the University of L'Aquila in Italy with TU Wien, TU Hamburg, the Autonomous University of Barcelona and Université Côte d'Azur. Students study at two or more partners and gain a strong mix of modelling, analysis and computation.

The 2027 call is open with 18 EU-funded scholarships, at least three reserved for targeted regions including Sub-Saharan Africa. A scholarship pays EUR 1,400 a month, waives the EUR 18,000 participation costs and includes insurance. One application form covers InterMaths and the sister programmes RealMaths and MathMods.

Applicants of any nationality with a strong maths background can apply, and there is no application fee.

English at CEFR B2 (certificate not older than 4 years, or medium-of-instruction proof)
Any nationality

Degree completed before 15 August 2027

opportunities.about_provider: The InterMaths network is led by the Department of Information Engineering, Computer Science and Mathematics (DISIM) at the University of L'Aquila and includes more than 20 universities worldwide.

opportunities.title: Mandela Scholarship supported by FirstRand Empowerment Foundation (2027)

Two scholarships are offered for September 2027. Each covers the full master's tuition fee and pays GBP 16,440 for living costs in monthly instalments. Candidates must hold a Sussex offer and be assessed as overseas fee payers.

It is a valuable, fully funded route to UK postgraduate study for South African graduates from African universities, especially those with work experience.

opportunities.title: McMaster University Award of Excellence (international) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International fee-paying students applying to McMaster's Business, Engineering, Humanities, Science or Social Sciences faculties can apply for up to $200,000 over four years.

The McMaster University Award of Excellence is a large entrance award for international undergraduates at McMaster University in Hamilton, Canada. It can be worth up to $200,000 over four years, with the exact value set by the faculty and the student's course load.

It is open to international fee-paying students entering the faculties of Business, Engineering, Humanities, Science or Social Sciences. An offer of admission is not needed to apply. The award renews in years two to four as long as the student stays full time, pays international tuition and remains in the original faculty.

Applications opened on 15 November 2026 and close on 19 February 2027 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, so African secondary-school students applying to McMaster can apply now.

Strong academic record, community contribution and personal growth

opportunities.title: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Burslari) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Turkish citizens applying for degree study in Türkiye who meet the grade and age limits for their level.
opportunities.description:
Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) is the Turkish government's scholarship programme for international students at associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral level. Applications run through the TBBS online system, and the programme also has research, success, short-term and partnership schemes.

The official calendar gives the general application window as 10 January to 20 February each year, followed by document evaluation in March and April, interviews from April to June, results in early August and arrival in Türkiye in September.

Citizens of every country except Türkiye can apply, which makes it one of the most widely used government scholarships among African students. Pay attention to the age limits and minimum grades for each level.
requirements: Citizen of any country other than Türkiye (former Turkish citizens are not eligible)

Graduated or graduating before August of the application year
Not already enrolled at a Turkish university at the level applied for
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are evaluated in March and April, shortlisted candidates are interviewed between April and June, and results are announced in early August.
important_dates: General application window: 10 January to 20 February (annual)
opportunities.about_provider: Türkiye Scholarships is run by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB), the Turkish government agency for international students and diaspora relations.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online through the TBBS portal (tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr) during the January to February window, following the application steps on the Türkiye Scholarships website.
opportunities.notes: The calendar does not print the year; it describes the annual cycle. The Research Scholarship has four application periods a year and the Success Scholarship opens in October and November.

opportunities.title: EDCC 2027 Call for Posters (European Dependable Computing Conference, Trondheim)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anyone attending EDCC 2027, including PhD students presenting thesis work.

EDCC 2027, the 22nd European Dependable Computing Conference, will be held at NTNU in Trondheim, Norway, from 6 to 9 April 2027, with workshops on the first day. EDCC has been running since 1994 and focuses on dependable and secure computing systems.

This call is for the poster session. Posters can accompany another EDCC contribution, show previously published work, present a project, or stand alone, including PhD research and thesis projects. Reviews are light, posters are printed on site, and attendees vote for three Distinguished Poster awards.

It is an accessible way for African PhD students in reliability, security and fault tolerance to present early work at a European conference.
opportunities.benefits: Poster presentation at the conference, on-site printing and the chance to win one of three Distinguished Poster awards. Travel support is not stated on the poster call.

A0 portrait poster in English, submitted as PDF

opportunities.title: Caltech Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF) 2027

opportunities.description:
Caltech's Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF) let undergraduates spend ten weeks doing research with a Caltech faculty mentor in Pasadena, California. The programme has run since 1979. Students write a research proposal with their mentor, carry out the project in person, and present their results at the end of the summer.

In 2027 fellows receive USD 8,354 for the ten weeks. Students from other universities can apply, and the programme says international students are eligible, but every applicant must first find a Caltech mentor who agrees to supervise and co-fund the project.

For strong African undergraduates in science and engineering, SURF is a rare chance to do research at a top US institute; contacting potential mentors early is key.
opportunities.benefits: An award of USD 8,354 for the ten-week fellowship in 2027.
requirements: Continuing undergraduate in a degree programme, eligible to register for the fall
Non-Caltech students: cumulative GPA of at least 2.5/4.0

Full-time research in person for 10 weeks, no courses or other jobs
JPL projects are for US citizens and permanent residents only
documents: Two confidential recommendation letters (at least one from faculty)

opportunities.how_to_apply: Find and contact a Caltech faculty mentor and agree a project first, then submit the application, proposal and transcript in SFP Online by 22 February 2027 and ask your referees to send letters by the same date.
opportunities.notes: Caltech warns that visiting students may find it harder to secure a mentor, so start contacting faculty months ahead.

Session proposal via the EUNIS Orgo form

opportunities.title: Karolinska Institutet Global Master's Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tuition-fee-paying applicants who put a Karolinska Institutet master's programme as their first choice and are admitted can apply for this fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The KI Global Master's Scholarship is Karolinska Institutet's own award for international students who must pay tuition fees to study on one of its master's programmes in Stockholm. It removes the tuition fee bill for the programme, which is often the biggest obstacle for students from outside the EU/EEA, including applicants from African countries.

The scheme runs alongside the normal Swedish admissions round for autumn 2027. Students first apply for a KI master's programme through the national admissions portal and then, if they qualify, send a separate scholarship application to KI during a short window in February 2027. Only applicants who are actually admitted are considered.

Competition is strong: KI reports about 1,000 applicants and 12 awards in 2026, and 687 applicants and 10 awards in 2025. Each programme's best-ranked candidate on KI's CV form normally receives the award.

opportunities.title: Cyber-Defence Campus Doctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who are enrolled in, or accepted to, a doctoral programme at a Swiss university can apply with a cyber-defence research project.
opportunities.description:
The CYD Doctoral Fellowships fund PhD research on cyber-defence topics at the Cyber-Defence (CYD) Campus, the research centre of the Swiss federal defence administration. Fellows work under a professor at a Swiss university while being linked to the CYD Campus, which has sites on the EPFL and ETH Zurich premises and in Thun.

The fellowship lasts four years, with a possible one-year extension, and pays the doctoral salary plus money for research costs and conferences. The upcoming 15th call opens on 3 December 2026 and its first-stage deadline is 25 February 2027 (17:00 CET).

There is no nationality or age restriction, which makes it a real option for African computer scientists, engineers and mathematicians who want to do a funded PhD in Switzerland on security, privacy, cryptography or related fields.
opportunities.benefits: Salary contribution, including social security, on the host institution's PhD scale for four years (extension of one year possible); research costs of up to CHF 3,000 per year for specific equipment; and conference costs of up to CHF 5,000 per year.
requirements: Open to all nationalities, no age limit
Enrolled in or accepted into a doctoral programme at a Swiss higher education institution
Endorsement by a supervising Swiss professor at Stage 2
Excellent academic record (strong grade transcripts)
Project must link the CYD Campus with at least one Swiss higher education institution
All documents in English
Preference for candidates who have not yet started or are at the start of their PhD
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 pre-proposals are reviewed by a CYD Campus committee chaired by the CYD Director for fit and quality. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by a prospective CYD mentor, and only mentor-endorsed candidates move to Stage 2. A committee of three to five members chaired by the CYD Director makes the final decision, with academic excellence as the main criterion.
opportunities.about_provider: The CYD Campus belongs to armasuisse Science and Technology, part of the Swiss Federal Department of Defence. It runs the fellowship programme jointly with EPFL, whose Research Office manages the calls.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the call guidelines on the EPFL CYD page, then submit the Stage 1 pre-proposal on the EPFL research funds platform (epflresearchfunds.gomovein.com) by 25 February 2027. If shortlisted, meet your CYD mentor and submit the full proposal with your Swiss supervisor's endorsement.
opportunities.notes: The previous (14th) call closed on 19 August 2026. Sister schemes exist for postdocs, master's theses and proof-of-concept projects.

opportunities.title: Simons Dissertation Fellowship in Mathematics 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year students in a five-year mathematics PhD programme at a US institution, of any nationality.
opportunities.description:
The Simons Dissertation Fellowship in Mathematics is a two-year award from the Simons Foundation for strong doctoral students who are entering the final stretch of their PhD. The 2027 call funds up to 40 fellows, giving each one money for research, travel and departmental costs so that the last two years of the doctorate can focus on producing an excellent thesis.

The fellowship runs from 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2029. It is not a scholarship for study abroad: it supports students who are already enrolled full time in a mathematics PhD programme at a university in the United States, and the student must apply during the third year of a five-year programme. There is no citizenship rule, so African students who are already doing a maths PhD at a US university can apply on the same terms as anyone else.

The foundation reviews applications with its scientific staff and an expert committee, looking at the quality of the student, the importance of the research done so far and how promising the planned work is. Decisions come out in July 2027.
opportunities.benefits: USD 38,400 in total over two years (USD 19,200 per year, including 20% indirect costs). Each year covers USD 15,000 of general research support for the fellow, USD 1,000 of discretionary funds for the department and USD 3,200 of indirect costs. Tuition is not covered.
requirements: Enrolled full time in a PhD programme in a PhD-granting mathematics department at a US institution
Must be in the third year of a five-year PhD programme when applying (six-year programmes are not supported)
No citizenship or nationality requirement
The fellowship cannot be transferred to another institution
documents: Research statement (up to 2 pages, plus 1 page for references and figures)
Biosketch in SciENcv, NIH or NSF format
Statement on the use of generative AI
Confidential reference letter from the thesis advisor, uploaded in Simons Award Manager before the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by Simons Foundation scientific staff and an expert review committee. Awards are based on the quality of the applicant, the significance of their previous research and the promise of the planned research programme. Up to 40 awards are expected.
important_dates: Applications open: autumn 2026 (the foundation's pages give 12 October and 1 November 2026)
Deadline: 25 February 2027, 12 noon US Eastern time
opportunities.about_provider: The Simons Foundation is a private New York-based foundation that funds research in mathematics and the basic sciences. Its Mathematics and Physical Sciences division runs fellowships, collaborations and travel grants for mathematicians at every career stage.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Simons Award Manager portal (sam.simonsfoundation.org). The application needs your university's signing official and financial officer, and it goes through institutional sign-off before submission, so start early. Ask your thesis advisor to upload the reference letter in the portal before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Only students at US universities can apply; the page does not mention Canada. Apply in your third year, as later applications are not accepted. The foundation's office is closed on some days, including 15 February 2027, so do not leave questions to the last minute.

opportunities.title: DMM Conference Travel Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers (mainly PhD students and postdocs) of any nationality who need help to attend a scientific meeting.
opportunities.description:
The DMM Conference Travel Grants help early-career biologists attend scientific meetings, conferences, workshops and training courses, including online events. They are funded by The Company of Biologists through its journal Disease Models & Mechanisms (DMM), which publishes research on human disease.

The grants run in four rounds a year. The next one closes on 26 February 2027 for travel after 12 April 2027, followed by rounds on 28 May, 27 August and 26 November 2027. The money can go towards registration, travel, meals, accommodation and visa fees. Travel must happen within six months of the award, and events run by The Company of Biologists itself are excluded.

There is no nationality limit, which makes the scheme a practical option for African PhD students and postdocs who need help to present their work at a meeting in their own country or abroad.
opportunities.benefits: Up to GBP 300 for a meeting in your home country or up to GBP 500 for a meeting overseas. Funds can cover registration, travel, subsistence, accommodation and visa fees, but not travel insurance. Awards depend on demand and may cover only part of the costs.
requirements: Usually PhD students and postdoctoral researchers early in their careers; independent group leaders or PIs without their own funding are also welcome
Application written in English
Travel must take place within six months of the award; no retrospective funding
No other Company of Biologists funding in the previous 12 months
Unsuccessful applicants must wait 12 months before reapplying
No payments to recipients in sanctioned jurisdictions
documents: Letter from your supervisor confirming your status (or from the Head of Department for PIs), on headed paper, signed, in English
Short justification for attending the meeting
opportunities.selection_process: Applications in each round are assessed by The Company of Biologists and decisions are announced on a set date after the round closes (12 April 2027 for the February round). After the meeting, recipients send receipts, a 250-word report and at least two photos.
important_dates: Next rounds: 28 May 2027 (travel after 12 July 2027), 27 August 2027 (travel after 11 October 2027), 26 November 2027 (travel after 7 January 2028)
opportunities.about_provider: The Company of Biologists is a not-for-profit publisher that runs biology journals such as Development, Journal of Cell Science and Disease Models & Mechanisms. It returns its income to the research community through grants, meetings and workshops.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through The Company of Biologists' SmartSimple grants portal (cob.smartsimpleuk.com) before the round deadline. Upload the supervisor letter, justification, abstract and CV. Funds are paid 3 to 6 weeks after you return a signed grant agreement and bank details.
opportunities.notes: Pick the round whose travel window fits your meeting date. Keep every receipt, because unspent money must be returned within one month. The same publisher also runs BiO Global South Conference Travel Grants.

opportunities.title: Google Research Intern, PhD, Summer 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students in computer science or related technical fields who can be located in the US for a 12-14 week paid summer internship.
opportunities.description:
Google's Research Intern, PhD, Summer 2027 role is a paid, full-time internship of 12 to 14 weeks for doctoral students who want to work on research projects with Google teams. Interns work on real research problems in areas such as computer science, statistics, applied mathematics, economics and the natural sciences.

The internship takes place in the United States, and interns must be located in the US for the whole programme; the listed work locations are all US cities. It is aimed at students in the penultimate year of their PhD or those who will return to their studies afterwards. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the window may close earlier than planned if projects fill up.

For African PhD students, this is most relevant to those already studying at a US university or able to work legally in the US for the summer; it is a job, not a scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: Paid full-time internship of 12 to 14 weeks. The posting lists pay of USD 118,000 to 157,000 (US range, no bonus target), without saying whether this is an annualised figure.
requirements: Currently enrolled in a PhD in computer science, linguistics, statistics, biostatistics, applied mathematics, operations research, economics, natural sciences or a related technical field
Experience in at least one area of computer science
English proficiency
Must be located in the United States for the whole internship

Preferred: enrolled in a US degree programme, available full time for 12 weeks outside term, in the penultimate year (or returning to study afterwards), with research experience, publications and programming skills
documents: Updated CV or résumé showing expected graduation date (MM/YY)
Current official or unofficial transcript in English (PDF preferred)
opportunities.selection_process: Google reviews applications on a rolling basis and matches candidates to available research projects. The posting notes that a response can take more than 90 days.
important_dates: Application window: open until 26 February 2027, or earlier if all projects are filled
opportunities.about_provider: Google is a global technology company whose research teams publish widely in AI, machine learning, systems, algorithms and many other fields. Its research internships place PhD students on teams working on open research questions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply with the Apply button on the Google Careers job page, uploading your CV and transcript. Apply early because projects are filled on a rolling basis.
opportunities.notes: This is a US-based job: you must be able to be in the US for the full internship. Mention your anticipated graduation date clearly on your CV.

opportunities.title: IASH Edinburgh Visiting Research Fellowships 2027-28 (unfunded)
opportunities.provider: Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities (IASH), University of Edinburgh
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career and senior researchers with a doctorate or equivalent professional qualification in the arts, humanities or social sciences can apply for an unfunded 2-6 month research visit in Edinburgh.
opportunities.description:
IASH's Visiting Research Fellowships give mid-career and senior scholars in the arts, humanities and social sciences a base in Edinburgh for two to six months between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028. Fellows live in Edinburgh during their visit and work on their own research with an office, library access and the weekly fellows' lunch.

These fellowships carry no money: fellows bring their own funding, for example a sabbatical salary or an external grant, and IASH supports applications to other funders. What the fellowship offers is a place in a lively interdisciplinary institute and access to the resources of the University of Edinburgh.

The call has no nationality restriction. For 2027-28 the institute particularly welcomes Nordic and Baltic scholars and projects on disability and chronic illness, but other applicants, including researchers from African universities, may apply. The closing date is 17:00 GMT on 26 February 2027, with decisions by the end of April 2027.
opportunities.benefits: No stipend or bursary. Fellows receive an office at IASH, access to the University of Edinburgh libraries, the weekly fellows' lunch and help with applications to other funders.
requirements: A doctorate or equivalent professional qualification
Mid-career or senior researcher in the arts, humanities or social sciences
Own funding for a visit of 2 to 6 months between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028
Residence in Edinburgh during the fellowship
Contact with Edinburgh researchers is an advantage; preference may go to those without a previous IASH fellowship
documents: Two or three references, at least one from outside your institution, emailed to IASH by the deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on merit and applicants are told the outcome by the end of April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: IASH is the University of Edinburgh's institute for advanced study in the arts, humanities and social sciences, one of the oldest such institutes in the UK. It hosts visiting researchers from around the world, who join an interdisciplinary community of fellows in Edinburgh.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete IASH's online application form with your CV and proposal before 26 February 2027 and ask your referees to email their references to IASH by the same date.
opportunities.notes: Because the fellowship is unfunded, line up sabbatical pay or an external grant first; IASH can advise on funders.

opportunities.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Development professionals from eligible developing countries (most of Africa) with 3+ years of relevant paid work and admission to a participating Master's.
opportunities.description:
The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) pays for mid-career development professionals from developing countries to complete a Master's degree in a development-related subject abroad. It is funded by Japan and run by the World Bank, and most African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia, are on its 2027 eligible list.

Subject to funding, scholars can study in one of 44 participating Master's programmes at 24 universities in the United States, Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan, outside their own country. The award lasts for the length of the programme or two years, whichever is shorter, and scholars commit to returning home to apply what they learn.

The 2027 application has two windows tied to the participating programmes: Window 1 runs from 18 January to 26 February 2027 and Window 2 from 29 March to 21 May 2027. Applicants must first secure unconditional admission to a participating programme, and the application link is only sent to candidates shortlisted by their university.
opportunities.benefits: Economy round-trip airfare at the start and end of studies plus a US$600 travel allowance per trip, full tuition, basic medical insurance through the university, and a monthly living allowance that depends on the host country. Visa costs, family expenses, extra courses or travel, research costs and equipment are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of a country on the JJ/WBGSP 2027 eligible list and not a dual citizen of a developed country
Bachelor's degree earned at least 3 years before the deadline
Currently in a paid, full-time, development-related job
At least 3 years of paid development-related work since the bachelor's, within the last 6 years
Unconditional admission (except funding) to a participating Master's programme outside your country of citizenship and residence
Not currently enrolled in a participating programme and not World Bank Group staff or a close relative
Good health
documents: Two professional recommendation letters from paid employment, submitted online
CV in the programme's Annex 4 format
Finalists: ID page and a recent health certificate
opportunities.selection_process: Two assessors score each eligible application from 1 to 10, weighting professional experience (30%), recommendations (30%), commitment to the home country (30%) and education (10%). The Secretariat also considers geographic and gender balance, hardship and limited means, and the Steering Committee approves the finalists.
important_dates: Winners notified after Steering Committee approval
opportunities.about_provider: The World Bank is an international financial institution that lends to and advises developing countries. Its scholarships programme, funded by the Government of Japan, has supported development professionals through graduate study since 1987.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply first to one or more participating Master's programmes and obtain unconditional admission. Shortlisted candidates then receive the JJ/WBGSP online application link from their university and submit one application with two recommendations before the window closes. Questions go to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org (English or French).
opportunities.notes: Recommenders must be from paid employment, not professors or volunteer work (fragile-state citizens have some flexibility). Do not apply from a mobile phone. Check which window your programme belongs to.

opportunities.title: TASE 2027: 21st International Symposium on Theoretical Aspects of Software Engineering
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students of any nationality with original work on theoretical aspects of software engineering may submit.
opportunities.description:
TASE 2027, the 21st International Symposium on Theoretical Aspects of Software Engineering, invites research papers on the formal and theoretical foundations of software engineering. The symposium will take place in Hong Kong SAR from 28 to 30 July 2027.

Authors can submit long papers of up to 16 pages or short papers of up to 6 pages (bibliography excluded) in Springer LNCS format. Accepted papers appear in the Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science proceedings. Abstracts must be registered by 19 February 2027 and full papers submitted by 26 February 2027.

The call is open to researchers from any country, so African computer scientists and PhD students working on formal methods, verification, programming theory or software semantics can submit. The call does not mention travel grants or fee waivers.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered. Accepted papers are published in Springer LNCS proceedings and presented at the symposium in Hong Kong.
requirements: Original work not published or under review elsewhere
Long paper up to 16 pages or short paper up to 6 pages, excluding bibliography
Springer LNCS format
Open to authors of any nationality
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed by the programme committee for the Springer LNCS proceedings.
opportunities.about_provider: TASE is an annual international symposium on the theoretical side of software engineering, with proceedings published by Springer in the LNCS series. The 2027 edition is hosted in Hong Kong SAR.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register an abstract and then upload the full paper through the TASE 2027 EasyChair page (https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=tase2027). The abstract must be in by 19 February 2027, a week before the paper deadline.
opportunities.notes: The call text still mentions a 'TASE 2026 submission page' in one place; use the tase2027 EasyChair link.

opportunities.title: Carroll College International Academic Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time first-year students entering Carroll College in autumn 2027, including international students, are considered for merit awards based on school grades and test scores.
opportunities.description:
Carroll College, a private Catholic college in Helena, Montana, gives merit scholarships to new first-year students for the 2027-2028 year. The awards are based on secondary school grades and official test scores and are made regardless of financial need, so international students who are admitted can benefit.

There are five levels, from USD 2,000 to USD 9,000 a year, and they renew automatically for three more years with satisfactory progress. Students who apply by the 28 February regular decision date get priority consideration for scholarships.

The awards only cover part of the cost of study, so African applicants should plan for the remaining tuition and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: Annual merit awards for 2027-2028 first-year students: Bishop Carroll USD 9,000; Presidential USD 7,000; Trustee USD 5,000; All Saint USD 3,000; Founder USD 2,000. Renewable for three further years with satisfactory progress. Transfer awards range from USD 2,000 to USD 9,000 depending on GPA.
requirements: Graduated from an accredited secondary school
Less than one full year of university study completed
Full-time enrolment (at least 12 credits per semester)
Award level based on official test scores and secondary school grades
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic merit from the admission file (grades and test scores); financial need is not considered.
important_dates: Regular decision and scholarship priority: 28 February
opportunities.about_provider: Carroll College is a small private Catholic liberal arts college in Helena, Montana, USA, known for its health sciences, engineering and pre-professional programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Carroll College for autumn 2027 by 28 February for scholarship priority and send official transcripts and test scores. Merit awards are assigned from the admission file.
opportunities.notes: The page gives dates without a year under a 2027-2028 heading. International enquiries: intl@carroll.edu.

opportunities.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) at Northwest A&F University, 2027 intake
opportunities.provider: Northwest A&F University (NWAFU) / China Scholarship Council
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese citizens under 35 (master's) or under 40 (PhD) with a bachelor's or master's degree and a supervisor's acceptance letter from NWAFU.
opportunities.description:
Northwest A&F University in Yangling, Shaanxi province, recruits international master's and doctoral students each year through the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) university programme, known as Type B. Under this route the university itself nominates candidates, so applicants apply both in the CSC online system and on NWAFU's own portal.

Two strands are offered. The High-Level Programme covers most doctoral disciplines (four years) and selected master's disciplines (three years), with applications from early November to the end of February. The Silk Road Programme covers a shorter list of PhD and master's programmes such as plant pathology, soil science and crop genetics and breeding, accepts applications until the end of April, and is limited to listed countries, among them Egypt and Ethiopia.

NWAFU is one of China's leading universities for agriculture, forestry and water science, which makes this scholarship especially relevant for African students working on food security, land and water management.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition waiver, free on-campus accommodation, comprehensive medical insurance and a monthly living stipend (amount not stated on the page). International travel and off-campus internships are not covered.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen in good physical and mental health
Under 35 for master's, under 40 for PhD
Bachelor's degree for master's applicants; master's degree for PhD applicants
English-taught programmes: IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL 79 or institutional proof (the detailed section says IELTS is encouraged rather than compulsory)
Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 4 or above
Passport valid for at least 9 months
Not holding any other scholarship
Silk Road Programme: only listed nationalities (including Egypt and Ethiopia)
documents: CSC application form (Type B, agency code 10712)
Acceptance letter from an NWAFU supervisor (mandatory)
Notarised highest degree certificate (or provisional certificate)
Notarised translations for documents not in English or Chinese
opportunities.selection_process: NWAFU reviews the qualifications of each applicant after the online applications are submitted; qualified candidates then pay the application fee and are considered for nomination to the CSC, which makes the final award.
important_dates: High-Level Programme: early November 2026 to 28 February 2027
Silk Road Programme: early November 2026 to 30 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Northwest A&F University is a national key university in Yangling, Shaanxi, that was part of China's Project 985 and Project 211 and specialises in agriculture, forestry and water resources. The scholarship is funded by the Chinese government through the China Scholarship Council.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First secure an acceptance letter from an NWAFU supervisor (staff lists are on the university's colleges page). Then apply in the CSC system (https://studyinchina.csc.edu.cn) with agency code 10712 and on the NWAFU portal (https://nwsuaf.17gz.org/). After passing the qualification review, pay the non-refundable fee of CNY 400 or USD 75; questions go to admission@nwafu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: The page states that the deadline is 28 February "every year" and was published on 20 October 2026, so it applies to the 2027 intake. A supervisor acceptance letter is required before you apply.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EGEI Master in Economics of Globalisation and European Integration 2027
opportunities.provider: EGEI Consortium (University of Bari Aldo Moro, coordinator)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with 180 ECTS in economics or a related field and TOEFL 90 / IELTS 6.5 can apply for 10 full scholarships.
opportunities.description:
EGEI is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Economics of Globalisation and European Integration, offered by a consortium of seven universities and a think tank, with partners including the University of Bari (coordinator), Ghent University, the University of Lille, the University of Tartu, the University of Cantabria (Santander), Xiamen University, the Pontifical Catholic University of Valparaíso and the CEPS think tank in Brussels.

The two-year, 120 ECTS programme (90 ECTS taught) studies international trade, globalisation and European economic integration, moving students between partner institutions. The 2027-28 cohort starts in early September 2027 in Lille, France.

The application platform opened on 15 November 2026. Ten full Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available, and only applications submitted by 28 February 2027 are considered for them. Students from Africa and every other region can apply; later deadlines apply only to self-funded applicants.
opportunities.benefits: Ten full scholarships for 2027-28 covering subsistence, installation and travel at EUR 1,400 per month (maximum EUR 33,600 per student) plus a full fee waiver.
requirements: At least 180 ECTS (bachelor's) in economics, applied economics or a related field; final-year students can apply with a letter
English: TOEFL 90, IELTS 6.5, or enough credits from an English-taught programme
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: Diploma scan, transcripts and legalised degree copy
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on academic excellence (0-60), experience and other qualifications including languages (0-20) and the motivation letter (0-20). Shortlisted candidates have an online interview, likely in the last week of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The EGEI consortium is coordinated by the University of Bari Aldo Moro in Italy and brings together European, Chinese and Chilean universities with the Brussels think tank CEPS under the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the two-step online application linked from the EGEI 'How to apply' page: first an eligibility survey, then the full application with documents, before 28 February 2027 if you want a scholarship. Questions go to egei@uniba.it.
opportunities.notes: The page gives several result dates (second half of March, early April, early May 2027); expect final news by early May. Only applications in by 28 February are considered for scholarships.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EMerald Master in Georesources Engineering Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality in georesources-related fields with B2-C1 English can apply for full Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
EMerald is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Georesources Engineering, funded by the European Union and coordinated by the Université de Liège in Belgium. It also carries the EIT Label and trains engineers in mineral resources, processing and the raw materials value chain across several European partner universities over two years.

The Round 1 call for Erasmus Mundus full scholarships is open now: applications run from 3 November 2026 to 28 February 2027. The full scholarship is available to applicants worldwide, so African mining, geology, chemical and metallurgical graduates can compete on equal terms.

The top 40 applicants are interviewed, and the consortium takes its final decision and contacts all candidates on 16 April 2027. A second round for self-funded students follows, with interviews in May for non-EU students.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus full scholarship worth EUR 33,600, paid as 24 monthly allowances of EUR 1,400 to cover travel, visa, installation and living costs, with participation (tuition) costs paid directly to the coordinating university. Self-funded non-European students pay EUR 8,000 per year; living costs are estimated at about EUR 14,000 a year.

Higher education degree in a relevant field with transcripts
Must not have held an Erasmus Mundus joint master scholarship before
Open to applicants worldwide

Motivation letter in English (the consortium asks applicants not to use AI tools)
High school diploma with sworn English translation
Higher education diploma and transcript with sworn English translation
Proof of accomplishments if not studying in the last five years
opportunities.selection_process: Complete files are ranked and the best 40 applicants are invited to an interview, which covers their motivation and background and a discussion of a scientific paper sent a few days beforehand. The consortium announces its final decision on 16 April 2027.
important_dates: Round 2 (self-funded) interviews: May for non-EU applicants
opportunities.about_provider: The Université de Liège is a major public university in Belgium and coordinates the EMerald consortium of European universities working on georesources engineering under the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the EMerald admissions portal (emerald.uliege.be/apply) using a computer, upload all sworn copies and the video, and submit before 28 February 2027. Incomplete forms are not considered; originals are checked on arrival in Belgium.
opportunities.notes: The EIT RawMaterials partial grant is not available in the 2027 call. Contact: emerald@uliege.be.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EPS - European Politics and Society: Václav Havel Joint Master Degree
opportunities.provider: Charles University, Faculty of Social Sciences (EPS consortium)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's graduates of any nationality with C1 English can apply; most Africans qualify for the partner-country full scholarship tier.
opportunities.description:
EPS, the Václav Havel Joint Master in European Politics and Society, is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master that combines European politics, contemporary history and culture, economics, international relations and policymaking. It is coordinated by Charles University's Faculty of Social Sciences in Prague with partners Leiden University, Universitat Pompeu Fabra in Barcelona and Jagiellonian University in Krakow.

The admission window for the 2027-2029 cohort is open. Every application received by midnight CET on 28 February 2027 is automatically considered for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship; a self-funding window follows from 1 March to 30 April 2027. There is no application fee.

Most African applicants fall into the 'Partner Country' scholarship tier, which covers full tuition plus a monthly allowance, provided they have not lived or worked in an Erasmus+ programme country for more than 12 months in the last five years. Decisions and scholarship results are announced on 30 April 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship with a living allowance of EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months (EUR 33,600). Partner-country scholars also have full tuition of EUR 18,000 (EUR 4,500 per semester) covered; programme-country scholars have EUR 11,000 tuition deducted. Insurance, extra-curricular activities and guest lectures are included.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant subject (or final-year study)
English at C1, e.g. IELTS 7.0, TOEFL 95 or CAE, or a university language confirmation
Partner-country tier: not a national of, nor resident in, an Erasmus+ programme country for more than 12 months in the last five years
No previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship
documents: Translated bachelor's or master's diploma (or proof of ongoing study)
A second diploma (second bachelor's or high school)
Proof of residence issued within 12 months before the deadline
Translated transcripts from both previous studies
Supplementary questionnaire on study track preferences
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed against the consortium's published admission criteria; results and scholarship awards are announced on 30 April 2027, and applicants have two weeks to appeal to the EPS Programme Board.
opportunities.about_provider: Charles University in Prague is the oldest university in Central Europe. Its Faculty of Social Sciences coordinates the EPS consortium with Leiden, Pompeu Fabra and Jagiellonian universities under the EU's Erasmus Mundus programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through Charles University's admissions portal (is.cuni.cz) linked from the EPS admissions page, uploading all documents and the questionnaire before 28 February 2027 to be considered for a scholarship. Contact eps@fsv.cuni.cz for programme questions and admissions@fsv.cuni.cz for technical ones.
opportunities.notes: The consortium plans more than 50 scholarships over 2026-2031. Follow the motivation letter formatting rules exactly.

opportunities.provider: Taylor & Francis / Global South Literary Studies

opportunities.title: IEEE CEC 2027 Call for Papers (Edinburgh, Jul 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit evolutionary computation papers to IEEE CEC 2027 in Edinburgh by 28 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) is the flagship evolutionary computation event of the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society, held every year since 1994. CEC 2027 takes place in Edinburgh, Scotland, on 25-28 July 2027.

The call covers the full range of evolutionary computation, including optimisation, machine learning, theory and real-world applications. Full papers are due on 28 February 2027, with no extension, and short papers on 15 March 2027.

CEC is a strong venue for African researchers in AI, optimisation and computational intelligence to publish with IEEE and meet the international community.
opportunities.benefits: Publication with IEEE and presentation at CEC 2027 in Edinburgh. Awards and travel grants are not described on the call page.
requirements: Full papers of up to 8 pages following the IEEE submission instructions
Original, unpublished work in evolutionary computation or related areas
At least one author registers and presents
documents: Paper prepared to the initial submission instructions
opportunities.selection_process: Peer review by the programme committee; notification on 7 April 2027.
important_dates: Final paper and early registration: 1 May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Computational Intelligence Society is the IEEE body for neural networks, fuzzy systems and evolutionary computation; CEC is its main evolutionary computation congress.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the EDAS system linked from the call for papers before 28 February 2027.

opportunities.title: IEEE IVMSP Workshop 2027 Call for Papers (Paris, Jun 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to researchers and students of any nationality who submit an original paper in image, video or multidimensional signal processing.
opportunities.description:
The IEEE Image, Video, and Multidimensional Signal Processing Workshop (IVMSP) 2027 is a specialist research meeting of the IEEE Signal Processing Society. It brings together researchers who work on processing, analysing and understanding images, video and other multidimensional signals.

The 2027 workshop will be held in Paris, France, from 21 to 24 June 2027. Authors submit full conference papers, and the society's events calendar sets the paper submission deadline at 28 February 2027.

The call is open to researchers from any country, so it is a chance for African engineers, computer scientists and PhD students working on imaging, video coding, computer vision or multidimensional data to present their work at an IEEE venue in Europe. The workshop's own website had not yet been published when the official listing was checked, so applicants should watch the IEEE SPS page for the submission portal.
opportunities.benefits: This is a call for papers, not a funded award: the official page lists no fee waivers or travel funding specific to this workshop. Accepted papers are presented at the workshop in Paris.
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Signal Processing Society is the professional society within IEEE for signal processing researchers and engineers. It sponsors conferences and workshops worldwide and runs member programmes such as travel grants and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare a full research paper on image, video or multidimensional signal processing. The IEEE SPS events page lists the deadline but shows the conference website as still to be announced, so check that page for the submission system before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: The workshop website was marked 'TBD' when checked; the deadline may be confirmed or extended once it goes live.

opportunities.title: Master of Science in Aquaculture (IMAQUA, Ghent University) - VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship for nationals of the 25 eligible countries (17 in Africa) who also live in one of them, aged 35 or younger on 1 January 2027, with no earlier Belgian government study scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Ghent University's two-year Master of Science in Aquaculture (120 ECTS) is one of the programmes VLIR-UOS funds with full ICP Connect scholarships for the September 2027 intake. It is taught in English at the Faculty of Bioscience Engineering on the Coupure campus in Ghent.

The degree covers the farming of fish, crustaceans, molluscs and algae. The first semester consolidates the basics, the second and third become more specialised and research-driven, and the fourth is given to a master's thesis, usually built into an ongoing research project. Students can do an internship or thesis with a partner institution abroad, and scholarship holders are expected to do part of this work with a partner in the Global South (Africa, Latin America or South-East Asia). The programme is run by the Laboratory of Aquaculture and Artemia Reference Center, known for its work on live feed and microbial management.

Citizens and residents of 16 sub-Saharan African countries and Morocco aged 35 or younger on 1 January 2027 can apply. Applications opened in early October 2026 and the deadline for scholarship candidates is 28 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A full scholarship for the whole length of the programme (24 months) and no longer. It is paid mainly as a monthly allowance meant to cover living costs (board and lodging) and tuition; travel to and from Belgium and insurance are also covered. Depending on the institution, tuition, insurance or housing is either paid by you out of the allowance or paid by the university directly and taken off the allowance. There are no partial awards or extensions, and VLIR-UOS pays nothing extra for optional activities such as field trips to the Global South. ICP Connect programmes charge no application fee.
requirements: Nationality of one of the 25 VLIR-UOS ICP Connect countries (in Africa: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe; also Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam)
Living in one of those 25 countries when you apply (it does not have to be your own country)
Not older than 35 on 1 January 2027
Never awarded a Belgian government scholarship for study before, and not enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January 2027
Only one ICP Connect scholarship application per year: applying to two or more ICP programmes gets you excluded
No other scholarship or grant for this or any other programme at the same time
Good command of English (all ICP Connect programmes are taught in English; Dutch is not needed)
Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years with at least upper second class (or equivalent) results
Transcripts showing (bio)statistics, organic and inorganic chemistry and biology; a background in aquaculture, fisheries, microbiology, physics or biochemistry is recommended

English: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0), TOEFL iBT 90 (home edition accepted) or paper 570, or Cambridge B2 First; predictive tests and TOEIC are not accepted, and certificates must be under 5 years old (some exemptions apply)
documents: Online application in UGent's OASIS portal
Other documents listed in UGent's general application guidelines (CV, motivation, references, passport)
opportunities.selection_process: The host institution first checks and ranks every eligible application, then sends its shortlist to VLIR-UOS, which screens it again. Points that weigh in the ranking: motivation and your potential to act as an agent of change at home; professional experience, with preference for people working in (or heading for) higher education, government or civil society; gender balance, with women strongly encouraged to apply; balance between regions; the Leave No One Behind principle, which favours candidates from vulnerable groups when two files are equally strong; and preference for people who have never had a scholarship to study in a high-income country. VLIR-UOS emails the selected and reserve-list candidates; the programme tells the others. Results are due by mid-May 2027 at the latest. At Ghent, an admission board assesses each file, and admission is approved by the Faculty Council and the Rector's office.
important_dates: VLIR-UOS online information session: 26 November 2026, 14:30-16:30 CET (register through the Zoom link on the call page)
opportunities.about_provider: VLIR-UOS is the Flemish university network's programme for development cooperation, funded by the Belgian government. Through its ICP Connect scheme it pays full scholarships for a selected set of English-taught degree programmes at universities and university colleges in Flanders and Brussels, so that students from partner countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America can study in Belgium and take their skills back home. For the September 2027 intake it funds 12 programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply in UGent's OASIS portal (link on the programme page, https://www.ugent.be/bw/en/education/master-programmes/aquaculture.htm) and indicate that you are applying for the VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarship, before 28 February 2027. Contact: applications.itc@ugent.be.
opportunities.notes: Do not apply to more than one ICP Connect programme in the same year. New graduates or people from the private sector without work experience can still be considered if their motivation is strong. Students may work a few hours a week, but not during compulsory classes, and the scholarship should not be topped up by a job. Some countries need their diplomas legalised through a Belgian embassy or consulate; ask the university early. UGent estimates study costs at about EUR 400 a year and living costs at EUR 1,000 or more a month; the scholarship allowance is meant to cover these.

opportunities.title: Master of Science in Nutrition and Food Systems (Ghent University) - VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarship 2027

It is taught in English by the Faculty of Bioscience Engineering in Ghent and is accredited by the UK Association for Nutrition.

opportunities.title: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-stage startups, including student startups, from around the world can enter the Imagine Cup 2027 competition before 28 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Imagine Cup is Microsoft's global startup competition. The 2027 edition is open to early-stage startups building products with Microsoft's cloud and AI tools, and it has several categories, including a dedicated student startup category.

Applications are submitted online through the Award Force platform and close on 28 February 2027. Finalists compete for cash prizes and large amounts of Microsoft startup credits, with a world championship at the end of the cycle.

It is a strong opportunity for African student founders and young tech entrepreneurs, because entry is online and the prizes include both funding and cloud resources.
opportunities.benefits: Champion: USD 250,000 cash plus USD 1,000,000 in startup credits. Second place: USD 50,000 plus USD 350,000 in credits. Third place: USD 25,000 plus USD 350,000 in credits. Top Student Startup: USD 25,000 plus USD 250,000 in credits. Top 20 and category winners also receive recognition.
requirements: Must be an eligible early-stage startup (full rules on the official competition site)
Student founders can compete in the student startup category
Application submitted online by the deadline
documents: Online application through Award Force (materials as set out in the official rules)
opportunities.about_provider: Microsoft runs the Imagine Cup through Microsoft for Startups, its programme that supports new companies with technology, credits and mentoring.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Go to the official Imagine Cup site, follow the Apply link to the 2027 competition and complete the application on Award Force before 28 February 2027. Check the official rules there for entity and age requirements before applying.
opportunities.notes: It is a startup competition, not a scholarship.

opportunities.title: OFI Transforming Climate Action International Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers who completed a PhD within roughly the last four to six years (or will finish before starting) can apply for a two-year climate and ocean postdoc hosted at Dalhousie University or UQAR with an international co-supervisor.
opportunities.description:
The International Postdoctoral Fellowship (IPDF) is offered under Transforming Climate Action (TCA), a large ocean and climate research programme led by the Ocean Frontier Institute at Dalhousie University and funded through the Canada First Research Excellence Fund. Fellows carry out a two-year research project that links a host supervisor in Canada with a collaborator at an institution abroad.

The fellowship is built around international mobility: fellows are expected to travel between their Canadian and international co-supervisors' institutions at least once a year. Hosting is limited to Dalhousie University (Halifax) and the Université du Québec à Rimouski (UQAR); the page states that funding is not available for placements at Université Laval or Memorial University for this call.

Applications are accepted until 28 February 2027, although the page also notes that the call stays open only until the funds are fully allocated, so applying early is safer. The page sets no nationality restriction, which makes it a realistic option for African early-career researchers working on oceans, climate and related interdisciplinary questions.
opportunities.benefits: A target salary of CAD 70,000 per year plus fringe benefits at Dalhousie or UQAR, and travel support of up to CAD 10,000 per year for exchanges between co-supervisors. Terms are normally two years; UQAR is also considering one-year projects in this call.
requirements: A completed PhD, awarded no more than about 4 to 6 years before applying (the limit depends on the host; career leaves are deducted)
PhD candidates may apply if all degree requirements are completed before the fellowship starts
A host supervisor at Dalhousie University or UQAR
An international collaborator who will co-supervise
Strong qualifications in the field and commitment to interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary research
Ability to meet Canadian and international immigration rules
documents: Biographical details and a half-page bio
Research proposal of up to 10 pages (excluding CV, transcripts, work samples and letters)
Two confidential references using the form on the page
Letter from the PhD supervisor (for current PhD candidates)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed on research excellence and leadership (given the most weight), the merit of the project and of the proposed collaboration, the interdisciplinary perspective of the work, and the applicant's commitment to respectful engagement.
important_dates: Applications accepted until: 28 February 2027 (or until funds run out)
Award announcements expected: May 2027 (subject to funding)
Start: within one year of the offer letter
opportunities.about_provider: The Ocean Frontier Institute is a Canadian ocean research institute led by Dalhousie University. Its Transforming Climate Action programme brings together universities and partners to study the ocean's role in climate change and to support climate solutions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the full application package with your Canadian host supervisor and international collaborator, then email it to the TCA Training and Early Career Development Program Manager (Tracey.Woodhouse@dal.ca). Referees send their confidential references directly. There is no online portal.
opportunities.notes: The call is open only while funds last, so do not wait for the February deadline. OFI also runs a Visiting Fellowship (stipend up to CAD 4,000 per month for 14-120 day research visits) and an Industry Postdoctoral Fellowship on the same site.

opportunities.title: UCD Global Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU fee-paying students from Africa holding an offer for an eligible UCD undergraduate or taught master's programme starting September 2027 can apply by 28 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The UCD Global Excellence Scholarships are tuition awards from University College Dublin for outstanding international students starting an undergraduate or taught postgraduate programme in September 2027. A limited number of 100% and 50% tuition fee scholarships are given each year.

Applications for 2027/28 are open now. For applicants from Africa, the Middle East and Pakistan, the deadline is 28 February 2027. Applicants must already hold an offer or conditional offer, so anyone without an offer should submit the programme application by 5 February 2027.

The awards are merit-based and decided by a committee. They do not renew automatically, and they cover tuition only.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship of 100% or 50% of the tuition fee for the first year of study. Living costs, travel and housing are not covered.
requirements: Non-EU status for tuition fee purposes
Offer or conditional offer for an eligible UCD course starting September 2027
Course must be on the 2027/28 Eligible Programmes list
Regional eligibility as set out in the 2027/28 terms and conditions
Strong academic merit
documents: UCD programme application and its supporting documents
Scholarship application answers submitted in SISWeb
opportunities.selection_process: A UCD committee chooses recipients on academic merit from eligible applicants. Results are usually released about seven weeks after each regional deadline through SISWeb.
important_dates: Programme application for applicants without an offer: 5 February 2027
Scholarship deadline for Africa, Middle East and Pakistan: 28 February 2027, 11:59pm Irish time
Results: about seven weeks after the regional deadline
opportunities.about_provider: University College Dublin is Ireland's largest university, based on the Belfield campus in Dublin. UCD Global manages its international recruitment and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Get an offer for an eligible UCD course, then log in to SISWeb with your UCD Connect details. Under Applications, open Scholarship Applications, choose the Global Excellence Scholarship, answer the general questions and submit before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: If you hold several UCD offers, choose only one programme for the scholarship. The scholarship link only appears once your offer status is in place.

opportunities.title: VIU International Student Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New first-year undergraduate students at Vancouver Island University with excellent grades can apply for one of 20 awards of CAD 5,000.
opportunities.description:
Vancouver Island University (VIU) offers 20 International Student Entrance Scholarships of CAD 5,000 each to new first-year students in any undergraduate programme starting in autumn 2027. The awards are based on academic excellence.

Application is not automatic. Students need a VIU student number and then fill in one entrance award form that covers all VIU entrance awards. The form opened on 15 October 2026 and closes at 11:59pm on 28 February 2027.

The money is credited to tuition in the autumn once VIU confirms full-time enrolment. It is a modest award, so African applicants should plan for most of their costs from other sources.

Strong academic record (selection on academic excellence)
Full-time enrolment confirmed in the autumn
VIU student number (apply for admission first)

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to VIU to get a student number, then complete the single entrance award application on VIU's financial aid website before 28 February 2027.
opportunities.notes: Other VIU entrance awards on the same form include the Stan and May Radzik Entrance Scholarship (CAD 2,500) and VIU Entrance Scholarships (CAD 2,000). Some awards are limited to Canadian citizens or permanent residents. Contact: info@viu.ca.

opportunities.description:
VLIR-UOS has opened its ICP Connect call for students starting in Belgium in September 2027. It pays full scholarships for 12 English-taught programmes at Flemish and Brussels universities and university colleges: two professional bachelor's degrees (Hotel Management at VIVES and Applied Computer Science at Thomas More), seven two-year initial master's degrees (Aquaculture, Food Technology, Oceans & Lakes, Road Safety, Nutrition and Food Systems, Sustainable Land Management and TROPIMUNDO tropical biodiversity) and three one-year advanced master's degrees at the University of Antwerp's Institute of Development Policy (Development Evaluation and Management, Globalisation and Development, Governance and Development).

The overall call closes on 28 February 2027, but most programmes close earlier: TROPIMUNDO on 30 November 2026, Applied Computer Science on 15 January 2027, Hotel Management on 31 January 2027, and most of the others on 1 February 2027. Each programme also has its own entry in Scholarship Scout with full details.

Eight older ICP programmes (for example Nematology, Rural Development, Human Settlements, CADES, Epidemiology, Statistics and Data Science, Sustainable Development and Water Resources Engineering) are still taught but will not get VLIR-UOS scholarships for 2027-28.
