opportunities.title: A. Wilhelmsen Foundation Scholarship at BI Norwegian Business School 2027
opportunities.provider: BI Norwegian Business School / A. Wilhelmsen Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who live outside Norway and are admitted to a full-time master's at BI can be considered for a full-tuition scholarship for autumn 2027.
opportunities.description:
BI Norwegian Business School offers the A. Wilhelmsen Foundation Scholarship to international students starting a full-time master's degree in autumn 2027. The foundation has funded international students at BI since 2010 to help them finance an education in Norway.

The scholarship pays full tuition for up to two years, as long as the student keeps progressing well. Only three scholarships are available for the autumn 2027 intake, so competition is strong.

African applicants are eligible as citizens of countries outside Europe, and the committee considers financial need alongside grades, experience and ambitions.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees for up to two years of a full-time master's at BI. No stipend or living costs are included.
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, living outside Norway when applying
Admitted to a full-time master's programme at BI
First master's degree
Renewal requires 30 ECTS each semester and a cumulative GPA of at least B
Not eligible if entitled to Lånekassen loans or tuition reduction
documents: One-page scholarship letter to the A. Wilhelmsen Foundation Board (CV, goals, career ambitions, contribution, family and financial situation, and why you need the scholarship)
opportunities.selection_process: A committee from the foundation and BI selects recipients on previous grades, experience, ambitions and financial need, and may give priority to certain countries, partner schools or programmes to keep a balanced mix. Decisions cannot be appealed.
important_dates: Admission and scholarship application deadline: 1 March (for autumn 2027 start)
opportunities.about_provider: BI Norwegian Business School is Norway's largest business school, with its main campus in Oslo. The A. Wilhelmsen Foundation is a Norwegian foundation that funds the scholarship programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Upload the one-page scholarship letter with your master's application in BI's online application portal before 1 March; you cannot apply to the foundation directly.
opportunities.notes: Three scholarships for autumn 2027; one scholarship per student, tied to the programme and campus. The page gives the date as 1 March without a year, in the call for the academic year starting autumn 2027.

opportunities.title: APS Short-Term Resident Research Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders, advanced PhD candidates and degreed independent scholars of any nationality can apply for one to three months of funded research at the APS Library in Philadelphia.
opportunities.description:
The American Philosophical Society (APS) Library and Museum in Philadelphia awards about 25 to 30 short-term resident research fellowships each year. Fellows spend four to twelve consecutive weeks using the APS collections, which are strong in the history of science, early American history, Native American studies and related fields.

Fellowships for 2027-2028 may start no earlier than 1 June 2027 and must be finished by 31 May 2028. The application deadline is 1 March 2027 and decisions are announced in May 2027.

The programme is open to US citizens and foreign nationals, so African historians and researchers whose work draws on the APS holdings can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 3,000 per month for one to three months, paid after arrival. The stipend is taxable.
requirements: PhD or equivalent, or PhD candidate who has passed preliminary exams, or degreed independent scholar
Open to US citizens and foreign nationals
Research must need the APS Library and Museum collections
Residency of four to twelve consecutive weeks between 1 June 2027 and 31 May 2028
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed competitively; applicants living 75 miles or more from Philadelphia get some preference. About 25 to 30 fellowships are awarded.
opportunities.about_provider: The American Philosophical Society, founded in 1743 by Benjamin Franklin, is the oldest learned society in the United States. Its library holds major archives on science, early America and Indigenous languages.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the cover letter, CV and proposal through the APS online application portal by 1 March 2027 and ask two referees to send confidential letters through the same system.
opportunities.notes: Applicants should check the collections catalogue before applying and explain why the APS holdings are essential.

opportunities.title: APS-Voltaire Foundation 1776 Fellowships in Enlightenment Studies 2027
opportunities.provider: American Philosophical Society and Voltaire Foundation (University of Oxford)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders, advanced PhD candidates and independent scholars of any nationality researching the Enlightenment can apply by 1 March 2027 for research stays in Philadelphia and Oxford.
opportunities.description:
The 1776 Fellowships in Enlightenment Studies are a joint programme of the American Philosophical Society (APS) in Philadelphia and the Voltaire Foundation at the University of Oxford. Each year two fellows spend up to a month at each institution (and may stay longer) to research Enlightenment ideas, how they spread and how they were used.

Fellows work in the APS library and archives and in Oxford's collections, with the Voltaire Foundation as their base there. The programme marks the shared transatlantic history of the Enlightenment that shaped both institutions.

The call is open to scholars of any nationality, so African historians, philosophers and literary scholars working on the Enlightenment, its global reach or its critics can apply. It is especially useful for early-career researchers who need access to archives in the US and UK.
opportunities.benefits: $5,000 from the APS and £4,000 from the Voltaire Foundation, to cover travel, living and accommodation costs for up to two months of research (about one month at each institution). Two fellowships.
requirements: PhD or equivalent, or a PhD candidate who has passed preliminary exams
Independent scholars with a doctorate but no current academic post are also eligible
Research on Enlightenment ideas, their circulation or application, using APS and Oxford collections
Open to any nationality
documents: Two-page research proposal naming the collections you will use
opportunities.selection_process: A joint committee of the APS and the Voltaire Foundation reviews proposals, looking for strong projects on Enlightenment ideas that make good use of both institutions' collections.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 March 2027, 11:59 pm US Eastern Time
opportunities.about_provider: The American Philosophical Society, founded by Benjamin Franklin in 1743, is the oldest learned society in the United States and runs a major research library in Philadelphia. The Voltaire Foundation is a research department of the University of Oxford that publishes the complete works of Voltaire and research on the Enlightenment.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the APS online application portal (aps.onlineapplicationportal.com) by 1 March 2027, uploading the cover letter, CV and two-page proposal, and arrange for two referees to submit confidential letters.
opportunities.notes: Fellows may extend their stay beyond a month at their own cost. The APS also runs other short-term fellowships listed on its grants pages.

opportunities.title: African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UT Austin undergraduates with financial need, a GPA of 3.0 or more and some or all of their schooling in Africa can apply between 1 February and 1 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
The African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship at the University of Texas at Austin supports undergraduates who did all or part of their secondary education in Africa and who need financial help. It was set up in 2023 with the African Leadership Bridge, a nonprofit that helps African students study in the United States.

The award is USD 5,000 for the 2027-2028 academic year together with a waiver of the non-resident part of tuition, which greatly reduces the cost of study for international students. Incoming first-year students are given preference.

Applications for autumn 2027 are accepted from 1 February to 1 March 2027 through UT's LASSO scholarship system.
opportunities.benefits: USD 5,000 for the academic year (USD 2,500 each in autumn and spring) plus a waiver of the non-resident portion of tuition. It is a one-time award, not guaranteed in later years.
requirements: Currently enrolled (or incoming) undergraduate at UT Austin
Minimum GPA of 3.0
Demonstrated financial need
All or part of preparatory education completed in Africa
Preference for incoming first-year students
documents: Essays on your background and the aims of the award
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed against the eligibility criteria and essays; incoming first-year students receive preference.
opportunities.about_provider: Texas Global is UT Austin's international office, and its International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) team manages scholarships for international students. UT Austin is one of the largest public research universities in the United States.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Between 1 February and 1 March 2027, log in to LASSO, search for ISSS scholarships, choose the African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship and complete the questions and essays.
opportunities.notes: Questions: intlfinaid@austin.utexas.edu (replies in two to three business days).

opportunities.title: BI Future African Leader Scholarship (Master's, Autumn 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of African countries applying for their first full-time master's at BI in Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim, with a GPA of at least 4.0 (ECTS) and strong GMAT/GRE scores, can win full tuition plus NOK 50,000 per semester; apply by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
BI Norwegian Business School offers the Future African Leader Scholarship to citizens of African countries starting a full-time master's programme at its Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim campus. It covers full tuition for up to two years and adds a living-cost stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester, as long as the student keeps up the required academic progress.

BI is a member of the Global Business School Network (GBSN), and this award is one of two scholarships it uses to support initiatives in Africa. Preference goes to candidates who study or studied at a GBSN member school in Africa, or who attended a GMAC Study in Europe event or a SEED Business School Festival event in person in Africa.

The scholarship is merit-based. Applicants are also considered automatically for BI's Presidential, Master International and Women in Finance and Tech scholarships, which improves the chances of some funding.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition for up to two years of a full-time master's, plus a living-cost stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester, subject to academic progression.
requirements: Citizen of an African country, not resident in Norway and not a domestic applicant by education background
Applying for a first master's degree, full-time, at campus Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim
Minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale (BI converts international grades)
Strong GMAT or GRE scores (required for admission)
Not available for the BI-Luiss Joint Master in Marketing
Must submit a complete admission application and accept the offer of admission
documents: Scholarship application letter of up to one page
Complete master's admission documentation (uploaded in the online application)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are based on academic merit, not financial need. BI considers grades, GMAT/GRE scores, other academic achievements and extracurricular and personal achievements, and may apply institutional priorities such as programme, diversity, gender and partner schools. Decisions are made by the end of April, and the offer must be accepted by the date given.
important_dates: Scholarship decisions: by end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: BI Norwegian Business School is Norway's largest business school and one of Europe's largest, with campuses in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim and Stavanger. It holds EQUIS, AACSB and AMBA accreditation.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a full-time master's through BI's online admission portal (apply.bi.no) and upload your CV and a one-page scholarship letter in the 'Scholarship' section along with your admission documents. Applications by email are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Preference is given to GBSN-school students and attendees of GMAC Study in Europe or SEED Business School Festival events in Africa. The page gives the deadline as 'March 1' without a year; it was updated in October 2026 for the coming intake.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Merit scholarship for international MSc students.

opportunities.title: Carleton University Prestige Scholarships 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students entering Carleton University straight from secondary school with an admission average of 90% or more and strong leadership can apply for prestige scholarships of CAD 20,000 to 32,000.
opportunities.description:
Carleton University in Ottawa offers a set of Prestige Scholarships for outstanding students entering a first undergraduate degree in 2027-2028. They are worth between CAD 20,000 and CAD 32,000 over four years, and one award covers full tuition.

Candidates must come directly from secondary school, have an admission average of at least 90% and show leadership in school or community activities. The page sets no citizenship limit. Applicants send one form and a signed reference letter by email by 1 March 2027.

The awards renew each year if the student keeps a GPA of 10.0 on Carleton's 12-point scale.
opportunities.benefits: Ten Chancellor's Scholarships (CAD 32,000 over four years); seven Richard Lewar Entrance Scholarships (CAD 21,500); three Carleton Scholarships of Excellence (CAD 20,000); two SHAD awards (CAD 20,000); Jay Woo and CAA awards (CAD 20,000); one Riordon Scholarship (full tuition in years 1-4, capped at the domestic fee). A prestige award replaces the regular entrance scholarship.
requirements: Entering Carleton directly from secondary school or CEGEP
No previous college or university study
Admission average of 90% or higher
Demonstrated leadership in extracurricular or community activities
GPA of 10.0 each year to renew
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee reviews admission averages together with extracurricular and community involvement.
important_dates: Deadline: 1 March 2027, 11:59pm EST (next working day if on a weekend)
opportunities.about_provider: Carleton University is a public research university in Ottawa, Canada's capital, known for journalism, public affairs, engineering and computer science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Carleton, download the Prestige Scholarship form, complete it and email it with a signed reference letter and your student number to awards@carleton.ca by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: Riordon award is capped at the Canadian domestic tuition fee. Contact: awards@carleton.ca, 613-520-3600.

opportunities.title: FEBS Congress 2027 Bursaries for Young Scientists (Riga)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD students and young postdocs presenting an abstract who belong to a FEBS Constituent Society and work in a FEBS country.
opportunities.description:
The Federation of European Biochemical Societies (FEBS) offers about 175 bursaries to help young scientists attend the 51st FEBS Congress in Riga, Latvia, from 3 to 7 July 2027. The congress is hosted by the Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian Biochemical Societies.

Bursaries are for PhD students and postdocs within five years of their PhD who will present a research abstract as first author. Applicants must study or work in a country with a FEBS Constituent Society and be members of that society, so they suit African researchers based at European institutions (and in North African countries with FEBS member societies) rather than those working in most of Sub-Saharan Africa.

The deadline is Monday 1 March 2027 at 23:59 CET, and decisions are sent by the end of April 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Each bursary covers the young-scientist early registration fee plus EUR 475 towards travel and accommodation (EUR 850 in total), reimbursed by bank transfer after the congress.
requirements: First and presenting author of a research abstract
Registered PhD student, or postdoc within 5 years of the PhD
Studying or working at an institution in a FEBS Constituent Society country other than Latvia
Member of a FEBS Constituent Society
Travelling from outside Latvia
Not holding a FEBS Advanced Course 2027 registration grant or a FEBS YSF 2027 grant
documents: Single PDF with: proof of PhD status (enrolment or supervisor letter; for postdocs the PhD certificate plus PI letter)
Membership certificate or society letter valid through 1 March 2027
Abstract submitted in the congress system
opportunities.selection_process: FEBS assesses eligible applications and notifies applicants by the end of April 2027; previous FEBS travel awards may count against an applicant.
important_dates: Abstract submission opened: end of October 2026
opportunities.about_provider: FEBS is a federation of biochemistry and molecular biology societies across Europe and neighbouring regions. It runs the annual FEBS Congress, advanced courses and fellowships, including the PROBio-Africa fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register for the congress and pay the fee by 1 March 2027 (bank transfer accepted), then submit your abstract in the congress system, answer yes to the bursary question and upload the PDF with proof of status, membership and CV.
opportunities.notes: Researchers in Hinari countries such as Morocco and Tunisia can also use the FEBS Mathias Sprinzl scheme (deadline 11 January 2027). Russia and Belarus are currently suspended.

opportunities.title: FWO PhD Fellowship Fundamental Research 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Four-year doctoral fellowship at a Flemish university, open from 3 December 2026, with a starting grant of about EUR 2,700 a month.

opportunities.title: Heinrich Böll Foundation PhD Scholarship for International Students (Spring 2027 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International doctoral candidates from DAC countries (including all of Africa) or the EU with a foreign degree, German B2 and admission to a German PhD programme.
opportunities.description:
The Heinrich Böll Foundation, the political foundation linked to Germany's Green party, funds international doctoral candidates who want to do a PhD in Germany. Its scholarship department (Studienwerk) supports candidates from EU countries and from countries on the OECD's DAC list, which includes every African country, and it gives priority to DAC-country applicants who do not yet live in Germany.

The scholarship normally runs for three years and can be extended by up to six months. Applicants must already have a university degree completed abroad, have started preliminary work on their doctorate and hold (or be about to receive) admission to a doctoral programme at a state or state-recognised German university.

There are two application windows a year. The autumn 2026 round has closed; the spring 2027 round runs from 15 January 2027 to 1 March 2027, and the deadline is binding. Besides academic strength, the foundation looks for social engagement and political interest in line with its green values.
opportunities.benefits: Non-EU doctoral scholars receive EUR 1,400 per month plus a EUR 100 monthly mobility allowance and various individual allowances. Scholars from the EU or not educated in Germany receive a basic EUR 1,650 per month (from October 2025) plus EUR 100 per month for research costs. Tuition is not covered.
requirements: University degree completed outside Germany
Admission (or pending admission) to a doctoral programme at a state or state-recognised university, usually in Germany
Preliminary PhD work done and a realistic timetable
German at level B2 or DSH 1 with a certificate
Demonstrated social commitment and political interest
National of an EU or DAC-list country (DAC applicants not yet in Germany are prioritised)
documents: Certified copy of degree certificate (translated if needed)
Proof of doctoral admission or supervisor's letter
Research exposé of up to 10 pages including outline, bibliography, structure and a 36-month timetable
Two expert reports from professors or postdoctoral lecturers, one from the main supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Selection has three stages: a written application reviewed on academic record, research project, social and political engagement and motivation; an interview with a liaison lecturer (by mid-May for the March deadline); and a final online interview with the selection committee in May to July. Decisions are sent in June or July.
opportunities.about_provider: The Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung is a German political foundation affiliated with the Green party, promoting democracy, human rights and ecology. Its scholarship department in Berlin funds students and doctoral candidates, and it runs offices across Africa including Nairobi, Abuja, Dakar, Cape Town and Rabat.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the foundation's scholarship portal (stipendium.boell.de), which opens at least six weeks before the deadline. Upload all documents and arrange both expert reports and the social-commitment reference before 1 March 2027. Incomplete applications are not processed.
opportunities.notes: Do not wait for the last day, the portal can be slow. Applicants who were rejected at the final stage cannot reapply. The 'Tailwind for Talents' name used by listings does not appear on the foundation's pages. Contact: studienwerk@boell.de.

opportunities.title: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship for International Master's Students (Spring 2027 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International graduates from DAC countries (including all of Africa) or the EU with German B2 who plan a four-semester Master's in Germany.
opportunities.description:
The Heinrich Böll Foundation funds international students who completed their first degree abroad and want to do a full-time Master's degree in Germany. Students from the EU and from DAC-list countries, which include all African countries, can apply, and the foundation gives priority to DAC-country applicants who have not yet moved to Germany.

All disciplines at state or state-recognised universities are eligible, but only Master's programmes of at least four semesters are funded. The award runs for the regular study period and can be extended by one semester.

The spring 2027 window runs from 15 January to 1 March 2027. Note that the foundation's main page also says that from 1 March 2027 it will only accept applications for first-cycle programmes, which seems to conflict with this Master's offer, so applicants should confirm with the foundation before applying.
opportunities.benefits: Non-EU students not educated in Germany receive EUR 992 per month plus individual allowances. EU students not educated in Germany receive up to EUR 855 plus a EUR 300 monthly study-costs allowance, depending on parental income or own assets, with possible family, childcare and health allowances. Tuition is not covered.
requirements: First degree completed outside Germany
Plan to study full-time in a Master's of at least four semesters at a state or state-recognised German university
Very good academic record
German at level B2 or DSH 1 with a certificate
Social commitment and political interest
National of an EU or DAC-list country (priority to DAC applicants not yet in Germany)
opportunities.selection_process: There are three stages: review of the written application, an interview with a liaison lecturer, and a final online interview with the selection committee between May and July. Results are sent in June or July, and payments usually start by 1 October.
opportunities.about_provider: The Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung is a German political foundation affiliated with the Green party that promotes democracy, human rights and ecology. Its scholarship department in Berlin supports students and doctoral candidates from Germany and abroad.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online at the foundation's scholarship portal (stipendium.boell.de) during the 15 January - 1 March 2027 window. Send every document, including the expert report and social-commitment reference, before the deadline, because incomplete files are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Check first with studienwerk@boell.de whether Master's applications are still accepted in the March 2027 round, since the main page mentions a switch to first-cycle programmes only. The 'Tailwind for Talents' label used by listings is not on the official pages.

opportunities.title: ISM Graduate Scholarships in Mathematics 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Canadian and international PhD students in mathematics at an ISM member university in Quebec with a GPA of at least 3.5 can be nominated by their department.
opportunities.description:
The Institut des sciences mathématiques (ISM) is a consortium of Quebec universities that pools resources for graduate training in mathematics and statistics. Its Graduate Scholarships support excellent students doing a PhD at a member university, alongside matching funding from the host department.

Candidates do not apply to ISM directly. They send their file to their host department by 1 March 2027, departments rank their candidates, and ISM's director chooses the recipients. The award is open to both Canadian and international students, and departments are asked to seek a waiver of the higher international fee for foreign recipients.

For African mathematicians admitted to a PhD in Montreal, Quebec City or Sherbrooke, this adds to the departmental funding package.
opportunities.benefits: ISM pays up to CAD 10,000 a year, and the host department must add at least the same amount. Total funding from all sources is capped at CAD 34,000 a year. Foreign students may receive help obtaining a tuition differential waiver.
requirements: Registered (or admitted) full-time in a PhD programme at an ISM member university
Master's students are not eligible
Cumulative GPA of at least 3.5
Excellent academic record and research ability
Open to Canadian and international students
Paid work limited to 450 hours a year
documents: Two letters of recommendation, one from the current or future supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Departments rank their nominees and send lists to ISM between 15 March and 1 June. The ISM director selects recipients with input from programme groups.
important_dates: Departmental rankings to ISM: 15 March to 1 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The ISM, hosted by the Université du Québec à Montréal, brings together the mathematics departments of Quebec universities including McGill, Concordia, Université de Montréal, Université Laval, UQAM and Sherbrooke.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Send the ISM cover page, transcripts, CV and two letters to the graduate office of your host mathematics department by 1 March 2027. The department forwards ranked candidates to ISM.
opportunities.notes: Funding beyond the fourth PhD year is given only in exceptional cases. ISM also runs CRM-ISM undergraduate research internships (deadline 12 March 2027) and an Outstanding PhD Candidates award (deadline 14 May 2027). Contact: ism@uqam.ca.

opportunities.title: ITC Excellence Scholarship Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top-10% graduates from listed countries, including most African countries, who are admitted to ITC's master's in Geo-information Science or Spatial Engineering can apply by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
The ITC Excellence Scholarship Programme is offered by the University of Twente's Faculty of Geo-information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) in the Netherlands. It gives partial funding to a small number of very strong applicants to its two-year master's programmes in Geo-information Science and Earth Observation, and in Spatial Engineering.

The scholarship pays EUR 25,000 in support and waives ITC tuition of EUR 33,180. Recipients still contribute EUR 17,500 themselves towards tuition, living allowances, insurance and the residence permit, and must show they can pay it.

Applicants must be nationals and residents of a listed country, which includes most African countries, and must already hold an admission letter before applying.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 25,000 in financial support plus a waiver of ITC tuition worth EUR 33,180 (total programme cost EUR 75,680). The student pays an own contribution of EUR 17,500 (tuition EUR 12,080, allowances EUR 3,750, insurance EUR 1,400, residence permit EUR 270).
requirements: National and resident of a country on the official list
Academic admission to an eligible ITC master's received before applying
Bachelor's degree from a recognised university outside the Netherlands
Academic results in the top 10% of the class
IELTS overall 6.5 or equivalent
First enrolment at the University of Twente and not eligible for Dutch study finance
No other UT or Dutch scholarship (except the NL Scholarship) and no full external scholarship
Able to pay the EUR 17,500 own contribution and meet Dutch visa rules
documents: Supporting documents listed in the 2027 rules and regulations
opportunities.selection_process: A limited number of awards go to the strongest eligible candidates who meet the top-10% academic standard. To keep the award in year two, students must earn at least 45 of 60 credits and stay in the top 10%.
opportunities.about_provider: ITC is the University of Twente's faculty for geo-information science and earth observation in Enschede. It has trained professionals from developing countries in mapping, remote sensing and spatial planning for more than 70 years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for academic admission to one of the two ITC master's programmes through the University of Twente online system. Once admitted, submit the ITC Excellence Scholarship form in Osiris by 1 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: Contact the Study Information Centre at study@utwente.nl or +31 53 489 5489.

opportunities.title: Louis Cha Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with an offer from St John's College, Cambridge, for an MPhil or PhD on the literature, history or culture of China before 1912 are considered.
opportunities.description:
The Louis Cha Scholarship is a postgraduate award at St John's College, Cambridge, funded by a gift from the novelist Dr Louis Cha (Jin Yong). It supports one student doing an MPhil or PhD on the literature, history or culture of early and dynastic China, up to 1912.

The scholarship covers the approved University fee and pays a maintenance grant, reduced where the student holds other funding. It runs for the length of the course, up to three years, for study starting in October 2027.

There is no separate form: applicants apply to Cambridge for their course, naming St John's as first-choice college, and the application must reach St John's before 1 March 2027. African scholars working on pre-modern China are eligible on the same terms as everyone else.
opportunities.benefits: The approved University composition fee plus a maintenance grant, which St John's currently sets at GBP 20,700 a year; both are reduced by any other funding held. The Cambridge funding database lists the total value as GBP 32,650 to 59,600 a year. One award.
requirements: Offer to study an MPhil or PhD at Cambridge in pre-1912 Chinese literature, history or culture
St John's College named as first-choice college
Not already fully funded through another Cambridge college
Chosen on academic merit
No nationality restriction
documents: Cambridge postgraduate application (no separate scholarship form)
Annual research report once the award is held
opportunities.selection_process: St John's selects the recipient on academic merit after the University application has been assessed. Results are usually given by the end of May.
important_dates: University application must reach St John's: before 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: St John's College is one of the largest and oldest colleges of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1511. It funds a wide range of postgraduate studentships for its members.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your MPhil or PhD through Cambridge Postgraduate Admissions and put St John's as your first-choice college so the application reaches the college before 1 March 2027. Current St John's PhD students should email the Postgraduate Office for the separate form.
opportunities.notes: Contact: graduate-office@joh.cam.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Max Weber Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027-2028 (Economics late round)
opportunities.provider: European University Institute, Max Weber Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Economists of any nationality who finished (or will defend) their PhD within the last five years can apply in the late round.
opportunities.description:
The Max Weber Programme of the European University Institute (EUI) is one of the largest postdoctoral programmes in the social sciences and humanities, hosting about 65 fellows a year at the Badia Fiesolana in Florence, Italy. It is highly selective, with an acceptance rate below 2%.

The main 2027-28 deadline passed on 16 October 2026, but the EUI's Department of Economics accepts late applications until 1 March 2027 at 14:00 CET. Economics fellowships last one or two years, from September to August, starting on 1 September 2027.

The programme is open to every nationality, so recent African economics PhDs can apply. Fellows join a residential community, receive training in teaching and academic careers and can take a part-time assistant professor role in their second year.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of EUR 2,500 per month plus family allowances where applicable, health insurance, and a EUR 1,500 research and mission fund. In the second year fellows may take a part-time assistant professor contract adding about EUR 850 net per month.
requirements: Any nationality
PhD received between 1 September 2022 and 1 September 2027 (or approval to defend by 1 September 2027, defence by 31 December 2027)
Not an EUI doctoral student, employee or fellow at the deadline
English at CEFR C1 (certificate needed only if selected, e.g. IELTS 7.5 or TOEFL iBT 110)
Two to three academic referees, none from current EUI professors
documents: Two-page research proposal including a reflection on gender and diversity
At least two reference letters uploaded by referees
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic achievements and potential, the research proposal and fit with a mentor; country and background are also considered. About 2% receive offers and 5-10% go on a reserve list, and online interviews may be held. Economics recruitment runs until the end of March.
opportunities.about_provider: The European University Institute in Florence is an international postgraduate and postdoctoral institute founded by EU member states. Its Max Weber Programme trains early-career researchers in economics, history, law, political and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Use the EUI online application (the Max Weber 'Apply now' form on eui.eu) and select the Department of Economics. Upload the CV, statement, proposal and passport and ask referees to submit their letters online before 1 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: The information page still lists the October date for references, so confirm with Reference.Fellow@eui.eu what the late round needs. Externally funded candidates (at least EUR 15,000 for 12 months) have a separate ad hoc call.

opportunities.title: Mount Allison Marjorie Young Bell Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding high school graduates of any nationality applying for first year at Mount Allison in 2027-28.
opportunities.description:
The Marjorie Young Bell Scholarship is one of the largest undergraduate awards at Mount Allison University, a liberal arts university in Sackville, New Brunswick, Canada. Eight scholarships worth CAD 70,000 each (CAD 17,500 a year for four years) are offered to outstanding high school graduates starting university, and an optional internship is included.

The selection looks beyond grades to leadership, volunteering, extracurricular activities, work experience and citizenship. No nationality restriction is stated, so international and African applicants applying for 2027-28 can be considered.

There is no separate form: applicants use the general Mount Allison admission and scholarship application, then send a reference letter and an essay, by 1 March. Finalists who are not chosen receive the President's Scholarship worth CAD 20,000.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 70,000 over four years (CAD 17,500 per year) plus an optional internship. Finalists not selected receive the CAD 20,000 President's Scholarship. The award cannot be combined with other scholarships.
requirements: Outstanding high school graduate entering first year in 2027-28
Strong academic ability plus leadership, volunteer and extracurricular involvement, work experience and good citizenship
English proficiency proof if required for your country
Renewal: 3.5 GPA over 30 credits per year, community involvement and a yearly activities report
documents: Mount Allison admission and scholarship application
One reference letter emailed by the referee to admissions@mta.ca
Essay (question emailed after you apply), uploaded to your application account
Passport or government ID and English proof for international applicants
important_dates: Application and supporting documents due: 1 March (for 2027-28 entry)
opportunities.about_provider: Mount Allison University is a primarily undergraduate liberal arts and sciences university in Sackville, New Brunswick, consistently ranked among Canada's top undergraduate universities. It offers entrance scholarships from CAD 4,000 up to CAD 70,000.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Mount Allison online application (apply.mta.ca), which covers both admission and scholarships. After submitting, you will receive the essay question; upload the essay and ask your referee to email the reference letter before 1 March.
opportunities.notes: The page prints the deadline as 1 March without a year; it applies to the 2027-28 application cycle. International students can also be considered for the CAD 5,000 International Award. Contact: financialaid@mta.ca.

opportunities.title: OMGC Special Issue: AI Use in the Global South: Agency, Governance, and Knowledge Production
opportunities.provider: Online Media and Global Communication (De Gruyter Brill / SISU)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to researchers worldwide, especially Global South scholars, writing on AI agency, governance and knowledge production.
opportunities.description:
Online Media and Global Communication (OMGC) has opened a call for papers for a special issue titled "AI Use in the Global South: Agency, Governance, and Knowledge Production". The issue looks at how artificial intelligence is being taken up, contested and governed outside the Global North.

The guest editors are Amit Verma and Abhishika Sharma (Manipal University Jaipur, India), Svetlana S. Bodrunova (St. Petersburg State University, Russia) and Comfort Ene Obaje (University of Benin, Nigeria). Suggested themes include AI and data colonialism and epistemic justice; migration and diaspora; information integrity and platform governance; journalism and strategic communication; and digital inclusion and community agency.

Manuscripts are due by 1 March 2027 and publication of the issue is expected by 31 December 2027. With an African co-editor and a Global South focus, it is a strong outlet for African media, communication and AI-policy scholars.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in an open-access, Scopus-indexed journal. The call states no fee or funding; some published articles may also be translated into Chinese as book chapters.
requirements: Original research article on AI use in the Global South
Manuscript normally within 7,500 words, excluding references, tables and figures
Follows OMGC citation style with a structured abstract
Open to authors of any nationality
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions go through the journal's peer review via ScholarOne, handled by the special issue guest editors.
opportunities.about_provider: OMGC is an open-access journal indexed in Scopus (Q1), sponsored by Shanghai International Studies University and published by De Gruyter Brill. It covers digital media and global communication research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through ScholarOne Manuscripts at https://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/omgc and choose the special issue "AI Use in the Global South: Agency, Governance, and Knowledge Production" when submitting. Formatting rules are in the Submit section of the journal's De Gruyter page. Questions go to omgc@shisu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: Remember to select the special issue in the submission system, otherwise the paper goes to the general queue.

opportunities.title: St. Thomas University Chancellor's and President's International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top-ranked first-year international applicants with at least an 80% average can receive renewable tuition scholarships.

opportunities.title: University of Southern Mississippi Freshman Academic Excellence Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary school leavers fully admitted to the University of Southern Mississippi for autumn 2027 with qualifying GPA and ACT/SAT scores are automatically considered.
opportunities.description:
The University of Southern Mississippi (USM) gives Academic Excellence Scholarships to new first-year students based on their secondary school GPA and ACT or SAT score. Students fully admitted with final test scores by 1 March 2027 are considered automatically, with no essay or interview.

Awards range from USD 1,500 a year up to full tuition for the highest scores, and the top students can also get a free double room in their first year. They renew for four years if the student keeps a 2.5 GPA and completes 15 credits each semester.

USM's page notes that international students are taxed on scholarship amounts above full tuition, which shows international students can hold these awards; applicants from Africa should confirm the details with the scholarships office.
opportunities.benefits: Annual awards by GPA and test score. GPA 3.0-3.24: USD 1,500 to 4,500. GPA 3.25 and above: USD 1,500 (ACT 20) rising to USD 10,000 (ACT 31), and full tuition for ACT 32-36. Students with GPA 3.6+ and ACT 32+ (SAT 1420+) also receive a free double room for the first year. Renewable for four years.
requirements: Secondary school senior fully admitted for the autumn term after graduation
No prior college attendance
Cumulative secondary school GPA of at least 3.0
ACT or SAT taken before the deadline (SAT converted to ACT)
Renewal: 2.5 USM GPA and 15 credits each autumn and spring
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: awards are assigned from the GPA and test-score table once the student is fully admitted.
important_dates: Full admission with final test scores: 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Southern Mississippi is a public research university with its main campus in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, USA.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to USM, send your transcript and official ACT or SAT scores, and be fully admitted by 1 March 2027. Accept any award offered in the SOAR portal by 1 May.
opportunities.notes: Most undergraduate scholarships at USM mention a FAFSA, which international students cannot file; check international rules with USM before relying on this award.

opportunities.title: Vision-Conf 2027: Computer Vision, Pattern Recognition and Virtual Intelligence
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide working on computer vision or VR can submit papers to this hybrid conference.
opportunities.description:
Vision-Conf 2027, the International Conference on Creative Computer Vision and Virtual Reality Applications, is a four-day hybrid conference hosted by the Romanian-American University in Bucharest, Romania, from 22 to 25 June 2027. It covers computer vision, pattern recognition, image processing and virtual reality.

Papers go through IEEE-style review, and the organisers say they have applied for IEEE technical co-sponsorship and indexing (IEEE Xplore and Scopus after approval), which is not yet confirmed. Full papers are due on 1 March 2027, with acceptance notices on 15 April and camera-ready versions on 30 April 2027.

Because the event is hybrid and open to authors worldwide, African researchers can take part without travelling, although the pages checked do not mention grants or fee waivers.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is described. Accepted papers are presented in person or online and are planned for IEEE indexing if approval is granted.
requirements: Original paper not under review elsewhere
Topic in computer vision, pattern recognition, image processing or VR
Open to authors of any nationality
documents: Full paper following the conference submission guidelines
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed and authors are notified of acceptance on 15 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The Romanian-American University is a private university in Bucharest, Romania, which organises Vision-Conf with an international programme committee.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit your paper through the submission system linked from vision-conf.org (conferences.sparcly.ai/VisionConf2027) before 1 March 2027, after checking the submission and registration pages for format and fees.
opportunities.notes: IEEE indexing is applied for, not confirmed. Verify the contact email (the CFP shows two different addresses) before writing to the organisers.

opportunities.title: EACR 2027 Congress Travel Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: EACR members in financial need who are students, early-career researchers or based in low- and middle-income countries can apply.
opportunities.description:
The European Association for Cancer Research (EACR) offers travel grants so that members in financial need can attend its 2027 Congress, "Innovative Cancer Science", in Bilbao, Spain, from 14 to 17 June 2027, and present an oral or poster abstract.

Grants are aimed at students and early-career members with less than four years of postdoctoral experience, and at members based in low- and middle-income economies on the World Bank list, which covers most African countries. Each grant gives free congress registration and money towards travel and accommodation.

The travel grant application deadline is 2 March 2027, the same day abstracts close. Applications had not opened when the page was checked; abstract submission opens on 1 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Free congress registration plus funds towards travel and accommodation costs (amounts not stated).
requirements: EACR member at least 30 days before the deadline, without exception
Abstract submitted for the congress (non-refundable abstract fee plus VAT)
Registration fee not yet paid
Demonstrated financial need
Student or early-career member with under four years of postdoctoral experience, OR member based in a low- or middle-income economy
documents: Travel grant application (details to be published)
important_dates: Travel grant and abstract deadline: 2 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The EACR is Europe's largest membership association for cancer researchers and a registered charity in England and Wales. It runs congresses, conferences and grant schemes for cancer scientists worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Join the EACR well before the deadline, submit your abstract when the system opens on 1 December 2026, and apply for the travel grant by 2 March 2027 without paying the registration fee. The EACR suggests subscribing to its congress mailing list to be told when the grant form opens.
opportunities.notes: Membership must be active 30 days before the deadline, so join by about 31 January 2027.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: Emerging Concepts in Developmental Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Developmental biologists of any nationality can attend; grants up to EUR 1,000 support travellers from outside Europe.
opportunities.description:
The EMBO | EMBL Symposium "Emerging Concepts in Developmental Biology" takes place at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, from 8 to 11 June 2027, with a virtual option. It focuses on new ideas in developmental biology, with an emphasis on artificial intelligence, imaging and synthetic biology, and welcomes researchers at all career stages.

EMBL and EMBO offer registration fee waivers, travel grants and childcare grants. Travel grants go up to EUR 1,000 for participants travelling from outside Europe, which makes the meeting accessible to African developmental biologists.

Abstracts are due on 2 March 2027; on-site registration closes on 27 April 2027 and virtual registration on 1 June 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Fee waivers that refund the registration fee, travel grants for transport, accommodation and visas (up to EUR 400 from within Europe, up to EUR 1,000 from outside), and childcare grants. Registration fees: on-site EUR 650 (PhD), EUR 750 (academia); virtual EUR 190 (PhD), EUR 240 (academia).
requirements: Researchers of any career stage and nationality
Only on-site participants may submit abstracts
Abstract up to 2,000 characters excluding spaces, title up to 20 words
documents: Financial assistance application (link emailed after on-site registration; by abstract deadline for virtual)
Travel receipts within two months after the trip
opportunities.selection_process: Abstract results come about 21 days after the deadline. Financial support is awarded on scientific merit, location, need and expected career impact.
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL, the European Molecular Biology Laboratory, runs a conference and course programme in Heidelberg, and EMBO supports life scientists across Europe and beyond; together they fund the EMBO | EMBL Symposia.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on site via the EMBL event page, submit your abstract by 2 March 2027, and then use the emailed link to apply for a fee waiver, travel or childcare grant. Your place is confirmed only when the registration fee is paid, even if a waiver is later granted.
opportunities.notes: Hotel rooms are held until 11 May 2027 with booking code EES27-02. Contact: karoline.wolkersdorfer@embl.de.

opportunities.title: Exeter Excellence Scholarships 2027/28 Undergraduate
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International-fee students with an Exeter undergraduate offer and grades equivalent to AAB can apply for a GBP 15,000 yearly fee discount.
opportunities.description:
The University of Exeter in the UK is offering 150 Exeter Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships for international students starting a first-year degree in September 2027. Each scholarship is a GBP 15,000 reduction in tuition fees for every eligible year of study, and it is aimed at self-funded students.

Applicants must have international fee status and an offer (conditional or unconditional) for an eligible undergraduate programme across the faculties of Environment, Science and Economy; Health and Life Sciences; and Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences. A few programmes are excluded, including BMBS Medicine, BSc Medical Imaging and degree apprenticeships.

Round 1 closes on Thursday 4 March 2027 at 11:59 GMT, and results are emailed by 6 April 2027. African students with strong school results equivalent to AAB at A level are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 15,000 tuition fee discount for each year of study, recurring for the length of the degree. It cannot be combined with other Exeter scholarships.
requirements: International fee status for 2027/28
Offer for an eligible Exeter undergraduate degree, entering year one in September 2027
Academic merit equivalent to A-level grades AAB, judged from the UCAS application
Not progressing from the Exeter International Study Centre
Not applying to excluded programmes (e.g. BMBS Medicine, Medical Imaging, degree apprenticeships)
documents: Online scholarship form with a 300-word personal statement (two questions of up to 150 words each)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic merit from the UCAS application together with the personal statement about aspirations, community contribution and academic and career ambitions.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university and member of the Russell Group, with campuses in Exeter and Cornwall. It is ranked 136th in the QS World University Rankings, which sets the number of awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your degree through UCAS and receive an Exeter offer, then complete the scholarship webform linked on the award page before 4 March 2027. Questions go to admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Check the terms and conditions PDF on the award page and Exeter's country pages for how African qualifications such as WAEC or KCSE map to AAB.

opportunities.title: ICTP 8th Summer School on Climate Dynamics: Global Waves, Local Extremes (Jul 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career climate and atmospheric scientists worldwide can apply, with grant priority for those from developing countries.
opportunities.description:
The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy, will host the 8th Summer School on Theory, Mechanisms and Hierarchical Modelling of Climate Dynamics, titled "Global Waves, Local Extremes", from 12 to 23 July 2027 (event smr 4370).

The two-week school covers atmospheric, tropical and extratropical wave dynamics, weather and climate extremes and their predictability, with lectures, hands-on training and group projects. A parallel workshop on global Rossby waves and compound extremes runs during the school, with its own abstract submission.

There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants support selected participants, with priority for those from developing countries, which makes it a strong opportunity for African climate and atmospheric scientists. The application deadline shown is 5 March 2027; the call was marked as opening soon when checked.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants cover attendance costs for selected participants, with priority for participants from developing countries (amounts not stated).
requirements: Background suitable for an advanced school in climate dynamics
Priority for grants to participants from developing countries
Separate abstract application for those wishing to present at the parallel workshop
opportunities.about_provider: ICTP is a UNESCO Category 1 institute governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and the Italian government. It has supported physics and mathematics research in developing countries for more than 60 years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the 'Apply here' link on the ICTP event page (smr 4370) once the call opens, and request financial support in the form. To present a poster or talk, also apply to the parallel workshop (indico event 11445) with an abstract. Questions go to smr4370@ictp.it.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is printed as 05/03/2027 in ICTP's day-month-year format.

opportunities.title: Sciences Po Emile Boutmy Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: High-achieving non-EU students admitted to a Sciences Po bachelor's or master's programme can be awarded the Emile Boutmy scholarship towards tuition and living costs.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master imAGEin (Biology of Ageing) 2027-2029
opportunities.eligibility_summary: STEM bachelor's graduates of any nationality with strong English (e.g. IELTS 6.5) can apply; top-ranked applicants receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships.
opportunities.description:
imAGEin is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in the biology of ageing, coordinated by Université Côte d'Azur through its LIFE Graduate School in Nice, France. The third cohort runs from 2027 to 2029 and studies at partner universities in Coimbra, Seville, Cologne and Sorbonne Université in Paris.

The two-year, full-time programme trains STEM graduates in the science of ageing, with a personal training plan in which each student ranks three mobility tracks across the partner universities. Studies start between early September and early October 2027, after welcome days in the first week of September.

Applications for the 2027-2029 cohort open on 6 January 2027 and close on 6 March 2027 (midnight Paris time). The top candidates receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships, which are open to applicants from Africa and every other region, subject to the programme's nationality quotas.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months to cover living, travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, and they pay no participation (tuition) costs. Self-funded students pay EUR 12,000 in total if non-European (EUR 6,000 per year) or EUR 6,000 if European, plus a non-refundable EUR 1,000 pre-registration fee deducted from Year 1.
requirements: Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (180 ECTS) or equivalent; final-year students may apply but must graduate by July 2027

English: IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each part, TOEFL iBT (93 with 22 per section for tests before 21 Jan 2026, or 4.5 in each section for newer tests), Cambridge C1/C2 at 180 with no part below 176, or proof of a semester taught fully in English
English test no older than two years
Not eligible for the scholarship if you already held an Erasmus Mundus joint master scholarship
documents: Valid passport or ID (valid for the full two years if a visa is needed)
STEM bachelor's diploma with official English translation (or proof of enrolment and expected end date)
Official transcripts with GPA converted to a 4.0 scale
Europass CV (max 2 pages, showing age and cGPA on 4.0 scale)
Personal Training Plan from eCandidat with three ranked mobility tracks
Two signed recommendation letters in English on letterhead, dated within two years
Optional: module handbook, STEM experience or awards
opportunities.selection_process: After an eligibility check, Phase 1 scores the file from 0 to 10 on CV and experience, motivation letter, academic results, references, relevance of the training plan and English; an average of at least 7/10 is needed to move on. Phase 2 is an online interview in English of up to 20 minutes with two or three committee members (at most 200 slots). The final mark is 30% Phase 1 and 70% Phase 2 on a 20-point scale, and scholarships are given from the same ranking.
important_dates: Rankings and scholarship offers: early April 2027
Waiting-list notices: early to mid April 2027
Welcome days: first week of September 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Université Côte d'Azur is a research university in Nice, France; its LIFE Graduate School coordinates imAGEin together with the University of Coimbra, the University of Seville, the University of Cologne and Sorbonne Université.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the eCandidat platform of Université Côte d'Azur; the link appears on the imAGEin application page once the window opens on 6 January 2027. Upload all documents, including the personal training plan and two reference letters, before 6 March 2027. Shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview in March.
opportunities.notes: The document list on the page is indicative; the final list is published before the window opens. Contact: eur-life.imagein@univ-cotedazur.fr.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus InterCultural Leadership in Digital Era (CLIDE) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's graduates of any nationality with B2 English can apply for 12 Erasmus Mundus scholarships and 18 tuition-free places.
opportunities.description:
CLIDE, Intercultural Leadership in the Digital Era, is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master run by Nicolaus Copernicus University (NCU) in Toruń, Poland, with a consortium of five universities and co-funded by the European Union. The two-year, 120 ECTS programme offers two tracks: Leading Intercultural Teams, and Leadership in the Digital Era.

Students start at the University of Granada in Spain and then move, depending on the track, to the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria or NCU, followed by a semester taught by Simon Kuznets Kharkiv National University of Economics (delivered at NCU) or at Hassan II University of Casablanca in Morocco, before an internship and thesis semester at NCU.

For 2027/2028 there are 30 places: 12 with Erasmus Mundus scholarships and 18 tuition-free places. Admission opens on 22 February and closes on 7 March 2027, and scholarships are open to applicants from every region, with a cap of five per nationality across editions.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: no tuition, EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months and comprehensive insurance (travel and installation costs are not included). Tuition-free places give a fee waiver and insurance but no stipend. Self-funded students from outside the EU and consortium countries pay EUR 4,000 per semester.
requirements: Bachelor's degree that gives access to master's studies in the issuing country
English at B2 level with proof
Diploma recognition check (NAWA) where required; not needed for EU/OECD/EFTA diplomas
Applicants from any region; no more than five scholarships per nationality across four editions
documents: Bachelor's diploma scan with English translation
At least two recommendation letters (one academic, one professional)
opportunities.selection_process: Documents are verified, about 60-80 applicants are interviewed on motivation and leadership knowledge, and around 20-30 candidates are accepted. The consortium ranks scholarship candidates after the deadline and keeps a reserve list.
opportunities.about_provider: Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń is one of Poland's largest public universities. It coordinates CLIDE with the University of Granada, the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Simon Kuznets Kharkiv National University of Economics and Hassan II University of Casablanca.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through NCU's admission system (IRK) during the 22 February - 7 March 2027 window, following the 2027/28 admission rules on the CLIDE site. Contact clide@umk.pl for programme and scholarship questions and studywithncu@umk.pl for diploma and language questions.
opportunities.notes: The window is only two weeks long, so prepare documents and the video in advance. Support funding exists for students with long-term impairments.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: Evolutionary Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality in evolutionary biochemistry can attend, with travel grants up to EUR 1,000 for non-European participants.
opportunities.description:
The EMBO | EMBL Symposium "Evolutionary biochemistry and molecular biology: origin and diversification of molecular systems" brings together researchers studying how molecular systems arose and evolved, including ancestral sequence reconstruction, protein evolution and metabolic networks. It is held at EMBL Heidelberg, Germany, with a virtual option, and is aimed at researchers at all career stages.

The programme on the event page runs over four days from Tuesday 29 June to Friday 2 July 2027, although one part of the page mentions 19-23 July 2027, so check the dates with the organisers. Abstracts are due around 9 March 2027.

EMBL and EMBO offer fee waivers, travel grants of up to EUR 1,000 for participants from outside Europe, and childcare grants, which helps African evolutionary and molecular biologists to attend.
opportunities.benefits: Registration fee waivers, travel grants for transport, accommodation and visas (up to EUR 400 from within Europe, up to EUR 1,000 from outside Europe) and childcare grants. Fees: on-site EUR 650 (PhD), EUR 750 (academia); virtual EUR 190 (PhD), EUR 240 (academia).
requirements: Researchers at any career stage, any nationality
Only on-site registrants may submit abstracts
Abstract up to 2,000 characters excluding spaces, title up to 20 words
documents: Travel receipts within two months of travel
opportunities.selection_process: Abstract results come about three weeks after the deadline; financial support is decided on scientific merit, location, need and career impact.
important_dates: Abstract and virtual financial-assistance deadline: about 9 March 2027
Symposium: 29 June - 2 July 2027 (check; the page also mentions 19-23 July)
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL, the European Molecular Biology Laboratory, runs an international conference programme at its Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, and EMBO co-funds the EMBO | EMBL Symposia to promote life-science exchange.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register through the EMBL event page and submit an abstract before the deadline, requesting a fee waiver or travel grant during registration. A visa support letter is issued after payment. Contact: aline.schnieder@embl.org.
opportunities.notes: The page shows conflicting dates; confirm before booking travel. Registration must be paid to confirm a place even with a waiver.

opportunities.title: NTUT INTENSE Program Master's Scholarship (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International Master's applicants to Taipei Tech's STEM, finance or semiconductor programmes who will work in Taiwan after graduation.
opportunities.description:
The INTENSE programme is a Taiwanese initiative linking government, industry and universities to bring international students into Taiwanese degree programmes and then into jobs with partner companies. National Taipei University of Technology (Taipei Tech) takes part for its Fall 2027 intake, with funding launched by Taiwan's Ministry of Education.

Students admitted through INTENSE receive government funding and a monthly living allowance from a partner company, can do internships during their studies, and must work in Taiwan after graduating. For Fall 2027 the admitting programmes are STEM, finance and semiconductor-related Master's degrees, including the International Master's Program in Mechanical and Automation Engineering and the International Master's Program of the College of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.

The student nomination deadline is 10 March 2027 and results are announced in June 2027, for study starting in September 2027 in Taipei. The university stresses that the information is preliminary and may change with new Ministry of Education announcements.
opportunities.benefits: Government funding for studies plus a monthly living allowance paid by partner companies, with internship opportunities during the degree (amounts not stated).
requirements: International applicant for a Fall 2027 Master's in an admitting INTENSE programme
Willingness to accept an employment obligation in Taiwan after graduation
Eligibility details to follow Ministry of Education and NTUT announcements
opportunities.about_provider: National Taipei University of Technology (Taipei Tech) is a public university of technology in Taipei, Taiwan, known for engineering and industry links. Its Office of International Affairs runs international admissions and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the Taipei Tech INTENSE admissions page for the final rules and contact the Office of International Affairs (Andrew Liao, andrewliao@ntut.edu.tw, ext. 6526) to confirm how to be nominated before 10 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: The deadline is described as a nomination deadline and the page says eligibility may change, so confirm the process early.

opportunities.title: Blue Book Traineeship at the European Commission (October 2027 to February 2028)
eligible_nationalities: EU or EU candidate country nationals only
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Only for graduates who are nationals of EU member states or EU candidate countries; African nationals qualify only with such a second nationality.
opportunities.description:
The Blue Book traineeship is the European Commission's paid five-month traineeship for university graduates, run by the Directorate-General for Human Resources and Security. The session covered here runs from 1 October 2027 to 29 February 2028, mainly in Brussels and Luxembourg.

Applications open on 15 February 2027 at 10:00 and close on 12 March 2027 at 10:00 Brussels time. Preselection takes place in April and May 2027 and final selection in June and July 2027.

Important for African applicants: the administrative traineeship for graduates is only open to nationals of EU member states and of EU candidate countries (the latter for a limited number of DGs). African nationals can therefore apply only if they also hold an EU or candidate-country nationality.
opportunities.benefits: A five-month traineeship at the European Commission, from 1 October 2027 to 29 February 2028 (the monthly grant amount is not stated on the pages checked).
requirements: Nationality of an EU member state, or of an EU candidate country benefiting from a pre-accession strategy
Full university degree of at least three years (EQF level 6, 180 ECTS) completed with diploma by the application deadline
At least 18 years old on the start date
Valid passport or national ID card
Non-EU nationals: C1/C2 in English, French or German; EU nationals: two EU languages
No more than six weeks of previous work experience in any EU institution
documents: Proof of all declared qualifications and experience
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through preselection (April-May 2027) and a selection phase (June-July 2027) in which Commission departments choose trainees from the pre-selected pool.
opportunities.about_provider: The European Commission is the executive body of the European Union. Its Blue Book traineeship programme places about a thousand graduates a year across Commission departments and EU bodies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the EU traineeships portal (ec-stages.gestmax.eu) during the February-March window. Only one application per session and per type of traineeship is allowed.
opportunities.notes: Most African nationals are not eligible unless they hold dual EU or candidate-country nationality. A separate translation traineeship and a vocational (VET) traineeship exist with their own rules.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus EMIMEP Master in Microwave Electronics and Photonics 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Engineering and physics graduates of any nationality with some work or research experience and English proof can apply for full EMIMEP scholarships.
opportunities.description:
EMIMEP is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Microwave Electronics and Photonics, co-funded by the European Union and coordinated by the Université de Limoges in France, with partners including the University of Brescia in Italy and the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) in Spain.

The programme trains engineers in microwave, telecommunications and photonic technologies across several European universities. Erasmus Mundus scholarships for the 2027-2029 intake are open to applicants worldwide, including Sub-Saharan Africa, which the consortium lists among its partner-country regions.

Applications must be submitted by Friday 12 March 2027 at 23:59 Paris time, and the official selection list is usually known around April.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship of EUR 1,400 per month for up to 24 months, covering travel, visa and living costs, plus health and travel insurance and all tuition fees. Seven extra places are reserved for South America, Brazil/Mexico and the Balkans.
requirements: Bachelor's (180 ECTS) in electrical and electronic engineering, telecommunications, photonics, applied physics, computer science or physics; final-year students may apply if they graduate before September
At least 4 weeks of work or research experience with a positive assessment
Official English test results for applicants from non-English-speaking countries (B1 minimum at some partners)
Must not already hold an Erasmus Mundus scholarship
documents: Certified secondary and bachelor's certificates and transcripts in English
English test report (e.g. TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic)
Three reference letters, one from a non-academic referee
Proof of employment or internships in the last 5 years
opportunities.selection_process: Shortlisting weighs average marks (50%), professional or research experience (10%), references and publications (20%) and career continuity (20%). Shortlisted applicants have an online interview in English, and final ranking is 70% interview and 30% file, producing main and reserve lists.
opportunities.about_provider: The Université de Limoges is a French public university that coordinates the EMIMEP consortium with European partner universities such as Brescia and UPV/EHU, under the EU's Erasmus Mundus scheme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online on the Université de Limoges eCandidat platform (ecandidat-scol.unilim.fr), uploading certified English copies of all documents. No paper copies are needed.
opportunities.notes: The site banner still mentions 2025-2027 while the call page is for 2027-2029; the call page dates apply. The consortium says it uses AI tools for eligibility checks.

opportunities.title: Mozilla Foundation Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Innovators worldwide can apply for ten 12-month fellowships worth up to USD 125,000; a letter of intent is due 17 December 2026 and the full application by 12 March 2027.

opportunities.title: Confucius Institute Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholarship for Chinese language and teaching study in China.

opportunities.title: Damon Runyon Postdoctoral Fellowship Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early postdocs doing cancer research at a US institution can receive a four-year stipend of USD 70,000-76,000 a year plus expenses.

opportunities.title: Fitzwilliam College Charlton Scholarships 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's offer-holders of any nationality who are members of Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge, can be considered for up to four awards of GBP 15,000.
opportunities.description:
Fitzwilliam College at the University of Cambridge offers up to four Charlton Scholarships of GBP 15,000 each to students starting a master's course in the 2027/28 academic year. The awards are listed on the college's postgraduate funding page alongside its other studentships.

The scholarships are open to all nationalities, and the closing date is 15 March 2027. As with the college's other master's awards, applicants must hold a Cambridge offer and a place at Fitzwilliam to be considered.

For African students admitted to a Cambridge master's, a Charlton award can be combined with other funding to close the gap between fees, living costs and what a main scholarship pays.
opportunities.benefits: Up to four awards of GBP 15,000 for master's study in 2027/28.
requirements: Offer for a Cambridge master's course starting in 2027/28
Membership of Fitzwilliam College
Open to all nationalities
documents: Cambridge postgraduate application naming Fitzwilliam College
opportunities.about_provider: Fitzwilliam College is a college of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1869 to open the University to students of all backgrounds. It runs several of its own postgraduate scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's through Cambridge Postgraduate Admissions and choose Fitzwilliam as your college. Check the Fitzwilliam postgraduate funding page for any extra steps before 15 March 2027.
opportunities.notes: Fitzwilliam also offers the Cleaver-Wang Studentship (GBP 20,000) with the same closing date.

opportunities.title: Fitzwilliam College Cleaver-Wang Studentship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with an offer for a Cambridge master's course and membership of Fitzwilliam College by 15 March 2027 are considered automatically.
opportunities.description:
The Cleaver-Wang Studentship is a GBP 20,000 award from Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge, for one student starting a master's course in 2027/28. It was created in 2021 by alumnus David Wang and can be used for fees, at home or international rate, and for living costs.

All full-time and part-time master's courses starting in October are eligible except the MRes, MBA, MFin and PGCE. The award is based on academic merit, with preference for students working across disciplines or using innovative methods.

There is no separate application: anyone holding a Cambridge offer and a place at Fitzwilliam by 15 March 2027 is considered. The college advises applying to the University by 2 December 2026 to give yourself time.
opportunities.benefits: One award of GBP 20,000 for one year, usable towards tuition fees (home or international) and maintenance.
requirements: Offer of a place on a Cambridge master's course starting in October 2027
Membership of Fitzwilliam College by 15 March 2027
Not on an MRes, MBA, MFin or PGCE course
Open to all nationalities and fee statuses
Chosen on academic merit
documents: Cambridge postgraduate application (no separate studentship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Fitzwilliam considers all eligible offer-holders automatically and chooses on academic merit, preferring interdisciplinary or methodologically innovative work. Results are given in April to May 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Fitzwilliam College is a college of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1869 to widen access to the University. It offers several postgraduate studentships of its own.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's course through Cambridge Postgraduate Admissions and choose Fitzwilliam as your college. Once you hold an offer and Fitzwilliam membership by 15 March 2027, you are considered automatically.
opportunities.notes: Fitzwilliam also offers Charlton Scholarships (up to four of GBP 15,000, same deadline) and smaller subject awards.

opportunities.title: Joan and Eugene Vanderpool Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate students and PhD holders of any nationality researching the Athenian Agora may apply.
opportunities.description:
