opportunities.title: Taiwan Ministry of Education Scholarship for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students can apply through a Taiwan representative office for tuition and a monthly stipend for degree study in Taiwan.

opportunities.title: UIST 2027: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students of any nationality can submit papers on new user interface technology.
opportunities.description:
UIST 2027, the 40th ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, is the leading venue for research on new user interfaces and interaction technology. It is sponsored by ACM SIGCHI and SIGGRAPH and will be held at the Vienna Congress and Convention Center (VIECON) in Austria from 26 to 29 October 2027.

Workshops and the Doctoral Symposium take place on 26 October and the main conference on 27-29 October. Paper abstracts are due on 31 March, full papers on 7 April and supplementary materials on 9 April 2027.

The call is open to researchers everywhere, giving African HCI and systems researchers a route to a top-tier ACM venue. The conference also has student volunteer chairs and a Student Innovation Contest, though the pages do not yet describe travel support.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is described yet. Accepted papers are published by ACM and presented in Vienna.
requirements: Original research on user interface software and technology
Abstract registered before the full paper
Open to authors of any nationality
opportunities.about_provider: ACM SIGCHI and ACM SIGGRAPH are the special interest groups of the Association for Computing Machinery for human-computer interaction and computer graphics. Together they sponsor UIST each year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Follow the submission instructions on the UIST 2027 website: register an abstract by 31 March, then upload the full paper by 7 April and any supplementary files by 9 April 2027. Questions go to chairs2027@uist.org.
opportunities.notes: The deadline dates are printed without a year on the site but sit within the 2027 conference page. Watch for student volunteer calls, which often cover registration.

opportunities.title: University of Edinburgh Global Health Scholarship for Africa 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African students admitted to an Edinburgh MSc or PhD in global health, public health, medicine or biomedical sciences can receive a tuition waiver and possible living allowance.

opportunities.title: University of Glasgow African Excellence Award 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African-domiciled passport holders with first-class-equivalent grades who hold or are seeking an offer for a one-year taught master's at Glasgow starting September 2027 can apply for a 75% tuition fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The University of Glasgow African Excellence Award is a merit scholarship for outstanding students from across Africa who want to take a one-year, full-time taught master's degree at Glasgow in Scotland. The 2027/28 round is for the September 2027 intake and covers almost every subject the university teaches.

The award takes the form of a 75% reduction in tuition fees, which in most colleges is worth more than £20,000. Up to 16 awards are available, and shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.

Applicants must live in Africa and hold a passport from an African country, have grades equivalent to a UK first-class degree, and set out a clear career or development plan. You can apply for the award before you have an offer, but you need an offer to be considered for interview.
opportunities.benefits: A 75% tuition fee waiver for one year of study. Examples given by the university: about £20,543 off in Arts and Humanities, £25,281 in Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, £26,111 in Science and Engineering and the Adam Smith Business School, and £21,206 in Social Sciences. The actual value depends on the fee in your offer letter.
requirements: Domiciled in Africa and holding a passport from an African country
Grades equivalent to a UK first-class honours degree
Holding or applying for an offer for a one-year full-time taught master's starting September 2027
International fee status
Clear career and/or development plan
Must meet the UKVI living-cost requirement
documents: Online scholarship application form, including your career or development plan
Offer for an eligible master's programme (needed before interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on academic excellence and their plans. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview and contacted by 7 May 2027. Up to 16 awards are made.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world and a member of the UK's Russell Group of research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme at Glasgow, then complete the African Excellence Award form on the university's scholarship portal (linked from the award page). Questions go to student.recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Postgraduate diplomas and certificates are not eligible. The award cannot be combined with other Glasgow scholarships or discounts except the alumni discount; if you are offered more than one award, the lower one is withdrawn.

opportunities.title: Zhejiang University Chinese Government Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Chinese Government Scholarship via Zhejiang University.

opportunities.title: American University of Sharjah President's Scholarship (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Top international school leavers from outside the UAE (98% average or 40 IB points, IELTS 7.0) can apply by 1 April 2027 after admission to AUS.
opportunities.description:
The President's Scholarship is the top award of the American University of Sharjah (AUS) in the United Arab Emirates for new students who finished secondary school outside the UAE. It covers full tuition and lab fees, housing, a monthly stipend, flights and medical insurance for students starting in Fall 2027.

The scholarship is renewable while the student meets its conditions. Applicants must first receive an AUS admission offer, then submit a separate scholarship application with a portfolio, a short video and recommendation letters. The online form opens in December 2026 and the Fall 2027 deadline is 4:00 pm on 1 April 2027.

The bar is very high: for example, a 98% average in grades 10 to 12 with an SAT score of 1400, or 40 points in IB. For outstanding African school leavers, it offers a fully funded American-style education in the Gulf.
opportunities.benefits: 100% of tuition and lab fees, application fee waiver, a monthly stipend, on-campus housing, three round-trip tickets during the course of study, and student medical insurance. Renewable while requirements are met.
requirements: Completed secondary education outside the UAE; first-time student starting in Fall 2027
AUS admission offer
IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL iBT 94
IB: 40 points in grades 10-11 and 40 points in the final diploma; other systems: 98% in grades 10-11 and grade 12 plus SAT 1400
documents: Portfolio with an essay and evidence of leadership, scientific or literary contributions, honours and community service
Predicted grades and SAT or AP scores
opportunities.selection_process: Selection relies heavily on academic excellence and the portfolio. Grades from the last three years, including predicted final-year grades, are reviewed; conditional awards are withdrawn if predicted grades are not achieved.
opportunities.about_provider: The American University of Sharjah is a private university in Sharjah, UAE, offering an American-style liberal arts education with programmes in engineering, business, architecture and the arts and sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account at apply.aus.edu and apply for admission. After receiving an offer, submit the President's Scholarship application through the AUS Pulse financial-grant portal before 4:00 pm on 1 April 2027; AUS notes a VPN may be needed. Advising appointments can be booked online.
opportunities.notes: AUS also offers automatic merit scholarships of 10-20% of tuition for students with a 95% average in grades 10-11, and need-based financial grants.

opportunities.title: Augustana College Academic Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students of any nationality admitted to Augustana College for fall 2027 are automatically considered for merit awards of $29,000 to $33,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Augustana College, a private liberal arts college in Rock Island, Illinois, awards academic merit scholarships automatically to students it admits for fall 2027. There are three levels: the Presidential Scholarship ($33,000 a year), the Dean's Scholarship ($31,000) and the Founders Scholarship ($29,000).

No separate application is needed: the award level is set when the admission decision is made. The last regular-decision date for fall 2027 is 1 April 2027.

These large yearly awards can make a US liberal arts degree far more affordable for African students, who can apply as international first-year students.
opportunities.benefits: Presidential Scholarship $33,000 a year, Dean's Scholarship $31,000 a year, Founders Scholarship $29,000 a year, renewable each year subject to keeping the required GPA.
requirements: Admitted to Augustana College as a first-year student for fall 2027
Award level depends on academic record at admission
Renewal requires a cumulative GPA of 3.0 (Presidential), 2.75 (Dean's) or 2.5 (Founders)
documents: Standard Augustana admission application (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are assigned automatically from the academic record reviewed for admission.
important_dates: Regular decision deadline for fall 2027: 1 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Augustana College is a private liberal arts college in Rock Island, Illinois, on the Mississippi River, affiliated with the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission to Augustana College for fall 2027 by 1 April 2027 (or earlier rounds). Admitted students are considered automatically for the merit scholarships.
opportunities.notes: Augustana also offers a separate Mission and Meaning Scholarship ($1,000 a year) for students who complete four short online sessions by 7 December 2026.

opportunities.title: CIMPA Fellowship: Advances in Quantum Cryptography (IHP Paris trimester, Sep-Dec 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young mathematicians (36 or under or PhD within 5 years) based in developing countries can apply by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
CIMPA, the International Centre for Pure and Applied Mathematics, offers fellowships for young mathematicians from developing countries to take part in the thematic trimester 'Advances in Quantum Cryptography' at the Institut Henri Poincaré (IHP) in Paris. The trimester runs from 13 September to 10 December 2027 and is free of charge.

The programme opens with an introductory school (13-17 September) and continues with three workshops (11-15 October, 15-19 November, and 29 November to 3 December 2027). Fellows must take part in at least two-thirds of the programme.

The fellowship pays return travel, accommodation and a monthly allowance, which makes it a rare chance for African master's graduates, doctoral students and young researchers in mathematics and computer science to spend a term at a leading Paris institute. Applications close on 1 April 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Return travel up to EUR 1,600 (including visa fees), accommodation provided by IHP, and an allowance of EUR 700 per month.
requirements: Aged 36 or under, or doctorate obtained within the last 5 years
Based in a developing country according to the IMU classification
At least Master 2 level
Able to attend at least two-thirds of the trimester
documents: Up-to-date CV with details of master's-level courses
Up to two recommendation letters sent directly by the referees
opportunities.selection_process: The event organisers examine the applications. CIMPA informs applicants by letter in the weeks after the deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: CIMPA is an international centre based in France that supports mathematics research and training in developing countries through schools and fellowships. The Institut Henri Poincaré in Paris hosts thematic trimesters in mathematics and theoretical physics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the CIMPA applications platform (applications.cimpa.info) and submit your CV, motivation letter and project, and ask your referees to send their letters directly. CIMPA advises applying well before 1 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: Eligibility depends on the IMU list of developing countries, which includes most African countries. Another CIMPA fellowship in 2027 covers 'Learning over Structured High-Dimensional Objects' (15 March-23 April 2027).

opportunities.title: IUPAB 2027 Berlin Congress Bursary
opportunities.provider: International Union for Pure and Applied Biophysics
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-European PhD students and recent postdocs can apply from January to 1 April 2027 for help attending the IUPAB Congress in Berlin.
opportunities.description:
The International Union for Pure and Applied Biophysics (IUPAB) offers up to 25 bursaries to help early-career scientists attend its triennial IUPAB Congress, which will be held in Berlin, Germany, from 5 to 9 September 2027.

The bursaries are aimed at applicants from outside Europe. They help pay for four nights of hotel accommodation and the congress registration fee, and in some justified cases part of the air ticket for people from less favoured and overseas countries. European applicants are considered only if fewer than 25 awards go to non-European candidates.

Applications open after 1 January 2027 and must arrive by 1 April 2027. For African PhD students and postdocs in biophysics, this is a chance to present at one of the field's major world meetings.
opportunities.benefits: A contribution to accommodation (four hotel nights in a double room) and the registration fee; in a few justified cases, part of the air ticket for applicants from less favoured and overseas countries. Up to EUR 700 per bursary for European applicants.
requirements: Current PhD student, or postdoc who obtained the PhD within the last five years
Applicants from outside Europe are prioritised (European applicants only if fewer than 25 non-European awards are made)
Attend the IUPAB Congress in Berlin, 5-9 September 2027
Submit a one-page report within two months after the award
documents: IUPAB bursary application form (the page currently links the 2026 general travel-bursary form)
opportunities.selection_process: The IUPAB Executive decides eligibility, scientific merit and the level of support for each applicant.
opportunities.about_provider: IUPAB is the international scientific union for biophysics, registered in Paris, France. It organises the world biophysics congress every three years and supports young scientists with bursaries and prizes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: From January 2027, download the bursary application form from the IUPAB bursaries page, complete it and send it to IUPAB (inbox@iupab.org) before 1 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: The Berlin-specific form was not yet posted when checked; the page links the 2026 travel-bursary form. IUPAB also runs prizes for young investigators.

opportunities.title: Kipaji Scholarship – University of Twente 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UTS recipients from listed least-developed and low-income countries (including many African countries) starting a UT master's can be nominated by their faculty; deadline 1 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Kipaji Scholarship Fund at the University of Twente (UT) in the Netherlands gives extra support of up to €12,000 to master's students who already hold a University of Twente Scholarship (UTS). It is meant for students from the least developed and low-income countries, and can turn a partial UTS into full support.

The fund was started by UT alumni and friends and is kept going by an annual fundraising campaign among staff and alumni. Students cannot apply for it directly: their faculty nominates them.

It is a strong option for students from eligible African countries such as Ethiopia, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania or Malawi who are competing for a UTS on a Twente master's programme. ITC master's programmes and current UT students are excluded.
opportunities.benefits: Up to €12,000 as compensation for study-related costs, on top of a University of Twente Scholarship. Number of awards not stated.
requirements: Receive a University of Twente Scholarship (partial UTS qualifies) for a UT master's

Nationality of one of the listed DAC least-developed or low-income countries (African countries listed: Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Congo (DR), Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, São Tomé and Príncipe, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia)
Bachelor's degree from your home or a neighbouring country (not from UT)
Average grade of 8 for a pre-master programme, where one applies
Not a current UT student; not an ITC master's programme
documents: UTS application (stating in your motivation that you also want to be considered for Kipaji)
Motivation letter on how your studies will strengthen science or entrepreneurship in your home country (may be requested by the faculty)
opportunities.selection_process: There is no direct application. Faculties nominate suitable UTS candidates from eligible countries for the Kipaji award.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Twente is a technical university in Enschede, the Netherlands, known for engineering, technology and social sciences. It funds international master's students through the University of Twente Scholarship and related schemes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to a UT master's programme and for the University of Twente Scholarship before the deadline, and say in your UTS motivation that you wish to be considered for the Kipaji Scholarship. Your faculty then decides whether to nominate you. Questions go to study@utwente.nl.
opportunities.notes: Check the UTS page for its own conditions and deadline, since Kipaji depends on receiving a UTS.

opportunities.title: NL Scholarship at the University of Twente (master's, 2027/2028)
opportunities.provider: University of Twente with the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Excellent non-EU/EEA students in the top 5-10% of their class (CGPA 7.5/10) admitted to a University of Twente master's starting in 2027/2028 who have not studied in the Netherlands before.
opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship (formerly the Holland Scholarship) is a one-off grant from the Dutch government and Dutch universities for talented students from outside the EU/EEA. At the University of Twente it supports students starting a master's programme in the 2027/2028 academic year.

The grant is EUR 5,000 for the first year only. It is paid to the student as a contribution to study costs rather than being deducted from tuition. Applicants must first apply to a Twente master's and then complete a separate scholarship form between 15 October 2026 and 1 April 2027; results come in the first week of May 2027.

The programme is open to many African countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, Egypt, Morocco, Tanzania and South Africa, but it is very selective: only students in the top 5 to 10 percent of their class qualify.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 5,000 for the first year of study only; no costs such as tuition are paid on the student's behalf.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA nationality
(Provisional) admission to a qualifying University of Twente master's starting in 2027/2028
Cumulative GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and ranking in the top 5-10% of your class
No previous full degree study in the Netherlands and no Dutch degree
Meet the English test requirements of the academic application
Meet Dutch entry visa conditions if applicable
Not eligible for Dutch study finance and not paying the statutory (EU) fee
documents: Student number from the University of Twente master's application
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Twente is a Dutch technical university in Enschede offering English-taught master's programmes in engineering, technology, social sciences and geo-information science.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a University of Twente master's programme first, then submit the NL Scholarship form using your student number before 1 April 2027. Admission decisions can take up to eight weeks, so apply to the programme well before the scholarship deadline.
opportunities.notes: It can be combined with other Twente awards such as the University of Twente Scholarship. Contact: sgw-scholarships-ces@utwente.nl.

opportunities.title: NL Scholarship at the University of Twente 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students, including most Africans, in the top 5-10% of their class and admitted to a Twente master's can apply by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship, formerly known as the Holland Scholarship, is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch universities. At the University of Twente in Enschede it supports excellent students from outside the EU/EEA who start a master's programme in 2027/2028.

The award is a one-off EUR 5,000 for the first year of study, meant to help with study costs rather than to pay tuition. The application form opened on 15 October 2026 and closes at 16:00 CET on 1 April 2027 for programmes starting in September 2027. Results come in the first week of May 2027.

Most African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia, are on the eligible list. Applicants need to be in the top 5-10% of their class and must be provisionally admitted to a master's first.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 5,000 for the first year of study only, as a contribution to study costs (tuition is not paid).

No previous full degree from a Dutch institution
Cumulative GPA of 7.5 out of 10, in the top 5-10% of your graduating class
Provisional admission to a qualifying University of Twente master's
Meet the English requirements of the master's application
Not eligible for Dutch student finance or paying the statutory EU/EEA fee
documents: University of Twente master's application (with student number)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed against the eligibility criteria, especially academic excellence. Results are announced in the first week of May 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Twente is a Dutch public technical university in Enschede, known for engineering, technology and social sciences. It administers the NL Scholarship for its incoming master's students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a University of Twente master's first, allowing up to eight weeks for a provisional admission decision. Then complete the NL Scholarship pre-application form on the university's scholarship finder using your student number before 1 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: Apply for the master's early so you have a student number and provisional admission before the scholarship deadline. Contact sgw-scholarships-ces@utwente.nl.

opportunities.title: Signal Processing Symposium SPSympo 2027 Call for Papers (Warsaw)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and early-career researchers worldwide can submit signal processing papers to SPSympo 2027 in Warsaw by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
SPSympo 2027 is the Signal Processing Symposium organised by Warsaw University of Technology, together with partners and with IEEE technical co-sponsorship, including the IEEE Signal Processing Society Poland Chapter. It will be held at CKA 'Mrówka' in Warsaw, Poland, from 28 to 30 September 2027.

The symposium is designed mainly for students, PhD candidates and early-career researchers, and covers signal processing and related fields such as radar. Authors submit manuscripts of up to six pages by 1 April 2027 and hear the outcome on 31 May 2027.

The event offers African students and young researchers a friendly first international venue for their work. Submissions were not yet open when the page was checked, and no travel support is mentioned.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered to authors. The symposium also runs a Young Scientist Contest.
requirements: Students, PhD candidates and early-career researchers in signal processing or related fields
Manuscript of up to 6 pages including figures
Submission by 1 April 2027
No nationality restriction is stated
documents: Paper manuscript of up to 6 pages
opportunities.selection_process: Submitted manuscripts are reviewed and authors are notified on 31 May 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: SPSympo is organised by Warsaw University of Technology, a leading Polish technical university, with technical co-sponsorship from the IEEE and the IEEE Signal Processing Society Poland Chapter.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare a manuscript of up to six pages and submit it through the paper submission page on the SPSympo website once submissions open, before 1 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: When checked, the call said submissions were not yet open. See the site for the Young Scientist Contest.

opportunities.title: Toronto Metropolitan University Global Migration Institute Scholarships 2027-2028 (Bridging Divides Graduate Stipend)
opportunities.provider: Toronto Metropolitan University, Global Migration Institute
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Domestic and international students admitted to TMU research master's or PhD programmes on migration themes can apply by 1 February (PhD) or 1 April 2027 (master's).
opportunities.description:
The Global Migration Institute at Toronto Metropolitan University (TMU) offers Bridging Divides graduate stipends for full-time master's and PhD students whose research links to one of the four Bridging Divides research themes on migration. Recipients join the institute's team and take part in its research training.

The stipends are for 2027-28 and are open to both domestic and international students. Master's students can receive up to $35,000 a year for up to two years, and PhD students up to $45,000 a year for up to three years. PhD applications close on 1 February 2027 and master's applications on 1 April 2027.

For African graduates interested in migration, displacement, integration or related research, this is a well-funded route into graduate study in Toronto. A limited number of stipends are available, and course-based programmes are not eligible.
opportunities.benefits: Master's: up to $35,000 per year for up to two years (incoming students). PhD: up to $45,000 per year for up to three years. Top-ups may be possible for students holding external grants.
requirements: Admitted to a full-time, research-based TMU master's or PhD programme (course-based programmes are not eligible)
Research topic linked to a Bridging Divides research theme
Open to domestic and international students
FEAS applicants need a named supervisor and an Associate Dean statement
documents: Statement of interest or letter of intent from the TMU application
Bridging Divides motivation letter (up to 2 pages)
Existing PhD students: TMU student ID and a writing sample of up to 10 pages
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on fit with the Bridging Divides themes and the motivation letter. A limited number of stipends are awarded.
opportunities.about_provider: Toronto Metropolitan University is a public university in downtown Toronto, Canada. Its Global Migration Institute hosts the Bridging Divides research programme on migration and inclusion.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to a TMU graduate programme first. Then submit the Bridging Divides online form linked from the Global Migration Institute's scholarships page with your documents by 1 February 2027 (PhD) or 1 April 2027 (master's). Questions go to global.migration@torontomu.ca.
opportunities.notes: The PhD deadline is earlier than the master's deadline. The page writes amounts in dollars without a currency code.

opportunities.title: DL 2027: 40th International Workshop on Description Logics
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit description logic papers to DL 2027 in Amsterdam by 2 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
DL 2027 is the 40th International Workshop on Description Logics, the main annual meeting of the description logic research community. It will be held in person in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, from 8 to 11 July 2027, with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam's Patrick Koopmann as general chair.

The workshop invites regular papers of up to 11 pages and extended abstracts of 2 to 4 pages (excluding references) on description logics, ontologies, knowledge representation and automated reasoning. Abstracts must be registered by 26 March 2027 and papers submitted by 2 April 2027 (anywhere on Earth).

For African researchers and students in AI, logic and the semantic web, DL is a focused venue that welcomes early work. Accepted papers are presented as talks or posters, and at least one author must attend in person. No travel support is mentioned.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered to authors.
requirements: Research on description logics, ontologies or related reasoning topics
Regular papers up to 11 pages or extended abstracts of 2-4 pages, excluding references, in CEURART format
Abstract registration by 26 March 2027 and submission by 2 April 2027
At least one author of each accepted paper attends in person
documents: Paper or extended abstract in the CEURART template, submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed (single-blind by default) and accepted for oral or poster presentation based only on content quality. Notification is on 7 May 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The DL workshop is the yearly event of the international description logic research community. The 2027 edition is organised in Amsterdam with programme chairs from CNRS & ENS and Université Sorbonne Paris Nord.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the CEURART template from the DL 2027 website, register your abstract and submit the paper through the DL 2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=dl2027) by 2 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: Extended abstracts of recently published work are a good low-effort way to present at DL.

opportunities.title: ICTP 3rd Workshop on Dynamics of Tropical and Extratropical Rossby Waves, Compound Extremes and Their Impacts (Jul 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Climate researchers worldwide can apply by 2 April 2027 to the free ICTP workshop on Rossby waves and compound extremes, with grants prioritising developing countries.
opportunities.description:
The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy, will host the 3rd Workshop on Dynamics of Tropical and Extratropical Rossby Waves, Compound Extremes and Their Impacts (smr 4371) from 14 to 16 July 2027. The workshop looks at how compound weather and climate extremes arise, how predictable they are and what impacts they have, through talks and poster sessions.

There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants are available, with priority for participants from developing countries. The application deadline shown is 2 April 2027, but the call had not yet opened when checked.

The workshop follows ICTP's 8th Summer School on climate dynamics (12-23 July 2027), which needs a separate application. For African climate scientists, meteorologists and graduate students, this pairing is a funded route into current research on extremes.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants are available, with priority for participants from developing countries (amounts not stated).
requirements: Researchers and students working on climate dynamics, Rossby waves or compound extremes
Abstract required for those wishing to give a talk or poster
Separate application needed to attend the companion summer school (smr 4370)
No nationality restriction; grant priority for developing countries
documents: Online application through the ICTP e-applications system
Abstract using the ICTP template (for talks or posters)
opportunities.selection_process: The organisers select participants and grant recipients; the page does not give criteria.
opportunities.about_provider: ICTP is an international research centre in Trieste, Italy, governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and Italy, and a UNESCO Category 1 Institute. It runs many schools and workshops for scientists from developing countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Once the call opens, apply through the ICTP e-applications portal for event 4371 and upload an abstract using the template if you want to present. Apply separately to the summer school (smr 4370) if you also wish to attend it. Questions go to smr4371@ictp.it.
opportunities.notes: The call was marked as opening soon when checked. The date is written 02/04/2027 on the page, which ICTP uses as day/month.

opportunities.title: Bocconi4Access to Education: 100% Tuition Waivers for International Bachelor's and Law Students 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students entering the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor's or Law programme in 2027-28 can apply, after enrolling, for a full tuition and fees waiver based on their family's economic situation.
opportunities.description:
Bocconi University in Milan runs the Bocconi4Access to Education scheme to make its degrees affordable for students from families with limited means. For the 2027-28 academic year it offers a waiver of 100% of Bocconi's ordinary tuition and fees to international students starting the first year of a Bachelor's or Law degree. Applicants who do not qualify for the full waiver are automatically considered for one of the university's other benefits.

The waiver is assessed mainly on the family's economic and asset situation under Bocconi's rules, rather than on a single requirement. It is renewable each year as long as the student meets the merit requirements, so it can fund a whole degree.

For African students admitted to Bocconi, this is one of the most valuable awards available in Italy, because it removes tuition entirely at one of Europe's leading business and economics universities. The application is only possible once the student has completed enrolment, so timing matters.
opportunities.benefits: A 100% waiver of Bocconi's ordinary academic tuition and fees, renewable each year if merit requirements are met. Students who miss the full waiver are considered for other partial benefits. The first tuition instalment is paid upfront and refunded by the end of December if the conditions are met.
requirements: International student starting the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor's or Law programme in 2027-28
Assessment of the family's economic and asset situation under Bocconi rules
Must have completed enrolment before applying
Must keep meeting merit requirements to renew each year
documents: Bocconi4Access to Education 2027-28 application in MyApplication
Required documentation on family income and assets (listed on Bocconi's documentation page)
Documents signed by hand, with the signature matching your ID
opportunities.selection_process: Bocconi evaluates the family's economic and asset situation according to its general rules; awards are not decided on any single criterion. Results for the early session come by 25 February 2027 and for the winter session by 27 May 2027. Winners must formally accept the benefit or lose it.
important_dates: Early Session and HEC 1st round: apply 12-30 November 2026, results by 25 February 2027
Winter Session and HEC 2nd round: apply 15 March - 5 April 2027, results by 27 May 2027
HEC 3rd round: 27 May - 4 June 2027, results by 8 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Bocconi University is a private university in Milan, Italy, specialising in economics, management, finance, law and data science. It consistently ranks among Europe's top business schools.
opportunities.how_to_apply: After enrolling at Bocconi, wait about two hours for portal access, then submit a single 'Bocconi4Access to Education a.y. 2027-28' application through MyApplication within your session's window. opportunities.notes: The winner is expected to attend a formal dinner hosted by the donors.

opportunities.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard), FY2027 2nd recruitment
opportunities.provider: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from countries with diplomatic ties to Japan with a PhD from the last six years can be nominated by a Japanese host by 23 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard) lets early-career researchers from abroad spend 12 to 24 months doing joint research with a host researcher at a Japanese university or research institution. It is funded by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and covers every field of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences.

This item is the second recruitment for fiscal year 2027. About 120 fellowships are planned in this round. The host institution must send the application to JSPS by 5 p.m. Japan time on 23 April 2027; because the host applies on the candidate's behalf, its own internal deadline will be earlier. Results are expected in early August 2027, and fellows must arrive in Japan between 1 September and 30 November 2027.

The scheme is open to citizens of any country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, which covers African countries, and is a strong option for recent African PhD holders who want to build research links with Japan.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000; settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000; a round-trip air ticket; and overseas travel insurance. The fellowship lasts 12 to 24 months.
requirements: Citizen of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Japanese citizens and permanent residents cannot apply)
Doctoral degree received within the last six years as of 1 April of the fiscal year, or expected before the fellowship starts (maternity or parental leave is not counted)
Not a previous JSPS Postdoctoral Fellow (Standard) or Pathway fellow
A host researcher who is full-time at an eligible Japanese university or research institution
documents: Application prepared with and submitted by the Japanese host through the JSPS electronic system
Doctoral degree certificate (needed before the fellowship starts)
opportunities.selection_process: Fellows are chosen either through the Open Call, where the Japanese host applies to JSPS, or through nominations from overseas partner organisations. JSPS reviews the applications and announces results in early August 2027.
important_dates: Host institution deadline to JSPS: 23 April 2027, 5 p.m. JST
Arrival in Japan: 1 September to 30 November 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) is Japan's main public agency for funding scientific research and international research exchange. It runs fellowships that bring overseas researchers to Japanese universities and institutes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a host researcher in Japan and agree a joint research plan. The host then applies to JSPS through the JSPS electronic application system before 23 April 2027, so check the host institution's own earlier internal deadline. Questions can be sent to the JSPS postdoctoral fellowship office.
opportunities.notes: The first FY2027 recruitment closed on 28 August 2026. About 120 fellowships are planned for the second recruitment. The application is in the host's hands, so contact potential hosts several months ahead.

opportunities.title: IEEE APCCAS 2027: Asia Pacific Conference on Circuits and Systems
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit circuits and systems papers to IEEE APCCAS 2027 in Hangzhou by 27 April 2027.
opportunities.description:
APCCAS 2027 is the IEEE Asia Pacific Conference on Circuits and Systems, sponsored by the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society, with technical sponsorship from the International Innovation Institute of Beihang University in Hangzhou. It will be held at the Midtown Shangri-La in Hangzhou, China, from 22 to 24 September 2027, and for the first time is co-located with AICAS 2027.

The call covers circuits and systems topics including AI circuits, analogue and mixed-signal design, RF and biomedical circuits. Papers of up to five pages, including references, are reviewed double-blind. The conference website gives the paper deadline as 27 April 2027, with notification on 27 June 2027.

The conference invites work from the Asia-Pacific community and beyond, so African electrical engineers and graduate students can submit. No travel grants are mentioned.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered to authors.
requirements: Original research in circuits and systems
Paper of up to 5 pages including references, IEEE template, US Letter
Submission by 27 April 2027
No nationality restriction is stated
documents: Full paper (up to 5 pages) submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are reviewed double-blind; notification of acceptance is on 27 June 2027.
important_dates: Special session and tutorial proposals: 10 March 2027
Final paper and author registration: 6 August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The IEEE Circuits and Systems Society is the IEEE's professional community for circuit and system design. APCCAS is its flagship regional conference for the Asia-Pacific.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare a paper of up to five pages using the IEEE template and submit it through the APCCAS 2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=apccas2027) by 27 April 2027. Questions go to apccas2027@youngac.cn.
opportunities.notes: No travel grants are mentioned on the call.

opportunities.title: Ajit Singh Janeway Institute Scholarship in Economics 2027 (Queens' College, Cambridge)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality to the Cambridge PhD in Economics with Queens' as first-choice college can apply by 30 April 2027 for a top-up of up to £6,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The Ajit Singh Janeway Institute Scholarship supports one student starting the PhD in Economics at Cambridge in 2027/28 who names Queens' College as their first-choice college. It is offered jointly by Queens' College and the Janeway Institute.

The award runs for three years and can be extended to a fourth with the Janeway Institute's agreement. It pays £6,000 a year, or £3,000 a year if the student already has full funding from elsewhere, and the holder may also be offered up to 40 hours a year of paid supervision teaching.

The scholarship is a top-up rather than full funding, but it is open to students of any nationality, so African economists admitted to the Cambridge PhD can use it alongside other awards.
opportunities.benefits: £6,000 a year for three years (extendable to a fourth), reduced to £3,000 a year if the student is already fully funded. May be used towards Home or International fees. Possible paid supervision work of up to 40 hours a year. One award.
requirements: Applying for the PhD in Economics at Cambridge for 2027/28
Queens' College named as first-choice college
Strong academic record in economics
No nationality restriction
documents: Research proposal of up to four pages
One academic reference, sent by the referee to graduate.office@queens.cam.ac.uk
opportunities.selection_process: Queens' and the Janeway Institute select on academic merit from PhD applicants who complete the separate scholarship form.
opportunities.about_provider: Queens' College is one of the oldest colleges of the University of Cambridge, founded in 1448. The Janeway Institute is Cambridge's centre for research in economics, based in the Faculty of Economics.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for the PhD in Economics through the Cambridge Postgraduate Applicant Portal with Queens' as first-choice college. Then complete the separate online scholarship form by 30 April 2027 at 3 pm, uploading your CV and research proposal and asking your referee to email a reference to the Queens' graduate office.
opportunities.notes: The Cambridge funding search lists 'first or second preference' but the Queens' page and the award text require Queens' as first choice; choose it first to be safe. Queens' also lists other awards for overseas students, such as the Allianz Scholarships for some master's courses (form by 30 April 2027).

For African master's applicants, this is an additional College-level source of money to combine with University or Cambridge Trust funding, whose 2027/28 deadlines fall on 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027.

Member of Queens' College

Cambridge postgraduate application via the Applicant Portal

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your Cambridge master's course through the Applicant Portal, then complete the Queens' College online postgraduate funding form by 3pm on 30 April 2027.

opportunities.title: Boise State Global Broncos Scholarship 2027-28 (continuing international undergraduates)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduates already studying full time at Boise State on an F-1 visa, with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, can apply by 30 April 2027 for a partial non-resident tuition waiver for 2027-28.
opportunities.description:
The Global Broncos Scholarship is a partial waiver of the non-resident part of tuition and fees at Boise State University in Idaho, USA. It is meant for international undergraduates who have already completed at least one full-time semester at Boise State, and it covers one academic year.

The continuing-student application for 2027-28 closes on 30 April 2027 at 5:00 p.m. The waiver is worth between USD 2,400 and USD 9,800, depending on the award, and is not open to new applicants who have not yet enrolled.

For African students already at Boise State, the waiver can make a substantial difference to the cost of a US degree, and it rewards good grades and steady progress.
opportunities.benefits: A waiver of USD 2,400 to USD 9,800 of the non-resident portion of tuition and fees for up to one academic year (2027-28).
requirements: Continuing international undergraduate at Boise State, not already on a full non-resident waiver for 2027-28
At least one semester of full-time study at Boise State (12 credits or more) completed by the end of Spring 2027
F-1 visa status
Cumulative Boise State GPA of at least 3.00
Satisfactory academic progress
Eligible declared major (Nursing, Pre-Nursing, Radiological Science, Pre-Radiological Science, alternative-fee programmes and self-supported or fully online programmes are excluded)
documents: Online application in the Boise State scholarship portal
Essay of 500 words or fewer answering every part of the question
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the essay and the student's academic record. Essays longer than 500 words are not considered.
opportunities.about_provider: Boise State University is a public research university in Boise, Idaho. Its International Student Services office supports F-1 students and manages scholarships for international undergraduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in to Boise State's AcademicWorks scholarship portal, open the Global Broncos continuing-student application and submit your essay before 30 April 2027 at 5:00 p.m.
opportunities.notes: New students cannot apply; this is only for students already enrolled. The same page lists the Trang Doan Memorial Scholarship (USD 300-600, GPA 2.75, same deadline). Contact: internationalinfo@boisestate.edu.

opportunities.title: ERCIM Alain Bensoussan Postdoctoral Fellowship (deadline 30 April 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who earned a PhD within the last eight years (or are finishing an outstanding PhD) can apply for a 12-month postdoc at an ERCIM member institute in a country other than their own.
opportunities.description:
The ERCIM "Alain Bensoussan" Fellowship Programme is the main postdoctoral scheme of the European Research Consortium for Informatics and Mathematics. Each fellowship places a young researcher for twelve months at one of the consortium's member institutes, which include national research centres such as CNR in Italy, CWI in the Netherlands, Fraunhofer in Germany, INESC in Portugal, NTNU in Norway and RISE in Sweden.

The programme runs two application rounds a year, and the next official deadline is 30 April 2027. Fellows work on research topics in computer science, information technology and applied mathematics that the host institutes list for each round, so applicants should check the expertise areas posted for the current round before choosing a host.

The scheme is open to PhD holders of every nationality, which makes it a realistic route into European research for African computer scientists and mathematicians. Its mobility rules mean that a fellow always moves to a new country and a new institution, and it can be held for at most two terms.
opportunities.benefits: Fellows receive a monthly stipend or a working contract from the host. Approximate net monthly amounts given for the latest round are EUR 2,240 at CNR (Italy), EUR 2,625 at CWI (Netherlands), EUR 3,000 at Fraunhofer (Germany), EUR 1,807 at INESC (Portugal, working contract), EUR 4,415 at NTNU (Norway) and EUR 2,925 at RISE (Sweden). Stipends do not include social insurance, so ERCIM pays for a Campus France health insurance. Travel is reimbursed up to EUR 500 per trip for two trips, and fellows can claim up to EUR 100 a month for research exchanges and up to EUR 100 a month for conference attendance when a paper is accepted.
requirements: Open to applicants of any nationality
PhD obtained within the eight years before the round's deadline, or in the final year of a PhD with an outstanding record (proof of the degree needed before the fellowship starts)
Research profile in computer science, information technology or applied mathematics matching a host's listed expertise areas
A host institute cannot take a candidate of its own nationality
You cannot be hosted by an institute where you worked for six months or more in the three years before the deadline
Maximum of two fellowship terms (one reselection)
documents: Detailed CV without sensitive personal data
opportunities.selection_process: Senior scientists from the consortium review each application. They judge the candidate's scientific expertise, the quality of their publications, the relevance of the proposed research agenda, the added value for the consortium and the candidate's earlier mobility and experience.
opportunities.about_provider: ERCIM is a European consortium of leading public research institutes in computer science and applied mathematics. It promotes collaboration between its members and runs the Alain Bensoussan Fellowship as its flagship programme for early-career researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and apply through the ERCIM fellowship online system at fellowship.ercim.eu, choosing a host from the expertise areas listed for the round. Upload your CV, publication list and two papers, and give the contacts of two referees. The application guide on the same site explains each step.
opportunities.notes: Read the round's list of host expertise areas carefully, because applications are matched to hosts. Questions go to the ERCIM fellowship contact listed on the official site.

opportunities.title: IASH Edinburgh Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.provider: Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities (IASH), University of Edinburgh
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the arts, humanities or social sciences who were awarded a doctorate normally within the last three years, hold no permanent post and have secured an Edinburgh mentor can apply for a bursary of up to £20,000.
opportunities.description:
The Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities (IASH) at the University of Edinburgh offers postdoctoral fellowships for early-career scholars in the arts, humanities and social sciences. Fellows spend between three and ten months in Edinburgh, at any time between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028, working on their own research project with an office, full library access and a University of Edinburgh mentor.

The fellowship carries a bursary of up to £20,000, which can be used to cover living costs or to top up another award. Fellows have no teaching duties, although they may take up to a 0.4 post separately. For the 2027-2030 period the institute especially welcomes projects on disability and chronic illness, but this theme is not a requirement.

There is no nationality or residence condition, so African researchers with a recent PhD are eligible. Applicants must contact Edinburgh researchers and secure a mentor before applying. The online portal opened in November 2026 and the closing date is 17:00 GMT on 30 April 2027; decisions are made in July.
opportunities.benefits: A bursary of up to £20,000 (for living costs or to supplement another award), an office at IASH, access to the University of Edinburgh libraries and a University mentor. No teaching is required.
requirements: Doctorate awarded at the time of application, normally within the last three years (exceptions for career breaks)
No permanent university post
No previous IASH fellowship
A mentor at the University of Edinburgh secured before applying and named on the form
A research project in the arts, humanities or social sciences, for a visit of 3 to 10 months between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028
documents: Two academic references (up to three) sent directly to IASH by the deadline; one referee must confirm the PhD viva
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on merit: academic record, publications, and the quality and timeliness of the project. IASH receives hundreds of applications each year; decisions are made in July 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: IASH is the University of Edinburgh's institute for advanced study in the arts, humanities and social sciences, one of the oldest such institutes in the UK. It hosts visiting researchers from around the world, who join an interdisciplinary community of fellows in Edinburgh.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact researchers at the University of Edinburgh and agree a mentor, then complete IASH's online application form with your CV and proposal, and arrange for your referees to email their letters to IASH by 30 April 2027.
opportunities.notes: The 2027-2030 theme (disability and chronic illness) is welcome but optional. IASH also runs separate fellowships for researchers from ODA-recipient countries (British Council 90th Anniversary) and other early-career schemes.

opportunities.title: ICICN 2027: 15th International Conference on Information and Communication Networks
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit original networking papers to ICICN 2027 in Guangzhou by 30 April 2027.

ICICN 2027 is the 15th International Conference on Information and Communication Networks, to be held in Guangzhou, China, from 24 to 27 September 2027. It is hosted by the College of Cyber Security at Jinan University and co-sponsored by the IEEE and the IEEE Photonics Society.

The conference invites original, unpublished research papers on information and communication networks. Papers are reviewed double-blind, and accepted papers appear in the conference proceedings, which are published in IEEE Xplore and indexed by EI Compendex and Scopus. The submission deadline is 30 April 2027.

For African students and researchers in networking, telecommunications, cyber security and related areas, the conference offers an indexed publication and a chance to present at an international venue. No travel grants are mentioned, so authors need their own funding for registration and travel.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered. Submitting an abstract is free, and accepted papers are published in the proceedings (IEEE Xplore, indexed by EI Compendex and Scopus). Registration fees are not stated on the call.
requirements: Original, unpublished work on information and communication networks
Written in English
4 to 10 pages; title of no more than 125 characters
No more than 4 papers per author
No nationality restriction is stated
documents: Full paper of 4 to 10 pages in English, submitted through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Papers go through double-blind peer review by the programme committee.
opportunities.about_provider: ICICN is an annual international conference on communication networks. The 2027 edition is hosted by the College of Cyber Security, Jinan University, in Guangzhou, with co-sponsorship from the IEEE and the IEEE Photonics Society.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare a 4-10 page paper in English that follows the conference rules and submit it through the ICICN 2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=icicn2027) by 30 April 2027. More details are on the conference website icicn.org, and questions go to icicn_conference@163.com.
opportunities.notes: Each author may submit at most four papers. Check the conference website for the notification and camera-ready dates, which the call does not list.

African women and other under-represented applicants admitted to a Cambridge STEM PhD should consider applying through the College's online funding form by 3pm on 30 April 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Fees and subsistence up to the UK home rate for three years (a fourth year possible).

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to your Cambridge PhD through the Applicant Portal (ticking the box to be considered for funding), then submit the Queens' College online postgraduate funding form by 3pm on 30 April 2027.

opportunities.title: Queens' College AI Scholarship (MPhil Advanced Computer Science) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students admitted to Cambridge's MPhil in Advanced Computer Science for October 2027 can apply to Queens' College for a scholarship worth GBP 25,000 towards overseas fees.

African applicants to the MPhil should apply to the course early enough to meet the University funding deadlines, list Queens' as their college if possible, and then submit the College form for this scholarship.

opportunities.title: Southampton GREAT Scholarship 2027 for Nigerian Students
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nigerian passport holders living in Nigeria with an offer for a one-year taught master's in Arts and Humanities, Medicine or Education at Southampton can apply by 30 April 2027 for GBP 10,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The GREAT Scholarship at the University of Southampton takes GBP 10,000 off the tuition fee for Nigerian students joining a one-year, full-time, on-campus taught master's starting in 2027. It is offered jointly with the British Council and the UK government's GREAT Britain campaign, which funds scholarships for students from selected countries to study in the UK.

The award is limited to master's programmes in three parts of the university: the Faculty of Arts and Humanities, the Faculty of Medicine and the Southampton Education School. Study takes place on the Southampton campus in the south of England.

Because it is reserved for Nigerian nationals who live in Nigeria, competition is narrower than for general international awards. Successful applicants are also expected to act as ambassadors for UK higher education and to show how their degree will help build capacity back home.
opportunities.benefits: A GBP 10,000 reduction in the tuition fee for the one-year master's.

Permanently resident in Nigeria (living there for at least three years before the course starts)
Conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible one-year full-time taught master's in Arts and Humanities, Medicine or the Southampton Education School
English language requirements met by the scholarship deadline
Willing to act as an ambassador for UK higher education and explain how the degree will build capacity in Nigeria
documents: Scholarship application form (linked from the official page)
Master's offer from the University of Southampton
Evidence of meeting the English requirement

opportunities.about_provider: The University of Southampton is a research-intensive UK university and a member of the Russell Group. The GREAT Scholarships are a partnership between UK universities, the British Council and the GREAT Britain and Northern Ireland campaign.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for an eligible master's at the University of Southampton and get an offer. Then complete the separate GREAT scholarship application form linked from the official page before 30 April 2027.

opportunities.title: USTB International Student Dingxin Scholarship 2027
opportunities.provider: University of Science and Technology Beijing
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese citizens in good health can apply between 1 November 2026 and 30 April 2027 for full or partial funding of bachelor's, master's or PhD study at USTB, within the age limits for each level.
opportunities.description:
The Dingxin Scholarship is the University of Science and Technology Beijing's own award for international students. It is offered as a full scholarship, covering tuition, campus housing, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance, or as a partial scholarship that covers one or more of those items.

The 2027 call, published on 16 October 2026, accepts applications from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027 for undergraduate (four years), master's (two to three years) and doctoral (four years) programmes starting in September 2027. Awards are reviewed every year and the study period cannot normally be extended.

USTB is one of China's leading universities for materials, metallurgy, mining, engineering and computer science, so the award is a strong option for African students in these fields. Graduate applicants are advised to apply first for the Chinese Government Scholarship High-Level Postgraduate Program at USTB, which can also lead to Dingxin consideration.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition, on-campus accommodation, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance. Partial scholarship: one or several of these items. The monthly allowance amount is not published in the notice.

Good health
Bachelor's applicants: high-school graduate under 30
Master's applicants: bachelor's degree holder under 40
PhD applicants: master's degree holder under 45
Annual review of the scholarship
documents: Application materials listed in USTB's materials guide (uploaded in the portal)
Payment of the non-refundable application fee

Check the materials guide at isc.ustb.edu.cn for the list of documents for your level.
opportunities.notes: Graduate applicants are encouraged to apply first to the CSC High-Level Postgraduate Program at USTB. The application fee is non-refundable.

opportunities.title: University of Galway Business International Postgraduate Scholarships (September 2027)
opportunities.provider: University of Galway (J.E. Cairnes School of Business & Economics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU fee-paying applicants with an H1 (first-class) or equivalent primary degree who apply for an eligible full-time taught Master's at Galway's Cairnes School of Business & Economics for September 2027.
opportunities.description:
The J.E. Cairnes School of Business & Economics at the University of Galway offers two merit scholarships to international (non-EU) students who start one of its full-time taught Master's programmes in September 2027. The International Postgraduate Merit Scholarship is worth €4,000 and the International Postgraduate Excellence Scholarship is worth €10,000; both are applied as reductions of the tuition fee rather than paid in cash.

There is no separate scholarship form. Every complete application for an eligible Master's is considered automatically, and the award depends on the strength of your first degree: a result of 70% to 89.99% (H1 level or international equivalent) is the band for the €4,000 award, while 90% or above is the band for the €10,000 award. The school also weighs its recruitment priorities across programmes, and places are limited.

The awards run in two rounds. Applications completed by 15 December 2026 are in the early round, with decisions by mid-January 2027; the main round closes on 30 April 2027, with decisions made on a rolling basis from May 2027. African graduates with top grades who are classed as non-EU fee payers can therefore cut a large part of their Galway business Master's fees by applying early.
opportunities.benefits: Either a €4,000 International Postgraduate Merit Scholarship (degree result 70% to 89.99%) or a €10,000 International Postgraduate Excellence Scholarship (90% or above), given as a tuition fee reduction.
requirements: Assessed as a non-EU applicant for fee purposes
Primary degree at H1 honours (first-class) or international equivalent or above
Degree result of 70% to 89.99% for the €4,000 award, or 90% or above for the €10,000 award
A complete application for an eligible full-time taught Master's at the Cairnes School for September 2027
An offer of a place (the scholarship decision follows the offer)
documents: A complete Master's application through the university's online portal (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are considered automatically once their programme application is complete. Awards are based on academic merit and the school's recruitment priorities; places are limited and competitive. Successful applicants are told by email after receiving an offer and have 10 business days to accept the offer and pay the deposit.
important_dates: Early round deadline: 15 December 2026 (decisions by mid-January 2027)
Main round deadline: 30 April 2027 (rolling decisions from May 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Galway is a public research university on Ireland's west coast. Its J.E. Cairnes School of Business & Economics runs a range of full-time taught Master's programmes in business, economics and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible full-time taught Master's at the Cairnes School through the University of Galway's online application portal and make sure the application is complete. You are then considered for both scholarships automatically; if successful you are notified by email after your offer.
opportunities.notes: Apply by 15 December 2026 to be in the early round. You do not need to accept your offer or pay a deposit before the scholarship decision. Check the school's list of eligible programmes.

opportunities.title: University of Regina International Student of Distinction Scholarship (Tier 1, Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students applying straight from high school to a University of Regina undergraduate degree for Fall 2027 with an average of at least 90% can be considered for Tier 1 housing and meal-plan support.
opportunities.description:
The International Student of Distinction Scholarship is the University of Regina's top entrance award for new international undergraduates. Instead of a tuition credit, it pays for life on campus: Tier 1 covers on-campus housing and a meal plan, worth about CAD 22,500 a year and around CAD 90,000 over four years.

The university has posted that Tier 1 places for the Winter 2027 and Spring/Summer 2027 intakes are already filled, so new applicants should aim for the Fall 2027 intake. The lower Tier 2 award, which covered housing only for students with averages of 85 to 89.99%, has been suspended for the 2027 academic year until further notice.

The award suits strong African secondary-school graduates who want to study in Saskatchewan, Canada, and who need help with the cost of living. It can be renewed for up to three further years (three and a half for Engineering) if the student keeps a full course load and good grades.
opportunities.benefits: Tier 1: on-campus housing plus a meal plan, valued at about CAD 22,500 a year (approximately CAD 90,000 over four years). It is not a tuition credit, so tuition must still be paid. Tier 2 (housing only, about CAD 11,250 a year) is suspended for 2027.

Fall 2027 intake (Winter and Spring/Summer 2027 places are filled)
Early conditional or final high-school average of at least 90% (converted) for Tier 1
Complete admission application and all supporting documents by 30 April 2027
Renewal: at least 24 credit hours per calendar year and a minimum university average of 80%
documents: Completed University of Regina undergraduate admission application
All supporting admission documents (transcripts and other items required for admission)
opportunities.selection_process: Students are considered on the basis of their converted high-school average once the admission application and supporting documents are complete. Places are limited and are filled intake by intake, so early, complete applications have the best chance.
important_dates: Fall 2027 application and documents deadline: 30 April 2027
Winter and Spring/Summer 2027 Tier 1 places: filled
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Regina is a public comprehensive university in Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada. Its UR International office supports international recruitment, admission and student services, and manages the university's international entrance awards.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission through the University of Regina online application and submit every required supporting document by 30 April 2027 for Fall 2027. There is no separate essay; eligible students are considered through the admission file. Then complete the housing application by 15 June.
opportunities.notes: The same page lists automatic awards for international undergraduates: an International Entrance Scholarship of CAD 12,000 over four years for averages of 83% or more, and an International Undergraduate Student Bursary of CAD 20,000 over four years for students who deposit two years of tuition before their study permit application. Contact: International.Recruitment@uregina.ca.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Entry Scholarship for Outstanding Academic Applicants (International Undergraduates, 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduate applicants whose results exceed XJTLU's entry requirements and who are offer-ready by a round deadline (final round 30 April 2027) can receive up to 50% off tuition each year.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) in Suzhou, China, rewards strong international undergraduate applicants with an Entry Scholarship for Outstanding Academic Applicants worth up to 50% of tuition each year. International tuition is RMB 99,000 a year, so the top award is worth about RMB 49,500 annually.

The scholarship is merit-based and renewable each year if the student keeps up strong academic results. A Scholarship Panel meets several times during the admissions cycle, and applications are judged in five rounds between November 2026 and April 2027.

XJTLU teaches in English and awards University of Liverpool degrees alongside its Chinese degree, which makes it attractive for African students who want a UK-linked degree at a lower cost in a major Chinese city.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 50% of the tuition fee per year (international tuition is RMB 99,000 a year), renewable annually with strong academic performance. A separate 10% Early Bird tuition discount applies to applications, offers and deposits completed by 31 March 2027.
requirements: International undergraduate applicant
Academic results that exceed the standard entry requirements
Offer-ready (enough documents for a conditional or unconditional offer) by the round deadline
Applicants not offer-ready for a round cannot be reconsidered later in the year
documents: Academic transcripts (originals with English translations; final-year transcript can follow)
English test certificates if already taken
Online programme application with the Entry Scholarship section completed
opportunities.selection_process: A Scholarship Panel assesses applicants on academic merit at meetings held throughout the admissions year, round by round.
opportunities.about_provider: XJTLU is an international joint-venture university founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool, based in Suzhou near Shanghai. It teaches in English and its graduates receive a University of Liverpool degree.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for your undergraduate programme at xjtlu.edu.cn/en/apply and indicate your interest in the XJTLU Entry Scholarship in the relevant section. Upload enough documents to be offer-ready before the round deadline you are aiming for.
opportunities.notes: Late applications after 30 April 2027 are not considered. Applying in an early round gives more chances, as the panel meets through the year. XJTLU also lists master's and research scholarships.

opportunities.title: THUAS World Citizen Talent Scholarship for Master's Students 2027
opportunities.provider: The Hague University of Applied Sciences
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants from outside the Netherlands who are conditionally admitted to one of three THUAS master's programmes and have IELTS Academic 7.0 can compete with an essay, due 1 May 2027, for one of three EUR 5,000 awards.
opportunities.description:
The World Citizen Talent Scholarship is a one-time award of EUR 5,000 from The Hague University of Applied Sciences (THUAS). Up to three are given each year to international students starting a THUAS master's programme.

Only three programmes qualify: the Master in Business Administration, the Master in Financial Management & Control and the Master in International Communication Management. Candidates compete by writing an English essay of 600 to 800 words about being part of an international, multicultural community, and the deadline for the 2027 round is 1 May 2027.

The award is open to people from any country outside the Netherlands, including all African countries, and winners are expected to act as ambassadors for their programme during their studies in The Hague.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time scholarship of EUR 5,000. Up to three are awarded each year.
requirements: From outside the Netherlands and not living in the Netherlands
Enrolling for the first time in one of the three eligible THUAS master's programmes (Business Administration, Financial Management & Control, International Communication Management)
Conditionally accepted to the programme for the coming academic year
IELTS Academic overall score of at least 7.0
Has never applied for this scholarship before
documents: English essay of 600 to 800 words on being part of an international, multicultural community
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reads all essays and chooses the three best. AI tools may not be used to write the essay, and the jury's decision is final. Winners must be conditionally admitted and meet all enrolment conditions.
opportunities.about_provider: The Hague University of Applied Sciences is a Dutch university of applied sciences with a strongly international student body. It offers bachelor's and master's programmes taught in English with a practical, professional focus.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for one of the three eligible master's programmes through THUAS's online application tool. Then write the essay and submit it through the form linked on the official scholarships page before 1 May 2027.
opportunities.notes: Read the scholarship regulations PDF linked on the page. THUAS also offers NL Scholarships for five other master's programmes, listed on its study finance page.

opportunities.title: TRANSCODE 2027: The Science and Development of Transport
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Transport and logistics researchers worldwide can submit papers to TRANSCODE 2027 in Zagreb by 1 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
TRANSCODE 2027, 'The Science and Development of Transport', is an international scientific conference organised by the Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences of the University of Zagreb, with TU Dresden's Faculty of Transport 'Friedrich List' and the UNF Crowley Center. It will be held at Hotel International in Zagreb, Croatia, on 9 and 10 December 2027.

The conference covers transport, logistics, mobility and the use of AI in transport, and draws participants from more than 20 countries. Papers are submitted through EasyChair by 1 May 2027.

For African transport engineers, planners and logistics researchers, TRANSCODE is a European venue to present work and meet partners. The call does not offer funding, and registration fees are listed on the conference site.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is offered to authors. Early-payment discounts on registration are listed on the conference site.
requirements: Research on transport, logistics, mobility or related topics
Submission by 1 May 2027 through EasyChair
Open to researchers, academics and industry practitioners; no nationality restriction is stated
