opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the guidelines on transcode.fpz.hr and submit your paper through the TRANSCODE 2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=transcode2027) by 1 May 2027. Questions go to transcode@fpz.unizg.hr.
opportunities.notes: No travel grants are mentioned on the call.

opportunities.title: Wageningen NL Scholarship MSc 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: South African and other listed-country students with a GPA of 80% admitted to a WUR MSc can apply for EUR 5,000 awards by 1 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
Wageningen University & Research (WUR) awards the NL Scholarship, funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and Dutch universities, to international students starting an on-campus MSc in September 2027 or February 2028. Each award is EUR 5,000, and a student can receive up to three (EUR 15,000 in total). Eight scholarships are available.

The scholarship is limited to nationals of a set list of countries. South Africa is the only African country on the list, alongside countries such as India, Japan, Mexico, Vietnam and the United States. Applicants need a GPA of 80% or higher and admission to an eligible WUR master's, and must not have studied in a Dutch degree programme before.

Eligible admitted students are invited to apply, with invitations sent weekly from 1 February 2027, and the scholarship application must be in before 1 May 2027. African applicants from other countries should look at WUR's Africa Scholarship Programme and Anne van den Ban Fund instead.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 5,000 per NL Scholarship; a student may receive one to three awards (EUR 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000). It is a partial award and cannot be used to meet WUR's payment requirements. Eight scholarships are available.
requirements: Nationality from WUR's eligible list (South Africa is the only African country)
GPA of 80% or higher
Conditional or unconditional admission to an eligible on-campus WUR MSc (not online or double-degree)
No previous study in a Dutch degree programme
No EU/EEA dual nationality
opportunities.selection_process: Eligible admitted candidates receive an invitation to apply; the scholarship committee then reviews applications.
important_dates: WUR invoice payment: 1 July 2027 (September intake) or 1 December 2027 (February intake)
opportunities.about_provider: Wageningen University & Research is a Dutch public university in Wageningen focused on life sciences, agriculture, food and the environment. Its scholarship committee coordinates the awards it offers to master's students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible WUR master's through the university's admissions process. If you are eligible, WUR will invite you to apply for the NL Scholarship; submit that application before 1 May 2027, after which applications are no longer possible.
opportunities.notes: WUR's Africa Scholarship Programme and Anne van den Ban Fund are open to more African nationalities but require the MSc application before 1 December 2026.

opportunities.title: Jönköping University Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying applicants of any nationality to Jönköping University on-campus programmes starting autumn 2027 can apply by 2 May 2027 for a 10-30% tuition reduction.
opportunities.description:
Jönköping University (JU) in Sweden offers a limited number of merit scholarships to fee-paying students starting an on-campus bachelor's or master's programme in autumn 2027. Each award reduces tuition by 10% to 30%.

The scholarship application is open from 16 October 2026 to 2 May 2027, and awards are announced by 5 May. Selection is on academic merit with an emphasis on excellence. You do not need an admission offer to apply, only a completed programme application, and you apply through JU's online scholarship form with a short statement and a recommendation letter.

All citizens of countries required to pay tuition in Sweden, which includes every African country, may apply. Living and travel costs are not covered, so the scholarship is best combined with other funds.
opportunities.benefits: A reduction of 10% to 30% of the programme's tuition fee. Living and travel costs are not covered. Number of awards limited and not stated.
requirements: Citizen of a country required to pay tuition fees in Sweden (residence there not required)
Required to pay tuition at JU
Applied to an on-campus bachelor's or master's programme starting autumn 2027 by the scholarship deadline
Cannot be combined with FIDERH, FUNED or COLFUTURO awards
documents: One English reference letter of no more than one page (up to two allowed)
Personal statement of no more than 200 words about education and career plans

opportunities.about_provider: Jönköping University is a foundation university in Jönköping, southern Sweden, with schools of business, engineering, health and education, and a large share of international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First complete your programme application for autumn 2027. Then fill in JU's online scholarship form (using the same email address) with your application number, reference letter and statement before 2 May 2027. Confirm acceptance if you are awarded.
opportunities.notes: If you already paid tuition before 5 May, the award is deducted from the second instalment.

opportunities.title: Loughborough-Ferguson Trust African Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Africa-domiciled offer holders with first-class records for a one-year Loughborough master's starting September 2027 can apply by 3 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Loughborough-Ferguson Trust African Scholarship supports students who live in Africa and want to take a one-year taught master's at Loughborough University in September 2027, at either the Loughborough or London campus. It is funded by a mix of external donations and university funds.

The award pays 100% of course fees for one year, replacing any other departmental or university scholarship, and the award page also mentions help with living expenses. The deadline is 3 May 2027, and applicants are told the outcome by 1 July 2027.

The standard is very high: candidates normally have first-class honours and must show a commitment to return home and contribute to their country's development. Only a limited number of awards are made, so it suits exceptional African graduates with a clear plan for impact.
opportunities.benefits: 100% of tuition fees for one year (replacing any other Loughborough scholarship). The award page also refers to living expenses, but the general terms say awards are applied as a fee reduction with no cash alternative, so confirm the living-cost element with the university.

Conditional or unconditional Loughborough offer for a one-year taught master's starting September 2027
Commitment to return home and contribute to your country after the course
Cannot be combined with any other Loughborough award
documents: Scholarship application form (on the official page)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on exceptional academic achievement, their commitment to return and contribute to their home country, their understanding of UK study and living costs, and their motivation. A limited number of awards are made to a very high standard.
opportunities.about_provider: Loughborough University is a public research university in Loughborough, England, with a second campus in London. It is known for engineering, sport science, design and business.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Secure an offer for an eligible one-year master's at Loughborough first. Then complete the application form on the scholarship page before 3 May 2027. Contact global.engagement@mailbox.lboro.ac.uk with questions.

opportunities.title: ECSQARU 2027: European Conference on Reasoning with Uncertainty
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit papers on reasoning with uncertainty to ECSQARU 2027 in Palermo by 10 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
ECSQARU 2027 is the 19th European Conference on Symbolic and Quantitative Approaches to Reasoning with Uncertainty. It will be held at the Sala delle Capriate in the Steri complex in Palermo, Italy, from 8 to 10 September 2027, hosted by the University of Palermo with proceedings in Springer's LNAI series.

The single-track conference covers reasoning under uncertainty in AI, including probability, belief functions, logic and decision making, with three keynote talks. One of the two programme chairs, Nahla Ben Amor, is from the University of Tunis. Abstracts must be registered by 3 May 2027 and full papers submitted by 10 May 2027; the submission system opens on 4 January 2027.

Two best paper awards of EUR 500 are offered, one reserved for a young researcher. For African AI and statistics researchers, it is an established venue with a strong North African link.
opportunities.benefits: No travel funding. Two Best Paper Awards of EUR 500 each (one for a young researcher), supported by Springer. Proceedings in Springer LNAI.
requirements: Original paper not under review elsewhere
Up to 12 pages excluding references, in Springer LNCS/LNAI format
Abstract registration by 3 May 2027 and paper by 10 May 2027
At least one author registers and attends
documents: Abstract registration and full paper in Springer LNCS/LNAI format through EasyChair
opportunities.selection_process: Single-blind peer review on originality, significance, technical soundness and clarity.
opportunities.about_provider: ECSQARU is a long-running European conference series on reasoning with uncertainty. The 2027 edition is hosted by the University of Palermo with support from Springer.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register your abstract by 3 May 2027 and upload the full paper through the ECSQARU 2027 EasyChair page (easychair.org/conferences/?conf=ecsqaru2027) by 10 May 2027, using the Springer LaTeX template.
opportunities.notes: Abstract registration is mandatory before the paper deadline.

opportunities.title: Ryukoku University Numata Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students of any nationality studying Buddhism at Ryukoku University can apply; new September 2027 entrants apply 15 April to 13 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Numata Scholarship at Ryukoku University in Kyoto, Japan, supports international students who study, or want to study, Buddhism there. It was established by Dr Yehan Numata, founder of the Mitutoyo company and the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (BDK).

Undergraduates receive ¥80,000 a month and graduate students ¥100,000 a month for up to 12 months; students who start in September receive six months. Students continuing beyond a year may reapply.

People from anywhere, including Africa, can apply if they enrol at Ryukoku (as regular or exchange students) to study Buddhism and do not hold another major scholarship. The next window for new students starting in September 2027 is 15 April to 13 May 2027.
opportunities.benefits: ¥80,000 a month (undergraduate) or ¥100,000 a month (graduate) for up to 12 months; September starters receive six months. A select number of awards.

Good academic record
Hold or obtain a Japanese student visa
Not receiving another major scholarship
Likely to finish within the normal study period
documents: Recommendation letter on the set form from a full-time Ryukoku faculty member
Academic transcript (not needed for newly admitted students)
Three research papers (only for second-year and later research students)

important_dates: September 2027 entry, prospective students: 15 April to 13 May 2027 (results early July 2027)
April 2027 entry, current students: 1 March to 2 April 2027
September 2027 entry, current students: 2 August to 2 September 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Ryukoku University is a private university in Kyoto founded in 1639 by the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji school of Buddhism, and is one of Japan's main centres for Buddhist studies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the forms from the official page, get a recommendation from a full-time Ryukoku faculty member, and post or hand-deliver the documents to Ryukoku's Center for the Promotion of Global Education so that they arrive within the application window.
opportunities.notes: Holders must submit their grades and a 10-page study report at the end; graduate students also need a supervisor's report.

opportunities.title: IEEE MMSP 2027 Call for Papers (Klagenfurt)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality can submit multimedia signal processing papers for MMSP 2027 in Klagenfurt by 14 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
MMSP 2027 is the 29th edition of the IEEE International Workshop on Multimedia Signal Processing, a yearly meeting of researchers who work on how images, video, audio and other media are captured, coded, analysed and delivered. The 2027 workshop will be held in Klagenfurt, Austria, over three days from 6 to 8 October 2027.

The organisers are inviting research papers for the workshop programme. Papers have to be in by 14 May 2027, and authors will hear whether their work has been accepted on 16 June 2027. Presenting at an IEEE workshop gives early-career researchers a chance to show their results to an international audience and to have them reviewed by specialists in the field.

The call is relevant to African master's students, doctoral candidates, postdocs and engineers working on multimedia, signal processing, computer vision, audio or communications. The official site does not list travel grants, fee waivers or other funding, so authors should plan to cover registration and travel from their own or institutional budgets.
opportunities.benefits: No funding is listed. Accepted authors get to present their paper at the workshop in Klagenfurt, Austria (6-8 October 2027).
requirements: Original research in multimedia signal processing or a related area
Paper submitted by 14 May 2027
At least one author able to attend the workshop in Klagenfurt, 6-8 October 2027
No nationality restriction is stated on the official site
documents: Full conference paper submitted by the 14 May 2027 deadline
opportunities.selection_process: Submitted papers are reviewed by the workshop's programme committee, and authors are told the outcome on 16 June 2027.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the important-dates and author pages on the MMSP 2027 website and prepare a paper on a multimedia signal processing topic. Submit it by 14 May 2027 through the submission link the organisers publish on the site; the site does not yet show the portal, and questions can be sent through its contact form.
opportunities.notes: The workshop's call-for-papers page currently shows an older special-session text, so rely on the important-dates page for the 2027 schedule. No travel grants are mentioned.

opportunities.title: Africa Development Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Sub-Saharan African offer holders for a one-year Leicester Master's starting September 2027 with a 2:1 or better can apply between 1 February and 21 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Africa Development Scholarship is a University of Leicester award that pays the full tuition fees of a one-year taught Master's degree for students from Sub-Saharan Africa. Two awards are planned for September 2027 entry: one for a student from East or Southern Africa and one for a student from West Africa.

The scholarship reflects the university's stated commitment to education and development in Sub-Saharan Africa. It is meant for applicants who can show how they have helped their communities and how they will use their studies to tackle local challenges. The award covers tuition only, so winners must be able to pay for their living costs, accommodation and visa themselves.

Applications open on 1 February 2027 and close at 11.59pm UK time on 21 May 2027. Shortlisted candidates hear by 31 May 2027, must prove they have the money for living costs by 14 June 2027, and all applicants are told the result by 28 June 2027.
opportunities.benefits: A full tuition fee waiver for a one-year, full-time, campus-based Master's starting in September 2027. Two awards: one for East or Southern Africa, one for West Africa. Living costs, accommodation and visa costs are not covered.
requirements: Permanent resident and passport holder of a Sub-Saharan African country
International fee status
Offer for a full-time, campus-based one-year Master's at Leicester starting September 2027
2:1 or first-class bachelor's degree, or equivalent
PGCE, postgraduate certificate and postgraduate diploma courses are not eligible
Cannot be combined with other Leicester scholarships or discounts unless stated; deferring the place cancels the award
documents: Essay of about 500 words on the challenges your community faces and your past contributions
Proof of funds for living costs, accommodation and visa, in UKVI-format bank statements (shortlisted applicants)

opportunities.about_provider: The University of Leicester is a public research university in the city of Leicester in the English Midlands. It offers a wide range of taught and research postgraduate programmes and runs several scholarships for international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First apply for and secure an offer on an eligible one-year Master's at Leicester. Between 1 February and 21 May 2027, complete the scholarship application form on the official page, including the 500-word essay. If shortlisted, send proof of funds by 14 June 2027.
opportunities.notes: Only two awards are made, so a strong essay showing real community impact matters. Make sure you can fund your living costs, because the award pays tuition only.

opportunities.title: University of Wollongong 2028 Main Round HDR Scholarships (international round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants for a UOW PhD or MPhil starting Autumn 2028 can be considered for main-round scholarships by applying by 23 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Wollongong (UOW) in New South Wales, Australia, runs a yearly Main Round in which applicants for research degrees (PhD and Master of Philosophy) are considered for stipend and tuition scholarships. The 2028 Main Round is for candidates starting in Autumn 2028, and UOW says international applications are open now and close on 23 May 2027.

UOW's scholarships page names the Australian Government Research Training Program (AGRTP) and the University Postgraduate Award (UPA) as the round's awards. The AGRTP page, however, says AGRTP itself is only for Australian and New Zealand citizens and permanent residents, so international applicants should expect to be considered for university-funded awards such as the UPA. The value and terms of the UPA were not confirmed on the pages read.

For African researchers, the round is a way to apply for a funded research degree in Australia well ahead of the 2028 start. International outcomes are expected in mid-August 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend and tuition scholarships for research degree candidates. For reference, the AGRTP stipend for 2027 is AUD 38,420 a year, tax-free for full-time candidates and indexed each year, for 3.5 years (PhD) or 2 years (MPhil); AGRTP is for domestic candidates only. The value of the UPA for international candidates is not stated on the pages read.
requirements: Applying for a PhD or Master of Philosophy at UOW starting in Autumn 2028
International applicants: apply by 23 May 2027
AGRTP is limited to Australian and New Zealand citizens and Australian permanent residents
Meet UOW's admission requirements for the chosen research degree
documents: Research degree application through UOW Apply Online (scholarship consideration is part of the degree application)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates are considered for scholarships as part of the research degree application in the Main Round. International outcomes are released in mid-August 2027.

opportunities.title: REMHU 2027 Dossier: Contemporary African Diasporas (call for papers)
opportunities.provider: REMHU, Centro Scalabriniano de Estudos Migratórios (CSEM)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers anywhere, and especially in Africa and the Global South, can submit empirical articles on African diasporas until 31 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
REMHU, the Interdisciplinary Journal of Human Mobility, is inviting articles for its 2027 dossier "Contemporary African diasporas: transnational mobility and relationalities", to appear in volume 35. The dossier is edited by Andréa Lobo of the University of Brasília and Claudio Furtado of the University of Cabo Verde, and submissions are accepted on a rolling basis between 1 October 2026 and 31 May 2027.

The editors want original empirical research, for example ethnography, demographic data or historical work, on topics such as African transnational families, the mobility of children, care work, transnational marriages, masculinities, ageing and migration within Africa. They say they especially welcome work by researchers based in Africa and the wider Global South.

The journal is published by the Scalabrinian Centre for Migration Studies in Brazil and is indexed in SciELO, Redalyc, DOAJ and Scopus, so a paper here gives African migration scholars an indexed, open-access outlet.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of a peer-reviewed article in an indexed open-access migration journal. The call page does not mention a publication fee or any payment to authors.
requirements: Original empirical research on contemporary African diasporas and transnational mobility
Articles may be written in Portuguese, English, Spanish, French or Italian
Submission between 1 October 2026 and 31 May 2027
Work must not be published elsewhere
documents: Article manuscript prepared to the journal's submission guidelines
Submission through the journal's online system
opportunities.selection_process: Articles submitted to the dossier go through the journal's editorial and peer-review process, coordinated by the dossier editors.
opportunities.about_provider: REMHU (Revista Interdisciplinar da Mobilidade Humana) is published by the Centro Scalabriniano de Estudos Migratórios in Brasília, Brazil. It is indexed in SciELO, Redalyc, DOAJ and Scopus and holds a Qualis A1 rating.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare your article following REMHU's guidelines and submit it through the journal's online submission page, indicating that it is for the African diasporas dossier. Submissions are accepted until 31 May 2027.
opportunities.notes: The same call also includes a second 2027 dossier on migration policy and legislation, open until 30 April 2027.

opportunities.title: University of Nottingham Ningbo China Global Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time international students of any nationality with a UNNC offer for 2027 can apply by 31 May 2027 for a 100% or 50% first-year tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
UNNC offers competitive first-year tuition scholarships to full-time international students who hold an offer for 2027 entry. There are two tiers: the Provost International Excellence 100% Scholarship, which covers the whole of the first year's tuition, and the Emerging Leaders 50% Scholarship, which covers half.

The awards exist for both undergraduate and taught postgraduate students. On two-year master's courses the award still covers the first year only. Undergraduate candidates are judged mainly on their predicted grades (A-level, IB or high-school results) and postgraduates on their university GPA; English ability is not part of the selection.

Because UNNC teaches in English and awards a British university degree in China, the scholarships are an affordable route for African students to a UK qualification in Asia. No nationality is excluded.

opportunities.selection_process: Awards are competitive. Undergraduate applicants are ranked mainly on predicted grades and postgraduate applicants on their university GPA, with the statement on wider contribution also considered. English ability is not used in selection.

opportunities.title: Hagan International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens aged 24 or under who have never studied in the US, hold a foreign bachelor's and are starting a first graduate degree at a US institution in Fall 2027 with substantial financial need can receive up to USD 30,000.
opportunities.description:
The Hagan International Scholarship is a need- and merit-based award from the Hagan Scholarship Foundation for international students starting their first graduate degree in the United States. For the 2027-2028 academic year it supports students who are not US citizens and who have never studied in the US, beginning graduate study in Fall 2027.

The scholarship pays up to USD 7,500 per semester, with a maximum of USD 30,000, for up to four consecutive fall and spring semesters. It is limited to tuition, required fees, books and supplies, after subtracting other free financial aid. Recipients also attend a free workshop on investing and retirement planning, and there is no application fee.

For African graduates with strong results and real financial need, this is one of the few private US awards that is open to students who have never been in the US. Applications open on 15 January 2027, and applicants need an acceptance letter and a graduation plan approved by their US department.

opportunities.title: IEEE BDAI 2027: 10th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (call for papers)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers and students from any country can submit original big data and AI papers by 1 June 2027.
opportunities.description:
The 2027 IEEE 10th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI 2027) will take place at Chongqing University in Chongqing, China, from 15 to 17 October 2027. The conference invites original research papers on big data and AI, and accepted full papers are published in conference proceedings; authors can also submit an abstract to present without publication.

BDAI is sponsored by Chongqing University. Its site notes that the 2026 edition was on IEEE's conference list with proceedings in IEEE Xplore indexed by Scopus.

The call is open to researchers from any country, so it is a chance for African students and researchers in data science and AI to publish and present at an international IEEE-linked venue.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted full papers in the conference proceedings and the chance to present in Chongqing. The call does not offer travel funding; papers longer than six pages pay an extra page charge at registration.

Full paper of 4 to 10 pages (5-6 recommended) in IEEE format, or an abstract for presentation only
At least one author registers by the registration deadline
documents: Paper in the IEEE Word template (PDF)
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are screened by the technical programme committee and then peer reviewed by external reviewers; the programme chair makes the final decision.
opportunities.about_provider: BDAI is an annual international conference on big data and artificial intelligence sponsored by Chongqing University in China. Its conference secretary can be reached through the contact details on the conference website.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Format your paper with the IEEE template and upload it as a PDF through the BDAI 2027 EasyChair submission site by 1 June 2027, choosing full paper or abstract-only presentation.

opportunities.title: RGU International Merit-Based Scholarship for Master's Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funding international students with first-class-equivalent degrees and an offer for a September 2027 RGU master's can apply by 1 June 2027.
opportunities.description:
Robert Gordon University in Aberdeen, Scotland, offers an International Merit-Based Scholarship worth £8,000 off postgraduate tuition fees for outstanding self-funding international students starting a full-time, on-campus master's degree in September 2027. Applications are open now and close on 1 June 2027.

The award is a fee discount rather than a cash stipend, and it is open to students from every country of residence and in every subject area. Only three scholarships are available, so competition is strong and applicants need first-class results.

For African graduates with top grades who plan to fund their own UK master's, the scholarship can cut the tuition bill substantially.
opportunities.benefits: An £8,000 discount on postgraduate tuition fees (reduced by the value of any other RGU scholarship the student holds). Three awards are available.
requirements: Self-funding international fee-paying student
Open to all countries of residence and all subjects
Equivalent of a UK first-class honours undergraduate degree
An offer for a full-time, on-campus postgraduate place starting September 2027
Must meet the offer's conditions before its deadline
documents: RGU offer for a September 2027 postgraduate programme
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic merit to applicants who meet the criteria; the page does not describe further stages.
opportunities.about_provider: Robert Gordon University (RGU) is a university in Aberdeen, Scotland, and a registered Scottish charity (SC013781). Its international team handles scholarship questions at international@rgu.ac.uk.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an RGU master's programme starting in September 2027, then complete the online scholarship application form before 1 June 2027. Questions can be sent to international@rgu.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Only three awards are offered, so apply early.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Master's Entry Scholarship (September 2027 intake)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to full-time taught master's or MRes programmes at XJTLU who request scholarship consideration when they apply.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University in Suzhou offers merit-based Master's Entry Scholarships to new full-time taught master's and MRes students. Awards cut 20%, 30% or 50% off total tuition, and a few applicants to 13 named MRes programmes (such as MRes Computer Science, Bioinformatics and Management) can receive a full tuition waiver.

For the September 2027 intake the scholarship deadline is 1 June 2027. A panel reviews applications in January, March, May and July, so applying early improves the chances while funds remain.

International applicants, including Africans, can apply. XJTLU awards UK-recognised degrees from the University of Liverpool alongside its own, which makes it a popular English-medium option in China.
opportunities.benefits: A tuition reduction of 20%, 30% or 50% of total tuition; full tuition waiver for a few applicants to 13 listed MRes programmes. Tuition for 2026 entry ranges, for example, from RMB 150,000 (MSc Actuarial Science) to RMB 320,000 (International MBA).
requirements: Applying to a full-time taught master's or MRes at XJTLU (part-time study not eligible)
Meets the programme's entry requirements
Indicates interest in the scholarship when submitting the programme application
documents: Master Scholarship Application section: justification of up to 200 words and up to 10 achievements
Supporting documents for the listed achievements
opportunities.selection_process: Merit-based; a panel reviews scholarship applications in January, March, May and July. Late applications are not considered.
important_dates: Panel reviews: January, March, May and July
opportunities.about_provider: XJTLU is an international joint-venture university in Suzhou, China, founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool. It teaches in English.
opportunities.how_to_apply: When submitting your programme application in the XJTLU system, tick the scholarship option and complete the Master Scholarship Application section, then upload your supporting documents. If you do not indicate interest at submission, you will not be considered.
opportunities.notes: Alumni of XJTLU, Liverpool or XJTU get a separate 20% discount that cannot be combined with this scholarship. Contact: pgadmissions@xjtlu.edu.cn.

opportunities.title: University of Lincoln Global Leaders Scholarship – September 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time overseas fee payers of any nationality with a Lincoln offer for September 2027 can apply by 7 June 2027 for a 50% one-year tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Global Leaders Scholarship at the University of Lincoln in England pays 50% of tuition for one year for full-time overseas students who already hold an offer. It covers both undergraduate and taught postgraduate degrees, and this round is for courses starting in September 2027.

The award is competitive and judged on academic results together with personal and extracurricular achievement. Undergraduates need school results equal to at least 128 UCAS points and postgraduates a 2:1 or higher.

It is open to overseas fee payers of every nationality, including African students, and can halve one year's international fee.
opportunities.benefits: 50% of tuition fees for one year. The number of awards is not stated.

Full-time study
An offer from Lincoln for 2026/27 or 2027/28 entry
Undergraduate: school grades equivalent to 128 UCAS points or more

opportunities.about_provider: The University of Lincoln is a public university in the city of Lincoln in the East Midlands of England, with a modern waterside campus and a focus on teaching and applied research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Accept or hold an offer from the University of Lincoln, then complete the Global Leaders Scholarship application form linked from the official page for September 2027 entry by 7 June 2027, attaching transcripts if you are still studying.
opportunities.notes: There is a separate January 2028 round closing 18 October 2027. The 2027-28 international scholarship terms are linked from the page.

opportunities.title: IESEG International Merit-Based Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a business or management bachelor's admitted to the Master Cycle of IESEG's Grande Ecole Program can receive up to 30% off tuition on merit, plus early-bird and partner discounts (capped at 50% in total).
opportunities.description:
IESEG School of Management, with campuses in Lille and Paris, offers merit-based tuition reductions to applicants admitted to the Master Cycle of its Grande Ecole Program, a master's-level programme in management. The reduction can reach 30% of tuition and is decided from the whole application: academic results, the rigour of previous studies, motivation, extracurricular activities and professional experience.

Two further discounts can be added: a 10% early-bird reduction for applications submitted before 1 March 2027 and a 10% reduction for students from partner institutions. All financial aid combined is capped at 50% of tuition. Tuition for 2026-2027 was EUR 13,200 and the application fee is EUR 100.

Admission runs in rolling sessions. The first session closed on 1 November 2026, the next closes on 1 December 2026 and the final session (Session 9) closes on 15 June 2027. African applicants benefit most by applying early, before 1 March 2027, to stack the early-bird discount with a merit award.
opportunities.benefits: Merit-based tuition reduction of up to 30%; early-bird reduction of 10% (apply before 1 March 2027); partner-institution reduction of 10%; total aid capped at 50% of tuition (2026-27 tuition EUR 13,200).
requirements: Bachelor's degree in management, business or a related field from a recognised university
Strong academic performance
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 85, TOEIC (4 skills) 850, Duolingo 115 or Cambridge B2 (native speakers and those with two years of English-taught study are exempt)
GMAT/GRE optional
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored out of 20: application file (8), English written test (2), interview (8) and English interview (2). Merit reductions are based on the overall profile.
opportunities.about_provider: IESEG School of Management is a French business school with campuses in Lille and Paris. It holds the AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through IESEG's candidate portal (candidate.ieseg.fr) for the Master Cycle, uploading transcripts, an English test, CV, recommendation and a motivation video, and paying the EUR 100 fee. Shortlisted applicants sit an English test and interviews; merit reductions are communicated with the admission decision.
opportunities.notes: Apply before 1 March 2027 for the extra 10% early-bird reduction. The total of all reductions cannot exceed 50%.

opportunities.title: Organoids and Beyond: From Development to Disease Conference 2027 (bursaries)
opportunities.provider: Wellcome Sanger Institute Scientific Training and Events (Wellcome Connecting Science)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can attend; bursaries of up to half the registration fee favour students, trainees, LMIC-based applicants and under-represented groups who submit an abstract.
opportunities.description:
Organoids and Beyond: From Development to Disease is a two-and-a-half-day scientific conference on the Wellcome Genome Campus at Hinxton, near Cambridge in the UK, running from midday on Monday 20 September to early afternoon on Wednesday 22 September 2027. It can be attended in person or online, and the programme combines talks, poster sessions and a panel discussion on how organoids are being used in drug discovery.

The meeting is organised by the scientific training and events team of the Wellcome Sanger Institute, which used to trade as Wellcome Connecting Science. Participants submit abstracts, and the scientific committee picks some of them for oral presentations, so it is a chance for early-career researchers to show their work to an international audience working on stem cells, development and disease models.

For researchers based in Africa the conference is relevant in two ways: delegates from low- and middle-income countries can join the virtual meeting free of charge, and in-person attendees can apply for a bursary covering up to half of the registration fee, with priority given to PhD students, trainees, applicants from LMICs and under-represented groups.
opportunities.benefits: Bursaries usually cover up to 50% of the registration fee for in-person delegates. Carers' grants of up to £500 are also available (form emailed to the organiser by the registration deadline). Delegates from low- and middle-income countries can attend the virtual conference free. For reference, in-person fees are £269/£359/£429 for students (early/standard/late) and £369/£459/£529 for academics; on-site accommodation is £240.
requirements: Open to researchers of any nationality working in organoid, stem cell, developmental or disease biology
Bursary priority: PhD students and trainees, applicants from low- and middle-income countries, and under-represented or minoritised groups; other early-career researchers if funds allow
Bursary applicants must submit an abstract before the bursary deadline (exceptions only in exceptional circumstances)
Oral presenters must attend on site
Free virtual registration applies to delegates based in listed LMICs
documents: Abstract prepared to the organiser's abstract guidelines
Short statement explaining financial need and how attending will benefit you
Carers' grant form (only if applying for that grant)
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts are reviewed by the scientific programme committee, which chooses some for talks and others for posters. Bursaries are awarded on need and expected benefit, giving priority to students, trainees, LMIC applicants and under-represented groups. In-person places are limited.
important_dates: Bursary deadline: 28 June 2027 (deadlines box on the event page)
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome Sanger Institute Scientific Training and Events runs courses and conferences on the Wellcome Genome Campus and with partners worldwide. It is part of the Sanger Institute, operated by the charity Genome Research Limited and funded by the Wellcome Trust.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register through the event's online registration portal and tick the bursary option while registering. Explain your financial need and the benefit of attending, and submit your abstract before the bursary deadline. All deadlines close at 23:59 UK time.
opportunities.notes: The event page shows two bursary dates: a 16 November 2026 date in its financial assistance text (already passed) and 28 June 2027 in its deadlines box, so confirm with events@sanger.ac.uk before relying on the later date. Abstract decisions are sent about two weeks after the abstract deadline. On-site rooms are first come, first served.

opportunities.title: Lingnan University Entrance Scholarships for Non-local Undergraduates 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-local applicants with international qualifications who apply to Lingnan's UGC-funded first-year programmes are considered automatically for full, full-tuition or half-tuition scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Lingnan University in Hong Kong automatically considers applicants to its government (UGC)-funded first-year undergraduate programmes for entrance scholarships. There are three levels: a Full Scholarship covering tuition, hostel and part of academic and living costs; a Full-tuition Scholarship; and a Half-tuition Scholarship. Each can be renewed for the normal length of the degree, subject to an annual review.

Non-local students, meaning those who will study on a student visa or entry permit, pay HK$205,000 a year in tuition for 2027-28, so these scholarships make a large difference. There is no separate scholarship form: applying for admission is enough.

Lingnan is Hong Kong's liberal arts university, with small classes and a strong residential culture, which makes it a good fit for African students looking for a broad, English-taught education in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: Full Scholarship (tuition, hostel and partial academic and living expenses), Full-tuition Scholarship, or Half-tuition Scholarship; each renewable up to the normal study period subject to annual review. For reference, non-local tuition for 2027-28 is HK$205,000 a year.
requirements: Non-local applicant (student visa/entry permit, IANG or dependant visa)
Recognised international qualification (e.g. IB, GCE A-level/IAL, national curricula on Lingnan's list)
English: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall (one skill retake accepted) or another listed test
Applying to a UGC-funded first-year programme (self-financed programmes are not covered)
documents: Secondary school results / transcripts (IB, SAT, AP and ACT results sent by the exam board)
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on merit to applicants for UGC-funded first-year programmes, who are considered automatically when their admission application is assessed. Awards are reviewed annually for renewal.
important_dates: Final Round for non-local applicants: 30 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Lingnan University is a public liberal arts university in Tuen Mun, Hong Kong. It is known for whole-person education, small classes and a residential campus.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online at apply.ln.edu.hk, paying the HK$200 fee per programme choice. Choose a UGC-funded programme to be considered automatically for the scholarships; no separate scholarship application is needed.
opportunities.notes: Applying in an earlier round is wise because scholarships are limited. A student visa fee of HK$700 is payable on accepting an offer. Lingnan also lists faculty-specific entrance scholarships for non-local Year 1 students.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: The Role of Temperature in Biology Across Scales 2027 (travel grants and fee waivers)
opportunities.provider: EMBO and EMBL (EMBL Course and Conference Office)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers at all career stages in biology, biophysics or modelling can register; on-site participants submitting abstracts can apply for fee waivers and travel grants.
opportunities.description:
The Role of Temperature in Biology Across Scales is a four-day EMBO | EMBL Symposium at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, from Tuesday 12 to Friday 15 October 2027, with an option to take part online. It looks at how temperature shapes living systems at the molecular, cellular and organism level, through six sessions, 24 short talks chosen from abstracts, poster sessions and a conference dinner.

The meeting is aimed at PhD students, postdocs and established researchers in biology, biophysics and modelling. On-site participants can submit an abstract for a talk or poster.

African researchers can apply for EMBL's financial assistance, which includes registration fee waivers and travel grants of up to €1,000 for people travelling from outside Europe, with priority for early-stage researchers.
opportunities.benefits: Financial assistance: registration fee waivers, travel grants of up to €400 from within Europe or up to €1,000 from outside Europe, and childcare grants, with priority for early-stage researchers. On-site fees otherwise range from €650 (PhD students) to €950 (industry) and include meals; travel and accommodation are not covered.

Only on-site registrants can submit abstracts
Abstract body of at most 2,000 characters
Virtual participants may request financial assistance but cannot submit abstracts

opportunities.about_provider: EMBL's Course and Conference Office, set up in 1983, organises courses, conferences and symposia at EMBL Heidelberg, many of them jointly with EMBO.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register for on-site or virtual attendance through EMBL's registration system, then submit your abstract and any financial assistance request using the link in your confirmation email before 6 July 2027.
opportunities.notes: Some deadlines were read from a summary of a long page, so confirm them on the event page. Contact: events@embl.de.

opportunities.title: Sheffield International Postgraduate Scholarship 2027 (selected regions)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded overseas-fee students who have lived in Kenya or Nigeria (or other listed countries) for the past three years and accept a Sheffield taught master's offer for September 2027 by 6 July 2027 automatically get GBP 7,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The University of Sheffield's International Postgraduate Scholarship 2027 (selected regions) is a GBP 7,000 tuition reduction for full-time taught postgraduate students starting in September 2027. It is aimed at applicants from a set of countries and regions, including Kenya and Nigeria in Africa, along with India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Türkiye, Vietnam and the USA.

Eligibility is based on residence, not passport: you must be a permanent resident of, or have lived in, one of these countries for the last three years. The award is automatic for self-funded offer holders with overseas fee status, so there is no form to fill in, but you must accept your offer before 4pm UK time on Tuesday 6 July 2027.

For Kenyan and Nigerian applicants, this is a straightforward saving on a Russell Group master's. On two-year master's programmes the reduction is applied in year two if year one is passed.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 7,000 reduction in tuition fees for a full-time taught postgraduate programme starting September 2027 (for two-year master's, applied in year two after successful completion of year one).

Not PGDip/PGCert, Erasmus Mundus/Crossways, online or distance learning, or a higher clinical fee course
Accept the offer by 4pm UK time on 6 July 2027

opportunities.notes: Cannot be combined with external sponsorship (except repayable loans) or most other Sheffield scholarships; it cannot be deferred or backdated. USIC students and MArch programmes are eligible.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: Organoids: Modelling Organ Development and Disease in 3D 2027 (travel grants and fee waivers)
opportunities.provider: EMBO and EMBL (EMBL Course and Conference Office)

Organoids: Modelling Organ Development and Disease in 3D is the sixth edition of an EMBO | EMBL Symposium on how three-dimensional organoids are used to study organ development and model disease. It runs for four days, from Wednesday 20 to Saturday 23 October 2027, at EMBL in Heidelberg, Germany, with virtual participation available.

The organisers welcome researchers at every career stage, from master's students to principal investigators. Only on-site participants can submit abstracts, and places are confirmed on a first-come, first-served basis once payment is made.

For African scientists the symposium offers fee waivers and travel grants of up to €1,000 for those travelling from outside Europe, which can make attending a leading international organoid meeting affordable.

Only on-site registrants can submit abstracts
Place confirmed only after payment (first come, first served)

opportunities.provider: EMBO and EMBL (EMBL Course and Conference Office)

Cell Biology of the Nucleus is the second edition of an EMBO | EMBL Symposium on how the cell nucleus is built and how it works, covering themes such as the nuclear envelope, biomolecular condensates and the biophysics and mechanics of the nucleus. It runs for four days, from Tuesday 16 to Friday 19 November 2027, at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, with an option to take part online.

The symposium is organised jointly by EMBO and EMBL through the EMBL Course and Conference Office. It is aimed at scientists at different career stages and from several disciplines, and on-site participants can submit an abstract to be considered for a talk or a poster.

For African researchers the main attraction is the financial assistance: EMBL offers registration fee waivers and travel grants of up to €1,000 for participants travelling from outside Europe, and gives priority to people from EMBL member states and low- and middle-income countries.

Registration fees otherwise range from €650 to €950 on site and €190 to €290 online; travel and accommodation are not included.

opportunities.title: Introduction to Tropical Medicine (INTROMED) 2027-2028, Antwerp
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nurses, midwives and other health professionals who want an introduction to tropical medicine; open internationally, with higher fees for non-EEA participants.
opportunities.description:
Introduction to Tropical Medicine (INTROMED) is a five-week short course at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, running from 30 August to 1 October 2027. It is taught in English in a hybrid format and is worth 5 ECTS credits.

The course is aimed at nurses, midwives and other health professionals who work, or plan to work, in tropical or low-resource settings and need a solid grounding in the main tropical diseases and how they are managed. It also forms the first block of several of ITM's longer postgraduate programmes, so it can serve as a stepping stone to further study.

ITM is one of Europe's leading centres for tropical medicine and public health, and many of its students come from Africa. Note that no scholarships are offered for this particular course, so applicants must cover the fee themselves.
opportunities.benefits: A fee-paying course: EUR 770 for EEA participants and EUR 1,995 for non-EEA participants. ITM states that no scholarships are available for this course; travel and living costs are the participant's own responsibility.

opportunities.title: DAAD-EPOS Scholarship for the MA in Development Management, Ruhr University Bochum (2028-2030 intake)
opportunities.provider: Institute of Development Research and Development Policy (IEE), Ruhr University Bochum / DAAD
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates from the Global South with a strong social-science degree and at least two years of development work experience can apply for a DAAD-EPOS scholarship by 30 September 2027.

The MA in Development Management at Ruhr University Bochum is a three-semester, full-time master's programme (90 ECTS) taught in English by the Institute of Development Research and Development Policy. It includes a period of field research in a developing country and has been run under DAAD's EPOS scheme for development-related postgraduate courses since 2000, so a limited number of DAAD-EPOS scholarships are available for each intake.

Applications open on 18 January 2027, and candidates who want a DAAD-EPOS scholarship must apply by 30 September 2027, a year ahead of the start of studies; other candidates have until 31 December 2027. Scholarship holders must also join a German preparatory language course that starts in July before the programme.

The scholarship targets excellent candidates from the Global South with professional experience in development work, which makes it a strong option for African public servants, NGO staff and development practitioners.

opportunities.title: Dundee Vice-Chancellor's Africa Undergraduate Scholarship (September 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students from eligible African countries starting a full-time on-campus Dundee bachelor's in September 2027 receive £2,000 a year automatically.
opportunities.description:
The University of Dundee in Scotland awards its Vice-Chancellor's Africa Undergraduate Scholarship to students from a long list of African countries who start a full-time, on-campus bachelor's degree on 11 September 2027. The scholarship is worth £2,000 for each year of study, for up to five years.

There is no separate application: the university's admissions team checks every eligible international applicant automatically. The programme must carry a tuition fee of at least £19,450, and Medicine and Dentistry are excluded.

For African school leavers planning to study in the UK, this is a guaranteed-style discount that rewards simply choosing Dundee, and it can be worth up to £10,000 over a degree.

About 55 African countries are on the list of eligible countries, among them Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia.

There is no separate application. Once an applicant has an offer and sends their final results, the Admissions Team checks whether they meet the grade requirement of AAB at A level or equivalent; predicted grades are not accepted.

Any faculty except Medicine and Dentistry is eligible, as long as the programme fee is at least £19,450.

opportunities.title: Dundee Vice-Chancellor's Africa Postgraduate Scholarship (September 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals of the African countries on Dundee's list who hold an offer, with international fee status, for a full-time on-campus taught Master's starting in September 2027 with a fee of £19,900 or more.
opportunities.description:
The Vice-Chancellor's Africa Scholarship for postgraduate study is a University of Dundee award for students from African countries who begin a full-time, on-campus taught Master's degree in September 2027 (programmes start on 11 September 2027). It is worth £2,000 and is applied as a reduction of the tuition fee.

The page lists a long range of eligible nationalities across the continent, including Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia, which makes this one of the simplest UK fee reductions for African graduates planning a 2027 start.

opportunities.title: Du Bois-Mandela-Rodney Postdoctoral Fellowship 2028-2029
opportunities.provider: University of Michigan, Department of Afroamerican and African Studies (DAAS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality working on Africa or the African diaspora who earned (or will earn) a PhD from another university between January 2023 and August 2028.
opportunities.description:
The Du Bois-Mandela-Rodney Postdoctoral Fellowship is a one-year residential fellowship at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor for early-career scholars whose research focuses on Africa or the African diaspora. The current call is for the 2028-29 academic year, and scholars from every discipline are considered.

The fellowship is hosted by the Department of Afroamerican and African Studies in the College of Literature, Science and the Arts. Fellows spend the year developing their own research, and in return they teach a short mini-course of five to six weeks for undergraduate and graduate students, present at the department's work-in-progress seminar and give a colloquium talk.

Because the fellowship sets no nationality rule and centres on African and diaspora studies, it is a strong option for recent African PhD graduates who want a funded year at a major US research university to turn their dissertation into publications.
opportunities.benefits: A total package of $56,000 plus benefits: a $52,000 stipend (which includes health insurance), $3,000 for research and travel, and up to $1,000 towards relocation to Ann Arbor.
requirements: PhD from an institution other than the University of Michigan
PhD earned no earlier than 1 January 2023 and no later than 31 August 2028
Research on Africa or the African diaspora, in any discipline
Candidates still finishing (ABD) must prove completion of the PhD by 31 August 2028 if selected
Must be able to reside in Ann Arbor for the academic year and teach a 5-6 week mini-course
documents: Writing sample of up to 30 double-spaced pages
Three reference letters submitted through the online system
ABD applicants: advisor contact for verification and an ABD transcript
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by the department after the November deadline, and applicants are notified of the outcome by 29 January 2028.
important_dates: Reference letters due: 8 November 2027, 5 p.m. EST
opportunities.about_provider: The Department of Afroamerican and African Studies (DAAS) at the University of Michigan, based in Haven Hall in Ann Arbor, teaches and researches the histories, cultures and politics of Africa and the African diaspora. It runs a work-in-progress seminar series where fellows share their research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The online application link will be posted on the fellowship page in September 2027. Upload all materials by 1 November 2027 and register your three referees in the system so their letters arrive by 8 November. Questions go to daas-info@umich.edu.
opportunities.notes: The 2028-29 call is not open yet; check the page from September 2027. Applicants more than five years past their PhD are not eligible.

opportunities.title: Federation University 2027 Global Merit Scholarship

The scholarship takes 25% off tuition fees for the duration of the course, calculated on the units enrolled each semester. There is no separate application: International Admissions assess applicants automatically when an offer is made. The scholarship opened on 9 November 2026 and closes on 7 November 2027.

African applicants should note the application route: applicants from Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda and Ghana are asked to apply through an authorised Federation agent, while applicants from other countries apply through StudyLink.
opportunities.benefits: 25% reduction of tuition fees for the full course (no cash value; non-refundable and not deferrable).

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible Federation University course. Applicants from Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda and Ghana should use an authorised Federation agent; other applicants apply through StudyLink (AUD 25 fee, waived through an agent). The scholarship is assessed with the offer.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship is forfeited if you withdraw; it is reinstated after approved compassionate leave.

opportunities.title: ECU Africa International Scholarship 2027

opportunities.title: ANU International Achievement Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international coursework students (outside the excluded East Asian countries) with strong grades receive 20% off tuition automatically.
opportunities.description:
The ANU International Achievement Award is a tuition discount that the Australian National University gives to academically capable overseas students starting an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme. Most recipients receive 20% off their tuition fees for up to four years, with higher rates for students from South East Asia (25%) and the Pacific (50%).

The award is open all year and there is no separate application: eligible students are considered automatically when they apply for admission, and the value appears in the letter of offer. Students from China, Japan, Mongolia, South Korea and North Korea are excluded from this award and are covered by a separate one.

African students who meet the grade thresholds therefore receive the 20% discount simply by applying to ANU.

Not resident in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau), Japan, Mongolia, South Korea or North Korea

No external sponsorship covering any part of tuition

opportunities.title: American-German Institute (Halle Foundation/AGI) Internships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate and graduate students who have completed at least four semesters of college and are eligible to intern at a US organisation can apply for a semester internship in Washington, DC.
opportunities.description:
The American-German Institute (AGI), a Washington, DC think tank affiliated with Johns Hopkins University, takes interns each semester through its Halle Foundation/AGI internship programme. Interns support research on transatlantic relations and German policy, write for the Institute's website, help with social media and partnership research, and assist with events, including the annual gala.

The internship runs for a full semester of at least three months at 28 hours a week, in three cycles a year: Spring (January to May), Summer (June to August) and Fall (September to December). Each cycle has its own application deadline, so the programme works as a rolling, recurring call.

Foreign nationals are welcome to apply as long as they are eligible to intern at a US organisation, so African students who already hold suitable US status (for example through CPT or OPT) can use it to gain policy experience in Washington. German language skills help but are not required.
opportunities.benefits: A cost-of-living stipend of USD 1,850 per month. Interns must arrange their own housing in Washington, DC.
requirements: Enrolled undergraduate or graduate student with at least four semesters of college completed
Eligible to intern at a US organisation (foreign nationals must already have the right status)
Able to work 28 hours a week in Washington, DC for a full semester (minimum three months)
Strong English writing skills; German is preferred but not required
documents: Two writing samples in English, each four pages or fewer
One letter of recommendation (may be sent separately by the recommender)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed for each semester cycle. Interns who are selected receive a mid-point and an end-of-term evaluation during the internship.
opportunities.about_provider: The American-German Institute is a non-partisan Washington, DC think tank, affiliated with Johns Hopkins University, that studies relations between Germany, Europe and the United States. It runs research programmes, publications and events on politics, economics and society.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine your résumé, cover letter, writing samples and recommendation letter into one PDF and email it to the AGI Operations Coordinator (jweiller@aicgs.org) before the deadline for the semester you want.
opportunities.notes: The page gives deadlines by month only (1 April for Summer, 1 July for Fall, 1 November for Spring). The Institute does not say it sponsors visas, so confirm your US internship eligibility before applying.

opportunities.title: Audencia International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants admitted to Audencia's bachelor's, master's or MBA programmes are considered automatically for partial tuition waivers, with extra early-application discounts until 31 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
Audencia Business School in Nantes, France, offers partial tuition waivers to international applicants admitted to its programmes for the fall intake. Scholarships are assessed during admission, so there is no separate application.

There are several types. Early Application awards give 10% off master's and first-year bachelor's tuition for applications before 31 December 2026 and 5% before 31 January 2027 (15% and 10% for the International MBA). Solidarity Scholarships, based on financial need, and Excellence Scholarships, based on academic merit, are worth up to 30% for all programmes, and a Project-based Scholarship of up to 30% exists for the International MBA.

For African students, applying before the end of December gives the best chance of combining an early discount with a merit or need award, since places and funding are allocated on a rolling basis while money lasts.

Example tuition: MSc 1 year EUR 19,900; 2-year MSc EUR 29,800; Master in Management EUR 38,250; plus EUR 500 service fee per year.

Only one scholarship in addition to the Early Application discount

Other scholarships: rolling, while funds last

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online to your chosen Audencia programme; scholarships are considered automatically with the admission file. Apply before 31 December 2026 for the largest early discount. Contact international@audencia.com with questions.
opportunities.notes: Early Application and the MBA project-based award cannot be combined. Funding is limited and allocated on a rolling basis.

opportunities.title: Australian Institute of Music International Scholarship 2027

The Australian Institute of Music (AIM) offers an International Scholarship to overseas students who begin a course with it in 2027. AIM is a specialist music and performing arts college with campuses in Sydney and Melbourne.

The scholarship reduces tuition by up to 10% for the full length of the course, and it can only be awarded before the course begins. AIM takes students in February, May and September 2027, so applicants should arrange the scholarship as soon as they hold an offer.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African students planning to study music in Australia can use it to lower their fees, but they will still need to fund the rest of their tuition and living costs.

opportunities.notes: Failing a class means losing the scholarship. The award covers at most 10% of tuition, so plan funding for the remainder and for living costs in Australia.

opportunities.title: CDU Global Merit Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students starting their first full-time course at Charles Darwin University in 2027 (TAFE, bachelor's or coursework master's) automatically receive 30% off tuition for the whole course.
opportunities.description:
The CDU Global Merit Scholarship is Charles Darwin University's automatic tuition discount for international students who begin their first course at CDU in 2027. It applies to full-time award study in TAFE, undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programmes.

The scholarship reduces international tuition by 30% for the entire duration of the course, and the university offers multiple awards. It is granted automatically to eligible students, at the university's discretion. To keep it, students must maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 4.0 (on CDU's 7-point scale) and progress on time.

For African students considering northern Australia, this can be a significant saving. Note the exclusions: the Bachelor of Nursing, the Doctor of Philosophy, the Master of Research, English for Academic Purposes, Study Abroad and several health and certificate or diploma courses are not covered.

Full-time award study in an eligible TAFE, undergraduate or postgraduate coursework course
Not in an excluded course (e.g. Bachelor of Nursing, PhD, Master of Research, EAP, Study Abroad)
Maintain cumulative GPA of 4.0 or above and on-time progress to keep the award

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible CDU course for a 2027 start. The scholarship is applied automatically if you qualify; questions go to scholarships@cdu.edu.au or international@cdu.edu.au.
opportunities.notes: Cannot be combined with any other CDU tuition discount and is non-transferable. Cancelling, transferring or changing course can mean repaying 30% of the published fee for each study period attempted.

opportunities.title: CQUniversity International Research Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students starting a research degree (research master's or PhD) at CQUniversity, or CQU coursework graduates moving into research, automatically receive 25% off tuition.

For African researchers looking at Australia, this is a useful saving because nothing extra has to be submitted: the discount is applied once you are admitted to an eligible research programme and meet the academic and English entry rules.
opportunities.benefits: 25% off tuition fees for the full duration of the research course. The page lists no stipend or living allowance.

opportunities.title: Chinese Government Scholarship China Link Short-term Scientific Exchange at Sichuan University (start by August 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students or staff registered full-time at a CSC partner university abroad, under 45 (general scholar) or under 50 (senior scholar), with pre-admission from Sichuan University.
opportunities.description:
The China Link programme is a short-term strand of the Chinese Government Scholarship that funds research and study visits of one to twelve months at Chinese universities. Sichuan University in Chengdu accepts China Link scholars in all disciplines except Chinese language study, with exchanges that must begin no later than 31 August 2027.

There are two categories. General scholars are current undergraduate or graduate students, while senior scholars are PhD candidates or university faculty. Applicants must be registered full-time at one of the foreign partner universities named on the CSC list throughout the visit, and need a pre-admission from Sichuan University before applying in the CSC system.

For African students and lecturers whose home universities are on the partner list, this is a fully funded way to spend up to a year doing research in a major Chinese university without enrolling in a full degree.
opportunities.benefits: Full CSC scholarship: tuition waiver, free on-campus accommodation, medical insurance and a monthly stipend of CNY 3,000 for general scholars or CNY 3,500 for senior scholars.

Under 45 (general scholar) or under 50 (senior scholar)
Registered full-time at a CSC foreign partner university when applying and during the stay
Pre-admission from Sichuan University for the coming intake
Exchange of 1 to 12 months starting no later than 31 August 2027
Any discipline except Chinese language study
documents: Documents required by the CSC online application guide (Appendix 2 on the page)
opportunities.selection_process: Sichuan University first gives pre-admission, then the application is reviewed through the CSC system; the page gives no further criteria.
important_dates: Apply at least 3 months before the planned start
opportunities.about_provider: Sichuan University is a large comprehensive university in Chengdu, south-west China; its Overseas Students Office handles international admissions. The scholarship is funded by the Chinese government through the China Scholarship Council.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact the Sichuan University Overseas Students Office for pre-admission, then complete the CSC online application (https://studyinchina.csc.edu.cn) with agency number 10610. opportunities.notes: There is no fixed closing date: applications must be made at least three months before the start, so the last practical date for an August 2027 start is around the end of May 2027. The contact email shown on the page differs from its link target, so confirm the address before writing.

opportunities.title: Deakin Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international coursework students of any nationality with an average of 85% or more can apply for a 50% or 100% tuition scholarship.

Applications are assessed on a rolling basis ahead of each trimester, and the scholarship form must reach Deakin at least one month before the course starts. Applicants who are not selected are considered automatically for the Deakin International Scholarship.

The award is open to all nationalities, so African students with an average of 85% or more can use it to study in Australia at little or no tuition cost.
opportunities.benefits: 100% or 50% of tuition fees for the normal duration of the course, membership of the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program (a condition of the award), and priority access to on-campus accommodation at the student's own cost.

opportunities.title: EMBO Scientific Exchange Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Life scientists of any nationality with at least a year of graduate research, working in an EMBC member state or partner country (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan), can get travel and subsistence for a 7-90 day lab visit; apply at least 30 days ahead.
opportunities.description:
EMBO Scientific Exchange Grants pay for short research visits between laboratories so that scientists can learn new techniques and start collaborations. The visit can last from seven days to three months and must be between labs in EMBC Member States or EMBO's global partner countries (Chile, India, Singapore and Taiwan), but not between two labs in the same country.

The grant covers travel and subsistence for the researcher only, with daily rates that depend on the country visited. There is no deadline: applications are accepted all year, but must arrive at least 30 days before the visit starts, and EMBO advises applying about three months ahead.

Eligibility depends on where you work, not your passport. African scientists qualify if they are working at an institute in an EMBC Member State or partner country (or are funded by JST programmes), for example as PhD students or postdocs in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs and subsistence for the fellow (country-dependent rates) for visits of 7 days to 3 months. Not covered: dependants, courses, conference travel, bench fees, overheads and visa costs.
requirements: Active researcher with at least one year of graduate-level research experience (or equivalent) at submission
Working at an institute/university in an EMBC Member State, EMBC/EMBO global partner (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan) or funded by JST programmes
Visit to a lab in a different country, for 7-90 days
No visits to former supervisors/colleagues or labs with a prior collaboration
Return to the home lab for at least six consecutive months afterwards
documents: Signed English letter from the home institution confirming your return
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by EMBO against its selection criteria (see the selection page); applicants should allow about three months for a decision.
important_dates: Submit at least 30 days before the visit starts (three months recommended)
opportunities.about_provider: EMBO, the European Molecular Biology Organization, is an organisation of leading life scientists that supports research and researchers through fellowships, grants, courses and conferences. Its funding is provided through the European Molecular Biology Conference (EMBC) member states.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the EMBO guidelines for applicants, then register and apply through EMBO's online application system (applications.embo.org). Arrange two referees and a confirmation from the host lab before submitting.
opportunities.notes: Extensions of up to three more months are possible, but EMBO funds only the first three months. Workshops, courses and symposia are not eligible.

opportunities.title: ESSEC Master in Management Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants admitted to ESSEC's Master in Management for the 2027 intake are automatically considered for a EUR 10,000 ESSEC Scholarship based on the quality of their application.
opportunities.description:
ESSEC Business School's Master in Management (MiM) is its flagship Grande École programme, leading to a French state-recognised master's degree. It can be taken on the Paris-Cergy, Singapore or Rabat campuses, either as a one-year Intensive track (Cergy only, for applicants with professional experience) or a two-to-three-year Flexible track.

International applicants to the 2027 intake are automatically reviewed for the ESSEC Scholarship worth EUR 10,000, with no separate form: the decision is based on the overall strength of the admission file. Scholarship holders also pay a reduced deposit of EUR 500 instead of EUR 6,000 when they accept their place.

For African applicants the award reduces but does not remove the cost of a programme whose tuition ranges from EUR 25,500 to EUR 39,400 a year. Applying in an early round is advisable, especially for those who also want ESSEC to nominate them for France's Eiffel Excellence scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: ESSEC Scholarship of EUR 10,000 for international applicants, plus a reduced acceptance deposit of EUR 500 (instead of EUR 6,000). For reference, 2027 intake fees: Intensive track EUR 39,400 tuition (EUR 43,580 total); Flexible track EUR 25,500 per year (EUR 57,490 total).
requirements: International applicant to the MiM 2027 intake (no nationality restriction for the ESSEC Scholarship)
Management test: GMAT or GRE (valid 5 years) or TAGE MAGE (valid 2 years); GMAT Quant-only not accepted
English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 95, TOEIC L&R 850 or Cambridge B2 First 175, unless you studied full-time entirely in English for at least 3 years
Intensive track: at least 6 months of professional experience before joining
Flexible track: at least 8 months of professional experience completed during studies
Documents in English or French, or certified translations
documents: Two recommendations (ideally one academic and one professional)
English test result or exemption proof
opportunities.selection_process: Files are assessed on application quality, academic record, management test score and motivation. Shortlisted candidates take a 45-minute video interview in English. Scholarship decisions are made automatically together with the admission decision.
important_dates: Applications in several rounds for the 2027 intake (dates not published on the programme page)
Deposit due within two weeks of the admission result
Final diploma due by mid-December of the start year
opportunities.about_provider: ESSEC Business School is a French business school with campuses in Paris-Cergy, Singapore and Rabat. Its Master in Management was ranked 10th worldwide by the Financial Times in 2025.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on ESSEC's online application portal (essec.myapply.online), choose the MiM track and campus, upload the documents and pay the EUR 180 fee. You may apply only once per programme per academic year, and the application cannot be edited after submission. No separate scholarship application is required.
