opportunities.notes: ESSEC nominates eligible non-French applicants under 30 for the Eiffel Excellence scholarship (EUR 1,181 a month); apply in the first round to be considered. Campus choice is final once your application is validated.

opportunities.title: Global Excellence Scholarship – QMBS, SEF & CCLS (January 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Overseas-fee students with a UK first-class degree or equivalent who hold an offer for an eligible January 2027 business, finance or law master's at Queen Mary automatically get GBP 7,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
Queen Mary University of London offers Global Excellence Scholarships worth GBP 7,000 to high-achieving international students who start an eligible taught master's in January 2027. This version of the award covers programmes in the School of Business and Management (QMBS), the School of Economics and Finance (SEF) and the Centre for Commercial Law Studies (CCLS).

Eligible courses include the MSc Finance and Banking, MSc Management, MSc Marketing and a range of LLMs, such as Commercial and Corporate Law, International Business Law, Intellectual Property Law, Comparative and International Dispute Resolution and Technology, Media and Telecommunications Law. The amount is deducted from tuition at enrolment and there is no limit on the number of awards.

For African applicants with first-class results, this is an automatic saving: there is no separate form, and awards are allocated on a rolling basis to offer holders who meet the criteria.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 7,000 tuition fee reduction, applied at enrolment for January 2027 entry; cannot be deferred to later years.
requirements: UK first-class bachelor's degree or overseas equivalent
Offer for an eligible full-time taught master's starting January 2027 (QMBS, SEF or CCLS)
Overseas fee status (must remain overseas for the whole programme)
Not receiving another Queen Mary scholarship or tuition discount
Able to fund remaining tuition and living costs
documents: None for the scholarship (standard master's application only)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: offer holders who meet the criteria are awarded on a rolling basis; the award is confirmed once the offer is unconditional firm and the student enrols. No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Queen Mary University of London is a research-intensive member of the Russell Group based in east London. It runs Global Excellence Scholarships for international postgraduate students across its faculties.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible January 2027 master's at Queen Mary. Eligible offer holders are considered automatically; make your offer unconditional and enrol to receive the reduction. Contact globalengagement@qmul.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Unlimited awards. Pre-master's programmes and Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry courses are excluded (FMD has its own scheme). Partially funded students can still qualify.

opportunities.title: Guelph International Doctoral Tuition Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time international PhD students at the University of Guelph admitted with an average of at least 80% (A-) automatically receive CAD 12,500 a year for up to four years.
opportunities.description:
The International Doctoral Tuition Scholarship (IDTS) is an automatic award from the University of Guelph's Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies in Ontario, Canada. It is designed to close most of the gap between the international and domestic tuition that doctoral students pay.

Each award is worth CAD 12,500 per year for up to four years, paid in three equal instalments a year. Students who transfer from a master's into a doctorate can hold it for up to 12 semesters in total. No application is required: every international doctoral student who meets the conditions receives it.

For African applicants considering a PhD in Canada, this makes Guelph's doctoral fees close to domestic rates, provided their admission average is at least 80% (A-). Students admitted with a lower average can still become eligible after passing the qualifying exam, for the remainder of the four-year window.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 12,500 per year for up to four years (up to 12 semesters for master's-to-PhD transfers), paid in three equal instalments each year; it roughly covers the difference between international and domestic tuition.
requirements: International full-time doctoral student paying international tuition
Admission average of at least 80% (A-); lower averages become eligible after the qualifying exam
Maintain full-time registration and satisfactory progress
Residency status identified by the 14th class day
Not held with certain other scholarships or third-party funding (e.g. employer or home-government funding)
Ends if the student becomes a Canadian permanent resident or citizen
documents: None for the scholarship itself (standard PhD admission documents only)
opportunities.selection_process: No competition: every student who meets all the conditions receives the award automatically.
important_dates: Awarded automatically each year for up to four years
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Guelph is a public research university in Ontario, Canada, known for agriculture, veterinary medicine and life sciences. Its Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies administers internal awards with Student Financial Services, departments and colleges.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a Guelph doctoral programme. Once admitted and registered full-time with international fee status, the scholarship is applied automatically. Questions go to the Graduate Program Assistant in your department.
opportunities.notes: Guelph also offers International Masters Tuition Scholarships (CAD 6,000 course-based, CAD 10,000 a year thesis-based), but these require a four-year honours degree from Guelph.

opportunities.title: HKUST RedBird PhD Award for International Students (Fall 2027 intake)
opportunities.provider: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Fok Ying Tung Graduate School
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to a full-time HKUST PhD programme are considered for the award as part of admission; there is no separate application.
opportunities.description:
The HKUST RedBird PhD Award is a recruitment award that HKUST gives to new international (non-local) PhD students on top of their admission. It is not applied for separately: applicants are considered when they apply to an HKUST research postgraduate programme, and the award follows the deadline of the PhD programme they choose. The current cycle is the 2027/28 Fall intake, for which applications opened on 1 September 2026.

The award sits alongside HKUST's main funding routes for research students. Most full-time PhD students receive a Postgraduate Studentship, and the strongest applicants can be nominated for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme. Candidates who are eligible for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship but not selected may still be considered for the studentship, the RedBird award and a first-year tuition waiver.

For African applicants this means a PhD at HKUST can come with a monthly studentship, a waived first-year tuition fee and a cash award, which together cover most of the cost of studying in Hong Kong.
opportunities.benefits: RedBird PhD Award: a recruitment award of HK$40,000 (about US$5,130) and a tuition fee waiver in the first year, then an Academic Excellence Award of HK$20,000 (about US$2,560) per year in later years, renewable subject to conditions. Full-time PhD students may also receive a Postgraduate Studentship of HK$229,620 per year for up to 4 years; Hong Kong PhD Fellowship awardees receive HK$344,400 per year for 4 years, a 4-year tuition waiver, the RedBird award and HK$14,400 per year for conference travel.
requirements: Non-local (international) applicant admitted to a full-time PhD programme at HKUST
Apply through an HKUST research postgraduate programme by that programme's deadline
Meet the admission requirements of the chosen PhD programme
Award in later years depends on meeting the renewal conditions
documents: Documents required by the chosen PhD programme (listed on the programme's Application tab)
opportunities.selection_process: There is no separate RedBird application; candidates are considered for the award during PhD admission. Hong Kong PhD Fellowship applicants are first nominated by HKUST and then assessed by the Research Grants Council, and those not selected can still be considered for the studentship and the RedBird award.
important_dates: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship registration with RGC: 1 December 2026, 12 noon (GMT+8)
Hong Kong PhD Fellowship application to HKUST: 1 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. (GMT+8)
Programme deadlines: from December 2026 onwards (vary by programme)
opportunities.about_provider: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology is a research university in Hong Kong; its Fok Ying Tung Graduate School manages admissions and funding for MPhil, PhD and taught programmes. HKUST says it has recruited more Hong Kong PhD Fellowship awardees than any other local institution, from over 50 countries and regions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a PhD programme on the HKUST programmes page and check its Application tab for the deadline and documents, then submit the online research postgraduate application. If you want to be considered for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship as well, register with the Research Grants Council and apply to HKUST by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Tuition for research programmes is HK$47,000 (subject to review); the student visa fee is HK$1,000. A bench fee of HK$150,000 applies only to full-time non-local self-financed research students in 2026/27.

opportunities.title: IAEA Internship Programme (Vienna)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students aged 20+ with at least three years of university study, or graduates within one year of finishing a degree, can apply for 3-12 month IAEA internships in Vienna with a EUR 1,000 monthly stipend.
opportunities.description:
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) offers internships that give students and recent graduates practical work experience linked to their studies. Interns work mainly at the agency's headquarters in Vienna, Austria, for a period that is normally between three months and one year.

Full-time interns receive a stipend of EUR 1,000 per month, which the IAEA stresses is not a salary. Applications are made against specific internship vacancies posted on the IAEA job board, and the agency typically processes them six to nine months after a vacancy closes.

Fields range from nuclear science and engineering to law, communication, IT and administration, so African students in many disciplines can find a relevant posting. Working English is essential, and another UN language is an advantage.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of EUR 1,000 per month for full-time interns (not a salary). The page does not mention travel or insurance.
requirements: At least 20 years old
At least three years of full-time university study towards a first degree, or within one year of finishing a bachelor's, master's or doctorate
Study discipline relevant to the vacancy
Working oral and written English (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish an asset)
Not previously an IAEA intern
documents: Online application for a specific internship vacancy (all mandatory questions answered)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed per vacancy, usually six to nine months after the vacancy's closing date; only selected candidates are contacted with next steps.
important_dates: Deadlines: set by each internship vacancy on the IAEA job board
opportunities.about_provider: The IAEA is the United Nations-family organisation for cooperation in the nuclear field, promoting the safe, secure and peaceful use of nuclear technology. It is based in Vienna, Austria.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Search the IAEA job board for internship vacancies in your field, create a profile and apply to a specific posting, answering all mandatory questions and uploading two signed recommendation letters. Track your status under 'My Jobpage'.
opportunities.notes: Apply as soon as a relevant vacancy appears; processing is slow, so plan many months ahead.

opportunities.title: IIE Scholar Rescue Fund Fellowship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Threatened professors, researchers and public intellectuals from any country who face danger to their life or career; applications are rolling with quarterly awards.
opportunities.description:
The IIE Scholar Rescue Fund (IIE-SRF) supports established academics whose lives or careers are under threat in their home countries. It arranges fellowships at host universities and research institutions around the world, so that threatened scholars can keep teaching, researching and writing in safety.

This is not a scholarship for study. It is meant for professors, researchers and public intellectuals in any country, field or discipline who face danger, persecution or the collapse of their academic system. People who want to continue their studies, including PhD study, are normally not considered.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and fellowships are awarded each quarter. IIE-SRF also runs time-bound calls; its most recent call ran until 11 October 2026 for consideration in December 2026. African academics at risk because of conflict, political pressure or threats linked to their work can apply or be referred by colleagues.
opportunities.benefits: A fellowship placing the scholar at a host institution where they can continue academic work in safety. The official pages reviewed do not state stipend amounts or the length of the fellowship.
requirements: Professor, researcher or public intellectual from any country, field or discipline
Preference for a PhD or the highest degree in the field, plus significant teaching or research experience
A record of scholarly work or publications
A current threat to life, liberty or academic career
Not a citizen or permanent resident of a safe second country
Not displaced or living outside the home country for more than two years
Has not already completed two years on a comparable fellowship
Students seeking to continue study, including PhD study, are normally not eligible
documents: Personal statement describing the threat (at least one page)
At least three original reference letters
Copy of PhD or highest degree
Optional letter of commitment from a host institution
opportunities.selection_process: IIE-SRF reviews applicants' academic qualifications, the quality of their work and the urgency of the threat they face. Not every eligible applicant is funded. Fellowships are awarded quarterly.
important_dates: Applications: rolling, with fellowships awarded quarterly
Most recent call closed: 11 October 2026 (for consideration in December 2026)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of International Education (IIE) is a non-profit based in New York that runs international education and exchange programmes, including the Fulbright programme. Its Scholar Rescue Fund has been placing threatened scholars at host institutions worldwide since 2002.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the application form from the IIE-SRF website, prepare the statements, CV, degree copy, publications and at least three reference letters, and email the complete package to srf@iie.org; postal and fax options are also listed. Colleagues can also refer a scholar at risk. Statements must be your own original writing; IIE-SRF discourages AI-generated text.
opportunities.notes: This is for threatened academics, not for students looking for study funding. The official site also lists alternative scholarship and fellowship opportunities for scholars.

opportunities.title: ISTA Year-Round Scientific Internships
opportunities.provider: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and master's students or recent graduates in science, maths or computer science from any country can arrange a paid 2-12 month internship (min. EUR 1,583/month) at ISTA year-round.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) offers paid scientific internships throughout the year in its research groups at Klosterneuburg, just outside Vienna. Students and recent graduates can join a lab for anything from two months to one year.

Interns are employed by ISTA on a contract paying at least EUR 1,583 gross per month. There is no central deadline: you contact a research group leader directly, ideally four months before you want to start, and the group decides whether to take you on.

The programme is open to all nationalities, and English is ISTA's working language, so African bachelor's and master's students in the natural sciences, computer science or mathematics can gain hands-on research experience at a top European institute.
opportunities.benefits: An employment contract with a minimum salary of EUR 1,583 gross per month. Housing in ISTA apartments may be available for a fee. No separate travel grant.
requirements: Current student or recent graduate of a bachelor's or master's in natural sciences, computer science, mathematics or a related field
Available for at least 2 months (up to 1 year)
Good English
Not employed or funded elsewhere during the internship
Non-EU interns need an Austrian visa/residence permit; eligibility is reviewed under ISTA's research security policy
opportunities.selection_process: Research group heads or staff scientists choose interns, subject to available salary funding and approval by Academic Affairs. Not all groups take interns, and only selected candidates receive a reply.
important_dates: Apply at least 4 months before your desired start
Portal registration completed at least 2 months before start
opportunities.about_provider: ISTA is an international research institute in Klosterneuburg, Austria, dedicated to basic research in the natural sciences, mathematics and computer science. It runs a graduate school and does not charge application fees for any programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Browse ISTA's research groups and staff scientists, then email the group leader whose work interests you with a short motivation, your CV and possible dates. If they are interested, they will invite you to complete the application portal.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not processed. People affiliated with EU-sanctioned institutions in the past 12 months are not eligible. Admin questions go to predoc@ista.ac.at.

opportunities.title: ITM DGD Scholarships for students from low- and middle-income countries (2027 courses)
opportunities.provider: Institute of Tropical Medicine Antwerp (ITM) with the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (DGD)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early- and mid-career citizens and residents of low- and middle-income countries admitted to an ITM master's, short course, internship, PhD or postdoc; most awards go to Belgian priority countries.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp manages a scholarship programme funded by the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (DGD). It supports citizens of low- and middle-income countries to take ITM master's programmes, short courses, internships, predoctoral traineeships, PhD studies and postdoctoral traineeships, with partial or full scholarships.

There is no separate scholarship deadline: candidates apply through the application for their chosen ITM course, before that course's own deadline, and the DGD form is part of the online application. Most scholarships go to Belgium's development partner countries, which include many African states such as Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda.

For the PhD route, ITM offers 3 to 5 DGD PhD scholarships a year for candidates admitted to its doctoral programme, lasting up to 48 months as a sandwich PhD with up to 24 months in Antwerp.
opportunities.benefits: Registration and tuition fees, required insurance, accommodation and a living allowance. Travel to and from Belgium is not covered, except in truly exceptional cases decided individually. Amounts are not stated on the page.
requirements: Citizen of, and resident in, a low- or middle-income country on the OECD-DAC list
Early- or mid-career professional
Meet all academic admission criteria of the chosen ITM course
Not a dual citizen of a high-income country and not employed in a high-income country
Previous master's study in a high-income country rules out travel support
documents: DGD scholarship application form (downloaded within the online application)
For exceptional travel support: motivation letter and supporting documents
opportunities.selection_process: Academic selection for the course comes first. ITM and DGD then jointly award scholarships to top-ranked candidates, considering motivation, gender (women preferred when candidates are equal), no previous DGD scholarship, employer support, likelihood of returning, and a job where the training can be applied.
important_dates: Apply by the deadline of the chosen ITM course (e.g. MSc programmes: 15 January 2027; many 2027-28 short courses: 15 July 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp is a Belgian research and training institute in tropical medicine and international health. The DGD is the Belgian government's development cooperation administration.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose an ITM course, apply online through the ITM student portal before that course's deadline, and complete the DGD scholarship form included in the application. Requests for travel support go to itmedu@itg.be with your name and 'Travel Support' in the subject.
opportunities.notes: Some ITM courses state that no scholarships are available (for example Introduction to Tropical Medicine and Tropical Medicine and Clinical Decision Making), so check the course page. ITM also offers the Romain De Cock, Marleen Boelaert and Armand Van Deun scholarships.

opportunities.title: International Student Support Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students with an offer for a UniSQ degree starting in 2027 automatically receive 10% off tuition for the whole degree.
opportunities.description:
The International Student Support Scholarship 2027 is an automatic 10% tuition reduction from the University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) in Australia. It applies to new international students in all fields and at all levels, undergraduate, postgraduate and research, who receive an offer for an eligible award degree starting in the 2027 teaching year.

The reduction lasts for the length of the degree shown in the offer letter. There is no application and no extra selection criteria, and the scheme stays open across all 2027 study periods. It covers on-campus, external and online study, but not non-award programmes or programmes delivered by offshore or online partners.

African applicants should note that UniSQ accepts applications from Africa only through its official representatives (agents). For Trimester 1 2027, the recommended last date to apply is 12 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: 10% reduction of tuition fees for the duration of the degree as stated in the offer letter. No application fee for UniSQ applications.
requirements: New international student
Offer for an eligible UniSQ award degree starting in the 2027 teaching year
Meet the academic and English language entry requirements
Not combined with any other UniSQ tuition scholarship
Applicants from Africa must apply through a UniSQ representative
documents: English proficiency evidence (if from a non-English-speaking country)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic at admission: there are no selection criteria beyond eligibility.
important_dates: Trimester 1 2027: apply by 12 December 2026, accept by 21 December 2026, start 15 February 2027
Trimester 2 2027: apply by 22 March 2027, start 31 May 2027
Trimester 3 2027: apply by 5 July 2027, start 13 September 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) is a public Australian university with campuses in Toowoomba, Springfield and Ipswich and a large online student body.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your UniSQ degree through a UniSQ representative (required for applicants from Africa), who submits via the OMEGA online system. Processing takes about 14 days for undergraduate and postgraduate applications, and the 10% reduction is shown in your offer.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship does not transfer if you defer. The listed application dates are recommended dates; late applications may be delayed.

opportunities.title: KAIST International Student Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Tuition and monthly stipend for international master's and PhD students admitted to KAIST.

opportunities.title: KAUST Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP) Internship
opportunities.provider: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year-plus undergraduates and master's students of any nationality with a GPA of at least 3.5/4 and proof of English can apply to a funded 2-6 month research internship.
opportunities.description:
The Visiting Student Research Program lets advanced undergraduate and master's students spend between two and six months doing hands-on research in a faculty-led lab at KAUST, on the university's campus in Thuwal on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast. Start and end dates are flexible and applications are accepted all year round.

Interns join one of more than 100 active research projects across KAUST's science, technology and engineering programmes, using its core laboratories and taking part in campus social and cultural life. The internship is a common route into KAUST's fully funded master's and PhD programmes.

The programme is fully funded and has no nationality restriction, so it is a practical way for strong African STEM students to gain international research experience without paying for travel or housing.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend of US$1,000, a private bedroom and bathroom on campus, return airfare to KAUST, coverage of tuition and housing, access to core research labs, and social and cultural activities.
requirements: Undergraduate in the third year or above, or a master's student
Minimum GPA of 3.5 on a 4-point scale or equivalent

English: IELTS 6.5 (at least 6 in each section), TOEFL iBT new scale 4.5 (at least 4 per section), PTE Academic 64 (61 per section), Cambridge C1/C2 176 (169 per section) or Duolingo 110 (100 per section)
English test waived for in-person degrees from accredited institutions in the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand
Recent graduates eligible only if the degree was completed within one year before the internship start
Current PhD students, KAUST students and KAUST alumni are not eligible
Passport valid for at least 6 months
documents: Official English transcripts for all degrees
One recommendation letter from a faculty member at your current institution (KAUST contacts the recommender)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants apply to a specific research project, and KAUST and the supervising faculty member evaluate the application; there is no fixed release date for decisions. Only one application can be active at a time.
important_dates: Internship length: 2 to 6 months, flexible start dates
opportunities.about_provider: KAUST is a graduate research university in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, offering 17 STEM degree programmes. Its campus community includes people of more than 100 nationalities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Browse open research projects on the KAUST internship search page and click Apply on the project you want. Fill in the online form, upload your documents and give your recommender's contact details. There is no application fee.
opportunities.notes: You can request the internship brochure through the KAUST contact form by choosing Internships in the programme field.

opportunities.title: Lancaster Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students starting a full-time Lancaster degree in 2027 with A*AA-equivalent grades and Lancaster as firm choice receive £3,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Lancaster University in the UK offers its Undergraduate International Excellence Scholarship to international fee-paying students who start a full-time, on-campus degree in 2027 with top grades and who make Lancaster their firm choice. The scholarship reduces tuition fees by £3,000 for every year of study.

There is no separate application. Applicants are considered automatically through their university application once they firm Lancaster and meet the grade conditions of A*AA at A level or equivalent. The award cannot be deferred and does not apply to study-abroad, placement or repeated years.

The scholarship can be combined with Lancaster's regional scholarships, so some African students may be able to stack it with other awards.
opportunities.benefits: A £3,000 tuition fee reduction for each year of study.
requirements: International (overseas) fee status
Starting a full-time, on-campus undergraduate degree in 2027
Lancaster as firm choice on UCAS
A*AA at A level or equivalent (graduate-entry LLB: first or 2:1 average)
Not for International Study Centre pathway students
Not deferrable
documents: UCAS undergraduate application (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: students who firm Lancaster and achieve the required grades receive the scholarship.
opportunities.about_provider: Lancaster University is a university on the Bailrigg campus near Lancaster in north-west England. It runs several automatic scholarships for international undergraduates.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Lancaster through UCAS, accept Lancaster as your firm choice and achieve the grade conditions. The scholarship is then applied automatically.
opportunities.notes: It can be combined with Lancaster's Undergraduate International Regional, India or EU scholarships. Refugees and people with humanitarian protection can also look at the Lancaster Sanctuary Scholarship.

opportunities.title: Leakey Foundation Joan Cogswell Donner Field School Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students from countries with limited resources for human-origins fieldwork can be nominated by a field school director for up to $2,000 towards one field school season.
opportunities.description:
The Joan Cogswell Donner Field School Scholarship helps students from countries with limited resources for human-origins fieldwork attend a university-affiliated field school in archaeology, palaeoanthropology or primatology. Each award supports one student for one field school season, and a field school usually receives support for two students.

The scholarship was created with a gift from Joan Cogswell Donner, a Life Trustee of the Leakey Foundation who joined its board in 1979. Unusually, the application is made by the field school director on the student's behalf, not by the student.

Because priority goes to students from regions where primates and fossils are found, the scholarship is especially relevant to African students who want hands-on field training at sites in their own region or abroad.
opportunities.benefits: Up to $2,000 per student for one field school season, which can cover travel to and from the field school, living costs during fieldwork and other costs of attending. It does not pay salaries or wages, conference travel, tuition, overheads or publication costs.
requirements: Student enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate programme
Student from a country with limited resources to support human-origins fieldwork
Priority for students from regions where primates and fossils are found
Field school must be university-affiliated and in archaeology, palaeoanthropology or primatology
Application must be submitted by the field school director
documents: Letter on letterhead (PDF) from the field school director describing the training programme, including chances to work with international participants
Explanation of why the student is a good choice
Total tuition and what it covers
Additional expenses and other funding sources
opportunities.selection_process: The Foundation first reviews an inquiry email from the field school director; if the school is suitable it sends an application link, and applications are assessed with priority for students from regions where primates and fossils are found.
opportunities.about_provider: The Leakey Foundation is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) that funds research and education on human origins, evolution and behaviour.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The field school director emails an initial inquiry to the Leakey Foundation grants office. If the school qualifies, the Foundation sends an application link, and the director submits the documents in PDF on behalf of the student.
opportunities.notes: Students cannot apply directly, so ask your field school director to apply for you.

opportunities.title: Leakey Foundation Primate Research Fund (emergency grants for long-term field sites)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Leaders of long-term wild primate field sites with at least 10 years of continuous individual-level data can request emergency bridge funding at any time.
opportunities.description:
The Leakey Foundation's Primate Research Fund gives emergency bridge funding to long-term field studies of wild primates that are at risk of stopping because their regular funding has run out. The aim is to keep a field site running, and its long-term records unbroken, until the team can secure new money.

Grants are made for one year, and a second year can be funded after an evaluation. Priority goes to sites that combine research with conservation and that would otherwise lose datasets built up over many years.

Many of the world's longest-running primate field sites are in Africa, so the fund is relevant to African principal investigators and site directors who manage such projects.
opportunities.benefits: Up to $25,000 for one year, with the possibility of a second year of funding after evaluation.
requirements: Applicant must be the Principal Investigator, Director or Co-Director of an established long-term field site studying wild primates
The site must hold 10 or more years of continuous behavioural data on individual animals
Priority for sites with a research and conservation focus that risk losing long-term datasets
documents: Information request form on the Foundation's website
Full application form (sent by the grants office after the eligibility check)
opportunities.selection_process: The grants office first checks eligibility from the information request form, then invites eligible applicants to submit a full application for review.
opportunities.about_provider: The Leakey Foundation is a US non-profit (501(c)(3)) based in San Francisco that funds research into human origins, evolution and behaviour, including primate field studies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the information request form on the fund's page. If the grants office confirms that your site is eligible, it will send you the full application form. Questions go to the Foundation's grants email address.

opportunities.title: Luther College Academic Merit Scholarships for International Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Luther College in Iowa are automatically considered for renewable merit scholarships of up to USD 39,000 a year, with best chances by 1 January or 1 March.
opportunities.description:
Luther College, a liberal arts college in Decorah, Iowa, USA, automatically considers every international first-year applicant for academic merit scholarships worth up to USD 39,000 a year, renewable through the fourth year of full-time study.

The awards are based on academic performance, predicted exam results and the whole admission file. Even with a large award, Luther expects families to contribute a substantial share, often half or more, of the estimated USD 78,655 yearly cost for 2027-28, and need-based aid is limited.

For African students, applying by the 1 January Early Action date or the 1 March Fall priority date gives the best chance of merit funding at a small US college.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of up to USD 39,000 per academic year, renewable through the fourth year. 2027-28 costs for reference: tuition USD 57,160, room USD 6,430, meals USD 7,170, fees USD 3,195 (total about USD 78,655 with personal costs).
requirements: International first-year undergraduate applicant
Strong academic record and predicted exam results
English proficiency if not from an English-medium school: IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 80 (old scale) or 4 (new scale), Duolingo 115 or TOEFL Essentials 8.5
SAT/ACT optional
documents: Certified secondary school transcripts and school-leaving results
Signed 2027-2028 ISAFA financial aid form with certified bank or wage statements
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are decided automatically from the admission file; admissions staff interview applicants as a final step.
important_dates: Early Action deadline: 1 January (decision by 1 February)
Later applications considered while space and aid remain
opportunities.about_provider: Luther College is a private liberal arts college in Decorah, Iowa. For 2026 entry it received 718 international applications, admitted 166 and enrolled 37 students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application with your transcripts, recommendations and English results, and submit the ISAFA form with financial documents. Merit scholarships are considered automatically.
opportunities.notes: Plan to fund a significant part of the cost yourself; on-campus jobs pay about USD 1,700-3,800 a year. Contact worldadmissions@luther.edu.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Talented young people from under-represented backgrounds, mainly in Africa, apply through individual partner universities for fully funded secondary, bachelor's or master's study.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program funds young people, mostly from Africa, to complete secondary, undergraduate and master's studies at a network of partner universities and organisations. It has run since August 2012, the Foundation has committed more than 58,000 scholarships through 62 partners, and it aims to reach 100,000 scholars by 2030.

There is no central application. Each partner institution, in Africa, North and Central America, Europe and the Middle East, runs its own call with its own deadline, eligibility rules and selection process, so applicants must apply directly to a partner. PhD study is not currently covered.

The programme is aimed at academically talented, service-minded young people from under-represented backgrounds who want to contribute to change in their communities. Individual partner calls, such as those at UC Berkeley, Arizona State, Edinburgh, Cambridge and Sciences Po, are listed as separate items on this site.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the partner, the scholarship covers tuition fees, accommodation, books and other study materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and, where needed, a return air ticket. Application fees are refunded to applicants who are selected.
requirements: Young people with strong academic talent and a commitment to serving their communities
Priority for applicants from under-represented or economically disadvantaged backgrounds
Study at secondary, undergraduate or master's level (PhD not currently eligible)
Eligibility rules, including nationality and grades, are set by each partner institution
documents: Documents are set by each partner institution's call (typically an admission application, transcripts and essays)
opportunities.selection_process: Each partner institution selects its own scholars. Being admitted to a partner university does not guarantee a scholarship.
important_dates: Deadlines: set by each partner institution
opportunities.about_provider: The Mastercard Foundation has run the Scholars Program since 2012, committing more than 58,000 scholarships through 62 partners. It works through partner universities and organisations mainly in Africa, and also in North and Central America, Europe and the Middle East.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a partner institution from the Foundation's where-to-apply page and follow that partner's application process and deadline. The Foundation does not accept applications directly.
opportunities.notes: The Foundation warns that it never asks individuals for payments, so ignore social media posts that request application fees.

opportunities.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cambridge (Master's, 2027-28 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Africans living in Africa who hold a bachelor's degree can apply for a fully funded one-year Cambridge master's by their course's funding deadline (usually early December or January).
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cambridge funds young Africans to take a full-time one-year master's course at Cambridge. The current round is open for entry in the 2027-28 academic year, and almost any full-time master's can be chosen; only the MBA, MCL, MFin and MAcc are excluded.

There is no separate scholarship deadline: applicants opt in for the programme on their course application, which must be submitted by that course's own funding deadline, usually in early December or January. Applicants from countries not on Cambridge's application fee waiver list must also send a fee waiver request, due by 20 November 2026.

The programme looks for candidates committed to giving back to their communities and to a sustainable, climate-resilient Africa. Scholars receive full funding and join a community of African scholars at Cambridge.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition costs and a monthly maintenance allowance for the one-year master's (amounts not stated on the programme pages).
requirements: Be from, and live in, an African country (temporary residence abroad for study or work is allowed)
Hold a bachelor's degree
Meet the academic entry requirements of the chosen course (some ask for a UK first-class degree, others an upper second)
Apply to a full-time one-year master's, not the MBA, MCL, MFin or MAcc
Show commitment to giving back and to sustainability and climate resilience in Africa
English: IELTS 7.0 or 7.5 for most courses (outstanding documents due by 31 July 2027)
documents: Scholarship statement (education and career history, leadership, goals and contribution to sustainable futures in Africa)
Fee waiver request with transcript and passport copies (for applicants from countries not on the waiver list)
English test results (usually IELTS) by 31 July
opportunities.selection_process: Departments review course applications on a rolling basis and make offers from December to February, sometimes after an interview. The Mastercard Foundation team then selects scholars from the course application and scholarship statement, and award letters are sent in late March or early April.
important_dates: Course funding deadlines: usually early December 2026 or January 2027 (check each course)
Scholarship offers: late March or early April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Cambridge is one of the world's oldest and highest-ranked universities. The Mastercard Foundation, a Canadian foundation, funds the Scholars Program at partner universities to educate young Africans who will lead change on the continent.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find your course in the Cambridge postgraduate course directory and start the application with 'Apply Now'. Complete the fee waiver if needed, opt in for funding and select the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, then submit before your course's funding deadline.
opportunities.notes: Because each course sets its own funding deadline, check the course directory early; some close in early December.

opportunities.title: Mitacs Globalink Research Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Senior undergraduates, graduate students and postdocs at universities abroad can apply year-round, with a Canadian host professor, for CAD 6,000 per 12-24 week research stay in Canada.
opportunities.description:
The Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) funds research stays between Canada and other countries for senior undergraduates, graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. A student at a university abroad can come to Canada (or a Canadian-based student can go abroad) to work on a project jointly supervised by a home professor and a host professor.

Each internship unit is worth CAD 6,000 and covers a stay of 12 to 24 weeks; two units fund either one 24-48 week project or two shorter ones. The money goes towards the intern's travel, accommodation, research costs and a stipend.

Applications are taken on an ongoing basis, ideally at least 16 weeks before the planned start, so African students enrolled at their home universities can use it for a funded research visit to a Canadian lab once a Canadian professor agrees to host them.
opportunities.benefits: CAD 6,000 per internship unit (12-24 weeks), or CAD 12,000 for two units, to cover travel, accommodation, research expenses and a stipend for the intern. The host supervisor is not funded.
requirements: Full-time senior undergraduate (past second year), graduate student or postdoc (PhD within 5 years) registered at an eligible institution throughout the award
Joint supervision by a home professor and a Canadian (or host) professor at eligible universities
Project not at an institution where you previously earned a degree, and not in your country of citizenship
Aged 18 or over and able to meet visa requirements
Lifetime limit of two GRA units
documents: Online GRA application completed by all participants
Mitacs pre-departure form and confirmed project dates
opportunities.selection_process: An interdisciplinary team reviews proposals on research quality, benefits to industry, society and Canada, and the opportunities for the intern. Applications are also checked for research security and conflicts of interest. Outcome letters usually come 10-12 weeks after submission.
important_dates: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
Apply at least 16 weeks before the planned start
Projects must start within one year of the outcome letter
opportunities.about_provider: Mitacs is a Canadian not-for-profit organisation funded by the Government of Canada and the provinces and territories. It builds research and innovation partnerships between universities, industry and international partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a host professor yourself (Mitacs does not match interns), then contact your local Mitacs Advisor for the application portal link. Each participant completes their section, the Canadian university signs, and the application is submitted at least 12-16 weeks before the start date.
opportunities.notes: You cannot travel until you hold both the outcome letter and the award letter. Allow 1-3 weeks for the Canadian university's signature.

opportunities.title: Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international students enrolled full-time in Japan with strong grades and financial need can be nominated by their institution.
opportunities.description:
The Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship is a monthly allowance that JASSO pays to self-funded international students in Japan who have excellent academic and personal records but face financial difficulty. It is meant for students already enrolled full-time at a Japanese university, graduate school, college or language institute, not for applicants still abroad.

The scholarship runs for either 12 months (April to March) or 6 months (October to March). Students apply through the institution where they are enrolled, which can recommend only a limited number of candidates, so the internal deadline depends on each school.

For African students paying their own way in Japan, this is one of the main sources of support once they have arrived.
opportunities.benefits: 48,000 yen per month at graduate and undergraduate level, or 30,000 yen per month at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months (April-March) or 6 months (October-March).
requirements: Privately financed international student with 'Student' residence status
Full-time enrolment at an eligible Japanese institution
Excellent academic and character record and financial need
Japanese at JLPT N2 or higher, EJU Japanese 200+, or English at CEFR B2 or higher (not required in language institutes or preparatory courses)
Other allowances must not average more than 90,000 yen a month
A financial supporter in Japan must earn under 5 million yen a year
Not holding a MEXT or foreign government scholarship
documents: Application through the enrolling institution (documents set by the institution's guidelines)
opportunities.selection_process: Each institution selects and recommends a limited number of students to JASSO based on academic and character records and financial need.
important_dates: Scholarship periods: April to March (12 months) or October to March (6 months)
Internal deadlines: set by each institution
opportunities.about_provider: The Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO) is the Japanese agency that administers support for international students, including this scholarship funded by the Ministry of Education (Monbukagakusho).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Ask the international student office at your Japanese institution about its internal call and deadline, then apply through the institution, which nominates candidates to JASSO.
opportunities.notes: A separate reservation programme links the scholarship to strong EJU results for students before enrolment.

opportunities.title: NUS Research Scholarship (PhD and Master's by Research)
opportunities.provider: NUS Graduate School, National University of Singapore
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students with at least an upper second-class honours degree who are admitted to an NUS PhD or research master's can receive a tuition waiver and monthly stipend.
opportunities.description:
The NUS Research Scholarship is the National University of Singapore's main funding award for students doing a research degree, either a PhD or a Master's by research, in any graduate programme. It is open to international students as well as Singapore citizens and permanent residents, and it is awarded to outstanding applicants as part of graduate admission.

There are two intakes a year, in August and January, and each faculty sets its own application deadline. The scholarship normally lasts up to four years for a PhD and two years for a research master's; it is granted for one year at a time and renewed each semester depending on progress.

For African graduates with a strong honours degree, the scholarship offers a fully funded research degree at one of Asia's leading universities with a monthly stipend and no service bond.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend (rates from 1 January 2026). For international students: SGD 3,000 per month for PhD and SGD 2,900 per month for Master's by research. Singapore citizens receive SGD 3,800 (plus CPF) and permanent residents SGD 3,400 (PhD) or SGD 3,000 (Master's).
requirements: Open to all international students, Singapore citizens and permanent residents
Admission to a PhD or Master's by research programme at NUS
Undergraduate degree with at least Second Class Honours (Upper Division) or Honours (Distinction), or equivalent
TOEFL or IELTS for non-native English speakers (considered in the assessment)
International scholars must meet the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirements
No other employment or scholarship without approval
documents: Graduate application on the NUS GradApp portal
Optional: GRE scores and evidence of publications or research
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on their academic record, research interests and fit, references and CV, along with any optional test scores or research evidence. Outcomes are usually released around May for the August intake and around October for the January intake.
important_dates: Application deadlines: set by each faculty
Outcomes: around May (August intake) and October (January intake)
opportunities.about_provider: The NUS Graduate School manages graduate research admissions and scholarships at the National University of Singapore. It is based at University Hall on the Kent Ridge campus.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your chosen research programme through the NUS GradApp portal and indicate in the application that you want to be considered for the scholarship. Check the faculty's website for its deadline.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship is renewed semester by semester and carries no service bond.

opportunities.title: Nipissing University Guaranteed Entrance Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school leavers, including international students, entering Nipissing with an average of 80% or more.
opportunities.description:
Nipissing University in North Bay, Ontario, gives guaranteed entrance scholarships to students who apply straight from secondary school, and international applicants are included. There is no separate application: every eligible new student is considered automatically on the basis of their admission average, for September or January entry.

The award is renewable, so a strong average can reduce tuition for the whole degree as long as the student keeps up their grades and course load. For African school-leavers comparing Canadian options, it is a predictable, merit-based discount rather than a competition.
opportunities.benefits: Based on the 2026-27 table: an average of 95% or more earns free tuition at the domestic rate (worth over $24,000 in total); 90-94% earns $2,500 a year; 85-89% earns $1,500 a year; 80-84% earns $1,000 a year.
requirements: Applying directly from secondary school for September or January entry
Canadian and international applicants are both considered
Admission average of at least 80%, based on the best six Grade 12 (4U/4M) courses or the IB score as of 30 June
Not in Consecutive Education, the Commerce/BBA college-partnership or Nursing Scholar Practitioner programmes
Renewal requires the set cumulative GPA and 24 credits each year
documents: None beyond the normal undergraduate admission application
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: the award level is set by the admission average, with no separate application or competition.
opportunities.about_provider: Nipissing University is a public, primarily undergraduate university in North Bay, Ontario, known for small classes and its education and liberal arts programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to Nipissing as a secondary-school applicant; the scholarship is assessed automatically from your grades. January entrants must take 9 credits in the winter term, and their payment is deferred to September.
opportunities.notes: The official page gives no deadline; the listing's 13 and 20 November dates are not on it, so this entry is marked rolling. The amounts shown are from the 2026-27 table and may be updated for 2027 entry.

opportunities.title: OECD Internship Programme (Paris)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Paid one- to six-month internships in Paris for master's and PhD students, open year-round to applicants worldwide.

opportunities.title: Pulitzer Center Gender Equality Reporting Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and newsrooms worldwide can propose data-driven reporting on gender equality at any time.
opportunities.description:
The Pulitzer Center's Gender Equality Reporting Grant funds investigative, data-driven reporting projects on gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. It is supported through a partnership with PIMCO and is open to newsrooms and independent journalists in the United States and around the world.

The Center reviews proposals as soon as they arrive and usually tells applicants within a month if their project is being considered. The average Pulitzer Center grant is about $5,000, though awards can be larger or smaller.

The grant suits African journalists and newsrooms planning in-depth data stories on gender issues that elevate under-represented voices.
opportunities.benefits: Reporting costs for the project, with grants averaging about $5,000. Freelancer stipends are allowed only in exceptional cases. The grant does not fund books, feature films, staff salaries, equipment purchases, general outlet costs, start-up seed money, routine breaking news, advocacy or purely academic data projects.
requirements: Freelance or staff journalists, or groups of newsrooms, anywhere in the world
Investigative, data-driven project on gender equality or the empowerment of women and girls
Project must be journalism, not advocacy, marketing or academic research
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are reviewed as they arrive; applicants are usually notified within a month if their project is under consideration. The Center favours stories that elevate under-represented voices and use data.
important_dates: Applications: reviewed on receipt (no fixed deadline)
opportunities.about_provider: The Pulitzer Center is a non-profit organisation that supports independent global journalism.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Send a project proposal with a budget to the Pulitzer Center through the contact given on the grant page. Expect to hear within about a month if your proposal goes forward.

opportunities.title: Pulitzer Center Reporting (Travel) Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and media makers of any nationality with a plan to publish in US or European media can seek travel funding for international reporting at any time.
opportunities.description:
The Pulitzer Center's main reporting grants pay the hard costs of travel for international reporting projects, with a focus on important issues that receive too little coverage. Applications are considered on a rolling basis, so there is no fixed annual deadline.

The grants are open to journalists, writers, photographers, radio producers and filmmakers of any nationality, whether they are staff reporters or freelancers. Applicants need a credible plan for getting the work published or broadcast in US and/or European media, and projects that combine several formats are encouraged.

For African journalists this is a route to fund in-depth stories from the continent for international outlets.
opportunities.benefits: Most awards are between $5,000 and $15,000, and some are larger. Half of the grant is paid just before travel and the rest when the main material is delivered.
requirements: Journalists, writers, photographers, radio producers or filmmakers of any nationality
Staff journalists and freelancers can apply
A credible plan to publish or broadcast in US and/or European media
Project must involve travel for international reporting
documents: Project proposal with budget for travel costs
Distribution plan or commitment from a US and/or European outlet
opportunities.selection_process: The Pulitzer Center reviews proposals on a rolling basis, looking at the importance of the issue, how under-reported it is and the strength of the distribution plan.
opportunities.about_provider: The Pulitzer Center on Crisis Reporting is a non-profit organisation that supports independent global journalism, especially on issues that receive little coverage.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit a project proposal through the Pulitzer Center's grants pages, setting out the story, the travel costs and where it will be published. The general grants page does not list detailed steps, so follow the application link for the specific grant.
opportunities.notes: The Center also runs other schemes, such as the Persephone Miel Fellowship for non-native English-speaking journalists and the Catalyst Fund for freelance multimedia journalists.

opportunities.title: Seattle Pacific University Merit Scholarships for International First-Year Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted as first-year students for the fall term are automatically considered for SPU's renewable merit scholarships worth roughly USD 20,000-30,000 a year; there is no need-based aid for international students.
opportunities.description:
Seattle Pacific University (SPU), a private Christian university in Seattle, Washington, gives merit scholarships to incoming first-year students, and international students are eligible for most of them. There is usually no separate scholarship application: every admitted student is reviewed for merit awards at the moment of admission, based mainly on the cumulative unweighted secondary school GPA.

The largest awards are the SPU Merit Scholarships and the Faith for the Future Merit Scholarship, and both are renewed automatically for up to four years if the student keeps meeting the academic and full-time enrolment conditions. Smaller stackable awards exist for Christian leadership, alumni families, church matching and engineering. The top Distinguished Scholar full-tuition award is not open to international students.

For African applicants this means a substantial, predictable tuition discount at a US university that charges the same tuition to international, in-state and out-of-state students. Students should plan for the remaining costs themselves, because SPU does not offer need-based aid or full rides to international students and proof of funds is required before an I-20 is issued.
opportunities.benefits: Renewable merit scholarships (published 2026-27 amounts): SPU Merit Scholarships USD 20,100-30,400 per year; Faith for the Future Merit Scholarship USD 25,400-30,400 per year. Awards renew for up to 4 years. Possible add-ons: Christian Leader Award USD 1,500 (first year), Alumni Legacy USD 2,000, Church Match up to USD 500, Engineering Scholarship USD 5,000 for incoming engineering freshmen (international eligibility for add-ons not stated). No need-based aid and no full-ride awards for international students.
requirements: Admitted as a new first-year student for the fall term
International students are eligible for most merit awards (not the Distinguished Scholar award)
Award level depends on cumulative unweighted GPA
Faith for the Future: unweighted GPA 3.0 or higher plus faith or service involvement, a Christian high school, or a parent in full-time ministry
English proficiency test if English is not the first language
SAT/ACT not required for international students
Full-time enrolment (at least 12 credits) and academic progress to renew
documents: English proficiency results if English is not your first language
Proof of funds after admission, before the I-20 is issued
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants receive a holistic academic review covering GPA, course rigour, grade trends, any test scores, activities and fit. All admitted students are considered for merit scholarships automatically when they are admitted; the GPA largely sets the award band. SPU may arrange an interview (Zoom possible) where circumstances are unusual.
important_dates: Early Action (and Distinguished Scholar consideration): 1 November
Scholarship consideration: apply by the regular admission deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Seattle Pacific University is a private Christian university in Seattle, Washington. It charges the same tuition to in-state, out-of-state and international undergraduates and bases its first-year merit awards on unweighted cumulative GPA.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission to SPU as an international student by the regular admission deadline; no separate scholarship form is needed for most awards, as you are considered when admitted. Some awards, such as fine arts scholarships, require their own application. After admission, submit proof of funds so SPU can issue the I-20.
opportunities.notes: Amounts and rules can change at the university's discretion; the figures above are the 2026-27 published values. Government aid and need-based aid are not available to international students.

opportunities.title: Trent University International Entrance Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduate applicants to Trent University with a final average of 80% or more are automatically considered for renewable awards of CAD 2,500-5,500 a year.
opportunities.description:
Trent University automatically considers every international undergraduate applicant for its International Entrance Scholarships, renewable awards worth up to CAD 22,000 over four years. Trent has campuses in Peterborough and Durham (Greater Toronto Area), Ontario, Canada.

The value depends on your final high-school average converted to the Canadian scale: CAD 5,500 a year for 95-100%, CAD 4,500 for 90-94.9%, CAD 3,500 for 85-89.9% and CAD 2,500 for 80-84.9%. Students entering in Fall, Winter or Summer 2027 receive the award in two payments each year.

There is no separate application, so African students who apply for undergraduate admission with strong results get it automatically, and can also apply for Trent's larger Prestigious Scholarships.
opportunities.benefits: Renewable entrance scholarship per academic year: CAD 5,500 (average 95-100%, CAD 22,000 over four years), CAD 4,500 (90-94.9%, CAD 18,000), CAD 3,500 (85-89.9%, CAD 14,000) or CAD 2,500 (80-84.9%, CAD 10,000).
requirements: International fee-paying student on a Canadian study permit
Applying to a Trent undergraduate degree (not graduate or postgraduate certificate programmes)
Final high-school average of at least 80% (Canadian equivalent)
Meet admission requirements, including English proficiency
Renewal requires a full course load and at least an 80% average
documents: Trent undergraduate admission application with school transcripts and English proficiency proof (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: all international undergraduate applicants are assessed, and the amount is set by the final admission average.
important_dates: Payments: 50% in each of the first two terms of the year
opportunities.about_provider: Trent University is a public university in Ontario, Canada, known for small classes and a collegiate system. Its Trent International office supports students from around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission through the Trent Applicant Portal; the entrance scholarship is assessed automatically and appears on your account statement near the start of your first term.
opportunities.notes: Trent's separate International Prestigious Scholarships (up to CAD 15,000 a year) need an application through the Applicant Portal, open 1 November to 15 February. Contact international@trentu.ca.

opportunities.title: Türkiye Scholarships Research Program
opportunities.eligibility_summary: PhD holders and doctoral candidates at the dissertation stage from any country can apply year-round for a 37,000 TL monthly stipend for 3-12 months of research in Türkiye.
opportunities.description:
The Türkiye Scholarships Research Program funds international researchers and academics to spend three to twelve months carrying out research with Turkish academics at leading universities in Türkiye. It is part of the Türkiye Bursları scholarship system run by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB).

Applications are open all year and assessed in four rounds: January-March (results in April), April-June (July), July-September (October) and October-December (results in January). Researchers receive a monthly stipend of 37,000 Turkish lira, but must cover accommodation and other costs themselves.

The official page sets no nationality limit, so African PhD holders and doctoral candidates at the dissertation stage can use it for a funded research stay in Türkiye.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend of 37,000 TL for the 3-12 month research stay. Accommodation and other expenses are not covered.
requirements: PhD holder, or PhD candidate at the dissertation stage
A research plan to carry out with academics at a Turkish university
Research stay of 3 to 12 months in Türkiye
documents: Online application on the Türkiye Scholarships application system (TBBS)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed in four periods each year, with results announced in April, July, October and January.
important_dates: Current round: October-December, results in January
opportunities.about_provider: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) is the Turkish government's international scholarship programme, managed by YTB. It funds degree and short-term programmes for students and researchers from around the world.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the Türkiye Scholarships application system (tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr) and submit your research programme application; it will be assessed in the next round.
opportunities.notes: Budget for accommodation, which is not included. Türkiye Scholarships also runs a General Scholarship for degrees with an annual window of 10 January to 20 February.

opportunities.title: UCC College of Business and Law International Undergraduate Scholarship 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU students admitted to a full-time undergraduate programme in UCC's business school or law school for 2027/28 automatically receive EUR 2,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
University College Cork's College of Business and Law gives an automatic scholarship of EUR 2,000 per year to non-EU international students on full-time undergraduate programmes in Cork University Business School or the School of Law. The award is based on previous academic results and needs no separate application.

The scholarship is offered once to each eligible full-time international undergraduate and is awarded annually. It cannot be combined with any other UCC scholarship.

For African school leavers aiming for a business or law degree in Ireland, it is a modest but guaranteed reduction once they hold an accepted offer through UCC's application portal.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 2,000 per year towards costs for eligible non-EU undergraduates (cannot be combined with other UCC scholarships).
requirements: Non-EU international student
Full-time undergraduate programme in Cork University Business School or the School of Law
Accepted offer in the UCC application portal
Awarded on the basis of previous academic results
documents: None for the scholarship (standard undergraduate application only)
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic, based on previous academic results; no application or interview.
opportunities.about_provider: University College Cork is a public research university in Cork, Ireland. Its College of Business and Law includes Cork University Business School and the School of Law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to an eligible undergraduate programme through the UCC application portal (ucc.elluciancrmrecruit.com/Apply) and accept your offer. The scholarship is applied automatically. Contact internationaloffice@ucc.ie with questions.
opportunities.notes: UCC also lists automatic international undergraduate scholarships in its science/engineering (SEFS) and arts/social sciences (CACSSS) colleges for 2027/28.

opportunities.title: UMass Lowell Graduate Scholarship for Emerging Leaders - Africa
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International master's applicants committed to advancing science, health, technology or leadership in Africa, studying on campus on an F-1 visa.
opportunities.description:
UMass Lowell's Graduate Scholarship for Emerging Leaders - Africa supports international master's students who want to strengthen science, healthcare, technology, management and leadership in Africa. The award is worth up to $20,000, paid as $5,000 a semester for four consecutive semesters, and up to $25,000 over five semesters for the Master of Public Health.

There is no separate application: the graduate admission application, including the statement of purpose, is used to consider candidates. For a fall start, applicants are strongly encouraged to apply by 15 January of that year; for a spring start, by 15 July of the previous year. Later applicants can still be considered while funds remain.

The scholarship requires full-time on-campus study (or at least two on-campus courses and one online course per semester) on an F-1 visa sponsored by UMass Lowell.
opportunities.benefits: Up to $20,000 for master's students ($5,000 per semester for four consecutive semesters), or up to $25,000 over five semesters for the Master of Public Health, for students who remain in good standing.
requirements: Admitted to a UMass Lowell master's programme and meeting its academic standards
International tuition residency and F-1 status sponsored by UMass Lowell
Full-time on-campus study, or at least two on-campus and one online course each semester
Preference for a demonstrated interest in advancing science, healthcare, technology, management and leadership in Africa
Enrolment deposit paid within 21 days of the award
documents: Statement of purpose (used to assess the Africa focus)
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted applicants who meet the academic standards are considered automatically, with preference for those who show a commitment to development in Africa. The award can be withdrawn if the deposit is not paid within 21 days.
important_dates: Priority deadline for fall 2027 entry: 15 January 2027
Priority deadline for spring entry: 15 July of the previous year
Later applications considered while funds last
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Massachusetts Lowell is a university in Lowell, Massachusetts, USA. Its Graduate Admissions office runs this scholarship for international master's students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to a UMass Lowell master's programme and use your statement of purpose to explain how your studies will contribute to Africa. Apply by 15 January 2027 for fall 2027 to be in the priority round.

opportunities.title: UNESCO Internship Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: One- to six-month internships at UNESCO in Paris and field offices for students and recent graduates from Member States, with a stipend only in some locations.

opportunities.title: UNHCR Internship Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate programme, or recent graduates, from any country can apply for stipended UNHCR internships at offices worldwide.

opportunities.title: UNICEF Internship Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students and graduates of the last two years aged 18 or over who speak English, French or Spanish can apply to paid UNICEF internships advertised year-round.
opportunities.description:
UNICEF offers paid internships throughout the year in its headquarters, regional and country offices, giving students and recent graduates hands-on experience in work for children. Each internship is advertised as its own vacancy with its own deadline, and internships normally last between six and twenty-six weeks, full-time or part-time.

Interns work on real tasks in areas such as programmes, communications, data and operations, depending on the office. Offices range from New York to field locations worldwide, including many in Africa.

UNICEF pays a monthly stipend to interns and may help with travel costs, which makes the programme realistic for African students who could not afford an unpaid placement.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly stipend (amount set per vacancy); a one-off lump sum towards travel and visa costs may be granted when funds allow; visa support letters where needed.
requirements: At least 18 years old
Enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or PhD programme, or graduated within the past two years
Proficiency in English, French or Spanish (the office's working language may be required)
No immediate relatives working in UNICEF in the same reporting line
Strong academic record and motivation
documents: Online application through the UNICEF careers portal
Documents requested in each vacancy notice (typically CV/profile and proof of enrolment or graduation)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed against each vacancy; because of the high volume, only shortlisted candidates are contacted for interview.
important_dates: Applications: year-round, each vacancy has its own deadline
opportunities.about_provider: UNICEF is the United Nations agency for children. Its internships place students and recent graduates in offices such as New York headquarters, the Pacific office in Suva and country offices worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Search for internship vacancies on the UNICEF jobs site, choose a position and click Apply Now to complete the online application. Apply separately to each internship that interests you.
opportunities.notes: An internship does not lead to an expectation of employment with UNICEF.

opportunities.title: United Nations Secretariat Internship Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Two- to six-month internships at UN headquarters and field offices, posted continuously, for students and recent graduates worldwide.

opportunities.title: University of Canberra UC Merit Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students with at least 70% (bachelor's) or 65% (master's) in prior studies get 10% off tuition automatically.
opportunities.description:
The UC Merit Scholarship gives commencing international students a 10% reduction in tuition fees for CRICOS-registered programmes at the University of Canberra's Australian campuses. It is based on academic achievement and is always open, with no closing date.

Students do not apply separately: they are assessed automatically when they submit their international student application, and scholarships are granted on a first-come, first-served basis until they run out. The award is valid only for the intake and course stated in the offer.

African students with solid grades who are considering study in Australia can secure the discount simply by applying early.
opportunities.benefits: A 10% reduction in tuition fees.
requirements: Commencing international student (diplomatic students excluded)
Enrolling in a CRICOS-registered programme at a University of Canberra Australian campus
For bachelor's degrees: 70% or equivalent in previous studies
For master's degrees: 65% or equivalent in previous studies
Excludes research degrees, standalone honours years, non-award, offshore and some listed courses
documents: International student application to the University of Canberra (no separate scholarship form)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed automatically against the grade thresholds when their international application is processed, and awards are made first come, first served until filled.
