opportunities.about_provider: The University of Canberra is a public university in Australia's capital (CRICOS provider 00212K, TEQSA PRV12003). It enrols international students in CRICOS-registered undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit an international student application to the University of Canberra. Eligible applicants are considered automatically, and the scholarship appears in the offer.
opportunities.notes: Apply early, because awards are given first come, first served.

opportunities.title: University of Glasgow Global Leadership Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students from eligible countries, including almost all of Africa, with first-class-equivalent results and an offer for a one-year Glasgow master's starting September 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Global Leadership Scholarship is a tuition fee discount of £10,000 for high-achieving international and EU students starting a one-year, full-time, in-person master's programme at the University of Glasgow in September 2027. The university offers 350 of these awards for the 2027/28 academic session, and the scholarship is open now.

Around 250 taught master's programmes are eligible, in fields ranging from global development and human rights to public health. Decisions are made on a rolling basis, usually within six weeks of the applicant's programme offer or scholarship application, whichever comes later, so applying early improves the chances.

Nearly every African country is on the list of eligible countries, making this one of the larger merit discounts available to African graduates for UK master's study.
opportunities.benefits: A £10,000 tuition fee waiver for one year of study. 350 awards are available.
requirements: International or EU fee status
Nationality of an eligible country (almost all African countries are listed)
Academic results equivalent to a UK First Class Honours degree
An offer for an eligible one-year, full-time, on-campus master's programme starting September 2027
Cannot be combined with other University of Glasgow discounts (except the alumni discount)
documents: Scholarship application on the university's scholarship portal
Programme offer from the University of Glasgow
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic excellence. Decisions are made on a rolling basis within six weeks of the programme offer or scholarship application, whichever is later.
important_dates: Applications: open now for September 2027 entry
Closing date: to be confirmed, usually late August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow is a university in Glasgow, Scotland, and a registered Scottish charity (SC004401). It offers several Global Leadership Scholarships each year across about 250 eligible taught master's programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible master's programme first, then register on the University of Glasgow scholarship portal and submit the Global Leadership Scholarship application. Awards are made on a rolling basis until the places are filled.
opportunities.notes: Diplomas and certificates are not eligible, and the award covers only one year.

opportunities.title: University of Mississippi International Academic Excellence Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year students from secondary schools outside the US with a GPA of 3.25 or higher (US scale) are automatically awarded USD 5,000 to USD 28,893 a year for four years at the University of Mississippi.
opportunities.description:
The University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) in Oxford, Mississippi, gives automatic merit scholarships to international first-year undergraduates who completed secondary school outside the United States. The amount depends on the student's GPA converted to the US 4.0 scale, and the award is sent with the admission letter.

There are four tiers: Mississippi Premier (USD 28,893 a year, about 93% of tuition, for GPA 3.9-4.0, limited to 20 awardees per country each year in order of admission), Mississippi Champion (USD 12,000 a year for GPA 3.75-3.89), Mississippi Magnolia (USD 9,500 a year for GPA 3.5-3.74) and Mississippi Legacy (USD 5,000 a year for GPA 3.25-3.49). Each is renewable for four years if the conditions are met.

For African students with strong school results, applying early matters, because the top tier is capped per country and given in order of admission.
opportunities.benefits: Automatic awards per year for four years: Premier USD 28,893 (about 93% of tuition); Champion USD 12,000 (40%); Magnolia USD 9,500 (32%); Legacy USD 5,000 (17%).
requirements: First-time international freshman
Secondary school completed outside the United States
Minimum GPA 3.25 on the US 4.0 scale (3.9+ for Premier)
Meet English proficiency: e.g. IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 110, PTE-A 53 or TOEFL iBT (79, or 4.5 on the 2026 scale); Nigeria and South Africa are on the exempt list
Admitted to the University of Mississippi
documents: English proficiency scores sent directly by the testing agency (less than two years old)
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are automatic and based on GPA tier; Premier awards are limited to 20 per country per year and given in order of admission.
important_dates: Awards: automatic with the admission decision
Separate Competitive Scholarship: apply by 10 January before fall admission
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Mississippi, known as Ole Miss, is the flagship public university of Mississippi, located in Oxford. Its Office of Global Engagement runs international admissions and scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission at olemiss.edu/applynow and send official school records and English scores. No separate scholarship application is needed; the award is stated in the admission letter.
opportunities.notes: Cannot be combined with SAT/ACT scholarships (the larger award applies). Ole Miss also offers transfer international scholarships of up to 100% of non-resident tuition.

opportunities.title: University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Domestic and international students starting a first doctorate at Otago can apply at any time for a 3-year stipend and fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship funds students doing a PhD or professional doctorate at the University of Otago in New Zealand. It is open to both domestic and international students, and applications can be made at any time of year.

The scholarship pays a stipend for 36 months together with a domestic tuition fee waiver, and up to 164 scholarships are offered each year. Candidates are chosen mainly on academic merit and their potential for research, and they should normally be seeking their first doctoral qualification.

For African graduates with a strong research record, this is a rolling route to a funded doctorate in New Zealand.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of NZ$32,544 per year plus a domestic tuition fee waiver for 36 months (student services fee and insurance not included). The page does not say whether international tuition fees are covered beyond the domestic waiver.
requirements: Open to domestic and international students
Enrolling in a PhD or professional doctorate at the University of Otago
Usually seeking a first doctoral qualification
Strong academic merit and research potential
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made mainly on academic merit and potential for research.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Otago is a New Zealand university that offers up to 164 doctoral scholarships a year to domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for doctoral study and the scholarship through the University of Otago's doctoral application process described on its website; applications are accepted all year.
opportunities.notes: Check with the Graduate Research School whether international tuition is fully covered, since the page mentions only a domestic fee waiver.

opportunities.title: University of Surrey International Excellence Award (Postgraduate) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded international students with a conditional offer for most full-time taught master's starting February or September 2027 automatically receive GBP 5,000 off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The International Excellence Award at the University of Surrey gives international students GBP 5,000 off the tuition fee of a full-time taught master's, with no separate application. It applies to courses starting in February 2027 or September 2027 and is open regardless of nationality.

The award goes to overseas fee-paying students who pay their own fees, so it suits African applicants who are self-funding or funded by family rather than by a government or employer sponsor. For two-year master's it covers the first year only.

A handful of courses are excluded, including the MBA and several science master's, so applicants should check the list before relying on the discount.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 5,000 off tuition fees (first year only for two-year courses). It cannot be paid in cash or used for accommodation and cannot be combined with alumni or early-bird discounts.
requirements: Overseas (international) fee status
Conditional offer for a full-time taught master's starting February or September 2027
Self-funded: fees paid from your own or family funds, not a government, employer or other scholarship
Not progressing from the Surrey International Study Centre

Course not on the exclusion list (part-time, distance learning, MBA, MSc Applied Analytical Chemistry, MSc AI (Conversion), MSc Biotechnology, MSc Food Science, MSc Human Nutrition, MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences)
documents: No separate application: the award follows from the master's application
opportunities.selection_process: Awarded automatically on a first-come, first-served basis to eligible applicants; a scholarship letter is sent about five days after the conditional offer.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Surrey is a UK university in Guildford known for its links with industry, professional training placements and research in engineering, health and the sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible full-time taught master's at Surrey. If eligible you receive a scholarship letter after your conditional offer; accept the offer in the applicant portal and pay the deposit to secure it.
opportunities.notes: Contact: international@surrey.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: VU Block Model International Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international students starting an eligible foundation, bachelor's or coursework master's at VU Melbourne are automatically assessed for up to 30% off tuition.
opportunities.description:
The VU Block Model International Scholarship is a tuition reduction from Victoria University (VU) in Melbourne, Australia, for new international students. Applicants to foundation, undergraduate and postgraduate coursework courses are assessed for it automatically when they apply for a course.

The award can reduce tuition fees by up to 30%. It is named after VU's Block Model, in which students take one unit at a time in short, intensive blocks. The official page does not give an intake year or a separate scholarship deadline, so the discount follows the normal course application timetable.

For African applicants, the attraction is that no extra essay or form is needed: a complete course application with certified documents and English test results puts you in consideration.
opportunities.benefits: Up to 30% off tuition fees for new international students in eligible courses. No living allowance is mentioned.
requirements: New international student starting at VU Melbourne
Eligible foundation, undergraduate or postgraduate coursework course
English test (IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced or B2 First) taken no more than two years before the course starts, unless exempt through English-medium study
Course-specific requirements where applicable (work experience, portfolio, police check)
documents: Certified academic transcripts and supporting documents
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed automatically for the scholarship when their course application is processed; competitive courses rank applicants for admission.
important_dates: Apply by the standard course application deadline for your intake
Credit applications: at least 10 business days before the course application deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Victoria University is a public dual-sector university in Melbourne, Australia, offering vocational, undergraduate and postgraduate study. It teaches most courses through its Block Model of one subject at a time.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply directly through VU's online portal (eaams.vu.edu.au) or through an education agent (agents are compulsory for applicants from some countries). Upload certified transcripts, English results and your passport; the scholarship is assessed with the application.
opportunities.notes: Tuition fees are adjusted each year. Check the VU international scholarships page for the full terms before accepting an offer.

opportunities.title: WHO Internship Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students aged 20 or over with three years of university study, or recent graduates within 18 months, can apply to WHO internship vacancies year-round.
opportunities.description:
The WHO Internship Programme places students and recent graduates in short, full-time internships of six to twenty-four weeks at WHO headquarters in Geneva, at regional offices (including the Africa regional office) and at country offices. Interns work in technical health programmes or in administrative areas such as communications, external relations and human resources.

Vacancies are posted continuously, each with its own closing date, and applications are made only through WHO's online recruitment system. Selection is very competitive and only a small number of interns are taken each year.

Since January 2020 WHO pays a living allowance to interns who need financial support, which opens the programme to African students in public health, medicine and related fields who could not otherwise afford it.
opportunities.benefits: Medical and accident insurance during the internship, a living allowance for eligible interns who need financial support (amount given in the vacancy notice) and lunch vouchers at some duty stations. Travel and insurance outside the internship are the intern's responsibility.
requirements: At least 20 years old on the application date
Enrolled in a university course leading to a formal qualification in a related field, or applying within 18 months of completing one
At least three years of full-time university study
Fluency in one working language of the hiring office
Valid passport of a WHO Member State
Degree from an institution listed in the World Higher Education Database
Not related to a WHO staff member and not a previous WHO intern
documents: Online application in WHO's recruitment system
Proof of enrolment or of the last qualification (when requested)
Declaration of Interest, including any financial support
WHO medical certificate of fitness before starting
opportunities.selection_process: Hiring units review applications to each vacancy; the process is very competitive and only a small number of interns are selected each year. Do not send documents until WHO asks for them.
important_dates: Applications: vacancies posted continuously, each with its own deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The World Health Organization runs its internship programme at its Geneva headquarters and at regional and country offices. Interns work in technical programmes and administrative units.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Browse internship vacancies on WHO's careers site and apply online to each position that interests you through the Stellis recruitment system. Applications sent by other routes are not accepted.

opportunities.title: WIPO Young Experts Program (YEP) Internship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Final-year students and recent graduates of any nationality with English or French can join WIPO's rolling paid internship roster in Geneva.
opportunities.description:
The WIPO Young Experts Program is the World Intellectual Property Organization's paid internship scheme for students in the final stages of a bachelor's or master's degree and for recent graduates. Most interns work at WIPO's headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, for between two and twelve months depending on the position and category.

Applications go into a general roster that is reviewed on a rolling basis, and a new roster is advertised each year; saved applications remain valid for one year. Suitable candidates are invited to a short online interview or test.

WIPO reimburses travel for interns from developing and least developed countries who live in their home country, which makes the programme accessible to African students interested in intellectual property, law, economics, technology and communications.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipend of CHF 1,645 (Category I) or CHF 2,170 (Category II); round-trip travel reimbursement of up to CHF 1,500 for nationals of developing, least developed or transition countries who live in their home country; visa assistance; medical and accident insurance paid by WIPO.
requirements: Category I: final-year (3rd or 4th year) bachelor's students, bachelor's graduates of the last two years, or master's students still completing coursework or thesis
Category II: master's graduates of the last two years, graduate students who have finished coursework, or students pursuing an additional advanced degree
Professional working knowledge of English and/or French
No age limit
Former WIPO interns cannot apply again (other UN internships are fine)
documents: Detailed online profile in WIPO's recruitment system
opportunities.selection_process: WIPO human resources reviews roster applications and motivation letters. Shortlisted candidates take a 30-45 minute online interview or test assessed against WIPO competencies, followed by an offer.
important_dates: Applications: rolling roster, renewed each year
Internship length: 2-6 months (Category I) or 2-12 months (Category II)
opportunities.about_provider: The World Intellectual Property Organization is the United Nations agency for intellectual property, based in Geneva. Most of its internship positions are at its Geneva headquarters.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the current internship roster, create a profile on WIPO's online recruitment system and submit your application with a motivation letter. You will receive a confirmation email, and shortlisted candidates are contacted for an online interview or test.

opportunities.title: Webster University Academic Scholarship for International Students
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International undergraduates admitted to Webster receive renewable tuition-only academic scholarships.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Career Development Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career researchers at eligible not-for-profit organisations in the UK or low- and middle-income countries of Africa and Asia can apply year-round.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome's Career Development Awards support mid-career researchers from any discipline who have the potential to become international research leaders. An award usually lasts eight years (it can be shorter or part-time) and pays for the researcher's salary if needed, up to four full-time staff and research costs.

The administering organisation must be a not-for-profit university, research institute or healthcare body in the UK or in a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (excluding mainland China), so researchers at eligible African institutions can apply. The scheme page says applications are accepted year-round.

Candidates go through an eligibility check, review by a Career Advisory Group and external experts, and an interview in London (remote attendance is possible) before a decision board makes the award.
opportunities.benefits: Salary (if needed), up to four full-time-equivalent staff, research costs usually below £250,000 excluding the applicant's salary, overheads capped at 20%, £2,000 a year for conferences and visa costs for successful awardees.
requirements: Mid-career researcher who has completed one or two substantial periods of research after initial training
Important contributions to their field and potential to become a research leader
At least 80% of time devoted to research
Administering organisation must be a not-for-profit in the UK or a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (not mainland China)
Sponsor and mentor at the organisation
Not already holding an equivalent award
documents: Application on the Wellcome Funding platform
Finance director letter if overheads are requested
Equipment quotes for items of £100,000 or more
opportunities.selection_process: Wellcome checks eligibility, then the Career Advisory Group shortlists, external experts review in writing, and shortlisted applicants are interviewed in London (or remotely) with a presentation. The Discovery Research Decision Board decides, weighting the proposal at 50%, skills and experience at 25% and the research environment at 25%.
important_dates: Next shortlisting listed on the scheme page: 19-21 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome is a UK charitable foundation that funds health research around the world. Its funding schemes are managed through the Wellcome Funding platform.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the application on the Wellcome Funding platform with your sponsor and mentor; your organisation's approver submits it to Wellcome.
opportunities.notes: Parts of the long scheme page were read only in summary, so confirm round dates on the Wellcome Funding platform before applying.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Discovery Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established research leaders at eligible not-for-profit organisations in the UK or low- and middle-income countries of Africa and Asia can apply at any time.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome Discovery Awards fund established researchers, or teams led by one, to pursue bold and creative research on human life, health and wellbeing in any discipline. The average award is about £3.5 million over about seven years (between three and eight years), and teams usually have two to eight applicants.

The administering organisation must be a not-for-profit body, such as a university, research institute, healthcare organisation, charity or social enterprise, in the UK or in a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (excluding mainland China). The scheme page says applications are accepted at any time.

This makes the scheme one of the largest open funding routes for established African research leaders based at eligible African institutions.
opportunities.benefits: Research costs, staff salaries, equipment and overheads (capped at 20% for eligible organisations), plus fees for PhD or master's study for up to two research staff per applicant (maximum eight per team). The lead applicant's salary can be covered only if they are based in a low- or middle-income country on a long-term contract funded by external grants. Average award about £3.5 million; applications over £5 million get extra scrutiny.
requirements: Established researcher with international standing as a research leader
Experience leading innovative research and managing and training others
Permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract (or a guarantee of one)
Not-for-profit administering organisation in the UK or a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (not mainland China)
Only one Discovery Award as sole lead at a time
documents: Application on the Wellcome Funding platform
Research proposal, team details and budget
opportunities.selection_process: Wellcome checks eligibility, one of nine Discovery Advisory Groups shortlists, external experts review, and shortlisted teams present at an interview in London (remote possible). The Discovery Research Decision Board decides, weighting the proposal at 50%, skills and experience at 25% and the research environment at 25%.
important_dates: Interviews: usually in March and July
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome is a UK charitable foundation that funds health research around the world. Its funding schemes are managed through the Wellcome Funding platform.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the scheme guidance, complete the application on the Wellcome Funding platform, and ask your organisation's approver to submit it.
opportunities.notes: Parts of the long scheme page were read only in summary, so confirm current round dates on the Wellcome Funding platform.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Early-Career Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers with a PhD and up to three years of postdoc experience, based at an eligible UK or African/South Asian/South-East Asian organisation.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome's Early-Career Awards fund researchers from any discipline who are ready to lead their own research project for the first time. Awards usually last five years and pay the researcher's salary plus up to £400,000 for research expenses, and the grantholder must spend at least 80% of their time on research.

The administering organisation must be based in the UK or in a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (excluding mainland China), which means researchers at eligible African universities and institutes can apply. The scheme page says applications can be submitted at any time.

Applicants need a sponsor at their organisation and a mentor, and they are assessed on their proposal, their skills and experience, and their research environment.
opportunities.benefits: The grantholder's salary and up to £400,000 for research expenses, usually over five years. The page also mentions relocation support of up to £1,000, training support of up to £500 a year per person and conference support of up to £2,000 a year for the grantholder.
requirements: PhD passed (viva completed) by the submission date, or at least four years of research experience equivalent to a PhD
No more than three years of postdoctoral experience
Must not hold a tenured post
Administering organisation in the UK or a low- or middle-income country in Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia (not mainland China)
At least 80% of working time on research
Sponsor and mentor at the administering organisation
documents: Application on the Wellcome Funding platform
Finance director letter if overheads are requested
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted, reviewed and, if shortlisted, the applicant is interviewed. Assessment weights the research proposal at 50%, skills and experience at 25% and the research environment at 25%.
important_dates: Shortlisting: usually in February, June and September
Interviews: usually in May, September and January
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome is a UK charitable foundation that funds health research around the world. Its funding schemes are managed through the Wellcome Funding platform.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the application on the Wellcome Funding platform with your sponsor and mentor. The administering organisation's approver then submits it to Wellcome.
opportunities.notes: Only one Early-Career Award application can be under consideration at a time, and the award cannot be renewed. Some round dates on the long scheme page could not be read verbatim, so check the Wellcome Funding platform for the next shortlisting date.

opportunities.title: Western Michigan University Global Education Undergraduate Merit Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New international undergraduates on F-1 or J-1 visas with at least a 3.0/4.0 GPA admitted to Western Michigan University can receive up to USD 10,000 a year, awarded on a rolling basis.
opportunities.description:
The Global Education Undergraduate Merit Scholarship is Western Michigan University's main merit award for international bachelor's students. It is managed by the Haenicke Institute for Global Education and is offered to students starting at WMU in Kalamazoo, Michigan, either straight from secondary school or as transfer students.

The scholarship is worth up to USD 10,000 per year, paid in two halves for the fall and spring semesters, and can be held for up to eight semesters or until graduation, whichever comes first. It is applied only to WMU academic tuition. Awards are made on a rolling basis while money lasts, and the university says it receives more eligible applicants than it can fund.

Because there is no separate application, African students simply need to complete their WMU admission file early. Students admitted for fall, spring or summer can be considered.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 10,000 per year towards WMU tuition, paid in two instalments (fall and spring), for up to eight semesters or until graduation.
requirements: Initial F-1 or J-1 visa undergraduate (first-year or transfer)
Non-resident international status
Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (international grades are converted)
Admitted to WMU for fall, spring or summer
Not fully funded by a government/NGO scholarship or a full WMU assistantship
Not enrolled in a fully online programme
documents: Complete WMU undergraduate admission application with all required materials (transcripts, English proficiency proof, financial documents as listed on the admissions page)
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted students are considered automatically. Awards depend on academic merit and the student's total estimated cost, and are made on a rolling basis until funds run out.
opportunities.about_provider: Western Michigan University is a public research university in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Its Haenicke Institute for Global Education runs international admissions and scholarships, and the university notes it is among the half of US public universities that offer a scholarship for international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to Western Michigan University and submit every required document. No additional scholarship application is needed; the university reviews admitted students for the award. Apply early because funds are limited.
opportunities.notes: Cannot be combined with full government/NGO scholarships or full WMU assistantships. F and J students may face US tax withholding (14%) on aid that exceeds qualified expenses. WMU also offers a Global Education Graduate Merit Scholarship (up to USD 10,000 a year for up to four semesters).
